story_body: After nearly three decades building communal life in Jaffa, R' Chaim Shmuel Schmerling passed away on 2 Adar 5654 (February 1894). His biography appears in the Schmerling pamphlet (Tidhar, Tel Aviv 5706) and in Toldos Mishpachas HaRav MiLadi p. 76.

title_en: Chabad community in Jaffa appoints its own rabbi
summary_en: In 5660 the growing Chabad community of Jaffa brought in their own dedicated rabbi.
story_body: As Chabad's presence in Jaffa expanded year by year, the community took the step in 5660 (1900) of installing its own dedicated rabbi. The move marked the maturation of what had begun as a single family's migration in 1866 into a self-governing kehillah.

title_en: Chabad community of Jaffa announces construction of its synagogue
summary_en: On 24 Iyar 5663 the heads of Kollel Chabad announced that the Anash synagogue in Jaffa had been built up to and including the dome.
story_body: On 24 Iyar 5663, leaders of Kollel Chabad recorded in the kollel pinkas that 'in Jaffa Anash are building a beis midrash, and it is already complete up to and including the dome; finishing touches remain.' This was the first synagogue dedicated to Chabad chassidim in Jaffa.

title_en: Refugee Chabad families from Russia resettle in Tel Aviv
summary_en: Between 5695 and 5697 dozens of Chabad families escaped from Soviet Russia and settled in Tel Aviv, founding a new center of Chabad life.
story_body: Between 5695 and 5697, dozens of Chabad families escaped the Soviet Union and arrived in the Land of Israel, most settling in Tel Aviv. They organized themselves and even established a yeshiva. The Rebbe Rayatz founded Agudas Chabad B'Eretz HaKodesh, headquartered in Tel Aviv, alongside the older Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem.

title_en: Montefiore census documents Chabad synagogues in Jerusalem and Hebron
summary_en: The 5615 Montefiore census recorded the synagogues and study halls of Chabad communities in Jerusalem and Hebron.
story_body: The 5615 Montefiore census, published as 'Luach Shemos HaBatei Knesios D'Chabad,' documented Chabad's synagogues and study halls in Jerusalem and Hebron. It described a Jerusalem beis midrash named 'Dat Moshe ViYehudis' (after Montefiore) where twelve bachurim studied gemara, poskim and chassidus under R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin.

title_en: Chabad community in Jerusalem acquires Beit Menachem synagogue
summary_en: From 5618 onward the Chabad community in Jerusalem took possession of the Beit Menachem synagogue on a mashkanta arrangement.
story_body: After being 'wanderers without a synagogue,' as the 5626 Montefiore report put it, the Chabad community in Jerusalem acquired the Beit Menachem synagogue starting in 5618 (1858). They added a study room on its roof, where the Dat Moshe ViYehudis beis midrash later hosted 20 bachurim and 15 baalei batim.

title_en: Cheder branch of Torat Emet founded in Jaffa
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayyatz instructed R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin to establish a cheder in Jaffa as a branch of the Torat Emet yeshiva in Jerusalem.
story_body: In a letter dated Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5684, the Rebbe Rayyatz responded to pleas from Chabad chassidim in Jaffa about their dire spiritual situation and instructed Havlin, director of Torat Emet in Jerusalem, to organize a children's cheder and yeshiva there under the Torat Emet name. R' David Patash, a prominent member of the Tel Aviv chareidi community who had recently arrived from Russia, helped lead the effort. The Rebbe also wrote directly to Patash a few weeks later seeking his help to support the new institution.

title_en: Rebbe Rayyatz writes to R' David Patash about the Jaffa cheder
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayyatz wrote to R' David Patash on 3 Tevet 5684 urging him to assist in founding a talmud torah and yeshiva in Jaffa.
story_body: Having received a letter from Chabad chassidim in Jaffa describing the spiritual ruin of their community, the Rebbe explained that Torat Emet of Jerusalem lacked resources to open a branch. Since Patash, recently arrived from Russia, was known for his devotion to Torah causes, the Rebbe asked him to take up the project. The letter set the stage for Patash to become a central supporter of the new institution.

title_en: Jaffa branch of Torat Emet officially opens
summary_en: During the summer of 5684 the Chabad cheder opened in Jaffa as a branch of the Torat Emet yeshiva of Jerusalem.
story_body: Following months of planning and the Rebbe Rayyatz's letters from late 5683 and early 5684, the cheder finally opened in Jaffa during the summer of 1924. By Elul of that year the Rebbe was already referring to it as an established branch in a fundraising letter for Torat Emet. R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin oversaw the institution from Jerusalem, with local support led by Patash, R' Yaakov Malkov, and R' Zalman Aharon Menevitch.

title_en: Havlin reports over 100 students at the Jaffa cheder
summary_en: On 15 Elul 5684 R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin wrote that more than 100 children of immigrants were studying at the new Jaffa cheder.
story_body: In a letter to R' Yehuda Leib Horowitz, Havlin described how he was compelled to fulfill the Rebbe Rayyatz's instruction to establish the cheder after the chassidim of Jaffa pleaded with the Rebbe to provide schooling for their children. He reported that more than one hundred children of immigrants, who otherwise had no place for traditional Torah education, were now learning in the cheder.

title_en: Kol Yisrael article exposes Tel Aviv municipality's pressure on Chabad cheder
summary_en: R' Yaakov Malkov published an article in Kol Yisrael on 6 Tevet 5685 exposing the Tel Aviv municipality's hostility toward the Chabad cheder.
story_body: After a donor offered to fund a building for the cheder, Malkov reported that the Tel Aviv municipality demanded either Hebrew-only instruction under municipal supervision, or a 40-pound permit fee. The municipality referred the matter to Ahad Ha'am, who refused to support the institution while it taught in Yiddish. Malkov framed this as religious persecution dressed in linguistic guise and a painful absurdity for Jewish life in Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: Branch of Torat Emet opens in Rishon LeZion
summary_en: A second branch of the Torat Emet network opened in Rishon LeZion during 5685, the year after the Jaffa branch.
story_body: Building on the precedent set in Jaffa, a further branch was opened in Rishon LeZion. The Rebbe Rayyatz referred to both branches in his letter of 2 Shvat 5686 to R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin, asking for more detailed reports from Tel Aviv and Rishon LeZion.

title_en: Rebbe Rayyatz urges restoring Tel Aviv cheder as Torat Emet branch
summary_en: On 3 Adar Sheni 5687 the Rebbe Rayyatz wrote lamenting the decline of the Tel Aviv cheder and urging its reorganization as a Torat Emet branch.
story_body: Responding to a report about the diminished state of the Tel Aviv cheder, the Rebbe expressed sorrow that financial shortfall had shrunk the institution. He emphasized that the original plan was for Torat Emet to plant branches in every city in Eretz Yisrael, and asked the new local manager R' Uri to formally re-establish the Tel Aviv cheder as a branch of Torat Emet under Jerusalem's direction.

title_en: Last documented mention of the original Tel Aviv cheder
summary_en: On 15 Sivan 5689 R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin wrote from the U.S. to his son about the cheder's building and its administration.
story_body: Writing from America, Havlin asked his son to coordinate with R' Yaakov Malkov regarding fundraising and synagogue matters, while keeping the actual cheder and the courtyard and houses under the supervision of his other son Shalom. This is the last reference to the original Tel Aviv cheder in the documented record before it apparently closed.

title_en: Tel Aviv cheder has closed; Havlin seeks to rent the building
summary_en: On 20 Menachem Av 5695 Havlin asked the Beit Din for permission to rent out the closed cheder's building on Rav Kook Street to support Torat Emet.
story_body: Citing the dire financial state of Torat Emet in Jerusalem, Havlin requested rabbinic approval to rent out the building at 16 Rav Kook Street in Tel Aviv, which had been donated by Mr. Friedman and registered in Havlin's name to circumvent registration restrictions. The rental did not actually take place, and the building was soon dedicated as a Chabad synagogue.

title_en: Separate Chabad fund for Eretz Yisrael is founded
summary_en: In 5565 the Alter Rebbe established a separate fund for Chabad chassidim living in Eretz Yisrael, distinct from the older joint kollel.
story_body: Whereas the Alter Rebbe had previously served as nasi over Eretz Yisrael funds in general, sent through the chief gabbai R' Yaakov of Smilyan and distributed in the Land by R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and then R' Avraham of Kalisk, in 5565 he founded a dedicated kollel fund for Anshei Chabad. This created the institutional framework that would evolve into Kollel Chabad of Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: Founding of Kollel Chabad as a fourth separate kollel in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In 5587 Kollel Chabad was constituted as a fourth distinct kollel, alongside the Sephardim, Perushim, and Chassidim kollelim.
story_body: Building on the dedicated Chabad fund founded by the Alter Rebbe two decades earlier, Kollel Chabad emerged as an independent kollel structure in 5587. Over the following 40 years the four general kollelim subdivided into dozens of subsidiary kollelim corresponding to towns and regions of origin, until the 5626 merger created the Vaad HaKollel HaKlali.

title_en: Vaad HaKlali unites all Ashkenazi kollelim in Jerusalem
summary_en: In 5626 the various Ashkenazi kollelim in Jerusalem united under the Vaad HaKlali, established to address the fragmentation of the yishuv.
story_body: Seeing that the Ashkenazi community had splintered into many particular kollelim, each looking after its own interests while the community as a whole declined, the rabbis and trustees of Jerusalem established a unified Vaad to oversee shared communal needs and represent the community to the Ottoman authorities. Both Perushim and Chassidim subdivisions participated, with one trustee from each kollel sitting on the Vaad.

title_en: Amsterdam Pekoa"M directs Hebron trustees to share funds with Jerusalem Chabad chassidim
summary_en: On 26 Tishrei 5626 the Amsterdam Pekoa"M wrote to the Hebron trustees endorsing distribution of Kollel Chabad funds to chassidim in Jerusalem.
story_body: The Amsterdam Pekudei Eretz Yisrael had sent funds to Hebron on the understanding that they would be distributed to Kollel Chabad members across the land. The trustees confirmed that since the regular kollel income was already feeding Jerusalem chassidim, they had now allocated the new donation accordingly, drawing it from the Hebron portion. This exchange illustrates Hebron's role as the Kollel Chabad center distributing funds throughout the four holy cities.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab letter to Jerusalem trustees on schools and chalukah
summary_en: On 21 Av 5662 the Rebbe Rashab decreed that Kollel Chabad members sending children to secular schools or shaving their beards must be denied chalukah.
story_body: Reacting with anguish to news that some Kollel Chabad members were sending their children to modern schools, the Rebbe Rashab insisted that the kollel was founded for those engaged in Torah and avodah in Eretz Yisrael, not for supporting those undermining traditional Jewish life. He ruled that beard-shavers and parents enrolling children in such schools must be cut from the chalukah lists, a position the Jerusalem trustees only partially implemented after a year of dispute.

title_en: Jerusalem trustees report partial implementation of Rashab's school ruling
summary_en: On 4 Nisan 5663 the Jerusalem trustees informed the gabbaim abroad that beard-shavers and parents sending children to secular schools received only one-third of their chalukah.
story_body: After a year of correspondence about how strictly to apply the Rebbe Rashab's ruling, the Jerusalem trustees reported that those violating the standards had now received only a third of their normal portion. They pushed back on the gabbaim's complaint that these recipients had been paid before God-fearing poor families, asserting that the God-fearing poor had in fact been paid first.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab letter to trustees defining Kollel Chabad's purpose
summary_en: On 27 Tevet 5666 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to the Jerusalem trustees defining the kollel's purpose as supporting Torah and avodah, not merely settling the land.
story_body: The Rebbe articulated his understanding that the holy fathers had founded the Eretz Yisrael fund specifically because the land was uniquely suited to Torah and avodah, and not for the sake of artisans and businessmen lacking the yoke of Torah. He returned to this theme in many later letters, in ongoing tension with the Jerusalem trustees who maintained a broader yishuv-support mission.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab appoints R' Yisrael Dovber Frumkin as Kollel Chabad trustee
summary_en: On 21 Menachem Av 5666 the Rebbe Rashab notified Jerusalem trustees that he had appointed R' Yisrael Dovber Frumkin as an additional trustee.
story_body: Hoping that Frumkin's character and standing would help reform the kollel's distribution practices in line with the policy he had set out the same day in a parallel letter to Frumkin, the Rebbe instructed the existing trustees to admit Frumkin to the vaad and make no decisions without him. The Jerusalem trustees and the rebbes of Lyadi and Bobruisk resisted the appointment, and after months of dispute it was unclear whether Frumkin ever effectively served.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab confirms broader rabbinic consensus around Kollel Chabad reform
summary_en: On 8 Iyar 5667 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to his son the Rayyatz that the rebbes of Lyadi, Bobruisk and Retzitza all now agreed to Frumkin's appointment.
story_body: Writing to the future Rebbe Rayyatz, the Rashab reported that R' Yeshaya Berlin had received word from the Rebbe of Lyadi confirming consensus around Frumkin, with the rebbes of Bobruisk and Retzitza also agreeing. He hoped this would finally settle the matter so that the land might be quiet, though as he wrote a week later he could only hope it was truly so.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel Naeh appointed Kollel Chabad trustee
summary_en: In the summer of 5672 R' Menachem Mendel Naeh became a trustee of Kollel Chabad and received instructions from the Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab wrote to Naeh asking him to undertake reforms in the kollel concerning prayer and Torah study, so that it would at least partially correspond to the holy intent of its founders. The appointment came amid a broader period of transition in the kollel leadership, including the death of R' Dovber Efrat on Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz that same summer.

title_en: R' Dovber Efrat passes away
summary_en: R' Dovber Efrat, a Jerusalem trustee and ba'al ha'adres of Kollel Chabad, passed away on Erev Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5672.
story_body: Efrat had been one of the Jerusalem trustees and also served as a ba'al ha'adres handling the Chabad fund's mail address. His death left two key positions vacant. The Rebbe Rashan of Bobruisk wrote to Jerusalem proposing that the elderly R' Gershon Lipschitz be appointed as trustee in his stead.

title_en: Rebbe Rayyatz reaffirms Kollel Chabad is for Torah scholars only
summary_en: On 29 Shvat 5682 the Rebbe Rayyatz wrote that Kollel Chabad exists solely for those who dwell in the tent of Torah.
story_body: Echoing his father the Rashab's earlier letter, the Rayyatz declared that he could not extend his hand to anyone who wished to maintain the kollel for the sake of general yishuv-support. The kollel was created for those sitting in Torah, he insisted, and they were its essential beneficiaries. This continued a multi-decade debate over the kollel's purpose.

title_en: R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov serves as chief gabbai of Kollel Chabad
summary_en: From around 5615 R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov was appointed by the Tzemach Tzedek as chief gabbai of Kollel Chabad, a role he held for over thirty years.
story_body: Joining the existing gabbaim R' A. of Rogachov and R' Yitzchok Aizik of Bichov, Tomarkin became the dominant figure in administering Kollel Chabad's overseas fundraising. The Tzemach Tzedek himself prepared the lists of distribution recipients, and after the Rebbe's passing in 5626 Tomarkin continued under the leadership of the Tzemach Tzedek's sons. He led the Rogachover Vaad that prepared the distribution lists in the decades that followed.

title_en: Tel Aviv trustees attempt to dismantle Rogachov Vaad and Hebron leadership
summary_en: In 5648 the Jerusalem Kollel Chabad trustees moved to abolish R' Dan Tomarkin's appointment, eliminate the shadarim, and shift the center from Hebron to Jerusalem.
story_body: Calling themselves "heads of Kollel Chabad," the Jerusalem trustees circulated public notices proposing that every city send its donations directly through the post to Jerusalem, bypassing the overseas shadarim and the Hebron trustees. The Hebron community and many Jerusalemites protested fiercely in a counter-broadside, but the Jerusalem trustees succeeded on all three counts. From this point Hebron lost its place as the administrative center of the kollel.

title_en: R' Chaim Eliezer Bichovsky enters the etrog trade for Kollel Chabad
summary_en: In 5651 R' Chaim Eliezer Bichovsky took over the Kollel Chabad etrog trade, a cover for the Eretz Yisrael fund.
story_body: Bichovsky later recounted in a public reply that he had begun handling "the etrog business" of Kollel Chabad in 5651, the trade serving as a discreet front for the Eretz Yisrael fundraising operation. He partnered with R' Chaim Bagin, and the two ran the renamed Vaad Mesadrei HaReshimah until 5673, when leadership changed again.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab affirms Slonim-Shlank as Kollel Chabad address
summary_en: Rebbe Rashab wrote that the official address for Kollel Chabad donations should remain 'Slonim Shlank'.
story_body: On 26 Cheshvan 5672 (Nov 1911), the Rebbe Rashab wrote in letter 349 affirming that the official mailing address for Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem should be 'Slonim Shlank' – the names of administrators R. Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R. Mordechai Shlank. This was meant to maintain the existing administrative structure of the kollel.

title_en: Jerusalem Anash hold elections, install three new Kollel administrators
summary_en: A group of 76 Anash in Jerusalem held elections and chose three new administrators for Kollel Chabad.
story_body: On 15 Tammuz 5672 (July 1912), 76 members of Anash gathered in Jerusalem and ran their own election for kollel administrators, choosing R. Shmuel Halevi Levin, R. Gershon Lapshitz, and R. Moshe Kazarnovsky. The move was undertaken without the consent of the Rebbe Rashab and ultimately led to a years-long split in Kollel Chabad.

title_en: Bobruisk Rebbe writes about Kollel donations after R. Dovid Aharon's passing
summary_en: The Rebbe of Bobruisk wrote that etrog donations should now be sent in the names of Slonim and Shlank.
story_body: In a letter dated 5 Menachem Av 5672 (July/Aug 1912), the Bobruisker Rebbe instructed the local administrators to publish in HaModia news of the passing of R. Dovid Aharon and direct that those sending money for etrogim send it under the names of Shlank and Slonim. The letter was preserved in several public circulars of the time.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab appoints R. Menachem Mendel Naeh as Kollel administrator
summary_en: Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Menachem Mendel Naeh asking him to accept appointment as a Kollel Chabad administrator.
story_body: On 16 Elul 5672 (Aug/Sept 1912), the Rebbe Rashab wrote letter 341 (vol. II) asking R. Menachem Mendel Naeh, an experienced accountant who had managed Kollel finances for years, to formally accept the title of administrator. Naeh had previously refused the title in 5669 but agreed to participate informally. He now accepted out of deference to the Rebbe.

title_en: Eretz Yisrael Anash ratify R. Menachem Mendel Naeh's appointment
summary_en: Anash throughout the Holy Land ratified the Rebbe's appointment of R. Menachem Mendel Naeh as Kollel administrator.
story_body: At the beginning of Marcheshvan 5673 (Oct/Nov 1912), the public of Anash from all parts of Eretz Yisrael affirmed the Rebbe Rashab's appointment of R. Menachem Mendel Naeh and signed letters confirming the new administrative arrangement. This was documented in the kuntres 'Tumas Yesharim'.

title_en: Bobruisker Rebbe describes growing rift in Kollel Chabad
summary_en: The Bobruisker Rebbe wrote a public letter describing the growing split between the old and new Kollel administrators.
story_body: In Adar 5673 (Feb/March 1913), the Bobruisker Rebbe published a circular describing how R. Gershon Lapshitz had proposed forming a separate kollel. He recounted that the old administrators threatened poor recipients with loss of stipends if they accepted money from the new ones, but in the end the breach widened. The letter was circulated under the title 'Copy of Letters of the Bobruisker Rebbe Regarding Etrog Trade'.

title_en: R. Naeh reports formation of rival Lapshitz-Kazarnovsky vaad
summary_en: R. Menachem Mendel Naeh wrote to his brother-in-law describing the formation of a separate Lapshitz-Kazarnovsky vaad.
story_body: On 13 Iyar 5673 (May 1913), R. Menachem Mendel Naeh wrote that on Sunday, Gershon Lapshitz and Moshe Kazarnovsky had gathered ten men at the home of R. Shmuel Levin and signed a paper agreeing to form their own vaad. This is the earliest dated documentation of the formal organizational split.

title_en: Bobruisker Rebbe formally approves separate Kollel under Lapshitz-Kazarnovsky
summary_en: The Bobruisker Rebbe wrote that he had approved formation of a separate vaad under Lapshitz and Kazarnovsky.
story_body: In Iyar 5673 (May 1913), the Bobruisker Rebbe issued a letter stating that a gathering of important Kollel members had concluded that a separate vaad must be established and that he had consented. He directed that any money sent in their names would reach the poor efficiently.

title_en: Founding of separate 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad'
summary_en: A formal separate kollel called 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad' was founded, splitting Kollel Chabad in two.
story_body: In the summer of 5673 (1913), the three new administrators – Lapshitz, Kazarnovsky and Levin – decided to formally constitute a separate kollel, named 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad'. They explained their decision in two kuntreisim, 'Tzedek u-Mishpat u-Meisharim' and 'Divrei Shalom v'Emes'. This separate kollel persisted for roughly ten years before reunification.

title_en: Post-WWI Kollel elections install three administrators and four-man council
summary_en: After WWI displacement, Kollel Chabad held secret-ballot elections for three administrators and a four-man council.
story_body: At the end of Tevet 5680 (Jan 1920), after most Anash had returned from wartime exile and one of the administrators (R. Mordechai Dovber Slonim) had passed away, the surviving members of Kollel Chabad held elections by secret ballot. They selected three administrators and four council members to jointly manage the kollel, explicitly declaring the kollel under the authority of the Rebbe of Lubavitch.

title_en: Kollel Chabad accepts Rebbe Rayatz as Nasi after Rashab's passing
summary_en: Upon news of Rebbe Rashab's passing, the Kollel Chabad community signed a statement accepting Rayatz as Nasi.
story_body: In Shvat 5681 (Feb 1921), as the time for the kollel's annual elections arrived, the shocking news of the Rebbe Rashab's passing reached Jerusalem. Most members of the kollel gathered and signed a document accepting Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak (Rayatz) as their rebbe in spiritual guidance and as Nasi of the kollel, and asked the existing administrators to continue for another year.

title_en: Kollel administrators ask Rebbe Rayatz to formally accept Nesius
summary_en: Kollel Chabad administrators wrote to Rebbe Rayatz formally asking him to accept the Nesius of the kollel.
story_body: On 10 Kislev 5682 (Dec 1921), administrators Menachem Mendel Naeh and Moshe Ornstein wrote to Rebbe Rayatz describing the post-war renewal of the kollel and the community's vote in Shvat 5681 to accept him as Nasi. They asked him to confirm and direct the next round of elections.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes lengthy response to Kollel administrators
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz wrote a detailed reply to the 10 Kislev letter, but it was delayed in transit for months.
story_body: On 24 Tevet 5682 (Jan 1922), Rebbe Rayatz composed a long reply to Naeh and Ornstein about kollel management, but the original letter has not survived. Its contents are known only through later correspondence in which he summarized it. The letter took roughly four months to arrive in Jerusalem.

title_en: Rayatz writes to R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin about Kollel matters
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin acknowledging news from Jerusalem about the kollel.
story_body: On 10 Shvat 5682 (Feb 1922), Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter 106 to R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin in Jerusalem, thanking him for regular updates and expressing hope that the kollel was being run faithfully along the lines his late father had outlined in tarav. He also referenced his 24 Tevet letter to Naeh, which Havlin had not yet seen.

title_en: R. Naeh writes that Rebbe's 24 Tevet letter has not arrived
summary_en: R. Naeh wrote to Rayatz expressing concern that the long-awaited 24 Tevet letter had been lost in the mail.
story_body: On 7 Nissan 5682 (April 1922), R. Menachem Mendel Naeh wrote to Rebbe Rayatz expressing anxiety that the substantial letter of 24 Tevet had not arrived after such a long delay. He worried that the postal route had encountered some disaster and that the letter was lost.

title_en: R. Naeh responds to Rayatz's letter on Kollel's mission
summary_en: After receiving the long-delayed 24 Tevet letter, R. Naeh replied affirming the kollel's mission to support scholars.
story_body: On 18 Sivan 5682 (June 1922), R. Naeh wrote a substantive reply to Rebbe Rayatz's recently-received letter. He agreed with the Rebbe's vision that the original purpose of the RMBN (Rabbi Meir Baal HaNes) fund was to support scholars in Eretz Yisrael, while acknowledging that since the era of the Tzemach Tzedek, simple working families had also been supported.

title_en: R. Naeh notes long correspondence delays before Sukkos 5683
summary_en: R. Naeh wrote that multiple summer letters had not been acknowledged, and promised to send a copy.
story_body: Erev Sukkos 5683 (Oct 1922), R. Naeh wrote to Rebbe Rayatz that he had sent multiple letters that summer with no acknowledgment, and that he was puzzled by the Rebbe's failure to receive his 18 Sivan response. He promised to send a carbon copy of the letter after the holiday.

title_en: R. Naeh sends Rayatz a carbon copy of his Sivan letter
summary_en: R. Naeh sent Rebbe Rayatz a carbon copy of his 18 Sivan letter after the original failed to arrive.
story_body: On 4 Marcheshvan 5683 (Oct/Nov 1922), R. Naeh fulfilled his Erev Sukkos promise and sent Rebbe Rayatz a copy of the long letter he had written on 18 Sivan, enclosing the carbon. This is illustrative of how slowly correspondence flowed between Eretz Yisrael and Soviet Russia in this period.

title_en: Rayatz writes to R. Zalman Yitzchak Volshanik of Riga about Kollel
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Zalman Yitzchak Volshanik of Riga about Kollel finances and supporting Torah scholars.
story_body: On 3 Adar Sheni 5684 (March 1924), Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter 191 to R. Zalman Yitzchak Volshanik of Riga. He explained that he had purposely refrained from replying earlier, overwhelmed by his struggle to sustain Torah scholars under Soviet conditions, and emphasized that the kollel must focus on supporting scholars rather than on the schism between the two kollels.

title_en: Rayatz appoints five trusted men to oversee Kollel matters
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz appointed five trusted associates to evaluate Kollel Chabad and report back to him.
story_body: On 7 Iyar 5684 (May 1924), after two more years of inconclusive correspondence, Rebbe Rayatz appointed a committee of five trusted associates: R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin, R. Shiloh, R. Yitzchak Shmuel Luria, R. Menachem Mendel Naeh and R. Moshe Dov Rivkin. He asked them to examine the kollel's true situation so he could direct its restoration.

title_en: Five-man committee proposes formalizing Rayatz's Kollel Nesius
summary_en: Rayatz's five appointees wrote to the Kollel administrators proposing government recognition of his Nesius.
story_body: On 12 Sivan 5684 (June 1924), the five-man committee wrote to the kollel administrators proposing that they formalize Rebbe Rayatz's Nesius through official government recognition, granting him authority to manage all kollel matters via his representative and to amend its bylaws. The administrators replied affirmatively, contingent on Rayatz's formal acceptance.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz founds Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz issued the founding letter establishing Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: On 19 Tammuz 5701 (July 1941), during WWII, Rebbe Rayatz issued the founding letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. V, 1482) establishing Agudat Chasidei Chabad in Eretz Yisrael. He called for branches in every city to host public chassidus classes and gatherings, and appointed R. Shaul Dov Zislin, R. Moshe Gurary and R. Chaim Yosef Rosenblum as the founding committee.

title_en: Founding Vaad of Agudat Chasidei Chabad reports first progress
summary_en: The Founding Vaad of Agudat Chasidei Chabad sent Rebbe Rayatz its first detailed progress report.
story_body: On 8 Kislev 5702 (Nov 1941), the Founding Vaad wrote to Rebbe Rayatz reporting that branches of Agudat Chasidei Chabad had been established in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem (as central branches), as well as in Haifa, Petach Tikvah, Bnei Brak, Ramat Gan, Rishon LeTzion, Chadera, Kfar Yechezkel and Migdal.

title_en: Rayatz responds to Agudat Chasidei Chabad first report
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged the first report from the Founding Vaad but urged greater effort.
story_body: On 6 Adar 5702 (Feb 1942), Rebbe Rayatz wrote letter 1719 acknowledging receipt of the Vaad's 8 Kislev report, the first since the founding letter of 19 Tammuz tashah. While crediting them for what was accomplished, he urged that more must be done to spread chassidus and strengthen Torah learning.

title_en: RMM of Vitebsk leads chassidic caravan from Russia to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a chassidic caravan of over 300 souls from Russia toward Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: In Adar 5537 (March 1777), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk set out from Russia with two of the Maggid's disciples, R. Avraham of Kalisk and R. Yisrael of Polotsk, intending to lead a select group to Eretz Yisrael. Along the way more than 400 people joined them, gathering at Mohilov Podolsk on the Dniester to sail in several ships via Constantinople.

title_en: Chassidic caravan ship sinks in Black Sea; some 30 of 80 survive
summary_en: One of the chassidic caravan's ships sank in the Black Sea; about 30 of 80 Jewish passengers survived.
story_body: On the journey from Mohilov to Constantinople in 1777, a severe storm sank one of the caravan's ships near Crimea. About 80 Jews were aboard; only some 30 survived, landing destitute in Gozlov (Eupatoria). With help from Jews of Krasov and Keilah and the Karaite community of Kafa, some survivors made their way back to Russia while others continued on to Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: RMM of Vitebsk and chassidic caravan arrive in Tzfat
summary_en: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and roughly 300 chassidim arrived in Tzfat after a six-month journey.
story_body: On 5 Elul 5537 (September 1777), the chassidic caravan led by R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk arrived safely in Tzfat. The six-month journey from Russia had cost many lives in a Black Sea shipwreck, but the remaining group of about 300 souls reached the Holy Land, an event documented in letters by R. Yisrael of Polotsk and R. Avraham of Kalisk.

title_en: R. Yisrael of Polotsk writes from Jassy to Vitebsk-Polotsk leaders
summary_en: R. Yisrael of Polotsk, returning as an emissary, wrote from Jassy reporting on the aliyah and shipwreck.
story_body: On 9 Iyar 5538 (May 1778), R. Yisrael of Polotsk wrote from Jassy, while traveling as a shadar (emissary), to the leaders of the Vitebsk and Polotsk communities. He reported the arrival of the caravan in Tzfat on 5 Elul tarki''z, described the Black Sea shipwreck and the miraculous survival of about 30 souls, and detailed the spiritual aims of the new community.

title_en: R. Avraham of Kalisk writes to Smilian about the aliyah journey
summary_en: R. Avraham of Kalisk wrote to the community of Smilian recounting the aliyah journey from Russia.
story_body: In the winter of 5538 (1777-1778), R. Avraham of Kalisk wrote a letter (Likkutei Amarim 29) to the community of Smilian recounting the chassidic caravan's journey from Russia in Adar 5537 and its eventual arrival in Eretz Yisrael. This is one of the earliest documentary sources for that aliyah.

title_en: RMM of Vitebsk writes first letter from Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote his first letter from Eretz Yisrael describing the arrival and shipwreck.
story_body: In the winter of 5538 (1777-1778), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk composed his first letter from the Holy Land. He described the safe arrival of the caravan in Tzfat despite the tragic shipwreck, marveled at the survival of about 30 souls who later joined him in Eretz Yisrael, and asked his disciples in Russia to pray for the new community.

title_en: Three tzaddikim issue decree forbidding loans from Eretz Yisrael fund
summary_en: R. Yisrael of Polotsk, R. Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and the Alter Rebbe banned loans from the Eretz Yisrael fund.
story_body: Around 5541 (1781), the three tzaddikim entrusted with managing the Eretz Yisrael fund in Russia issued a binding decree (with nidui and shamta) forbidding anyone, including themselves, from borrowing even a single peruta from the money collected. The decree was prompted by losses sustained when administrators had used the money for other mitzvah purposes.

title_en: RMM of Vitebsk endorses three tzaddikim's leadership of Russian chassidim
summary_en: RMM of Vitebsk wrote endorsing R. Yisrael of Polotsk, R. Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and the Alter Rebbe.
story_body: On 4 Adar 5542 (Feb 1782), R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote that Russian chassidim should not travel long distances to other leaders in Volhynia but should consult the three great tzaddikim already among them. He named R. Yisrael of Polotsk, R. Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and the Alter Rebbe (R. Shneur Zalman), affirming their authority over the Eretz Yisrael fund.

title_en: Alter Rebbe describes R. Yaakov of Smilian's two years as ma'amados gabbai
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe wrote that R. Yaakov of Smilian had served for two years as a faithful collector of Eretz Yisrael funds.
story_body: In early summer 5543 (1783), the Alter Rebbe wrote in a letter (Yagdil Torah NY 51) that R. Yaakov of Smilian had served with great effort for two years as a trusted emissary collecting Eretz Yisrael funds. This implies that R. Yaakov was appointed in 5541, around the time the three tzaddikim formalized their joint leadership.

title_en: Beginning of opposition against the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: A formal dispute against the Alter Rebbe by R. Avraham of Kalisk began in 5563.
story_body: In 5563 (1802/1803), the dispute against the Alter Rebbe – originating from R. Avraham of Kalisk in Eretz Yisrael – formally erupted. The Alter Rebbe later noted that twenty-two years of supportive correspondence (beginning in 5542) had ended with this conflict, marking a significant rupture in the chassidic leadership of the time.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk announces emissary's safe return
summary_en: In a Nisan 5541 letter from Tiberias, R' Menachem Mendel announces the safe return of emissary R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen.
story_body: Writing from Tiberias in Nisan 5541, R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk reports that 'our beloved, wondrous rabbi R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen, our emissary,' has returned safely with his person and finances intact. The letter does not specify when he had departed for the diaspora. Scholars conjecture, based on R' Shlomo Segal's 5539 journey, that R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen left on his first shadar mission in 5540.

title_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen departs Tiberias on second shadar mission
summary_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen leaves Tiberias as emissary toward the end of winter 5545.
story_body: His signature on a Mi Sheberach written by the chassidim of Tiberias during winter 5545 places him in the city at that time. He left Tiberias at the end of that winter as shadar on his second mission to the diaspora, returning to the Land of Israel in the autumn of the following year.

title_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen returns to Tiberias with companions
summary_en: In mid-Cheshvan 5546 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen reaches Tiberias with two companions and all collected donations.
story_body: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk writes that in mid-Cheshvan 5546 the emissary R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen arrived safely back in Tiberias, accompanied by R' Tzvi Hirsch Besht of Vitebsk and R' Gershon Shochet. All three were in good health and brought the entirety of the trumah funds raised abroad.

title_en: Passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
summary_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, leader of the chassidic settlement in the Holy Land, passes away in summer 5548.
story_body: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, the foremost disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch who led the 1777 chassidic aliyah, passed away in summer 5548. After his passing, R' Avraham of Kalisk continued to guide the Holy Land community, while the Alter Rebbe assumed responsibility for the chassidim in Russia and their fundraising for Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen begins third shadar mission
summary_en: In late summer 5549 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen departs as emissary for a third time, carrying a letter signed by 21 chassidim.
story_body: At the end of summer 5549 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen left the Land of Israel as shadar for the third time. His authorization letter was signed by 21 chassidim from Tiberias, Tzfat, and Pekiin. This mission lasted three full years before he returned home.

title_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen returns to Tiberias from three-year mission
summary_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen returns to Tiberias for the Shabbat between Yom Kippur and Sukkot of 5553.
story_body: After three years abroad, R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen reached Tiberias for the Shabbat between Yom Kippur and Sukkot 5553. In a letter to the chassidim in Russia he announced his return, writing that 'we have arrived in the holy city safely, all is peace.'

title_en: First printing of the Tanya
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe's foundational chassidic work, the Tanya, is printed in winter 5557.
story_body: During the winter of 5557 the Alter Rebbe published the Tanya, formalizing the Chabad approach to chassidic teachings in print. Until this point no doctrinal disputes had surfaced between him and R' Avraham of Kalisk, but the printing immediately drew a sharp critical response from R' Avraham, who argued that disseminating intellectual chassidic doctrine broadly contradicted the path of the Maggid of Mezritch.

title_en: R' Avraham of Kalisk critiques the Tanya in writing
summary_en: After the Tanya's printing, R' Avraham of Kalisk writes a long letter critiquing the work and the Chabad doctrinal approach.
story_body: Following the appearance of the Tanya in 5557, R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote to the Alter Rebbe that he found no value in 'the Book of the Beinonim' for saving souls, since common chassidim need only faith in their teachers, not intellectual analysis. He simultaneously addressed the Russian chassidic community, urging that chassidic texts be gathered and kept hidden among the spiritually refined rather than studied broadly. He grounded his position on the rabbinic teaching 'the righteous shall live by his faith.'

title_en: Alter Rebbe's first arrest – Tzok HaItim
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe is arrested in 5559, leaving him unable to respond to correspondence until 5560.
story_body: In 5559 the Alter Rebbe was arrested during what he later called 'tzok haitim' – the pressing times. As a result, although R' Avraham of Kalisk's letter had reached him in 5558, he was unable to compose a proper reply until 5560. This first imprisonment in Petersburg is the famous episode that Chabad commemorates each Yud-Tes Kislev as the day of his miraculous liberation.

title_en: Passing of R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen in Tiberias
summary_en: R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen, three-time shadar of the Tiberias chassidim, passes away on 10 Adar II.
story_body: On 10 Adar II 5559 R' Shlomo Zalman HaKohen passed away in Tiberias. He had served the chassidic communities of the Holy Land on three lengthy shadar missions over more than two decades. His son R' Yitzchak later took up emissary duty in 5571.

title_en: Alter Rebbe sends full doctrinal reply to R' Avraham of Kalisk
summary_en: After the delay caused by his imprisonment, the Alter Rebbe sends a substantive reply to R' Avraham of Kalisk in 5560.
story_body: Only in 5560, after his release from imprisonment, did the Alter Rebbe finally answer R' Avraham of Kalisk's doctrinal challenges with what he called 'a proper response.' That foundational explanation of his approach has not survived. R' Avraham accepted the answer fully in his letters of 5561.

title_en: R' Avraham of Kalisk reconciles with the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: In 5561 R' Avraham of Kalisk writes accepting the Alter Rebbe's reply, calling for unity and asking that past disputes be forgotten.
story_body: Two letters from R' Avraham of Kalisk in 5561 survive. One, addressed to the Alter Rebbe, asks that 'former matters not be remembered, what has passed is past.' The other, to the entire Chabad community in Russia, declares that no real difference exists between him and the Alter Rebbe — 'not a hairsbreadth' — especially regarding the practice of hitbonenut (contemplative meditation).

title_en: R' Aryeh Leib of Volochisk emigrates to the Holy Land
summary_en: R' Aryeh Leib of Volochisk ascends to Eretz Yisrael in summer 5565, carrying funds from R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev.
story_body: In summer 5565 the elderly R' Aryeh Leib of Volochisk made aliyah, carrying with him funds entrusted by R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev for distribution to the poor in the Land of Israel. The Chozeh of Lublin's letter to R' Levi Yitzchak references this transmission. From this point a distinct Volhynian channel of support, separate from the Russian-Chabad collection, began operating openly.

title_en: Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev family unites with Alter Rebbe family
summary_en: R' Yekutiel Zusman, grandson of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, marries the Alter Rebbe's granddaughter in Sivan 5567.
story_body: In Sivan 5567 R' Yekutiel Zusman, grandson of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, married a granddaughter of the Alter Rebbe. The two rebbes had been calling each other 'mechutan' (in-law) in earlier letters in anticipation of the match. R' Levi Yitzchak had stood with the Alter Rebbe through the dispute with R' Avraham of Kalisk, both regarding chassidic doctrine and regarding fundraising for the Land of Israel.

title_en: Alter Rebbe describes separate Chabad fund for Tzfat exiles
summary_en: In a 5570 letter the Alter Rebbe describes raising and sending funds separately to the Chabad chassidim displaced from Tiberias to Tzfat.
story_body: In a 5570 letter the Alter Rebbe writes that he is sending separate support 'to revive the spirit of the lowly and crushed' Chabad community that had moved from Tiberias to Tzfat to escape harassment. Followers of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev who had also fled to Tzfat stood with the Chabad chassidim. The Alter Rebbe coordinated with R' Levi Yitzchak's trusted messenger to transmit the funds.

title_en: Passing of the Alter Rebbe of Lubavitch
summary_en: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad, passes away on 24 Tevet 5573.
story_body: On 24 Tevet 5573 the Alter Rebbe, founder of Chabad chassidut, passed away during the flight from Napoleon's invading armies. His son Rabbi Dovber Schneuri (the Mittler Rebbe) succeeded him as leader of Chabad. The Mittler Rebbe continued his father's practice of collecting and sending funds to the Chabad community in Tzfat, in coordination with R' Yisrael of Pikov, son of R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev.

title_en: R' Shimon Shmerling departs as first Chabad shadar from Hebron
summary_en: R' Shimon Shmerling of Shklov leaves Hebron in summer 5581 as the first Chabad emissary from the city.
story_body: In summer 5581 R' Shimon Shmerling, originally of Shklov, departed Hebron as the first Chabad shadar sent from the Hebron community to the diaspora. He returned to Hebron after Pesach 5583. On his journey he registered communities such as Dubna for annual donations.

title_en: Dubna community settles annual Hebron pledge with emissary
summary_en: On 12 Av 5583 the council of Dubna records settling its annual 200-zehuvim pledge to Hebron with a visiting emissary.
story_body: The Dubna kahal pinkas records that on Sunday 12 Av 5583 an emissary arrived from Hebron carrying a register of communal pledges, showing Dubna obligated to send 200 zehuvim annually. The community settled all accumulated dues, exempting future leaders from the obligation, and the emissary signed the pinkas. It is unclear whether the messenger was R' Shimon Shmerling, R' Leib of Belz, or another shadar 'connected to Hebron.'

title_en: First Chabad–Sephardic agreement in Hebron
summary_en: In 5585 the Chabad and Sephardic communities of Hebron sign their first agreement, setting Chabad's contribution at 1,000 grush per year.
story_body: The first agreement obligated the Chabad community in Hebron to pay 1,000 grush annually to the Sephardic kollel to share city expenses, including protection payments to the tyrant Sheikh Abdul Rahman who held Hebron under his patronage. Two subsequent agreements would lower this amount as Chabad argued that its own direct payments to the sheikh deserved credit.

title_en: Passing of the Mittler Rebbe
summary_en: Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, second rebbe of Chabad, passes away on 9 Kislev 5588.
story_body: On 9 Kislev 5588 the Mittler Rebbe passed away. His son-in-law and nephew Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the Tzemach Tzedek, succeeded him as leader of Chabad. The Tzemach Tzedek continued sending funds to the Chabad community in Hebron, one of the three primary support channels for the Hebron chassidim alongside the Pekidim of Amsterdam and the joint Italy emissaries.

title_en: Second Chabad–Sephardic Hebron agreement lowers payment
summary_en: A revised agreement in 5590 reduces Chabad's annual contribution to the Sephardic kollel from 1,000 to 900 grush.
story_body: Chabad argued that since they also paid Sheikh Abdul Rahman one riyal every Rosh Chodesh and additional gifts at weddings and at the arrival of emissaries, those sums should count toward shared protection payments. The 5590 agreement reduced their annual obligation to 900 grush, paid each year upon the ship's arrival to the head pakid R' Chaim HaLevi. The agreement explicitly named Sheikh Abdul Rahman as 'sar ha'ir' (ruler of the city).

title_en: Arab revolt against Egyptian deputy reaches Hebron Jews
summary_en: On 9 Iyar the Arabs of the Hebron region rebel against the Egyptian deputy ruler, putting the local Jews in mortal danger.
story_body: On Sunday 9 Iyar the Arabs of the Hebron region rebelled against the deputy of the king. For weeks they threatened the Jews of Hebron with cruel and unusual deaths. Only the intervention of certain notables saved the community from immediate harm during this initial period of unrest.

title_en: Earthquake strikes Hebron
summary_en: On 16 Iyar an earthquake collapses walls in Hebron's Jewish quarter, forcing residents to flee to open fields.
story_body: On Sunday 16 Iyar an earthquake struck Hebron, collapsing several walls in the Jewish courtyard. Residents abandoned their dwellings and fled, spending seven days and nights in the open fields in great fear. They returned to the city only when the immediate danger passed, awaiting the arrival of Ibrahim Pasha's forces — which would bring far worse violence within weeks.

title_en: Ibrahim Pasha's army sacks Hebron's Jewish community
summary_en: On 28 Tammuz the Egyptian deputy enters Hebron with his army and his soldiers loot, rape, and murder Jews.
story_body: On Monday 28 Tammuz the deputy of the king (Ibrahim Pasha) entered Hebron with his army, having defeated the Arab rebels. The soldiers were given license to destroy: Jews were killed by sword and arrow, women were raped, Torah scrolls were torn apart and trampled, tefillin batim were smashed open in search of hidden treasure, and synagogue vessels and curtains were looted. Survivors were forced to carry the plunder on their shoulders to the army camp two hours' journey from the city.

title_en: Third Chabad–Sephardic Hebron agreement at 500 grush
summary_en: A third agreement in 5602 reduces Chabad's annual payment to the Sephardic kollel to 500 grush, effective from Tishrei 5603.
story_body: By 5602 Sheikh Abdul Rahman had increased his protection demands and required separate payments from each kollel directly. The third agreement therefore reduced the Chabad contribution to general Hebron expenses from 900 to 500 grush per year, effective Tishrei 5603 onward. The text acknowledges that the Sephardim were the original Jewish settlers under whose communal umbrella the Chabad community had arrived in Hebron.

title_en: R' Tzvi Hirsh Lehrin notifies Hebron Chabad of Mindel's London oil endowment
summary_en: On 18 Elul 5592 the head of the Amsterdam Pekuam wrote to Hebron Chabad about Mrs. Mindel's 25-pound permanent fund for synagogue oil, secured through R' Asher ben Shimshon of London.
story_body: R' Tzvi Hirsh Lehrin, who headed the Pekidim and Amarkalim in Amsterdam, informed the Hebron Chabad leadership of a new fund obtained through his London trip that summer. Mrs. Mindel daughter of Yehudah of London consecrated 25 pounds as keren kayemet whose interest would purchase oil for lamps in the community's synagogue and beit midrash. The arrangement was made through R' Asher ben Shimshon, a regular benefactor of Hebron Chabad.

title_en: Dr. Eliezer HaLevi sees Asher ben Shimshon's silver menorah in Hebron
summary_en: On 15 Menachem Av 5598 Dr. Eliezer HaLevi recorded seeing a beautiful silver menorah donated by R' Asher Shimshon of London hanging before the Holy Ark in Hebron.
story_body: Writing for 'Mevaseret Tzion' (Tobolsk 1847), Dr. Eliezer HaLevi described arriving for the afternoon prayer in Hebron and being shown an elegant silver menorah hanging before the holy ark. The inscription identified its donor as R' Asher Shimshon of London, described as a long-standing benefactor of Eretz Israel residents.

title_en: R' Asher ben Shimshon of London donates 1000 grush for Hebron mikveh
summary_en: In 5607 R' Asher ben Shimshon of London donated 1000 grush via the Pekuam toward constructing a mikveh for Hebron's Chabad community after years of discussion.
story_body: After lengthy debate about building a ritual bath in Hebron, the wealthy London philanthropist R' Asher ben Shimshon donated 1000 grush through the Amsterdam Pekidim and Amarkalim in 5607. Difficulties securing a suitable site led local administrators to request the funds be redirected, which the Pekuam refused without the donor's explicit consent.

title_en: Pekuam refuses to redirect Hebron mikveh donation without donor consent
summary_en: On 15 Elul 5607 the Amsterdam Pekuam wrote Hebron Chabad refusing to reassign R' Asher ben Shimshon's 1000-grush mikveh donation to other charities without his approval.
story_body: Heads of the Pekidim and Amarkalim responded to Hebron Chabad's request to redirect the stalled mikveh donation toward a free-loan fund or bikur cholim. R' Asher had insisted any unused sum be returned to him to capitalize a different kollel, with interest funding synagogue lamp oil. The Pekuam declined to act without his decision.

title_en: Hebron Chabad locates Cave of Othniel for mikveh site
summary_en: On 8 Nisan 5608 the Pekuam celebrated word from Hebron Chabad that a suitable mikveh location—identified as the Cave of Othniel ben Kenaz—had been recovered from non-Jews.
story_body: After receiving reports from Hebron Chabad dated 2 Kislev and 9 Iyar that a suitable mikveh site had been found, the Pekuam relayed the news to R' Asher ben Shimshon in London. He responded with an additional 550 grush to cover the increased cost. The Pekuam praised the recovery of the Cave of Othniel ben Kenaz from strangers but declined to solicit further donations due to widespread economic distress among former donors.

title_en: Hebron Chabad letter to the Tzemach Tzedek
summary_en: In 5591 Hebron's Chabad leaders wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek acknowledging support funds, with R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin signing last as the youngest at 29.
story_body: The letter from Hebron Chabad leaders confirmed receipt of support funds sent by the third Lubavitcher Rebbe. R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, who would later become Hebron's Chabad rav, signed last as the youngest of the signers and identified himself as 'son of R' Moshe shochet,' showing his trade was shechita while he was also active in community affairs.

title_en: R' Leib Baal HaYisurim of Hebron dies in Tzfat
summary_en: R' Leib of Hebron, known as the 'baal hayisurim' (man of sufferings), passed away in Tzfat on 15 Cheshvan 5597.
story_body: R' Leib, one of the founders of the Chabad settlement in Hebron alongside R' Shimon Shmerling, moved to Tzfat late in life and died there as an old man. According to 'Shaarei Yerushalayim,' he instructed before death that anyone in distress should prostrate on his grave for aid, a practice that continued for generations. His tombstone identifies him as 'R' Leib of Hebron, baal hayisurim, died 15 Cheshvan 5597.'

title_en: Abd al-Rahman escapes Jerusalem prison and resumes ruling Hebron
summary_en: In early 1852 Hebron's persecutor Abd al-Rahman was briefly chained in Jerusalem's seraglio, then escaped over the city wall and reinstalled himself as mutasallim, immediately fining the Jewish community.
story_body: Captured by the Ottoman government, Abd al-Rahman was held briefly in chains in Jerusalem's seraglio before being permitted to walk freely with three guarantors. He escaped one night carrying his chains, jumping from the city wall, and reinstalled himself as mutasallim of Hebron. He immediately began imposing heavy fines on the population, especially the Jews.

title_en: Consul James Finn intervenes during Hebron extortion crisis
summary_en: On 9 August 1852 British Consul James Finn received reports of severe disturbances in Hebron and traveled there to restrain Abd al-Rahman's outrages against the Jews.
story_body: Reports reached the British consulate that Abd al-Rahman intended to extort 40 purses (about 200 pounds) from Hebron's Jewish quarter that very morning. Finn traveled to Hebron where the European hospital doctor confirmed the news. Finn described the Jews' terror—pale faces and darting eyes, hanging on every word and movement. His presence temporarily restrained the persecutor, though the depredations resumed after Finn left.

title_en: Consul Finn halts Salama's persecution of Hebron Jews
summary_en: On 8 February 1854 Consul James Finn ended the harassment that Salama, brother of Abd al-Rahman, was inflicting on Hebron's Jewish community.
story_body: James Finn recorded in his diary: 'In Hebron I succeeded in ending the harassment which Salama, brother of Abd al-Rahman Amr, was inflicting on the Jews.' His interventions in Hebron during 1853-1856 were later documented in his book 'Stirring Times, or Records from Jerusalem Consular Chronicles' (London 1878), an important record of the persecutions endured by Hebron's Jewish community.

title_en: Abd al-Rahman taken in chains to Constantinople and sentenced to death
summary_en: In 5618 the Hebron persecutor Abd al-Rahman was finally captured by the government and taken in iron chains to Constantinople, where he was sentenced to death.
story_body: After years of tormenting Hebron's Jewish community, Abd al-Rahman was finally seized in 5618. R' Moshe Risher recorded in 'Tevuot HaAretz' (5626/1866) that 'God in His mercy, eight years ago, seized him and took him to Constantinople in iron chains and there gave him the sentence of death.' The community treated his demise as deliverance from a sustained persecution.

title_en: Hungarian Hoizman brothers settle in Hebron from Liska
summary_en: In 5625 R' Alexander Zisha Hoizman emigrated with his family from Liska via Trieste to Hebron, where he joined his brother R' Aryeh Leib, beginning the Hungarian community there.
story_body: R' Alexander Zisha Hoizman, born in Hungary in 5578, emigrated in 5625 with his wife Bat-Sheva and three children—Shimon, Menachem Manes, and Tzvi Hersh—via Trieste, where he met his brother R' Aryeh Leib also bound for Eretz Israel. The two Karlin Chassidim families initially worshipped with the Chabad community but eventually founded 'Kahal Ungarit' with its own synagogue as their families grew and intermarried with other non-Chabad families.

title_en: R' Meir Tzvi Hershler immigrates from Hungary to Eretz Israel
summary_en: R' Meir Tzvi Hershler, born 5615, immigrated from Hungary in 5625 and later married Sarah Mendelsohn of Hebron, settling there between 5630-5634.
story_body: R' Meir Tzvi Hershler arrived from Hungary in 5625 at age 10 and later married Sarah, daughter of R' Yonatan Zeev Wolf Mendelsohn of Hebron. He settled permanently in Hebron between 5630-5634. Decades later he would represent the non-Chabad communities during the 5647 din torah between the kollels and serve as their representative on Hebron's Vaad HaKlali.

title_en: Sephardic Chief Rabbi appeals to Tzemach Tzedek's sons for kollel support
summary_en: On 25 Shevat 5627 Rishon LeTzion R' Chaim David Chazan wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek's sons urging them to continue their late father's support of the Hebron and Jerusalem Chabad kollels.
story_body: Following the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, Hebron and Jerusalem Chabad communities feared the loss of their crucial support. Sephardic Chief Rabbi Chaim David Chazan dispatched R' Yehuda Leib Slonim to Lubavitch with his letter urging the rebbe's sons to assume their father's role. He warned that without their oversight Chabad communities would become 'like sheep without a shepherd' and praised how splendid the kollelot had been until then.

title_en: Hebron Chabad beit din bans modern schools
summary_en: In 5633 R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin and his Hebron beit din signed a ruling forbidding the new modern schools, following the 5631 Jerusalem rabbis' ruling.
story_body: Following the 5631 ruling by Jerusalem's rabbis against the new haskalah-influenced modern schools, the Hebron Chabad rav R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin signed a parallel prohibition with his beit din of R' Chaim Yaakov and R' Shaul. Hungarian Chassidim of Hebron including R' Alexander Zushe Hoizman, his son R' Shimon, and R' Aryeh Leib also added their signatures. The ban appears in 'Maaseh Avot' (Jerusalem 1901).

title_en: Binyamin Aba grandson of R' Leib of Belz dies
summary_en: Binyamin Aba ben R' Meir, identified in 'Avnei Zikaron' as grandson of the holy R' Leib of Belz, passed away on 21 Adar 5639.
story_body: The record in 'Avnei Zikaron' chapter 12 of Binyamin Aba's death on 21 Adar 5639 has been cited in the scholarly discussion attempting to identify R' Leib of Belz with R' Leib Baal HaYisurim of Hebron, though the connection remains unproven.

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim makes his last trip to Lubavitch
summary_en: In 5645 R' Yehuda Leib Slonim of Hebron made his final journey to Lubavitch in his capacity as administrator of Kollel Chabad.
story_body: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, who along with his brothers managed Kollel Chabad after R' Shimon Menashe took on rabbinic duties, made numerous trips to Lubavitch to coordinate the kollel's affairs over decades. His last trip in 5645 is documented in a letter from Rebbe Rashab (vol. 1, letter 4). He died eight years later in 5653.

title_en: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Hebron Chabad rav, dies at age 92
summary_en: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, who served as head of Hebron's Chabad community for approximately fifty years, died on 29 Sivan 5653 at age 92.
story_body: Born in Shklov around 5562, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin emigrated to Eretz Israel at age 18 in 5580 and moved from Tzfat to Hebron at the Mitteler Rebbe's directive. He served as Av Beit Din of Hebron's Chabad community for some fifty years. Hachavatzelet reported that 'all Hebron's inhabitants, Sephardic and Ashkenazi, streamed in reverence behind his bier and aroused bitter mourning over him.'

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, Kollel Chabad administrator, dies
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, principal administrator of Kollel Chabad in Hebron, passed away on 27 Tammuz 5653—just weeks after R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin.
story_body: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, who together with his brothers R' Levi Yitzchak and R' Mordechai Dovber managed Kollel Chabad's affairs in Hebron, traveled repeatedly to Lubavitch to coordinate funds and policy with successive rebbes. His passing on 27 Tammuz 5653, weeks after Hebron's chief rav, marked the end of an era for the community.

title_en: Hebron Yeshiva Magen Avot renewed
summary_en: With the renewal of Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron in 5663, the idea immediately arose to affiliate it with Tomchei Tmimim of Lubavitch.
story_body: Upon the renewal of yeshiva Magen Avot in Hebron in 5663, R' Yaakov Yosef Slonim of Hebron raised with the future Rebbe Rayatz the possibility of affiliating it with the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva network. The Rayatz, then practical director of Tomchei Tmimim, initially deferred the idea due to upheavals in Russia, though the affiliation was implemented several years later.

title_en: Future Rebbe Rayatz defers Hebron yeshiva affiliation due to Russian unrest
summary_en: On 5 Adar II 5665 the future Rebbe Rayatz wrote R' Yaakov Yosef Slonim of Hebron that adding another branch to Tomchei Tmimim was difficult given internal Russian upheavals.
story_body: In response to a Hebron request to add Magen Avot as a branch of Tomchei Tmimim, the Rayatz explained that the present year's 'great storms in our country, from within and from without'—a reference to the 1905 Russian Revolution upheavals—made expansion impossible. He expressed hope that with God's help fruitful approaches would emerge.

title_en: R' Moshe Mordechai Chaikin visits Hebron for father-in-law's yahrzeit
summary_en: On 27 Sivan 5665 Moshe Mordechai Chaikin wrote from Hebron noting his annual arrival with his mother for R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin's yahrzeit.
story_body: R' Moshe Mordechai Chaikin, stepson and son-in-law of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, came each year from Jerusalem with his mother Devorah for the yahrzeit. His 27 Sivan 5665 letter to ShILA from Hebron mentioned the upcoming yahrzeit on the eve of 1 Tammuz. Moshe Mordechai later published R' Akiva Yosef Schlesinger's 'Brit Olam' with his own annotations in Jerusalem 5662-5663.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim funds Magen Avot students in Hebron
summary_en: On the eve of 1 Adar 5671 R' Shneur Zalman Landau of Lubavitch sent 200 rubles and a stipend list for Magen Avot students, formalizing the yeshiva's affiliation with Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: The accompanying receipt template had each student in Hebron acknowledge that his stipend came 'from the association Tomchei Tmimim of Lubavitch, under the leadership of the Rebbe.' Each student signed individually. The disbursements covered Tammuz and Menachem Av 5670, marking a concrete step in establishing Lubavitch's institutional presence in the Land of Israel before the founding of Torat Emet.

title_en: Yeshivat Torat Emet founded in Hebron
summary_en: At the beginning of 5672 the Chabad Yeshivat Torat Emet was founded in Hebron after extended preparations.
story_body: Following years of efforts to build a Chabad yeshiva presence in Eretz Israel—including the affiliation of Magen Avot with Tomchei Tmimim—Yeshivat Torat Emet was founded in Hebron at the beginning of 5672. The yeshiva would become a major center for Chabad learning in the Land of Israel and was supervised by Rebbe Rashab from Lubavitch.

title_en: Mrs. Devorah Chaikin, widow of Hebron Chabad rav, dies
summary_en: Mrs. Devorah, second wife of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin and granddaughter of R' Wolf of Tcharnostre, passed away on 13 Kislev 5674.
story_body: Mrs. Devorah—a widow with son Moshe Mordechai whom R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin married after his first wife Zissel died between 5626-5635—passed away on 13 Kislev 5674. Through her first marriage her son Moshe Mordechai was a descendant of R' Wolf of Tcharnostre buried in Tiberias, and later became son-in-law of R' Akiva Yosef Schlesinger.

title_en: Mrs. Rashka Rivlin, granddaughter of Hebron's Chabad rav, dies at 92
summary_en: Mrs. Rashka Rivlin, granddaughter of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin of Hebron, died in Jerusalem in Tevet 5695 at age 92.
story_body: Rashka Rivlin, wife of R' David Tzvi Rivlin, was according to the introduction of 'Ohalei Yosef' on the Talmud (Jerusalem 1956) and a letter from M.S. Slonim, the granddaughter—not daughter—of Hebron's chief rabbi R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin. Born in 5603, she lived to 92 and died in Tevet 5695 in Jerusalem.

title_en: R. Shneur Zalman of Lublin, author of Toras Chesed, passes away
summary_en: The renowned posek R. Shneur Zalman of Lublin, author of Toras Chesed, died on 5 Nisan 5662 in Jerusalem.
story_body: R. Shneur Zalman of Lublin lived in a house in Jerusalem purchased for him by R. Yeshaya Berlin and dedicated to Kollel Chabad. His passing on the night of 5 Nisan 5662 prompted the Jerusalem trustees to propose using his house as a new Chabad yeshiva. This proposal was the catalyst for the multi-year discussion that culminated in establishing Chabad yeshivas in Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga of Bobruisk receives haskamah on Likutei Torah
summary_en: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga, Av Beis Din of Bobruisk, signed his approbation on the Likutei Torah on 17 Sivan 5608.
story_body: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga served as rabbi of Bobruisk for some fifty years before making aliyah. His haskamah on Likutei Torah, dated 17 Sivan 5608, marks the last time he is documented outside of Eretz Yisrael. Shortly thereafter he prepared for his long-anticipated move to Jerusalem.

title_en: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga makes aliyah to Jerusalem
summary_en: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga, after fifty years as rabbi of Bobruisk, fulfilled his lifelong dream and settled in Jerusalem in 5611.
story_body: Already in 5574-5 R. Baruch Mordechai had asked the Mitteler Rebbe about settling in Eretz Yisrael. Although he was instructed to remain in Bobruisk and continued there for another 35 years, in 5611 he finally made the move. By then the Chabad community in Jerusalem had grown, and he chose to settle there rather than in Hebron or Tzefas.

title_en: R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga passes away in Jerusalem
summary_en: After roughly a year in the Holy City, R. Baruch Mordechai Ettinga died in Jerusalem on 14 Elul 5612.
story_body: R. Baruch Mordechai had only enjoyed his long-awaited residence in Jerusalem for about a year before his passing. Letters from the Pekuamim sent in advance of Rosh Hashanah 5613 still presumed him living, and the funds dispatched arrived after his death. His matzevah, copied in Yerushalayim vol. 1, mistakenly led some later researchers to place his death in 5617.

title_en: Sasson donation enables acquisition of the Beis Menachem synagogue
summary_en: The Chabad community in Jerusalem secured the Beis Menachem synagogue courtyard via a mortgage funded by David Sassoon's 100-pound-sterling donation, commemorated on 20 Sivan 5618.
story_body: Lacking a synagogue, the Chabad community in Jerusalem received 100 lira sterling from David Sassoon of India as a key-money donation to take the courtyard under a four-year mortgage. The courtyard contained a synagogue, women's section, mikveh, and other facilities. A commemorative inscription was installed on 20 Sivan 5618 honoring Sassoon's generosity.

title_en: Chabad community purchases Beis Menachem synagogue outright
summary_en: With additional donations and a 250-Napoleon loan, the Chabad community of Jerusalem acquired the Beis Menachem synagogue courtyard permanently in 5622.
story_body: After four years on a mortgage backed by Sassoon's donation, the community faced losing the property when the seller wanted his money back. A donor from Kherson contributed 150 lira sterling, additional gifts came in, and they took a permissible-interest loan to reach the full 600 lira sterling purchase price. The acquisition secured the synagogue for the Jerusalem Chabad community permanently.

title_en: Rashab decides to send Tomchei Temimim students to expand Hebron yeshiva
summary_en: On the night of 25 Iyar 5671, after a three-hour meeting with Tomchei Temimim leadership, the Rashab resolved to send select students and a mashpia to strengthen the Magen Avos yeshiva in Hebron.
story_body: After more than a year of discussion, the Rashab convened the directors of Tomchei Temimim on 25 Iyar 5671 for over three hours to plan support for Hebron. He decided to dispatch outstanding avreichim, including a mashpia in Chassidus, to establish the Magen Avos yeshiva on a sound footing and to make it an open branch of Tomchei Temimim. The decision was reported in letters Shilo sent to Hebron on 9-10 Sivan.

title_en: Hebron yeshiva officially renamed 'Toras Emes'
summary_en: In a letter to mashpia R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin dated Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5672, the Rebbe Rayatz formally designated the new Hebron yeshiva 'Toras Emes'.
story_body: Following the Rashab's decision to send a contingent of avreichim to Hebron, the mashpia R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin and his group arrived in the city. The Rebbe Rayatz then wrote to him on Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5672 instructing that the yeshiva be called 'Toras Emes'. This name change reflected not only renaming but a reorganization absorbing the existing Magen Avos yeshiva.

title_en: Magen Avos yeshiva absorbed into Toras Emes
summary_en: By Lag B'Omer 5672, Shilo instructed that funds sent from Russia for Magen Avos belonged to Toras Emes, confirming the older yeshiva's full absorption.
story_body: In a Lag B'Omer letter to his brother-in-law R. Menachem Mendel Nae, Shilo specified that the 40 ruble donation from Meir Vozlinski for Magen Avos in fact belonged to Toras Emes. He further warned not to hand over funds from Russia to the Magen Avos gabbaim without his knowledge. This documents how Magen Avos was administratively folded into the newly established Toras Emes.

title_en: Toras Emes opens branch in Jerusalem
summary_en: Following the founding of Toras Emes in Hebron in 5672, a branch of the yeshiva opened in Jerusalem with the gaon R. Tzvi Pesach Frank as rosh yeshiva.
story_body: After Toras Emes was established in Hebron, a Jerusalem branch was opened the same year. R. Tzvi Pesach Frank served as the rosh yeshiva of the Jerusalem branch. Only fragmentary information about this branch has reached us.

title_en: Toras Emes reopened in Jerusalem after WWI
summary_en: After the First World War's disruption, Yeshivas Toras Emes was reopened in 5682, this time based in Jerusalem rather than Hebron.
story_body: The First World War interrupted operations of the Toras Emes yeshiva in Eretz Yisrael. In 5682, after the war ended, the yeshiva was reestablished, now centered in Jerusalem rather than Hebron. This re-founding is documented in detail in the following chapter of the source.

title_en: Rashab's letter on the decline of Chassidus study in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In an epistle dated 14 Elul 5663, the Rashab lamented the collapse of Chassidus study among Chabad avreichim in Eretz Yisrael and welcomed the new initiative to open Chabad yeshivas in Jerusalem and Hebron.
story_body: The Rashab described how Chassidus study in Eretz Yisrael had reached its lowest ebb, with young Chabad avreichim studying in Perushim yeshivas instead. He expressed deep distress at the situation but rejoiced that a spirit of purification had stirred his followers there to establish Chabad yeshivas in Jerusalem and Hebron. This letter contextualizes the simultaneous push to found dedicated Chabad institutions in the Holy Land.

title_en: Chabad settlement in Tzfat renewed
summary_en: Around 5630, the Chabad community in Tzfat was reestablished by R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe and his son-in-law R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz.
story_body: R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe, son of one of the Hebron Kollel Chabad administrators, relocated from Hebron to Tzfat to live near his father-in-law R' David Yehuda Leib. Around the same time, the widow Mrs. Bila, niece of the Tzemach Tzedek, immigrated to Tzfat with her five orphaned sons. The two families merged through marriage and became the nucleus of the renewed Chabad community in Tzfat.

title_en: Mrs. Bila immigrates to Tzfat with orphaned sons
summary_en: Mrs. Bila, niece of the Tzemach Tzedek, immigrated to Tzfat with her five orphaned sons around 5630.
story_body: After her husband R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz of Beshenkovichi died in 5624, Bila returned to her uncle the Tzemach Tzedek's home with her five young orphans. The Tzemach Tzedek corresponded with R' Aharon of Karlin and R' Aharon of Chernobyl, and together they agreed to support her settlement in the Holy Land. She then made aliyah to Tzfat with her sons, joining the renewed Chabad community there.

title_en: Death of R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz of Beshenkovichi
summary_en: R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz, a leading chasid of the Tzemach Tzedek in Beshenkovichi, died in 5624.
story_body: R' Yeshaya was a prominent chasid of the Tzemach Tzedek and the husband of Bila, niece of the Rebbe. His death left her widowed with five young orphans, leading to her eventual aliyah to Tzfat with her sons. The family became foundational to the renewed Chabad community in Tzfat.

title_en: R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe dies of plague in Tzfat
summary_en: R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe, a founder of the renewed Chabad community in Tzfat, died of plague on 27 Tishrei 5636.
story_body: After several years supporting his son-in-law R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz at his table, R' Yisrael Dover Yaffe died from the plague. His death left R' Asher Yechezkel as head of the family and the emerging Chabad community in Tzfat, a leadership role he would hold for decades.

title_en: Mrs. Bila Horowitz dies in Tzfat
summary_en: Mrs. Bila Horowitz, niece of the Tzemach Tzedek and matriarch of the Tzfat Chabad community, died on 4 Tammuz 5647.
story_body: Bila had immigrated to Tzfat around 1870 with her five orphaned sons, becoming a foundational figure in the renewed Chabad community there. Her descendants, listed as 'sons of Bila' in the Kollel Chabad distribution records, remained prominent in the Tzfat community after her death.

title_en: Kollel Chabad funds Tzfat Beit Midrash
summary_en: In 5633, Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem allocated funds for the Tzfat Beit Midrash as the community there began to develop again.
story_body: The Chabad Beit Midrash in Tzfat dated back to the pre-5583 Chabad settlement there. As the community redeveloped in 5633, Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem began allocating funds for its upkeep, recognizing the resurgent presence of Chabad in the holy city.

title_en: Birth of R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz of Tzfat
summary_en: R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz, future rabbi of the Chabad community in Tzfat, was born in 5643.
story_body: Son of R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz, he was named for his paternal grandfather. He would later serve as rabbi of the Chabad community in Tzfat from 5669 to 5684, before relocating to the United States.

title_en: R' Leib Menuchin letter on Tzfat yeshiva proposal
summary_en: On 15 Sivan 5664, R' Leib Menuchin wrote to Kollel Chabad administrators abroad opposing R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz's plan to open a yeshiva in Tzfat.
story_body: R' Asher Yechezkel hoped to open a Chabad yeshiva in Tzfat headed by his son R' Yeshaya. R' Leib Menuchin advised the kollel's overseas administrators that the kollel's funds should not be used for this venture. The yeshiva ultimately did not come to fruition.

title_en: Kollel reports damage to Tzfat Chabad Beit Midrash
summary_en: On 25 Elul 5668, Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem wrote that the Tzfat Beit Midrash had cracked and required government-mandated repairs costing twenty napoleons.
story_body: The Tzfat Chabad community appealed for help after government-ordered repairs to their damaged Beit Midrash cost twenty napoleons. Kollel Chabad arranged for Jerusalem and Hebron to cover ten napoleons and forwarded the additional request to overseas administrators, illustrating the poverty of the small community.

title_en: R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz dies in Tzfat
summary_en: R' Asher Yechezkel Horowitz, head of the Tzfat Chabad community and kollel administrator, died on 24 Elul 5680.
story_body: R' Asher Yechezkel had led the renewed Tzfat Chabad community for decades and managed the Kollel Chabad distribution in Tzfat. After his death, his son R' Yeshaya succeeded him in administering the kollel's affairs in the city.

title_en: R' Yeshaya Horowitz leaves Tzfat for America
summary_en: Around mid-winter 5684, R' Yeshaya Halevi Horowitz left his post as rabbi of Chabad in Tzfat and emigrated to the United States.
story_body: After serving as rabbi of the Chabad community in Tzfat since 5669 and managing the kollel's distribution there after his father's death, R' Yeshaya departed for America. From this point his name no longer appeared in the Tzfat distribution lists of Kollel Chabad.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim appointed rabbi in Yafo
summary_en: In 5660, the Lublin Gaon (Toras Chesed) ordered R' Shneur Zalman Slonim to leave his Hebron affairs and accept the Chabad rabbinate in Yafo.
story_body: R' Shneur Zalman submitted to the Lublin Gaon's directive and moved to Yafo to serve the Chabad community. His first task was building a kosher mikveh for women in Neve Shalom, since the existing one was in dangerous and remote old Yafo. He also organized shechita, built a Chabad synagogue, and gave weekly chassidus discourses.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim arrives in Yafo
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim arrived in Yafo on Wednesday, 13 Kislev 5660, to assume the Chabad rabbinate there.
story_body: His arrival was reported in the HaTzvi newspaper on 15 Kislev, noting that the new rabbi had been brought from Hebron at the request of chasidim and prominent householders. A reception followed on Shabbat with representatives of Bnei Brit, Achva, and Bnei Yisrael societies, lasting through the night.
