title_en: Public letter confirms Slonim's Yafo appointment
summary_en: On 23 Adar I 5660, R' Yitzchak Shmerling published an open letter in HaTzvi affirming that the Lublin Gaon had personally appointed R' Shneur Zalman Slonim to Yafo.
story_body: Some had questioned whether the Lublin Gaon had truly directed Slonim's move to Yafo. R' Yitzchak Shmerling responded with an open letter to HaTzvi, stating that he had spoken with the Gaon directly and heard from him that he had chosen R' Shneur Zalman to take the Yafo rabbinate.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab encourages Slonim's Yafo rabbinate
summary_en: On 3 Menachem Av 5660, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim to encourage his son in his new Yafo rabbinate.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab acknowledged that the family had endured distress over the Yafo arrangement but explained that since the Lublin Gaon had directed it, they should trust in Hashem. He expressed confidence that R' Shneur Zalman would succeed in his new post.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab declines to move Slonim from Yafo
summary_en: On 22 Iyar 5663, the Rebbe Rashab wrote that R' Shneur Zalman Slonim could not be moved from Yafo to lead a new Jerusalem yeshiva.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab had wanted to appoint R' Shneur Zalman to oversee a new Chabad yeshiva in Jerusalem, but worried that leaving Yafo after three years of intense work there would unravel everything he had built. He concluded that pulling him out would undo the essential reforms he had instituted.

title_en: Rashab general letter on Jerusalem yeshiva leadership
summary_en: On 14 Elul 5663, the Rebbe Rashab issued a general letter announcing that R' Shneur Zalman Slonim would supervise the Jerusalem yeshiva's studies.
story_body: After deliberating throughout the summer, the Rebbe Rashab decided to prioritize the Jerusalem yeshiva over the Yafo rabbinate. In his general letter to chasidim, he announced that R' Shneur Zalman would oversee both the nigleh and chassidus learning. For unknown reasons, however, the plan never came to fruition.

title_en: Slonim writes Shiloh on remaining in Yafo
summary_en: On 2 Adar 5664, R' Shneur Zalman Slonim wrote to R' Shiloh that he had concluded he must remain in Yafo despite earlier plans to move to Jerusalem.
story_body: R' Shneur Zalman had initially expected to relocate to Jerusalem per the Rebbe's decision, but was told not to move without explicit instruction from the Rebbe himself. He recounted the hardships of his arrival in Yafo, observed that the community now had a clear path forward, and accepted that his lot was to remain in Yafo.

title_en: Slonim notes lack of confirmation on Jerusalem move
summary_en: On 18 Iyar 5664, R' Shneur Zalman Slonim wrote again to R' Shiloh that he had still received no clarifying word about relocating to Jerusalem.
story_body: Although he had been told the Rebbe Rashab had decided he should settle in Jerusalem, he was also instructed not to move until receiving definitive word. By 18 Iyar 5664 no such word had come, confirming that he would remain in Yafo as rabbi.

title_en: Rashab tells Slonim not to leave Yafo for Hebron
summary_en: On 22 Elul 5672, after Toras Emes opened in Hebron, the Rebbe Rashab told R' Shneur Zalman Slonim not to abandon Yafo for his hometown.
story_body: Following the founding of Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron, R' Shneur Zalman wished to lay down his Yafo burdens and return to Hebron. The Rebbe Rashab replied that he could not abandon Yafo after all the effort and toil he had invested to bring the community to its current state.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim dies in Yafo
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman Slonim died on 11 Tammuz 5696 after serving as rabbi in Yafo-Tel Aviv for 37 years.
story_body: He had built the Chabad community in Yafo from the ground up: founding the women's mikveh, organizing shechita, building a Chabad shul in Neve Shalom, delivering weekly chassidus, and serving on the Tel Aviv Chief Rabbinate until his death. His 37-year tenure shaped Chabad presence in the city.

title_en: Kollel Chabad in Hebron formally established with first leadership
summary_en: In 5587, Kollel Chabad in Hebron took its definitive form with three named overseers: R' Tzvi Hirsh Lifshitz, R' Ephraim Yaffe, and R' Moshe Meizlish.
story_body: These three men signed as appointees on the shadarut documents of 5587, the founding year of Kollel Chabad as a formal entity. Alongside them, R' Leib Chitrik of Sena was appointed ne'eman (treasurer/bookkeeper). They styled themselves the 'appointees of the community of Ashkenazim called Chabad in Hebron.'

title_en: Hebron Chabad-Sephardic agreement signed
summary_en: In 5590 an agreement was signed between the Chabad community and the Sephardic community in Hebron.
story_body: Among the Chabad signatories were R' Moshe Meizlish, joined by R' Shmuel Segal, R' Yehuda Leib Sener, and others — without R' Tzvi Hirsh Lifshitz or R' Ephraim Yaffe of the original 5587 trio. The agreement allocated a quarter of all Chabad collections in Sephardic regions to the Hebron Sephardic community.

title_en: R' Ephraim Yaffe returns to Hebron Kollel leadership
summary_en: In 5603, R' Ephraim Yaffe rejoined the Hebron kollel leadership after a 13-year absence from the signature list.
story_body: From 5590 to 5602 he had not signed kollel documents, but starting in 5603 his name appeared again among the first signatories. He served alongside R' Shmuel Segal and R' Yehuda Leib of Sena until 5606.

title_en: R' Moshe Shmerling joins Hebron Kollel leadership
summary_en: On 5 Menachem Av 5606, R' Yehuda Leib Sener stepped down from the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Moshe Shmerling replaced him.
story_body: R' Yehuda Leib appears to have retired due to old age — his successor R' Moshe Shmerling, son of Shimon, joined R' Shmuel Segal and R' Ephraim Yaffe on the kollel board. R' Yehuda Leib lived past 5609.

title_en: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin joins Hebron Kollel
summary_en: On 6 Elul 5606, R' Ephraim Yaffe retired from the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin was added in his place.
story_body: R' Ephraim Yaffe apparently retired due to old age and died between 5606 and 5609. His successor, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, would go on to become the central figure in Hebron Chabad leadership for nearly half a century.

title_en: R' Shlomo Zalman Kovelkin joins Hebron Kollel signatories
summary_en: On 22 Iyar 5608, the Hebron Pekuam administrators directed the two remaining overseers to choose a third co-signer.
story_body: By summer 5608, R' Shlomo Zalman ben Shmuel Sender Kovelkin was named alongside the two remaining overseers. Born in Polotsk in 5548, he was a regular signatory but not formally counted among the appointees in the 5609 census.

title_en: Hebron Kollel leadership recorded in 5609 census
summary_en: The 5609 Montefiore census formally listed the leadership of Hebron's Chabad community: Shmuel Segal, Avigdor, Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Avraham Dovber Chitrik, and Nachum Aryeh Halevi.
story_body: These five men were registered as 'sages, rabbis, leaders, appointees and overseers' of the Hebron Chabad community. The same individuals signed the power-of-attorney document to Montefiore that year. R' Yosef Yehuda Leib Shmerling was listed separately as 'engaged in kollel matters.'

title_en: R' Shmuel Segal dies, leadership reshuffled
summary_en: In the summer of 5610, R' Shmuel Segal's name was dropped from the Hebron kollel leadership, around the time of his death.
story_body: His passing left R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Avigdor, and R' Uri Volabriker on the kollel board. The reshuffling marked another step in R' Shimon Menashe's gradual rise to becoming the dominant figure in Hebron Chabad affairs.

title_en: R' Menachem Aryeh Segal replaces R' Avigdor in kollel
summary_en: In mid-winter 5611, R' Avigdor stepped down from the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Menachem Aryeh ben Shmuel Segal took his place.
story_body: The administrators reported that R' Avigdor had withdrawn due to old age and wished him renewed vigor. They welcomed his replacement R' Menachem Aryeh — son of the late R' Shmuel Segal — citing 'the threefold cord that is not quickly broken.'

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Epstein joins Hebron Kollel
summary_en: In the summer of 5613, R' Uri left the Hebron kollel leadership and R' Shneur Zalman ben Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein was named in his place.
story_body: Curiously, R' Shneur Zalman Epstein was registered as a Jerusalem resident in all the censuses, suggesting that the senior Jerusalem leader was also listed among the Hebron appointees because Hebron was then the seat of the central Kollel Chabad council.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn added to Hebron Kollel
summary_en: In 5615, R' Shneur Zalman ben Menachem Yosef Schneersohn — known by the initials SHZBNY — was added to the Hebron kollel leadership.
story_body: Like R' Shneur Zalman Epstein before him, SHZBNY was registered as a Jerusalem resident in the censuses. His inclusion among the Hebron overseers reinforces the pattern that senior Jerusalem leaders were named to the central Hebron council during this period.

title_en: Pekuam letter names new Hebron Kollel leadership
summary_en: On 26 Tishrei 5626, the Pekuam administrators addressed a letter to R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Shneur Zalman, and R' Dov Ber ben Naftali Hirsch as heads of the Hebron Chabad community.
story_body: This is the latest surviving Pekuam letter to the Hebron leadership. The three named men headed the community administration; R' Dov Ber ben Naftali Hirsch may have been R' Dover of Lobki, registered in the 5626 census as a member of R' Shimon Menashe's beit din.

title_en: Hebron Chabad-Sephardic agreement of 5628
summary_en: In 5628, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, and R' Shneur Zalman Pundaminski signed an agreement on behalf of Kollel Chabad in Hebron.
story_body: This marked the formal entry of R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim into kollel leadership. He would soon dominate Hebron Chabad affairs, with later agreements stating that 'no significant matter could be concluded without R' Levi Yitzchak as long as he was the chosen representative of Chabad.'

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Slonim joins Hebron Kollel leadership
summary_en: In 5632, R' Yehuda Leib Slonim was added to the Hebron Chabad leadership team.
story_body: He joined the existing trio of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, and R' Shneur Zalman Pundaminski. The four men together appeared as overseers in the 5635 census, alongside R' Yeshaya Ornstein, who served as the kollel's scribe while living in Jerusalem.

title_en: R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin dies
summary_en: In 5653, R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin — rabbi and chief overseer of Hebron Chabad — died, along with R' Yehuda Leib Slonim.
story_body: R' Shimon Menashe had served continuously in Hebron Chabad leadership since 5607, becoming the principal overseer in his later years while remaining 'honorary president' due to extreme old age. Active leadership had long since shifted to R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, but his death ended an era.

title_en: R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim dies
summary_en: R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, the dominant figure in Hebron Chabad administration, died in 5655.
story_body: He had managed all affairs of Kollel Chabad in Hebron and was considered the de facto head of the community. According to family history, 'nothing was done in Hebron without him during all his days.' His death cleared the way for new leadership under R' Dovber Efrat.

title_en: R' Shaul Ashkenazi dies in Jerusalem
summary_en: R' Shaul ben Yaakov Mordechai Chevroni (Brimt/Shaulzon) died on Erev Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5656 in Jerusalem.
story_body: Born in 5583 in Mohilev, R' Shaul made aliyah with his family in 5592. He taught Tanach and Gemara in Jerusalem according to the 5615 census, returned to Hebron in 5626 to join the kollel leadership, served on R' Shimon Menashe's beit din, and eventually returned to Jerusalem where he is buried. His descendants adopted the surname Shaulzon.

title_en: R' Dovber Efrat takes over Hebron Chabad leadership
summary_en: Around 5655, R' Dovber Efrat arrived in Hebron, became rabbi of the Chabad community, and took over kollel administration.
story_body: Following the deaths of R' Shimon Menashe Chaikin, R' Yehuda Leib Slonim, and R' Levi Yitzchak Slonim, R' Dovber Efrat was appointed rabbi of Hebron Chabad and took over the kollel administration. He was joined by R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R' Binyamin Rivlin in leading the community.

title_en: R' Dovber Efrat moves to Jerusalem; R' Shiloh takes Hebron
summary_en: In late 5662, R' Dovber Efrat moved to Jerusalem and R' Shiloh assumed the Hebron rabbinate and kollel administration.
story_body: R' Dovber Efrat relocated to Jerusalem at the end of 5662. R' Shiloh succeeded him in both the rabbinate and kollel leadership in Hebron, working alongside R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R' Binyamin Rivlin until World War I.

title_en: Hebron Chabad settlement disrupted by World War I
summary_en: In 5674 the First World War broke out and the Chabad settlement in Hebron ceased functioning.
story_body: The Hebron Chabad community had been led for nearly twenty years by R' Dovber Efrat (until 5662) and then by R' Shiloh together with R' Mordechai Dovber Slonim and R' Binyamin Rivlin. When World War I began in 5674, the Chabad presence in Hebron came to a halt.

title_en: Shadarut shaliach sets out to North Africa
summary_en: At the beginning of 5618, R' Shaul Ashkenazi set out as the shaliach of Kollel Chabad to Egypt and North Africa.
story_body: He carried a shadarut document signed by Chabad leaders in both Hebron and Jerusalem. His route went through Izmir, where he received a recommendation from R' Chaim Palagi in Marcheshvan, before continuing to Alexandria, Tunisia, Tripoli, Algeria, Oran, and Tlemcen — an unusual mission since these were traditionally Sephardic donor territories.

title_en: R' Chaim Palagi endorses Chabad shaliach in Izmir
summary_en: In Marcheshvan 5618, R' Chaim Palagi of Izmir gave R' Shaul Ashkenazi a letter of recommendation for his mission to North Africa.
story_body: On his way to Egypt and North Africa, R' Shaul stopped in Izmir to obtain endorsement from the renowned Sephardic posek R' Chaim Palagi. This recommendation was important because the shaliach was traveling to traditionally Sephardic communities on behalf of an Ashkenazic kollel.

title_en: Founding of Kollel Chabad in the Land of Israel
summary_en: Kollel Chabad was founded in the Holy Land in 5565.
story_body: The shadarut document of 5618 recounts that Kollel Chabad was founded over fifty years earlier when 'the great luminaries, the righteous foundations of the world,' established the seat of Chabad in the Holy Land. Settlement followed first in Hebron (5581–83) and later in Jerusalem (5607).

title_en: Sheikh Abd al-Rahman terrorizes Hebron Jews
summary_en: Beginning in 5612, Sheikh Abd al-Rahman tormented the Hebron Jewish community with violent extortion until the early 5614s.
story_body: The 5618 shadarut letter described how the 'wicked Gentiles of Hebron' imposed a heavy yoke on the Jews, extracting money through false accusations and lawless violence. The sheikh was eventually arrested and taken to Istanbul in iron chains, where he received a death sentence.

title_en: Chabad settlement reestablished in Hebron
summary_en: Between 5581 and 5583, Chabad chasidim established their settlement in Hebron.
story_body: Following the founding of Kollel Chabad in 5565, organized Chabad settlement in Hebron took shape between 5581 and 5583. This community would form the institutional base of Kollel Chabad until the central council later operated from there during the mid-19th century.

title_en: Chabad settlement established in Jerusalem
summary_en: In 5607, Chabad chasidim established their organized settlement in Jerusalem.
story_body: Following the Hebron settlement of 5581–83, Chabad presence was formally established in Jerusalem in 5607. This expansion broadened Kollel Chabad's footprint across the Holy Land and led to a Jerusalem-based administrative branch that worked alongside the Hebron council.

title_en: Agreement among Ashkenazi Kollelim in Eretz Yisrael over Siberian shlichim revenue
summary_en: Heads of all Ashkenazi Kollelim in Eretz Yisrael signed a binding agreement assigning donations from five Siberian cities and Smolensk exclusively to Kollel Reisin.
story_body: On 19 Tammuz 5628, leaders of the Perushim, Volyn Chassidim, and Chabad kollelim in Jerusalem, Hebron, Tzfat and Tiberias formalized in writing that revenue from Chita, Verkhneudinsk, Petrovsky Zavod, Barguzin and Achinsk would belong solely to Kollel Reisin. Chabad signatories Shimon Menashe Chaikin, Levi Yitzchak Slonim and Shneur Zalman Pundaminsky signed on behalf of Kollel Chabad of Hebron. The text was preserved in the Kollel Chabad letter register and copied again in 5662 when the kollel debated dispatching dedicated shlichim to Siberia.

title_en: Kollel Chabad writes Rebbe Rashab on Siberian shlichim, citing 1868 agreement
summary_en: Kollel Chabad officials wrote to Rebbe Rashab on 10 Adar I 5662 about sending dedicated shlichim to Siberia, citing the existing pesher with the Perushim.
story_body: When the Kollel Chabad officials in Jerusalem debated dispatching their own emissaries to the cities of Siberia, they wrote to Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch explaining that they were bound by an earlier pesher with the Perushim Vaad HaKlali. They attached a copy of the 1868 agreement which had been preserved in the kollel's letter register. The letter is the earliest known reference to that agreement in Chabad correspondence.

title_en: Pesher allocates Siberian-city revenue 41% Chabad, 59% Kollel Reisin
summary_en: A Tammuz 5668 Kollel Chabad letter records the existing split of donations from Petrovsky Zavod, Chita, Verkhneudinsk and Barguzin: 41% to Chabad, 59% to Kollel Reisin.
story_body: Per a longstanding pesher with the Vaad HaKlali, four of the five Siberian cities were treated as shared between Kollel Reisin and Kollel Chabad rather than belonging to Reisin exclusively. The Tammuz 5668 entry in the Kollel Chabad letter register pinpoints the division as Chabad 41% and Reisin 59%. The fifth city, Achinsk, is not mentioned in this allocation.

title_en: Kollel Chabad center shifts from Hebron to Jerusalem
summary_en: Around 5648 the operational center of Kollel Chabad shifted from Hebron to Jerusalem after Jerusalem leaders challenged the Hebron officials' authority.
story_body: Jerusalem-based Chabad figures began calling themselves 'heads of Kollel Chabad' and asked donors abroad to send funds directly to them rather than through the Hebron officials or the Rogachover Vaad's general gabbai R. Dan Tumarkin. The Hebron officials under R. Shimon Menashe Chaikin responded with a public kruz, supported by some 50 Hebron and 50 Jerusalem Chabad signatories. Although the Jerusalem activists did not get everything they wanted immediately, by 5651 the ba'al ha'address (the kollel's primary postal point of contact) was already based in Jerusalem, and from then on Jerusalem was effectively the kollel's center.

title_en: R. Chaim Avraham Bichowsky begins serving Kollel Chabad
summary_en: In 5651 R. Chaim Avraham Bichowsky began his service in Kollel Chabad, as he later recounted in his kruz 'Teshuva LeDorshei HaAddress'.
story_body: Bichowsky wrote that when he entered the kollel's service in 5651, the ba'al ha'address was already R. Moshe Wienberg in Jerusalem. After Wienberg's death the post passed jointly to R. Manus Werevoleanski and R. Mordechai Schlank, and when Manus died, R. DovBer Efrat was appointed alongside Schlank. His chronology established that Jerusalem had already been the kollel's central address before 5651.

title_en: Rabbinic conference establishes 'Vaad HaChevronim' to expand pushke network
summary_en: In summer 5665 prominent Chabad rabbis convened on the affairs of the Rambahn fund; Rebbe Rashab decided to create a dedicated 'Chevronim' vaad to oversee Eretz Yisrael donations.
story_body: The conference, later described by Rebbe Maharayatz, sought ways to improve the income flowing to Kollel Chabad through R. Meir Baal HaNes pushkes. Rebbe Rashab concluded that a specialized oversight body, named the 'Chevronim', was needed to closely monitor donations. The vaad's first priority was to install pushkes in every Jewish home across Russia.

title_en: Maharayatz letter describes founding of 'Chevronim' vaad and new shadar
summary_en: On 18 Shvat 5666 Rebbe Maharayatz wrote a letter recounting the 1905 conference, the founding of the Chevronim vaad, and the appointment of new shadarim.
story_body: The letter describes how the Chevronim vaad was tasked with expanding pushke placements 'in every place'. R. Meir Leib Horowitz had just been appointed as a new emissary to Russian cities, and R. Zalman Yitzchak Walshanik of Riga was named the dedicated gabbai for Eretz Yisrael funds. The decisions overrode an earlier proposal to abolish traveling shadarim in favor of mailing funds directly to Jerusalem, which Rebbe Rashab had opposed.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab issues general letter on Eretz Yisrael donations and shadar Horowitz
summary_en: On 19 Shvat 5666 Rebbe Rashab issued a circular to Anash on the mitzvah of supporting Eretz Yisrael and introducing R. Meir Leib Horowitz as his new shadar.
story_body: The Rebbe extolled the founding role of the Alter Rebbe in establishing the mitzvah of tzedakas Eretz Yisrael in Russia, and lamented that in recent years the practice had weakened in many towns. He instructed Anash to welcome Horowitz, install pushkes in homes lacking them, and follow detailed procedures spelled out in an accompanying letter from his son Maharayatz. A second circular soon clarified that the new pushkes were for the kollel as a whole and not specifically for Hebron.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab kuntres clarifies new pushkes are for entire kollel, not Hebron alone
summary_en: A Cheshvan 5667 kuntres by Rebbe Rashab reiterated that the new shoferos were intended for the entire kollel and not solely for the Hebron community.
story_body: Some had interpreted the Chevronim vaad's expanded fundraising as specifically aiding Chabad's Hebron yishuv, prompting Rashab to publish a clarifying kuntres. He restated his earlier kruz that 'it never occurred to me that the new shoferos would be for Hebron alone.' The clarification reaffirmed that all new income belonged to the general kollel infrastructure.

title_en: R. Shainfinkel reports finding Kollel Chabad accounts in order to Bobruisker Rebbe
summary_en: On 27 Cheshvan 5673 R. Shalom Simcha Shainfinkel wrote to Rebbe Shemarya Noach of Bobruisk that he had audited the Kollel Chabad cashbox and found the accounts trustworthy.
story_body: Following accusations of embezzlement against the Jerusalem officials, Rebbe Rashab of Lubavitch and Rebbe Shemarya Noach of Bobruisk had asked the wealthy laymen R. Shalom Simcha Shainfinkel and R. Gershon Lifshitz to inspect the kollel's books. Shainfinkel reported that he had visited the kollel office repeatedly, examined the cashbox and ledgers, and found administration 'in proper and upright order' with no grounds to doubt the officials' integrity. Lifshitz participated only on condition that this not be construed as accepting any formal appointment.

title_en: Shainfinkel and Chagiz confirm to Rebbe Rashab that Kollel Chabad books are accurate
summary_en: On 7 Tevet 5673 Shainfinkel and Yitzchak Chagiz wrote to Rebbe Rashab confirming that accounts 1–20 sent by Kollel Chabad matched the office's day-book with no discrepancies.
story_body: Their certification, attached to Rashab's later circular, vouched that the figures aligned with the kollel's 'tagebuch' which was largely signed by recipients upon receipt of funds. Chagiz added his own confirmation that he too had reviewed the accounts and the ledgers and found everything correct. The document became a key piece of evidence in defending the Jerusalem officials against the gabbaim abroad.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab circular endorses Jerusalem etrog officials amid public controversy
summary_en: In Tammuz 5673 Rebbe Rashab issued a printed circular defending the Jerusalem etrog officials as trustworthy and directing donors to continue using the Slonim-Schlank address.
story_body: Amid public uproar over fresh accusations, Rashab told Anash that the Eretz Yisrael etrog officials were honest and that the auditors Shainfinkel and Chagiz had testified their accounts were entirely straight. The circular was distributed via mimeograph together with Shainfinkel's audit letter and signed by hand at the opening and close. It instructed senders to use the established 'Slonim Schlank' address for kessef hakodashim.

title_en: 200+ Chabad members in Eretz Yisrael publicly remove gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin
summary_en: In Tevet 5674 over 200 Chabad members across Eretz Yisrael published a kruz declaring the gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin removed from their posts.
story_body: Responding to accusations and a unilateral decision by the gabbaim abroad to dismiss the Jerusalem-based officials, 204 signatories from Jerusalem, Hebron, Tzfat and Tiberias issued a 'Moda'a Rabba' from the Kollel Chabad etrog office. They declared the two gabbaim and their faction removed, and asked that all funds be sent only to the established address of R. Mordechai Dov Slonim and R. M. Schlank. Bichowsky soon published 'HaTaynos VeHa'ashomos' detailing his charges, and the officials responded in the kuntres 'Tumas Yesharim'.

title_en: Six-member delegation arrives in Jerusalem to audit Kollel Chabad accounts
summary_en: In early summer 5674 a six-member delegation arrived in Eretz Yisrael — three each from Lubavitch and Bobruisk — to audit Kollel Chabad's books and adjudicate the conflict.
story_body: Lubavitch sent R. Eliezer Moshe Modyevsky of Kharol, R. Yitzchak Yoel Rapaporowitz and R. Nosson Gurary of Kremenchug; Bobruisk sent R. Menachem Mendel (son of the Bobruisker Rebbe), R. Yitzchak Shmuel Luria and R. Shemarya Mekler. The gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin also came to face beis-din proceedings with the Eretz Yisrael officials. The visit triggered roughly a month of intensive ledger review and public testimony in Jerusalem.

title_en: 'Emet MeEretz Titzmach' clears Jerusalem officials and invites public claims
summary_en: At the end of Iyar 5674 the Lubavitch delegates published the kruz 'Emet MeEretz Titzmach' affirming the trustworthiness of officials Slonim, Schlank and Naeh.
story_body: After nearly a month of daily review, the delegates announced they had examined every ledger of income from every place and individual, and found all properly recorded with matching orders, talons and receipts. They had posted notices inviting anyone with a complaint to come forward — even offering a reward to whoever could prove a missing share — and received only generic complaints about small allowances rather than evidence of misappropriation. They concluded with full confidence in the integrity of the kollel officials Slonim, Schlank and Naeh.

title_en: Bichowsky faction founds breakaway 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad' in Jerusalem
summary_en: On 24 Iyar 5674 Bichowsky, Luria and Mekler convened a meeting of 'Bnei Kolleinu Chabad HaMeyuchad', formalizing a permanent split in the kollel.
story_body: When the unity proposal required retaining the existing Jerusalem managers, members of the Bichowsky group refused, citing past suffering at the hands of those managers. The next day they published a kruz announcing the founding of 'Kollel Chabad HaMeyuchad' as a separate body, and stating that the din torah against the previous managers would be conducted only once R. Chaim Bagin — who was ill — arrived. The split between the two kollelim from this point became final.

title_en: Din torah opens before Jerusalem Beis Din Tzedek between Kollel officials and gabbaim
summary_en: On 11 Tammuz 5674 both sides appeared before the Ashkenazi Beis Din Tzedek of Jerusalem, which heard the parties before the gabbaim withdrew.
story_body: After Bagin arrived, the parties presented their claims before the Beis Din Tzedek. The gabbaim ultimately refused to continue litigating before that beis din, and the dispute dragged on for two months. The gabbaim returned abroad at the start of Elul, and on 16 Elul the beis din published its ruling 'Emet UMishpat Kasuv' siding with the Jerusalem officials.

title_en: Jerusalem Beis Din publishes 'Emet UMishpat Kasuv' in favor of Kollel officials
summary_en: On 16 Elul 5674 the Jerusalem Beis Din Tzedek published a public ruling supporting the Kollel Chabad officials against the gabbaim Bichowsky and Bagin.
story_body: The ruling, titled 'Emet UMishpat Kasuv', came after the two gabbaim had returned abroad without completing the formal din torah. It formalized the beis din's position that the Jerusalem officials were vindicated. Even so, accusations and counter-accusations between the two camps continued in printed pamphlets for years afterward.

title_en: Jerusalem Beis Din Tzedek reaffirms trust in Kollel Chabad officials during WWI
summary_en: On 20 Adar I 5679 the Jerusalem Beis Din published a further ruling defending the Kollel Chabad vaad amid wartime accusations from Anash abroad.
story_body: Critical letters had circulated in the Diaspora attacking the Jerusalem vaad under Rebbe Rashab's nesius, sowing discord and discouraging donors. The beis din declared that it knew the officials well as honest and trustworthy men, and that whenever funds arrived from America and England — Russian remittances having been cut off by the war — they were distributed to the poor of the kollel in Jerusalem, Hebron, Tzfat, Tiberias, Yafo and the moshavot. The pesak became a recurring touchstone in the kollel correspondence of 5681–5682.

title_en: Rebbe Maharayatz visits Eretz Yisrael and inspects Kollel Chabad
summary_en: During his summer 5689 visit to Eretz Yisrael, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn personally inspected the Kollel Chabad office and its work.
story_body: The Rebbe reported being pleased with the kollel's administration and orderly procedures, and witnessed the scope of its activity in supporting Torah scholars, the holy yishuv, widows, orphans and the very poor. He saw the institution as continuing the legacy of his ancestors, and the visit set the stage for his formal acceptance of the kollel's nesius days later. The visit also fell during the summer that included the 1929 Arab riots in Hebron.

title_en: Maharayatz issues public letter endorsing Kollel Chabad
summary_en: On 13 Menachem Av 5689 Rebbe Maharayatz wrote a letter of strengthening for Kollel Chabad describing what he had seen at its Jerusalem office.
story_body: He praised the kollel's leadership, administration, and orderly procedures, and described the breadth of its work in supporting Torah scholars and the yishuv of Eretz Yisrael. The letter was meant to encourage donors and to recommit the worldwide Chabad community to the kollel's mission. It accompanied his decision in principle to accept the formal nesius of the kollel.

title_en: Maharayatz formally accepts nesius of Kollel Chabad; appoints Eliezerov as bakoach
summary_en: On the eve of 15 Menachem Av 5689 Maharayatz informed the kollel officials that he would assume the nesius and appointed R. Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov as his permanent bakoach.
story_body: The Rebbe accepted the nesius on condition that an institutional 'bakoach hanesius' — distinct from the regular officials — be installed to oversee all kollel affairs, sign in the name of the nesius, and handle all correspondence with him. He named his relative R. Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov to that position. The appointment restored the traditional structure of Chabad rebbes serving as nesi'im of the kollel that had been founded in the time of the Alter Rebbe.

title_en: Maharayatz to Kollel Chabad: a dedicated staffer for the kollel is essential
summary_en: On 7 Cheshvan 5691 Maharayatz wrote to the Kollel Chabad leadership that a dedicated staff person, even part-time, was indispensable to handling its affairs.
story_body: After returning from his year-long trip to America, the Rebbe redoubled his involvement in kollel matters, sending shadarim and writing extensively to town gabbaim across Eastern Europe. His letter to the leadership argued that the cost of a dedicated staffer would itself be 'income, not expense', because of how much fundraising and administration it would unlock. The letter is part of an intense burst of administrative reorganization spanning 5690–5691.

title_en: Maharayatz urges Eliezerov to focus on youth and children of Kollel Chabad
summary_en: On 6 Menachem Av 5692 Maharayatz wrote to R. Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov urging deeper engagement with the youth, girls and children of Kollel Chabad families.
story_body: Beyond his focus on the elders and avreichim, the Rebbe wanted a dedicated vaad to periodically examine children studying in cheders and yeshivos, give prizes for good behavior and excellence in learning, and gently discipline those who needed it. For the older youth he proposed structured study sessions or printed materials to keep them connected to the kollel. The same theme is taken up in his 12 Cheshvan letter to the kollel's nesius committee.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's aliyah to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and his group ascended to Eretz Yisrael, with primary financial support coming from the Hasidim of White Russia and Lithuania.
story_body: In 5537 (1777), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and R' Avraham of Kalisk led a group of Hasidim from White Russia and Lithuania to settle in Eretz Yisrael. The main flow of financial support came from those regions, though some assistance also arrived from Volhynia and Poland. This aliyah marked the foundation of the Hasidic Yishuv whose support eventually became the responsibility of the Alter Rebbe.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's letter on declining Volhynia support
summary_en: R' Menachem Mendel wrote that Volhynia's support had dropped to only fifty gold coins for the year.
story_body: In 5542 (1782), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote a letter noting that financial support from Volhynia had dropped sharply, sending only fifty gold pieces. He explained that since beginning his service as a leader, he had moved his residence from Volhynia to Russia, which may have weakened the relationship. The letter is preserved in Likutei Amarim, letter 5.

title_en: Polish Hasidim led by R' Yaakov Shimshon settle in Tiberias
summary_en: A group of Polish Hasidim led by R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka made aliyah and settled in Tiberias.
story_body: In 5554 (1794), several Hasidim from Poland led by R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka ascended to the Holy Land and settled in Tiberias. R' Avraham of Kalisk then turned to them and to the Hasidic communities in Volhynia and Poland, asking them to contribute proportionately to the Hasidic Yishuv. This aliyah eventually triggered demands for a separate Polish-Volhynian kollel in Tiberias.

title_en: R' Mordechai of Neskhiz issues general appeal for Eretz Yisrael fund
summary_en: R' Mordechai of Neskhiz issued a general appeal for the Eretz Yisrael fund, joined by the Chozeh of Lublin.
story_body: In 5556 (1796), R' Mordechai of Neskhiz published a general appeal regarding the dire poverty of the Hasidic Yishuv in Eretz Yisrael, noting that he had previously stayed clear of fundraising. The Chozeh of Lublin joined the appeal, writing that Polish Jewry had until now lacked someone to organize collections as White Russia had. This launched a parallel Polish-Volhynian fundraising effort outside the Alter Rebbe's network.

title_en: Alter Rebbe sends two shadarim to Volhynia to mediate kollel dispute
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe dispatched two shadarim to Volhynia in winter to mediate the dispute over the separate Volhynia-Poland kollel in Tiberias.
story_body: In winter 5556 (1796), the Alter Rebbe wrote about the 'great noise' that had erupted over the Eretz Yisrael funds from Volhynia and Ukraine, where new voices were challenging the long-standing arrangement of channeling all monies through R' Avraham of Kalisk. He dispatched two shadarim, R' Dovber of Dubrovna and R' Refael, to Volhynia to negotiate a compromise. The talks eventually produced an agreement that Volhynia's funds would be transported separately by a Polish shadar from Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: R' Asher of Stolin's letter on R' Mordechai of Neskhiz's new role
summary_en: R' Asher of Stolin wrote to R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh that R' Mordechai of Neskhiz was now involved in Eretz Yisrael fundraising.
story_body: In winter 5557 (1797), R' Asher of Stolin wrote a letter to R' Baruch of Mezhibuzh describing how R' Mordechai of Neskhiz had received a letter from R' Avraham of Kalisk and the rav of Shepetivka about a new fundraising effort, and had begun involving himself for the first time. The letter also shows that the dispute over the proposed separate Volhynia-Poland kollel in Tiberias was still active a year after the Alter Rebbe's mediation attempt.

title_en: R' Yaakov Shimshon distributes funds independently, sparking conflict
summary_en: R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka brought and distributed Polish funds alone in Tiberias, sparking conflict that R' Nachman of Breslov tried to mediate.
story_body: In 5559 (1799), R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka brought the Polish-Volhynian funds to Tiberias and distributed them solely among his people, breaking from the previous arrangement under R' Avraham of Kalisk. The conflict between the two leaders intensified sharply. R' Nachman of Breslov attempted to mediate between them, as documented in Kovetz Beit Aharon V'Yisrael.

title_en: Passing of R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka ends separate Volhynia kollel
summary_en: With the passing of R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka, the separate Volhynia kollel in Eretz Yisrael appears to have dissolved.
story_body: R' Yaakov Shimshon of Shepetivka passed away in 5561 (1801). From that point on, no separate Volhynia kollel existed in the Holy Land; funds again flowed through R' Avraham of Kalisk. Volhynian collections continued to be raised separately abroad, but distribution in Eretz Yisrael was reunified under a single Hasidic kollel.

title_en: R' Avraham of Kalisk on the troubles from separating Volhynia and Russia
summary_en: R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote that great harm followed the separation of Volhynia's Hasidim from Russia's in the fundraising system.
story_body: In 5565 (1805), R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote that 'from the day the people of Volhynia were separated from the people of Russia, all the problems came out into the open, and great damage came from this.' Nevertheless, although collections in Europe remained organized separately by region, when the funds reached Eretz Yisrael they all passed through his hands. The letter is preserved in Yagdil Torah.

title_en: R' Chaim Halevi begins 42-year tenure as gabbai of Hebron
summary_en: R' Chaim Halevi ibn Yakar began his 42-year tenure as gabbai and pakid of the Hebron community.
story_body: In 5548 (1788), R' Chaim Yaakov Halevi ibn Yakar began serving as gabbai and pakid (treasurer and officer) of the Hebron Sephardic community. He held the post for 42 years, handling all communal affairs until 5590 (1830). As a sign of trust and recognition, in 5590 his son R' Yosef Halevi was appointed as his deputy and eventual successor.

title_en: R' Yisrael Yaffe of Kapust prints Shulchan Aruch HaRav
summary_en: The Yaffe brothers in Kapust published the first three volumes of Shulchan Aruch HaRav, Orach Chaim.
story_body: In 5576 (1816), the brothers R' Yehuda and R' Yisrael Yaffe, sons of the late R' Alexander Sender Feivish Yaffe, printed volumes 1-3 of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim, at their press in Kapust. This R' Yisrael Yaffe is distinct from R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, also a printer in Kapust who later settled in Hebron. Both Yaffes eventually made aliyah and lived in Hebron.

title_en: Aliyah of R' Yisrael Yaffe (the younger) of Kapust
summary_en: R' Yisrael Yaffe (the younger, son of A.S. Feivish) made aliyah to Eretz Yisrael from Kapust.
story_body: In 5580 (1820), R' Yisrael Yaffe — son of Alexander Sender Feivish Yaffe and one of the Kapust printers of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch — made aliyah and settled in Hebron. The 5599 census recorded him as 64 years old, having come from Kapust in 5580. He is distinct from R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, also of Kapust, who arrived in 5583.

title_en: Aliyah of R' Mordechai of Shklov to Hebron
summary_en: R' Mordechai of Shklov made aliyah and settled in Hebron, where his son R' Yisrael joined him two years later.
story_body: R' Mordechai made aliyah from Shklov in 5581 (1821), as recorded in the 5599 census. His son R' Yisrael Yaffe joined him in Hebron in 5593 (1833). R' Mordechai signed the 5594 shadar document and the 5603 power-of-attorney for Jerusalem adjudication.

title_en: Aliyah of R' Yisrael Yaffe the Kapust printer
summary_en: R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, the senior Kapust printer, made aliyah and settled in Hebron.
story_body: In 5583 (1823), R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe of Kapust — a signatory of the 5556 Liozna takanot and one of the founders of the Hebron Yishuv — made aliyah to Eretz Yisrael. He soon served as a shadar before 5587 and held a yechidut with the Alter Rebbe documented in Igrot Kodesh. He passed away before Shvat 5589 (early 1829).

title_en: First agreement between Hebron Sephardic and Chabad communities
summary_en: The Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron reached a first agreement dividing Hebron's share of the Pekuam funds.
story_body: In 5585 (1825), the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron concluded their first agreement, dividing Hebron's portion of the Pekuam Amsterdam funds between the two communities. The Pekuam committee did not accept their compromise, however, and additional negotiations were required regarding shdarus to other lands. These discussions ultimately produced the broader 5590 agreement.

title_en: Yosef David Ayash sent as shadar to Italian cities for Hebron
summary_en: Yosef David Ayash began a four-year shlichut from Hebron through the cities of Italy.
story_body: Starting in 5586 (1826), Yosef David Ayash traveled through the cities of Italy as a shadar on behalf of Hebron, continuing until 5590. His shlichut was conducted independently because the Pekuam committee did not handle fundraising in Italy. Ayash later left the Jewish people, but his shlichut is described in detail in Sheluchei Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: Death of R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe of Kapust
summary_en: R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe, founding settler of the Chabad community in Hebron, passed away before Shvat 5589.
story_body: R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak Yaffe of Kapust, one of the founding settlers of the Chabad community in Hebron, passed away before Shvat 5589 (January 1829). He had served as a shadar and signatory on key documents of the community. His son R' Ephraim later succeeded him as memuneh (administrator) of the Chabad kollel in Hebron.

title_en: Hebron agreement: shdarus to Italy, Sephard, and Persia
summary_en: Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron formalized joint shdarus arrangements for Italy, Persia, and Sephardic lands.
story_body: In 5590 (1830), the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron signed a detailed agreement governing joint shdarus operations to Italy ('Frankia'), Persia ('Urmili and Arabistan'), and other lands. Italy's proceeds were to be divided 80% to Sephardim and 20% to Ashkenazim, while collections from Sephardic and Persian cities, fundraised by Ashkenazi shadarim, would be divided three-quarters to Ashkenazim and one-quarter to Sephardim. This agreement formalized cooperation alongside the Pekuam's centralized fundraising in Amsterdam.

title_en: R' Yosef Halevi appointed assistant gabbai in Hebron
summary_en: R' Yosef Halevi was appointed as assistant and successor to his father R' Chaim Halevi as Hebron's gabbai.
story_body: In 5590 (1830), after R' Chaim Yaakov Halevi ibn Yakar's 42 years of service as gabbai and pakid of the Hebron community, his son R' Yosef Halevi was appointed as his deputy and successor. The appointment was described as 'a sign of trust and honor' to the elder Halevi. R' Chaim Halevi was the first signatory on the 5590 inter-community agreement.

title_en: Pekuam letter to Hebron Chabad leaders praising unity
summary_en: The Pekuam committee wrote to Hebron's Chabad leaders expressing satisfaction at the renewed peace with the Sephardic pakid.
story_body: On 18 Elul 5592 (September 14, 1832), the Pekuam Amsterdam committee wrote to the rabbis and administrators of the Chabad kollel in Hebron. They expressed great satisfaction with a recent letter announcing peace and unity between Chabad and the Sephardic pakid R' Chaim Yaakov Halevi ibn Yakar. The letter was published in Bezalel Landau's Kerem HaChasidut.

title_en: Founding of Chevrat Trumat HaKodesh in USA
summary_en: Chevrat Trumat HaKodesh was founded in the United States, on the model of the Amsterdam Pekuam.
story_body: In early 5593 (1833), the Chevrat Trumat HaKodesh society was established in the United States, modeled on the Amsterdam Pekuam. Like its European counterpart, it sought to consolidate American Eretz Yisrael fundraising and discourage independent shadarim, withholding allocations from communities that hosted unauthorized envoys. The organization later interacted closely with the Pekuam and the Hebron Chabad kollel.

title_en: Aliyah of R' Yisrael ben Mordechai from Shklov to Hebron
summary_en: R' Yisrael ben Mordechai made aliyah from Shklov to join his father in Hebron.
story_body: In 5593 (1833), R' Yisrael ben Mordechai, age 25 and married with a son and daughter, made aliyah from Shklov to Hebron. His father R' Mordechai had preceded him by two years, arriving in 5581. This R' Yisrael Yaffe of Shklov is the third Hebron-based figure of that name in the period.

title_en: Pogroms during the Peasants' Revolt against Hebron's Jewish community
summary_en: Arab rebels rose against Hebron and threatened the Jewish community with daily violence on 9 Iyar.
story_body: On 9 Iyar 5594 (May 17, 1834), Arabs in Hebron rebelled against the regional ruler, and for many days threatened the Jewish community with cruel deaths. R' Chaim Halevi, the pakid, used his standing with local nobles and significant payments to secure their protection. The pogroms were followed by an earthquake, both of which were described in a fundraising letter signed by the Chabad kollel leaders sent with shadar R' Natan Amram.

title_en: R' Natan Amram appointed joint shadar to Italy and Europe
summary_en: R' Natan Amram, later rabbi of Alexandria, was appointed as a joint shadar from Hebron's Sephardic and Chabad communities to Italy and Europe.
story_body: In Nissan 5594 (1834), R' Natan Amram — later rabbi of Alexandria, Egypt — was designated to travel as a joint shadar from the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron through Italy and surrounding European countries. His departure was delayed by the pogroms and earthquake, and his mission was expanded. The expanded shlichut letter, signed primarily by Chabad leaders, was preserved in Sarid V'Palit.

title_en: Second Hebron inter-community agreement expanding shdarus reach
summary_en: Hebron's Sephardic and Chabad communities renewed their agreement, expanding the joint shdarus territories to include Turkey and North Africa.
story_body: In 5602 (1842), the Hebron Sephardic and Chabad communities signed another agreement renewing the joint shdarus arrangements. The terms largely matched the 5590 agreement, but added Turkey and the Maghreb (North Africa, inner and outer) to the list of joint shlichut territories alongside Italy, Persia, and Sephardic lands. The expansion reflected growing fundraising operations across the Mediterranean and Ottoman lands.

title_en: R' Yechiel Cohen sent as joint shadar to USA from Hebron
summary_en: R' Yechiel Cohen traveled to the United States as a shadar bearing letters from both Hebron communities.
story_body: In 5607 (1847), R' Yechiel Cohen was sent as a shadar to the United States, carrying credentials from both the Sephardic and Chabad communities of Hebron. He stopped in London on the way and met the philanthropist R' Asher b'R' Shimshon. The Pekuam later sought clarification from the Chabad kollel about the trip's fundraising results.

title_en: Pekuam queries Hebron Chabad on R' Yechiel Cohen's American mission
summary_en: The Pekuam wrote on 15 Elul to ask Hebron's Chabad leaders for accounting of R' Yechiel Cohen's American collections.
story_body: On 15 Elul 5607 (August 27, 1847), the Pekuam Amsterdam committee wrote to the heads of Hebron's Chabad kollel inquiring about R' Yechiel Cohen's shadarus to America. The philanthropist R' Asher b'R' Shimshon of London had told them Cohen claimed to represent both Hebron kollelim. The Pekuam wanted to know exactly how much had been collected and what share Chabad had received.

title_en: R' Yechiel Cohen sent again to USA from Beit El kabbalists
summary_en: R' Yechiel Cohen was sent again to America, this time from the Beit El kabbalist beit midrash in Jerusalem, while still apparently linked to Chabad's kollel.
story_body: In 5609 (1849), R' Yechiel Cohen was sent again to America, this time on behalf of the Beit El kabbalists' beit midrash in Jerusalem. Despite the change of sender, the Chabad kollel of Hebron remained connected to the mission, as seen in subsequent Pekuam correspondence. The journey extended for several years.

title_en: Pekuam complains about R' Yechiel Cohen's prolonged American mission
summary_en: On 25 Tammuz, the Pekuam wrote that New York donors had instructed them not to give Hebron a penny because of R' Yechiel Cohen's continued shadarus.
story_body: On 25 Tammuz 5611 (July 24, 1851), the Pekuam wrote to Hebron's Chabad kollel that on several occasions they had received donations from New York with explicit instructions not to give a single penny to Hebron — because R' Yechiel Cohen was still touring America after a very long time. The letter is preserved in Pinkas 11 of the Pekuam records.

title_en: Pekuam further correspondence about R' Yechiel Cohen
summary_en: The Pekuam continued discussing R' Yechiel Cohen's American shadarus in a letter of 28 Tishrei.
story_body: On 28 Tishrei 5612 (October 23, 1851), the Pekuam wrote another letter to Hebron continuing to discuss R' Yechiel Cohen's prolonged American shadarus and its impact on New York donations. The letter is recorded in Pinkas 11 of the Pekuam records.

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin appointed rav of Hebron Chabad
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin made aliyah from Konstantinograd and was appointed rabbi of Hebron's Chabad community.
story_body: In 5647 (1887), the elderly R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin, then 85, sought a deputy. That year, R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin, formerly rabbi of Konstantinograd in Ukraine, made aliyah and settled in Hebron. After examining Levin's learning, Chaikin and the leading scholars of Hebron unanimously appointed him as rabbi, signing a formal kesav of acceptance.

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Levin's letter on his Hebron rabbinate
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote to his family from Hebron on the 4th day of Selichot describing his new rabbinic appointment.
story_body: On the 4th day of Selichot 5647 (September 1887), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote to his family from Hebron, describing the elderly R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin and the process by which Levin had been examined and accepted as rabbi by the city's scholars. The letter is preserved in Sinai journal volume 87.

title_en: R' Levin's letter on the modest salary of the Hebron rabbinate
summary_en: On 19 Tevet, R' Levin wrote home that his salary was only 12 rubles a month with no other income.
story_body: On 19 Tevet 5648 (January 3, 1888), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote home that his total salary in Hebron was only 12 rubles a month, with no wedding fees, mechirat chametz revenue, or Purim funds as in the diaspora. He noted that prior to him, the Hebron rabbi had not taken a salary at all. The letter is preserved in Sinai journal.

title_en: R' Levin's letter on Hebron's Jewish court system
summary_en: On 22 Sivan, R' Levin wrote that Hebron had abundant Torah-court cases, including disputes between Jews and Muslims who also turned to the beit din.
story_body: On 22 Sivan 5648 (June 2, 1888), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote that din Torah cases in Hebron were numerous because the community did not use gentile courts, and even Jew-Muslim disputes were brought before the Jewish beit din. He explained that despite this, the rabbi received no fees for rulings, only the basic small salary. The letter is preserved in Sinai journal.

title_en: RSM Chaikin publishes Chabad kollel proclamation
summary_en: R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin issued a public proclamation regarding Chabad kollel affairs, co-signed by R' Levin.
story_body: In 5648 (1888), R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin continued his active role in Hebron after Levin's appointment, publishing a kruz regarding matters of the Chabad kollel. R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin co-signed the proclamation, marking the new dual rabbinic leadership. The proclamation is preserved in Migdal Oz.

title_en: Hebron Chabad rabbis issue 5649 kruz
summary_en: R' Chaikin and R' Levin co-signed another public proclamation related to the Chabad kollel.
story_body: In 5649 (1889), R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin and R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin co-signed another kruz related to the Hebron Chabad kollel. By this point Levin was consistently signing with the title 'rav and moreh in Hebron,' while Chaikin signed without titles. The signing order — Chaikin first, then Levin — reflected respect for the elder while acknowledging Levin's official rabbinic role.

title_en: Letter to Pekuam regarding Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron
summary_en: R' Chaikin and R' Levin wrote to the Pekuam regarding the Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron.
story_body: In 5650 (1890), R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin wrote to the Pekuam Amsterdam committee on behalf of the Magen Avot yeshiva in Hebron, with R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin co-signing as rabbi. The dual signature pattern continued: Chaikin signed first, Levin added the title 'rav and moreh in Hebron.' The yeshiva was a Chabad institution requiring external support.

title_en: R' Levin's final letter from Hebron
summary_en: R' Levin wrote his last letter from Hebron on 17 Tammuz, still signing as rav of the city.
story_body: On 17 Tammuz 5651 (June 23, 1891), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin wrote his last preserved letter from Hebron, still signing 'rav and moreh in Hebron.' The following year he relocated to Jerusalem. His letters from Hebron are preserved in Sinai journal volume 87.

title_en: R' Levin moves from Hebron to Jerusalem
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin ended his Hebron rabbinate and moved to Jerusalem.
story_body: Toward the end of 5652 (1892), R' Yehuda Leib Shaul Levin moved from Hebron to Jerusalem, ending five years of service as rav of Hebron's Chabad community. His departure is documented in the biographical work Zekher Aviad. The move closed the dual-rabbinate era he had shared with R' Shmuel Menachem Chaikin.

title_en: Death of R' Nechemiah of Dubrovna, gabbai of Kollel Chabad
summary_en: R' Nechemiah of Dubrovna, first general gabbai for the Tzemach Tzedek's Eretz Yisrael fund, died on 15 Shevat.
story_body: R' Nechemiah of Dubrovna, author of Divrei Nechemiah, served as the general gabbai appointed by the Tzemach Tzedek to receive funds in the diaspora destined for the Chabad community in Eretz Yisrael. After his death on 15 Shevat 5612, the position passed to R' Zev of Retzitzeh and R' Avraham, rabbi of Drogichov. His death is recorded in Beis Rebbi.

title_en: R' Dan Tomarkin appointed gabbai of Kollel Chabad
summary_en: The Tzemach Tzedek appointed R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov as gabbai of Kollel Chabad in 5615.
story_body: In 5615 the Tzemach Tzedek appointed the wealthy chasid R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov as a gabbai of Kollel Chabad, a position he held for over thirty years. He initially served alongside others on the committee and later became the general gabbai, transferring funds to the Tzemach Tzedek for distribution. Because R' Dan lived in Rogachov, the committee that became known as the 'Rogachov Vaad' was established in that city.

title_en: Hebron Chabad community's letter to Montefiore on agricultural plan
summary_en: Leaders of the Hebron Chabad community wrote to Sir Moses Montefiore on 4 Tammuz responding to his plan for agricultural settlement in Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: Sir Moses Montefiore traveled to Eretz Yisrael with a plan to lease land from Mohammed Ali for fifty years and settle Jews in agricultural villages. The Hebron Chabad community responded with an elaborately phrased letter dated 4 Tammuz endorsing the plan in principle but explaining that most of their members were elderly Torah scholars unsuited for farming, and that direct financial support would be a greater mitzvah for their community.

title_en: Jerusalem Jews tell Montefiore agricultural plan is no longer viable
summary_en: During Montefiore's 5609 visit, Jerusalem leaders explained that Egyptian rule had ended and farming the villages was now too dangerous.
story_body: On Montefiore's return visit in 5609, the Jerusalem community informed him that conditions had reversed: with the end of Egyptian rule over Eretz Yisrael, weapons had returned to local hands and the countryside had become too dangerous for Jewish agricultural settlement. The letter was signed by several Chabad leaders in Jerusalem including R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin, R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein, and R' Uri Ornstein.

title_en: Chabad community settles in Jerusalem
summary_en: Chabad chasidim settled in Jerusalem in 5607.
story_body: Several leaders of the Chabad community in Jerusalem, including R' Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin, R' Ephraim Yitzchak Epstein, R' Uri Ornstein, R' Yosef Yehuda Leib Mishyov, and R' Tzvi Hirsch Fundaminsky, settled in the holy city in 5607. They later joined signatories on community petitions addressed to Sir Moses Montefiore.

title_en: First record of Rogachov committee in Kollel Chabad ledger
summary_en: The earliest documented mention of the Rogachov committee appears in the Kollel Chabad financial ledger of 5633.
story_body: The 'Rogachov Vaad' served as the central committee receiving funds for Kollel Chabad in the diaspora. The earliest extant mention appears in a Kollel Chabad accounting ledger of 5633 noting 'sent from Rogachov.' The committee likely was established earlier, perhaps by the Tzemach Tzedek himself.

title_en: Agreement between Kollel Chabad and other kollelim in Hebron
summary_en: In 5635 the Chabad and other Ashkenazi kollelim in Hebron agreed to share funds incoming to Kollel Chabad equally.
story_body: In 5635 the Chabad community in Hebron reached an agreement with the other Ashkenazi kollelim there that all funds entering Kollel Chabad's coffers in the name of the Hebron Ashkenazi community would be shared equally with members of the other kollelim. Oversight of the fund remained exclusively with Kollel Chabad's Hebron managers, with the official name being 'Kollel Ashkenazim Chabad of Hebron.'

title_en: Frumkin describes plight of Hebron's Jews in Chabatzelet
summary_en: Yisrael Dov Frumkin published a report in Chabatzelet on 9 Marcheshvan describing the degraded state of Hebron's Jewish community.
story_body: The editor of Chabatzelet, Yisrael Dov Frumkin, described how Hebron's Jews lived in conditions worse than Jews of other Palestinian cities. He depicted them as outnumbered by Turks of low moral standing, with weak local government and constant harassment — a Jew dared not even respond to insults lest a mob accuse him of insulting the religion and beat him severely.

title_en: Murder of Rachamim Turgeman in Hebron
summary_en: Hebron Jewish notable Rachamim Turgeman died from beating injuries, reported in Chabatzelet on 14 Tevet 5638.
story_body: Rachamim Turgeman, a notable of the Hebron Jewish community and a British protégé, was severely beaten by a local Turk and died seven days later. The Hebron community alerted the governor, and because he was under British protection a commission including the British consul's representative and Dr. Chaplin came from Jerusalem, performed an autopsy confirming the cause of death, and arrested the assailant for trial.

title_en: Hebron arbitration ruling establishes joint Ashkenazi Vaad
summary_en: Arbitrators in Jerusalem ruled on 20 Tammuz 5647 to create a joint Vaad of Ashkenazi communities in Hebron.
story_body: After disputes arose between Kollel Chabad in Hebron and the other Ashkenazi kollelim, both sides turned to the Jerusalem beis din under R' Shmuel Salant. The arbitrators Zalman Chaim Rivlin and Yoel Moshe Salomon, with R' Shmuel Salant's approval, ruled on 20 Tammuz 5647 that two Chabad representatives and one from the other kollelim would form a three-man 'Vaad of the Ashkenazi communities in Hebron' with shared seal and shared distribution of communal funds.

title_en: Hebron Joint Vaad publicly announced in Chabatzelet
summary_en: An announcement in Chabatzelet on 3 Marcheshvan 5648 informed world Jewry of the new Hebron unified Vaad and its three elected leaders.
story_body: Following the arbitration ruling, the new joint Vaad published an announcement in Chabatzelet on 3 Marcheshvan 5648 declaring that all disputes between Chabad chasidim and the other Ashkenazi kollelim of Hebron were ended. The three elected leaders — R' Baruch Mordechai Halevi Gloiberman, R' Binyamin Rivlin, and R' Meir Tzvi Hershler — would receive all donations for the Hebron Ashkenazi community.

title_en: R' Shalom Mordechai Chaikin publishes pamphlet honoring R' Dan Tomarkin
summary_en: In 5648 R' Shalom Mordechai Chaikin printed a proclamation honoring R' Dan Tomarkin's forty years of service to Kollel Chabad.
story_body: In 5648 R' Shalom Mordechai Chaikin published a proclamation describing how the Tzemach Tzedek and his sons had ordained R' Dan Tomarkin of Rogachov as gabbai of Kollel Chabad, praising his forty years of trustworthy service in distributing the funds that sustained the Chabad community in Eretz Yisrael. The text was later reprinted in Migdal Oz.

title_en: Hebron Vaad in financial crisis as R' Baruch Mordechai resigns
summary_en: At the end of Kislev 5650 Hebron community leaders begged the remaining two Vaad members to continue serving despite empty coffers.
story_body: By late Kislev 5650 the Hebron Ashkenazi Vaad faced severe financial distress: R' Baruch Mordechai Halevi resigned, doctors and shochtim went unpaid, and the pharmacy ran out of medicine. The community's rabbis and notables wrote to the two remaining members, R' Binyamin Rivlin and R' Meir Tzvi Hershler, urging them to continue managing the Vaad's affairs until new elections on Rosh Chodesh Elul.

title_en: Hebron Vaad publishes public appeal for funds
summary_en: On 8 Tevet 5650 the two remaining Hebron Vaad members published an appeal to world Jewry for emergency assistance.
story_body: After community leaders begged them to continue, R' Binyamin Rivlin and R' Meir Tzvi Hershler published in Chabatzelet on 8 Tevet 5650 a public appeal describing the Vaad's emptied coffers, unpaid communal workers, and inability to pay the doctor and shochet, calling on diaspora Jewry to come to the aid of the Ashkenazi communities of Hebron.

title_en: Hebron Vaad letter signed by four gabbaim
summary_en: A Hebron Vaad letter dated 5 Tammuz 5658 was signed by Mordechai Dovber Slonim, Binyamin Rivlin, Yaakov Slonim, and Levi Eliezer Klansky.
story_body: By 5 Tammuz 5658 the Vaad of the Ashkenazi community in Hebron was led by four signatories: Mordechai Dovber Slonim, Binyamin Rivlin, Yaakov Slonim, and Levi Eliezer Klansky. The same first two signed Vaad documents in 5663 and 5669, when Chaim Avraham Fundaminsky was added, all stamping with the seal 'Zechus Avos LeBanim Tizkor — Seal of the Vaad HaKlali of the Ashkenazi Communities of Hebron.'

title_en: Rebbe Rashab purchases Hebron building for future yeshiva
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab purchased a large multi-story building in Hebron in Av 5668.
story_body: In Av 5668 the Rebbe Rashab of Lubavitch purchased a large multi-story stone building in Hebron containing eighteen dwellings, three large water cisterns, surrounding land suitable for additional construction, and a khan rented for two hundred rubles annually. The building would later house the Toras Emes yeshiva established in 5672.

title_en: Hebron Vaad correspondence dated 14 Kislev
summary_en: Hebron Vaad stationery preserved in the Shila Archive bears a letter dated 14 Kislev 5664.
story_body: A photograph of the Hebron Vaad's letterhead from the Shila Archive includes a letter dated 14 Kislev 5664 that appears unrelated to the Vaad itself. The stationery printed the official name of the Vaad and the address of the Ashkenazi rabbi.

title_en: Last known appointment of Hebron Joint Vaad
summary_en: On 15 Kislev 5670 seventy-five Hebron heads of household signed the last known appointment of the joint Vaad.
story_body: The last known appointment document of the Hebron joint Vaad is dated 15 Kislev 5670 and bears the signatures of seventy-five heads of family in Hebron. The names of the three elected members were not specified in the document, which simply addressed them as 'three who walk uprightly chosen by majority to manage the Vaad HaKlali.'

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim 'Toras Emes' yeshiva opens in Hebron
summary_en: The Toras Emes yeshiva opened in Hebron at the start of 5672.
story_body: At the start of 5672 a branch of Tomchei Tmimim, the Toras Emes yeshiva, opened in Hebron and operated for nearly three years. Studies began in the house donated by R' Shneur Zalman Berlin, which had previously housed the Magen Avos yeshiva, and were later moved to the Romano courtyard. Sleeping quarters for students and the mashpia's family were assigned in the large building purchased by the Rebbe Rashab in 5668.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz instructs R' Shimon Hauzman to prepare Hebron quarters
summary_en: In Tammuz 5671 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to prepare rooms in Hebron for the new yeshiva's mashpia and students.
story_body: In Tammuz 5671, as the decision was reached to send students from Lubavitch to Hebron, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shimon Hauzman, who managed the Hebron building, asking him to prepare five rooms in the property — three on the upper floor for the mashpia and yeshiva office, and two on the lower floor for the visiting students. A parallel letter went to R' Yitzchak Chen, who had settled in Hebron that year.

title_en: Toras Emes yeshiva closes in Hebron
summary_en: The Toras Emes yeshiva ceased operating in Hebron at the end of 5674.
story_body: After nearly three years of operation in Hebron, the Toras Emes yeshiva ceased functioning at the end of 5674. The yeshiva had operated first in the home donated by R' Shneur Zalman Berlin and later in the Romano courtyard, with student housing in the Rebbe Rashab's large property.

title_en: Kol Aryeh published in Jerusalem
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman Mendelovitch published Kol Aryeh in Jerusalem in 5626.
story_body: While serving as a Kollel Chabad emissary to the eastern lands, R' Shneur Zalman ben R' Menachem Mendel Mendelovitch obtained a major donation from the Sassoon family in Bombay for the Chabad synagogue in Jerusalem. He documented the trip in the introduction to his book Kol Aryeh, published in Jerusalem in 5626.

title_en: Zikhron Yerushalayim published in Jerusalem
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman Mendelovitch published Zikhron Yerushalayim in Jerusalem in 5636.
story_body: In 5636 R' Shneur Zalman Mendelovitch published Zikhron Yerushalayim in Jerusalem, which included a description of the Chabad Ashkenazi synagogue in Jerusalem. He recorded that the synagogue was founded with donations from Sir Abdullah Meir Sassoon and his brothers Eliyahu, Reuven, Avraham Shalom, and Sliman — sons of Sir David Sassoon — through the intermediation of the author and R' Zalman ben R' Nachum Yosef.

title_en: Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek founded in Jerusalem
summary_en: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Nae founded Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in Jerusalem for kollel avreichim to study Chassidus two hours daily.
story_body: After WWI, exiles of Eretz Yisrael returned home, with Hebron's community largely resettling in Jerusalem. Upon his return from Egypt, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Nae launched the yeshiva as part of his repair work for Kollel Chabad. The yeshiva convened in the Beit Menachem Tzemach Tzedek synagogue, fulfilling the Rebbe Rashab's wish to bind kollel scholars to regular Chassidus study.

title_en: Letter to Rebbe Rayatz describing founding of Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva
summary_en: R. Menachem Mendel Nae wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz detailing the founding and program of Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek in Jerusalem.
story_body: Writing on 18 Sivan 5682, Rabbi Nae reported he had returned to his post at the kollel in Tevet 5680 and secured a 15 pound sterling monthly budget. The funds enabled avreichim and bachurim from various Jerusalem yeshivot to gather twice daily at Beit Menachem Tzemach Tzedek for structured Chassidus study. The yeshiva was thereby named Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek.

title_en: Kollel Chabad signs agreement with Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva managers
summary_en: Yeshiva managers signed an agreement with Kollel Chabad's leadership regulating fundraising for the yeshiva and the kollel.
story_body: On 25 Sivan an agreement clarified that the gathering of scholars studying Chassidus daily at Beit Menachem—founded by the kollel in 5680—would remain the kollel's institution and property. It would continue to be called Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek as printed in the yearly calendar. All internal and external affairs would be conducted under the kollel managers' directives.

title_en: Kollel Chabad sends summary of Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva to Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: Kollel Chabad's leadership submitted a protocol and roster of 22 Tzemach Tzedek students to the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: The 19 Adar I 5698 protocol included a short overview of the yeshiva and a list of its students with their stipends. The report described the institution as fulfilling the Rebbe Rashab's wish to bind kollel scholars to Chassidus study and to memorialize donors through Mishnah study. The 22 students were avreichim from various Jerusalem kollelim spending two hours daily at Beit Menachem.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz requests detailed roster of Tzemach Tzedek students
summary_en: On 3 Menachem Av 5698 the Rebbe Rayatz asked Kollel Chabad for detailed information on each Tzemach Tzedek student.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote requesting names, ages, family situation, intellectual capacities, duration of study in revealed Torah and Chassidus, and how long each student had been at Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek. The letter reflects his close attention to the Jerusalem institution and ongoing concern for the spiritual development of its students.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Tzemach Tzedek yeshiva students
summary_en: On 11 Iyar 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the students of Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek urging them to spread Torah study.
story_body: The Rebbe asked about their fixed Chassidus learning schedule on weekdays and Shabbat and instructed them to study his recently delivered maamarim. He emphasized that each student of Tzemach Tzedek must create an atmosphere of Torah study around himself. He blessed them and their families with health, livelihood, and protection from trouble.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz responds to R. Nissan Horowitz on Tzemach Tzedek learning
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz replied on 17 Elul 5701 expressing satisfaction with the Chassidus learning at Yeshivat Tzemach Tzedek.
story_body: Responding to a detailed letter from mashpia R. Nissan Horowitz dated 22 Sivan, the Rebbe expressed great pleasure at the description of Chassidus study at the yeshiva. He blessed the students that their learning should bear fruit in heartfelt service through prayer. The exchange shows the close ongoing supervision the Rebbe Rayatz maintained over the Jerusalem yeshiva.

title_en: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Nae returns to Jerusalem to rebuild Yeshivat Torat Emet
summary_en: Returning to Jerusalem, R. Avraham Chaim Nae took the initiative to reestablish Yeshivat Torat Emet there.
story_body: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Nae joined SiLA and R. Moshe Aryeh Leib Shapira to issue a public appeal to revive the yeshiva originally established by the Rebbe Rashab in Hebron. Rabbi Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov, who had returned from his wartime exile, was enlisted to lead the yeshiva based on the Rebbe Rashab's mandate. The appeal stressed completing what they had begun in the holy work of rebuilding Torat Emet.

title_en: Yeshivat Torat Emet reestablished in Jerusalem
summary_en: Yeshivat Torat Emet was reopened in Jerusalem in 5682 after its Hebron branch had been completely disbanded.
story_body: Kollel Chabad's leadership wrote to R. D.M. Rabinovitch of Boston that the Hebron Torat Emet yeshiva had ceased entirely and could not yet be reconstituted there. Rabbi Eliezerov together with two distinguished avreichim were establishing the yeshiva anew in Jerusalem according to the Rebbe Rashab's original plan. Donors were urged to support the renewed institution.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to RashZ Hablin about Yeshivat Torat Emet
summary_en: On 19 Cheshvan 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz informed RashZ Hablin he was being sent to direct Yeshivat Torat Emet in Jerusalem.
story_body: Anash in America had inquired about the signatories of the public appeal to rebuild Torat Emet and whether the Rebbe was still its director. The Rebbe Rayatz replied that the signatories were former students of the institution and that RashZ Hablin had been dispatched to Eretz Yisrael to take charge of Torat Emet. The letter clarified institutional authority during the transition.

title_en: Death of RashZ Hablin
summary_en: RashZ Hablin, the director of Yeshivat Torat Emet in Jerusalem, passed away in 5696.
story_body: SiLA later recounted to RashZ Hablin's sons the early days of the yeshiva's reestablishment, describing how on the day of his arrival in Jerusalem he had been given a note from the Rebbe Rayatz indicating that Hablin alone should direct the institution. SiLA helped him in good faith with all that was needed for the yeshiva.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz besieged in Warsaw during German invasion
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz spent most of the winter of 5700 trapped in besieged Warsaw before being rescued to Riga and then America.
story_body: As WWII engulfed Europe, funding from abroad to Yeshivat Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv nearly ceased. The Rebbe Rayatz himself spent much of the winter caught in the siege of Warsaw until divine assistance enabled his escape from the persecutors to Riga and onward to America. The crisis severely disrupted communication and support for Chabad institutions in Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: Achei Tmimim students escape Otwock through Vilna to America
summary_en: Some students of the Achei Tmimim yeshiva in Otwock fled to Vilna and were rescued via Russia, Japan, and China to America.
story_body: With the Rebbe Rayatz's rescue from Warsaw, part of the Otwock yeshiva's students escaped to Vilna. From there they were saved through Russia, Japan, and China, eventually reaching the United States and Canada. The dispersal made it impossible to send support to the Tel Aviv yeshiva from abroad.

title_en: R. Sholom Noach Berzovsky appointed RaM at Achei Tmimim Tel Aviv
summary_en: Rabbi Sholom Noach Berzovsky—later the Slonimer Rebbe—was appointed RaM for the older class at Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv during 5700.
story_body: When external funding nearly collapsed and the yeshiva nonetheless flourished with growing enrollment, the administration restructured staff. R. Shaul Bruk was named mashpia in addition to his roles as RaM and supervisor, while R. Berzovsky was newly appointed for the senior class. R. Nissan Eber remained with the younger class, allowing the yeshiva to continue functioning that year.

title_en: Anonymous donor begins funding Achei Tmimim children's class
summary_en: An anonymous monthly donor was secured for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim in Tel Aviv at the start of 5701.
story_body: The funds enabled hiring R. Refael Nachman HaKohen to teach the small children ages 6-9; the yeshiva then had about 25 students. The anonymous donor, revealed later, was Baruch Eliyahu Schneersohn, son of the holy R. Mendel of Babruysk, a truly God-fearing man and great philanthropist. He insisted his identity remain unpublicized.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz responds about Achei Tmimim Tel Aviv leadership
summary_en: On 23 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote seven letters about the reorganization of Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Tel Aviv.
story_body: The Rebbe expressed great pleasure at the appointment of two committees—financial and spiritual—to assist director R. Eliezer Karasik. He acknowledged the institution's difficult material situation and committed to borrowing funds to send support, despite uncertainty about repayment. He sent personal greetings to each RaM, mashpia, teacher, and committee member by name.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz describes financial difficulty supporting Achei Tmimim
summary_en: On 29 Tishrei 5702 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that he had no source from which to take funds for the yeshiva.
story_body: The Rebbe explained that even prior sums sent to Achei Tmimim had been borrowed and remained unpaid. He nonetheless committed to sending 200 shekels soon to ease their debt burden but stated he could not undertake regular monthly support. The letter reflects the severe financial straits during wartime.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz sends 150 shekels to Achei Tmimim by telegraphic transfer
summary_en: On 21 Cheshvan 5702 the Rebbe Rayatz sent 150 shekels via R. Moshe Gurary to Yeshivat Achei Tmimim.
story_body: The Rebbe described the transfer as coming not from any cash reserve but from his 'trust fund' confident that God would help him repay. The letter highlights the personal sacrifice involved in sustaining the Tel Aviv yeshiva during WWII when normal channels of support had collapsed.

title_en: Chabad community established in Jerusalem
summary_en: The Chabad community in Jerusalem was established in the year 5607.
story_body: The founding of the Chabad presence in Jerusalem marked the beginning of an institutional infrastructure that would soon include trustees, census records, and ties to philanthropists abroad. By 5609 a formal census listed Rabbi Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin and Rabbi Uri Orenstein as appointed trustees. They would also sign the 5609 letter to Sir Moses Montefiore as the trustees of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem.

title_en: Kollel Chabad letter to Montefiore signed by Jerusalem trustees
summary_en: Rabbis Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin and Uri Orenstein signed as trustees of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem in the letter to Montefiore.
story_body: The 5609 census listed Rabbi Eliyahu Yosef Rivlin and Rabbi Uri Orenstein as the trustees of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem. The same two trustees signed the kollel's letter to Sir Moses Montefiore that year.
