summary_en: In winter 5710, six senior students of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Tel Aviv received permission from the Rebbe Rayatz to travel to the Central Yeshiva in New York.
story_body: Six older students from the Tel Aviv branch of Tomchei Tmimim received approval from the Rebbe Rayatz to relocate for advanced study at the central yeshiva in New York. The approval letters were later printed in Igrot Kodesh vol. 10 (letters 3640-3641). They departed in Tevet 5710 and arrived in New York.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim students arrive in New York
summary_en: In Tevet 5710 the six Tel Aviv yeshiva students reached New York to study at the central Lubavitch yeshiva.
story_body: After receiving the Rebbe Rayatz's approval, the six older students from Tel Aviv traveled overseas and arrived in New York during Tevet 5710. They had come from Eretz Yisrael, having studied in Tel Aviv before the wave of refugees arrived from Russia in 5709.

title_en: Ramash directs Tel Aviv students to remain studying in New York
summary_en: In Shvat 5710, after the passing of the Rebbe Rayatz on 10 Shvat, the Ramash instructed the six visiting students to remain learning in New York.
story_body: The six students from the Tel Aviv yeshiva had only just arrived in New York when the Rebbe Rayatz passed away on 10 Shvat 5710. Despite the changed circumstances, the Ramash (later the Rebbe) directed them to remain at the central yeshiva and continue their studies there.

title_en: Rebbe's letter recommending move of Tel Aviv yeshiva to Lod
summary_en: On the seventh night of Chanukah 5710 the Ramash wrote endorsing the proposal to relocate the Tel Aviv yeshiva to its Lod campus.
story_body: Mashpia R' Shmuel Chaim Kesselman had suggested moving the yeshiva from noisy Tel Aviv to the quieter Lod campus near the railway station. On the seventh night of Chanukah the Ramash replied (Igrot Kodesh vol. 4, letter 842) strongly endorsing the move, citing the Rebbe Rayatz's praise of the calm environment of Lubavitch over big-city yeshivot, while recommending that one class remain in Tel Aviv as a feeder.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim's main class moves from Tel Aviv to Lod
summary_en: After Pesach 5711 the main division of the Tel Aviv yeshiva moved to the Lod campus by the railway station.
story_body: Following the Rebbe's endorsement, after Pesach 5711 the main shiur of the Tel Aviv yeshiva relocated to the existing Lod campus. Only the local 'Bnei Tmimim' children's cheder remained in Tel Aviv; once those boys finished cheder they moved on to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Lod.

title_en: R' Shmuel Chaim Kesselman reports new arrangement at Lod yeshiva
summary_en: On 8 Iyar 5711 the mashpia R' Shmuel Chaim Kesselman reported that the consolidated yeshiva at Lod was operating with about forty students.
story_body: On 8 Iyar 5711 R' Shmuel Chaim Kesselman wrote that as of Rosh Chodesh Iyar, the study schedule at Tomchei Tmimim at the Lod railway station was running well. The students transferred from Tel Aviv joined the older students already there plus the senior shiur, totalling about forty students all housed together in one large multi-room building suitable for study, meals, and lodging.

title_en: Hebron Chabad community signs authorization for kollel emissaries
summary_en: On 15 Shvat 5603 the leaders of the Hebron Chabad community signed a power of attorney appointing R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov and R' Moshe Shmerling to litigate against the Perushim community.
story_body: The administrators and overseers of the Chabad community in Hebron, joined by the seven communal trustees, formally appointed R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov and R' Moshe Shmerling as their representatives to negotiate and litigate with the Perushim kollel leadership in Jerusalem regarding shared funds from Hungary and Vienna. They were also empowered to settle outstanding claims with the community's own emissary R' Moshe ben David Yaffe.

title_en: R' David Leib Yaffe of Hebron passes away in Jerusalem
summary_en: R' David Leib ben Moshe Yaffe, born in Eretz Yisrael to a Hebron Chabad family, died in Jerusalem on 3 Cheshvan 5670.
story_body: R' David Leib was the son of the emissary R' Moshe ben David Yaffe of Hebron and was born in Eretz Yisrael, listed as a child of three in the 5599 census and as age 31 in the 5626 census. He later moved to live in Jerusalem, where he passed away on 3 Cheshvan 5670, his death recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' vol. 12.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek instructs family members to settle in Hebron
summary_en: Around 5604 the Tzemach Tzedek directed several relatives to make aliyah and settle in Hebron, becoming the foundation of the Chabad community there.
story_body: Around 5604 the Tzemach Tzedek instructed several members of his family to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael and settle in Hebron. Three granddaughters of the Alter Rebbe came from Lubavitch with their families: Menucha Rachel (daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe) with R' Yaakov Slonim, Sarah Rivka with R' Nachum Yosef Schneersohn, and Rachel with R' Moshe Tzvi Pundeminsky. They became the cornerstone of the Chabad settlement in Hebron.

title_en: R' Yaakov 'Kuli' Slonim passes away in Hebron
summary_en: R' Yaakov (Kuli) Slonim, husband of Menucha Rachel and a leader of the Hebron community, died on 2 Tevet 5617.
story_body: R' Yaakov Slonim, married to Menucha Rachel daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, served as gabbai of the Hebron synagogue and chazzan on the High Holidays. He headed both the Chevra Kadisha and the Gemilut Chasadim society in Hebron. He passed away on 2 Tevet 5617, leaving three sons and three daughters.

title_en: Sheterna Riza and R' Shalom Kaznovsky make aliyah to Hebron
summary_en: In 5620-5621 Sheterna Riza Slonim and her husband R' Shalom Kaznovsky immigrated to Hebron by order of the Tzemach Tzedek.
story_body: Sheterna Riza, eldest daughter of Menucha Rachel and R' Yaakov Slonim, had married R' Shalom Kaznovsky abroad before her parents' aliyah. In 5620-5621, following the directive of the Tzemach Tzedek, the couple themselves made aliyah to Hebron. Their son R' Eliezer Shimon was already married at the time and remained abroad temporarily.

title_en: R' Eliezer Shimon Kaznovsky and family settle in Hebron
summary_en: In 5633 R' Eliezer Shimon Kaznovsky immigrated with his family to Hebron, accompanied by his grandson R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov.
story_body: R' Eliezer Shimon Kaznovsky, son of Sheterna Riza Slonim, made aliyah from abroad with his family in 5633 and settled in Hebron. His grandson R' Shlomo Yehuda Leib Eliezerov (known as Shila) came with him and would go on to become a leader of the Hebron community, its rabbi, and an administrator of Kollel Chabad from 5663 onward.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn (Shazbani) passes away
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman ben Nachum Yosef Schneersohn, author of Nimukei Shazbani, died in the winter of 5642 leaving young orphans.
story_body: R' Shneur Zalman ben Nachum Yosef Schneersohn (known by his initials Shazbani), author of Nimukei Shazbani and other works, died in the winter of 5642 in Hebron. He left behind several adult daughters and minor orphan sons. The beit din, together with his brothers Chaim Tzvi and Pinchas, appointed two trustees over his estate to act on behalf of the orphans, including reaching settlements with his daughters.

title_en: R' Yitzchak ben Aharon of Königsberg, donor of Ohel Yitzchak, dies
summary_en: R' Yitzchak ben Aharon, the Königsberg shochet who funded the Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash in Meah Shearim, passed away on 15 Kislev 5666.
story_body: R' Yitzchak ben Aharon, a shochet from Königsberg, together with his wife Breina, donated the funds to build the magnificent Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash in Meah Shearim, named for him. He also funded four kollel houses adjacent to it that were allotted by lottery to needy Chabad families every three years. He passed away on 15 Kislev 5666 as recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' vol. 12.

title_en: Report on attendance at Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash
summary_en: In mid-Tamuz 5663 Kollel Chabad director R' Yehuda Leib Menuchin reported that only five Anash plus about ten other Jews were studying at Ohel Yitzchak.
story_body: R' Yehuda Leib Menuchin, the administrator of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem, wrote in mid-Tamuz 5663 that he had sent the shamash Shalom Yaakov to Ohel Yitzchak the previous Shabbat to attend R' Yaakov ben Tzvi Trisspolsky's class and report on activity there. The report counted five Chabad members and more than ten other Jews regularly present in the beit medrash. Attendance would later grow significantly as Jews moved from the Old City to the new neighborhoods.

title_en: Publication of Chukei Chevrat Binyan Yehuda VehaGalil
summary_en: In 5663 the Jerusalem society for building shelters for needy Kollel Chabad members in Jerusalem and Hebron published its bylaws, documenting the Ohel Yitzchak gift.
story_body: In Jerusalem 5663 a small 18-page pamphlet entitled 'Sefer Chukei Chevrat Binyan Yehuda VehaGalil' was published, setting out the rules of the society that built shelters for the poor of Kollel Chabad in Jerusalem and Hebron. The booklet records R' Yitzchak ben Aharon's donations for the Ohel Yitzchak beit medrash in Meah Shearim and for four adjacent kollel houses, distributed to families by lottery every three years.

title_en: R' Moshe Meisels of Hebron passes away
summary_en: R' Moshe Meisels, a senior figure of the Hebron Chabad community, died in Menachem Av 5609.
story_body: R' Moshe Meisels was one of the leading signatories of Hebron Chabad emissary documents in the 1840s. He passed away in the month of Menachem Av 5609, a fact later used to redate undated communal documents bearing his signature to before that point.

title_en: R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov's Pesach letter from Shklov
summary_en: On Erev Pesach 5606 the Hebron emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov wrote from Shklov to Dr. Eliezer Halevi, Montefiore's secretary, reporting his fundraising progress.
story_body: From Shklov on Erev Pesach 5606, the Hebron Chabad emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov wrote to Dr. Eliezer Halevi, secretary to Sir Moses Montefiore (letter published in Kerem Chabad vol. 2). He reported that he had already, in the previous Kislev, transmitted via Vilna to Sir Moses some 600 rubles (roughly 200 guineas) intended to reach Hebron via Damascus, and announced his plan to return home after the festival.

title_en: Sir Moses Montefiore transfers 600 rubles to Hebron Chabad
summary_en: In Kislev 5606 emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov routed 600 rubles for Hebron Chabad through Vilna to Sir Moses Montefiore and on to Damascus.
story_body: During Kislev 5606, the Hebron Chabad emissary R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov forwarded 600 rubles, equivalent to about 200 guineas, from Shklov via Vilna to Sir Moses Montefiore. The funds were to be transmitted to Damascus and from there to the Chabad community in Hebron, demonstrating the cross-continental philanthropic network supporting the kollel.

title_en: R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov sent as Hebron Chabad emissary
summary_en: Around 5604 the Hebron Chabad community sent R' Yosef Yehuda Mashiov of Shklov abroad as their emissary, charged with collecting funds and conveying their hardships.
story_body: Around 5604 the Hebron Chabad community appointed R' Yosef Yehuda Leib Mashiov of Shklov as their emissary to collect previously gathered donations and to inform Diaspora Jewry of the suffering they had endured in those years. The mission also reflected his personal need, as his son had reached marriageable age. He served two years on this mission, returning in the summer of 5606.

title_en: R' Moshe Yaffe travels as Tiberias chassidim emissary
summary_en: In 5606 R' Moshe ben David Yaffe undertook an additional emissary mission, this one on behalf of the chassidim of Tiberias.
story_body: R' Moshe ben David Yaffe, listed in the 5609 census as a talmid chacham and emissary, undertook a second mission in 5606. This later mission was on behalf of the chassidic community of Tiberias rather than Hebron, as documented in 'Shluchei Eretz Yisrael' p. 788.

title_en: R' Moshe ben David Yaffe immigrates from Shklov
summary_en: R' Moshe ben David Yaffe immigrated to Eretz Yisrael from Shklov in 5580.
story_body: According to the 5599 census, R' Moshe ben David, then aged 30, had immigrated from Shklov to Eretz Yisrael in 5580. He was married with two sons at the time of the census and would later serve as an emissary for the Hebron Chabad community and subsequently for the chassidim of Tiberias.

title_en: R' Uri sent as Hebron Chabad emissary
summary_en: R' Uri served as an emissary of the Hebron Chabad community in 5601.
story_body: From 5601 onward R' Uri is known as an emissary of the Hebron Chabad community, one of several shaderim sent abroad in that period to collect funds and convey the community's needs to Diaspora donors.

title_en: Death of R' Yehuda Leib, great-grandson of the Maharal of Prague
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib, son of R' Shmuel and great-grandson of the Maharal of Prague, died in Tishrei 5466.
story_body: According to the Prague tombstone records compiled by R' Sinai Hock, R' Yehuda Leib ben R' Shmuel (grandson of R' Bezalel, the Maharal's only son) died in Tishrei 5466. This discovery overturned the long-held claim by R' Meir Pereles and others that R' Shmuel left only daughters, and helped establish the Alter Rebbe's descent from the Maharal through his great-great-grandfather R' Yehuda Leib of Posen.

title_en: R' Meir Pereles completes Megillat Yuchasin in Prague
summary_en: R' Meir Pereles of Prague finished his genealogical work Megillat Yuchasin in 5487.
story_body: Megillat Yuchasin, a key source on the descendants of the Maharal of Prague, was written by R' Meir Pereles in 5487 (he states 'until today, which is the year 5487'). The work omitted the male line through R' Yehuda Leib ben R' Shmuel, an omission that later researchers had to correct using Prague gravestone evidence.

title_en: R' Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe, joins Liozna Chevra Kadisha
summary_en: R' Baruch ben R' Avraham was accepted into the Liozna burial society on 15 Kislev 5507.
story_body: The Liozna communal register records that on 15 Kislev 5507 (December 8, 1746), 'the Torah scholar Moreinu Baruch ben Moreinu Avraham was accepted into the Chevra Kadisha.' This entry is one of the earliest documentary anchors for the Alter Rebbe's father and identifies his own father's name as Avraham, contradicting other traditions that named him Shneur Zalman.

title_en: Birth of MaharI"L of Yanovich, brother of the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib of Yanovich, younger brother of the Alter Rebbe, was born approximately in 5509.
story_body: MaharI"L of Yanovich, author of Shearit Yehuda and constant collaborator of his brother the Alter Rebbe, was born around 5509 (~1749). He would become the household manager of the Alter Rebbe's affairs, the chief transcriber of his discourses (later printed in Torah Or), and editor of his Shulchan Aruch.

title_en: Young Shneur Zalman accepted into Liozna Chevra Kadisha
summary_en: The child Shneur Zalman ben R' Baruch was inducted into the Liozna burial society on 15 Kislev 5510.
story_body: The Liozna ledger records that on 15 Kislev 5510 (December 5, 1749), 'the boy Shneur Zalman ben Moreinu Baruch was accepted into the Chevra Kadisha,' with his grandfather obligated to make annual donations on his behalf. This entry is a key biographical anchor for the future Alter Rebbe's earliest years in Liozna.

title_en: Marriage of the Mitteler Rebbe
summary_en: Dovber Schneuri, later the Mitteler Rebbe, was married in 5548.
story_body: The future Mitteler Rebbe's wedding took place in 5548, a date deduced from the fact that his son R' Menachem Nochum was born after that year. The marriage is one of several family events that anchor the chronology of the Alter Rebbe's grandchildren born in 5549-5551.

title_en: Birth of the Tzemach Tzedek
summary_en: R' Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the future Tzemach Tzedek, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550.
story_body: The Tzemach Tzedek, third Chabad Rebbe and author of monumental halachic and Chassidic works, was born on Erev Rosh Hashanah 5550 (September 19, 1789) to R' Shalom Shachna and Devorah Leah (daughter of the Alter Rebbe). He was raised by his grandfather the Alter Rebbe after his mother's early death.

title_en: Death of R' Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: R' Yisrael Baruch ben Avraham, father of the Alter Rebbe, died on 8 Tishrei 5552 in Sulish, Hungary.
story_body: After self-exile in his later years, R' Baruch settled in the town of Sulish (Sulish/Sulez) in Hungary, where he died on 8 Tishrei 5552 (September 16, 1791). His tombstone inscription records his name as 'Yisrael Baruch ben Avraham' — supporting the tradition reported in Eden Tzion that he originally bore the name Yisrael but dropped it after joining the Baal Shem Tov's circle out of deference to his teacher.

title_en: Alter Rebbe delivers the 'Frumer Vaera' discourse
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe delivered the famous 'Frumer Vaera' discourse on Shabbat Parshat Vaera 5554.
story_body: The discourse known as 'Der Frumer Vaera,' given on Shabbat Parshat Vaera 5554 (January 1794), survived in MaharI"L's transcript with handwritten glosses by the Alter Rebbe himself — one of the very few such doubly-authenticated manuscripts to reach later generations. It became a touchstone for understanding how the Alter Rebbe edited the discourses his brother recorded for him.

title_en: MaharI"L co-signs psher ruling for Horodishtch community
summary_en: MaharI"L signed a community settlement document at the Alter Rebbe's direction on 25 Tevet 5556.
story_body: On 25 Tevet 5556 (January 5, 1796), MaharI"L of Yanovich signed a written compromise ruling for the community of Horodishtch, noting that 'all the above was done by law and by settlement, as my brother and master the Rabbi instructed me, with the consent of the entire community.' The document, preserved in the genizah, shows the Alter Rebbe routing communal halachic work through his trusted younger brother.

title_en: Printing of Amudei Gola in Ladi with the Alter Rebbe's approbation
summary_en: The book Amudei Gola was printed in Ladi in 5565 with the Alter Rebbe's approbation.
story_body: The Ladi printing house, operated in part by R' Baruch ben Eliyahu, produced Amudei Gola in 5565 (1805) carrying the Alter Rebbe's haskama. The same printer would issue Tanya the following year in Shklov, and his role has often been confused in the literature with that of a grandson of the Alter Rebbe.

title_en: R' Baruch ben Eliyahu prints Tanya in Shklov
summary_en: The printer R' Baruch ben Eliyahu issued an edition of Tanya in Shklov in 5566.
story_body: In 5566 (1806) the Shklov printer R' Baruch ben Eliyahu, working with his partner R' Yitzchak ben Shmuel, brought Tanya to press. Earlier authorities mistakenly identified this printer as a grandson of the Alter Rebbe (son of Freida); in fact he was the well-known printer who had previously worked in Shklov, Dubrovna and Ladi.

title_en: R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz studies with MaharI"L in Yanovich
summary_en: MaharI"L of Yanovich taught R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz in 5572, confirming he was settled in Yanovich by that year.
story_body: R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz, who later served ten years as rabbi of Lubavitch, recorded that he heard a particular teaching from MaharI"L 'while studying with him in 5572.' This testimony fixes the earliest documented year for MaharI"L's residence in Yanovich, where he served as moreh tzedek.

title_en: Three-judge din Torah in Lubavitch
summary_en: A din Torah convened in Lubavitch in 5577 with MaharI"L, the Mitteler Rebbe, and R' Chaim Avraham.
story_body: In 5577 (1816/17) a rabbinical court sat in Lubavitch composed of MaharI"L of Yanovich, the Mitteler Rebbe, and his brother R' Chaim Avraham. The proceedings, preserved in the genizah, illustrate how MaharI"L continued to anchor halachic decision-making in the Chabad center even after the Alter Rebbe's death.

title_en: MaharI"L approbates Kapust edition of the Siddur
summary_en: In 5582 MaharI"L gave his approbation to the Kapust printing of the Alter Rebbe's siddur.
story_body: The 5582 (1822) Kapust edition of the Alter Rebbe's siddur, produced by the printer R' Yisrael Yaffe, carried MaharI"L's published haskama. The approbation was one of MaharI"L's continuing roles as guardian of his late brother's textual legacy.

title_en: Joint psak by Tzemach Tzedek and MaharI"L in Lubavitch
summary_en: In Elul 5583 the Tzemach Tzedek and MaharI"L of Yanovich co-signed a halachic ruling in Lubavitch.
story_body: A teshuva and psak written and co-signed in Lubavitch in Elul 5583 (August-September 1823) by MaharI"L and the Tzemach Tzedek, printed in Shearit Yehuda Even Haezer §5, documents their collaborative halachic work during the Mitteler Rebbe's tenure.

title_en: Death of MaharI"L of Yanovich
summary_en: MaharI"L of Yanovich died between late 5585 and the end of Adar I 5586.
story_body: MaharI"L's death can be bracketed by two letters: a responsum the Tzemach Tzedek addressed to him in late summer 5585, and a letter from R' Yissachar Ber Horowitz dated 28 Adar I 5586 (March 1826) that already refers to him as 'the late.' He was buried in Yanovich, where local residents long revered his memory.

title_en: Simcha Kisin denounces the Mitteler Rebbe
summary_en: Simcha Kisin, a relative of the Mitteler Rebbe, denounced him to the authorities in 5586.
story_body: Simcha Kisin — son of R' Lipman Kisin, parnas of Vitebsk and cousin of the Alter Rebbe's wife Sterna — turned informant against the Mitteler Rebbe in 5586 (1826). The denunciation led to the well-known arrest and release recorded in Maasar U'Geulat Admur Ha'emtza'i, despite the family's earlier closeness to the Rebbe's household.

title_en: Shearit Yehuda published in Vilna by MaharI"L's grandson
summary_en: Shearit Yehuda, MaharI"L's halachic work, was brought to press by his grandson R' Ze'ev Wolf in 5601.
story_body: In 5601 (1841), R' Ze'ev Wolf, grandson of MaharI"L (through his son R' Yeshaya), brought to press Shearit Yehuda — MaharI"L's collected rulings on melicha together with extensive responsa, glosses on his brother the Alter Rebbe's writings, and oral teachings transmitted in his name.

title_en: Beginning of Chabad settlement in the Holy Land
summary_en: Chabad aliyah to Eretz Yisrael begins in 5537.
story_body: The Chabad presence in the Land of Israel traces to 5537 (1777), when the first Chassidic settlers arrived. This year became the starting point used in the companion volume 'Toldot Chabad B'Eretz HaKodesh,' which covers the history of the movement in the Holy Land through 5710.

title_en: Beginning of Chabad settlement in the United States
summary_en: Chabad settlement in America begins in 5660.
story_body: The companion volume 'Toldot Chabad B'Artzot HaBrit' opens with the first Chabad settlement in the United States in 5660 (1900), tracing the movement's growth in America through 5710 (1950).

title_en: Soviet rule begins in Russia
summary_en: Soviet rule begins in 5678, opening the era covered by Toldot Chabad in Soviet Russia.
story_body: The Soviet regime took hold in 5678 (1918), launching a generation of underground Chabad activity. The companion volume 'Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit' covers the movement under Soviet rule from this year through 5710.

title_en: Passing of the Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: The sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, R' Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, passed away in 5710.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz's passing in 5710 (1950) marks the closing date for the first three companion volumes of Toldot Chabad — covering the movement in the Holy Land, the United States, and Soviet Russia respectively — each of which ends with his lifetime.

title_en: Sh. D. Levin begins editing Igrot Kodesh series
summary_en: In 5740, the Lubavitcher Rebbe assigned R' Shalom DovBer Levin the editing of Igrot Kodesh of the Chabad Rebbes.
story_body: Starting in 5740 (1980), at the Lubavitcher Rebbe's directive, R' Shalom DovBer Levin began assembling and editing the Igrot Kodesh series of the Chabad Rebbes' letters. The historical research generated by this editorial work became the seed material for the Toldot Chabad volumes — including this one on Tsarist Russia.

title_en: Author visits Jerusalem and consults genealogist Shmuel Gur
summary_en: Sh. D. Levin visited Jerusalem in summer 5746 and discussed Maharal-descent genealogy with R' Shmuel Gur.
story_body: During a summer 5746 (1986) visit to Jerusalem, R' Sh. D. Levin consulted the genealogist R' Shmuel Gur on the disputed question of whether R' Shmuel ben Bezalel (grandson of the Maharal) had any sons. Gur pointed him to a Prague tombstone inscription that resolved the question and validated the Rebbe Rayatz's family tradition.

title_en: Publication of Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaTza'arit
summary_en: Sh. D. Levin signs the preface to Toldot Chabad B'Russia HaTza'arit in Brooklyn on 12 Tammuz 5770.
story_body: The fourth volume of the Toldot Chabad series, covering Tsarist Russia in selected chapters across the first five generations of Chabad leadership, was completed in Brooklyn on 12 Tammuz 5770 (June 24, 2010) and published by Otzar HaChassidim at 770 Eastern Parkway. The preface acknowledges R' Yitzchak Wilhelm and R' Dovid Moshe Olidort for their editorial review.

title_en: Maggid of Mezeritch grants approbation to 'Halakhah Pesukah' (Turka)
summary_en: The Maggid of Mezeritch issued his only known approbation, for the halachic work 'Halakhah Pesukah' printed in Turka.
story_body: The Maggid, who normally declined to give approbations, made an exception for 'Halakhah Pesukah' because of its value in clarifying practical halachic rulings. The approbation testifies to his deep concern for clear and accessible psak halacha among his circle and is the only such endorsement of his preserved to us.

title_en: Alter Rebbe arrives at the Maggid of Mezeritch around age 20
summary_en: Around the age of 20, R. Schneur Zalman traveled from Vitebsk to study Kabbalah and chassidut under the Maggid of Mezeritch.
story_body: After exhausting available sources of knowledge in revealed Torah, the future Alter Rebbe sought a teacher of inner Torah. Around age twenty he left his father-in-law's home in Vitebsk to study under the Maggid, where he found 'rest for his soul' and was eventually entrusted with composing a new Shulchan Aruch.

title_en: Alter Rebbe begins composing the Shulchan Aruch HaRav
summary_en: After being pressed repeatedly by the Maggid of Mezeritch, the young Alter Rebbe began work on his Shulchan Aruch after the year 1770.
story_body: The Maggid searched among his disciples for one who could compose a clear, reasoned compendium of halachic rulings and chose the young Schneur Zalman, refusing to relent until he agreed. Composition of the Shulchan Aruch HaRav began after 5530, becoming the authoritative halachic work of Chabad.

title_en: Brothers R. Shmelke and R. Pinchas Horowitz praise Alter Rebbe's halachic writings
summary_en: While studying together at the Maggid's court, R. Shmelke and R. Pinchas Horowitz reviewed and praised the Alter Rebbe's nascent halachic writings.
story_body: The 'two golden pipes' — the brothers Horowitz — joined the Maggid's circle and examined two halachic works the young Alter Rebbe had composed. They praised him highly and urged him to 'be strong and complete the work,' showing that halachic study was part of the curriculum at Mezeritch alongside chassidic teaching.

title_en: Alter Rebbe meets R. Pinchas of the Hafla'ah at Rovno
summary_en: By Tishrei 1771 the Maggid had relocated to Rovno, where the Alter Rebbe encountered R. Pinchas Horowitz, author of the Hafla'ah.
story_body: The Alter Rebbe's later letter recalls a 'beloved acquaintance from days past in Mezeritch and Rovno' with R. Pinchas Horowitz. Since R. Pinchas left for the Frankfurt rabbinate by Tishrei 1771, the meeting at Rovno must have occurred no later than that date — establishing that the Maggid had already moved from Mezeritch to Rovno by then.

title_en: Winter 1772: Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel attempt debate with Vilna Gaon
summary_en: During the winter of 1772 the Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk traveled to Vilna seeking a debate with the Vilna Gaon, who refused to meet them.
story_body: Hoping to refute the slanders being told to the Vilna Gaon and forestall a herem against chassidim, the two emissaries went to his home twice and were turned away each time. When city leaders pressed the Gaon to debate, he left the city and only returned after they had departed.

title_en: Winter 1772: Shklov debate between Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk
summary_en: After the failed Vilna mission, the Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk traveled to Shklov for a public debate with mitnagdim, which ended badly for the chassidim.
story_body: The mitnagdim of Shklov broke prior assurances and confronted the chassidic leaders with force. Unable to answer the chassidic arguments, they appealed back to the Vilna Gaon, who then leaned toward declaring chassidim as 'moridin' — kindling the wider campaign against the movement.

title_en: Summer 1772: 'Zemir Aritzim v'Charvot Tzurim' published in Brody
summary_en: Mitnagdim in Vilna sent material to Brody where the polemical 'Zemir Aritzim v'Charvot Tzurim' against the chassidim was printed in late summer 1772.
story_body: Following the Shklov debate, the sages of Shklov wrote to the Vilna Gaon, who in turn coordinated with Brody. The resulting pamphlet attacked chassidic practices — including the upside-down acrobatics ('koliyen zich') of R. Avraham of Kalisk's circle — and triggered widespread persecution of the tzaddikim of Volyn.

title_en: Summer 1772: Volyn tzaddikim convene at Rovno around the Maggid
summary_en: Driven from their homes by the campaign against chassidim, the tzaddikim of Volyn gathered in Rovno around the Maggid of Mezeritch to take counsel.
story_body: The Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk arrived together; R. Avraham, fearful of the Maggid's reproach, waited at the outskirts while R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk interceded on his behalf. Only then did the Alter Rebbe bring him into the Maggid's chamber. The gathering attempted to coordinate the chassidic response to the herem.

title_en: Summer 1772: Alter Rebbe's halachic deliberation with the Maggid in Rovno
summary_en: In summer 1772 at Rovno the Alter Rebbe debated with the Maggid the laws of sirkhot, with the Maggid ruling it sufficed to remove the protruding adhesion.
story_body: The Alter Rebbe's responsum on the leniency of R. Levi Yitzchok of Berditchev in checking lungs records this earlier discussion at Rovno. The Maggid demonstrated from the Talmud that residual filaments on the lung are not themselves a sirkha, illustrating how halacha was taught alongside chassidut in Mezeritch/Rovno.

title_en: Maggid of Mezeritch delivers final Sukkot teaching
summary_en: The Maggid of Mezeritch gave his last recorded Sukkot teaching in Tishrei 5533 (autumn 1772), preserved through the Alter Rebbe.
story_body: A maamar of the Alter Rebbe from 1812 cites a teaching he heard from the Maggid 'on the last Sukkot, 5533.' It is one of the latest surviving teachings of the Maggid before his passing two months later.

title_en: Passing of the Maggid of Mezeritch in Anipoli
summary_en: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezeritch, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533 in Anipoli, with the Alter Rebbe present at his passing.
story_body: After moving from Rovno to Anipoli, the Maggid passed on 19 Kislev. The Alter Rebbe is recorded as having been present, and the lot fell on him to perform the taharah and burial. The date later took on iconic significance in Chabad after the Alter Rebbe's release from imprisonment on the same date in 1798.

title_en: Aliyah of R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In 1777 R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a group of chassidim in aliyah to the Land of Israel, settling first in the north.
story_body: Following years of persecution and the mounting conflict with the mitnagdim, R. Menachem Mendel emigrated with a chassidic group to Eretz Yisrael, eventually settling in Tzfat. He would continue to guide the Russian chassidic community by letter from there.

title_en: R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk writes from Tzfat to chassidim of Vilna
summary_en: From Tzfat in 1778, R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote to the chassidim of Vilna recalling his unsuccessful efforts to be cleared in the eyes of the mitnagdim.
story_body: The letter calls on the Vilna chassidim as witnesses to his earlier attempts to reconcile and explain the chassidic position. It is among the foundational documents of the chassidic side of the early conflict, paralleling the Alter Rebbe's later epistles on the same theme.

title_en: Final letter of R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk to chassidim in Russia
summary_en: In early summer 1788 R. Menachem Mendel sent his last letter to the chassidim of Russia, designating the Alter Rebbe as their teacher and guide.
story_body: The letter describes how the Alter Rebbe wore down his feet traveling 'to seek God' and was 'anointed' to be moreh tzedek for the Russian community. Printed as the 22nd letter of Likutei Amarim/Tanya, it formally transferred leadership of the Russian chassidim to the Alter Rebbe.

title_en: Passing of R. Baruch, father of the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: R. Baruch, the father of the Alter Rebbe, passed away in Tishrei 5552 (autumn 1791).
story_body: Dating internal evidence in the Alter Rebbe's responsum on matza-baking practices relies on this yahrtzeit: since he still signs himself as 'son of my master and teacher R. Baruch,' the responsum predates Tishrei 5552, placing the change in matza-baking custom around 1772.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes letter to chassidim of Vilna defending the movement
summary_en: In 1797 the Alter Rebbe wrote to the chassidim of Vilna recounting the rebuffed attempts to debate the Vilna Gaon a quarter-century earlier.
story_body: The letter (Iggeret 34) is a key source for the early conflict, describing how the Vilna Gaon twice closed his door on R. Menachem Mendel and the Alter Rebbe and left town to avoid public debate. It frames the chassidic response to renewed persecution near the end of the century.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes again to Vilna chassidim describing flight to Rovno
summary_en: In summer 1798 the Alter Rebbe sent a second letter to the chassidim of Vilna recalling the 1772 gathering at Rovno around the Maggid.
story_body: The letter narrates how the Volyn tzaddikim, unable to remain in their homes amid persecution, fled to the Maggid in Rovno to plan a response. It supplements the earlier 1797 letter and reinforces the chassidic memory of the foundational conflict.

title_en: Alter Rebbe testifies under interrogation during his Petersburg imprisonment
summary_en: During his 1798 imprisonment, the Alter Rebbe testified that at about age twenty he had left Vitebsk for Mezeritch to study Kabbalah under the Maggid.
story_body: Among the autobiographical testimony recorded by the Russian authorities, the Alter Rebbe describes his discipleship of the Maggid as the formative period of his life. The recorded testimony is preserved in his collected letters and is a primary biographical source for his early years.

title_en: R. Avraham of Kalisk writes about the early 'talk' period
summary_en: An 1801 letter of R. Avraham of Kalisk references 'the whole matter of the talk' from his Kalisk period before emigrating.
story_body: The letter alludes to the boisterous, head-down behavior of the early Kalisk chassidim that had drawn fierce criticism from the mitnagdim. R. Avraham's remark contextualizes the practice as part of a passing early stage in chassidic development.

title_en: R. Chaim of Volozhin visits Belarus and discusses polished shechitah knives
summary_en: In 1803 R. Chaim of Volozhin, visiting Belarus, reported in the name of the Vilna Gaon that there was no halachic prohibition on polished shechitah knives.
story_body: Notables who were not chassidim heard from R. Chaim that the Vilna Gaon's ban on the chassidic-style polished shechitah knives had been issued as a 'distancing' measure against the chassidim, not as inherent halachic law. The Alter Rebbe cites this account in his 1811 epistle defending the practice.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes summer 1805 letter recounting Maggid's regard for him
summary_en: In summer 1805 the Alter Rebbe wrote a letter recounting how he and R. Avraham of Kalisk arrived in Rovno in 1772 and the latter feared meeting the Maggid.
story_body: The letter provides the most detailed first-person account of the 1772 Rovno gathering: R. Avraham waiting at the outskirts, R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk interceding, and the Alter Rebbe escorting him into the Maggid's chamber. It also defends the Alter Rebbe's status as a beloved disciple of the Maggid.

title_en: R. Levi Yitzchok of Berditchev passes away
summary_en: R. Levi Yitzchok of Berditchev passed away in 5570 (1810), after which questions on his lenient ruling on sirkhot were sent to the Alter Rebbe.
story_body: Late in life R. Levi Yitzchok had permitted certain sirkhot via squeezing, generating controversy among Berditchev rabbis. After his passing the queries on his ruling were referred to the Alter Rebbe, who defended R. Levi Yitzchok's psak in several responsa.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes Tishrei 1811 epistle on polished shechitah knives
summary_en: Late in his life, in 5571 (1811), the Alter Rebbe wrote a major epistle defending the chassidic enactment of polished shechitah knives.
story_body: The letter (Iggeret 61) reports R. Chaim of Volozhin's 1803 disclosure and lists the many regions and communities that had by then accepted the polished knives — including Ukraine, parts of Poland, Volyn, and the Holy Land. The enactment, instituted at the Maggid's beit midrash, eventually became universal Jewish practice.

title_en: Passing of the Alter Rebbe of Chabad
summary_en: R. Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe and founder of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573 (Dec 1812) during the flight from Napoleon's army.
story_body: The Alter Rebbe's passing in 5573 is the date by which his descendants name their sons Schneur Zalman in his memory. The text uses this fact to estimate the birth year of his namesake R. Schneur Zalman b. Yaakov Mordechai Twer.

title_en: R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer born in Mogilev
summary_en: R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, a descendant of MaHaRIL (brother of the Alter Rebbe), was born in Mogilev in 5554 (c. 1794).
story_body: The 1839 Montefiore census lists him as age 45 having been born in Mogilev, allowing reconstruction of his birth year. He would later make aliyah and become the patriarch of the Brimat, Saulson, Singer and Grossman families in Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: R. Shaul ben Yaakov Mordechai Twer born
summary_en: R. Shaul, son of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, was born around 1823 (5583), per the 1839 Montefiore census record.
story_body: Listed in the Montefiore census as age sixteen, married, and a student, R. Shaul made aliyah with his father in 1832. His descendants would adopt the surname Saulson and form one of the well-known Chabad-Hebron families.

title_en: R. Yisrael ben Yaakov Mordechai Twer born
summary_en: R. Yisrael, son of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, was born around 1828 (5588).
story_body: His birth date is reconstructed from the 1839 Montefiore census of the Chabad community of Hebron, which records him at age 11. He and his brothers adopted the family name BeRiMaT (ben R. Mordechai Twer).

title_en: Aliyah of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer and family to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In 5592 (1832) R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer made aliyah from Mogilev with his sons Shaul, Yisrael and Leib, settling in Hebron's Chabad community.
story_body: Aged 38 at the time of aliyah, R. Yaakov Mordechai descended from MaHaRIL, the brother of the Alter Rebbe. His family became the root of the Brimat, Saulson, Singer, and Grossman families in the Holy Land; his eldest son R. Schneur Zalman remained behind in Mogilev and later emigrated separately.

title_en: R. Leib ben Yaakov Mordechai Twer born
summary_en: R. Leib, youngest son of R. Yaakov Mordechai Twer, was born in Eretz Yisrael around 1835 (5595).
story_body: Recorded at age 4 in the 1839 Montefiore census of the Chabad community of Hebron, R. Leib was the first of the Twer brothers born after the family's aliyah. He too adopted the family name Brimat.

title_en: Montefiore census records Twer family in Chabad Hebron community
summary_en: The 5599 (1839) Montefiore census recorded the Twer family among the Chabad Jews of Hebron, listing R. Mordechai (45), Saul (16), Israel (11), and Leib (4).
story_body: The census itself constitutes a major demographic event for the Old Yishuv, providing the most detailed snapshot of the Chabad community of Hebron in the early nineteenth century. The Twer family entries allow reconstruction of birth years, family composition, and migration date for what would become several major Chabad families.

title_en: Montefiore 1875 census lists the three Brimat brothers in Hebron
summary_en: The 5635 (1875) Montefiore census of the Chabad community of Hebron records the three Twer brothers — Saul, Leib, and Israel — under the family name 'Brimat'.
story_body: By 1875 the patriarch R. Yaakov Mordechai had already passed, and only his three Hebron-resident sons were enumerated, each under the BeRiMaT (ben R. Mordechai Twer) surname they had adopted. The census documents the consolidation of the family identity in the Old Yishuv.

title_en: Death of R. Zev Wolf b. Yeshayahu, buried in Chabad section of Mount of Olives
summary_en: R. Zev Wolf b. R. Yeshayahu, a grandson of the brother of the Admur of Yanovich, died on 6 Elul 5642 and was buried in the Chabad plot on the Mount of Olives.
story_body: His name and date are recorded in 'Avnei Zikaron' chelek 12 (copied in 'Oholei Lyubavitch' vol. 3 p. 75 ff.). The entry establishes the presence of MaHaRIL's family descendants in nineteenth-century Eretz Yisrael and confirms their continued affiliation with the Chabad community.

title_en: Death of R. Schneur Zalman b. Yaakov Mordechai (Singer/Grossman ancestor)
summary_en: R. Schneur Zalman b. Yaakov Mordechai — eldest son of the Twer patriarch — died on 14 Kislev 5647 and was buried on the Mount of Olives.
story_body: Named for the Alter Rebbe, he was likely born around 1814, married young, and remained in Mogilev when his father and brothers made aliyah in 1832, joining them only many years later. His descendants include R. Yaakov Mordechai Singer (rabbi/shochet of Rishon LeTzion) and the Grossman family of Jerusalem.

title_en: Death of R. Shaul Chevroni (Saulson ancestor)
summary_en: R. Shaul b. R. Yaakov Mordechai Chevroni died on erev Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5656 (Oct 17, 1895) and was buried on the Mount of Olives.
story_body: His descendants would adopt the surname Saulson, which would become a well-known family in Hebron and beyond. His death notice is preserved in 'Avnei Zikaron' alongside other members of the Twer family.

title_en: Rashab delivers 19 Kislev 1903 discourse (later printed in Torat Shalom)
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5664 (Dec 1903) the Rebbe Rashab discussed the letter of R. Levi Yitzchok about the Maggid's high regard for the Alter Rebbe.
story_body: The Rashab cited the letter and noted its unusual phrasing — 'I did not hear' rather than 'I do not know' — calling it a wonder. The discourse was later printed in 'Torat Shalom' and is the source of an enduring puzzle about R. Levi Yitzchok's wording.

title_en: R. Z. Veliszher reminiscence published in Kfar Chabad magazine
summary_en: On 27 MarCheshvan 5744 (Nov 1983), Kfar Chabad magazine issue 118 published R. M. Z. Gringlas's note recording R. Zalman Veliszher's recollection of the Rashab's 1903 talk.
story_body: Gringlas's account preserves R. Zalman's recollection that as the Rashab uttered 'lo shamati,' he turned his head and confirmed: 'It is not written lo yadati but lo shamati.' The note resolves the textual puzzle that the Rashab had raised about R. Levi Yitzchok's letter.

title_en: R. Yisrael Grossman writes to cousin documenting MaHaRIL descent
summary_en: In 5756 (1996) R. Yisrael Grossman, rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Temimim in Kfar Chabad-Lod, wrote a letter detailing the family's descent from MaHaRIL, brother of the Alter Rebbe.
story_body: The letter identifies three brothers — R. Schneur Zalman, R. Yisrael, and another — buried on the Mount of Olives, and traces the line back to MaHaRIL. It is a primary source for the family tree linking the Brimat/Saulson/Singer/Grossman families to the brother of the Baal HaTanya.

title_en: Alter Rebbe and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak study with the Maggid in Ravna
summary_en: In summer 5532, Rabbi Schneur Zalman and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak study halacha together at the Maggid of Mezeritch's court in Ravna, where the Maggid rules leniently on a kashrut question.
story_body: In the summer of 5532, the Alter Rebbe and Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev studied together at the Maggid of Mezeritch's home in Ravna. A halachic question about sirchot in the lung was brought before the Maggid, who ruled leniently and proved it from the Talmud. Nearly four decades later, when rabbis challenged Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's late ruling on the same question, the Alter Rebbe defended it by citing this very session with their teacher.

title_en: Passing of the Maggid of Mezeritch
summary_en: Rabbi Dovber, the Maggid of Mezeritch, passes away on 19 Kislev 5533, after which his disciples return to Russia to spread Chassidism.
story_body: On 19 Kislev 5533, the Maggid of Mezeritch—chief disciple of the Baal Shem Tov—passed away. His three Russian-Lithuanian disciples, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk, and Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, returned to Russia to spread Chassidic teaching. Decades later, this date acquired additional weight when the Alter Rebbe was released from Tsarist imprisonment on the same day in 1798.

title_en: Aliyah of Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk; Alter Rebbe turns back at Mohilev
summary_en: In summer 5537, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk lead a group of Chassidim on aliyah; the Alter Rebbe accompanies them as far as Mohilev on the Dniester before being persuaded to return.
story_body: In summer 5537, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk led an aliyah of Chassidic disciples to Eretz Yisrael. The Alter Rebbe joined them as far as Mohilev in Podolia, where Chassidim and his fellow rebbes pleaded with him to remain in Russia to oversee their spiritual and material welfare. He stayed in Mohilev about a year and a half before returning to Vitebsk in 5539.

title_en: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk names three Russian Chassidic leaders
summary_en: From Eretz Yisrael, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk writes on 4 Adar 5542 directing Russian Chassidim to attach themselves exclusively to three named leaders.
story_body: On 4 Adar 5542, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote from Eretz Yisrael instructing his Russian Chassidim not to travel to Volhynia for Chassidic guidance but to bind themselves only to three named leaders in Russia: Rabbi Yisrael of Polotsk, Rabbi Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch, and Rabbi Schneur Zalman. The letter notably omitted other Maggid disciples then in Russia—Rabbi Levi Yitzchak (then in Pinsk), Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin, and Rabbi Chaim Chaikel of Amdur—marking the beginning of what would become the proto-Chabad line of leadership.

title_en: Alter Rebbe becomes sole leader of Russian-Lithuanian Chassidim
summary_en: Around 5543, Rabbi Yisrael of Polotsk passes away and Rabbi Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch defers, leaving the Alter Rebbe—now settled in Liozna—as the sole leader appointed by Rabbis Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Avraham of Kalisk.
story_body: About a year after the three-leader appointment letter, Rabbi Yisrael of Polotsk passed away around 5543, and Rabbi Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch deferred to the Alter Rebbe. Rabbis Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk and Avraham of Kalisk, writing from Eretz Yisrael, then designated him sole leader of Russian and Lithuanian Chassidim. In the same year he settled in his hometown Liozna as maggid-meisharim, where he would lead Chabad until 5561.

title_en: Tanya first printed
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe's Tanya appears in print for the first time in 5557, formalizing the Chabad approach to Chassidic thought.
story_body: In 5557, Rabbi Schneur Zalman's Tanya appeared in print for the first time, presenting his systematic Chabad approach to Chassidism. The same year, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk launched a public critique of the Tanya's method, drawing in other Maggid disciples in Volhynia and Poland. The dispute lasted years and ultimately crystallized the separation between general Chassidism and the distinct Chabad movement.

title_en: Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk opposes the Tanya's approach
summary_en: In 5557, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk publicly opposes the Alter Rebbe's Chabad approach, drawing other Maggid disciples into a multi-year dispute.
story_body: Soon after the Tanya was printed in 5557, Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk—then leading Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael—came out publicly against its method. Disciples of the Maggid in Volhynia and Poland were drawn into the dispute, which continued for years and eventually produced a permanent split between general Chassidism and Chabad. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev took the Alter Rebbe's side, writing that the Tanya approach reflected 'the entire essence of the Maggid's own conduct.'

title_en: Alter Rebbe freed from Petersburg imprisonment on 19 Kislev
summary_en: Rabbi Schneur Zalman is released from imprisonment in Petersburg on 19 Kislev 5559—the yahrzeit of the Maggid—after being denounced by opponents of Chassidism.
story_body: Following denunciations by opponents of Chassidism, the Alter Rebbe was arrested and interrogated in Petersburg. On 19 Kislev 5559, while reading from Psalms the verse 'He redeemed my soul in peace,' he was released. He immediately wrote a letter announcing the redemption to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, noting that the date doubled in meaning as the yahrzeit of their teacher, the Maggid of Mezeritch.

title_en: Alter Rebbe moves from Liozna to Liadi
summary_en: Rabbi Schneur Zalman relocates from Liozna to Liadi in 5561, the move that gives the dynasty its standard appellation 'the Liadier Rav.'
story_body: After roughly eighteen years in Liozna, the Alter Rebbe moved to Liadi in 5561. The move came shortly after his first Petersburg imprisonment and just before a second arrest the following year. He would lead Chabad from Liadi until his passing in 5573.

title_en: Chabad Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael form a separate kollel
summary_en: In 5565, Alter Rebbe-aligned Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael break from Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk's leadership to organize what would later be called Kollel Chabad.
story_body: Following years of disagreement between Rabbi Avraham of Kalisk and the Alter Rebbe over the Chabad approach to Chassidism, the rift carried into Eretz Yisrael. In 5565, Chassidim in Tzfat who followed the Alter Rebbe organized their own kollel, separate from the general Chassidic community led from Tiberias. The same year, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev sent dedicated funds for his own Chassidim in the land through Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk.

title_en: Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk carries Berditchever pidyon funds to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In summer 5565, Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk carries funds from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev to his Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael during his own aliyah.
story_body: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev maintained a fund for his Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael, parallel to the Alter Rebbe's similar effort. In summer 5565, he sent that year's contribution with Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Volochisk, who was making his own journey to the land. The Chozeh of Lublin referenced the transfer in a letter to Rabbi Levi Yitzchak from that same season.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev
summary_en: Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, passes away in Kislev 5566; the Alter Rebbe sends a letter of consolation later printed as Iggeret HaKodesh chapter 28.
story_body: Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, passed away in Kislev 5566. The Alter Rebbe wrote a letter of consolation to his in-law that was later included as Iggeret HaKodesh chapter 28 in Tanya. His death is thought to have delayed the major Berditchev–Liadi marriage of his son, eventually held in summer 1807 after the year of mourning.

title_en: The grand Zhlobin wedding unites the Berditchev and Liadi dynasties
summary_en: The famous 'Zhlobiner chasunah' takes place around Parshat Naso 5567, joining a grandchild of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev to Sarah, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe.
story_body: Around Parshat Naso in summer 5567, the celebrated 'Zhlobiner chasunah' was held in Zhlobin, drawing thousands of Chassidim from across Russia. The bride was Sarah, daughter of Rabbi Dovber (the future Mitteler Rebbe); the groom was a son of Rabbi Meir, son of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev. The match had been arranged by 5564 but was delayed by Rabbi Meir's death in 5566 and the subsequent mourning year.

title_en: Second Berditchev–Liadi marriage links the dynasties
summary_en: Rabbi Yekutiel Zalman, grandson of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, marries Rebbetzin Rivka, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe, in the winter of 5568.
story_body: Months after the grand Zhlobin wedding, a second match further tied the two dynasties: Rabbi Yekutiel Zalman, son of Rabbi Yosef Bunem and grandson of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, married Rebbetzin Rivka, daughter of the Mitteler Rebbe. The Tzemach Tzedek—their future brother-in-law—noted in a manuscript a discourse delivered by the Alter Rebbe on the second night of Parshat Yitro 5568, identifying it with this winter wedding.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev
summary_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, fellow disciple of the Maggid and close associate of the Alter Rebbe, passes away on 25 Tishrei 5570 after some 25 years leading the Berditchev community.
story_body: On 25 Tishrei 5570, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev passed away after leading the Berditchev community since around 5545. The Alter Rebbe traveled to Berditchev for the consolation of mourners and remained in Volhynia through the winter of 5570. At the widow's request, he spent Pesach in Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's home and personally conducted the seder; during his stay there he was also asked to weigh in on one of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's final halachic rulings on sirchot.

title_en: Passing of the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, founder of Chabad Chassidism, passes away on 24 Tevet 5573 during the upheaval of Napoleon's invasion of Russia.
story_body: On 24 Tevet 5573, the Alter Rebbe Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi passed away while displaced by Napoleon's advance into Russia. He was succeeded by his son, Rabbi Dovber, the Mitteler Rebbe, who continued his father's joint efforts with the Berditchever line—including the parallel program of support for Chassidim in Eretz Yisrael, now coordinated with Rabbi Yisrael of Pikov, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's son and successor.

title_en: R' Shlomo of Karlin becomes rabbi of Karlin
summary_en: R' Shlomo of Karlin took up the rabbinate of Karlin around 5532.
story_body: The historical record establishes that R' Shlomo HaKohen of Karlin served as rabbi of Karlin starting in 5532 (1772) and continued there until shortly before 5544. He was a leading disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch and later a major chassidic leader in Lithuania.

title_en: Alter Rebbe settles in Liozna
summary_en: R' Schneur Zalman of Liadi moved from Horodok to Liozna around summer 5543.
story_body: After roughly two years in Horodok, the Alter Rebbe relocated to Liozna in the summer of 5543 (1783). In his later 1798 interrogation he himself testified that he had lived in Liozna 'about 15 years and more.' Liozna became the seat of his leadership of Belorussian and Lithuanian chassidim until 1801.

title_en: R' Aharon of Tiveria recommends Alter Rebbe to Russian chassidim
summary_en: R' Aharon HaGadol wrote from Tiveria in 5543 urging Russian chassidim to draw close to R' Schneur Zalman.
story_body: In 5543 (1783) R' Aharon HaGadol of Tiveria sent a letter to the chassidim of White Russia, advising them to attach themselves to R' Schneur Zalman of Horodok as 'unique in his generation among you in wisdom and chassidut.' This is the earliest documented signal of the Alter Rebbe's emerging role as exclusive leader of Russian chassidim.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk endorses Alter Rebbe and R' Yissachar Ber
summary_en: In winter 5544 R' Menachem Mendel wrote from Tiveria directing Russian chassidim to the Alter Rebbe and R' Yissachar Ber.
story_body: From Tiveria in the winter of 5544 (1784), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk responded to complaints about livelihood and leadership reaching him from Russia. He instructed the chassidim to be content with the guidance of R' Yissachar Ber of Lubavitch and R' Schneur Zalman of Liozna rather than seeking new leadership from abroad.

title_en: R' Shlomo of Karlin relocates to Ludmir
summary_en: After being expelled by mitnagdim from Karlin, R' Shlomo was already in Ludmir by 5544.
story_body: R' Shlomo of Karlin was driven from Karlin by the mitnagdim and resettled in Ludmir in Volhynia. The precise date of relocation is undocumented, but by 5544 (1784) he was already established in Ludmir, having earlier been denied the Alter Rebbe's full agreement to settle in Beshenkovich because of a doctrinal disagreement about the role of the tzaddik.

title_en: R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev expelled from Pinsk
summary_en: In summer 5545 R' Levi Yitzchak was driven from Pinsk by mitnagdim and moved to Berditchev.
story_body: R' Levi Yitzchak had served as av beit din of Pinsk from 5535 to 5545. In the summer of 5545 (1785) the mitnagdim succeeded in expelling him from the city, and he relocated to Berditchev in Volhynia. His departure further consolidated the Alter Rebbe's position as sole chassidic leader in White Russia and Lithuania.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel formally appoints Alter Rebbe as leader of Russia
summary_en: In 5546 R' Menachem Mendel wrote insisting that the Alter Rebbe accept exclusive leadership of Russian chassidim.
story_body: In 5546 (1786), responding to the Alter Rebbe's hesitation, R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote from Tiveria urging him to 'be strong and courageous… for Hashem has given you as a shepherd' and to lead all the chassidim of Russia. R' Avraham of Kalisk wrote in parallel echoing the appointment.

title_en: Alter Rebbe replies to summons from Mohilov rabbinate
summary_en: In 5547 the Alter Rebbe wrote refusing to appear before the Mohilov rabbinate and defending chassidim against shklov decrees.
story_body: Between 5546–47 the heads of the Mohilov community summoned the Alter Rebbe to stand judgment before them and even appealed to the civil courts. In 5547 (1787) he responded with a lengthy letter rejecting the summons, refuting the charges, and protesting the harsh distancing decrees issued by some Shklov scholars against chassidim.

title_en: R' Chaim Chaikel of Amdura passes away
summary_en: R' Chaim Chaikel of Amdura died in winter 5547.
story_body: In the winter of 5547 (1786/87) R' Chaim Chaikel of Amdura, one of the disciples of the Maggid of Mezritch active in Lithuania, passed away. His son and successor R' Shmuel, then twenty years old, began traveling to the Alter Rebbe to receive Torah from him.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's final letter on Alter Rebbe's leadership
summary_en: R' Menachem Mendel's last extant letter in 5548 again confirmed the Alter Rebbe as moreh tzedek for Russia.
story_body: In his final letter from Tiveria, dated 5548 (1788), R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk wrote: 'We have anointed him to be moreh tzedek in their land, so that the congregation of Hashem should not be like sheep without a shepherd… who like him is teacher and rav in their country.' This sealed the Alter Rebbe's standing as exclusive leader.

title_en: Passing of R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk
summary_en: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk passed away on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5548.
story_body: R' Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, leader of the chassidic aliyah to Eretz Yisrael and mentor to the Alter Rebbe, passed away on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5548 (May 7, 1788) in Tiveria. After his passing, R' Avraham of Kalisk continued to write to the Russian chassidim affirming that R' Schneur Zalman alone was their leader.

title_en: R' Shmuel of Amdura first travels to the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: R' Shmuel of Amdura first traveled to learn from the Alter Rebbe in 5550.
story_body: According to his own 1799 interrogation testimony, R' Shmuel of Amdura traveled to the Alter Rebbe to study from him three times: in 5550, 5554, and 5558. His extant letters also cite teachings received from the Alter Rebbe, evidencing the latter's growing role as teacher across Lithuanian chassidic communities.

title_en: R' Shlomo of Karlin killed in Ludmir
summary_en: R' Shlomo of Karlin was killed in Ludmir in 5552.
story_body: In 5552 (1792) R' Shlomo of Karlin was killed in Ludmir. In subsequent years two of his leading disciples — R' Mordechai of Lechovich and R' Asher son of R' Aharon HaGadol of Stolin — would return to settle in White Russia and Lithuania, laying foundations for the spread of general chassidut into the region after 19 Kislev 5559.

title_en: Alter Rebbe releases Tanya for copying and distribution
summary_en: In 5552 the Alter Rebbe handed over the Tanya manuscript for copying and circulation.
story_body: In 5552 (1792) R' Schneur Zalman released the Likutei Amarim (Tanya) for copying and dissemination. In its 'Introduction of the Compiler' he explained that the work collected his answers to the questions chassidim brought him in private audience, since 'time no longer permits' him to address each one individually — directly linking the Tanya's publication to the Liozna takanos limiting yechidus.

title_en: Alter Rebbe reaffirms Liozna takanos at handover of Tanya for print
summary_en: On 27 Adar I 5556 the Alter Rebbe and chassidic leaders re-signed the Liozna takanos.
story_body: On 27 Adar I 5556 (March 7, 1796), at the same time the Tanya was given to the printers, the Alter Rebbe re-confirmed his signature on the Liozna takanos and added new provisions, co-signed by leading chassidim including R' Yisrael ben Yitzchak of Kapust. The takanos restricted how often chassidim could come to him and limited entry to yechidut.

title_en: Printing of the Tanya completed
summary_en: The first printing of the Tanya was completed on 20 Kislev 5557.
story_body: After the manuscript was handed to the printer in late 5556, the first edition of the Tanya was completed on 20 Kislev 5557 (December 20, 1796). The publication marked the formal release of the Alter Rebbe's foundational Chabad text and signaled a new stage in chassidic instruction by the written word.

title_en: Denouncement of Alter Rebbe to Russian government
summary_en: In summer 5558 mitnagdim denounced the Alter Rebbe and some thirty chassidim to the Russian authorities.
story_body: In the summer of 5558 (1798) the mitnagdim lodged a formal denunciation against the Alter Rebbe together with a group of about thirty chassidim. The charges led to the arrests at the beginning of 5559 and the Alter Rebbe's transfer to St. Petersburg for interrogation.

title_en: Alter Rebbe arrested and taken to St. Petersburg
summary_en: At the start of 5559 the Alter Rebbe was arrested and sent to St. Petersburg for interrogation.
story_body: At the beginning of 5559 (autumn 1798) the Alter Rebbe was arrested following the mitnagdim's denunciation and immediately sent to the capital for questioning, while interrogations of the Vilna chassidim arrested with him began in Vilna itself. Some were later sent toward St. Petersburg but recalled to Vilna en route.

title_en: Tsar Paul I orders release of Alter Rebbe
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5559 Tsar Paul ordered the Alter Rebbe and the Karliner chassidim freed.
story_body: After interrogation and the Alter Rebbe's written replies in Hebrew were translated for Tsar Paul, the Tsar issued a decree on 19 Kislev 5559 finding nothing harmful to the state in the conduct of 'the Karliner sect' and ordering all of them released. The day became the festival of 19 Kislev, Chag HaGeulah, the founding holiday of Chabad.

title_en: Alter Rebbe receives release certificate
summary_en: On 20 Kislev 5559 the Alter Rebbe was issued his official release document.
story_body: On 20 Kislev 5559 (Nov 17, 1798 OS / Nov 28 NS) the Alter Rebbe received his written release certificate identifying him as 'Zalman ben Baruch' and authorizing his return to White Russia via Vitebsk. The same day, Prokuror General Pyotr Lopukhin formally notified the Belorussian governor Semyon Zhegulin of the imperial decision.

title_en: Vilna chassidim freed on fifth night of Chanukah
summary_en: On 28 Kislev 5559, the eve of the fifth Chanukah light, the Vilna chassidim were freed.
story_body: On 28 Kislev 5559 the chassidim arrested in Vilna together with the Alter Rebbe were also released. Tradition holds that the release occurred at night after candle-lighting, which is why the fifth light of Chanukah became associated with the redemption of the Vilna chassidim.

title_en: Prokuror Beklashov orders chassidim be tolerated
summary_en: On 8 Shevat 5560 Prokuror Beklashov instructed Vilna police to inform the kahal that the Karliner sect must be tolerated.
story_body: After a second mitnagdic denunciation at the start of 5560, Prokuror General Alexander Beklashov issued an order on 8 Shevat 5560 (Feb 4, 1800) to the Vilna municipal police instructing them to summon the kahal heads and inform them that 'by the will of His Imperial Majesty the Karliner sect must be tolerated.' The order would later be cited in the Alter Rebbe's second interrogation.

title_en: Alter Rebbe's second arrest and transfer to St. Petersburg
summary_en: A renewed denunciation at the start of 5561 brought the Alter Rebbe to St. Petersburg again for interrogation.
story_body: At the beginning of 5561 (autumn 1800) a fresh denunciation against the Alter Rebbe was filed and he was once more brought to St. Petersburg for questioning. In his testimony there he cited Tsar Paul's earlier release decree and Beklashov's order tolerating the chassidim as proof of the lawfulness of the movement.

title_en: Alter Rebbe placed under house arrest in St. Petersburg
summary_en: On 23 Kislev 5561 Tsar Paul ordered the Alter Rebbe held under house arrest until investigation concluded.
story_body: Following his second interrogation, an imperial order issued on 23 Kislev 5561 (Nov 30, 1800) directed that the Alter Rebbe be released to house arrest within St. Petersburg until the inquiry was completed, rather than being held in prison.

title_en: Assassination of Tsar Paul I
summary_en: Tsar Paul was assassinated on the night before 10 Nissan 5561 and succeeded by his son Alexander.
story_body: On the eve of 10 Nissan 5561 (March 23/24, 1801) Tsar Paul I was murdered in his palace and his son Alexander I ascended the throne. Within two weeks the new Tsar issued a full release for the Alter Rebbe, ending his second imprisonment.

title_en: Tsar Alexander issues full release certificate for Alter Rebbe
summary_en: A copy of the imperial release certificate reached the Alter Rebbe in Vitebsk on 15 Av 5561.
story_body: By order of Tsar Alexander I, 'the Jew Zalman ben Baruch' was declared free to return home and enjoy full liberty in his former place of residence. A copy of the release was delivered to the Alter Rebbe through the Vitebsk governor's office on 15 Av 5561 (July 25, 1801), accompanied by a certificate from Pyotr Tarabeev confirming the Alter Rebbe's right to exercise his liberties throughout White Russia.

title_en: Alter Rebbe relocates from Liozna to Liadi
summary_en: After his St. Petersburg release the Alter Rebbe did not return to Liozna but settled in Liadi in summer 5561.
story_body: Following the conclusion of his summer 5561 stay in St. Petersburg, the Alter Rebbe did not return to Liozna but established his court in Liadi. From this point onward he was the rebbe of an identifiable Chabad community rather than the universal leader of Russian chassidim, and the special Liozna takanos limiting yechidut were not reinstated.

title_en: R' Avraham of Kalisk's emissaries seek to displace Alter Rebbe's emissaries
summary_en: In winter 5563 Kalisk emissaries demanded replacing all the Alter Rebbe's collectors with new ones not called Chabad.
story_body: In the winter of 5563 (1802/03) emissaries from R' Avraham of Kalisk in Eretz Yisrael came to the Alter Rebbe asking that the existing chassidic emissaries handling the Land of Israel maamadot be removed and replaced with new ones from among 'true lovers who are not called by the name Chabad.' The dispute marked the open split between Chabad and the general chassidic movement led by Kalisk.

title_en: First documented use of the name 'Chabad' for the Alter Rebbe's chassidim
summary_en: The name 'Chabad' first appears as a designation for the Alter Rebbe's chassidim in winter 5563.
story_body: The earliest known use of 'Chabad' as the name of the Alter Rebbe's chassidim is in the demand brought by R' Avraham of Kalisk's emissaries in winter 5563 (1803) that maamadot emissaries 'not called by the name Chabad' replace the existing ones. This implies that by that point the designation had already become familiar in the chassidic world.

title_en: Alter Rebbe begins editing Hilchos Tzitzis and Pesach at the Maggid's court
summary_en: In summer 5531 (1771) the Alter Rebbe completed the first drafts of Hilchos Tzitzis and Hilchos Pesach for his Shulchan Aruch while residing at the Maggid of Mezritch's court.
story_body: Selected by the Maggid of Mezritch from among his disciples to compose a new Shulchan Aruch with clear halachic rulings and their reasoning, the young Alter Rebbe began the project with Hilchos Tzitzis and Hilchos Pesach. According to the introduction by his sons, both sections were begun and finished while he sat at the Maggid's court. This marked the start of what would become a multi-decade halachic project.

title_en: R. Shmelka and R. Pinchas Horowitz visit the Maggid in Rovno and praise Alter Rebbe's work
summary_en: Before traveling to take up their rabbinates in Germany, the brothers R. Shmelka and R. Pinchas Horowitz visited the Maggid in Rovno, where they reviewed and lavishly praised the Alter Rebbe's draft of Hilchos Tzitzis and Pesach.
story_body: After being chosen as rabbis of Nikolsburg and Frankfurt-am-Main respectively, the two brothers came to take counsel from the Maggid before assuming their posts. At his court they saw the Alter Rebbe's draft of the Shulchan Aruch and praised it greatly, telling him to be strong and complete the work. The Alter Rebbe later recalled this meeting in his correspondence with R. Pinchas, the Baal Haflaah.

title_en: R. Pinchas Horowitz stays in Brod en route to the Frankfurt rabbinate
summary_en: On 15 Cheshvan 5532 R. Pinchas Horowitz, the Baal Haflaah, was in Brod en route to assume the rabbinate of Frankfurt-am-Main, where he wrote a haskamah for Sefer Totza'os Chaim.
story_body: Traveling from Volhynia to Germany after taking leave of the Maggid, R. Pinchas Horowitz stopped in Brod for Shabbos. His approbation for the Zolkva 5532 edition of Totza'os Chaim was dated there on Wednesday 15 Cheshvan 5532, fixing the timing of his journey precisely. From Brod he continued westward toward Frankfurt.

title_en: R. Pinchas Horowitz arrives in Frankfurt-am-Main to take his rabbinical seat
summary_en: According to the Frankfurt community register, R. Pinchas Horowitz arrived in Frankfurt-am-Main on 26 Tevet 5532 to begin his tenure as rabbi.
story_body: After being elected by the Frankfurt community in spring 1771 and traveling via Brod, the Baal Haflaah's journey from Volhynia stretched from Cheshvan to Tevet of 5532. Frankfurt's communal records date his arrival to 26 Tevet 5532. He would serve as Frankfurt's rabbi for more than thirty-three years until his passing in 5565.

title_en: Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk fail to meet the Vilna Gaon
summary_en: During the winter of 5532 the Alter Rebbe and R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk traveled to Vilna to meet the Vilna Gaon, but the Gaon refused to receive them and left the city.
story_body: Hoping to defuse the opposition to chassidus by direct dialogue, the two leaders came to the Gaon's home but the door was closed against them twice. When they pressed further the Gaon departed Vilna entirely, staying away until they left. The Alter Rebbe recounted the failed attempt in his Iggeres 34.

title_en: Alter Rebbe disputes with mitnagdim in Shklov
summary_en: Following the failed Vilna visit in winter 5532, the Alter Rebbe and R. Avraham of Kalisk went to Shklov to debate the mitnagdim there, but the local opponents reneged on their promise of safe debate and resorted to force.
story_body: After leaving Vilna the two chassidic leaders attempted a public disputation in Shklov. The local mitnagdim initially agreed to a peaceful debate but, unable to refute the chassidic arguments, broke their word and acted aggressively. The Alter Rebbe described the events in Iggeres 34 and Iggeres 51.

title_en: Alter Rebbe travels to the Maggid in Rovno in summer 5532
summary_en: In summer 5532 (1772) the Alter Rebbe traveled with R. Avraham of Kalisk to the Maggid of Mezritch in Rovno, where he continued editing his Shulchan Aruch and discussed halachic questions with the Maggid.
story_body: After the Vilna and Shklov debates, the two leaders went up to their teacher in Rovno. The Alter Rebbe remained with the Maggid in Rovno, and later in Anipoli, until the Maggid's passing. He continued working on Hilchos Orach Chaim during this period and presented halachic novellae to the Maggid for approval.

title_en: Passing of the Maggid of Mezritch
summary_en: The Maggid of Mezritch, R. Dov Ber, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533 in Anipoli.
story_body: R. Dov Ber, successor to the Baal Shem Tov and teacher of the founders of the major chassidic dynasties including the Alter Rebbe, passed away on 19 Kislev 5533. His passing marked the close of the period during which the Alter Rebbe consulted him on the editing of the Shulchan Aruch. Decades later 19 Kislev would also become the date of the Alter Rebbe's own redemption from imprisonment.

title_en: Initial editing of Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim concludes
summary_en: Around the time of the Maggid's passing in late 5533, the Alter Rebbe completed the first round of editing of his Shulchan Aruch on Orach Chaim.
story_body: According to his sons' introduction, the foundational editing of Orach Chaim took roughly two years. Beginning in summer 5531 with Tzitzis and Pesach, the Alter Rebbe continued through Vilna, Shklov, Rovno and Anipoli, completing the section in proximity to the Maggid's histalkus on 19 Kislev 5533. He continued to revise and add to the work in the following years until about 5537.

title_en: Alter Rebbe accompanies aliyah group as far as Mohilov on the Dniester
summary_en: In 5537 the Alter Rebbe joined R. Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk's group setting out to settle in the Land of Israel, traveling with them as far as Mohilov on the Dniester.
story_body: Reaching Mohilov in Podolia near the Turkish border, the leaders agreed that the Alter Rebbe should not continue but remain in Russia to care for the spiritual and material needs of the chassidim. R. Mendel and his colleagues parted from him with great weeping. The Alter Rebbe remained in Mohilov for about a year and a half, where he completed his sixteenth review of the entire Talmud, standing day and night.

title_en: Alter Rebbe begins revising Hilchos Netilas Yadayim for the Siddur
summary_en: While residing in Mohilov in 5538-5539 (1778-1779), the Alter Rebbe began producing a second, revised edition of the laws of his Shulchan Aruch starting with Hilchos Netilas Yadayim.
story_body: His sons relate that after his sixteenth review of the Talmud the Alter Rebbe began emending and renewing his Shulchan Aruch, starting with Hilchos Netilas Yadayim. The revised version was later printed as the kuntres 'Luach Birchas Hanehenin' and 'Seder Netilas Yadayim Lese'udah' in his Siddur. This opened a roughly twenty-year middle period of writing thirty kuntreisei halachos, lasting through 5557.

title_en: Disputes over Alter Rebbe's chassidic approach begin; his system called 'Chabad'
summary_en: In 5558 internal disputes broke out within the chassidic community over the Alter Rebbe's approach, and during the years 5558-5562 his system came to be known as 'Chabad'.
story_body: Until 5558 the Alter Rebbe served as the sole acknowledged leader of the general chassidic community in Russia and Lithuania. That year, disputes emerged regarding his particular path in chassidus. Over the course of the controversy between 5558 and 5562, his approach became identified by the name 'Chabad'.

title_en: Period of arrests and redemption of the Alter Rebbe begins
summary_en: Starting in 5559 the Alter Rebbe entered the final fifteen-year period of his life, marked by the arrests and redemptions of 5559-5561 and the editing of the final 'mahadura basra' of his Shulchan Aruch.
story_body: The years 5559-5561 saw the Alter Rebbe's two imprisonments and miraculous releases at the hands of the Czarist government. From this period onward he undertook the third and final phase of editing his Shulchan Aruch, the mahadura basra in three layers. This work continued through the last fifteen years of his life.

title_en: Hilchos Talmud Torah first printed
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe's Hilchos Talmud Torah, part of his kuntreisim of essential laws, was first printed in 5554 (1794).
story_body: Unlike most of the other kuntreisim, which mainly summarize earlier poskim, Hilchos Talmud Torah contains many original rulings the Alter Rebbe derived from Talmudic sugyos in his Kuntres Acharon. Its first printing in 5554 provides one of the few firm dating anchors for the middle period of his halachic writing. The work was composed in the same era as the other Hilchos Hatzrichos compilations of 5545-5550.

title_en: Luach Birchas Hanehenin first printed
summary_en: The Alter Rebbe's 'Luach Birchas Hanehenin', a kuntres on the laws of berachos over food, was first printed around 5555 (1795).
story_body: This work was printed several times together with Seder Netilas Yadayim Lese'udah and likely edited in the same period. It would later be supplanted by a revised version, 'Seder Birchas Hanehenin', integrated into the Alter Rebbe's Siddur of 5563. The revised edition departed from the Magen Avraham in several places based on study of the rishonim.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes Seder Hachnasas Shabbos and Hilchasa Rabsa LeShabsa
summary_en: In 5557 the Alter Rebbe wrote his Seder Hachnasas Shabbos and Hilchasa Rabsa LeShabsa, as recorded in a contemporary manuscript index.
