story_body: About a year after his arrival in Frankfurt, a police officer ordered Reb Avraham Chaim to leave German territory. He moved to Amsterdam, intent on avoiding America at all costs. There he conducted some business with the chassid Persson but found no steady livelihood.

title_en: Rosenbaum works as proofreader in Berlin Torah publishing house
summary_en: During the winter of 5653 Rosenbaum worked in Berlin preparing a Torah-scholarly journal for press while residing in the home of its publishing rabbi.
story_body: In winter 5653 Reb Avraham Chaim worked in Berlin as the editor and proofreader of a Torah-scientific journal, lodging in the home of the rabbi who issued it. From there he wrote to Rabbi Tzvi Tietz, author of Zikhron Yehudah on Eichah, explaining why he had cut a passage from a submitted article on the wording of the bris-milah blessing 'tziva yedidut.'

title_en: Rosenbaum moves from Berlin to Königsberg seeking business
summary_en: At the start of summer 5653 Rosenbaum left Berlin for Königsberg to try his hand at business, but his efforts there did not succeed.
story_body: In early summer 5653 Reb Avraham Chaim moved from Berlin to Königsberg, pursuing a commercial venture he hoped would establish him. He labored at it all summer without success and confessed that 'the design did not come to fruition because God did not consent to it.'

title_en: Rosenbaum writes from Königsberg about why he avoids emigrating to America
summary_en: On Wednesday of Parshat Ki Tavo 5653 Rosenbaum told the Kugel brothers that R' Chaim Yaakov Widerewitz had warned him from New York that America suited only strong workers, not delicate scholars.
story_body: Writing from Königsberg in Parshat Ki Tavo 5653 to R' Zev Wolf and R' Chaim Gershon Kugel, Reb Avraham Chaim quoted at length a letter he had received on 16 Iyar from R' Chaim Yaakov Widerewitz, rabbi of the Sephardic association in America. Widerewitz advised that any family with three or four strong working hands would find livelihood, but 'soft and delicate people' would suffer terribly. Knowing himself to be of the second type, Rosenbaum reluctantly resolved not to cross the ocean.

title_en: Rosenbaum family arrives in New York on the SS Moravia
summary_en: On 13 Kislev 5655 / 11 December 1894 Reb Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum, his wife Yetta and sons Zalman and Yosef reached New York on the ship Moravia from Hamburg.
story_body: Having finally decided to emigrate, the Rosenbaum family sailed from Hamburg and arrived at the port of New York on 11 December 1894 aboard the SS Moravia. The passenger manifest recorded Abraham (54), Yetta (53), Solomon (21) and Joseph (11). In New York he would settle, deal in diamonds and jewelry at 444 Grand Street, and gather chassidim around him.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab encourages New York anash via letter through Rosenbaum
summary_en: On 24 Adar I 5662 the Rebbe Rashab replied to Rosenbaum, acknowledging a 100-ruble donation and urging the New York chassidim to gather thrice weekly to study Chassidut, daven with kavanah and strengthen mitzvah observance.
story_body: Receiving Rosenbaum's report on the New York group together with 100 rubles, on 24 Adar I 5662 the Rebbe Rashab wrote a long letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1 #114). He praised the men of the Rebbe Maharash's circle for retaining their spiritual life in a distant land, urged them to meet on Thursday nights, Shabbat and motzaei Shabbat to learn Chassidut together, and to correct shortcomings in their tefillah and observance.

title_en: Death of Yetta Rosenbaum in New York
summary_en: In 5664 Yetta Rosenbaum, wife of Reb Avraham Chaim, died after four months of severe illness, in a year of major financial losses for the family.
story_body: In the course of 5664 Reb Avraham Chaim's wife Yetta lay ill for about four months before she died, and he expended over 1,000 dollars on her medical care. In the same year his diamond business lost nearly 2,000 dollars when merchandise from Germany failed to arrive, together amounting to roughly three-quarters of his savings in his old age.

title_en: R' Yehoshua Kostral writes from San Remo consoling Rosenbaum
summary_en: On 7 Shevat 5664 R' Yehoshua Kostral wrote from San Remo consoling Rosenbaum on his wife's death and gently suggesting that he ought to consider remarriage.
story_body: From San Remo on 7 Shevat 5664, R' Yehoshua Kostral acknowledged Rosenbaum's letter informing him of Yetta's passing. He admitted he scarcely knew the deceased or Rosenbaum's American household and so could hardly comfort him, yet he urged that 'you are not yet old' and that sitting alone is impossible—he should seek a second match.

title_en: Rosenbaum recounts losses and widowhood in Rosh Chodesh Adar II letter
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5665 Rosenbaum wrote describing the death of his wife and major business losses, and reported on his brother R' Zalman's fundraising tour for Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: On Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5665 Reb Avraham Chaim summarized the previous year: his wife of his youth had died after a four-month illness costing over 1,000 dollars, his diamond business had lost nearly 2,000 more, and he had been visited by his brother R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum, dispatched by the Rebbe Rashab as an emissary for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshivas. He noted with pride his brother's success in raising funds in New York and Philadelphia.

title_en: Rosenbaum sends 1,000 rubles of lottery winnings to Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: After winning 5,000 rubles in a New York lottery, Rosenbaum sent 1,000 to the Rebbe Rashab, who acknowledged receipt on 12 Tishrei 5667.
story_body: Reb Avraham Chaim won 5,000 rubles in a lottery and immediately sent 1,000 of them to the Rebbe Rashab. On 12 Tishrei 5667 (1 October 1906) the Rebbe wrote from Lubavitch confirming arrival of the money, enclosing a distribution list, and praying that Rosenbaum continue to merit livelihood and the ability to do tzedakah.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab advises Rosenbaum to invest lottery winnings in a house
summary_en: On 18 Cheshvan 5667 the Rebbe Rashab advised Rosenbaum that the prudent use of his prize money would be to purchase a stone house yielding income proportionate to his needs.
story_body: Continuing the conversation about Rosenbaum's lottery winnings, the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Lubavitch on 18 Cheshvan 5667 that 'in my opinion it is correct that he buy a stone house from which he will have income according to his needs.' He blessed him that God should send him a good and successful property and prosperity in body and soul.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim funding collapses in Russia after 1905 pogroms
summary_en: In a summer 5667 fundraising letter Rosenbaum reported that the recent Russian pogroms had severely weakened Russian donors and left Tomchei Tmimim's roughly 500 students in dire need.
story_body: Writing to R' Gershon Kapilowitz in summer 5667, Rosenbaum described Tomchei Tmimim, founded by the Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch, with some 500 outstanding students supplied with all their needs. Until then Russian philanthropists had given tens of thousands of rubles per year, but the recent pogroms and disturbances had crippled their ability to give. American donors now had to step in with fixed annual pledges to keep the yeshivas functioning.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab writes from Würzburg accepting Tzemach Tzedek manuscript
summary_en: On 11 Elul 5667 the Rebbe Rashab wrote to Rosenbaum from Würzburg asking him to send the Tzemach Tzedek's handwritten power-of-attorney to Lubavitch by registered mail.
story_body: From Würzburg on 11 Elul 5667 the Rebbe Rashab acknowledged receipt of 100 marks Rosenbaum had sent on his behalf, and turned to a more precious offer. He told Rosenbaum that the Tzemach Tzedek's autograph was 'dearer to us than any wealth,' and asked him to send it by registered mail to Lubavitch, while books should go via Königsberg.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab accepts Rosenbaum's first will from Marienbad
summary_en: On 23 Tammuz 5668 the Rebbe Rashab wrote from Marienbad acknowledging a copy of Rosenbaum's will and praising him for ordering his affairs as a God-fearing person should.
story_body: Reb Avraham Chaim drafted a will in 5668 and sent a copy to the Rebbe Rashab. On 23 Tammuz 5668 the Rebbe replied from Marienbad commending him for arranging his affairs—'as a God-fearing and sensible man should do'—and blessing him with long life, livelihood, peace of mind for Torah and avodah, and good health.

title_en: Rosenbaum writes private will for son Yaakov, designating burial in New York
summary_en: On 2 Iyar 5671 Rosenbaum wrote a private will instructing his son Yaakov that he be buried in the New York chevra plot and that 1,050 dollars be transmitted as tzedakah to the Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: On 2 Iyar 5671 (April 30, 1911) Reb Avraham Chaim wrote a personal will to his son Yaakov. He insisted on burial in the New York chevra plot, refusing offers from New Haven where R' David Schifrin lived. He also reminded his son that 1,050 dollars from the estate were earmarked as tzedakah for the Rebbe, to be sent through his brother R' Zalman.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz recalls Rosenbaum's Tzemach Tzedek gift in 5696 letter
summary_en: On 12 Tishrei 5696 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' David Schifrin recalling how Rosenbaum had years earlier sent the Rebbe Rashab a handwritten power-of-attorney of the Tzemach Tzedek, a gift the Rebbe had cherished greatly.
story_body: In a letter dated 12 Tishrei 5696 (Igrot Kodesh vol. 3 #803), the Rebbe Rayatz reminded R' David Schifrin that many years earlier the chassid Avraham Chaim Rosenbaum had presented the Rebbe Rashab with a handwritten power-of-attorney signed by the Tzemach Tzedek. The Rebbe Rashab had treasured the gift, and the memory was preserved in the Rebbe Rayatz's correspondence decades later.

title_en: Birth of Rebbe Rashab in Lubavitch
summary_en: Rabbi Shalom DovBer Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born in Lubavitch on 20 Marcheshvan.
story_body: Rabbi Shalom DovBer Schneersohn (Rashab) was born in Lubavitch on 20 Marcheshvan 5621. He was the son of Rebbe Maharash. He would later become the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe and founder of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva system.

title_en: Histalkus of Rebbe Maharash
summary_en: Rebbe Maharash passed away on 13 Tishrei 5643, leaving his 22-year-old son Rashab.
story_body: On 13 Tishrei 5643, Rebbe Shmuel Schneersohn (Maharash) passed away. His son Rashab was still in his 22nd year. Though he composed maamarim and recorded them, Rashab did not yet agree to formally accept the leadership of the Chabad movement.

title_en: Rashab's first public maamar on Sukkos
summary_en: Rashab delivered his first public maamar 'Keser Yitnu Lecha' on the second day of Sukkos 5643.
story_body: On the second day of the festival of Sukkos in 5643, Rashab delivered his first public Chassidic discourse, beginning 'Keser Yitnu Lecha.' This marked his first public teaching following his father Maharash's passing earlier that month.

title_en: Rashab formally accepts Chabad leadership
summary_en: After eleven years, Rashab accepted the full yoke of Chabad leadership in 5654.
story_body: In 5654 (1893/4), Rashab fully accepted the leadership of the Chabad movement, including holding regular yechidus, responding to written queries for guidance, and permitting his Chassidic discourses to be transcribed and distributed. He had hesitated to assume formal leadership for over a decade after his father's passing.

title_en: Founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch
summary_en: Rashab founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in summer 5657.
story_body: In the summer of 5657, Rashab established the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch. The yeshiva initially operated in various rooms of the Rebbe's courtyard. It would continue operating in Lubavitch for over twenty years before relocating during World War I.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim expands into main hall
summary_en: Tomchei Tmimim student numbers grew enough to require using the main hall (Zal) in 5661.
story_body: In 5661, the number of students at Tomchei Tmimim had grown sufficiently that classes began being held in the main hall (Zal) of the courtyard in Lubavitch.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim builds dedicated kitchen and dining hall
summary_en: A kitchen and dining hall were built in the Lubavitch courtyard for yeshiva students in 5662.
story_body: In 5662, a kitchen and dining hall were constructed in the Lubavitch courtyard to serve Tomchei Tmimim students. This facility lasted for several years until the yeshiva grew further and required additional building expansion.

title_en: Lubavitch mikvah rebuilt in courtyard
summary_en: After earlier plans were blocked by local opposition, the Lubavitch courtyard mikvah was rebuilt and reached the spring waters in Elul 5667.
story_body: Following a failed attempt in 5666 to build a mikvah on one side of the courtyard due to opposition from non-Jewish neighbors near their church, Rashab rebuilt the existing mikvah at a deeper level during summer 5667. On 5 Elul 5667 he wrote of his joy that the diggers had reached the spring waters.

title_en: Lubavitch mikvah building reconstruction
summary_en: Rashab built a stone structure over the rebuilt mikvah during summer 5669.
story_body: In summer 5669, Rashab oversaw construction of a stone wall building over the Lubavitch mikvah, with internal partitions of timber. This mikvah served the community until the family's evacuation to Rostov in 5676.

title_en: Rashab and family flee Lubavitch for Rostov
summary_en: As the German army approached during WWI, Rashab and his family fled Lubavitch and settled in Rostov-on-Don in early 5676.
story_body: At the start of 5676 (late 1915), with World War I raging and the German army advancing toward the Lubavitch region, Rashab and his household were forced to flee Lubavitch. After spending several days in Orel, they settled in Rostov-on-Don, deep within the Russian interior. The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva also relocated.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim relocates from Lubavitch
summary_en: After over 20 years in Lubavitch, Tomchei Tmimim relocated to Kremenchug and other cities in 5678.
story_body: In 5678, Tomchei Tmimim left Lubavitch after operating there for over twenty years. The yeshiva relocated to Kremenchug and other Russian cities as the wartime disruption continued. The Lubavitch era of the yeshiva had come to an end.

title_en: Histalkus of Rashab in Rostov
summary_en: Rashab passed away in Rostov on 2 Nissan 5680.
story_body: On 2 Nissan 5680, Rebbe Shalom DovBer Schneersohn passed away in Rostov-on-Don. His passing transferred leadership of Chabad to his only son, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz). At the time of his passing, Rashab held funds entrusted by R' Asher of Nikolayev for his unmarried daughter's dowry.

title_en: Death of R' Avraham Chaim, chassid in New York
summary_en: R' Avraham Chaim, a senior chassid who emigrated to New York, passed away on the first day of Chanukah 5675.
story_body: R' Avraham Chaim ben Dov Ber passed away on 25 Kislev 5675 (first night of Chanukah). He left a detailed will specifying no eulogies, no newspaper announcements, and burial directly touching the earth per the Zohar. Decades later in 5760, his grave was located not at the Achuzas Olam plot but at Mount Zion cemetery in Brooklyn, correcting an earlier transcription error that had given his death year as 5674.

title_en: R' Avraham Dovid Lavut moves to Nikolayev as rabbi
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel, moved from Romanovka to serve as rabbi of Nikolayev in 5616.
story_body: In 5616, Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, the grandfather of the Rebbe (Ramash) and author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel, moved from his rabbinic post in Romanovka to become rabbi of Nikolayev. He would serve as rabbi of Nikolayev until his passing in 5650.

title_en: Chassidim of Nikolayev outgrow single beis midrash
summary_en: In 5649 the growing Nikolayev Chabad community required a second synagogue, prompting R' Asher Grossman to begin efforts to build one.
story_body: By 5649, the Chabad community in Nikolayev had grown so large that a single beis midrash no longer sufficed. R' Asher Grossman began efforts to build an additional synagogue. On 8 Tevet 5649, the city's rabbi, Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, wrote forbidding him from splitting off into a separate minyan now that the decision to build a new shul for the whole community had been made.

title_en: Passing of R' Avraham Dovid Lavut, rabbi of Nikolayev
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, author of Kav Naki and Shaar HaKollel, passed away on 18 Adar 5650 in Nikolayev.
story_body: On 18 Adar 5650, Rabbi Avraham Dovid Lavut, grandfather of the future Rebbe (Ramash), passed away. He left a written request that the chassidim of Nikolayev appoint his grandson Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky as his successor, and that the chassidim of Romanovka appoint his son-in-law R' Isser Yanovsky. The Nikolayev appointment was carried out; Romanovka instead appointed R' Shaymen Atkin.

title_en: Birth of Chaya Mushka, daughter of R' Asher Grossman
summary_en: Chaya Mushka, second daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev, was born in 5649.
story_body: In 5649, after many years following the marriage of her elder sister, Chaya Mushka was born to R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev. She would later marry R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel of Pahar in 5666.

title_en: Birth of R' Shmuel Grossman in Nikolayev
summary_en: R' Shmuel Grossman, son of R' Asher of Nikolayev, was born in 5650.
story_body: About a year after his sister Chaya Mushka's birth, R' Shmuel Grossman was born in Nikolayev in 5650 to R' Asher Grossman. On 4 Elul 5650, Rashab responded to R' Asher's question about hiring a wet nurse given his wife's weakened state after the births. R' Shmuel would later study in Tomchei Tmimim and serve as shochet.

title_en: R' Yosef Eliezer Friedman appointed rabbi of Hadiach
summary_en: Rabbi Yosef Eliezer Friedman was appointed rabbi of Hadiach in 5654, after R' Isser Yanovsky's candidacy did not materialize.
story_body: In 5654, Rabbi Yosef Eliezer Friedman became rabbi of Hadiach, the city associated with the burial place of the Alter Rebbe. The post had been considered for R' Isser Yanovsky two years earlier, when Rashab wrote on 15 Adar 5652 endorsing such an appointment, but that arrangement never came to fruition.

title_en: R' Isser Yanovsky appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog
summary_en: R' Isser Yanovsky was appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog in Kherson province around 5654/5.
story_body: Around 5654/5, R' Isser Yanovsky was appointed rabbi of the town of Krivoy Rog in Kherson province, not far from Nikolayev. Rashab's letter of 23 Marcheshvan 5655 references his receipt of letters from both Kremenchug and Krivoy Rog, apparently related to this appointment.

title_en: Publication of the corrected Tanya edition (Vilna 5660)
summary_en: Rashab issued the corrected edition of Tanya printed in Vilna 5660, edited by R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev.
story_body: In 5660, Rashab published a corrected edition of the Tanya in Vilna. The proofreading was performed by R' Asher Grossman, shochet of Nikolayev, whom Rashab called 'the chief compiler' in letters of that year. R' Asher's signed 'Modaa Rabba' notice has appeared in every subsequent edition of the Tanya.

title_en: Marriage of Chaya Mushka Grossman to R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel
summary_en: Chaya Mushka Grossman married R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel of Pahar, a Tomchei Tmimim alumnus, in 5666.
story_body: In 5666, Chaya Mushka, daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev, married R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel of Pahar, a student of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. On 6 Av 5666 Rashab wrote R' Asher congratulating him on the engagement. After their wedding, R' Yosef became shochet in Kislovodsk.

title_en: Death of R' Isser Yanovsky, rabbi of Krivoy Rog
summary_en: R' Isser Yanovsky, rabbi of Krivoy Rog and great-uncle of the Rebbe (Ramash), passed away in winter 5668.
story_body: In winter 5668, R' Isser Yanovsky passed away. He had served as rabbi of Krivoy Rog for about fifteen years and had traveled to Carlsbad for medical treatment in 5666 with Rashab's support. On 21 Adar I 5668, Rashab wrote his father-in-law R' Asher requesting that any valuable items, especially writings from Rebbeim, found in R' Isser's estate be sent to him.

title_en: R' Aleksander Sender Yudasin appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog
summary_en: R' Aleksander Sender Yudasin, a Tomchei Tmimim alumnus, was appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog with rabbinical certificate dated 14 Marcheshvan 5683.
story_body: After approximately fifteen years without clear succession following R' Isser Yanovsky's death, R' Aleksander Sender Yudasin was appointed rabbi of Krivoy Rog in early 5683. His rabbinical certificate is dated 14 Marcheshvan 5683. Yudasin was an alumnus of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.

title_en: Death of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev
summary_en: R' Asher Grossman, longtime shochet of Nikolayev and editor of Tanya, passed away on 15 Marcheshvan 5680.
story_body: R' Asher Grossman, shochet of Nikolayev and one of the leading chassidim of Rashab and Maharash, passed away on 15 Marcheshvan 5680. He had served as shochet of Nikolayev until at least 5678 and edited Rashab's corrected Tanya edition. Before his death he left dowry funds with Rashab for his still-unmarried daughter Chaya Frieda, which transferred to Rayatz after Rashab's passing months later.

title_en: Marriage of R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky to Chaya Frieda Grossman
summary_en: R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky married Chaya Frieda Grossman in 5681 after consulting Rayatz and visiting the Ohel.
story_body: In 5681, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky (born Mogilev 5657, studied in Lubavitch 5671-5677) married Chaya Frieda Grossman, youngest daughter of R' Asher of Nikolayev. He inquired about the shidduch from Rayatz, who instructed him to travel to the Ohel to ask Rashab. After the wedding, he received the dowry funds R' Asher had entrusted before his death.

title_en: Kazarnovsky family emigrates from Russia to USA
summary_en: After several years in Russia, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky and family emigrated to the United States in 5687.
story_body: In 5687, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky and his family emigrated from Russia to the United States. They first settled in Rochester, New York, where he served as rabbi of the Ein Yaakov synagogue, before moving to New York.

title_en: Kazarnovsky becomes rabbi of Bensonhurst congregations
summary_en: Kazarnovsky was appointed rabbi of Bnei Yitzchak and Tiferes Yisrael in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, with Rayatz's blessing on 21 Tevet 5689.
story_body: In winter 5689, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky was appointed rabbi of both Bnei Yitzchak and Tiferes Yisrael synagogues in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, where he served for the rest of his life. On 21 Tevet 5689, Rayatz wrote congratulating him and praying he would succeed in providing proper Torah teaching.

title_en: Founding of Achos Hatmimim in Brooklyn
summary_en: Achos Hatmimim, a Chabad study group for girls, was founded in Brooklyn in 5698 with Kazarnovsky as one of three appointed mashpi'im.
story_body: In 5698, the Achos Hatmimim study group for Chabad girls was established in Brooklyn. Rayatz appointed R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky as one of three mashpi'im to serve as 'shepherds' of this group of young women.

title_en: Rayatz arrives in New York from Europe
summary_en: Rayatz arrived safely in New York on 9 Adar Sheni 5700, after being rescued from Nazi-occupied Europe.
story_body: On 9 Adar Sheni 5700, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (Rayatz) arrived safely in New York after being rescued from Nazi-occupied Europe. R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky immediately began searching for a building to serve as the Chabad headquarters and the Rebbe's residence. On 13 Nissan, Rayatz wrote thanking him for these efforts.

title_en: Chabad purchases 770 Eastern Parkway as movement headquarters
summary_en: At the end of summer 5700, Chabad purchased the building at 770 Eastern Parkway as its central headquarters.
story_body: At the end of summer 5700, the Chabad movement purchased the building at 770 Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn. From that point on, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky was responsible for managing the building. He later led the expansion construction of the enlarged main synagogue in 5719-5720, built on what had previously been the courtyard.

title_en: Chabad purchases Montefiore cemetery section
summary_en: In 5702 R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky arranged the purchase of the Chabad section at Montefiore Cemetery in Queens.
story_body: In 5702, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky arranged the purchase of the Chabad section at Montefiore Cemetery. This is the cemetery that would later house the Ohel of Rayatz and the Rebbe.

title_en: Death of R' Yosef Garfinkel in wartime exile
summary_en: R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel passed away on 28 Nissan 5703 in Ferghana while in WWII exile.
story_body: On 28 Nissan 5703, during the World War II evacuation of Chabad families from Russia, R' Yosef Shmuel Garfinkel passed away in exile in Ferghana, Uzbekistan. His widow Chaya Mushka, along with their son Nechemia Sholom Rephael and daughter Rivka, later left Russia during the 5706-7 mass emigration of Chabad chassidim.

title_en: R' Shmuel Grossman appointed director of Tomchei Tmimim in Wegscheid DP camp
summary_en: After leaving Russia in 5707, R' Shmuel Grossman served as director of the newly founded Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in the Wegscheid DP camp in Austria.
story_body: Following his emigration from Russia in 5707, R' Shmuel Grossman served for a period as director of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva that was established at the Wegscheid displaced persons camp in Austria. He later moved to Paris before eventually settling in London.

title_en: R' Shmuel Grossman becomes shochet in London
summary_en: R' Shmuel Grossman moved from Paris to London to serve as shochet in 5708, with blessings from both Rayatz and the future Rebbe.
story_body: In 5708, R' Shmuel Grossman moved from Paris to London after receiving a visa through his brother-in-law R' Asher Abramson. On 10 Nissan 5708 he wrote Rayatz seeking approval, which Rayatz granted. On 3 Av 5708, the future Rebbe wrote to him expressing satisfaction at hearing he had not only settled successfully but was also engaging in outreach work to strengthen Chassidus and Torah observance.

title_en: Founding of Kfar Chabad vocational school
summary_en: The Rebbe founded the Beis Sefer Lemelacha vocational school in Kfar Chabad in 5716, appointing Kazarnovsky as his emissary for the dedication.
story_body: In 5716, the Rebbe founded the Beis Sefer Lemelacha (vocational school) in Kfar Chabad, Israel. He appointed R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky as his personal emissary for the dedication ceremony, and Kazarnovsky subsequently served as director of the fund supporting the institution.

title_en: Death of Chaya Mushka Garfinkel in New York
summary_en: Chaya Mushka Garfinkel, daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev, passed away in New York on Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5736.
story_body: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5736, Chaya Mushka Garfinkel passed away in New York. She had emigrated from Russia in 5706-7 with her children after her husband's death in wartime exile, and was buried in New York.

title_en: Death of R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky
summary_en: R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky passed away on 7 Marcheshvan 5743 after decades of service to Chabad institutions.
story_body: On 7 Marcheshvan 5743, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky passed away. His tombstone records his energetic work for Chabad institutions in Eretz Yisrael, his role as one of the planters of the Chabad orchard in America, his closeness to the Rebbeim, his decades of rabbinical service, and his outreach work, particularly with youth, up until his final day.

title_en: Death of Chaya Frieda Kazarnovsky
summary_en: Chaya Frieda Kazarnovsky, youngest daughter of R' Asher Grossman, passed away on 11 Nissan 5747.
story_body: On 11 Nissan 5747, Chaya Frieda Kazarnovsky passed away, almost five years after her husband R' Shlomo Aharon. She was the youngest daughter of R' Asher Grossman of Nikolayev and had married R' Shlomo Aharon in 5681.

title_en: Publication of 'Toldos Avraham Chaim' book
summary_en: The biographical work 'Toldos Avraham Chaim' was published at the start of 5758, including the detailed will of R' Avraham Chaim.
story_body: At the start of 5758, the book 'Toldos Avraham Chaim' was published, including on pages 62-64 the detailed will of R' Avraham Chaim. The will requested burial in Achuzas Olam cemetery in New York. Following publication, various searches were undertaken to locate the original Chabad cemetery plot in New York.

title_en: R' Avraham Chaim's grave located at Mount Zion cemetery
summary_en: After 5760 Tishrei, R' Yisrael Mordechai Kozaminsky located R' Avraham Chaim's grave at Mount Zion cemetery in Brooklyn.
story_body: After Tishrei 5760, R' Yisrael Mordechai HaLevi Kozaminsky discovered through a Brooklyn Charedi newspaper that R' Avraham Chaim's gravestone was at Mount Zion cemetery in Brooklyn rather than the Achuzas Olam plot in Staten Island where searchers had been looking. Upon visiting with R' Meir Simcha Abramovich, he confirmed the gravestone and corrected the recorded death year from 5674 to 5675.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab and family leave Lubavitch for Rostov
summary_en: On Sunday, 16 Marcheshvan 5676, the Rebbe Rashab departed Lubavitch with his entire household.
story_body: At 11 a.m. on Sunday, 16 Marcheshvan 5676 (24 October 1915), Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn left Lubavitch with his family, intending to return the following summer. He took the Rebbeim's manuscripts and a limited selection of books, while the bulk of the library — thousands of volumes in 35 crates — was deposited with the chassid R' Zalkind Persitz in Moscow. The hoped-for return never came, and a year-after-year exile began.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab arrives in Rostov-on-Don
summary_en: After a stopover in Orel, the Rashab reached Rostov on Wednesday morning, 26 Marcheshvan 5676.
story_body: Leaving Lubavitch on 16 Marcheshvan, the Rashab's party traveled some 29 hours to Orel, remained there until 25 Marcheshvan, then took the express train and arrived in Rostov at 10 a.m. on Wednesday, 26 Marcheshvan 5676. His internal Russian passport was stamped two days later, on 23 October 1915 (Julian) — 28 Marcheshvan. Rostov would remain the seat of Chabad leadership for the rest of his life.

title_en: Rashab moves into rented Rostov apartment on Pushkinsky Street
summary_en: On Friday, 5 Kislev 5676, the Rashab's household entered their first rented apartment in Rostov.
story_body: After two weeks in a hotel and a difficult search for housing, the Rashab moved his family into an apartment on Pushkinsky Street on erev Shabbos, 5 Kislev 5676. He described the rooms as good and high-ceilinged on a wide street, but complained in a Chanukah letter that the landlord was unpleasant and spoke improperly. The 19 Kislev farbrengen that year was held in this new apartment.

title_en: Final Tomchei Temimim students leave Lubavitch
summary_en: By the end of summer 5678, the last group of Tomchei Temimim students departed Lubavitch.
story_body: Although the Rashab left Lubavitch in late 1915, the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva students remained behind to learn for another two and a half years. Before the final group departed at the end of summer 5678 (1918), they organized the belongings left behind and buried valuables deep in the cellar of the Rebbe's house for safekeeping. The move ended Lubavitch's centuries-long role as the seat of Chabad.

title_en: Rashab purchases courtyard property at Bratsky Pereulok 44 in Rostov
summary_en: Amid revolution and nationalization, the Rashab bought a large two-story house with courtyard at Bratsky Pereulok 44.
story_body: After two years in the Pushkinsky apartment, in 5678 the Rashab moved to buy a substantial building — roughly 16 by 32 meters, two stories with a basement — at Bratsky Pereulok 44. The purchase fell during the chaotic onset of the Russian Civil War and Bolshevik nationalization of property; the down payment of 50,000 was made in January, and the Rashab wrote on 28 Adar that confirmation of the deed and the renovations were uncertain. The deal was nonetheless completed, and by the end of that summer the family moved in, with public prayers held there from Tishrei 5679 onward.

title_en: Bolsheviks requisition rooms in the Rashab's Rostov home
summary_en: In the week before 3 Kislev 5681, Soviet authorities seized rooms in the Rebbe's house.
story_body: Writing on the eve of 3 Kislev 5681, the Rashab reported that the previous week a 'rekvizitsia' had been carried out on his home — the two upper and lower wings, plus the room beside his hall and the corner room facing his bedroom. With great effort he managed to retain his own room, but his son's household lost their granddaughter Chana's room. 'We are now surrounded by neighbors,' he wrote; intervention had been useless.

title_en: Threat to nationalize the Rashab's Rostov home in summer 1923
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 5683 the Rayatz reported that authorities wished to nationalize the family's Rostov house.
story_body: In a letter dated Rosh Chodesh Elul 5683, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn relayed his mother's news that the authorities intended to nationalize the Rostov home. In the event, no further confiscation occurred that summer, and the Rebbe's household remained in the building another half year. The episode underscored the constant precariousness of Chabad's headquarters under Soviet rule.

title_en: House search and arrest threat force Rayatz to leave Rostov
summary_en: On 11 Nissan 5684 Soviet agents searched Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak's home and offered exile in lieu of arrest.
story_body: On 11 Nissan 5684, authorities conducted a search of the Rayatz's Rostov home and prepared to arrest him. The matter was resolved by an agreement that he would avoid imprisonment if he left Rostov for another city. The Rayatz and his family relocated to Leningrad shortly thereafter, and the Bratsky Pereulok house passed to local tenants, ending nearly a decade as the center of Chabad.

title_en: Gentiles seal the Rashab's underground mikvah in Rostov
summary_en: In summer 5684, after the Rayatz's departure, the mikvah built in the Rostov house was sealed and floored over.
story_body: Following the Rayatz's forced relocation in Nissan 5684, the new occupants of the Bratsky Pereulok house sealed up the ritual bath that the Rashab had constructed in the basement and laid the basement floor over it. The mikvah — a 'mikvah on mikvah' design the Rashab had personally specified in detailed letters from Slavyansk — would remain hidden for more than seventy years.

title_en: Rashab's Rostov home redeemed by Chabad
summary_en: In Marcheshvan 5758, several apartments on the upper floor of the Rashab's former Rostov residence were purchased.
story_body: After more than seven decades in foreign hands, in Marcheshvan 5758 the upper floor of the Rebbe's Rostov home was reclaimed through the purchase of several small apartments. The acquired rooms included most of the Rashab's living quarters: the 'zal' where he delivered chassidic discourses on Shabbos and yom tov and held yechidus, the dining room where he farbrenged, and the porch where the sukkah had stood.

title_en: Hidden Rostov mikvah uncovered intact on Lag B'Omer
summary_en: On Lag B'Omer 5758, excavators found the Rashab's sealed mikvah preserved beneath the basement floor.
story_body: Guided by the testimony of elder chassidim who had studied in Rostov decades earlier, workers on Lag B'Omer 5758 began excavating the suspected location of the Rashab's hidden mikvah. Beneath the basement floor they found the mikvah whole, and continuing to dig they exposed the lower reservoir — still holding the rainwater the Rebbeim had used to fill it, sealed there since 1924.

title_en: Founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva
summary_en: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was founded on 15 Elul 5657 by the Rebbe Rashab, with branches in Lubavitch and Zembin.
story_body: On 15 Elul 5657 (September 12, 1897), the Rebbe Rashab founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva, with R' Chanoch Hendel overseeing the Lubavitch branch and R' Shmuel Gronem Esterman overseeing the Zembin branch in Minsk province. The yeshiva was established to strengthen young men in Torah study and fear of Heaven amid growing Haskalah and Zionist movements. It became the central Chabad yeshiva network.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab opens letter campaign to youth
summary_en: Before founding the yeshiva in 5657, the Rebbe Rashab issued a general letter to young men and their parents about conduct and study.
story_body: In 5657, prior to founding Tomchei Tmimim, the Rebbe Rashab turned to youth and parents in a general letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 68) regarding their conduct and studies. He also waged battle against schools being established by the Society for the Diffusion of Enlightenment and by the ICA. This concern for the next generation motivated the founding of the yeshiva.

title_en: Rashab gathers group of bachurim as 'yoshvim'
summary_en: In 5654 the Rebbe Rashab gathered 16-17 young men as 'yoshvim' in Lubavitch, the seed that would become Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: In 5654 (1894), the Rebbe Rashab refused requests from Baron Ginzburg and Chovevei Tzion, and instead gathered a group of 16-17 bachurim, sons of chassidic balebatim, who came to Lubavitch as 'yoshvim' to study. This group became the foundation of Tomchei Tmimim, which the Rebbe saw as a vessel that would withstand both the Haskalah and Zionist movements.

title_en: Reb Shraga Feivish Zalmanov arrives in Lubavitch
summary_en: R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov first came to study in Lubavitch in 5655, between Pesach and Shavuot.
story_body: In 5655 (1895), between Pesach and Shavuot, R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov arrived in Lubavitch to study among the 'yoshvim'. He later recorded his memories of that period, describing how R' Chanoch Hendel would teach Tanya daily between Mincha and Maariv to the young men. The Rebbe Rayatz mentioned his arrival in Sefer HaSichot 5702.

title_en: R' Yechiel Heilprin among yoshvim during mourning year
summary_en: R' Yechiel Heilprin was among the yoshvim in Lubavitch in 5643, the year of mourning for the Rebbe Maharash.
story_body: R' Yechiel Heilprin was among the yoshvim in Lubavitch during 5643 (1883), which was the year of mourning of the Rebbe Rashab for his father, the Rebbe Maharash. From 5660 onwards, R' Yechiel served as a shadar (emissary) for Tomchei Tmimim, raising funds for the yeshiva.

title_en: Yeshiva relocated from Zembin to Lubavitch
summary_en: On the night of Simchas Torah 5659, the Rebbe Rashab announced that the yeshiva's main location was being moved from Zembin to Lubavitch.
story_body: On the night of Simchas Torah 5659 (1898), during the hakafot, the Rebbe Rashab publicly announced that the yeshiva, which had until then been based in Zembin in Minsk province, would henceforth be established in Lubavitch. In its first year, the main yeshiva had been in Zembin under R' Shmuel Gronem, while a smaller group of students remained in Lubavitch.

title_en: Death of R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel
summary_en: R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel, mashpia in Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch, passed away on 21 Tevet 5660.
story_body: R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel, who served as mashpia for the Lubavitch branch of Tomchei Tmimim from its founding, passed away on 21 Tevet 5660 (1900). His role was filled in the summer of 5660 by R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel as chief mashpia. The Rebbe Rashab was at the medicinal springs in Kharkov at the time and corresponded with his son about the appointment.

title_en: Rashbatz appointed chief mashpia
summary_en: In summer 5660, R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftel was appointed chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch.
story_body: In the summer of 5660 (1900), following the passing of R' Chanoch Hendel Kugel, R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel was appointed chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. He had previously taught the Rebbe Rashab's son in Lubavitch from 5654 onwards. Rashbatz served until his passing on 15 Sivan 5665.

title_en: R' Zev Wolf Lewitin appointed mashgiach
summary_en: At the start of Adar Rishon 5660, R' Zev Wolf Lewitin was appointed mashgiach over nigleh studies in Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: At the start of the month of Adar Rishon 5660, by call of the menahel, R' Zev Wolf Lewitin, son-in-law of R' Gershon Dov, came to Lubavitch and was appointed mashgiach over the bachurim's study of nigleh. He served as mashgiach until his passing in 5670. R' Yehuda Leib Bodnevitz was simultaneously appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies and R' Michoel Bliner as additional mashpia.

title_en: Inauguration of yeshiva's large hall
summary_en: On 8 Tammuz 5661 the renovated Great Hall in the Rebbe's courtyard was inaugurated as the yeshiva's study hall.
story_body: On the third day, 8 Tammuz 5661 (1901), the Great Hall (30 amos by 30 amos, originally built in 5632 as a prayer space) was renovated and inaugurated as the study hall of Tomchei Tmimim. The funds were donated by R' Yeshaya Berlin, one of the yeshiva's main supporters. The dedication ceremony was held with great splendor.

title_en: Branch opened in Nevel
summary_en: In early summer 5661 a branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in Nevel under R' Yehuda Leib Bodnevitz.
story_body: In early summer 5661 (1901), a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in the town of Nevel. About twenty students were selected and sent with the mashgiach R' Yehuda Leib (Tzites) Bodnevitz, who hailed from Nevel and thus was suited to lead this branch. The Nevel branch lasted about a year and a half before closing in late summer 5662.

title_en: Branch opened in Horodishtch
summary_en: R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin arrived in Horodishtch on 20 Iyar 5661 to lead a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: On 20 Iyar 5661 (1901), R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin arrived in Horodishtch to head a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim, with 20 students under his care. The Rashbatz had been sent ahead by the menahel to organize matters. The branch operated until 5671, when Havlin moved to Hebron to open the Toras Emes yeshiva.

title_en: Zembin branch moves to Kovlitz after fire
summary_en: About two weeks before Shavuot 5660, the entire town of Zembin burned down, forcing the yeshiva branch to relocate to Kovlitz.
story_body: About two weeks before Shavuot 5660 (1900), a terrible fire destroyed the entire town of Zembin where the yeshiva branch was located. All houses, study halls and lodgings burned, and students fled to Lubavitch. After requests from several towns to host the yeshiva, lots were drawn and Kovlitz was chosen. Immediately after Shavuot the students relocated to Kovlitz with R' Shmuel Gronem.

title_en: Branch in Dokshitz opened
summary_en: Following a council in Sivan 5662, a small branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in Dokshitz under R' Yehoshua Lein.
story_body: On 17 Sivan 5662 (1902), founders of the yeshiva society met with the Rebbe Rashab at the country house and decided to open a small branch of Tomchei Tmimim in Dokshitz at the urging of its residents. The avreich R' Yehoshua Lein was appointed as teacher. The branch is mentioned in correspondence through Erev Tisha B'Av 5666.

title_en: Cheder department opened in Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: In 5663-5664 a formal cheder department was opened in Tomchei Tmimim for younger boys.
story_body: While initial discussions about opening a cheder began in summer 5662 with R' Menachem Mendel Diskin teaching eight boys, the cheder department was formally opened in 5663-5664. The Rebbe Rashab sent his brother Rashaz to Mohilev to obtain a permit assuring no government oversight of studies in the cheder. Within three years, the cheder grew into two shiur classes and three chadarim.

title_en: Police raid on Tomchei Tmimim hall
summary_en: In summer 5662, the Mohilev district director and police raided the yeshiva hall following malicious denunciations.
story_body: After Shavuot 5662 (1902), on a Friday afternoon, the district director from Mohilev province arrived at the yeshiva hall with the local police chief and secret police, after denunciations claimed over 200 students were studying illegally. Only about 30 students were present, and the director was impressed by their appearance, but ordered the hall sealed pending official permits. Within a day, after the menahel telegraphed Mohilev, the seal was removed.

title_en: Death of Rashbatz Sheftel
summary_en: R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel, chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim, passed away on 15 Sivan 5665.
story_body: R' Shmuel Betzalel (Rashbatz) Sheftel passed away on 15 Sivan 5665 (1905), after serving as chief mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch for five years. Following his death, R' Shmuel Gronem Esterman (Reshag) from Zembin was appointed in his place. The Zembin branch was simultaneously closed.

title_en: Reshag becomes chief mashpia in Lubavitch
summary_en: Around summer 5665, R' Shmuel Gronem (Reshag) Esterman moved from Zembin to Lubavitch as chief mashpia.
story_body: Following the passing of the Rashbatz on 15 Sivan 5665, R' Shmuel Gronem (Reshag) Esterman was appointed chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch in summer 5665 (1905). The Rebbe Rashab wrote on 15 Menachem-Av 5665 that with Reshag's arrival in Lubavitch, the study of chassidut rose to new heights. He served until his passing in 5681.

title_en: Poalei Tzion attack at yeshiva office
summary_en: On Motzaei Shabbat after Purim 5666, members of Poalei Tzion attacked the yeshiva office in Lubavitch, firing pistols.
story_body: On Motzaei Shabbat after Purim 5666 (1906), after a student named Dovber Davzik who had joined Poalei Tzion was expelled and his belongings confiscated, a group of about 40 men and women from Poalei Tzion came to the courtyard, shooting pistols at the office window. The bullet passed by a guest rabbi from Romanov who was leaning over the table — miraculously no one was hurt. The Rabbanit Rivka (mother of the Rebbe) heard the shots from her nearby home.

title_en: Poalei Tzion attack at Rebbe's summer dacha
summary_en: On 7 Menachem Av 5666, Poalei Tzion members raided the Rebbe Rashab's summer dacha demanding ransom.
story_body: On the night of 7 Menachem Av 5666 (1906), six to eight Poalei Tzion members from Vitebsk came to the Rebbe Rashab's dacha with revolvers, destroyed the dining shed, broke tables, cabinets, and door glass. The Rebbetzin asked to take her terrified children outside but was forced back into the house at gunpoint. The attackers demanded 3,000 rubles. Eventually a settlement and ransom payment was reached during Elul.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab's siyum-pidyon at zaide's tziyun
summary_en: During 5666, the Rebbe Rashab wrote pidyonot at the graves of his grandfather and father seeking protection from Poalei Tzion threats.
story_body: During the Poalei Tzion crisis of 5666 (1906), the Rebbe Rashab wrote pidyonot at the tziyunim of his grandfather the Tzemach Tzedek and his father the Rebbe Maharash. He prayed for great mercy upon himself, his son Yosef Yitzchak, and the students of Tomchei Tmimim, who were being threatened with murder by Poalei Tzion if their financial and personnel demands were not met.

title_en: R' Gershon Chen temporarily appointed mashgiach
summary_en: At the start of 5667, student R' Gershon Chen was appointed acting mashgiach when R' Zev Wolf Lewitin fell ill.
story_body: At the start of 5667 (autumn 1906), when the mashgiach R' Zev Wolf Lewitin fell ill, the student R' Gershon Chen was temporarily appointed in his place. A letter from the Rebbe Rayatz dated 5 Marcheshvan 5667 announced that Chen would supervise order in the Great Hall. When Lewitin recovered, he resumed his post.

title_en: Babinovitch branch opens
summary_en: In summer 5668 a branch of Tomchei Tmimim was opened in Babinovitch under R' Zev Wolf Lewitin and R' Shlomo Risen.
story_body: In summer 5668 (1908), a Tomchei Tmimim branch opened in Babinovitch as an intermediate stage between the chadarim/shiurim and the Great Hall. R' Zev Wolf Halevi Lewitin oversaw nigleh and R' Shlomo Ben Dovid Risen oversaw chassidut. The Rebbe Rashab corresponded about it from Marienbad. The branch later relocated to Shchedrin.

title_en: Death of R' Gershon Dov of Driben
summary_en: In 5671 the rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim Shchedrin, R' Zalman Dov of Driben, passed away.
story_body: In 5671 (1911), the rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim in Shchedrin, the gaon R' Zalman Dov 'der Dribiner', passed away. The yeshiva placed advertisements in newspapers seeking a replacement, and various candidates came to deliver test shiurim before the staff and senior students, but none were chosen.

title_en: R' Gershon Chen leaves Lubavitch for Alexandria
summary_en: In 5671, R' Gershon Chen left Lubavitch to fill his late father-in-law's rabbinical post in Alexandria.
story_body: In 5671 (1911), R' Gershon Chen's father-in-law R' Chaim Leib Atkin, rabbi of Alexandria, passed away, and Chen left Lubavitch to fill the rabbinical position there. In 5679 he opened a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in Alexandria, as recorded in Toldot Chabad b'Russia haSovietit.

title_en: R' Yosef Friedman appointed mashgiach
summary_en: By Shevat 5671, R' Yosef Friedman of Rogachov had been appointed mashgiach replacing R' Zev Wolf Lewitin.
story_body: After the passing of R' Zev Wolf Lewitin, R' Yosef Friedman of Rogachov was appointed mashgiach over nigleh at Tomchei Tmimim, as mentioned in a letter dated 15 Shevat 5671 (1911). He later became rabbi of Ostrovna. R' Yisrael Jacobson recalled him as filling the role of the departed R' Zev Wolf Halevi.

title_en: R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik becomes mashgiach
summary_en: At the start of 5672, R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik was appointed mashgiach over nigleh in Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: At the start of 5672 (autumn 1911), R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik, who had previously been mashgiach over nigleh in Shchedrin, was appointed mashgiach over nigleh at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch. He retained this position until the yeshiva moved to Kremenchug in 5678, where he continued until his death in 5681.

title_en: Death of R' Michoel Bliner
summary_en: R' Michoel Bliner ('Reb Michoel der Alter'), mashpia in Tomchei Tmimim, passed away on Motzaei Shabbat Toldot 5672.
story_body: R' Michoel Bliner, known as 'Reb Michoel der Alter', served as an additional mashpia in Tomchei Tmimim from 5660 until his death on Motzaei Shabbat Toldot 5672 (November 1911). He was renowned for his extreme devotion and once shared with Ben-Zion Dinur how he had crossed the broken Dnieper ice three times to reach the Tzemach Tzedek before Pesach 5625.

title_en: R' Shilem Kuratin appointed mashgiach for chassidut
summary_en: In winter 5672, R' Shilem Kuratin of Disna was appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies at Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: In winter 5672 (early 1912), R' Shilem Kuratin from Disna was appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch. He was known for his deep meditation in prayer and his ability to repeat the Rebbe Rashab's chassidic discourses verbatim. He continued in his role when the yeshiva moved to Kremenchug, until his passing in early Elul 5679.

title_en: R' Avraham Dovid Pevzner becomes mashpia
summary_en: In late 5673, R' Avraham Dovid Pevzner was accepted as a mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Approximately at the end of 5673 (1913), R' Avraham Dovid Pevzner was accepted as a mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch. R' Yisrael Jacobson described him as humble and soft-spoken, but at farbrengens he spoke with great warmth and tailored his words to each listener's spiritual state.

title_en: Pesach seudah at Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: On 23 Nissan 5673, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote about the Pesach seudah at Tomchei Tmimim with 139 students.
story_body: In a letter dated 23 Nissan 5673 (1913), the Rebbe Rayatz described the customary Acharon Shel Pesach seudah at Tomchei Tmimim. The Rebbe Rashab, the menahel, mashgichim, mashpiim, melamdim and office workers ate together with 139 students that year (excluding the younger shiur and cheder students). The meal continued until close to 10 PM the previous evening.

title_en: Founding of Agudat HaTmimim
summary_en: At the start of 5670, the Agudat HaTmimim was founded for alumni of the yeshiva.
story_body: Agudat HaTmimim was founded at the start of 5670 (1909) as a support network for married alumni of Tomchei Tmimim who had taken positions as rabbis, shochtim, merchants and activists. About 45 alumni attended the founding meeting in Lubavitch with the Rebbe Rayatz as chairman. By 14 Tevet 5670, a pamphlet listed about 200 members.

title_en: Boys' division opened for Rostov children
summary_en: In Tevet 5670 a new department opened in Lubavitch for 11-12 year-old boys from Rostov.
story_body: On 7 Tevet 5670 (December 1909), the Rebbe Rashab approved opening a new younger department in Lubavitch, primarily for a group of children from Rostov aged 11-12. This addressed Rostov chassidim's request that their children be educated in Lubavitch, with a special melamed assigned. The Rashab saw this as building Jewish education in Rostov as well.

title_en: Donation for Beis Avraham veRachel building
summary_en: In Adar 5666, the gevir R' Avraham Rosenzweig pledged 8,000 rubles for a stone building for Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Around 16 Adar 5666 (1906), the wealthy R' Avraham Rosenzweig donated 8,000 rubles to build a stone building in Lubavitch called 'Beis Avraham veRachel', housing the chadarim and a dining hall. Construction was delayed by pogroms and the revolutionary upheaval but resumed and was completed around 5671.

title_en: Yeshiva relocation from Lubavitch begins
summary_en: During 5678, the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva relocated in stages from Lubavitch to Kremenchug.
story_body: Following the Rebbe Rashab's departure from Lubavitch in early 5676 and worsening conditions during World War I, the yeshiva students remained until 5678 (1918). The shiurim moved first under R' Yehoshua Arsh to Oryol for about a year and then to Kremenchug, while the Great Hall (Zal) remained until students gradually relocated to Kremenchug. The last farbrengen in Lubavitch took place on Shabbat Mevarchim Elul.

title_en: Volomin branch founded
summary_en: In 5672, a Tomchei Tmimim branch was established briefly in Volomin near Warsaw.
story_body: In 5672 (1912), R' Boruch Sholom HaKohen moved to Volomin near Warsaw, where he committed to fund half the expenses of the local yeshiva if a manager from Lubavitch was sent. The Rebbe Rashab sent R' Mordechai Perlov to lead the yeshiva. Students began preparing to travel to Lubavitch, but the outbreak of World War I in summer 5674 ended the project.

title_en: Death of R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik
summary_en: R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik, mashgiach of Tomchei Tmimim, passed away in Kremenchug in 5681.
story_body: R' Yaakov Boruch Krasik, who served as mashgiach over nigleh in Tomchei Tmimim throughout its years in Lubavitch and continued in Kremenchug after the move in 5678, passed away in Kremenchug in 5681 (1921). His brother R' Eliezer Krasik later wrote a memoir about him in Bitaon Chabad.

title_en: Death of R' Shilem Kuratin
summary_en: R' Shilem Kuratin, mashgiach for chassidut, passed away in Kremenchug on 5 Elul 5679.
story_body: R' Shilem Kuratin, mashgiach for chassidut studies at Tomchei Tmimim from winter 5672, continued in his post when the yeshiva moved to Kremenchug. He passed away on 5 Elul 5679 (1919) in Kremenchug at a relatively young age. The Rebbe Rashab was not told of his passing. R' Alter Simchowitz was later appointed in his place.

title_en: Death of R' Moshe Rosenblatt of Zembin
summary_en: R' Moshe Rosenblatt of Zembin, mashpia for younger students, passed away in Shevat 5675 in Lubavitch.
story_body: R' Moshe Rosenblatt of Zembin was accepted at Tomchei Tmimim in 5669 as a mashpia for younger students. He served until his passing in Shevat 5675 (1915) in Lubavitch. He was known as 'Moshe der Chozer' for his role repeating the Rebbe Rashab's discourses at guest lodgings, and he typically opened each farbrengen with a niggun.

title_en: R' Avraham Zaltzman arrives in Lubavitch
summary_en: R' Avraham Zaltzman arrived to learn at Tomchei Tmimim around Rosh Hashanah 5671.
story_body: R' Avraham Zaltzman recorded in a letter to his sons that he arrived in Lubavitch around Rosh Hashanah 5671 (1910). He progressed through the chadarim — studying with the Vietker melamed, then with Itzcheh, then with the Sener melamed, then with R' Yechiel, then with the Dvinsker R' Yehoshua Arsh, then with R' Shmuel Borisover — before being sent to study in Shchedrin.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz appointed mashgiach in Shchedrin
summary_en: On 16 Iyar 5677, the Rebbe Rashab arranged for R' Alter Simchowitz to be sent to Shchedrin as mashgiach.
story_body: On 16 Iyar 5677 (1917), the Rebbe Rashab wrote that R' Alter Simchowitz, who had come from Eretz Yisrael, should travel via Lubavitch to receive instructions from R' Shilem and from the office, before continuing to Shchedrin as mashgiach for chassidut. Simchowitz, son-in-law of R' Zalman Havlin, stayed in Shchedrin until 5679 when the yeshiva closed and moved to Kremenchug.

title_en: R' Alchanan Dov Morozov appointed mashgiach for chassidut
summary_en: Mid-winter 5668, R' Alchanan Dov Morozov was appointed mashgiach for chassidut in the Great Hall.
story_body: In the middle of winter 5668 (early 1908), R' Alchanan Dov Morozov was appointed mashgiach for chassidut studies in the Great Hall at Tomchei Tmimim. The appointment was announced through a letter from the Rebbe Rashab read by office manager R' Eliezer Kaplan. Morozov later served as secretary to the Rebbe Rayatz and was executed in Petersburg in 5698 (1938).

title_en: Royal decree on religious tolerance
summary_en: On 17 Tevet 5665 the Tsar issued a decree with eight clauses, the sixth dealing with religious tolerance.
story_body: On 17 Tevet 5665 (1905), the Russian Tsar issued an eight-clause decree, the sixth clause of which directed administrative measures to remove obstacles to religious practice for various faiths. This decree raised hopes for the Rebbe Rashab that the Yavneh society he wished to establish to legalize Tomchei Tmimim would now be approved, though it ultimately was not.

title_en: R' Yechezkel Himelstein perishes in Holocaust
summary_en: In 5693 R' Yechezkel Himelstein emigrated from Russia to Riga and headed a Tomchei Tmimim branch in Dankra, Latvia, where he later perished in the Holocaust.
story_body: R' Yechezkel Himelstein, who had served as general manager and mashgiach over the shiurim and chadarim in Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch from 5671, continued in this role through Kremenchug and managed branches in Polotsk, Homel and Cherson. In 5693 (1933) he emigrated from Russia to Riga and headed the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Dankra, Latvia, where he perished in the Shoah.

title_en: Society for Spreaders of Enlightenment founded in Russia
summary_en: The 'Society of Spreaders of Enlightenment' was founded in Russia in 1863 to spread secular learning among Russian Jews.
story_body: Originally named 'Chevra Marbei Haskalah,' the society later changed its name to 'Chevra Mefitzei Haskalah.' It established a wide network of schools and Talmud-Torah institutions across the Pale of Settlement, employing Maskilic teachers and aiming to draw Jewish children toward secular learning and away from traditional observance. The Rebbe Rashab viewed it as a grave spiritual threat and organized sustained opposition against it.

title_en: Crown Rabbinate established in Russia
summary_en: The Russian government established the system of 'Crown Rabbis' (rabbanim mitaam) between 1826 and 1835.
story_body: Russia required rabbis to maintain official registers of births, marriages, and deaths and to communicate with the government in Russian. Since most traditional rabbis could not fulfill these requirements, a system of state-approved 'Crown Rabbis' arose alongside the religious rabbinate, creating a dual rabbinate that persisted until the fall of the Tsarist regime.

title_en: Government rabbinical seminaries founded in Vilna and Zhitomir
summary_en: The Russian government established two seminaries for rabbis and teachers in Vilna and Zhitomir in 1848.
story_body: These seminaries emphasized secular studies and minimized traditional learning, with the government's aim of distancing students from Talmud study and traditional Jewish belief. They became the foundation for training future Crown Rabbis, though most graduates went on to attend universities rather than serve in the rabbinate.

title_en: Russian government establishes Rabbinical Commission
summary_en: Russia established an official Rabbinical Commission in 1848 to convene periodically in Petersburg on religious matters affecting Russian Jewry.
story_body: The commission was a state body that met in the capital approximately every several years to address questions concerning Russian Jewish religious life. Between its founding and the fall of the Tsarist regime, it convened six times, each session lasting one to four months and shaping policy on the rabbinate, education, and communal affairs.

title_en: Russian law confirms melamdim need no certification
summary_en: A Russian law issued in 1893 confirmed that melamdim in the western provinces did not require any certification of secular education.
story_body: Despite ongoing pressure from Maskilim and Russian officials to require state certification (tzenz) of melamdim, the law signed by the Minister of Education preserved the right of traditional teachers to operate cheders without such requirements. The Rebbe Rashab worked over many years to defend this status against repeated attempts to alter it.

title_en: Fifth Rabbinical Commission convenes in Petersburg
summary_en: The Fifth Rabbinical Commission convened in Petersburg in the winter of 1894 and agreed to require religious rabbis to hold secular education certificates.
story_body: Chaired by Rabbi Tzvi Hirsch Rabinowitz of Kovno, son of Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor, the commission accepted a proposal that religious rabbis also be required to obtain secular education certification (tzenz) to manage civil registers. The decision was made without consulting other leading rabbis of the generation, and the Rebbe Rashab only learned of it about three years later, prompting his sustained opposition.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab learns of Fifth Commission's decisions
summary_en: In 1897 the Rebbe Rashab learned of the Fifth Rabbinical Commission's decision and began years of intense efforts against it.
story_body: About three years after the Petersburg commission, the Rebbe became aware that participating rabbis had agreed to require state educational certificates for religious rabbis. He launched a sustained multi-year campaign to prevent the change, arguing that young rabbis with secular certification would be susceptible to heresy and would do more harm than the existing Crown Rabbis.

title_en: Society for Promotion of Enlightenment opens school in Lubavitch
summary_en: The Society for Promotion of Enlightenment opened a school in Lubavitch in the winter of 5659 (1898-99) despite the Rebbe's strenuous opposition.
story_body: Society representative Mordechai Ben-Hillel HaKohen had investigated and recommended Lubavitch as the historic cradle of Chasidism where a Maskilic school could influence the entire Chasidic population. The school first opened in rented quarters with Gedalyahu Weinstein as principal. The Rebbe Rashab personally traveled to Petersburg to plead with Baron Ginzburg to spare Lubavitch this 'shame,' but the appeal failed.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab writes letter against Zionism
summary_en: On 10 Tammuz 5659 (June 18, 1899) the Rebbe Rashab wrote his detailed letter setting out the case against the Zionist movement.
story_body: The letter, preserved as Igrot Kodesh letter 86, articulated the Rebbe's opposition to the political Zionist movement on religious and ideological grounds. It was written the same summer that he dispatched his emissary R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky to the Machzikei HaDat office in Kovno to help unite traditional Jewish leadership against both Zionism and the Haskalah.

title_en: R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky sent to Machzikei HaDat in Kovno
summary_en: In the summer of 1899 the Rebbe Rashab's emissary R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky was stationed at the Machzikei HaDat office in Kovno.
story_body: Madievsky was sent on behalf of the Rebbe Rashab to coordinate with the Machzikei HaDat office headed by R' Yaakov Lifshitz and R' Z. Landa, called by the secular press 'the Black Bureau.' The mission was to unite all 'God-fearing' Jews—rebbes, rabbis, and observant Maskilim—in a counter-offensive against the Zionist movement.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab writes long letter to JCA Paris committee
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab wrote a long letter (Igrot Kodesh 102) to the JCA Paris committee arguing that funds should support Jewish economic life rather than secular schools.
story_body: The Rebbe described the spiritual ruination caused by Mefitzei Haskalah schools and argued that JCA's true mission—aid to suffering Russian Jews—called for establishing factories and employment in the Pale of Settlement, not secular schools for religious children. He proposed redirecting the one-million-franc allocation toward economic relief, and the letter became the foundation document of a years-long lobbying campaign.

title_en: Hamelitz reports Baron Ginzburg secured one million francs from JCA
summary_en: On 1 Adar II 5660 (March 2, 1900) the Hamelitz newspaper reported that Baron David Ginzburg had secured one million francs from JCA in Paris for Mefitzei Haskalah schools.
story_body: The young Baron David Ginzburg traveled to Paris and persuaded the Jewish Colonization Association (JCA), founded by Baron Maurice de Hirsch, to allocate a million francs for schools run by the Society for Promotion of Enlightenment in Russia. When the Rebbe Rashab read of this in Hamelitz, he launched a sustained campaign to redirect the funds away from Maskilic schools and toward economic relief.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab writes letter on JCA schools to R' Moshe Avigdor Chaikin
summary_en: On 21 Av 5660 (August 16, 1900) the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Moshe Avigdor Chaikin in England about the JCA schools.
story_body: The Rebbe described the spiritual damage of the Mefitzei Haskalah schools—including the newly opened school in Lubavitch funded with 5,000 rubles from JCA—and detailed his plan to address the JCA committee in Paris. He asked R' Chaikin to translate his letter into French with the care of one whose soul was engaged in the cause, and revealed that he had personally traveled to Petersburg two weeks earlier to strategize against the schools.

title_en: Rebbe writes to R' Yeshaya Berlin on JCA campaign strategy
summary_en: On 11 Elul 5660 (September 5, 1900) the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R' Yeshaya Berlin urging that an emissary be sent to the Paris JCA committee.
story_body: The Rebbe argued that since Russian Jews desperately needed economic aid—not educational support—JCA had been deceived by the Petersburg committee. He proposed dispatching their own messenger to Paris to make the case directly, expressing cautious optimism that the request could succeed if pressed firmly.

title_en: R' Avraham Avli Persson dispatched to lobby JCA
summary_en: On 16 Cheshvan 5661 (November 8, 1900) the Rebbe wrote that R' Avraham Avli Persson would travel through Vilna, Brisk, and Lodz before heading to Paris on behalf of the JCA campaign.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab chose R' Avraham Avli Persson of Konigsberg to lead the JCA lobbying effort. Persson was to visit Vilna's R' Chaim Ozer Grodzinski, Brisk's R' Chaim Soloveitchik, and Lodz's R' Eliyahu Chaim Meisel to obtain their letters to JCA, then continue to Frankfurt, Karlsruhe, Halberstadt, Fulda, Baden, and finally Paris itself.

title_en: Rebbe summarizes Persson's tour of European rabbis
summary_en: On 22 Tevet 5661 (January 13, 1901) the Rebbe summarized R' Persson's two-month tour of Russian and German rabbis on behalf of the JCA campaign.
story_body: The Rebbe reported on visits to R' Chaim Ozer Grodzinski (whose letter to JCA was strong), R' Chaim Soloveitchik (whose letter was too harsh against committee members), and R' Eliyahu Chaim Meisel (where Persson stayed over two weeks). Persson was now traveling to Berlin and onward to Frankfurt, Karlsruhe, Halberstadt, Fulda, and Baden to gather support from German Orthodox rabbis before continuing to Paris.

title_en: Rebbe writes from Worishofen healing springs on JCA effort
summary_en: On 25 Shevat 5661 (February 14, 1901) the Rebbe Rashab, recuperating at Worishofen's healing springs, met with R' Persson to plan the next phase.
story_body: The Rebbe had traveled to Worishofen for medical treatment and Persson came to him to coordinate strategy. Together they prepared additional letters needed for Persson's mission and discussed how to manage the campaign going forward.

title_en: R' Persson recalled from Paris for Pesach
summary_en: On 9 Nisan 5661 (March 29, 1901) the Rebbe wrote to R' Persson to return home to Konigsberg for Pesach before resuming the Paris mission.
story_body: Persson had spent five weeks in Paris meeting with R' Tzadok Kahn, R' Shmuel Altmann, R' Shlomo Cohen, and JCA president M. Leven, struggling to overturn the Mefitzei Haskalah grant. The Rebbe instructed him to return home for the holiday and then travel back to Paris after Pesach for the JCA committee's late-April session, when the Rebbe himself would also travel to Paris.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab summarizes failed JCA Paris campaign
summary_en: On 19 Sivan 5661 (June 6, 1901) the Rebbe Rashab summarized the failure of the Paris JCA campaign to R' Eliezer Moshe Madievsky.
story_body: The Rebbe described how Baron Ginzburg had retained the JCA committee's full confidence, dismissing the rabbinic protest as 'Chasidism,' and how JCA president Leven had broken his promise to consult Polyakov independently. Although the committee acknowledged the schools' teachers were harmful, they refused to act on the rabbis' protest and merely forwarded the complaints to Petersburg. The Rebbe resolved to convene an assembly of Russian rabbis to escalate the effort.

title_en: Admor R' Shmuel of Slonim visits Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: In 1902 Admor R' Shmuel Weinberg of Slonim traveled to the Rebbe Rashab to discuss founding the Machzikei HaDat society.
story_body: R' Shmuel of Slonim and Rabbi Yosef Shlifer of Slonim had previously sent an emissary, R' Eliezer Yosef Klatzky, in late winter 5660 to engage the Rebbe Rashab. In Tevet 5662 R' Shmuel himself came to Lubavitch to plan a general organization called Machzikei HaDat that would unite multiple Chasidic and rabbinic factions in defense of traditional Judaism.

title_en: JCA halts Mefitzei Haskalah funding mid-grant
summary_en: In Adar 5663 (early 1903) the Rebbe Rashab heard that JCA had withheld the remaining 600,000 francs of the million-franc grant to Mefitzei Haskalah.
story_body: After three years of sustained protest, JCA stopped releasing funds, retaining 600,000 of the original million francs allocated for the Society for Promotion of Enlightenment's schools. The Rebbe speculated in a follow-up letter that the long campaign of rabbinic protests against Mefitzei Haskalah may finally have moved the committee.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab denounces Baron Ginzburg in 19 Kislev address
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5669 (December 12, 1908) the Rebbe Rashab spoke with great bitterness about Baron Ginzburg and the Maskilic school in Lubavitch.
story_body: In his 19 Kislev address the Rebbe denounced 'the architect of the movement in government circles,' Baron Hertz Ginzburg, and recounted that he had pleaded with him 'give me Yavneh'—asking that at least Lubavitch be spared a Mefitzei Haskalah school—and that the baron refused even this minimal concession.

title_en: Rabbinical assembly held in Vilna
summary_en: A rabbinical assembly was convened in Vilna in Iyar 5669 (May 1909) on the question of the Crown Rabbinate.
story_body: After more than a decade of failed attempts to organize a general rabbinical convention against the proposed reform of the Russian rabbinate, an assembly was finally held in Vilna in Iyar 5669. It addressed the dual-rabbinate question that had occupied the Rebbe Rashab and other leading rabbis since the Fifth Rabbinical Commission's decision.

title_en: Sixth Rabbinical Commission convenes in Petersburg
summary_en: The Sixth Rabbinical Commission convened in Petersburg in Adar Sheni 5670 (March 1910) to address Russian Jewish religious affairs.
story_body: The Sixth Commission was the final meeting of the state-convened Rabbinical Commission before the fall of the Tsarist regime. Like its predecessors it addressed matters of the rabbinate, but no change was made to the law on Crown Rabbis; the dual-rabbinate system continued until the Communist takeover.

title_en: Alexander I issues 'Regulations Concerning the Jews'
summary_en: Tsar Alexander I issued the 'Regulations Concerning the Jews,' which included a decree expelling Jews from rural villages.
story_body: These regulations launched a century-long process in which the Pale of Settlement steadily narrowed through ever new restrictions and prohibitions. The expulsion-from-villages decree set the template for later residency limits and gradually concentrated Russian Jewry into overcrowded urban areas of the Pale.

title_en: Pogroms erupt in southern Russia after Alexander II's assassination
summary_en: In the spring of 1881, anti-Jewish pogroms swept through southern Russia in the wake of the assassination of Tsar Alexander II.
story_body: The unrest devastated dozens of communities in the Pale of Settlement and gave the new tsar, Alexander III, a pretext to appoint Interior Minister Nikolai Ignatiev. Ignatiev would draft the punitive 'Temporary Regulations' of 1882, blaming the Jews themselves for the violence directed against them.

title_en: Ignatiev's 'Temporary Regulations' tighten the Pale of Settlement
summary_en: The Committee of Ministers adopted Ignatiev's 'Temporary Regulations,' barring Jews from rural residence and from holding rural property even within the Pale.
story_body: The regulations prohibited Jews from living outside cities and towns within the fifteen Pale provinces and outlawed Jewish-held sales, mortgages and leases on rural real estate beyond the Pale. Although labeled 'temporary,' they remained in force for 33 years until the middle of World War I, devastating Jewish livelihood and packing Jews into overcrowded urban districts.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab appeals to the JCA for industrial relief in the Pale
summary_en: Rebbe Rashab wrote to the Jewish Colonization Association describing catastrophic Jewish poverty in Russia and urging it to build factories in the Pale rather than fund Maskilic schools.
story_body: In a long, anguished letter (Igrot Kodesh #102), the Rebbe portrayed families starving from the combined effects of Pale residency restrictions and the new state monopoly on liquor sales. He argued that funding industrial infrastructure inside the Pale would allow Jews to earn a living where they were trapped by law, rather than supporting the Society for the Diffusion of Enlightenment.

title_en: Tsarist secret committee opens review of Jewish laws
summary_en: A secret committee under the Minister of the Interior was formed to review Russia's Jewish laws; a circular went out in August 1903 soliciting opinions from provincial governors.
story_body: On the eve of Sukkot 5664, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Yeshaya Berlin urging him to use his contacts to influence the governors' replies before the October 1 deadline. The committee, chaired by Interior Minister Vyacheslav Plehve, convened in early January 1904 to weigh partial easings of the Pale alongside new restrictions.

title_en: Kishinev pogrom
summary_en: Approximately 50 Jews were murdered, hundreds wounded and extensive property destroyed in the spring 1903 pogrom in Kishinev.
story_body: The Russian government blamed the Jews themselves, framing the violence as a response to Jewish involvement in revolutionary movements, particularly the socialist Bund. Local officials openly or covertly encouraged the rioters, and Interior Minister Plehve later cited Kishinev as a warning to Jewish notables in St. Petersburg.

title_en: Homel pogrom
summary_en: Ten Jews were murdered, many wounded and significant property looted in the late-summer 1903 pogrom in Homel.
story_body: Like Kishinev earlier that spring, the Homel violence enjoyed at least tacit government backing while officials blamed Jewish revolutionary activity. The two pogroms loomed over the Petersburg assembly of Jewish notables the following winter, with Plehve invoking them as an implicit threat of further violence.

title_en: Plehve rebukes Jewish notables in St. Petersburg
summary_en: Interior Minister Plehve summoned ten leaders of the Petersburg Jewish assembly, led by Baron Ginzburg, and warned that another Kishinev-style pogrom could recur.
story_body: Plehve rebuked the delegation over Jewish youth involvement in revolutionary movements, the alienating effect of Russian schooling on Jewish students, and the agitation of the foreign Hebrew press. He linked any easing of residency laws to internal Jewish reform and explicitly threatened a repeat of the 1903 Kishinev and Homel pogroms. The Rebbe Rashab, then in Paris, received the verbatim transcript with alarm and demanded active community response.

title_en: Rashab urges second Petersburg assembly to prioritize material relief
summary_en: On 17 Shevat 5665, Rebbe Rashab wrote that delegates to Baron Ginzburg's new Petersburg assembly must demand residency and land-purchase rights rather than university access.
story_body: The Rebbe warned that the assembly's lawyers and freethinkers would prioritize educational equality while neglecting Jews' physical survival. He pressed instead for the right to live anywhere in Russia, including villages, and for every Jew to be allowed to purchase at least fifty desyatinas of land in any locality.

title_en: Government-rabbi conference in the Kherson colonies
summary_en: Moshe Krebs, government rabbi of the Kherson Jewish colonies, organized a conference of crown rabbis and presented its conclusions to the Interior Minister in early 1900.
story_body: Krebs's initiative set the stage for a broader gathering of government-appointed rabbis in Nikolaev and alarmed the traditional rabbinic leadership. Religious authorities feared that resolutions adopted by reform-minded crown rabbis would be stamped with state authority and used against traditional Judaism.

title_en: Krebs publishes call for crown-rabbi assembly in HaMelitz
summary_en: On 8 Adar II 5660, Moshe Krebs published a proclamation in HaMelitz announcing a planned April 1900 assembly of government-appointed rabbis in Nikolaev.
story_body: Krebs reported he had already conveyed the conclusions of his Kherson colony rabbinical conference to the Interior Minister.
