story_body: Papov reports that the Schneersohn crates are intact except for one damaged by customs officials, that each crate weighs roughly 15 pud, and that at least 12 wagons would be needed to move the collection. The books are on the third floor accessible only by a manual hoist, and lacking funds to operate it, Papov seals the rooms. The report sets the stage for transfer of the collection from the nationalized Kokorev warehouses to the Rumyantsev Library (later the Lenin Library).

title_en: Rayatz organizes Rashab's manuscripts during the year of aveilus
summary_en: Throughout the mourning year 5680-5681, the Rebbe Rayatz organizes Rashab's manuscripts and prepares detailed indexes.
story_body: Rayatz arranged the maamarim chronologically, one binder per year, adding a handwritten label to each binder and compiling a detailed index of openings. These bound binders are now numbered 2541-2585 in the Library archive. He likewise organized Rashab's letters, and on 19 Marcheshvan 5681 recorded in his diary the count of maamarim and letters then in his possession.

title_en: Rayatz records inventory of manuscripts in his diary
summary_en: On 19 Marcheshvan 5681, Rayatz records in his diary the count of maamarim and letters from his father that are in his possession.
story_body: Following his year-long project of cataloging Rashab's manuscript output, Rayatz committed the inventory totals to writing in his personal diary. This count became one of the reference points for tracking what manuscripts existed in the Rebbe's collection at that moment in the early Soviet period.

title_en: Narkompros authorizes return of Schneersohn library (permit 670)
summary_en: In winter 5681, the Soviet Narkompros education commissariat issues permit number 670 authorizing return of the Schneersohn library to its owner.
story_body: Following an appeal from the Committee of Jewish Synagogues, the scientific libraries department of Narkompros formally resolved to return the books. The authorization carried the number 670, but Rayatz lacked the means to physically remove the books from storage and had nowhere to house them. The crates remained in Moscow and the original permit document was subsequently lost, becoming the centerpiece of a multi-year struggle as later officials disclaimed knowledge of it.

title_en: Rayatz petitions Rumyantsev Library director for return of books
summary_en: During a six-week stay in Moscow in summer 5682, Rayatz writes the Rumyantsev Library director requesting return of his confiscated books.
story_body: Lodging at the home of R. Meir Yaakovson during a stay focused on klal work, Rayatz petitions the library director, recounting the 1921 Narkompros decision in his favor and explaining that the collection had migrated from the nationalized Kokorev warehouses to the Rumyantsev Library only because he had lacked storage. The petition was not honored, and the books remained in the library's possession.

title_en: Rayatz renews request for library return from Leningrad
summary_en: In June 1924, having moved to Leningrad, Rayatz renews his application for return of the library now that he has space to house it.
story_body: In this petition (Beis HaGenazim ch. 63) Rayatz reminds officials of the Narkompros decision in his favor and explains that the obstacle to executing it — lack of housing for the books — has now been removed. He argues that the collection, by its sectarian content, would only interest a narrow circle of Jewish religious scholars, and asks for its return.

title_en: Soviet officials respond to Rayatz with two earlier library transfer decisions
summary_en: In response to Rayatz's renewed petition, officials cite a December 16, 1919 and May 21, 1921 decision transferring the library to the Rumyantsev Museum, now the Lenin State Library.
story_body: The denial referenced decisions of 16 December 1919 and 21 May 1921 by which Narkompros had transferred the Schneersohn library to what had become the Lenin State Public Library, and refused on that basis to return it to Yosef Sholom Berkovich Schneersohn.

title_en: Rayatz petitions Soviet scientific council for library return
summary_en: On 11 Shevat 5685, Rayatz petitions the scientific department council, again emphasizing his lawful ownership of the library now housed in the former Rumyantsev Museum.
story_body: Rayatz describes how the library had been transferred from the former Kokorev warehouses to the museum about a year earlier and still sat in the original Lubavitch crates. He explains that since moving to Leningrad he now has both the space and the need to resume scholarly use of his collection. The appeal is structured around his earlier Narkompros authorization, which library administrators were claiming they could not locate.

title_en: Lenin Library refuses to return Schneersohn collection
summary_en: On 2 Adar 5685, library administrators issue a refusal citing missing registration, scholarly value, and the advice of librarian Shmuel Eisenstadt.
story_body: The refusal letter listed several pretexts: the owners had failed to register the library with the Narkompros libraries department; absent registration it had been handed to the Rumyantsev Museum; librarian Shmuel Eisenstadt had opined the books were of special importance and should not be returned; the library's Jewish section was poor and would be enriched by the collection; and the books would otherwise serve only a narrow circle. The real obstacle was that officials could not locate the 1921 Narkompros authorization. Eisenstadt, a Zionist who later emigrated to Eretz Yisrael, was identified as the personal antagonist behind the refusal.

title_en: Rayatz writes Agudas HaTmimim in America accepting their offer to help recover books
summary_en: On 12 Tammuz 5686, Rayatz writes to the newly founded Agudas HaTmimim 'Beis Rebbi' in the United States, welcoming their initiative to help recover the books taken from Moscow.
story_body: Members of Agudas HaTmimim in America had informed Rayatz they had organized a society called 'Beis Rebbi' as a memorial to past Rebbes, whose aim was to help retrieve the books that had been improperly seized in Moscow. Rayatz responds with encouragement, urging them to consult lawyers and well-connected figures of standing and predicting that their effort would succeed with G-d's help.

title_en: Rayatz urges American Tmimim to mobilize scholarly petition for library
summary_en: On 21 Teves 5687, Rayatz writes Eliyahu Simpson with strategy for a coordinated international campaign of scholars and synagogues to pressure for library return.
story_body: Rayatz reports that his books are currently housed in a former church attached to the Rumyantsev Museum (renamed for Lenin) and that the Yevsektsiya in Belarus has been falsely claiming the library was given to them in perpetuity. He outlines a plan to involve bibliophile associations, prominent scholars in the world of Jewish studies, and synagogue leadership writing to influential figures — particularly to a person whose intervention with Soviet authorities would carry weight — to formally request access to his library for scholarly work.

title_en: Secretariat letter recounts collapse of Moscow library negotiations
summary_en: On 27 Adar Rishon 5687, the secretariat letter (Iggeres 3806) details how Eisenstadt and the library board ultimately denied the return.
story_body: The letter recounts that Rayatz had again obtained a Narkompros authorization through the prominent attorney I. S. Orinson, but when emissary R. Chaim Manesson came to collect the books, library staff confiscated the permit and stalled, eventually claiming the document was lost. When Orinson tried again, no new permit was forthcoming. After more than three years, the library board declared the books were now their property. Eisenstadt — described as acting from personal vengeance against the Rebbe's known anti-Zionist stance — was identified as the driving force.

title_en: Arrest of Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: In 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz is arrested for his work strengthening Torah and Jewish observance in Soviet Russia.
story_body: During the imprisonment, Rayatz worried in his cell about whether the manuscripts in his home would be seized by the authorities. Simultaneously, the future Rebbe — then his son-in-law — quickly distributed the manuscripts among trusted chassidim to hide them, returning them after the liberation. The episode is recorded in Rayatz's prison diary in Likutei Dibburim vol. 4 p. 1246.

title_en: Liberation of Rebbe Rayatz and return of hidden manuscripts
summary_en: On 12 Tammuz 5687, with Rayatz's release confirmed, R. Z. Duchman returns the manuscripts he had hidden during the arrest.
story_body: Duchman later wrote that he had received a large basket of manuscripts (ksvei-yad-kodesh) to hide and on Tuesday 12 Tammuz at 1:30 PM he brought them back. The future Rebbe — sitting in the western side of the great hall — told him as he handed them over: 'I will pay you for your effort with good news, that the Rebbe will arrive in time for Shabbos.' Years later in 5748, when asked whether some manuscripts may not have been returned, the Rebbe replied definitively: 'They were returned immediately!!'

title_en: Rayatz leaves Soviet Russia for Riga
summary_en: At the end of Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz leaves Soviet Russia and settles in Riga, Latvia.
story_body: Forced out at the beginning of 5688 after his imprisonment and exile, Rayatz immediately resumed efforts to recover the library — now from outside Russia. On Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan he wrote to the Soviet embassy in Latvia formally requesting their support in returning the books to him. The Soviet ambassador in Riga promised to intercede, but no concrete result followed in the short term.

title_en: Rayatz petitions Soviet ambassador in Riga for library return
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan 5688, immediately after settling in Riga, Rayatz petitions the Soviet ambassador in Latvia for help returning his library.
story_body: The letter closes with a firm request that the ambassador render every possible cooperation toward recovering and transferring the library to Riga. The ambassador subsequently promised to take up the matter, but in his 3 Teves letter to R. David Shifrin, Rayatz reports that no satisfactory answer had yet been received.

title_en: Rayatz writes Dr. A. Freimann about lost library
summary_en: On 16 Iyar 5688, Rayatz writes scholar Dr. A. Freimann that 'the Schneersohn Lubavitch library' remains in government hands but he hopes for return.
story_body: Writing from exile in Riga, Rayatz tells the noted Judaica scholar Freimann that the library, internationally known as 'the book treasury of the Lubavitcher Rebbe Schneersohn,' was unlawfully seized by the Soviet government during his Rostov exile, and that he draws strength from the hope that with G-d's help it will eventually be returned.

title_en: Future Rebbe makes inventory of Rayatz's manuscript holdings
summary_en: Around 5690, the future Rebbe (then Rayatz's son-in-law) compiles a three-page list of the manuscripts held by Rayatz.
story_body: The list, in the future Rebbe's own hand, notes that pages 1 and 2 are copied from the general index while page 3 records bichlach not found in the index but seen personally — possibly added after the index was compiled. The numbering on the right matches the order arranged by Rashab himself. This list aligns with the 265 bichlach catalogued in Rayatz's general index, suggesting the future Rebbe compiled it after Rayatz entrusted the manuscripts to him.

title_en: Rayatz sends future Rebbe on mission to Hans Gaslar in Berlin
summary_en: On 11 Shevat 5692, Rayatz instructs his son-in-law (the future Rebbe) to enlist Hans Gaslar of Berlin to lobby Minister Weizmann to pressure the Soviets.
story_body: Rayatz writes that he can no longer postpone using personal connections and recommendations to recover the library. He provides detailed identification markers: about 5000 catalogued numbers (Shas, Rambam, Tur, Mikraos), each cross-referenced in the list he kept; bindings mostly in distinctive blue, green, or chocolate-colored cloth. He emphasizes the chillul Hashem of the holy books of the Rebbeim — including ones with their marginal notations — sitting in captivity, and the great mitzvah of rescuing them.

title_en: Rayatz writes Boston Rabbi Rabinowitz seeking Senator Borah's intervention
summary_en: On 23 Sivan 5692, Rayatz writes Rabbi D. M. Rabinowitz of Boston hoping his son Asher will help obtain a letter from Senator Borah to Soviet Foreign Minister Litvinov.
story_body: Rayatz asks whether Rabbi Rabinowitz's son Asher can secure a letter from Senator Borah to Soviet Foreign Commissar Litvinov requesting return of the library according to Rayatz's existing inventory. At the time, the US had not yet recognized the Soviet government, and the senator's intervention did not produce the hoped-for result.

title_en: US Acting Secretary of State Phillips declines formal book intervention
summary_en: On December 19, 1933, US Acting Secretary William Phillips replies that the government cannot formally pressure the Soviets to return the books to a non-citizen.
story_body: Following efforts by R. Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod to mobilize American officials around Litvinov's Washington visit (negotiating US recognition of the Soviet Union), Acting Secretary Phillips writes that 'in view of the fact that Rabbi Schneerson is not a citizen of the United States, this Government is not in a position to take any formal steps to induce the Soviet Government to return to him the books and documents in question.'

title_en: Drabitscher writes Rayatz from Moscow with possible book recovery channel
summary_en: On 7 Tishrei 5695, R. Baruch Drabitscher, rav of Mezhibuzh, writes Rayatz from Moscow about a potential channel through Mezhdunarodnaya Kniga officials.
story_body: Drabitscher reports that R. A. A. Axelrod of Baltimore asked him to use a senior contact at Mezhdunarodnaya Kniga to obtain the Schneersohn libraries, originally taken from the Kokorev warehouses and now in the Lenin Museum. After meeting them, Drabitscher was told they would consider it only if a foreign catalog were submitted and a substantial foreign currency payment offered.

title_en: Rayatz writes Zislin about discreet inquiry on the Kokorev crates
summary_en: In Teves 5696, Rayatz writes chassid R. Zalman Idel Zislin asking him to discreetly locate where the crates from R. Zalka Persitz's storage are now held.
story_body: The letter (4745) instructs Zislin to obtain information about the location of the boxes taken from the bailee R. Zalka Persitz — but without revealing who sent him on the errand. This represents one of the last surviving traces of the active 1930s effort to track the library, before contact was largely lost for fifty years.

title_en: Rebbe references searching Rayatz's general index in Riga
summary_en: On 25 Tishrei 5730, during nichum aveilim for Rashag, the Rebbe recalls searching the general index of his father-in-law in Riga.
story_body: In Sichos Kodesh 5730 p. 719, recorded during the consolation visit for Rashag (Rabbi Shemaryahu Gurary), the Rebbe says 'I looked for this when I was in Riga, in the index of my father-in-law.' The reference confirms the general index was already a working scholarly tool while Rayatz lived in Latvia.

title_en: Rebbe describes Rayatz entrusting manuscripts to him in 5737 sicha
summary_en: In the sicha of 20 Kislev 5737, the Rebbe relates how Rayatz, when forced to leave his home, entrusted the manuscripts to him for safekeeping.
story_body: Published in the supplements to Hemshech BeSha'a SheHikdimu 5672 vol. 3 (1993 edition, p. 12), the sicha describes how, when his father-in-law had to leave his home, Rayatz sought someone he could trust to keep the manuscripts and return them intact — and apparently had no choice but to entrust them to him. This may correspond to the period in which the future Rebbe compiled the three-page manuscript inventory.

title_en: Rebbe affirms all hidden manuscripts were returned after Rayatz's release
summary_en: During the 5748 special mission to Russia, the Rebbe is asked whether some 5687 manuscripts may have been left behind, and answers definitively that all were returned immediately.
story_body: On the special shlichus to Russia in 5748 — documented in 'Yoman HaShlichus HaMeyuchedes' — the question was put to the Rebbe whether perhaps not all the manuscripts hidden during the 5687 arrest had been recovered, and whether it might be worth searching for them. The Rebbe replied: 'They were returned immediately!!' — closing the question on the manuscript dispersal during the 12 Tammuz episode.

title_en: Alter Rebbe settles in Liozna and begins leading White Russian Chassidim
summary_en: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi settled in Liozna and began guiding the Chassidic community in White Russia.
story_body: From 5543 (1783) onward, the Alter Rebbe based himself in Liozna and assumed leadership of the Chabad Chassidim across White Russia. From there, Chabad communities began to organize in Lithuania as well, especially in Vilna and Vidz. This marked the start of a structured Chabad presence in the region.

title_en: Chabad community established in Vidz, Lithuania
summary_en: A Chabad community existed in Vidz no later than 5552, with R' Moshe ben Yitzchak as its head and Eretz Yisrael fund gabbai.
story_body: Records of donations to the Chassidim settled in Tiberias, collected by R' Moshe ben Yitzchak of Vidz, prove that a Chabad kehilla functioned in Vidz from 5552 onward. Dozens of donors from Vidz are listed in the receipts covering the years 5552–5557 (1792–1797). The community grew under his leadership during this period.

title_en: R' Meir Refael's of Vilna draws close to Chassidus
summary_en: R' Meir ben Refael Yaffe of Vilna and his two sons became disciples of the Alter Rebbe.
story_body: Around 5549, the wealthy Vilna chassid R' Meir Refael's together with his sons Shlomo and Yaakov traveled to the Alter Rebbe in Liozna to study Chassidic conduct. He later became the head of the Chabad kehilla in Vilna and a close disciple of the Rebbe. He testified to this date during his interrogation in 5559.

title_en: R' Meir Refael's elected to the Vilna kahal
summary_en: R' Meir ben Refael Yaffe was elected a member of the kahal of Vilna in 5550.
story_body: Despite his Chassidic affiliation, R' Meir Refael's was elected to the Vilna kahal in 5550. In this early period there was no strong opposition in Vilna to the Chassidic kehilla, and the Chassidic minyan operated with the approval of the kahal head R' Moshe ben Asher.

title_en: Chassidic minyan in Vilna moves to R' Meir Refael's home
summary_en: The Chabad minyan in Vilna relocated from R' Eliezer ben Chaim's house to R' Meir Refael's home, with kahal approval.
story_body: Around 5555, the Vilna Chassidic minyan moved from the home of R' Eliezer ben Chaim to the home of R' Meir Refael's. The transfer was approved by Vilna kahal head R' Moshe ben Asher. This arrangement continued until persecutions intensified in 5557.

title_en: Alter Rebbe sends 800 rubles via R' Aryeh Leib to fund Vilna Chassidim
summary_en: R' Aryeh Leib ben Yehoshua Zelig brought 800 ruble assignats from the Alter Rebbe to support the Vilna Chassidic kehilla.
story_body: Around 5556, R' Aryeh Leib ben Yehoshua Zelig of Vilna drew close to Chassidus and traveled three times to the Alter Rebbe in Liozna. The Rebbe entrusted him with a letter and 800 ruble assignats to be delivered to R' Nachum ben Yitzchak, treasurer of the Vilna Chassidic kehilla. Around the same time R' Meir Refael's received two letters from the Rebbe.

title_en: Gabbaim of old Vilna beis midrash decide to oppress Chassidim
summary_en: On 18 Tishrei 5558 the gabbaim of the old beis midrash in Vilna resolved to pressure the Chassidim to abandon their nusach and not raise voices in prayer.
story_body: On the second day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5558, one day before the Vilna Gaon's passing, the gabbaim of the Old Kloiz met to address what they viewed as the Chassidic deviation in prayer. They resolved to harass the 'Karliner' faction, deny them honors and aliyos, and force them to use the standard nusach without raising their voices. This formalized the institutional opposition in Vilna.

title_en: Passing of the Vilna Gaon (Gra)
summary_en: Rabbi Eliyahu of Vilna, the Vilna Gaon, passed away on 19 Tishrei 5558 (3rd day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos).
story_body: The Vilna Gaon, leader of the Mitnagdim, died on the third day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos 5558. His death emboldened R' Moshe ben Asher and other opponents in Vilna to intensify their campaign against the Chassidim. The day after his passing they declared a cherem against the Chabad kehilla.

title_en: Vilna kahal declares cherem against the Chassidim on Hoshana Rabba
summary_en: On Hoshana Rabba 5558 Vilna kahal proclaimed a cherem on the Chassidim, treating any follower as a non-Jew and authorizing a special committee against them.
story_body: One day after the Vilna Gaon's burial, the Vilna kahal proclaimed a sweeping cherem on the Chassidim of the city. The decree, read in every shul amid shofar blasts and extinguished candles, declared Chassidim excommunicated, denied them communal standing, and barred their bread and wine. A committee of five empowered as 'rodef' was authorized to act against them, marking the legal start of the Vilna persecution.

title_en: Beis din ruling forbids R' Meir Refael's from hosting a Chassidic minyan
summary_en: On 21 Adar 5558 the Vilna beis din ruled that R' Meir Refael's could never again host a minyan in his home and must dissociate from the Chassidic 'chevra'.
story_body: After R' Meir Refael's defended himself before the beis din, replying that he had found the truth among the Chassidim rather than within the kahal, the court issued its ruling on 21 Adar 5558. He was barred from hosting any minyan for the rest of his life, ordered to stop supporting the Chassidic rebbes, and required to pray only in the main shul or kloiz. He was also told to make public confession before the appointed officials.

title_en: Imperial provincial decision permits Chassidim of Vilna to pray as they wish
summary_en: On 26 April 1798 the provincial government of Vilna ruled that Chassidim could pray according to their custom and that no fines or corporal punishments could be imposed on them.
story_body: Following the complaint submitted by R' Yehuda ben Eliyahu against the elected committee of five, the cherem, and the looting of his home, the provincial authorities ruled in the Chassidim's favor. On 26 April 1798 the government publicly announced that the Chassidim of Vilna were free to pray as they pleased and that no fines or physical punishments were to be levied against them. The ruling briefly checked the wave of persecution.

title_en: Mitnagdic denunciation submitted to Russian authorities against the Alter Rebbe
summary_en: On 4 Sivan 5558 the Mitnagdim filed a formal denunciation against the Alter Rebbe and the Chassidim of Lithuania with the Russian authorities.
story_body: On 4 Sivan 5558 the Mitnagdim submitted their formal denunciation against the Alter Rebbe and the Chassidim of Lithuania. The text of this denunciation was preserved and published in Kerem Chabad vol. 4. It led directly to the Alter Rebbe's arrest along with thirty Chassidim from Vilna, Vidz, Hamadora, Pandel and Vysokoye-Litovsk at the start of 5559.

title_en: Vidz kahal disavows R' Hirsh ben Yosef's complaint against Vilna
summary_en: On 19 Av 5558 the kahal of Vidz issued a written denial that they had authorized R' Hirsh ben Yosef's complaint against Vilna on behalf of the Chassidim.
story_body: After Chassidim in Vidz submitted a complaint against the Vilna kahal's authority over them, the Vidz kahal moved to distance itself. On 19 Av 5558 they wrote a formal disavowal, asserting the action was taken without their knowledge by 'people belonging to the Karliner sect.' The episode is referenced by the Alter Rebbe in a 5571 letter as an example of denunciation he opposed.

title_en: Alter Rebbe and thirty Chassidim arrested
summary_en: At the start of 5559 the Alter Rebbe was arrested together with thirty Chassidim from Vilna, Vidz, Hamadora, Pandel and Vysokoye-Litovsk.
story_body: Following the Mitnagdic denunciation of summer 5558, the Alter Rebbe was arrested at the start of 5559 along with thirty Chassidim from Vilna, Vidz, Hamadora, Pandel and Vysokoye-Litovsk. Heads of the Vilna Chassidic kehilla, including R' Meir Refael's, R' Aryeh Leib, R' Shlomo Zalman, R' Nachum ben Yitzchak, R' Yehuda Leib of Kraz and Rabbi Baruch Mordechai Ettinger, were interrogated. A separate arrest warrant was also issued against R' Moshe Meizlish, who managed to evade capture.

title_en: R' Moshe Meizlish flees Vilna amid Mitnagdic persecution
summary_en: R' Moshe Meizlish, former neeman of the Vilna kahal turned Chabad chassid, fled Vilna because of the machlokes and wandered abroad.
story_body: Once the Mitnagdim realized the Alter Rebbe had been freed, they turned their wrath on R' Moshe Meizlish, the former neeman of the Vilna kahal who had become a devoted disciple. He was stripped of his communal position and his livelihood, eventually being forced into wandering. The Alter Rebbe wrote a letter of introduction for him to the Baal HaHafla'ah in Germany. A pamphlet Meizlish printed in Kapust in 5572 dates his flight to the month of Ziv 5563.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes to Vilna scholars on polished shechita knives
summary_en: In 5571 the Alter Rebbe wrote to the rabbis of Vilna explaining why Chassidim used polished knives for shechita.
story_body: In 5571 the Alter Rebbe addressed a letter to the rabbis of Vilna detailing the reasons Chassidim insisted on polished shechita knives. In a handwritten note in the margin he asked R' Yehuda Leib of Kraz and the other learned Anash of Vilna to study the relevant gemara and poskim carefully so they could respond to objections. The letter shows that an active Chabad scholarly group remained in Vilna into the second decade of the 19th century.

title_en: Tsar Paul I orders release of Alter Rebbe and Chabad chassidim
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5559, Tsar Paul I issued a written order freeing the Alter Rebbe and his chassidim after finding no harm to the state in their conduct.
story_body: Following interrogations and the translation of his answers into Russian, the Tsar concluded that the Karliner sect (as the chassidim were called in the official record) had done nothing to disturb public order. On 19 Kislev 5559 he signed the order of release. This date later became the Chassidic festival of 19 Kislev.

title_en: Alter Rebbe receives his official release document
summary_en: On 20 Kislev 5559 the Alter Rebbe received the formal release certificate; Procurator General Pyotr Lopukhin wrote that day to Governor-General Zhegulin confirming the freedom of 'Zalman ben Baruch'.
story_body: The day after the Tsar's order, the Alter Rebbe was handed the document making his freedom official. Lopukhin's letter to Semyon Zhegulin, governor-general of White Russia, formally notified the regional administration that Zalman ben Baruch had been released without restriction.

title_en: Vilna chassidim freed on fifth night of Chanukah
summary_en: On 28 Kislev 5559, the fifth night of Chanukah, the chassidim arrested in Vilna were released home.
story_body: Although the Alter Rebbe had been freed on 20 Kislev, his chassidim from Vilna only reached their homes a week later. Because Chanukah candle-lighting in that region precedes 3 pm, the release after lighting was attributed to the fifth night, and that date entered chassidic memory as the day of the Vilna chassidim's geulah.

title_en: Russian officials dissolve Vilna kahal at the Great Synagogue
summary_en: On 10 Adar I 5559, government officials entered the Vilna Great Synagogue and announced the dissolution of the existing kahal and new elections.
story_body: After the flood of complaints against the chassidim, the imperial authorities concluded the Vilna kahal had abused its powers in persecuting the chassidic community. The administration ordered new elections, breaking the leadership of the anti-chassidic establishment.

title_en: New Vilna kahal elected with chassid R. Meir Refaels at head
summary_en: On 12 Adar I 5559 eight new kahal members were elected in Vilna, headed by the chassid R. Meir Refaels.
story_body: Two days after the imperial dissolution of the old kahal, fresh elections produced a kehillah board of eight men with the chassid R. Meir Refaels at its head. This was a dramatic reversal for the chassidim of Vilna, who had been the target of formal communal bans for over a decade.

title_en: R. Moshe ben Asher petitions to overturn new Vilna kahal
summary_en: On 15 Adar I 5559 R. Moshe ben Asher filed a petition with the Russian authorities seeking annulment of the new Vilna kahal elections and reinstatement of the deposed leadership.
story_body: Three days after the new chassidic-led kahal was sworn in, R. Moshe ben Asher, a leader of the mitnagdim, lodged a formal complaint demanding the old board be restored. He soon followed with a second petition urging the authorities to suppress the chassidic movement in Vilna entirely.

title_en: Procurator Beklashov rules Chabad chassidim must be tolerated
summary_en: On 8 Shvat 5560 Chief Procurator Alexander Beklashov instructed Vilna police to notify the mitnagdic leadership that, by the Tsar's will, the Chabad sect must be tolerated.
story_body: Responding to the mitnagdim's renewed petition to eliminate the chassidim of Vilna, Beklashov informed the city police that the imperial decision stood: the so-called Karliner sect was protected. The Alter Rebbe later referenced this ruling in answers given during his second arrest.

title_en: Lithuanian court rules against deposed Vilna kahal
summary_en: In late summer of 5560 a Lithuanian court ruled that the deposed Vilna kahal had exceeded its authority in persecuting the chassidim, confirming the dissolution as just.
story_body: The mitnagdim's appeal of the spring 1799 elections dragged on for over a year. The court ultimately upheld the government's winter 5558 decision to curtail the kahal's powers against the chassidim, ruling the old board had crossed legitimate bounds.

title_en: Death of R. Moshe ben Asher, leader of Vilna mitnagdim
summary_en: In Cheshvan 5562 (October 1801) R. Moshe ben Asher, the foremost campaigner against the chassidim of Vilna, passed away.
story_body: With his death, the bitter public agitation in the streets of Vilna died down. Subsequent kahal elections in 5562 and 5565 included both chassidim and mitnagdim, and chassidic minyanim continued openly, eventually gaining a permanent space near the Old Kloyz.

title_en: R. Avraham Avli of Pasvalys becomes rav of Vilna
summary_en: From 5564 onward R. Avraham Avli of Pasvalys served as rav of Vilna; he maintained warm relations with the Chabad rebbes.
story_body: His tenure marked a major shift from the era of the Vilna Gaon's followers. The Alter Rebbe and later the Tzemach Tzedek corresponded and met with him, and his cooperation helped contain disputes between chassidim and mitnagdim across Lithuania.

title_en: Alter Rebbe writes to rabbis of Vilna on polished knives and peace
summary_en: In the week of Parshat Nitzavim 5571 the Alter Rebbe wrote to the rabbis of Vilna concerning the chassidic practice of slaughtering with polished knives and the history of the disputes.
story_body: The letter, printed as Iggeret 61 in volume one of his published correspondence, was addressed to the great rabbis of Vilna and asked them to deal mercifully with the chassidim under their authority. The Alter Rebbe acknowledged the rabbis' authority and urged that 'all the people will have peace.'

title_en: Birz kehillah and Chabad chassidim sign shochet agreement
summary_en: On 7 Cheshvan 5580 the kehillah of Birz and the local Chabad chassidim signed a formal agreement permitting the chassidim their own shochet alongside the town's two existing shochtim.
story_body: Following the Alter Rebbe's ruling requiring polished knives for shechita, chassidim across Lithuania sought their own shochtim. In Birz, where mitnagdic bans had targeted the practice, the two camps reached a written settlement allowing a chassidic shochet provided he submitted to the town rav and shared revenue. The agreement was signed by R. Yitzchak Isaac, mara d'asra of Birz, and the shamash R. David.

title_en: Document of sale of Hebron land to chassid R. Yechiel Michel of Birz
summary_en: In 5582 four amot of land in Hebron were sold to the Birz chassid R. Yechiel Michel Zusnitz when the Mitteler Rebbe founded the Chabad settlement in Hebron.
story_body: Photographed and printed in the history of Chabad in Eretz Yisrael, the deed reflects the Mitteler Rebbe's broader initiative to establish a Chabad presence in Hebron. R. Yechiel Michel, a shochet from Birz, was among the supporters of the new settlement.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek visits Vilna
summary_en: In Av 5595 the Tzemach Tzedek arrived in Vilna to teach Chassidus, receive chassidim in yechidus, and meet with the local rav R. Avraham Avli of Pasvalys.
story_body: News of the visit reached the chassidim of Vilna at the end of Sivan or beginning of Tammuz. When the Rebbe arrived in Av, he delivered a public maamar in the great Ashkenazi beis medrash that drew leading mitnagdim, and he held learned discussions with R. Avraham Avli. The young maskil Shmuel Yosef Fuenn, then sixteen, attended the maamar and described it in print years later.

title_en: Apatov synagogue built in Vilna
summary_en: Around 5610 the wealthy R. Yehuda Apatov built a large synagogue and beis tefilah in his courtyard on Wileńska Street in Vilna.
story_body: Apatov endowed an entire courtyard to maintain the building and support scholars worthy of rabbinic ordination, registering the gift under imperial law to secure its permanence. The building would later become the central Chabad synagogue of Vilna.

title_en: Chabad chassidim of Vilna purchase the Apatov synagogue
summary_en: In the winter of 5669 the Chabad chassidim of Vilna purchased the Apatov synagogue building for fifty thousand rubles, later renaming it 'Beis Knesses Lubavitch'.
story_body: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak (later the Frierdiker Rebbe) wrote that the chassidim acquired the large brick building together with its sixty-year-old beis knesses, intending to install their own shochet as well. The building served as the heart of Chabad life in Vilna until the Holocaust.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab delivers maamar at Apatov synagogue on Lag B'Omer
summary_en: On Lag B'Omer 5669 the Rebbe Rashab visited the newly acquired Apatov synagogue in Vilna and delivered a Chassidic discourse.
story_body: The Frierdiker Rebbe later recalled in a 5684 letter that the building was already being called 'Beis Knesses Lubavitch' when his father, the Rashab, said Chassidus there on Lag B'Omer. The visit cemented the synagogue's identity as the chassidic center of the city.

title_en: Alter Rebbe's Tanya printed in Vilna
summary_en: In 5660 the Rebbe Rashab arranged the printing of the Tanya in Vilna, conducted through the chassid R. Anshil Aronovich at the Romm press.
story_body: All correspondence with the printers was handled by R. Anshil Aronovich, who served as the Rashab's representative in Vilna. The same arrangement was used four years later for the printing of Likutei Torah.

title_en: Likutei Torah printed in Vilna
summary_en: In 5664 the Rebbe Rashab oversaw the printing of Likutei Torah in Vilna at the Romm press, again through R. Anshil Aronovich.
story_body: Aronovich, who worked at the Romm printing house, conducted all the negotiations on the Rashab's behalf. His role as the Rebbe's representative in Vilna would later be formally acknowledged in the 'Modaah Rabbah' notice printed in later Tanya editions.

title_en: Rebbe writes about hunger in wartime Vilna
summary_en: In the summer of 5678 the Rebbe Rashab wrote describing the severe hunger suffered in Vilna during World War I, including by his own representative R. Anshil Aronovich.
story_body: After receiving a letter brought out by a traveler, the Rashab wrote that the chassidim of Vilna, including Aronovich, had endured terrible hunger, though conditions had since improved somewhat. The letter is preserved as Iggeret 1097 in volume five of his correspondence.

title_en: R. Akiva Gotmanovich reports lack of chassidim in Widz
summary_en: On 23 Iyar 5688 R. Akiva Gotmanovich reported to the Frierdiker Rebbe that he was teaching public classes in Widz but had 'no chassidim to talk with'.
story_body: The dispatch reflected a thinning chassidic presence in the small Lithuanian town. Three days later the Frierdiker Rebbe responded urging Gotmanovich to teach short maamarim on avoda before the local crowd, adapting Chassidus to the audience he had.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe responds on teaching Chassidus in Widz
summary_en: On 26 Iyar 5688 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Akiva Gotmanovich advising him to teach short maamarim on Chassidic avoda before the people of Widz.
story_body: Despite Gotmanovich's complaint that there were no chassidim in Widz, the Frierdiker Rebbe encouraged him to bring Chassidus to ordinary Jews by selecting brief, accessible discourses focused on practical service of G-d.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe writes about Pandel cheder of sixty pupils
summary_en: On 21 Tevet 5689 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to R. Yehuda Leib Bernstein concerning a cheder of sixty pupils in the Lithuanian town of Pandel.
story_body: The Rebbe also mentioned a meeting he had held with R. Avraham Levitan of Birz about establishing public shiurim in that town. The letter shows the Frierdiker Rebbe's active oversight of Chabad education in the small Lithuanian communities between the world wars.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe writes to R. Avraham Levitan in Birz
summary_en: On 24 Shvat 5689 the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to R. Avraham Levitan with feedback on his report about establishing public Chassidus classes in Birz.
story_body: Levitan would continue reporting to the Rebbe on shiurim and farbrengens in Birz over the following decade, including through the late 1930s. He remained a key figure in maintaining Chabad communal life in Birz until the war.

title_en: Vilna chassidim describe 19 Kislev farbrengens to Frierdiker Rebbe
summary_en: In Kislev 5697 chassidim of Vilna wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe about their 19 Kislev farbrengens at the Apatov synagogue and the Shnipishok minyan.
story_body: The letter was signed by Yitzchak Weiman, Anshil Aronovich, Menachem Mendel Levin and Chaim Yehoshua Baruch Kapelovich. It documents the active chassidic life in multiple Vilna minyanim on the eve of the Holocaust, including Apatov, Kirzner, Shnipishok and Novogrod.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe sends final letters to Anshil Aronovich in Vilna
summary_en: On 13 Nissan 5700 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent R. Anshil Aronovich six letters for distribution to chassidim and the yeshiva then operating in Vilna.
story_body: This letter, recorded as Iggeret 4382 in volume twelve, is the last known correspondence between the Rebbe and Aronovich, his long-time representative in Vilna. Aronovich was later murdered in the Holocaust.

title_en: R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson reports Lag B'Omer farbrengen in Ponevezh
summary_en: On 23 Iyar 5700 the Ponevezh mashpia R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson reported a Lag B'Omer farbrengen at which a maamar was repeated and chassidim drank lechaim.
story_body: Lisson, who had studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch from 5660 to 5669 and served as Ponevezh mashpia since 5669, wrote that the gathering was held at both Chabad minyanim in the city. The chassidim prayed for the speedy revelation of the wellsprings of Baal Shem Tov's teachings.

title_en: 12 Tammuz farbrengen held quietly in wartime Ponevezh
summary_en: On 12 Tammuz 5700, with Soviet occupation underway, more than ten chassidim gathered at R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson's minyan in Ponevezh, drank mashke and repeated a maamar.
story_body: Lisson wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe that 'the time caused it' that the celebration could not be public as in previous years. Despite the dangers of the new Soviet regime in Lithuania, the chassidim marked the Frierdiker Rebbe's redemption day in private.

title_en: Shavuot celebrated joyfully at Ponevezh Chabad minyan
summary_en: On both days of Shavuot 5700 the Chabad minyan in Ponevezh studied Chassidus, read the Baal Shem Tov's letter on his ascent of soul, and held a celebratory meal of the Chevra Tehillim.
story_body: R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson reported to the Frierdiker Rebbe that the chassidim learned the maamar 'Va'ehyeh Etzlo Amun' from Likutei Torah on the first day and held a festive meal with dancing on the second. The Soviet occupation had not yet extinguished chassidic joy.

title_en: R. Avraham Lisson flees Ponevezh as Germany invades
summary_en: On 24 June 1941 (29 Sivan 5701) R. Avraham Lisson fled Ponevezh as the German invasion overran Lithuania; his father R. Shmuel Tzvi and the rest of the family remained and were murdered in the Holocaust.
story_body: The Frierdiker Rebbe had obtained American visas for R. Shmuel Tzvi Lisson at the end of 5700, but they did not reach him in time. When the Germans invaded the Soviet Union, the son escaped while his father and household perished in the Shoah, may Hashem avenge their blood.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Soviet Russia
summary_en: At the end of Tishrei 5688, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn left Soviet Russia.
story_body: After years of persecution under the Communists, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Russia in late Tishrei 5688. Immediately upon his exit, Chabad chassidim in Warsaw appealed to him to settle in Poland, arguing it would allow them and the chassidim in the Polish-ruled regions of Lithuania (Vilna, Daksht, Dolhinov, Glubokie, etc.) to remain connected to their Rebbe.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes Raskin on dispatching mashpiim
summary_en: In mid-Tevet 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yehuda Leib Raskin about appointing traveling mashpiim for towns in Poland and Lithuania.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz outlined a plan to assign select chassidim as shadarim who would travel a regular circuit through Poland and Lithuania to strengthen Chassidic life. Among those named was R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin, who would be deployed wherever proved most useful. The letter is preserved as Igros Kodesh vol. 14, no. 5197.

title_en: R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin appointed mashpia of Vilna
summary_en: On 2 Elul 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz formally appointed R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin to teach Chassidus to anash in Vilna and surrounding towns.
story_body: The Rebbe wrote on 2 Elul 5684 to R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin directing him to repeat maamarei Chassidus before anash of Vilna and to travel periodically to nearby towns to encourage fixed Torah study and chavrusa learning. On the same day he wrote to the anash of Vilna asking them to receive R. Shimon Noach warmly and set up a venue for him to deliver Chassidus.

title_en: Founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Vilna
summary_en: In 5687 anash of Vilna founded the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva, with R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin on the executive committee.
story_body: The Chabad community of Vilna established a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in 5687. R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin, the mashpia for Vilna and its environs, served as a member of the yeshiva's governing committee.

title_en: New Toras Or shul built in Ponevezh
summary_en: A new, grand Chabad shul (known as Toras Or) was built in Ponevezh in 5689, alongside the existing older shtibel.
story_body: Ponevezh had two Chabad shuls in the interwar years. The newer and more elegant one, called Toras Or, was constructed in 5689; the older shtibel was where the tamim R. Shmuel Tzvi Lison, Hy"d, served as mashpia.

title_en: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch appointed mashpia for Lithuania
summary_en: In the summer of 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch to serve as traveling mashpia for the Kovno, Vilna, and Dvinsk districts.
story_body: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch, who served as rav of Kopishok, was commissioned by the Rebbe Rayatz in summer 5688 to travel among the towns of the Kovno, Vilna, and Dvinsk regions, establishing regular shiurim in Chassidus among anash.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes on global anash correspondence
summary_en: On 12 Adar 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch and R. Pinchas Mintz of Kovno about systematic correspondence with anash in Lithuania, Brazil, South Africa, and Russia.
story_body: The Rebbe instructed his correspondents in Kovno to gather scattered descendants of chassidim, organize letter-writing campaigns to anash who had emigrated to Brazil and South Africa, and engage in carefully worded correspondence with relatives still trapped in Soviet Russia. The letter (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, no. 6154) emphasized the duty to awaken in such Jews their ancestral connection to Chassidus.

title_en: R. Yechezkel Feigin letter on Vilna-region towns
summary_en: On 17 Shevat 5692 the Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson noting roughly forty small towns of anash in the Vilna province.
story_body: Reporting to R. Yisrael Jacobson, the Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin described plans for a tour of the Vilna province around Adar, mentioning that the region contained nearly forty small towns, most populated by anash. The letter offers one of the clearest contemporary snapshots of Chabad's geographic reach in interwar Lithuania.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz thanks R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch for reports
summary_en: On 15 Tammuz 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that reports of public Chassidus study by anash and tmimim were 'a true medicine' sustaining his health.
story_body: In Igros Kodesh vol. 17, no. 6369, the Rebbe Rayatz thanked R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch of Kovno for reports about anash holding public shiurim in Chassidus. The Rebbe wrote that such news literally sustained his physical strength, and blessed all who concerned themselves with this work.

title_en: 19 Kislev celebrations across Lithuania reported
summary_en: Around Zos Chanukah 5697, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on widespread 19 Kislev celebrations among anash throughout Lithuania.
story_body: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch detailed gatherings in Kovno (with over 200 attendees including students of the local yeshiva), Kelm, Telz, Ponevezh (both shtiblach), Vilkomir, Anikst, and other towns. R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevitch had come from Kopishok to spend the chag in Kovno; the Rebbe's klali letter for 19 Kislev was relayed by mail to each community.

title_en: Reports on 24 Tevet (Alter Rebbe yahrzeit) observances
summary_en: In a letter near Parshas Bo 5698, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported sending 22 letters to anash ahead of the Alter Rebbe's 24 Tevet yahrzeit, with farbrengens held across Lithuania.
story_body: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz that he had dispatched 26 letters to 24 communities urging hisva'adus and limud Chassidus on 24 Tevet, including double letters to Ponevezh (for both shtiblach) and Skopishok. He cited responses describing observances in Anikst, Traskun, Salok, Yanove, Mazheik, Vizun, and other towns.

title_en: Likutim Yekarim printed in Riga
summary_en: In 5699 R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin printed the sefer Likutim Yekarim in Riga.
story_body: R. Shimon Noach Nimoitin, mashpia of Vilna and its surrounding communities, produced the volume Likutim Yekarim through a Riga press in 5699, on the very eve of the Second World War.

title_en: Reports on 2 and 13 Nissan hilula observances
summary_en: On 23 Iyar 5700, after the outbreak of WWII, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported on Nissan hilula observances across Lithuania.
story_body: Even after the war had broken out in Europe but before the German conquest of Lithuania, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch continued his correspondence. He reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on hisva'aduyos held for the 2 Nissan (Rebbe Rashab) and 13 Nissan (Tzemach Tzedek) yahrzeits in Panidel, Kelm, Anishishok, Ponevezh, and Taurage, including the daily Tanya shiur of R. Yehoshua Asher Rotfeld's chaburah.

title_en: Report on Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz farbrengens
summary_en: In a letter of 18 Tammuz 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch described Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz observances of tehillim, Chassidus and farbrengens in Kovno and Vizun.
story_body: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported the full Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz seder in Kovno: tehillim said by the community, a Chassidus shiur, davening, and a farbrengen lasting until mincha. R. Yosef Genkin in Vizun wrote separately that they had also observed Shabbos Mevarchim with tehillim and a farbrengen, and intended to mark 12 Tammuz similarly.

title_en: Reports on 12-13 Tammuz Geulah celebrations
summary_en: On 24 Tammuz 5700 R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on 12-13 Tammuz farbrengens across Lithuania.
story_body: R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch transmitted reports from R. Leib Kamraz of Ushpol, R. Zev Razinkevitch of Birz (joined by bochurim from the Novardok yeshiva), R. Yosef Genkin of Vizun (who said the maamar 'Baruch HaGomel l'Chayavim Tovos'), and R. Itche Bangs of Taurage on the Chag HaGeulah farbrengens.

title_en: Report on Shabbos Mevarchim Av and tamim Zelig Glass tour
summary_en: On the eve of 8 Av 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch reported on the visiting tamim Zelig Glass who delivered Chassidus across Lithuanian shtetlach.
story_body: R. Yosef Genkin wrote that the tamim Zelig Glass had spent Shabbos Mevarchim Av in Vizun, delivering the maamar 'Ma Tovu' before three minyanim. The tamim Glass also spent four Shabbosos in Autian and visited the Amshinover Rebbe's shtibel in Kovno. R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch's brother-in-law R. Moshe Yosef Gottlieb meanwhile delivered Chassidus in Kovno every Shabbos.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz replies to Lithuania reports
summary_en: On 16 Tevet 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz responded to R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch expressing pleasure at news of how anash had passed the recent festivals.
story_body: Despite the deteriorating wartime situation, the Rebbe Rayatz continued to receive and respond to detailed reports from R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch. In Igros Kodesh vol. 5, no. 1337, he wrote of the great pleasure the letter brought him and expressed hope to soon receive similar updates from later dates.

title_en: Nazi conquest of Latvia and establishment of ghetto
summary_en: In the summer of 5701 the Nazis conquered Latvia and established a ghetto for its Jews.
story_body: Following Operation Barbarossa, Nazi Germany overran Latvia in the summer of 1941. A ghetto was set up to confine the Jewish population, ending centuries of Jewish communal life and the Chabad presence centered in Riga.

title_en: Great Aktion against Latvian Jewry
summary_en: At the beginning of Cheshvan 5702 the Nazis carried out the great Aktion in which the Jews of Latvia were murdered.
story_body: Only months after sealing the Latvian ghetto, the Nazis conducted the major Aktion at the start of Cheshvan 5702 (late October/November 1941), murdering the bulk of Latvian Jewry. The Chabad chassidim of Riga and the surrounding region were largely annihilated in this killing.

title_en: Chabad rabbi leaves Globoke
summary_en: The Chabad rabbi of Globoke departed in the winter of 5690, leaving the chassidic community to seek a replacement from the Rebbe.
story_body: In the winter of 5690 (1930), the rabbi of the Chabad community in Globoke left the town. The chassidic community (separate from the general kehilla, which had its own rabbi, R. Yosef HaLevi Katz) turned to the Rebbe Rayatz, then in America, asking him to send a Chabad rabbi to replace him.

title_en: Kuperstock visits Globoke for Shabbos Yitro
summary_en: At the Rebbe's instruction, R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock of Fastov visited Globoke for Shabbos Parshas Yisro and made a strong impression on the local chassidim.
story_body: From America, the Rebbe Rayatz directed R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock, the rabbi of nearby Fastov, to visit Globoke. He arrived for Shabbos Parshas Yisro, spoke publicly, repeated chassidic discourses, and left a positive impression on the chassidic community there.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz returns from America
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz returned to Europe from his trip to the United States in the summer of 5690.
story_body: After his historic visit to America, the Rebbe Rayatz returned in the summer of 5690 (1930). Shortly after, the Globoke chassidic community held a special meeting about the rabbinate vacancy and renewed their appeal to him.

title_en: Globoke chassidim petition Rebbe to appoint Kuperstock
summary_en: Forty-eight Globoke chassidim signed a formal request, dated 14 Elul 5690, appointing delegates to ask the Rebbe to install R. Kuperstock as their rabbi.
story_body: On 14 Elul 5690 the chassidic community of Globoke convened and signed a letter to the Rebbe Rayatz, naming three delegates - R. Elyakum Reier, R. Baruch Shalom Tzepeliowitz, and R. Moshe Leib Rothstein - to formally request that R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock be appointed as their rabbi. The letter expressed satisfaction with his earlier visit and was signed by 48 chassidim with the community's seals.

title_en: Rebbe endorses Kuperstock as Globoke's Chabad rabbi
summary_en: On 8 Tishrei 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a handwritten letter to the Globoke chassidim blessing them and supporting Kuperstock's appointment.
story_body: In his handwritten letter of 8 Tishrei 5691 (published in Igros Kodesh vol. 17, letter 275), the Rebbe encouraged the Globoke chassidim who were upholding R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock's appointment and blessed them with health and abundant livelihood. The letter survives only in part.

title_en: Rebbe rebuffs general rabbi's opposition in Globoke
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz replied on 8 Tishrei 5691 to the general kehilla's rabbi, rejecting his attempts to claim the Chabad rabbinate for his son-in-law.
story_body: The general kehilla's rabbi opposed Kuperstock's appointment, wanting to reserve the Chabad rabbinate for his son-in-law. The Rebbe Rayatz, in a letter dated 8 Tishrei 5691 (Igros Kodesh vol. 17, letter 6276), wrote that he had not expected such agitation and stressed that the chassidic community must not surrender its longstanding chazakah over its own rabbinate.

title_en: Kuperstock accepts the Globoke rabbinate
summary_en: On 13 Tishrei 5691 R. Kuperstock wrote to the Rebbe accepting the Globoke rabbinate alongside his Fastov post.
story_body: Writing to the Rebbe Rayatz on 13 Tishrei 5691, R. Kuperstock confirmed receipt of the Rebbe's letters and of the formal rabbinic appointment from Globoke. He accepted the role and expressed hope that the disputes around the position would be settled peaceably.

title_en: Fastov chassidim plead to keep Kuperstock
summary_en: Eighteen chassidim of Fastov wrote on 14 Tishrei 5691, asking the Rebbe not to transfer their rabbi to Globoke.
story_body: On 14 Tishrei 5691, the chassidim of Fastov sent a signed letter to the Rebbe Rayatz protesting the planned transfer of Kuperstock to Globoke. They asked why their community should be deprived of a rabbi who guided them in the ways of their forebears, given that they too held a longstanding right to his leadership.

title_en: Violent opposition forces Kuperstock back to Fastov
summary_en: On 28 Tishrei 5691 Kuperstock reported to the Rebbe that hostile crowds in Globoke's Lubavitcher and Starasele shuls forced him to flee the town at night.
story_body: Kuperstock had traveled to Globoke for Shabbos Bereishis but encountered intense opposition. Youths jeered him in the Lubavitcher shul after Torah reading, and rowdies brandished their fists at him when he tried to speak in the Starasele shul. By nightfall a coalition demanded he leave the town that very night. He wrote to the Rebbe on 28 Tishrei 5691 describing the events, thankful that he had escaped with his life.

title_en: Kuperstock installed in Globoke after two-year delay
summary_en: After the Globoke opposition forced a two-year postponement, R. Kuperstock was finally installed as rabbi of the Chabad community in the winter of 5693.
story_body: Following the violent rejection of his appointment, the decision was made to keep Kuperstock in Fastov for two more years. In the winter of 5693 (1933) he was at last accepted as the rabbi of the chassidic community in Globoke, where he then served for two years.

title_en: Kuperstock decides to make aliyah
summary_en: In the winter of 5695 R. Kuperstock resolved to leave Globoke and settle in Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: After two years of serving as rabbi of the Chabad community in Globoke, R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock decided in the winter of 5695 (1935) to make aliyah. He eventually settled in Haifa and founded a Chabad community there.

title_en: Globoke chassidim ask Rebbe for new rabbi
summary_en: On 4 Kislev 5695, sixteen Globoke chassidim wrote to the Rebbe in Yiddish lamenting Kuperstock's imminent departure for Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: Sixteen members of the Globoke chassidic community signed a heartfelt Yiddish letter on 4 Kislev 5695, telling the Rebbe Rayatz how Kuperstock had elevated the chassidic spirit not only locally but throughout the wider Vilna region. They mourned his impending departure to Eretz Yisrael and asked for a successor.

title_en: R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock passes away in Haifa
summary_en: R. Menachem Mendel Kuperstock, founder of the Chabad community in Haifa, passed away on 7 Adar I 5706.
story_body: After making aliyah from Globoke, R. Kuperstock settled in Haifa where he founded the local Chabad community. He passed away on 7 Adar I 5706 (February 8, 1946).

title_en: Rebbe asks R. Stein to push Freidin's election in Fastov
summary_en: On 6 Iyar 5693 the Rebbe wrote to R. Refael Stein, asking him to travel to Fastov and urge the chassidim to elect R. Yehuda Leib Freidin as Kuperstock's successor.
story_body: With Kuperstock to be relocated, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote on 6 Iyar 5693 (Igros Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3888) asking R. Refael Stein to travel to Fastov and remind the chassidim of their duty to choose a chassidic rabbi from anash. He specifically endorsed R. Yehuda Leib Freidin for the role.

title_en: R. Yehuda Leib Freidin elected rabbi of Fastov
summary_en: By mid-Sivan 5693, R. Yehuda Leib Freidin had been elected rabbi of Fastov, as reported by R. Yehuda Eber and noted in 'Shaarei Tziyon'.
story_body: R. Yehuda Eber, head of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, wrote to the Rebbe on 12 Sivan 5693 reporting that Freidin had been elected rabbi in Fastov. The journal 'Shaarei Tziyon' (vol. 13, no. 6-12) also announced his appointment. The general kehilla's rabbi, R. Shmuel Dovid Walkin, initially opposed it and even summoned Freidin to a din torah in Vilna, but tensions eventually subsided.

title_en: Mandelbaum sent to Krakow to teach chassidus
summary_en: In the summer of 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum to Krakow to deliver chassidus shiurim and try to open a Tomchei Tmimim branch.
story_body: In summer 5691 (1931), R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum, a Tomchei Tmimim student in Warsaw, was sent by the Rebbe to Krakow for a period to deliver chassidic discourses. He also attempted to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in his own town of Matzayov, though that effort did not materialize.

title_en: Mandelbaum sent to head Tomchei Tmimim Lodz
summary_en: During 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum to head the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lodz.
story_body: Mandelbaum had distinguished himself as a Tomchei Tmimim student in Warsaw, praised in 5686 as 'sharp-minded' with depth in nigleh and chassidus. In 5692 (1932) the Rebbe sent him to lead the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lodz.

title_en: Mandelbaum appointed rabbi of Globoke
summary_en: In 5695, after Kuperstock left for Eretz Yisrael, the Rebbe sent R. Yitzchak HaLevi Mandelbaum to fill the rabbinate of the Globoke chassidic community.
story_body: Following Kuperstock's aliyah and the appeal of the Globoke chassidim on 4 Kislev 5695, the Rebbe Rayatz sent Mandelbaum - a Tomchei Tmimim alumnus and head of the Lodz branch - to take over the Globoke rabbinate. He led weekly chassidus farbrengens, Tanya lessons, and oral discourses for the community.

title_en: Mandelbaum reports on 19 Kislev gatherings in Globoke
summary_en: On 2 Tevet 5697 Mandelbaum wrote to the Rebbe describing the 19 Kislev farbrengens and the new Torah-study programs he had launched in Globoke.
story_body: Mandelbaum reported that during the Yud-Tes Kislev celebrations he had pushed for strengthened Ein Yaakov shiurim in every minyan, Mishnayos and Shulchan Aruch classes, his own daily gemara shiur in the Starasele minyan, and a resolution to learn Tanya on Friday nights.

title_en: R. Reitchik visits Globoke amid 1939 flight
summary_en: Reporting on the eve of 14 Teves 5700, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik described how Mandelbaum wanted to flee Globoke for Vilna but felt bound to his community.
story_body: In Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Ki Sisa 5700, while Tomchei Tmimim students were fleeing Poland for Vilna, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik wrote to the Rebbe that he had traveled to Globoke on the eve of 14 Teves. He found Mandelbaum torn: he too wished to escape to Vilna but felt unable to abandon the town as its appointed rabbi.

title_en: R. Yitzchak Mandelbaum perishes in Globoke
summary_en: R. Yitzchak HaLevi Mandelbaum was murdered in Globoke on 19 Menachem Av 5703, as recorded in 'Churban Globak'.
story_body: According to the memorial volume 'Churban Globak' (p. 28), Mandelbaum perished in the Holocaust in Globoke on 19 Menachem Av 5703 (August 20, 1943), Hashem yikom damo.

title_en: R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin sent to influence Vilna and Minsk towns
summary_en: By 17 Shevat 5681 the Rebbe was directing R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin of Zembin to travel through the Vilna and Minsk provinces promoting Torah and chassidus study.
story_body: Sheinin, one of the foremost Tomchei Tmimim students in Lubavitch, was sent by the Rebbe in the winter of 5681 as a mashpia in the towns of the Vilna and Minsk regions. On 17 Shevat 5681 the Rebbe wrote (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 5723) singling him out as a model emissary urging communities to establish fixed Torah-study times in nigleh and chassidus.

title_en: Sheinin appointed rabbi of Dokshytsy
summary_en: In Tishrei 5682 the Rebbe sent R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin to serve as rabbi of the chassidic community in Dokshytsy.
story_body: In Tishrei 5682 (autumn 1921), the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched Sheinin to take up the rabbinate of the chassidic community in Dokshytsy. R. Yochanan Gordon, the town's shochet, later wrote of Sheinin's profound personal qualities and devotion to the Rebbe.

title_en: Sheinin tours Vilna-region towns to spread chassidus
summary_en: In 5684 the Rebbe sent Sheinin to visit communities in the Vilna region and strengthen public learning of chassidus.
story_body: After Sheinin reported in Shevat 5684 on his travels, the Rebbe responded (Igros Kodesh vol. 1, letter 171) urging more correspondence with chassidim, dedicated trips, and Tanya recitation in Donilovich. The same day the Rebbe also wrote to R. Yeshaya Friedman, shochet in Donilovich, and to R. Shraga Faivish Bronstein of Kurnits, both of whom had begun teaching Tanya publicly thanks to Sheinin.

title_en: Sheinin reports on 5690 tour of Vilna-region towns
summary_en: Writing on the eve of 16 Adar 5690 (תר"צ), Sheinin reported on his Shevat tour through Haloboutchi, Pliesy, Disna, and Vilna, where he energized Tanya and chassidus shiurim.
story_body: Sheinin recounted that during Shevat 5690 he visited multiple towns repeating chassidus and urging Tanya shiurim. In Haloboutchi, R. Yeshaya Refael recited chassidus each Shabbos; in Pliesy he prompted R. Yisrael to begin a daily Tanya shiur; in Disna he worked with R. Shemarya Yofeh to begin Tanya after his daily gemara; and in Vilna's Kirzner minyan he prompted R. Elye Weitz to add Tanya to his daily gemara shiur.

title_en: Sheinin's final letter from Dokshytsy
summary_en: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5700, Sheinin sent a Yiddish letter from Dokshytsy describing his weak health.
story_body: Sheinin's last surviving letter from Dokshytsy, addressed to R. Yochanan Gordon and dated Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini 5700, said simply that he was alive but his aunt was very weak and he himself was ill and had no strength to move about.

title_en: R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin perishes in the Holocaust
summary_en: R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin was murdered during Chol HaMoed Pesach 5702.
story_body: After more than two decades as rabbi of Dokshytsy and a tireless emissary of the Rebbe through the Vilna and Minsk regions, R. Aryeh Leib Sheinin perished in the Holocaust on Chol HaMoed Pesach 5702 (April 1942), Hashem yikom damo.

title_en: Birth of R. Shmuel Levitin
summary_en: R. Shmuel Levitin was born in Pahar in 5644.
story_body: R. Shmuel Levitin, future rabbi of Rakishok and later chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim in New York, was born in 5644 (1884) in Pahar. He went on to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch.

title_en: Levitin marries and becomes rabbi of Rakishok
summary_en: In 5666 R. Shmuel Levitin married the daughter of Rakishok's rabbi R. Asher Margolios and succeeded him in the rabbinate.
story_body: In 5666 (1906), Levitin married Mrs. Sheina, the daughter of R. Asher Margolios, rabbi of Rakishok, and was appointed in his father-in-law's place as rabbi of Rakishok.

title_en: Levitin sent to Georgia as chief shliach
summary_en: Forced to leave Rakishok during WWI in 5675, Levitin was sent by the Rebbe Rashab to Georgia as chief shliach to establish a network of educational institutions.
story_body: During World War I, in 5675 (1915), Levitin was forced to leave Rakishok. The Rebbe Rashab then sent him as chief shliach to Georgia, where he brought additional Tomchei Tmimim students and established a network of educational institutions, eventually building a major yeshiva in Kutaisi over roughly a decade.

title_en: Levitin appointed to lead rabbinical school in Nevel
summary_en: In 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz appointed Levitin to found and direct a beis midrash for rabbinical training in Nevel.
story_body: After roughly ten years in Kutaisi, Levitin was appointed by the Rebbe Rayatz in 5684 (1924) to establish and direct a beis midrash for rabbinical training in Nevel, attracting men in their 20s, 30s, and 40s to study laws of practical halacha.

title_en: Levitin arrested by the Yevsektzia
summary_en: In the winter of 5689 R. Shmuel Levitin was imprisoned by the Yevsektzia in Velikie Luki and sentenced to exile.
story_body: In Kislev 5689 the Yevsektzia accused Levitin of disseminating Torah to youth in Nevel. He was placed in harsh imprisonment in Velikie Luki and sentenced to internal exile, leaving the Nevel rabbinical school in crisis.

title_en: Rebbe organizes funds for Levitin's release
summary_en: On 24 Shevat 5689 the Rebbe wrote to the chassidim of Rakishok urging them to raise a larger sum toward Levitin's release.
story_body: Replying to a letter from the Rakishok chassidim on 24 Shevat 5689 (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6121), the Rebbe explained that Levitin's situation remained unclear. He told them the sum they had collected was inadequate and pressed them to raise a proper amount so it would be ready when an opportunity arose to bring him to them.

title_en: Rebbe appeals to R. Kahana-Shapira of Kovno for Levitin
summary_en: In Nissan 5689 the Rebbe wrote to R. Avraham Dovber Kahana-Shapira, rabbi of Kovno, asking him to enlist high officials to free Levitin to Lithuania.
story_body: In Nissan 5689 the Rebbe wrote (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6201) to the Kovno rabbi, detailing Levitin's biography and recent imprisonment in Velikie Luki. He asked Kahana-Shapira to intervene through high government officials so that Levitin would be permitted to relocate to Lithuania, specifically to his former rabbinate in Rakishok.

title_en: Levitin leaves the Soviet Union
summary_en: In Shevat 5697 R. Shmuel Levitin finally escaped the Soviet Union and was reaccepted as rabbi of Rakishok.
story_body: After years of struggle, in Shevat 5697 (January 1937) Levitin succeeded in leaving Russia. He returned to Lithuania and was once again accepted as rabbi of the Rakishok community.

title_en: Rebbe sends emissary to arrange Levitin's Rakishok role
summary_en: On 29 Tammuz 5697 the Rebbe informed Levitin he would send R. Mordechai the shochet of Riga as a special emissary to formalize matters in Rakishok.
story_body: Writing to Levitin on 29 Tammuz 5697 (Igros Kodesh vol. 4, letter 920), the Rebbe Rayatz said it was worthwhile to dispatch R. Mordechai, the shochet from Riga, as a special emissary with a letter to the chassidim in Rakishok, in order that Levitin's reinstallation be carried out properly and respectfully.

title_en: Levitin sent as shadar to America
summary_en: In Elul 5698 the Rebbe sent Levitin to the United States as a special emissary on his behalf.
story_body: In Elul 5698 (1938), R. Shmuel Levitin was sent by the Rebbe Rayatz to America as a shadar. When his primary mission concluded in the spring of 5699, he asked whether to return home to Rakishok, but the Rebbe instructed him to remain in America - which ultimately spared him from the Holocaust.

title_en: Rebbe asks U.S. government to keep Levitin in America
summary_en: On 9 Adar I 5700 the Rebbe wrote to the Agudas Chabad leadership in New York requesting that Levitin remain in America to assist his work after the move from Warsaw to Riga.
story_body: After escaping Warsaw to Riga, the Rebbe wrote on 9 Adar I 5700 (Igros Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5261) to the Agudas Chabad leadership in New York. He asked them to lobby the Washington government to allow Levitin to remain in America and to bring his family to join him, since he was essential to the work of disseminating chassidus and organizing Chabad chassidim worldwide.

title_en: Levitin becomes chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim NY
summary_en: From 5700 onward, R. Shmuel Levitin served as the head mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in New York.
story_body: Once the Rebbe Rayatz secured Levitin's right to remain in America, he was installed as the chief mashpia at the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in New York, a role he held for decades until his passing.

title_en: R. Shmuel Levitin passes away in New York
summary_en: R. Shmuel Levitin, longtime mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim in New York, passed away on 11 Elul 5734 and was buried in New York.
story_body: R. Shmuel Levitin - rabbi of Rakishok, builder of the Georgia network and the Nevel rabbinical school, and chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim in America - passed away on 11 Elul 5734 (August 29, 1974) and was buried in New York.

title_en: R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz becomes rabbi of Moscow
summary_en: In 5637 R. Chaim Yaakov Widrewitz left the Kupishok rabbinate to become rabbi of Moscow, and R. Avraham Tzvi Brodno succeeded him in Kupishok.
story_body: Widrewitz had served as rabbi of Kupishok during the era of the Tzemach Tzedek. In 5637 (1877) he was accepted as rabbi of Moscow, and R. Avraham Tzvi Brodno was appointed in his place in Kupishok.

title_en: Birth of R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich
summary_en: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich was born in Bakhmut in 5649.
story_body: Born in Bakhmut in 5649 (1889), R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich would go on to study in Lubavitch, become one of the 'chozrim' (those who repeated chassidic discourses from memory), and serve as rabbi in several Lithuanian communities.

title_en: Chatzkevich becomes rabbi of Ponimonek
summary_en: By 29 Sivan 5671 (June 25, 1911), R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich had been installed as rabbi of Ponimonek, as announced in the Tomchei Tmimim journal 'HaAch'.
story_body: In 5671 (1911) Chatzkevich succeeded his father-in-law R. Yitzchak Moshe Weiler as rabbi of Ponimonek. The Tomchei Tmimim journal 'HaAch' (29 Sivan 5671) congratulated him, calling him a beloved chossid and yarei shomayim and wishing him further elevation.

title_en: Chatzkevich settles in Abel after WWI exile
summary_en: Chatzkevich was forced from Ponimonek during the WWI expulsions and, upon return, was accepted as rabbi of the town of Abel.
story_body: Chatzkevich remained in Ponimonek until the WWI-era expulsion of Jews from frontline regions. Upon returning from exile, he did not return to Ponimonek but instead was accepted as rabbi of the town of Abel.

title_en: Rebbe deploys Chatzkevich across Lithuania and Latvia
summary_en: On 9 Elul 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz tasked R. Chatzkevich with traveling Lithuania and Latvia to write rousing letters and establish chassidus shiurim.
story_body: On 9 Elul 5683 the Rebbe wrote to Chatzkevich (Igros Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5178), formally charging him with founding chassidus-study groups in the provinces of Kovno, Vilna, and Dvinsk. The Rebbe also wrote to anash in those regions (letter 5181), asking them to support Chatzkevich and establish written and oral shiurim in every place anash lived.

title_en: Chatzkevich appointed rabbi of Kupishok
summary_en: On 15 Cheshvan 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz congratulated R. Chatzkevich and the chassidim of Kupishok on his appointment as their rabbi.
story_body: At the start of 5688 (autumn 1927), R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich was accepted as rabbi of Kupishok. The Rebbe wrote two letters dated 15 Cheshvan 5688 (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letters 5810-5811): one to Chatzkevich blessing his appointment and asking him to set up public shiurim in nigleh and chassidus, and one to the Kupishok chassidim congratulating them on selecting one of the foremost Tomchei Tmimim alumni.

title_en: Chatzkevich leads Lithuanian delegation to the Rebbe
summary_en: In Kislev 5691, R. Chatzkevich headed a delegation of Lithuanian chassidim asking the Rebbe Rayatz to visit Lithuania.
story_body: In Kislev 5691 (late 1930), as recorded by the Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin (Sefer HaMaamarim Kuntreisim vol. 1, p. 153a), the chassidim of Lithuania sent a delegation to the Rebbe. R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich of Kupishok headed the group, which formally renewed the request that the Rebbe visit anash in Lithuania and fix a date for the trip.

title_en: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich perishes in the Holocaust
summary_en: In late 5701 R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich was murdered in the Holocaust.
story_body: R. Yisrael Noach Chatzkevich, rabbi of Kupishok and longtime emissary of the Rebbe across Lithuania and Latvia, perished at the end of 5701 (1941), Hashem yikom damo.

title_en: Rebbe writes to R. Ushpal in Kornitz
summary_en: On 25 Iyar 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz addressed a letter to R. Shlomo Eliyahu Ushpal, rabbi of Kornitz.
story_body: R. Shlomo Eliyahu Ushpal served as rabbi of Kornitz, succeeding R. Yaakov Landa who had earlier held the position in place of his father R. Moshe Yehuda Leib Landa. On 25 Iyar 5688 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote him there.

title_en: Rebbe writes to Dalhinov chassidim
summary_en: On 28 Nissan 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a warm reply to the chassidim of Dalhinov, sent via their rabbi R. Gedalia Wilensky.
story_body: After the Dalhinov chassidim wrote to the Rebbe through their rabbi R. Gedalia Wilensky in late winter 5689, the Rebbe replied on 28 Nissan 5689 (Igros Kodesh vol. 16, letter 5186), blessing the community and their families with abundant life and material and spiritual blessing.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Vilna in summer 5692
summary_en: In the summer of 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Vilna, where many Chabad rabbis of Lithuania gathered to join him for seudah shlishis.
story_body: R. Yitzchak Dov Ushpal recalled that during the Rebbe Rayatz's Vilna visit in summer 5692 (1932), after davening the Rebbe went to his hotel where senior Chabad rabbis assembled for seudah shlishis. Among those present were R. Shlomo Eliyahu Ushpal of Kornitz, R. Kuperstock of Fastov, R. Mendelovitz, R. Leib Sheinin of Dokshytsy, and the rabbis of Dalhinov and Radoshkovitz.

title_en: Rebbe sends R. Refael Stein to Vilna region
summary_en: On 8 Menachem Av 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz praised R. Refael Stein for his work on the mikveh in Poretz.
story_body: Sent on a mission to strengthen Torah and Yiddishkeit in the Vilna region, Stein traveled first to Poretz to address the mikveh there. The Rebbe wrote to him on 8 Menachem Av 5692 (Igros Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3882) expressing great delight at the success of the mikveh effort in Poretz.

title_en: Rebbe directs further travels for R. Refael Stein
summary_en: On 22 Menachem Av 5692 the Rebbe wrote to Stein again, noting the Poretz mikveh's expected completion and instructing him on his next trips.
story_body: Following up on the Poretz mikveh project, the Rebbe wrote on 22 Menachem Av 5692 (Igros Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3883) that he expected the mikveh to be made fit soon. He decided that Stein should now travel further, with instructions to be communicated by R. Moshe Leib Rothstein. The Rebbe also addressed a letter to all anash in the Vilna region (letter 3884) introducing Stein as his emissary.

title_en: R. Shimon Levi Belastotzky reports from Disna
summary_en: On 13 Nissan 5694, R. Shimon Levi Belastotzky, rabbi of Disna, reported to the Rebbe on his chavura learning chassidus and attempts at a Tiferes Bachurim group.
story_body: Writing to the Rebbe on 13 Nissan 5694, R. Shimon Levi b'R. Shneur Zalman Belastotzky of Disna reported that the chavura studying chassidus was growing and gaining strength. However, his repeated attempts to establish a 'Tiferes Bachurim' group had not yet succeeded in taking firm hold.

title_en: Visa #42 issued for R. Betzalel Katz
summary_en: In the summer of 5700, visa #42 to the United States was arranged by the Rebbe Rayatz for R. Betzalel HaKohen Katz, the senior rabbi of Rakishok.
story_body: R. Betzalel HaKohen Katz, called the elder of Lithuania's rabbis, had served the Rakishok community alongside R. Shmuel Levitin. In the summer of 5700 (1940), as part of the rescue effort, the Rebbe Rayatz arranged visa #42 of the first list of recipients for him to travel to the United States.

title_en: Rebbe writes about R. Shmuel Abba Sneg
summary_en: In 5709 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Chief Rabbi Herzog of Eretz Yisrael describing R. Shmuel Abba Sneg, a former Lithuanian army chaplain then serving in postwar Germany.
story_body: In 5709 (1948/49), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote about R. Shmuel Abba Sneg to Israel's Chief Rabbi Herzog (Igros Kodesh vol. 10, letter 3499). The Rebbe noted Sneg's earlier role as chaplain in the Lithuanian army and his postwar role as av beis din for the Orthodox kehillos in the American zone of Germany, in connection with an offer he had received to serve as rabbi of Jaffa.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz's first visit to Vilna after leaving Russia
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Vilna for about a week in late Adar 5688, his first visit to Lithuania after leaving Russia.
story_body: A few months after leaving Soviet Russia, the Rebbe traveled to Warsaw and on his return to Riga stopped in Vilna at the urgent request of local chassidim and the Tomchei Tmimim students there. Originally planned for two days, he extended his stay to a full week after a further appeal from chassidim in Dolhinov.
