He delivered a maamar at the Apatov shul where the yeshiva was housed, prayed there on Shabbat, and met with Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski regarding aid to Russian Jewry.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva founded in Vilna
summary_en: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva was established in Vilna less than a year before the Rebbe's first visit there in Adar 5688.
story_body: A branch of the Chabad Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Vilna, then under Polish rule, in the period prior to Adar 5688. The Rebbe Rayatz visited the yeshiva during his first trip to Lithuania, addressing the students at the Apatov shul where it was housed.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Rakishok in Lithuania
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Rakishok from Rosh Chodesh Adar to 9 Adar 5691, meeting Anash from throughout Lithuania.
story_body: After the Lithuanian chassidim sent delegations led by Rabbi Yisrael Noach of Kupishok requesting a visit, the Rebbe traveled to Rakishok for nine days. He received hundreds for yechidus until late at night, addressed yeshiva students from Telz and Ponevezh, met with Yavneh school representatives and Tiferes Bachurim leaders, and delivered several maamarim including 'V'habriach Hatichon' and 'Atah Echad'.

title_en: Agudas Nashim women's society founded in Rakishok
summary_en: During his Rakishok visit, the Rebbe Rayatz founded an Agudas Nashim society dedicated to family purity.
story_body: On the evening following his arrival, the Rebbe convened a gathering of men and women in Rakishok and spoke about taharas hamishpacha. At that assembly an Agudas Nashim society was founded with a registry book opened with a blessing and signature from the Rebbe himself.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Tomchei Tmimim branches via Warsaw
summary_en: On 9 Tammuz 5691 the Rebbe left Riga for Warsaw to meet students from the Warsaw, Vilna and Lodz Tomchei Tmimim branches.
story_body: The Rebbe traveled from Riga to Warsaw to inspect the three Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot under his direction. Students from the Vilna and Lodz branches traveled to Warsaw, where they were received in yechidus during the visit.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Glubokoe and Postov
summary_en: In early Adar Sheni 5692 the Rebbe visited small towns in the Vilna region including Glubokoe and Postov for about ten days.
story_body: Responding to requests from Anash in the roughly forty small towns of the Vilna region who could not travel to see him, the Rebbe spent about ten days touring the area until Purim. He delivered three maamarim in Postov and was accompanied by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kupershtok of Postov and Rabbi Mordechai Chefetz. The train broke down en route, requiring a four-hour wait during which he received about fifty people in yechidus.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Lodmir in Volhynia
summary_en: From 23 Av 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Lodmir for several days, meeting Anash from across the Volhynia region.
story_body: Traveling from Druskininkai through Brisk and Kovel, the Rebbe arrived in Lodmir to be greeted by massive crowds requiring police escort. He delivered the maamar 'Re'eh Anochi Notein' before Shabbat at the great synagogue holding two thousand people, addressed an audience of hundreds in Yiddish on the nature of Chassidus, visited the gravesite of Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin, and discussed strengthening the mikveh and establishing a yeshiva with community leaders.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz stops in Vilna returning from Lodmir
summary_en: On his way back from Lodmir to Riga in early Elul 5692, the Rebbe stopped in Vilna for several days.
story_body: Accompanied by his son-in-law Rashag, the Rebbe stayed at the Briston Hotel and prayed at the Apatov Chabad synagogue. He held a third Shabbat meal with senior Chabad rabbis including those of Kornitz, Postov, Doksitz, Dolhinov and Radoshkovitz, received many for yechidus, and visited Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzinski and the wealthy chassid Shneur Zalman Zeligson.

title_en: Maamar Ani LeDodi delivered in Vilna
summary_en: On 6 Elul 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Ani LeDodi' in Vilna during his stop returning from Lodmir.
story_body: During his several-day stop in Vilna on the way back from Lodmir to Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Ani LeDodi' on Wednesday 6 Elul. The maamar is recorded in the index of the Rebbe's discourses for that period.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Glubokoe for two weeks
summary_en: From 20 Sivan to 6 Tammuz 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz visited Glubokoe, his final visit to the Vilna region.
story_body: Traveling from Warsaw via a brief stop in Vilna, the Rebbe was received at the Glubokoe station by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kupershtok and a large crowd. Over the two-week visit he delivered the maamar 'Az Yibaka' at the Lubavitch shul, received Anash for yechidus throughout each day, and prayed at the Starashele and Lubavitch synagogues. On 5 Tammuz community leaders informed him of their decision to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in the town.

title_en: Decision to open Tomchei Tmimim branch in Glubokoe
summary_en: On 5 Tammuz 5694 Glubokoe community leaders announced to the Rebbe their decision to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva.
story_body: On Monday 5 Tammuz during the Rebbe Rayatz's visit to Glubokoe, he met at the home of Rabbi Kupershtok with gabbaim of the local batei midrash and town notables. There they informed him of their decision to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva in the town.

title_en: City renamed from Dinaburg to Dvinsk
summary_en: The Latvian city formerly called Dinaburg was officially renamed Dvinsk.
story_body: Daugavpils, the second-largest city in Latvia, southeast of Riga, went through several name changes. Until 5653 (1893) it was known as Dinaburg, after which the authorities renamed it Dvinsk. The city would later be renamed again to Daugavpils.

title_en: City of Dvinsk renamed Daugavpils
summary_en: Dvinsk received its current Latvian name, Daugavpils, in 5681 (1921).
story_body: After Latvia gained independence, the city known as Dvinsk under Russian rule was officially renamed Daugavpils in 5681 (1921). This was the third name for the city, following Dinaburg and Dvinsk. It remains the country's second-largest city.

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind appointed rabbi of Dinaburg
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind, the 'Batlan,' was called from Wilkomir to serve as rabbi in Dinaburg around 5578 (1818).
story_body: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind, author of 'Zecher Yehuda,' was a leading disciple of the Alter Rebbe and study-partner of the Tzemach Tzedek. After serving in Wilkomir (Vilna district), he was called around 5578 (1818) to the rabbinate of Dinaburg, first in the old quarter and later in the central new district.

title_en: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind of Dinaburg passes away
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind, second rabbi of Dinaburg and author of 'Zecher Yehuda,' died on 23 Kislev 5618.
story_body: After roughly four decades as rabbi of Dinaburg, R' Yehuda Leib Zalkind passed away on 23 Kislev 5618 (December 1857). A disciple of the Alter Rebbe and contemporary of the Tzemach Tzedek, he had corresponded with the latter in halachic responsa from their youth.

title_en: R' Feivel Rappaport of Dinaburg passes away
summary_en: R' Feivel Rappaport, the third rabbi of Dinaburg, died around 5623 (1863).
story_body: R' Feivel Rappaport, a Chassidic scholar, served as the third rabbi of Dinaburg. He passed away around 5623 (1863), making way for R' Aryeh Leib Zivov of Smilevitz to assume the rabbinate.

title_en: R' Aryeh Leib Zivov assumes Dinaburg rabbinate
summary_en: R' Aryeh Leib 'Smilevitzer' Zivov, a leading disciple of the Tzemach Tzedek, became rabbi of Dinaburg around 5624 (1864).
story_body: R' Aryeh Leib Zivov, who had previously served in Smilevitz and earlier in Homil, was a senior chassid and emissary of the Tzemach Tzedek. He took up the Dinaburg rabbinate around 5624 (1864) and served until approximately 5647 (1887).

title_en: Dinaburg adopts dual-rabbi structure
summary_en: Starting in 5625 (1865), Dinaburg had two rabbis simultaneously — one Chassidic, one Misnagdic.
story_body: From 5625 (1865) onward, the Jewish community of Dinaburg was served by two rabbis at the same time, one chosen by the Chassidim and one by the Misnagdim. The Misnagdic community first brought R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen of Pruzhana to fill their post.

title_en: R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen passes away in Dinaburg
summary_en: R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen of Pruzhana, author of 'Teshuvot LaShoel' and 'Magen Shaul,' died in 5639 (1879).
story_body: Brought from Pruzhana around 5625 (1865) as Misnagdic rabbi of Dinaburg, R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen authored 'Teshuvot LaShoel' and 'Magen Shaul.' He served the community until his death in 5639 (1879).

title_en: R' Reuven HaLevi Levin succeeds him in Dinaburg
summary_en: R' Reuven HaLevi Levin filled the Misnagdic rabbinic chair of Dinaburg from 5639 (1879).
story_body: After R' Aharon Shaul Zelig HaKohen's death in 5639 (1879), R' Reuven HaLevi Levin assumed the Misnagdic rabbinate of Dinaburg. He served in that position until his own death in 5647 (1887).

title_en: R' Meir Simcha HaKohen of Dvinsk appointed
summary_en: R' Meir Simcha HaKohen, future author of 'Or Sameach' and 'Meshech Chochmah,' became Misnagdic rabbi of Dvinsk in 5647 (1887).
story_body: On the passing of R' Reuven HaLevi Levin in 5647 (1887), R' Meir Simcha HaKohen was selected to fill the Misnagdic rabbinic chair in Dinaburg/Dvinsk. He would become world-famous as the author of 'Or Sameach' and 'Meshech Chochmah.'

title_en: R' Yeshayahu Berlin settles in Riga
summary_en: R' Yeshayahu Berlin, a leading supporter of Tomchei Tmimim, settled in Riga around 5638 (1878).
story_body: R' Yeshayahu Berlin, a wealthy benefactor and one of the main supporters of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch as well as other activities of the Rebbe Rashab, established himself in Riga around 5638 (1878). His arrival anchored the growing Chabad community in the Latvian capital.

title_en: Latvian authorities permit second Riga synagogue
summary_en: In 1878 the Latvian authorities allowed an additional synagogue to be built within the Chassidic shul building in Riga.
story_body: In 5638 (1878) the Latvian authorities permitted the construction of an additional synagogue building within the Riga Chassidic shul complex. From then on, three minyanim — all called 'Draisin' minyanim — operated under one roof: a mixed Chabad minyan, one exclusively for Lubavitch chassidim, and a larger one for Kapust chassidim.

title_en: Chassidic prayer house built in Libau
summary_en: The Chassidic prayer house in Libau (Liepaja) was constructed by the Chassidic community in 5650 (1890).
story_body: In 5650 (1890) the Chassidic community of Libau (today Liepaja, Latvia) built their dedicated prayer house. The building was known simply as 'the Chassidishe Minyan' and followed Nusach Ha'Ari prayer rite.

title_en: R' Chaim Leib Gar's son R' Tzvi Gar born in Yakobshtadt
summary_en: R' Tzvi (Hershl) Gar, future representative of the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga, was born to R' Chaim Leib in Yakobshtadt.
story_body: R' Tzvi Gar was born in Yakobshtadt, Kurland — a stronghold of Chabad Chassidism — to his father R' Chaim Leib. He was educated at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch and later served as a mashgiach in the Riga slaughterhouse, becoming the Rebbe Rayatz's contact person in Riga in the early years of his leadership.

title_en: R' Yaakov Himelfarb's father dies in Libau
summary_en: R' Yaakov Himelfarb's father passed away on 7 Iyar 5651 in Libau, when his son was eleven years old.
story_body: On 7 Iyar 5651 (May 1891) R' Yaakov Himelfarb's father died in Libau, leaving his eleven-year-old son to grow up in the community. The Himelfarb family — father, grandfather, and great-grandfather — were all Chabad chassidim who prayed in Nusach Ha'Ari.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa born in Kornitz
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa, future rabbi of Libau and Bnei Brak, was born on 5 Iyar 5653 in Kornitz.
story_body: R' Yaakov Landa was born on 5 Iyar 5653 (April 21, 1893) in Kornitz to his father R' Moshe Yehuda Leib. He would go on to study at Tomchei Tmimim, serve as rabbi of Kornitz, Libau and finally Bnei Brak.

title_en: R' Yeshayahu Berlin opens additional Riga Chabad minyan
summary_en: R' Yeshayahu Berlin opened an additional Chabad minyan in Riga in 5661 (1901).
story_body: Building on his earlier work in Riga, R' Yeshayahu Berlin opened an additional Chabad minyan in the city in 5661 (1901). The synagogue at 22/24 Mills Street later carried his name as a memorial to his role.

title_en: R' Chaim Aba Veil begins shul attendance in Dvinsk
summary_en: R' Chaim Aba Veil began praying as a child in Dvinsk's 'Painters' Synagogue' in 5665 (1905).
story_body: In 5665 (1905) the young Chaim Aba Veil started accompanying adults to the 'Farbershe Minyan' — the Painters' Synagogue on the Zhitomir Street in the Pletzer district of Dvinsk. Founded originally by the city's painters, it had become by then a leading Chabad shul, and existed until the Nazi destruction.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa enters Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa began studying at the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in 5668 (1908).
story_body: R' Yaakov Landa entered the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Lubavitch in 5668 (1908). He continued his studies there until 5672 (1912), receiving a full Chabad chassidic and Talmudic education.

title_en: R' Yehoshua Arsh becomes Rosh Yeshiva at Zal Hakatan
summary_en: R' Yehoshua Arsh was accepted as Rosh Yeshiva of the Zal Hakatan in Lubavitch in 5671 (1911).
story_body: R' Yehoshua Arsh, who had been head of the Dvinsk yeshiva endowed by the wealthy R' Moshe Weitenberg, was accepted in 5671 (1911) as Rosh Yeshiva of the Zal Hakatan ('small hall') of Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. At the request of R' Dovid Volovich of Dvinsk, he brought his son Chaim Aba Veil along to study in Lubavitch.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa appointed rabbi of Kornitz
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa was appointed rabbi of Kornitz on 21 Elul 5673 (September 1913), succeeding his father.
story_body: At the end of 5673 (September 1913), R' Yaakov Landa was appointed to the rabbinate of Kornitz, filling the position of his late father R' Moshe Yehuda Leib. The appointment was formalized on 21 Elul 5673. He was forced to leave during World War I.

title_en: R' Yosef Rosen, the Rogatchover Gaon, ends first Dvinsk tenure
summary_en: R' Yosef Rosen of Rogatchov served as Dvinsk's Chassidic rabbi until 1915, when wartime conditions forced his departure.
story_body: R' Yosef Rosen, the famed Rogatchover Gaon, served as Chassidic rabbi at the Planover Minyan inside Dvinsk until 1915 (5675). World War I forced him to leave the city, though he would return more than a decade later.

title_en: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrives in Riga
summary_en: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrived in Riga from Russia on Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5685, en route to the United States.
story_body: On Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5685 (July 22, 1925), R' Yisrael Jacobson reached Riga as part of his journey out of Soviet Russia toward the United States. He was held there awaiting an American entry visa, and during his stay delivered chassidic discourses in the Bazaar Berg synagogue.

title_en: R' Yosef Rosen returns to Dvinsk rabbinate
summary_en: The Rogatchover Gaon returned to Dvinsk in 5686 (1926) and resumed his rabbinate.
story_body: After more than a decade in Russia, R' Yosef Rosen returned to Dvinsk in 5686 (1926) and resumed serving as rabbi of the city's Planover Minyan. He continued in that role until 5696 (1936).

title_en: R' Yisrael Jacobson departs Riga for America
summary_en: R' Yisrael Jacobson left Riga on 19 Kislev 5686 after months of stays with the city's Chabad community.
story_body: Mid-Yud-Tes Kislev Farbrengen on 5686 (December 6, 1925) at the home of the shochet R' Mordechai Chefetz, R' Yisrael Jacobson received parting blessings from his Riga friends and departed. He had spent several months in the city after leaving Russia, joining its tmimim for farbrengens and study of chassidus.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa leaves Russia and settles in Libau
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa left Soviet Russia at the start of 5688 and settled with relatives in Libau.
story_body: At the beginning of 5688 (1927), R' Yaakov Landa exited Soviet Russia, where he had served as rabbi in the Rebbe Rashab's court in Rostov and headed Tiferes Bachurim in Moscow. He settled with relatives in Libau (Liepaja), Latvia, with the Rebbe Rayatz personally directing him to assess the local community's needs.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Dvinsk en route to Warsaw
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz made a brief visit to Dvinsk in late Shevat 5688, traveling from Riga to Warsaw.
story_body: In late Shevat 5688 (February 1928), the Rebbe Rayatz stopped in Dvinsk en route from Riga to Warsaw. He addressed the local anash during this short visit, encouraging the Chabad community of the city.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa's rabbinical writ signed for Libau
summary_en: On 17 Tishrei 5689 about forty heads of Libau's Chassidic community signed R' Yaakov Landa's rabbinical writ.
story_body: After repeated encouragement from the Rebbe Rayatz to accept the Libau rabbinate, R' Yaakov Landa's rabbinical writ was signed on 17 Tishrei 5689 (October 1, 1928) by some forty heads of the local Chassidic community. The writ formalized his position as rabbi of the Libau Chassidim.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa marries Mina Rabinowitz
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa married Mrs. Mina Rabinowitz in the winter of 5690, with the Rogatchover officiating.
story_body: In the winter of 5690 (1929-1930), R' Yaakov Landa, rabbi of the Libau Chassidim, married Mrs. Mina Rabinowitz. A 9 Kislev 5690 article in the Frimorgn newspaper announced the wedding and noted that the Rogatchover Gaon would serve as the mesader kiddushin.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa serves as shadar in Latvia
summary_en: In early 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz sent R' Yaakov Landa as a Kollel Chabad emissary to the towns of Latvia.
story_body: At the start of 5692 (1932), the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R' Yaakov Landa as a Kollel Chabad shadar (fundraising emissary) to the Jewish communities of Latvia. That same year, his appointment as general rabbi of Libau was also under consideration, prompting correspondence from the Rogatchover.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa makes aliyah to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa left Latvia for Eretz Yisrael in 5694 (1934), initially serving as rabbi of Ramatayim.
story_body: In 5694 (1934), R' Yaakov Landa immigrated to Eretz Yisrael, leaving his Libau rabbinate. He first took up the rabbinate of Ramatayim (today part of Hod Hasharon) before being chosen the following year as rabbi of Bnei Brak.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa elected rabbi of Bnei Brak
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa was elected rabbi of Bnei Brak in 5695 (1935), a position he held for fifty years.
story_body: In 5695 (1935), R' Yaakov Landa was selected as rabbi of Bnei Brak. He would serve the city for half a century — a full jubilee — until his death in 5746, becoming one of the most influential Chabad rabbis in the Holy Land.

title_en: R' Yosef Rosen ends second Dvinsk tenure
summary_en: The Rogatchover Gaon's second tenure as rabbi of Dvinsk's Planover Minyan ended in 1936.
story_body: After returning to Dvinsk in 1926, R' Yosef Rosen, the Rogatchover Gaon, served at the Planover Minyan until 1936 (5696). His departure marked the close of one of the most renowned Chabad rabbinates in interwar Latvia.

title_en: Dvinsk anash commit to weekly chassidus study
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5697 the Dvinsk community held a farbrengen and committed to weekly chassidus study.
story_body: On 19 Kislev 5697 (December 3, 1936) a farbrengen was held in a Dvinsk hall, and the participants accepted upon themselves to learn chassidus together once a week. They signed a letter that day informing the Rebbe Rayatz, who responded with blessing on 29 Kislev. Organizer R' Baruch Eliyahu Peletz reported on 24 Tevet that 40-50 men, including older anash, were attending.

title_en: R' Yaakov Landa, rabbi of Bnei Brak, passes away
summary_en: R' Yaakov Landa passed away on 26 Shevat 5746 after fifty years as rabbi of Bnei Brak.
story_body: After serving Bnei Brak as its rabbi for a full jubilee — fifty years — R' Yaakov Landa passed away on 26 Shevat 5746 (February 5, 1986). His earlier career had taken him from Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch to Kornitz, the Rebbe Rashab's court in Rostov, Moscow's Tiferes Bachurim, and the Libau rabbinate before his aliyah.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz released from Soviet imprisonment and exile
summary_en: In summer 1927, the Rebbe Rayatz was released from Soviet imprisonment and exile but faced ongoing danger of re-arrest.
story_body: After his arrest and exile in Soviet Russia in summer 1927 (5687), Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was freed but remained under threat of further imprisonment. The danger compelled him to seek to leave Russia as quickly as possible. Latvian parliament deputy Mordechai Dubin worked through the summer to secure his exit visa by arranging his appointment as Chief Rabbi of Riga.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz departs Leningrad with family
summary_en: On Thursday 24 Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz and his family left Leningrad for Latvia.
story_body: After months of effort by Mordechai Dubin to secure exit papers, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Leningrad with his family on Thursday morning. Senior Chabad rabbis accompanied him by train to the border station at Pskov. From Pskov they wrote a farewell letter to Latvian Jewry on behalf of the Rebbe.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga from Soviet Russia
summary_en: On Friday 25 Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga, establishing the new center of Chabad activity outside the Soviet Union.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga with his family, having been appointed Chief Rabbi of the city, which had enabled his exit from Russia. His arrival expanded the existing Chabad community in Riga and made it the new hub of his work on behalf of Soviet Jewry. He first stayed at the Kommerz Hotel for about a month before securing apartments.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes thank-you letters to those who secured his release
summary_en: On Sunday 27 Tishrei 5688, two days after arriving in Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz began writing thank-you letters to those who worked for his release.
story_body: Although exhausted from his journey from Russia and not yet settled in housing, the Rebbe Rayatz immediately sat down to write thanks to the people who had advocated for his release. He had no secretaries at this time, as R. Chaim Lieberman was still in exile in Tambov and R. Yechezkel Feigin had not yet managed to leave Russia.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes 11+ letters from Riga in single day
summary_en: On Tuesday 29 Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote at least 11 letters to associates in Russia and abroad announcing his safe arrival.
story_body: Working alone without secretaries, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote letters to close associates inside Russia and abroad, announcing his arrival, asking about their welfare, and requesting greetings be passed to various figures. Within the first month from Russia, he wrote at least 70 letters, mostly to heads of the Chasidic community in Russia, encouraging them in their difficult situation and directing the continuation of religious activity.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz rents two apartments in Riga
summary_en: On 27 Cheshvan 5688, after a month in a hotel, the Rebbe Rayatz rented two apartments in Riga to house his family, his mother, and a place of prayer.
story_body: After about a month at the Kommerz Hotel, the Rebbe Rayatz secured two small apartments on two floors. The lower floor housed his mother the Rebbetzin and contained the prayer room and part of his library. The upper floor was for the Rebbe and his daughters Chaya Mushka and Sheina, while his daughter Chana and son-in-law Rashag took a separate apartment.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Berlin to meet Joint leadership
summary_en: Immediately after moving to his new Riga apartment, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Berlin to meet with Jewish leaders about aid for Soviet Jewry.
story_body: On the same day he moved into his new apartment, the Rebbe traveled to Berlin to meet with major activists including R. Meir Hildesheimer, the Rogatchover Gaon, R. M.M. Zack of Riga, and Mordechai Dubin to discuss the budget for Torah institutions in Russia. This meeting led to the establishment of a special bureau under his direction for the relief work.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for Warsaw visit
summary_en: On Sunday 28 Shevat 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Warsaw, responding to the Polish Chabad community's request for a visit.
story_body: After the Warsaw Chabad community invited the Rebbe to settle there following his exit from Russia, he replied that this was impossible but he wished to visit. He set out from Riga in the morning, stopping in Dvinsk, Vilna, and other towns en route. The trip combined visits to yeshivas and Chasidim with meetings on Soviet Jewry relief.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Warsaw for three-week visit
summary_en: On Monday eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Warsaw for a three-week stay, followed by a week in Otwock.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Warsaw on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar I. He spent three weeks in the city and nearly a week in Otwock, visiting the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva and meeting with Chasidim. He also held several meetings related to aid for Soviet Jewry, returning via a week-long stop in Vilna.

title_en: Rashag departs Riga for Paris fundraising mission
summary_en: On the night of motzei Shabbos 8 Iyar 5688, R. Shmaryahu Gourary (Rashag) left Riga for Paris to raise funds for Soviet Jewry.
story_body: After Passover, the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched his son-in-law Rashag to England and France to organize a fundraising effort for Soviet Jewry suffering under anti-religious persecution. In Paris he was joined by R. Alexander Sender Reinin, R. Menachem Mendel Rotshtein of Warsaw, and Mr. Guggenheim of Switzerland.

title_en: Rashag meets Chief Rabbi of France in Paris
summary_en: On Sunday 16 Iyar 5688, Rashag met with French Chief Rabbi Israel Levi and his secretary R. Moshe Lieber.
story_body: Rashag's Paris mission included a meeting with French Chief Rabbi Israel Levi and his secretary Moshe Lieber. The following day he met Mr. Warnser, personal secretary to Baron Edmond Rothschild, as well as Mr. Bigart of the Alliance Israélite Universelle and Mr. Unger of JCA, who pledged participation in the work.

title_en: Paris assembly convened for Soviet Jewry aid
summary_en: On Friday 21 Iyar 5688, Rashag convened a general assembly in Paris bringing together French Jewish leadership for Russian Jewry relief.
story_body: The assembly drew Chief Rabbi Israel Levi, Chief Rabbi Eisenstadt, R. Moshe Lieber, Baron Pierre Ginzburg, S. Pollak, Mr. Unger of JCA, Mr. Bigart of the Alliance, Mr. Tedesco of the Paris Consistoire, Mr. Warnser as Baron Rothschild's secretary, and attorney Matieu Miller. The meeting consolidated French support for the Rebbe's work.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Chief Rabbi Hertz of England
summary_en: On 21 Tammuz 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to British Chief Rabbi J.H. Hertz about 20,000 Soviet Jewish children needing Torah education.
story_body: The Rebbe described how 20,000 children in the USSR sought religious learning but could not access it primarily for lack of funds, urging European Jewry to mobilize on behalf of Soviet Jews. He argued that the persecution was not the only obstacle — financial means were the decisive missing element.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz vacations in Bulduri near Riga
summary_en: During summer 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz spent a month in Bulduri near Riga, though he continued working rather than truly resting.
story_body: Worn out by imprisonment, exile, and intensive work, the Rebbe Rayatz had been advised to rest. He delayed it until midsummer, when he took a month-long stay in the seaside resort of Bulduri near Riga. By his own account he did nothing for his health there, continuing to work through correspondence each day.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Berlin to meet Joint executives
summary_en: In mid-Elul 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Berlin to negotiate continuing Joint Distribution Committee support for Russian Torah work.
story_body: The Joint had funded the Rebbe's Soviet activities since 1922, but signaled they would not continue funding Torah work in Europe for 5689. In Berlin the Rebbe met with R. Aharon Teitelbaum, head of Central Relief, along with Hildesheimer, Mr. Cohen, Mr. Rosen, and Hildesheimer to argue for continued support specifically for Russia.

title_en: Wedding date set for Rebbe Menachem Mendel and Chaya Mushka
summary_en: On 16 Cheshvan 5689, the wedding of R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson to Chaya Mushka was set for 14 Kislev in Warsaw.
story_body: After waiting in hopes that the groom's father Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn would be granted Soviet permission to attend, the date was finalized for 14 Kislev in Warsaw, with the chuppah at the courtyard of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva. The father was ultimately denied travel papers. Mass invitations were sent to Chasidim, activists, rabbis, and Rebbes.

title_en: Wedding of Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson and Chaya Mushka in Warsaw
summary_en: On 14 Kislev 5689 in Warsaw, the future Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson married Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: The chuppah was held in the courtyard of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw. The groom's father R. Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn, in Soviet Russia, was denied a travel permit and could not attend. The Rebbe's uncle R. Moshe Hornstein and aunt served as unterfirer on the groom's side in place of the father.

title_en: Matzah operation for Soviet Jewry begins
summary_en: On 17 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed Rashag and Mordechai Dubin to begin organizing massive shipments of kosher matzah into Soviet Russia.
story_body: Reports from across the USSR indicated that Passover flour could not be obtained anywhere. The Rebbe launched an enormous operation to ship 28 train cars of matzah to communities in 17 Soviet towns and 5,689 packages of matzah flour to private addresses in 404 towns. Negotiations with the Soviet embassy in Riga and Berlin over export permits and customs duties dominated the next three months.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes urgent appeal to Aharon Teitelbaum
summary_en: On 19 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a desperate letter to R. Aharon Teitelbaum, chairman of Central Relief, after a telegram saying budget hopes were lost.
story_body: The Rebbe described receiving a telegram from R. Lukshin reading 'no hope for the budget,' which devastated him. A second telegram said Teitelbaum 'gives hope for next week,' indicating the question would return to the table. He spelled out that Soviet institutions were 'flailing between life and death,' with R. Rosen having loaned 15,000 rubles.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz raises possibility of trip to America
summary_en: On 20 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Agudas Chabad leadership in America that the budget crisis might force him to travel there.
story_body: Citing advice from R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski of Vilna and the Chofetz Chaim, the Rebbe wrote that he might have to make the journey to the United States to put the relief effort for Russian Jewry on a stable footing. The trip would be deferred until after the matzah operation, then take shape via the Holy Land starting Elul.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Berlin for matzah operation meetings
summary_en: On Sunday 21 Adar I 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Berlin and organized a week of meetings with European delegates on the matzah relief operation.
story_body: Through the week, the Rebbe convened representatives from several European countries to coordinate fundraising for the matzah operation. From Berlin he sent a detailed telegram to Riga to sign the contract for matzah baking under the supervision of Rabbi M.M. Zack. He returned to Riga at the end of Adar I.

title_en: All 28 matzah cars confirmed arrived in Soviet Russia
summary_en: On the night of 12-13 Nisan 5689, word reached the Rebbe Rayatz that all 28 train cars and 5,689 matzah-flour packages had reached their Soviet destinations.
story_body: After months of negotiations over export permits and customs rates — initially 5 kopecks per kilo, then a demand of 2 rubles per kilo before settling at half a ruble — 28 train cars of matzah were shipped from Riga and Berlin to 17 Soviet towns. Alongside the cars, 5,689 packages of matzah flour reached private addresses across 404 towns, all arriving by the eve of Passover 5689.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz announces trip to America via Holy Land
summary_en: On 27 Nisan 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Agudas Chabad in America agreeing to visit, planning to travel via the Holy Land first.
story_body: With travel back to the Soviet Union impossible to visit the graves of his ancestors, the Rebbe decided to route his journey through the Holy Land before reaching America. He targeted early Elul for the trip's beginning. The visit was meant to consolidate funding for Torah work in Russia under intensifying persecution.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz urges Latvia Anash to expand public Chassidus study
summary_en: From America the Rebbe Rayatz wrote an open letter to Anash in Latvia urging dedicated public Chassidus study and announcing a special committee to promote it.
story_body: While visiting the United States the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched a general letter (Vol. II, Iggeret 464) to Anash and Chassidic families across Latvia, urging each one to weigh his present spiritual state against the standard of earlier Chassidim and to commit to fixed times of public Chassidus study. He announced the formation of a special committee for this purpose and called on rabbis, ritual slaughterers, and synagogue gabbaim throughout Latvia to join hands in bringing the threefold blessing tied to such study to every town.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes coordinated letters blessing the Latvia Chassidus committee
summary_en: On 4 Nisan the Rebbe Rayatz sent a series of letters thanking and blessing the new committee in Riga, led by R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov, for the spread of Chassidus study.
story_body: On 4 Nisan 5690 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a coordinated set of letters: to R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov (later his personal secretary) who chaired the Riga committee, to R. Shneur Zalman Yitzchak Wolshonok, to Anash of Riga, and to the General Committee for Expanding Chassidus Study in Latvia. He thanked them for the news that additional batei midrash had opened Chassidus shiurim and proposed that during Chol HaMoed Pesach all of the city's study groups convene in one shul to review a discourse together, strengthen mutual love, and inspire the younger generation.

title_en: Chodakov reports growing Chassidus shiurim in Riga to Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov reported to the Rebbe Rayatz that the Latvia committee had opened new shiurim in synagogues that had not heard Chassidus for years.
story_body: Writing on 25 Nisan 5690, Chodakov informed the Rebbe Rayatz that batei midrash which had not heard a Chassidus discourse in living memory now hosted regular shiurim, and that a fresh shiur had just been started in an unexpected beis midrash in Riga. He singled out the contributions of refugee rabbis Israel Zuber, Avraham Eli Asherov, and Yehuda Eber, and especially R. Eli Chaim Althaus, whose enthusiasm and personal commitment to serve as mashpia in one shul made an entire shiur possible.

title_en: Riga committee meets at Wolshonok's home to plan citywide Chassidus gathering
summary_en: Twelve members of the Riga committee met at R. Shneur Zalman Yitzchak Wolshonok's home and resolved to hold a citywide gathering of Chassidus students on Rosh Chodesh Iyar at the Dreyzin shul.
story_body: Because the Rebbe Rayatz's instruction to hold the gathering during Chol HaMoed Pesach only reached Riga on the third day of the intermediate days, the committee had to postpone. On 29 Nisan 5690 twelve committee members gathered at R. Wolshonok's home and decided in protocol number 9 to convene the general assembly on Rosh Chodesh Iyar at the middle minyan of the Dreyzin beis midrash.

title_en: Citywide farbrengen of Riga Chassidus study groups at Dreyzin shul
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5690 the Riga committee held a large farbrengen of Chassidus study circles at the Dreyzin beis midrash, lasting from 9 pm to 2 am.
story_body: Fulfilling the Rebbe Rayatz's proposal, the Riga committee assembled a large gathering of Anash at the middle minyan of the Dreyzin beis midrash for a citywide farbrengen of all the Chassidus study groups. The event ran from 9 pm until 2 am, and Chodakov reported the same day that it would both strengthen existing learners and attract new ones to fixed Chassidus study.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz plans tour of Latvian towns
summary_en: On 6 Tevet 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that he hoped to visit several places in Latvia and was seeking funds to cover the travel.
story_body: In a letter dated 6 Tevet 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz revealed that the idea of personally visiting a number of Latvian communities had occurred to him, and that he was taking on the considerable burden of finding a source to cover the travel expenses. His stated intention was to learn first-hand what was happening in those places and to see whether direct encouragement might accomplish something.

title_en: Riga Anash plead with Rebbe Rayatz not to leave for Warsaw
summary_en: More than one hundred Anash in Riga signed a letter on 12 Elul 5691 begging the Rebbe Rayatz to stay through the upcoming Yamim Noraim rather than move to Warsaw.
story_body: When word spread that the Rebbe Rayatz planned to relocate from Riga to Warsaw, the Riga community at first refused to believe it. Once the plan was confirmed, over a hundred Chassidim signed a letter on 12 Elul 5691 describing their broken hearts and pleading with the Rebbe to remain among them at least for the coming High Holidays rather than take up the larger discussion at such a sensitive moment in the calendar.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz spends Tishrei in Otwock near Warsaw
summary_en: During Tishrei 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz stayed in Otwock near Warsaw, close to the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva, before returning to Riga.
story_body: Although the move from Riga to Warsaw had been postponed, the Rebbe Rayatz spent the month of Tishrei 5692 in Otwock near Warsaw, where the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was located. He had earlier hoped to relocate the senior division of the yeshiva from Warsaw to Riga, but when that plan fell through he decided to take up residence near the yeshiva instead.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz returns from Otwock to Riga
summary_en: In mid-Marcheshvan 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz returned from Otwock to Riga, where he remained for another two years before finally moving to Warsaw.
story_body: After his Tishrei stay in Otwock, the Rebbe Rayatz returned to Riga around the middle of Marcheshvan 5692. He remained there for two more years before the final relocation to Warsaw, and during that period a branch of the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva was also opened in Riga.

title_en: Assembly of Latvian rabbis convenes in Riga
summary_en: On 20 Adar II 5692 an assembly of Latvian rabbis convened in Riga to strengthen Judaism and Shabbos observance, opened by a short programmatic address from the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz urged R. Yaakov Landau to attend the gathering and arranged for him to come to Riga several days early to consult quietly with the organizers, Messrs. Chefetz and Chodakov. The Rebbe's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote on 26 Adar II to R. Israel Jacobson that the assembly produced concrete resolutions on strengthening Judaism in general and Shabbos observance in particular, and that the Rebbe himself opened the proceedings with a brief but substantive speech laying out a principal foundation for the discussions.

title_en: Rayatz settles in Warsaw after emigrating from Riga
summary_en: At the end of 5693, the Rebbe Rayatz moved his residence from Riga to Warsaw.
story_body: After several years of leading Chabad from Riga, where he had settled following his release from Soviet imprisonment, the Rebbe Rayatz relocated to Warsaw in late summer 1933. The transition marked a new phase of his European leadership, though he continued to visit Riga and maintain close ties with the chassidim there.

title_en: Rayatz visits Riga from Warsaw, 12-20 Adar
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz returned from Warsaw to visit Riga, staying from 12-20 Adar 5693.
story_body: Shortly after relocating to Warsaw, the Rebbe traveled back to Riga for a nine-day visit covering Purim. He recited the maamar 'Zachor Es Asher Asah Lecha Amalek' on the night of his arrival, delivered a talk to the women later published in Likkutei Dibburim vol. 3, and farbrenged at length with the temimim and anash on Shabbos.

title_en: Faigin reports on Rebbe's Riga visit to Jacobson
summary_en: Secretary Yechezkel Faigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson on 26 Adar 5693 describing the Rebbe's recent visit to Riga.
story_body: Faigin reported that the chassidic community in Riga had grown with newly arrived refugees from Russia, including R. Shlomo Tumarkin, Michael Dvorkin, and R. Rafael Cohen. They had established a shul named for the Rebbe with daily Gemara and Chassidus shiurim, plus chadarim for children and adults.

title_en: Rayatz writes to son-in-law on Erev Rosh Chodesh Nissan
summary_en: On 29 Adar 5693 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (later Rebbe) describing the Riga visit.
story_body: The letter (vol. 15, no. 5533) recounts the warm reception by the young temimim, the recital of maamarim including 'V'Hayah Kaasher Yarim Moshe', the Purim seudah lasting past midnight, and the Shabbos meals among anash that ran far longer than usual.

title_en: Rogatchover Gaon passes away in Dvinsk
summary_en: The Rogatchover Gaon (R. Yosef Rosen) passed away on 11 Adar 5696.
story_body: The death of one of the great halachic luminaries of the era prompted commemorations across the Jewish world. R. Rafael Cohen, rabbi of the Riga chassidic community, delivered a eulogy at Erev Rosh Chodesh Nissan in the beis medrash named for the Rogatchover, later published as the booklet 'Emunah V'Zechirah'.

title_en: Rafael Cohen eulogizes the Rogatchover in Riga
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5696, R. Rafael Cohen delivered a hesped for the Rogatchover Gaon.
story_body: The eulogy was delivered in the beis medrash bearing the Rogatchover's name. In 5699 it was printed as the kuntres 'Emunah V'Zechirah' with the Rebbe Rayatz's haskama affirming that 'the entire content is true and proper and worthy of publication.'

title_en: Letter on Chabad Chassidus translated and published in Yiddish
summary_en: In 5698 Achos Tmimim Riga published a Yiddish translation of the Rebbe's letter on the moral and educational meaning of Chabad Chassidus.
story_body: Members B. Gadin and Ch. Mikhailover of Achos Tmimim translated the Hebrew letter (vol. 3, no. 837) into Yiddish and printed it as a standalone kuntres in Riga. It was titled 'Di Moralishe un Dertzierishe Badaytung fun Chassidus Chabad' and presented as an answer to an inquiry from Germany.

title_en: Kislev farbrengens across Riga's Chabad minyanim
summary_en: Yud-Tes Kislev 5697 was celebrated in over ten minyanim across Riga, including the Rebbe's main minyan and the Beis Medrash Chabad.
story_body: R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse reported the festivities in detail: a newly received account of the arrest and liberation in colloquial language was read aloud in each minyan, the Shas was divided for the year, and chazaras maamarim and divrei hisorerus extended deep into the night. The Rebbe's minyan at Kurmanava 20/01 functioned as the central chassidic hub.

title_en: Altheuse reports on Yud-Tes Kislev to Faigin
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Tevet 5697, R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse wrote a detailed report to secretary Faigin about the Yud-Tes Kislev farbrengens.
story_body: Altheuse described the Lubavitcher Rebbe's minyan as 'der Lubavitcher Rebbe's minyan' - the central chassidic gathering place where shiurim in Chassidus were learned daily, where one could obtain a kuntres, kosher tefillin straps, or Lubavitcher tzitzis, and where the name 'Lubavitch' was constantly on every mispallel's lips.

title_en: Achos Tmimim founded in Riga
summary_en: The Achos Tmimim organization for daughters of Chabad chassidim was established in Riga during winter 5697.
story_body: Beginning the previous winter, daughters of Riga chassidim had organized informal gatherings. By Yud-Tes Kislev 5697 they were structured enough to send a collective letter to the Rebbe describing their celebration. Over the course of 5697 the framework crystallized into the named organization Achos Tmimim, with three appointed 'shepherds': R. Avraham Eliyahu Asherov, R. Mordechai Chefetz, and R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse.

title_en: Girls' letter to the Rebbe on Yud-Tes Kislev gathering
summary_en: A group of daughters of Chabad chassidim in Riga wrote to the Rebbe on 5 Tevet 5697 describing their Yud-Tes Kislev gathering.
story_body: The letter, photographed in Di Yiddishe Heim no. 88 (Tammuz 5742), opens 'We the daughters of Chabad chassidim celebrated this year as well the Chag HaGeulah Yud-Tes Kislev, as in the past year.' It shows that organized women's farbrengens preceded the formal naming of Achos Tmimim.

title_en: Rebbe formally addresses Achos Tmimim in letter
summary_en: On 23 Sivan 5697 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Mordechai Chefetz about the work of Achos Tmimim.
story_body: This is the earliest extant letter explicitly naming the organization. The Rebbe asked Chefetz to write in detail about the learning sessions and whether any practical results were visible, emphasizing how much he wanted to know about the conduct of every child of the chassidim.

title_en: Rebbe writes to Hatamim about Achos Tmimim Riga
summary_en: On 28 Cheshvan 5698 the Rebbe instructed the Hatamim editorial board to cover the new Achos Tmimim organization in Riga.
story_body: The Rebbe named the three appointed shepherds - R. Avraham Eliyahu Asherov, R. Mordechai Chefetz, and R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse - and asked Hatamim to solicit each of their perspectives on the new women's organization, with Altheuse particularly asked to describe the matter at length.

title_en: Rebbe urges founding similar Achos Tmimim chapters elsewhere
summary_en: On 14 Kislev 5698 the Rebbe called on anash and temimim worldwide to establish chapters modeled on the Riga Achos Tmimim.
story_body: The Rebbe wrote that 'recently the daughters of the chassidim in Riga have organized to learn maamarim and hold farbrengens' and that 'it is correct and necessary' for chassidim in other locales to take this as an example, founding similar groups to 'revive the hearts of their daughters with the dew of life of the pleasant ways of Chassidus.'

title_en: Rebbe writes about Dankra yeshiva branch
summary_en: On 8 Elul 5697 the Rebbe wrote to R. Rafael Cohen about establishing a Tomchei Temimim branch in Dankra under the leadership of his son-in-law R. Yeshaya Chanoch Berkhan.
story_body: R. Berkhan had been appointed rabbi of Dankra in 5695 and founded the yeshiva there in 5696. The Rebbe's letter (vol. 4, no. 949) addressed practical aspects of operating the branch as part of the Tomchei Temimim network.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz and family stay in Riga
summary_en: During Tevet through Adar Rishon 5700, the Rebbe and his family - including his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah - resided in Riga.
story_body: The extended stay came in the early months of World War II, before the Rebbe's departure to America. Photographs preserved from this period show classes of Achos Tmimim posing with Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah and with two of their mashpiim. Soviet Latvia would be invaded the following summer.

title_en: Achos Tmimim Riga designated central body for Latvia
summary_en: On 16 Shevat 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz officially designated the Riga Achos Tmimim as 'Achos Tmimim HaMerkazi d'Medinas Latvia'.
story_body: The Rebbe's letter to the leadership directed them to receive the central name, establish a board of directors with appropriate committees - first among them a publicity committee and a teachers' committee - and to draft appropriate regulations for the organization's central operation across Latvia.

title_en: Achos Tmimim chapter opened in Dvinsk
summary_en: On 17 Adar Rishon 5700 the first session of Achos Tmimim Dvinsk took place at the Pinkovich home with six girls present.
story_body: R. Baruch Eliyahu Peletz reported to the Rebbe that the chapter had begun in Dvinsk (renamed Daugavpils). Six girls attended; some committed to come weekly and others said they needed to consult their parents. Mrs. Esther Pinkovich corresponded with the Riga central office for guidance on curriculum and method.

title_en: Founding members of Dvinsk Achos Tmimim documented
summary_en: On 18 Adar Rishon 5700, R. Shraga Yitzchak Pinkovich listed the six founding girls of Achos Tmimim Dvinsk in a letter to the Rebbe.
story_body: The girls were Abigail Golda, Sara Sheskin, Mina Schneersohn, Roza Kagan, Zelda Westerman, and Chaya Zayer - all from chassidic families, several with fathers who had learned in Lubavitch or Rostov. R. Peletz spoke to them about the Baal Shem Tov and explained that the Rebbe wished such a society be founded in their city.

title_en: First Achos Tmimim Dvinsk farbrengen with Riga delegation
summary_en: On 6 Iyar 5700 the first formal farbrengen of Achos Tmimim Dvinsk was held, attended by three delegates from the Riga central office.
story_body: Mrs. Basya Chefetz, Mrs. Mina Skobla, and Mrs. Rivka Kramnikov traveled from Riga to attend. About fourteen girls came from Dvinsk. R. Peletz opened the gathering on the purpose of Chassidus, and three girls - Mrs. Kayder, Mrs. Zelikman, and Mrs. Kaufman - addressed the group. The Rebbe responded with a 200-lat gift to seed a gemach for Achos Tmimim Dvinsk.

title_en: Hillel Horwitz marries Rivka Cohen
summary_en: On 17 Elul 5700, R. Hillel Horwitz - son of R. Yitzchak Matmid - married Rivka, daughter of R. Rafael Cohen.
story_body: The Rebbe had blessed the engagement on 20 Iyar 5700 and worked to secure a rabbinical position for Hillel in the town of Livenhof (Livani), writing to R. Mordechai Dubin on 29 Nissan to advocate for the appointment. R. Yitzchak Matmid sent the Rebbe a wedding invitation with a pidyon nefesh attached.

title_en: Altheuse writes to Rebbe about returning to Russia
summary_en: On 6 Cheshvan 5701, after the Soviet conquest of Latvia, R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse wrote to the Rebbe about his plan to return to his family in Leningrad.
story_body: Altheuse - who had been the matchmaker for the Rebbe and Rebbetzin, accompanied the Rebbe into Kostroma exile in 5687, and remained the lifeblood of Riga anash after the Rebbe's departure - now considered returning to Russia to be with his son and household in Leningrad, despite worsening Soviet decrees. The plan never materialized.

title_en: Nazi conquest of Latvia; Riga Jews murdered
summary_en: In summer 5701 the Nazis conquered Latvia and murdered its Jewish community.
story_body: Among those killed were R. Rafael Cohen, who ran into the burning shul to save the Sefer Torah and was locked inside; R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse, the leading figure of Riga anash; and R. Hillel Horwitz and his family. The decades of Chabad institutional growth in Riga came to an abrupt and devastating end.

title_en: Rafael Cohen leaves Soviet Russia for Riga
summary_en: In Tishrei 5694, R. Rafael Cohen succeeded in leaving Russia and settled in Riga.
story_body: Cohen had served as rabbi in Osvet, Shchedrin, and Nevel before being forced to flee Nevel after the 5689 arrests. He served as ram in the Tomchei Temimim yeshivos in Vitebsk and Moscow before his emigration. The Rebbe wrote to welcome him to Riga, noting that 'here it is a land where the government does not interfere with the observance of Torah and mitzvos.'

title_en: Rafael Cohen elected rabbi of Riga chassidic community
summary_en: In Adar Sheni 5695, R. Rafael Cohen was elected to serve as rabbi of the chassidic community in Riga.
story_body: On Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Pekudei, R. Faigin had written to the Rashag (Chadakov) conveying the Rebbe's instruction that anash should work and campaign for Cohen's appointment. He was confirmed in the position in Adar Sheni 5695, with Chief Rabbi R. Menachem Mendel Zak requesting his official authorization to perform marriages.

title_en: Rafael Cohen elected rabbi of Nevel
summary_en: In 5682, R. Rafael Cohen was elected rabbi of Nevel, succeeding R. Yechezkel Faivish Neimark.
story_body: After serving in Osvet from his marriage in 5671 and then in Shchedrin following R. Yehuda Leib Esterin's death in Adar 5672, Cohen took the Nevel rabbinate. He served there until forced to flee after the 5689 arrests of Chabad rabbis in Nevel.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrested and exiled to Kostroma
summary_en: In summer 5687 the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested by Soviet authorities and exiled to Kostroma.
story_body: R. Eliyahu Chaim Altheuse accompanied the Rebbe into Kostroma exile, and when the Rebbe later left Russia and settled in Riga, Altheuse left with him. The arrest is referenced as background to Altheuse's lifelong devotion to the Rebbe.

title_en: Rebbe founds Agudas Nashim in Rakshik
summary_en: During Adar 5691, on his visit to Rakshik, the Rebbe founded a women's organization for strengthening taharas hamishpacha.
story_body: A pinkas was opened recording the founding members, with a handwritten introduction and blessing by the Rebbe at its front. The Rebbe wrote that 'every city and settlement where the women establish such an Agudas Nashim - whether by this name or another - whose aim is strengthening taharas hamishpacha, may they, their husbands and offspring be included in the blessing stated here.'

title_en: Rebbe writes to NY Agudas Nashim supporting yeshivos
summary_en: On 13 Nissan 5692 the Rebbe wrote to the New York Agudas Nashim supporting the yeshivos under his leadership.
story_body: The letter shows that beyond the original taharas hamishpacha focus, the women's organizations were taking on additional missions including financial support for Chabad yeshivos. The Rebbe's 5690 visit to America had launched the broader Agudas Nashim initiative.

title_en: Rebbe pushes Faigin on Agudas Nashim expansion
summary_en: On 26 Tammuz 5693 the Rebbe wrote to Faigin urging serious action on establishing Agudas Nashim chapters everywhere possible.
story_body: The Rebbe expressed frustration: 'I already spoke with R. Mordechai Leib about this in Druzgenik - that they needed to establish Agudas Nshei Yisrael in every possible place... But to my regret all proposals for work and action remain only on paper as good intentions. Going forward, with G-d's help, this general matter must be rectified.'

title_en: Booklet 'Kiyum Nefesh M'Yisrael' printed in Riga
summary_en: In 5699 Achos Tmimim Riga received permission to print the Rebbe's letter on saving a Jewish soul as a standalone kuntres.
story_body: The Rebbe noted to his son-in-law on 7 Tevet 5699 that 'the Achos Tmimim institution in Riga requested permission to print the letter that begins 'all who sustain one Jewish soul' - I have surely sent him a copy - and I granted them permission.' The original letter had been addressed to Mr. Elchanan Cohen of New York.

title_en: Final pre-war letter from Rebbe to Chadakov in Riga
summary_en: The Rebbe's last pre-war letter to R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chadakov in Riga was written 17 Menachem Av 5699, one month before World War II broke out.
story_body: The Riga correspondence covered farbrengens of anash, rabbinical appointments, taharas hamishpacha, mikvaos, tefillin campaigns, kosher food for Jewish soldiers, summer camps, education, refugee aid for Ashkenaz refugees in Riga, separation of boys' and girls' schools in Lvov, and plans for an Achos Tmimim monthly journal. War cut short the journal and many other plans.

title_en: Rayatz blesses Hillel Horwitz engagement
summary_en: On 20 Iyar 5700 the Rebbe wrote to R. Yitzchak Matmid Horwitz blessing the engagement of his son Hillel to the daughter of R. Rafael Cohen.
story_body: In the same letter the Rebbe addressed efforts to secure Hillel a rabbinical position in Livenhof. The Rebbe also wrote on the same date to Achos Tmimim Dvinsk acknowledging their first farbrengen and to R. Mordechai Chefetz about their Pesach gatherings.

title_en: Rebbe writes Achos Tmimim regulations and program
summary_en: On 17 Adar Sheni 5700 the Rebbe wrote to Achos Tmimim Riga regarding regulations and the order of their work and lectures.
story_body: Following his earlier instruction to formalize Riga as the central body for Latvia, the Rebbe sent detailed guidance on operating procedures. He also inquired in this letter whether Riga had received his earlier letter about Dvinsk and what had been done there.

title_en: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz settles in Warsaw after Moscow expulsion
summary_en: Following the 1891-1893 expulsion of Jews from Moscow, Chabad chassid R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz relocated to Warsaw.
story_body: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, son-in-law of R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, had originally lived in Dokshitz and then Moscow. When the Tsarist government expelled the Jews of Moscow in 5652-5653 (1892-1893), he resettled in Warsaw, becoming one of the earliest Chabad chassidim to establish himself there. He would later head Chabad activity in the city until his death.

title_en: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov arrives in Lubavitch to study
summary_en: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov of Lazovich arrived in Lubavitch in 5655 to learn as one of the 'yoshvim' before Tomchei Tmimim was founded.
story_body: Born in Lazovich near Klimovich, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov came to Lubavitch in 5655 to study. Tomchei Tmimim had not yet been founded, so he learned for two to three years among the 'yoshvim' under the mashpia R. Chanoch Hendel Kugel. He later married into the Horowitz family and settled in Warsaw.

title_en: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov marries and settles in Warsaw
summary_en: Around 5657, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov married Tzirla, daughter of R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, and joined his father-in-law in Warsaw.
story_body: After studying for several years in Lubavitch, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov married Tzirla, daughter of R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, around 5657. The couple settled with the bride's father in Warsaw, where R. Shraga Feivish would later become one of the central leaders of the Chabad community.

title_en: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen settles in Warsaw
summary_en: Around 5660, the chassid R. Baruch Shalom Cohen settled in Warsaw, joining the small but growing Chabad community there.
story_body: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen took up residence in Warsaw around the year 5660 (~1900). He remained there until 5672, when he relocated to nearby Volomin to open a branch of Tomchei Tmimim.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab rebukes Warsaw chassidim over splitting the minyan
summary_en: On 13 Tevet 5663, the Rebbe Rashab wrote to R. Yosef Yozik objecting to his founding a separate Chabad minyan in Warsaw.
story_body: When R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz established a second Chabad minyan in Warsaw apart from the existing one, the Rebbe Rashab disapproved. On 13 Tevet 5663 he wrote to him, expressing how heavily the split weighed on him because he sensed it would lead to division of hearts and machloket. The two minyanim would later become the well-known shuls at Franciscan 30 and Dzika 8.

title_en: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen moves to Volomin and opens Tomchei Tmimim branch
summary_en: In 5672, R. Baruch Shalom Cohen relocated from Warsaw to nearby Volomin, where he opened a branch of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: After living in Warsaw for over a decade, R. Baruch Shalom Cohen moved to the nearby town of Volomin in 5672 (1912). There he founded a branch of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim, extending the yeshiva network beyond Lubavitch itself into the Polish-Russian border region.

title_en: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz passes away in Warsaw
summary_en: At the start of 5675, R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, one of the earliest Chabad settlers in Warsaw, passed away.
story_body: R. Yosef Yozik Horowitz, who had built up Chabad life in Warsaw from the 1890s onward, died at the start of 5675 (autumn 1914). Leadership of the Warsaw Chabad community then passed to his son-in-law R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, his brother-in-law R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, and his nephew R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin.

title_en: R. Baruch Shalom Cohen returns to Russia during WWI
summary_en: In the winter of 5675, during World War I, R. Baruch Shalom Cohen left the Warsaw region and resettled in Moscow.
story_body: When the First World War swept through the Russian-Polish frontier in winter 5675 (1914-15), R. Baruch Shalom Cohen left Volomin and returned eastward into Russia, settling in Moscow. His departure marked the wartime disruption of the Volomin Tomchei Tmimim branch.

title_en: Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim founded in Warsaw
summary_en: In 5681, Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Warsaw under the leadership of R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin.
story_body: Building on the established Chabad community of Warsaw, Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim was founded there in 5681 (1921). At its head stood the three central Warsaw Chabad leaders: R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin. The yeshiva became a major hub of Chabad education in interwar Poland.

title_en: R. Natan Gurary passes away in Rostov
summary_en: In 5682, the chassid R. Natan Gurary passed away in Rostov, leaving his widow Esther and sons Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch and Shneur Zalman.
story_body: R. Natan Gurary died in Rostov in 5682 (1922). Three years later, his widow Esther and sons would leave Soviet Russia, with his elder son Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch eventually settling in Warsaw and becoming one of the leaders of Polish Chabad.

title_en: R. Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch Gurary settles in Warsaw
summary_en: In 5685, R. Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch Gurary left Soviet Russia with his mother and brother and settled in Warsaw, joining the Chabad yeshiva leadership.
story_body: R. Yechiel Tzvi Hirsch Gurary, son of R. Natan Gurary and son-in-law of the Radzyn Rebbe R. Mordechai Yosef Eliezer Leiner, left Soviet Russia in 5685 (1925). Together with his mother Esther and his younger brother Shneur Zalman, he settled in Warsaw. Immediately upon arrival he was appointed to the management board of the yeshiva, joining R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin at the head of Warsaw Chabad.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrested by Soviet authorities
summary_en: In the summer of 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested by Soviet authorities and sentenced to exile.
story_body: In summer 5687 (1927), the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested by the Soviet regime. He was sentenced to exile in 'eretz gezeira' before being released on 12 Tamuz. The arrest and subsequent release set in motion his emigration from Russia later that year.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz redeemed on 12 Tamuz
summary_en: On 12 Tamuz 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was redeemed from Soviet imprisonment and exile.
story_body: After his arrest in the summer of 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was released on 12 Tamuz (July 12, 1927). The day was thereafter commemorated as a Chabad chag ha-geulah. The circumstances forced him to leave Russia, and he settled in Riga shortly afterward.

title_en: Warsaw chassidim invite Rebbe Rayatz to settle in Poland
summary_en: On 27 Tishrei 5688, the leaders of Warsaw Chabad wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz urging him to make Poland or Polish-Lithuania his home.
story_body: After the Rebbe Rayatz left Soviet Russia and settled in Riga, the heads of Warsaw Chabad — R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, and R. Yechiel Tzvi Gurary — wrote on 27 Tishrei 5688 inviting him to relocate to Poland or the Polish-ruled parts of Lithuania. They argued that the bulk of anash and the Tomchei Tmimim students were now concentrated in Poland, and that travel from Riga was very difficult. The Rebbe declined the move but agreed to make a visit.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Warsaw for his first visit
summary_en: On erev Rosh Chodesh Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Warsaw from Riga for his first major visit to Polish anash.
story_body: Leaving Riga on Sunday morning 28 Shvat 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Warsaw via Dvinsk, the border stations, and Vilna, where chassidim greeted him at each stop. He reached Warsaw on the morning of erev Rosh Chodesh Adar (Feb 20, 1928), lodging in the home of R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov. Over the following weeks he received thousands of visitors, met with rabbanim and admorim, said maamarim, and traveled briefly to Otwock to visit R. Moshe Hornstein.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Otwock on Shushan Purim
summary_en: On Shushan Purim 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled from Warsaw to Otwock to visit his uncle R. Moshe Hornstein.
story_body: During his first Warsaw visit, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled on Shushan Purim 5688 (March 7, 1928) to Otwock, the home of his uncle R. Moshe Hornstein, son-in-law of the Rebbe Maharash. Anash and select Tomchei Tmimim students joined him in Otwock for Shabbat Parshat Ki Tisa before he returned to Warsaw for further yechidut sessions.

title_en: Wedding of Rayatz's daughter Chaya Mushka in Warsaw
summary_en: On 14 Kislev 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz's daughter married the future Rebbe in Warsaw, marking his second visit to the city.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz's second visit to Warsaw took place on 14 Kislev 5689 (November 27, 1928), for the wedding of his daughter to his son-in-law, the future Lubavitcher Rebbe. After the wedding, on the fourth night of Chanukah, the Rayatz wrote a public letter of thanks to all of Polish anash and the temimim for their efforts on behalf of the wedding arrangements.

title_en: R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin passes away in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: On 12 Adar 5689, the chassid R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, a leader of Warsaw Chabad who had moved to Eretz Yisrael, passed away.
story_body: R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin had relocated from Warsaw to Eretz Yisrael, returning periodically to visit Warsaw. He died on 12 Adar 5689 (Feb 22, 1929) and was buried on the Mount of Olives. On 29 Adar Sheni the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a letter of condolence to his sons and sons-in-law.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz's third visit to Warsaw
summary_en: On 9 Tamuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to visit the three Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot in Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz.
story_body: On 9 Tamuz 5691 (June 24, 1931), the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga on his third trip to Warsaw, this time to inspect the three Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot under his leadership in Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz. He summarized the journey in a letter dated 5 Menachem Av of that year.

title_en: R. Yehuda Eber appointed rosh yeshiva in Warsaw
summary_en: At the start of 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yehuda Eber to head the Warsaw yeshiva and organize Tanya shiurim across the city.
story_body: Early in 5692 (autumn 1931) the Rebbe Rayatz appointed R. Yehuda Eber rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. Together with the position came the assignment to organize Tanya classes in batei midrash across the city, a task R. Yehuda delegated in part to a young avreich named Moshe Chaim.

title_en: Chassidus distribution campaign launched in Warsaw
summary_en: Beginning in 5692, the Warsaw yeshiva ran a campaign of Tanya shiurim and maamar deliveries in shtieblach and yeshivot across the city.
story_body: Under R. Yehuda Eber's direction in 5692, a young avreich named Moshe Chaim was sent into Warsaw shuls and yeshivot to teach Tanya and disseminate Chassidus. He established daily Tanya classes in the Bagne beis midrash (forty students), the Sochaczow Beis Avraham yeshiva (thirty boys for five zlotys a week), and the Franciscan 22 Chabad shul (four Ger chassidim). He also began saying maamarim every Shabbat in the Dzika shul.

title_en: Mechina founded at Dzika 8 shul
summary_en: In 5692, the 'Mechina' preparatory program was established in the Agudas Chabad shul on Dzika 8 in Warsaw.
story_body: The Agudas Chabad shul on Dzika 8 (possibly also called Zamenhof 8) served the younger Chabad chassidim of Warsaw. In 5692 (1932) it became home to the newly founded Mechina, a preparatory program feeding into the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz makes brief stop in Warsaw en route from Ludomir
summary_en: On 28 Menachem Av 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz stopped in Warsaw on his way home from Ludomir to Riga.
story_body: On Tuesday 28 Menachem Av 5692 (August 31, 1932), the Rebbe Rayatz made a brief stop in Warsaw while traveling from Ludomir back to his home in Riga. It was one of two short visits to Warsaw in the years immediately preceding his 5693 relocation there.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz stops in Warsaw en route to Marienbad
summary_en: On 12 Tamuz 5693, the Rebbe Rayatz stopped in Warsaw for two days while traveling from Riga to Marienbad.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz left Riga on 10 Tamuz 5693 and arrived in Warsaw on 12 Tamuz (July 6, 1933) for a two-day stop that included a visit to the yeshiva. He continued onward to Marienbad on 13 Tamuz. This was the last of his short visits before relocating to Warsaw permanently later that year.

title_en: Mechina relocates to Murnowska 32
summary_en: In 5696, the Mechina moved into the Chabad shul built by R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin at Murnowska 32 in Warsaw.
story_body: Over the years, R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin had acquired a courtyard and building at Murnowska 32 in Warsaw, dedicating part of it as a Chabad shul. In 5696 (1936) the Mechina relocated there from Dzika 8. The same address would later host the Rebbe Rayatz himself during the first days of WWII.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz flees Otwock for Warsaw as WWII begins
summary_en: In late Elul 5699, as the war began, the Rebbe Rayatz left Otwock for Warsaw, taking refuge in the Shmotkin home at Murnowska 32.
story_body: At the outbreak of World War II in late Elul 5699 (early September 1939), the Rebbe Rayatz left his home in Otwock and traveled to Warsaw, where he stayed in R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin's house at Murnowska 32. During the German bombing of Warsaw, the building was hit and burned, destroying the Rebbe's clothing and belongings, and he relocated to the home of R. Yechiel Tzvi Gurary.

title_en: Town of Otwock founded by Jewish settlers
summary_en: The resort town of Otwock, about thirty kilometers from Warsaw, was founded around 1890 by wealthy Jews on a tract of forest land they had purchased.
story_body: Otwock developed rapidly into a large town with a population that was roughly half Jewish. Its clean air and proximity to Warsaw later made it the chosen residence of the Frierdiker Rebbe and the new home of Tomchei Tmimim in 1935. The town's character as a Jewish resort and sanatorium center shaped its role in Chabad history.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva in Rostov closed by Soviet authorities
summary_en: In late winter 1921, Soviet authorities shut down Tomchei Tmimim in Rostov, arrested its leaders, expelled students, and confiscated the Rebbe's property.
story_body: The closure marked the beginning of the underground period for the Tomchei Tmimim network across Russia. At the very same moment that the Russian network was being driven underground, a new branch was being founded in Warsaw, Poland, beginning what would become the central Tomchei Tmimim of the interwar period.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva founded in Warsaw
summary_en: On 2 Nissan 5681, the first yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rashab, Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Warsaw with twelve students drawn from local Chabad chassidim.
story_body: The founders included R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin. The yeshiva opened at the Lubavitch beis midrash at Franciszkańska 30 after Pesach, with R. Baruch Friedman of Russia soon appointed as mashpia. The founding effectively transferred the center of the Tomchei Tmimim network from Soviet Russia to Poland.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe writes celebratory letter to Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: On 11 Tammuz 5681, the Rebbe Rayatz, then still in Rostov, wrote an exuberant letter to the students of the newly founded Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Word of the Warsaw founding had reached the Rebbe only at the beginning of Tammuz, smuggled across the closed Soviet border by special messenger. He spent days speaking of his joy and called the students his sons, praying that the yeshiva would grow and spread its light. The next day he wrote a follow-up letter to R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz sends detailed organizational instructions for Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: In the days after learning of the Warsaw founding, the Rebbe sent two detailed letters laying out the name, structure, leadership committee, admissions, and daily schedule of the new yeshiva.
story_body: The Rebbe instructed that the institution be called 'Merkezet Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in Warsaw' and named R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin, R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, and R. Shneur Zalman Shmotkin as the core of a five-member governing committee. The letters specified standards of yiras shamayim, character development, and daily conduct expected of the Tmimim.

title_en: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld appointed rav at Tachkemoni in Warsaw
summary_en: In 5683, R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld, a co-founder of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim, was appointed as a rav at the Mizrachi rabbinical seminary Tachkemoni.
story_body: Blumenfeld's family had been expelled from Poland to Russia during World War I, where they encountered Chabad and became sympathizers. After returning to Warsaw he helped establish Tomchei Tmimim and gave shiurim there in Maseches Shabbos before his Tachkemoni appointment.

title_en: Anash request the Rebbe relocate from Riga to Poland
summary_en: In the winter of 5688, chassidim in Poland and Lithuania formally asked the Rebbe to move his residence from Riga to their region, a request the Rebbe declined.
story_body: The Rebbe responded that while their reasons were sound, various weighty considerations made the move impossible at that time. The request would be renewed repeatedly over the following years until the Rebbe finally agreed to move in 1933.

title_en: Rebbe arrives in Berlin returning from US trip
summary_en: On 1 Menachem Av 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived safely in Berlin on his way back to Riga from his extended trip to the United States.
story_body: R. Shmuel Zalmanov reported the arrival to R. Azriel Zelig Slonim, noting that the chassidim were again preparing a formal letter asking the Rebbe to settle in Poland rather than Riga and were hoping he would spend the upcoming High Holidays there.

title_en: Rebbe declines to come to Warsaw before holiday
summary_en: On 28 Menachem Av 5690, the Rebbe wrote to his son-in-law (the future Rebbe) that he could not come to Warsaw before the upcoming Yom Tov.
story_body: A second letter on Motzaei Shabbos Re'eh confirmed the same answer to the Warsaw chassidim. Despite repeated invitations and arguments that Riga was not suitable, the Rebbe judged that the timing for relocation had not yet come.

title_en: Meeting of Anash leaders from Poland, Lithuania and Latvia at Rashag's home
summary_en: On Motzaei Shabbos Vayelech, 5 Tishrei 5691, prominent chassidim from Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia gathered at the home of the Rashag in Riga to discuss founding an Agudat Chassidim.
story_body: The future Rebbe (Ramash) participated in the meeting. The participants resolved to establish a permanent inter-country committee to support the Rebbe's beis chayeinu, to form an Agudat Chassidim across European countries, and formally to ask the Rebbe to settle in Poland. The minutes were later printed in a 2005 tshura by the Stambler family.

title_en: Polish, Lithuanian and Latvian Anash send unified letter pleading Rebbe stay
summary_en: On 6 Tishrei 5691 the assembled chassidim wrote a formal letter to the Rebbe begging him not to leave them for America and to settle in Poland.
story_body: The letter, signed by Anash representatives from Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, and even Russia, had been triggered by rumors that American chassidim were lobbying for the Rebbe's move to the United States. The signatories committed to make all needed preparations to receive him.

title_en: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld publishes Kol HaMitzvah
summary_en: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld, a founder of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim, printed his sefer Kol HaMitzvah in Warsaw in 5691.
story_body: Blumenfeld had been born in 5653 (1893). He combined his role as a Mizrachi rav at Tachkemoni with continued support for Chabad institutions in Warsaw. He would later be murdered in the Warsaw Ghetto on Yom Kippur 5703.

title_en: Visa effort to bring Rebbe's family to Poland
summary_en: On 13 Nissan 5691, R. Shmuel Zalmanov reported that Polish Anash were actively working to obtain visas for the Rebbe's family.
story_body: Although no firm decision had yet been made about the move, the chassidim believed that once visas were secured the Rebbe would accept their request. The letter was sent to R. Azriel Zelig Slonim in Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: Plan to move Rebbe to Poland temporarily shelved
summary_en: On 19 Iyar 5691, R. Shmuel Zalmanov wrote that the relocation plan had been deferred and the Rebbe would likely remain in Riga for an extended time.
story_body: The letter also noted that the Rebbe was considering founding a Tomchei Tmimim branch in Riga itself, to which a group of senior students would be sent. This Riga plan would also fail to materialize, clearing the way for the eventual move to Otwock.

title_en: Secretary announces Rebbe will move to Otwock
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5691, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote that it was nearly certain the Rebbe would relocate entirely to Poland and settle in Otwock.
story_body: Feigin expected the move to occur in mid-Elul. While the full relocation would be delayed by two years due to apartment difficulties, the Rebbe did spend Tishrei 5692 in Otwock as a first trial of the new residence.

title_en: Rebbe agrees in writing to come to Poland for Elul
summary_en: On 3 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe wrote to the Warsaw vaad formally agreeing to come to Poland during the upcoming month of Elul.
story_body: The Rebbe noted that the exact date could not yet be fixed and that he would notify them in two to three weeks. The letter resolved months of correspondence and set in motion the first Tishrei stay in Otwock.

title_en: Anash informed Rebbe will spend High Holidays in Poland
summary_en: On 7 Menachem Av 5691 R. Shmuel Zalmanov shared the good news that the Rebbe had agreed to come to Poland for the upcoming Yamim Noraim.
story_body: Zalmanov expressed hope that the visit would lead to a permanent move. The letter was part of the continuing correspondence with R. Slonim documenting the campaign to bring the Rebbe to Poland.

title_en: Rebbe travels alone to Warsaw before Rosh Hashanah
