summary_en: On 20 Elul 5691, secretary Feigin reported that the Rebbe would travel to Warsaw the next day, alone, because no apartment was yet available for the family.
story_body: The Rebbe spent Rosh Hashanah and the entire month of Tishrei in Otwock. He returned to Riga around 10 Cheshvan after concluding that a suitable apartment could not yet be secured, and stayed in Riga for two more years before the relocation was completed.

title_en: Rebbe returns from Otwock to Riga
summary_en: Around 10 Cheshvan 5692 the Rebbe returned from his first extended stay in Otwock back to Riga.
story_body: Although the Rebbe had publicly indicated his decision to settle in Poland, no suitable apartment could be found in the tight Warsaw housing market. He returned to Riga 'for a few months' that turned into two more years.

title_en: Rebbe travels to Druskininkai for leg treatment
summary_en: During the summer of 5692 the Rebbe stayed in the spa town of Druskininkai to treat the recurrence of his leg ailment.
story_body: From Druskininkai he traveled briefly to visit Anash in Ludmir, Volhynia, and returned to Riga via stops in Warsaw and Vilna. The health challenges that summer foreshadowed a more severe medical crisis the following winter.

title_en: Rebbe travels to Berlin for medical treatment
summary_en: In the winter of 5693, after his condition worsened and his voice weakened, the Rebbe traveled to Berlin to consult the leading specialists, including Professor Loewy.
story_body: The Berlin doctors concluded they could not identify the underlying illness and that the Rebbe required ongoing expert supervision. From Berlin the Rebbe continued to Paris for further consultations before returning to Riga in late Adar.

title_en: Rebbe returns to Riga from Paris
summary_en: On 23 Adar 5693 the Rebbe returned to Riga after his medical consultations in Berlin and Paris.
story_body: Despite treatments through the spring and summer, his health did not noticeably improve. The doctors insisted he travel to a spa, and that summer he went to Marienbad for therapy.

title_en: Rebbe receives Latvian citizenship clearing way for Polish move
summary_en: On 26 Sivan 5693 the Rebbe wrote that the Latvian citizenship he had been waiting for had finally been granted, enabling him to proceed with the relocation to Poland.
story_body: The Rebbe explained to his daughter that he had nearly decided in favor of the move the previous summer in Druskininkai, but had waited several months for citizenship to simplify his future Polish residency. With citizenship now in hand, he expected to carry out the move successfully.

title_en: Rebbe departs Riga for Marienbad via Warsaw
summary_en: On 10 Tammuz 5693 the Rebbe left Riga, visiting the Warsaw yeshiva on 12 Tammuz and arriving in Marienbad on 13 Tammuz for spa treatment.
story_body: Doctors had warned of severe consequences if the Rebbe did not travel to a spa. He had nonetheless delivered Chassidus on Shavuos against medical advice, with no apparent ill effects. During the stop in Warsaw he gave the Warsaw vaad their first private notice of his decision to settle in the city.

title_en: Rebbe begins apartment search for Warsaw move
summary_en: On 22 Tammuz 5693, writing from Marienbad to R. Y. Y. Gourary, the Rebbe directed the start of organized preparations for moving his household to Warsaw.
story_body: The Rebbe instructed that the practical apartment search should be deferred until mid-Av while financial and organizational arrangements were settled first. From Marienbad over the next several weeks the Rebbe coordinated by detailed correspondence all the logistics of the relocation.

title_en: Rebbe arrives in Warsaw to settle permanently
summary_en: On 1 Elul 5693 the Rebbe arrived directly from Marienbad in Warsaw, beginning his residence in Poland.
story_body: He had written on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul that he was leaving for Warsaw that day. Upon arrival he reported that the trip went well and that several apartment options were under discussion. The struggle to find a suitable apartment would dominate the next month.

title_en: Warsaw apartment search proves difficult
summary_en: On 9 Elul 5693 the Rebbe wrote that he had been alternating between Warsaw and Otwock searching for an apartment, with rental terms heavy and no final agreement reached.
story_body: He had been staying at the Wiederszal pension in Otwock during the search. By 20 Elul a suitable apartment in Warsaw had been arranged and renovations begun. The Rebbe's family arrived in Warsaw on 21 Elul, but the renovations were not yet complete.

title_en: Ludmir Anash write joyful letter on Rebbe's settling in Warsaw
summary_en: On 12 Elul 5693, leaders of the Anash community in Ludmir, Volhynia, sent a letter expressing their joy at the Rebbe's relocation to Warsaw.
story_body: The signatories described how the spark of Chabad chassidus had burned only privately and in limited measure since the war years, and they now hoped that the Rebbe's nearness would rekindle it into a great fire. The letter was signed by twenty community members and concluded with New Year blessings.

title_en: Rebbe enters new Warsaw apartment
summary_en: On 8 Tishrei 5694 the Rebbe and his family moved into their new apartment in Warsaw.
story_body: Writing the next day on Erev Yom Kippur, the Rebbe noted with symbolic emphasis that the move had taken place in 'the seventh month, sated with joys, on the eighth day, oily with every good.' The household had spent Rosh Hashanah at the yeshiva while renovations were finished.

title_en: Rebbe decides to spend summer in Warsaw suburbs
summary_en: On 3 Sivan 5695 the Rebbe wrote that for several important reasons he could not travel abroad that summer and would rent a residence in the resort area around Warsaw.
story_body: This decision laid the groundwork for the Rebbe's extended summer stay in Otwock that year, which evolved into a permanent move of his household and the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim to Otwock by year's end.

title_en: Twelfth of Tammuz celebrated at Rebbe's residence in Otwock
summary_en: On 12 Tammuz 5695, the Rebbe's chag ha'geulah was celebrated with great honor in Otwock, where the Rebbe was then staying.
story_body: Many chassidim and Tmimim came from Warsaw and the surrounding towns. The Rebbe delivered numerous sichos and inyanim. By late summer it had been decided that both the Rebbe and the yeshiva would relocate permanently to Otwock.

title_en: Rebbe and Tomchei Tmimim relocate from Warsaw to Otwock
summary_en: In the summer of 5695 it was decided that the Rebbe Rayatz and the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva would move together from Warsaw to Otwock.
story_body: Otwock's clean air suited the Rebbe's health, and the resort town also proved a better setting for the yeshiva than Warsaw. The move fulfilled a plan the Rebbe had already harbored in 5691 but which had been deferred. Otwock would remain the seat of the court and the yeshiva until the outbreak of World War II.

title_en: Survey of Tomchei Tmimim history published in HaTamim
summary_en: In Tammuz 5697 the seventh issue of HaTamim journal published a general survey of the development of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
story_body: The survey recorded the 1921 transfer of the yeshiva to Poland on the yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rashab. HaTamim was the central scholarly journal of the Lubavitch yeshiva network during the interwar period.

title_en: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld murdered in Warsaw Ghetto
summary_en: R. Yechiel Meir Blumenfeld, a founding figure of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim and Tachkemoni rav, was murdered in the Warsaw Ghetto on Yom Kippur 5703.
story_body: Born in 1893, Blumenfeld had returned to Warsaw after wartime exile in Russia and helped establish Tomchei Tmimim there, while serving as a Mizrachi rav at Tachkemoni and publishing his sefer Kol HaMitzvah. His death on Yom Kippur 1942 was part of the Nazi destruction of the Warsaw Jewish community.

title_en: R' Yosef Goldstein joins Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at age 14
summary_en: In summer 5682, 14-year-old Yosef Goldstein was admitted to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw through a workaround, since he was considered too young.
story_body: Goldstein had been studying at Yeshivat Toras Chaim when he and several other boys decided to transfer to Chabad. Because he was only 14 the yeshiva refused him at first, so he arranged private study with R' Avraham Ziskind and R' Moshe Yehuda Reichman until he was gradually absorbed into the yeshiva. Shmuel Zalmanov served as his mentor; the total enrollment at that point was 15 students.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz announces opening of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
summary_en: On 8 Shevat 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote, via his secretary Elchanan Dober Marozov, announcing that a branch of Tomchei Tmimim had opened in Warsaw with about 25 talented students.
story_body: The letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5136) explained that the Warsaw branch had been founded on the suggestion of the Rebbe's son-in-law. R' Alter Simchowitz, who had previously directed the Shchedrin branch, was being dispatched to run it. The opening marked the formal re-establishment of Lubavitch yeshiva infrastructure outside Soviet Russia.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz comes to Lubavitch to study
summary_en: In Cheshvan 5665 R' Chaim Alter Nisan Shimon Simchowitz arrived in Lubavitch to study at Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Born in Pochep around 5650, Simchowitz had first studied at the yeshiva of R' Tzvi Netta Gnessin in Pochep, whose graduates often progressed to Tomchei Tmimim. After arriving in Lubavitch he spent time in the preparatory program in Horodisht before joining the main yeshiva hall.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz sent to found Yeshivat Toras Emet in Hebron
summary_en: At the beginning of 5672, R' Alter Simchowitz was chosen as one of seven students sent by the Rebbe Rashab to establish Yeshivat Toras Emet in Hebron.
story_body: The Rashab dispatched seven Tomchei Tmimim students to the Holy Land to seed a Chabad yeshiva in Hebron. Simchowitz returned to Lubavitch at the end of that same year and continued studying there until 5680, serving as a chozer who transmitted the maamarim of the Rashab.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz marries Rivka Havlin in Lubavitch
summary_en: In Shevat 5675 R' Alter Simchowitz married Rivka, daughter of the mashpia R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin, in Lubavitch.
story_body: Havlin was the director of Yeshivat Toras Emet in Hebron and later in Jerusalem. The marriage cemented a tie between two influential Chabad educational figures of the era.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz sent to direct Tomchei Tmimim branch in Shchedrin
summary_en: In the summer of 5680 the Rebbe Rashab sent R' Alter Simchowitz to direct the Shchedrin branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: The Rashab arranged for Simchowitz to travel from Lubavitch to Shchedrin with full instructions and orientation. The branch operated until 5678 when the yeshiva and its branches were relocated to Kremenchug, after which Simchowitz served there as supervisor of chassidus studies.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim central yeshiva relocates from Kremenchug to Rostov
summary_en: In the winter of 5681 the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva moved to Rostov, where R' Alter Simchowitz was appointed mashpia.
story_body: The yeshiva had previously been headquartered in Kremenchug. The Rostov tenure was short-lived, as Soviet authorities forced the yeshiva to close that same year, prompting the Rebbe to redirect his educational resources to Warsaw.

title_en: Soviet authorities close Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Rostov
summary_en: In 5681 the Soviet authorities forced the closure of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Rostov.
story_body: With the central yeshiva shut down by Soviet authorities, the Rebbe Rayatz opened a new branch of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and dispatched R' Alter Simchowitz from Russia to direct its spiritual program. This effectively shifted the institutional center of gravity for Lubavitch yeshiva education out of Russia.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to father-in-law about R' Alter's mission
summary_en: On 19 Cheshvan 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin reporting that his son-in-law R' Alter was still in Minsk on his way to Warsaw.
story_body: The letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 95) reported that Alter remained in Minsk after Sukkot but was likely to travel on to R' Shraga Feivish, since the Warsaw founders had pleaded for an experienced mashpia and supervisor. The correspondence shows the Rebbe coordinating an international transfer of personnel under difficult conditions.

title_en: Rebbe writes to Minsk arranging funds for R' Alter's journey
summary_en: On 5 Kislev 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote authorizing up to two million in funds for R' Alter Simchowitz in Minsk and laying out the logistics of his move to Warsaw.
story_body: The Rebbe instructed that Alter would first need to be issued a rabbinic certification by a Warsaw synagogue, which would help him secure travel papers. He would travel alone immediately and have his family follow about a month later; the Rebbe stressed that 'the time is precious.'

title_en: Rebbe writes to Warsaw Chabad leaders about R' Alter's arrival
summary_en: On 6 Kislev 5682 the Rebbe wrote to several Warsaw chassidim including R' Feivush Zalmanov, R' Bezpalov and R' Yehuda Leib Raskin promising central support once R' Alter arrived.
story_body: The Rebbe assured them that once Alter Simchowitz reached Warsaw and the yeshiva's affairs were organized, central Chabad would provide a subsidy for the yeshiva's operating expenses.

title_en: Rebbe urges R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin to expedite R' Alter's arrival
summary_en: On 7 Kislev 5682 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin in Warsaw urging that R' Alter from Pochep arrive as quickly as possible.
story_body: Shmotkin was directing the founding of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, and the Rebbe pressed him to do whatever was needed to bring Alter in without delay. The exchange documents how closely the Rebbe was managing both finances and personnel during the relocation.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz reaches Warsaw after losing foot crossing border
summary_en: Before Pesach 5682, R' Alter Simchowitz finally arrived in Warsaw after his foot was amputated in a Vilna hospital following a frostbitten illegal border crossing.
story_body: On his way from Russia to Poland, Simchowitz had smuggled himself across the border on foot through a forest, where the severe cold caused his foot to freeze. He was taken to a Vilna hospital where the foot was amputated, and only then continued to Warsaw, arriving just before Pesach to take up his post as mashpia.

title_en: Warsaw students meet R' Alter at Acharon shel Pesach farbrengen
summary_en: On Acharon shel Pesach 5682 the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim students first met R' Alter Simchowitz at a kiddush and farbrengen that ran into the following day.
story_body: The gathering, hosted at the home of R' Zalman Shmotkin, continued nonstop into the next day, and Alter delivered the maamar 'V'henif yado al hanahar.' With his arrival the yeshiva's level of study in nigleh and chassidus rose markedly and an elevated atmosphere took hold among the students.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw moves to Franciszkanska 8
summary_en: In 5683 Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, having grown to around 100 students, relocated from Franciszkanska 30 to a more spacious building at Franciszkanska 8.
story_body: The new site, a beit midrash of the Strikov chassidim, had two large halls plus a kitchen, dining area and dormitory rooms; a Jewish neighbor across the way cooked for the yeshiva. The yeshiva remained there through 5685, moving to Mlawska 7 in 5686.

title_en: R' Avraham Shimon Engel of Zelichov appointed rosh yeshiva in Warsaw
summary_en: In 5683 R' Avraham Shimon Engel-Horowitz of Zelichov was appointed rosh yeshiva at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw with the Rebbe Rayatz's approval.
story_body: Engel was renowned for encyclopedic mastery of Talmud and skill in explaining Rishonim; his opening shiur in Bava Metzia reportedly analyzed twenty-eight different Rishonic approaches. He had previously taught in yeshivot in Tzanz, Krakow, Krzanov and Stolin before joining Tomchei Tmimim. R' Shmuel Zalmanov reported to the Rebbe both his brilliance and his weakness in giving over the deeper analytical reasoning that students needed.

title_en: R' Avraham Naftali Hirtzka Goldberg joins as ram in Warsaw
summary_en: In winter 5683 R' Avraham Naftali Hirtzka Goldberg was hired as an additional ram at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw to teach the class below R' Shimon's.
story_body: Known as 'der Klobutzker' for the small town near Lodz where he grew up and studied, Goldberg later lived in Wielun before being brought to Warsaw. He was a classic Polish lamdan who loved pilpul; R' Shmuel Zalmanov reported to the Rebbe that his style was not quite the Chabad approach but that students were inspired by the vitality of his teaching.

title_en: Rebbe instructs R' Alter to train students to speak chassidus publicly
summary_en: On 15 Iyar 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Alter Simchowitz directing him to select short maamarim and train Warsaw students to deliver them publicly.
story_body: The Rebbe wrote that even shy students must be pushed to overcome their reluctance to speak, since training them this way would yield great benefit over time. He closed with strong encouragement, invoking his late father's spirit and reminding Alter that the work of spreading Torah is done 'not by might and not by power, but by knowing Him.'

title_en: Rebbe writes again to R' Alter pressing for expansion and student development
summary_en: At the end of Sivan 5683 the Rebbe again wrote to R' Alter, complaining of poor reporting and urging that students give chassidus publicly and that the institution be expanded.
story_body: The Rebbe noted he had received no updates since his Iyar letter and reiterated that students must repeat chassidus in public. He told Alter and the staff that the duty of rebuilding Tomchei Tmimim 'as it once was' rested on them, promising that a portion of the donations from overseas chassidim would be allocated to Warsaw's needs.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz urges Shmotkin to find a full-time fundraiser for Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: At the end of Shevat 5684 the Rebbe wrote to R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin urging him to find a dedicated administrator to grow the Warsaw yeshiva.
story_body: The Rebbe (Igrot Kodesh vol. 1, letter 179) offered generous percentage compensation to anyone who would take on Warsaw's fundraising and growth as a full-time mission, arguing the institution could easily be five or six times larger than its current state. He warned that 'a thing that stands in place is truly going down.'

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz leaves Warsaw to return to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: At the start of 5685, R' Alter Simchowitz was compelled to leave Warsaw to serve as mashpia at Yeshivat Toras Emet in Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: After roughly three years directing Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw's spiritual life, Simchowitz returned to Eretz Yisrael at the Rebbe's direction to take a mashpia role at Toras Emet. He would later be briefly recalled to Warsaw in 5689 before returning again to Jerusalem permanently.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz reappointed chief mashpia of Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: Before Tishrei 5689 R' Alter Simchowitz visited the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga and was appointed chief mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.
story_body: The reappointment was short-lived: within a few months Simchowitz had to return again to Eretz Yisrael, where he resumed serving as mashpia at Yeshivat Toras Emet and as mashpia of Anash in Jerusalem.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz passes away in Jerusalem
summary_en: On 7 Nissan 5699 R' Alter Simchowitz passed away in Jerusalem after years of service as mashpia at Yeshivat Toras Emet and for Anash in the city.
story_body: Simchowitz had been appointed by the Rebbe Rayatz to those roles after his final return from Warsaw. His career, traced in detail in Toldot Chabad b'Eretz HaKodesh, spanned founding roles in Hebron, Shchedrin, Kremenchug, Rostov, Warsaw and Jerusalem.

title_en: R' Shimon Engel of Zelichov born
summary_en: R' Avraham Shimon Engel-Horowitz was born in 5636 in the town of Zelichov.
story_body: After marriage he initially preferred to earn his living by selling vinegar rather than accept rabbinic positions, only consenting to teach after losing his money. He went on to teach in Tzanz, Krzanov, Stolin and ultimately Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.

title_en: R' Shimon Zelichover joins Yeshivat Chochmei Lublin as spiritual supervisor
summary_en: In the spring of 5692 R' Shimon Zelichover was accepted as spiritual supervisor at Yeshivat Chochmei Lublin.
story_body: Engel had taught the senior shiur at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at least through the end of 5687 before being recruited by R' Meir Shapiro for Chochmei Lublin. He remained in Lublin until shortly after Shapiro's passing.

title_en: R' Shimon Zelichover leaves Lublin for Krakow
summary_en: In 5694, following the death of R' Meir Shapiro, R' Shimon Zelichover left Lublin and settled in Krakow.
story_body: In Krakow he continued to teach select students. He remained there until 5703, when he was deported by the Nazis.

title_en: R' Avraham Naftali Goldberg publishes Maaseh Zayit
summary_en: In 5693 R' Avraham Naftali Hirtzka Goldberg published Maaseh Zayit, chiddushim and derashot on the midrashim of the weekly parshiot with halachic notes.
story_body: Goldberg, then teaching the lower class at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, also prepared a companion volume Yad LeKiddushin on Tractate Kiddushin, which did not appear in his lifetime and was finally published in Tel Aviv in 5746.

title_en: R' Shimon Zelichover deported from Krakow to the death camps
summary_en: In 5703 R' Shimon Zelichover was deported from Krakow to the Nazi extermination camps, where he was murdered.
story_body: After years of teaching in Tzanz, Krzanov, Stolin, Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, Yeshivat Chochmei Lublin and finally Krakow, Engel's life ended in the Shoah. His Torah was later collected in the volume Naharei Eish, printed in New York in 5753.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz leaves Warsaw yeshiva for Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R' Alter Simchowitz, mashpia at the Warsaw yeshiva, contracted tuberculosis at the start of 5685 and was forced to leave Poland for Eretz Yisrael to serve as mashpia at Yeshivas Toras Emes.
story_body: At the beginning of 5685 (autumn 1924), R' Alter Simchowitz fell ill with tuberculosis, attributed to his damp, dilapidated lodgings in Warsaw. Doctors advised that Jerusalem's air would be better for his health than Poland's humid climate. He left Poland to take up the position of mashpia at Yeshivas Toras Emes in Eretz Yisrael, and his departure significantly weakened the spiritual atmosphere of the Warsaw yeshiva.

title_en: R' Dovber Rivkin travels to Eretz Yisrael as Rosh Mesivta of Toras Emes
summary_en: R' Dovber Rivkin traveled to Eretz Yisrael at the start of 5685 to take up the position of Rosh Mesivta at Yeshivas Toras Emes.
story_body: Around the same time that R' Alter Simchowitz left for Eretz Yisrael, R' Dovber Rivkin also traveled there. He was appointed Rosh Mesivta (R"M) at Yeshivas Toras Emes, while R' Alter Simchowitz served as mashpia at the same institution.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin reports to R' Dovber Rivkin on Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: On the 7th day of Chanukah 5685, R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin wrote to R' Dovber Rivkin inquiring about the state of Yeshivas Toras Emes and reporting on the Warsaw yeshiva.
story_body: On the 7th of Chanukah 5685, R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin sent a letter to R' Dovber Rivkin in Eretz Yisrael, asking about R' Alter Simchowitz's arrival, his health, and the state of Yeshivas Toras Emes in both quantity and quality, in physical and spiritual matters. The same letter described the recent appointment of R' Yosef Blumenfeld as mashgiach in the Warsaw yeshiva.

title_en: R' Chaim Meir Lis appointed mashpia in Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: R' Chaim Meir Lis accepted the position of mashpia at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw after receiving a personal handwritten letter from the Rebbe encouraging him to take the role.
story_body: After R' Alter Simchowitz left for Eretz Yisrael, R' Chaim Meir Lis was appointed as one of the mashpi'im in the Warsaw yeshiva. He initially refused the position, wanting to support himself through his own labor, but accepted after receiving a second handwritten letter from the Rebbe explaining the role of tmimim as 'lanterns of light.' He served as mashpia until after Purim 5687 (1927).

title_en: Roster of 78 students compiled at Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: At the end of 5685 a detailed roster of 78 students of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was compiled, recording family details, talents, and diligence.
story_body: Toward the end of 5685, a list of 78 students of the Warsaw yeshiva was compiled and preserved in the archives. It included family details, abilities, and the diligence of each student, as well as the year each had been accepted, providing a record of the student body for the years 5682-5685. Of those listed, 54 were currently studying and 24 had already completed their studies.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz sends maamar to Warsaw students from Russia
summary_en: On 25 Iyar 5685, the Rebbe Rayatz sent the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba B'Truniya' from Russia to the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, instructing them to learn it by heart.
story_body: On 25 Iyar 5685, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote from Russia to the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, sending them the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba B'Truniya Im Briyosav' as a gift, with instructions to study it and know it by heart. He urged them to strengthen themselves in Torah study, both nigleh and Chassidus, and in avodah of prayer and refinement of character, promising Heaven's help in rising spiritually and materially.

title_en: R' Yosef Blumenfeld appointed mashgiach in Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: At the start of 5685, R' Yosef Blumenfeld of Dombrowa was appointed as a new R"M and mashgiach in the Warsaw yeshiva with the Rebbe's approval.
story_body: At the beginning of 5685, the Warsaw yeshiva received a new appointment of R"M and mashgiach with the Rebbe's consent: R' Yosef Blumenfeld of Dombrowa, who had studied for two years at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch. He later served as R"M in the Radomsk Chassidic yeshivas 'Keter Torah,' then as rabbi in Krolewska Huta, and in winter 5695 immigrated to Eretz Yisrael where he served on the beis din in Tel Aviv.

title_en: Warsaw yeshiva expands to additional apartment on Franciszkanska Street
summary_en: At the beginning of 5685, the Warsaw yeshiva rented a second apartment at 6 Franciszkanska Street to supplement its existing space at number 8.
story_body: Having moved to 8 Franciszkanska Street at the start of 5683, the Warsaw yeshiva outgrew the space by the beginning of 5685 and rented an additional nearby apartment at 6 Franciszkanska. The shiurim and main gathering remained at number 8, while the shiur lectures and Chassidus learning that couldn't fit took place in the shul at number 6.

title_en: R' Yosef Blumenfeld receives rabbinical ordination
summary_en: R' Yosef Blumenfeld received semicha for the rabbinate in 5687, with the ordination noting he was Rosh Mesivta in Warsaw.
story_body: R' Yosef Blumenfeld received his rabbinical ordination in 5687 (1927), which was later printed at the beginning of his commentary on the Kaftor VaFerach. The semicha noted that he had served as Rosh Mesivta in Warsaw.

title_en: R' Yosef Blumenfeld immigrates to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In winter 5695, R' Yosef Blumenfeld immigrated to Eretz Yisrael and served on the beis din in Tel Aviv.
story_body: After serving as rabbi in Krolewska Huta, R' Yosef Blumenfeld immigrated to Eretz Yisrael in the winter of 5695. There he served on the rabbinical court (beis din) in Tel Aviv and authored a commentary on the Kaftor VaFerach by Eshtori HaParchi.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw operates at Franciscan St. 30
summary_en: During 5681–5682 the Warsaw branch of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva studied in the synagogue at Franciscan Street 30.
story_body: In the years 5681–5682 (approximately 1920–1922) the Warsaw branch of Tomchei Tmimim was housed in the synagogue at Franciscan Street 30. The yeshiva was still in its early formative period in Poland and used existing study halls before later expansions. This location preceded its move to a more spacious house of study on the same street.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw relocates to Franciscan St. 8
summary_en: In the years 5683–5685 the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim moved to a more spacious house of study at Franciscan Street 8.
story_body: Between 5683 and 5685 (approx. 1922–1925) the yeshiva relocated within Warsaw to a roomier beit midrash at Franciscan Street 8. The move reflected steady growth in student numbers as the institution's reputation spread across Poland and neighboring countries. It remained at this address until the next, larger move in 5686.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz moves residence to Leningrad
summary_en: In 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz relocated his residence to Leningrad, from where he managed Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw by correspondence.
story_body: In 5684 (1923/24) the Rebbe Rayatz moved from his prior location to Leningrad. From there he maintained a steady correspondence with the Tomchei Tmimim administration in Warsaw on all matters of the yeshiva. The Warsaw committee — R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin, R' Tzvi Gurarie and R' Shmuel Zalmanov's father — handled day-to-day affairs while reporting regularly to him.

title_en: R' Yehiel Tzvi Gurarie emigrates from Russia to Warsaw
summary_en: In 5685 R' Yehiel Tzvi Gurarie escaped Soviet Russia and settled in Warsaw, soon joining the Tomchei Tmimim leadership.
story_body: In 5685 (1924/25) R' Yehiel Tzvi Gurarie succeeded in escaping Soviet Russia and settling in Warsaw. He joined the three-man directing committee of the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim, replacing R' Dov Moshe Shmotkin who had emigrated to the Holy Land. Together with R' Shneur Zalman Shmotkin and R' Shmuel Zalmanov's father, he bore the burden of running the yeshiva.

title_en: Wedding of R' M. Blizinski in Warsaw
summary_en: R' M. Blizinski married on 2 Nisan 5686, shortly before the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim moved into its new building.
story_body: On 2 Nisan 5686 (around mid-March 1926) R' M. Blizinski was married in Warsaw. He later recalled the date precisely in a 1977 letter to his grandson, noting that the wedding took place just before the yeshiva left Franciscan St. 8 and moved to its new building. The detail helped establish the exact timing of the yeshiva's relocation.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw moves to Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 17
summary_en: In spring 5686 Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw moved to a three-story rented building at Mlawska 7 (corner Sapuzinski 17), where it remained for ten years.
story_body: After Pesach 5686 the rapidly growing yeshiva — with nearly three hundred students drawn from Poland and abroad — left Franciscan Street and moved into a far larger leased building at Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 17. The three-story former flour-mill complex, fitted out as kitchen, dining hall, five large classrooms, dormitory attic and a prayer hall, was renovated with a grant from Mr. Bernhard Cohen of the Joint Distribution Committee's reconstruction fund. The yeshiva remained at this address until autumn 5696 (1935), when it relocated to Otwock.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz directs R' S. Z. Gurarie's course of study
summary_en: On 27 Nisan 5686 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the young R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie laying out his study program at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.
story_body: On 27 Nisan 5686 (April 1926) the Rebbe Rayatz, writing from Petersburg, instructed the teenage R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie that his principal study was to be Talmud with deep iyun. He asked the boy to inform him in detail which tractates he knew, including Tosafot, so that the studies could be properly arranged. The letter is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3795.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz instructs R' S. Z. Gurarie to study Mishnayot by heart
summary_en: On 28 Tishrei 5687 the Rebbe Rayatz directed R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie to learn Mishnayot by heart, beginning with Seder Taharot.
story_body: On 28 Tishrei 5687 (October 1926) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote again to R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie, instructing him to learn Mishnayot by heart starting from Seder Taharot. The pace was to be no more than one chapter every two days, with thorough memorization and calm review. The letter is found in Igrot Kodesh vol. 11, letter 3800.

title_en: 'Kol Korei' published describing the new yeshiva building
summary_en: In Elul 5687 the yeshiva published a 'Kol Korei' describing its new three-story building at Mlawska 7.
story_body: In Elul 5687 (August–September 1927) Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw issued a printed Kol Korei, describing for donors and the public the spacious accommodations at Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 15/17 — six classrooms, a large kitchen, prepared beds and orderly conduct in a dedicated three-story building. A photograph of the document later appeared in Beton Chabad issue 34.

title_en: Prof. Khavkin writes detailed survey of the Warsaw yeshiva building
summary_en: On 5 Tevet 5688 Prof. Mordechai Zev (Vladimir) Khavkin wrote a detailed English-language survey of the Tomchei Tmimim building in Warsaw.
story_body: On 5 Tevet 5688 (29 December 1927) Prof. Mordechai Zev (Vladimir) Khavkin penned a detailed report on the Warsaw yeshiva branch, describing its layout — kitchen and dining hall on the ground floor, five spacious classrooms above, a sleeping attic, and an old single-story wing converted to a prayer hall for the public. He noted that the equipment, of the simplest possible kind, was funded by a Joint Distribution Committee reconstruction grant from Mr. Bernhard Cohen. The report was later translated from English and printed in Beton Chabad issues 34–35.

title_en: Wedding of Rebbe's daughter; donor offers building for yeshiva
summary_en: At a wedding on 14 Kislev 5689, the Warsaw philanthropist R' Avraham HaKohen offered to fund a new yeshiva building.
story_body: On 14 Kislev 5689 (27 November 1928) — the date of a wedding in the Rebbe's family — R' Avraham HaKohen, a Warsaw philanthropist, expressed his desire to donate a new building for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva. The Rebbe Rayatz alluded to the offer days later in a Chanukah letter to him, and pursued the matter through R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov, hoping to acquire property in Warsaw or in nearby Otwock for the yeshiva. The plan ultimately did not come to fruition at that time.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to R' Avraham HaKohen on Chanukah
summary_en: On the fourth day of Chanukah 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Avraham HaKohen alluding to his promised donation for the yeshiva.
story_body: On the fourth day of Chanukah 5689 (around 11 December 1928) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Warsaw philanthropist R' Avraham HaKohen, gently alluding — without detail — to 'the great good things you wish to do.' The letter referred to Avraham HaKohen's earlier offer at the family wedding to fund a new yeshiva building. It is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6004.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov about yeshiva property
summary_en: On 3 Tevet 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov exploring purchase of a building or courtyard around Warsaw — preferably in Otwock — for the yeshiva.
story_body: On 3 Tevet 5689 (December 1928) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a confidential letter to R' Dov Nisan Bezpalov, asking him to identify properties around Warsaw suitable for purchase on long-term bank financing, with a preference for towns near Warsaw such as Otwock. He stressed that the matter be kept entirely private and not discussed even with close associates. The letter is found in Igrot Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6016.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes about Avraham HaKohen's proposed Riga visit
summary_en: On 9 Adar II 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote welcoming Avraham HaKohen's proposed visit to Riga to discuss the yeshiva's housing.
story_body: On 9 Adar II 5689 (February 1929) the Rebbe Rayatz wrote again to R' Avraham HaKohen, replying to a letter in which the philanthropist had proposed visiting Riga to continue their discussion of housing for the yeshiva. The Rebbe noted that such a visit would be most welcome and asked for the planned timing in detail. The letter is preserved in Igrot Kodesh vol. 16, letter 6153.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber's spring report on Warsaw yeshiva staff
summary_en: On 13 Iyar 5691 R' Yehuda Eber sent the Rebbe a written assessment of the Warsaw yeshiva's teachers and supervisors.
story_body: On 13 Iyar 5691 (30 April 1931) R' Yehuda Eber, sent to examine the Warsaw students, wrote a report to the Rebbe Rayatz evaluating each teacher and the chief mashgiach R' Yehoshua Berl. He praised R' David Teiblum's clear instruction, while observing that R' Yehoshua Berl, though a great scholar, was inclined to talmudic abstractions rather than the simple sense of the Gemara. The report set the stage for the Rebbe's later directive to reduce the Warsaw staff.

title_en: Plan to transfer Warsaw 'olam' students to Riga falls through
summary_en: In summer 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz planned to transfer senior Warsaw yeshiva students to Riga; the plan did not come to fruition.
story_body: In summer 5691 (1931) a plan was developed to move the advanced students of the Warsaw 'olam' to Riga, where the Rebbe Rayatz was then residing. R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was among those selected for the move. When the plan ultimately failed, the Rebbe instead dispatched Gurarie to a number of towns in Volyn to attempt opening branches of Tomchei Tmimim there.

title_en: Yeshiva relocates from Warsaw to Otwock
summary_en: In Tishrei 5696 Tomchei Tmimim left its Warsaw building of nearly a decade and moved to Otwock at Slovatzkenya 1.
story_body: In Tishrei 5696 (autumn 1935) the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim — having outgrown the building at Mlawska 7 / Sapuzinski 17 where it had operated for nearly ten years — relocated to the nearby town of Otwock, taking up new quarters at Slovatzkenya Street 1. The move responded to overcrowding that had developed even before the expansion noted in earlier internal reports.

title_en: R' Yosef Morgenstern, Rebbe of Kotzk-Pilov, passes away
summary_en: On 14 Adar 5699 the Rebbe of Kotzk-Pilov, R' Yosef Morgenstern, passed away leaving no descendants.
story_body: On 14 Adar 5699 (5 March 1939) the Admur of Kotzk-Pilov, R' Yosef Morgenstern, passed away. He left no descendants, and his chassidim sought a successor among his close circle. Their choice fell on R' David Teiblum, then a maggid shiur at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw.

title_en: R' David Teiblum crowned as Admur by Kotzk-Pilov chassidim
summary_en: In Nisan 5699 R' David Teiblum, a longtime Tomchei Tmimim maggid shiur, was crowned Admur by the Pilov chassidim.
story_body: In Nisan 5699 (April 1939) R' David Teiblum — known as R' David Riker after his hometown Reika — was crowned Admur by the chassidim of Kotzk-Pilov following the death of R' Yosef Morgenstern. He had served as maggid shiur of the lowest class at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw since 5686. Before accepting, he sought and received the affirmation of the Rebbe Rayatz; he was later murdered in the Holocaust.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie is born in Kremenchug
summary_en: On the first night of Chanukah 5672 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was born in Kremenchug.
story_body: On the first night of Chanukah 5672 (approximately 16 December 1911) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was born in Kremenchug. He was the son of R' Natan Gurarie and the younger brother of R' Yechiel Tzvi. His early years coincided with the upheavals of revolution and civil war in Russia.

title_en: Gurarie family relocates to Rostov, near the Rebbe's home
summary_en: At the start of 5680 the Gurarie family moved to Rostov, settling near the home of the Lubavitcher Rebbe.
story_body: At the start of 5680 (autumn 1919) the Gurarie family relocated to Rostov, settling close to the residence of the Rebbeim. R' Shneur Zalman was then about eight years old. The proximity allowed close contact with the Rebbes' court during a formative period of his life.

title_en: R' Natan Gurarie passes away
summary_en: In 5682 R' Natan Gurarie, father of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie, passed away in Rostov.
story_body: In 5682 (1921/22) R' Natan Gurarie, father of R' Shneur Zalman and R' Yechiel Tzvi, passed away. He left a widow, Mrs. Esther, and his sons, who continued in their father's path. R' Shneur Zalman was then about ten years old.

title_en: Bar mitzvah of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie in Nevel
summary_en: On Chanukah 5685 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie celebrated his bar mitzvah while a student at Tomchei Tmimim in Nevel.
story_body: On Chanukah 5685 (December 1924) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie reached bar mitzvah while studying at the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Nevel. Shortly afterward he, his mother Esther, and his older brother R' Yechiel Tzvi left Soviet Russia and settled in Warsaw. There he enrolled at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw and received personal study direction from the Rebbe Rayatz.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie heads Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw mechina
summary_en: At the start of 5693 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was appointed to head the preparatory division (mechina) of the Warsaw yeshiva.
story_body: At the start of 5693 (autumn 1932) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was appointed head of the mechina — the preparatory division of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, then located at Maranow 9 with two classes. The appointment marked his transition from senior student to leadership within the yeshiva system. He would soon take on broader organizational roles.

title_en: 'Igud Talmidei HaTemimim' association founded
summary_en: In 5694 the 'Igud Talmidei HaTemimim' association was founded under R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie's leadership.
story_body: In 5694 (1933/34) the Igud Talmidei HaTemimim — Union of Tomchei Tmimim Students — was established, with R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie at its head. The association coordinated alumni and student activities and would, the following year, launch the Chabad periodical HaTamim. It also took responsibility for printing the Rebbe Rayatz's discourses and addresses.

title_en: Chabad periodical 'HaTamim' begins publication
summary_en: In 5695 the 'Igud Talmidei HaTemimim' began publishing the journal 'HaTamim,' edited under R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie's responsibility.
story_body: In 5695 (1934/35) the Igud Talmidei HaTemimim began issuing the periodical HaTamim, with R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie responsible for its publication. The journal collected discourses, articles and historical material from the world of Chabad and Tomchei Tmimim. It became a major outlet for the movement's printed output in pre-war Europe.

title_en: Marriage of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie in New York
summary_en: In the winter of 5700 R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie married the daughter of the Admur of Kopytznitz, R' Avraham Yehoshua Heschel, in New York.
story_body: In the winter of 5700 (1939–40) R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie was married in New York to the daughter of the Admur of Kopytznitz, R' Avraham Yehoshua Heschel. The wedding took place against the backdrop of the European war, with much of the Chabad world already in flight. His position in New York would soon allow him to assist the Rebbe Rayatz in establishing new institutions in America.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in New York
summary_en: In the late winter of 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz reached New York after escaping war-torn Europe.
story_body: In the late winter of 5700 (early 1940) the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in New York, having been rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw. From New York he began the rebuilding of Chabad institutions on American soil. Within months he would found new branches of Tomchei Tmimim and youth divisions to anchor the movement in the New World.

title_en: Founding of 'Achei Temimim' youth division in New York
summary_en: In the winter of 5701 the Rebbe Rayatz founded the Achei Temimim youth division of Tomchei Tmimim in New York, appointing R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie to head it.
story_body: In the winter of 5701 (1940–41) the Rebbe Rayatz established Achei Temimim, the youth division of Tomchei Tmimim, in New York. He appointed R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie — newly settled in New York through his marriage into the Kopytznitz family — to head the new division. The story is recounted in Toldot Chabad in the United States, p. 180 onward.

title_en: Passing of R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie in New York
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie passed away in New York on the first day of Rosh Hashana 5764.
story_body: On the first day of Rosh Hashana 5764 (27 September 2003), Shabbat, R' Shneur Zalman Gurarie passed away in New York. He had served as a senior leader within the Chabad movement for decades — heading the Warsaw mechina in his youth, leading Achei Temimim in New York, and later serving on the Vaad HaMesader and the Vaad Hanhalat Agudat Chabad. His life spanned the destruction of pre-war European Chabad and its rebuilding in America.

title_en: R. Shmuel Zalmanov appointed chief supervisor of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
summary_en: At the start of 5687, R. Shmuel Zalmanov received a handwritten letter of appointment from the Rebbe Rayatz as general supervisor and coordinator of Nigleh studies across all branches of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
story_body: R. Shmuel Zalmanov, then one of the senior students, was appointed by the Rebbe Rayatz to supervise and centralize the study of Nigleh in every division of the yeshiva and to test the students. Soon after, he was also given responsibility for administrative management, including organizing funding sources. He remained in this role until his marriage in 5693 (1933).

title_en: R. Shmuel Zalmanov born in Warsaw
summary_en: R. Shmuel Zalmanov was born in Warsaw on the 8th of Tevet 5664.
story_body: Shmuel Zalmanov, who would later become a senior figure in Tomchei Tmimim, editor of Hatamim, and head of Nichoach in New York, was born in Warsaw on 8 Tevet 5664. He first attended the yeshiva only for Chassidus studies when it opened in summer 5681, and entered as a full student in summer 5684.

title_en: Shmuel Zalmanov enters Tomchei Tmimim as full student
summary_en: In summer 5684, Shmuel Zalmanov entered Tomchei Tmimim as a regular enrolled student after previously attending only for Chassidus studies.
story_body: Shmuel Zalmanov had been coming to the Warsaw yeshiva for Chassidus studies since its opening in summer 5681. In summer 5684 he was officially enrolled as a full student of the yeshiva, and was already noted in records as highly capable and qualified for rabbinic ordination.

title_en: Shmuel Zalmanov begins teaching Chassidus to younger students
summary_en: In 5686, R. Shmuel Zalmanov began giving Chassidus shiurim to younger students at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw.
story_body: By summer 5686, Zalmanov was noted as excelling in both Nigleh and Chassidus, studying Likkutei Torah with one group in the morning and Hemshech Ayin-Beis with the Tmimim in the evening. He reviewed Chassidus well and spent extended time in prayer, foreshadowing his later leadership roles.

title_en: Detailed yeshiva report sent to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad
summary_en: On 5 Chayei Sarah 5687, R. Shmuel Zalmanov sent a detailed report to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad describing the organization and class structure of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw.
story_body: Immediately upon assuming his role as general supervisor, Zalmanov reported in detail on yeshiva conditions to the Rebbe Rayatz, who was then living in Leningrad. The report described three divisions plus the main hall, with approximately 170 students, listing teachers, study material, and pedagogical structure. A follow-up report was sent on Parshas Va'eira covering academic progress through Kesubos daf 71.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz blesses Tomchei Tmimim students for Yud-Tes Kislev
summary_en: On 12 Kislev 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw with blessings for the upcoming festival of Yud-Tes Kislev.
story_body: In a letter dated 12 Kislev 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz blessed the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, along with their mashpi'im, mashgichim, and administrators, in advance of Yud-Tes Kislev. He invoked the path of the Rebbeim who had given their souls to disseminate Chassidus, and prayed they would elevate themselves and strengthen the world's pillars through Torah and mitzvos.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz invited to settle in Warsaw upon leaving Russia
summary_en: At the end of Tishrei 5688, immediately upon the Rebbe Rayatz's exit from Russia, the leaders of the Chassidic community in Warsaw invited him to settle there, but he declined.
story_body: Upon leaving Russia at the end of Tishrei 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz was invited by Warsaw's Chassidic leaders to take up residence in the city. He replied that various weighty reasons made this impossible, but expressed his intention to visit Warsaw at a designated future time.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz requests detailed report on Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: On 25 Marcheshvan 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the yeshiva director R. Shmuel Feivish Zalmanov requesting a detailed report on the state of Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: About a month after declining to relocate to Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the yeshiva administrator requesting that his son Shmuel write a thorough, organized account of the yeshiva's condition. He emphasized his strong desire to know every detail of the institution's affairs.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz announces plan to visit Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: On the first night of Chanukah 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that he intended to visit Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, no earlier than the month of Shevat.
story_body: Following the visit of R. Yisrael Pinchas to Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote on the first night of Chanukah 5688 that he planned to visit Tomchei Tmimim of Warsaw. He stated his intention to travel no earlier than the upcoming month of Shevat, beginning preparations for the journey from Riga.

title_en: Professor Chavkin inspects Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
summary_en: On 5 Tevet 5688, Professor Mordechai Zev (Vladimir) Chavkin inspected Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and wrote a detailed report on the institution.
story_body: Professor Chavkin visited the yeshiva and recorded that 8 teachers aged 35-50 ran four classes plus a self-study fifth class for older students. He counted approximately 250 students aged 10 to 20, of whom 80 lived on-site and received meals; the rest stayed with families. He documented the committee leadership including Zalmanov, Shmotkin, Gurarie, Rothstein, Blum, and Rabbi Yosef Kalisch.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz travels to Warsaw to visit Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: On 28 Shevat 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz departed from Riga for Warsaw to visit Tomchei Tmimim, staying about two weeks.
story_body: After preparations begun on the first night of Chanukah, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Warsaw on 28 Shevat 5688 and stayed approximately two weeks. The trip combined an inspection of Tomchei Tmimim with visits to Anash in Warsaw and the surrounding region. Detailed accounts were preserved by accompanying chassidim and later published in Sefer HaToldos and the Sefer HaMaamarim and Sichos of 5688.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz's first visit to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
summary_en: On Thursday of Parshas Tetzaveh 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz visited Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw for the first time, inspecting offices, classrooms, and dormitories.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz toured the entire yeshiva, beginning with the office where he examined account books and student records, then meeting individually with the rosh yeshivas, mashgichim, and mashpi'im. He proceeded through every classroom and the main study hall, telling the chief mashgiach 'fine personal property,' inspected the dormitories and dining hall, and recited Shehecheyanu. He later remarked that the yeshiva was 'an everlasting edifice — but in its inner dimension'.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz farbrengs with Tomchei Tmimim students on Purim
summary_en: On Purim 5688 in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz held a farbrengen with Tomchei Tmimim students that lasted past 2 a.m.
story_body: After the Megillah reading the night of Purim, a select group of Anash dined with the Rebbe Rayatz, who spoke of Chassidus and avodah until past midnight. The following afternoon at 3:30 he came to the yeshiva hall for the Purim seuda, with Anash seated at the tables and students standing in rows singing Chabad melodies. The farbrengen continued until 2 a.m., after which the Rebbe told a chassid in the office that he had not imagined the yeshiva in such an exalted state, calling it 'a piece of my father's work'.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz returns to Riga after five-week journey
summary_en: On 28 Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz returned home from a five-week journey that included visits to the yeshivos in Warsaw and Vilna.
story_body: In letters dated 6 and 8 Nissan 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz reported having returned on 28 Adar exhausted but spiritually nourished by his trip. He described the lasting positive impression made on him by Tomchei Tmimim of Warsaw and the yeshiva in Vilna. He resolved upon returning home to personally take on the project of expanding the Warsaw yeshiva.

title_en: R. Yechezkel Feigin writes about plans to expand Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: On 3 Iyar 5688, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson in America about plans to expand Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw to two or three times its size.
story_body: Feigin reported that the Rebbe Rayatz was deeply moved by the conduct and condition of the Warsaw yeshiva, which had approximately 250 students and was the largest Chabad yeshiva. He noted that there was great financial hardship despite the achievement, and that the Rebbe was determined to take responsibility for substantially expanding the institution materially and spiritually. The director of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in America was being informed in preparation for fundraising efforts.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz cites Warsaw activities as a distraction from expansion plans
summary_en: On 3 Marcheshvan 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his uncle R. Moshe HaKohen Horenstein that yeshiva and cheder administration in his own country had prevented him from advancing the Warsaw expansion.
story_body: Writing to his uncle, the Rebbe Rayatz explained that if properly organized, Tomchei Tmimim of Warsaw could bring real light to the world. He had resolved during his Warsaw visit to take this work upon himself, but upon returning home he was overwhelmed by the burdens of running the yeshivos and chadarim in his own country. Earlier, on 2 Marcheshvan 5689, he had written to the yeshiva administration confirming in writing that the impression made by the institution was beyond description.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz arrives in Riga for the Days of Awe
summary_en: R' Yechezkel Feigin notified R' Israel Jacobson that R' Alter Simchowitz had come from Jerusalem to spend Tishrei with the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga.
story_body: Following the Rebbe Rayatz's late-winter 5688 visit to Warsaw Tomchei Temimim, he resolved to overhaul the yeshiva's staffing. The chance arose when R' Alter Simchowitz of Jerusalem, who had served as mashpia in Warsaw from 5682-5685, traveled to Riga for the Days of Awe. On 18 Elul 5688, the Rebbe's secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin informed R' Israel Jacobson of the 'honored guest's' arrival, setting the stage for discussions to bring R' Alter back as chief mashpia.

title_en: Studies resume at Warsaw Tomchei Temimim with R' Alter as mashpia
summary_en: On the first day of Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5689, R' Alter Simchowitz began teaching chassidus each morning at the Warsaw Tomchei Temimim.
story_body: After Tishrei in Riga, R' Alter Simchowitz traveled to Warsaw to take up his new post. On Sunday, 30 Tishrei 5689, the students began studying chassidus with him at the appointed early hour. About thirty-five students filled the hall; their outward conduct was orderly but they urgently needed steady guidance and clearer instruction on the inner avodah expected of them.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz formally appoints R' Alter chief mashpia of Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote from Riga to the yeshiva's Va'ad and to R' Alter himself, charging him with general supervision of chassidus and overall yeshiva conduct.
story_body: On 2 Marcheshvan 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a letter to the Warsaw Va'ad declaring that he was placing on R' Alter Simchowitz the 'sacred yoke' of overseeing all hashpa'a and hadracha at the yeshiva. In a parallel letter that day to R' Alter, he charged him with ordering the studies, awakening the students' inner point of avodah she'b'lev through chassidic teaching, and producing fruit in middos and conduct.

title_en: Rebbe offers his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein the Warsaw yeshiva directorship
summary_en: On 3 Marcheshvan, the Rebbe Rayatz proposed that his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein of Otwock take charge of administering the Warsaw yeshiva.
story_body: Writing from Riga the day after his appointment letters for R' Alter, the Rebbe addressed his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein, who lived in Otwock near Warsaw. He asked him to accept overall management and financial stewardship of Tomchei Temimim, explaining that the institution had to be rebuilt from scratch and that he could now coordinate more easily than before. R' Alter Simchowitz was to convey the practical details, and Hornstein could leave his own business to his wife and son in order to focus on the yeshiva.

title_en: Warsaw yeshiva Va'ad meets to plan staff reorganization
summary_en: The Warsaw Tomchei Temimim Va'ad convened on Sunday 7 Marcheshvan 5689 to shrink the staff and reshape supervision under financial pressure.
story_body: R' Alter Simchowitz, R' Shmuel Zalmanov, and the senior administration committee met to plan how to reduce the yeshiva in size without weakening essential study. They resolved to release three staff members—the nigleh supervisor R' Yehoshua Ber, the second-division rosh yeshiva R' Zvi Meir, and the mashpia RSh"L—and proposed installing R' Boruch Friedman as the new nigleh supervisor. They also decided that R' Shmuel Zalmanov would travel to Otwock to formally press R' Moshe Hornstein to accept the directorship.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz reports yeshiva conditions to the Rebbe
summary_en: R' Alter wrote on 9 Marcheshvan that fixing the yeshiva hinged on appointing a chief director, but R' Moshe Hornstein's answer was still pending.
story_body: On Monday 8 Marcheshvan R' Alter had visited Otwock to relay the Rebbe's proposal to R' Moshe Hornstein, but Hornstein gave only a tentative response pending the Rebbe's letter. Writing on 9 Marcheshvan, R' Alter described being overwhelmed by the disorder—the financial straits, the gap in nigleh supervision, and the absence of mature students to whom hashpa'a could yet be delegated—and stressed that nothing could be set right until a chief director was installed.

title_en: R' Shmuel Zalmanov reports Va'ad and Otwock visit to the Rebbe
summary_en: R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz the night of 10 Marcheshvan 5689 describing the Va'ad's decisions and R' Moshe Hornstein's hesitations.
story_body: Zalmanov reported the Va'ad's plan to reduce the institution while replacing the nigleh supervisor with 'our man' R' Boruch Friedman, and to draw senior students into giving hashpa'a in chassidus. He recounted his Monday 8 Marcheshvan trip to Otwock, where Hornstein seemed willing in principle but had unresolved doubts and would only answer after writing the Rebbe himself. The yeshiva's financial state was 'awful and terrifying,' with creditors pressing and no income.

title_en: R' Alter writes Rebbe about ill health and yeshiva difficulties
summary_en: On 11 Marcheshvan 5689, R' Alter described his weakness and the strain of his daily schedule to the Rebbe Rayatz, still awaiting Hornstein's answer.
story_body: R' Alter wrote that he was 'very weak' and that his daily seder was unsustainable: he ate only mezonot before tefilla, taught chassidus until nine, but often could not hold out for davening to conclude after noon. He still hoped R' Moshe Hornstein would accept the directorship within a week and asked the Rebbe for guidance and a berachah for strength to serve b'mesirah amitis.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz blesses R' Alter Simchowitz with a refuah shleima
summary_en: Responding on 15 Marcheshvan 5689, the Rebbe wished R' Alter full recovery and strength to guide the talmidim in the path set by the Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz answered R' Alter's letter with a blessing that Hashem grant him a refuah shleima and a calm, strong mind to teach Torah and avodah she'b'lev. He invoked the inner authority his father, the Rebbe Rashab, had given them, that the students should ascend to the level of halacha through 'the form overpowering the matter'.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz holds chassan mohl for Tomchei Temimim students
summary_en: On the eve of the Rebbe's wedding, the Rebbe Rayatz convened a chassan mohl at the Warsaw yeshiva with a maamar, niggunim, and dancing with the students.
story_body: On 13 Kislev 5689, the day before his daughter Chaya Mushka's wedding in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz held a chassan mohl gathering specifically for the talmidim of Tomchei Temimim. He delivered a maamar of chassidus, niggunim of Chabad were sung, and after Birkat HaMazon the Rebbe danced with the students of the yeshiva.

title_en: Wedding of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka and Rebbe Menachem Mendel in Warsaw
summary_en: On 14 Kislev 5689, Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz, married the future Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson in Warsaw.
story_body: The kabbalat panim was held in the Tomchei Temimim hall and the chuppah in the yeshiva's courtyard. Tomchei Temimim students joined the wedding meal in a separate hall alongside the mashpia R' Alter, whom the Rebbe Rayatz instructed to distribute mashke to the talmidim for l'chaim. The Rebbe then addressed them with a sicha on the principle that 'Torah is preserved only in one who puts himself to death over it,' and afterward danced with the yeshiva's director and supervisors.

title_en: Rebbe arranges R' Moshe Hornstein's interim directorship of Warsaw yeshiva
summary_en: On 23 Kislev 5689, the Rebbe wrote to R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov and R' Moshe Hornstein finalizing a three-month engagement for Hornstein to organize the yeshiva.
story_body: After traveling with R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov, the Rebbe Rayatz had persuaded his uncle R' Moshe Hornstein to step in and put the yeshiva in order for about three months. He now asked Zalmanov to send his son Shmuel to Otwock to acquaint Hornstein with the operations, ledgers, and correspondence, and wrote Hornstein himself to confirm the plan. The arrangement does not appear in later sources, suggesting it was never carried out.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes Toras Emes students upon R' Alter's return
summary_en: On 5 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe wrote to the Toras Emes students in Jerusalem announcing R' Alter Simchowitz's safe return journey.
story_body: After roughly two months in Warsaw, R' Alter began the return trip to Jerusalem rather than relocating his family. On 5 Tevet 5689 the Rebbe wrote to the students of Toras Emes urging them to give themselves fully to R' Alter's program of study and avodah, signaling that he would now remain permanently in Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: R' Alter Simchowitz reports safe arrival back in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R' Alter wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz on 14 Tevet 5689 from Eretz Yisrael confirming his safe return.
story_body: On 14 Tevet 5689, R' Alter sent the Rebbe a brief report announcing his safe arrival in Eretz Yisrael. The Rebbe later acknowledged the letter and asked for word that he had resumed his work at Toras Emes.

title_en: Rebbe responds to R' Alter on resuming Toras Emes leadership
summary_en: On 27 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz blessed R' Alter with strength of health to take up his leadership of the Jerusalem yeshiva.
story_body: Replying to R' Alter's 14 Tevet letter, the Rebbe gave thanks for his safe arrival and prayed that Hashem strengthen his health so he could diligently lead the Toras Emes yeshiva in Jerusalem. He assumed by then that R' Alter had already re-entered his duties at the yeshiva.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz reaffirms R' Alter's mission at Toras Emes
summary_en: On 16 Shevat 5689, the Rebbe wrote again to R' Alter with blessings for health and success in fulfilling his role at Toras Emes.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz prayed for R' Alter's strength to fulfill 'his task and his calling' as designated and blessed by his father, the Rebbe Rashab. He invoked the special kochos given to R' Alter for leading and sustaining Tomchei Temimim — but the plan to bring his family to Warsaw was now permanently set aside, and his role at Toras Emes was treated as fixed.

title_en: Passing of R' Alter Simchowitz, mashpia of Toras Emes in Jerusalem
summary_en: R' Alter Simchowitz, longtime mashpia of Toras Emes in Jerusalem, passed away on 7 Nissan 5699.
story_body: After his brief 5689 stint in Warsaw, R' Alter continued serving as mashpia of the Toras Emes yeshiva in Jerusalem for the next decade. He held that post until his passing on 7 Nissan 5699.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber reports Warsaw yeshiva mashpia shortage to Rebbe
summary_en: R' Yehuda Eber wrote on 13 Iyar 5691 that no truly suitable senior mashpia had filled R' Alter's place at Warsaw Tomchei Temimim since his departure.
story_body: On 13 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe Rayatz that the chief weakness at the Warsaw yeshiva, since R' Alter Simchowitz's return to Jerusalem, was the absence of capable senior staff. R' Zalman Shmotkin studied with the students and supervised them, but his other responsibilities prevented him from giving the role the full devotion it required.

title_en: Rabbi Yehuda Eber leaves Russia for Riga
summary_en: Rabbi Yehuda Eber departed Russia in the winter of 5690 (1930) and arrived in Riga after years of leading underground yeshiva branches.
story_body: After serving as a leading rosh yeshiva in the underground Tomchei Tmimim network in Poltava, Rostov, Nevel, and Vitebsk, Rabbi Yehuda Eber received permission to leave Soviet Russia in the winter of 5690. He arrived in Riga intending to continue on to the United States, but was unable to obtain entry papers despite efforts by Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson of Agudas Chabad. He remained stranded with his family in Riga while pursuing the American visa.

title_en: Rabbi Eber sent to examine students in Warsaw and Vilna
summary_en: In the summer of 5690 (1930) the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched Rabbi Yehuda Eber from Riga to examine the students of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and Vilna.
story_body: While stranded in Riga awaiting an American visa, Rabbi Yehuda Eber received word through Rabbi Yisrael Jacobson and Rabbi Y. Feigin that the Rebbe Rayatz wished him to travel immediately to Warsaw and Vilna to examine all the students of Tomchei Tmimim there. A telegraphic visa was arranged from Warsaw. The journey set in motion his future role as rosh yeshiva of the central yeshiva in Warsaw.

title_en: Roster of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw students compiled
summary_en: A detailed roster of the students learning at Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw was compiled for the summer of 5690 (1930), recording family and academic details of each bochur.
story_body: The summer 5690 student list documents nearly sixty bochurim studying in the Warsaw yeshiva, with notes on their hometowns, ages, family backgrounds, chassidic affiliations, and academic progress through the yeshiva's classes. The list preserves a rare demographic snapshot of pre-war Polish Chabad youth, including students from Warsaw, Chelm, Lublin, Stopnica, Riga, Romania, and dozens of Polish towns. It serves as a key document for tracing the talmidim of Tomchei Tmimim before the Holocaust.

title_en: Semicha granted to Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw students by Warsaw rabbinic luminaries
summary_en: In Adar 5690 (March 1930) leading Warsaw rabbis granted semicha to a group of Tomchei Tmimim students after rigorous examinations.
story_body: A landmark celebration marked the awarding of semicha to the first group of Tomchei Tmimim bochurim in Warsaw by major poskim including Rabbi Menachem Zemba, Rabbi Shlomo Dovid Kahane, Rabbi Chaim Leib Yudkovsky, Rabbi Yehoshua Plate, and Rabbi Yitzchak Meir Kanal. Surviving semicha documents from the estate of Rabbi Moshe Pinchas Katz, dated Adar 5690, were issued by Rabbi Shlomo Dovid Kahane, Rabbi Yitzchak Meir Kanal, Rabbi Sholom Shachna Cherniak of Maciejów, and Rabbi Yechezkel Michelson. The achievement demonstrated the high Talmudic level the yeshiva had reached in exile.

title_en: R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov sent to help establish Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron
summary_en: Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, a Tomchei Tmimim student, was among those sent to help found Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron.
story_body: In 5672 (1912), R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov of Surazh, who had studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Lubavitch, was part of the group sent to establish Yeshivas Toras Emes in Hebron. He later returned to Russia during World War I, eventually serving as rabbi of Drivin and then emigrating to Riga.

title_en: Reports on the state of mikvaot in Drivin recorded by R' Ashurov
summary_en: Documentation about the condition of the mikvaot in Drivin was created in 5688, later published in Toldos Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit.
story_body: In 5688 (1928), R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, then rabbi of Drivin, submitted reports on the state of the local mikvaot. These reports were later published in Sefer Toldos Chabad B'Russia HaSovietit, p. 174.

title_en: Rayatz writes R' Ashurov reassuring him over informants' libels
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov assuring him not to worry about denunciations made against him.
story_body: On 24 Tishrei 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov of Drivin, reassuring him not to worry about informers who had denounced him. He stated that truth shines and all libels are nullified, and that those who sit in judgment recognize the truth.

title_en: Rayatz writes R' Ashurov about appointing his successor in Drivin
summary_en: Before R' Ashurov's planned departure from Russia, the Rebbe asked him to arrange a successor rabbi and shochet for Drivin.
story_body: On 26 Tevet 5689, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov regarding the appointment of a rabbi and shochet in Drivin to replace him after his planned departure. The Rebbe urged him to make arrangements for the community before leaving for Riga.

title_en: Rayatz writes R' Gutnik in London asking aid for refugee rabbis in Riga
summary_en: The Rebbe asked R' Mordechai Zev Gutnik in London to help two refugee Chabad rabbis stranded in Riga.
story_body: On 21 Cheshvan 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Mordechai Zev Gutnik, a rabbi in London, requesting help for two students of his stranded in Riga: R' Yaakov Yisrael Zuber and R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov. Both had hoped to emigrate to America but had been rejected by the American consul; the Rebbe asked Gutnik to secure entry permits and positions for them elsewhere.

title_en: Chadakov writes Rayatz that refugee rabbis are benefiting Riga
summary_en: R' Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chadakov wrote the Rebbe describing the benefit Riga drew from rabbis who had arrived from Russia.
story_body: On 25 Nisan 5690, R' Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chadakov wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz that the Riga community was benefiting greatly from the rabbis who had come from the valley of weeping (Russia), namely R' Yisrael Zuber, R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, and now also R' Yehuda Eber.

title_en: Rayatz announces plan to establish a Torah study circle in Riga
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote R' Yehuda Leib Nimoitin announcing his decision to establish a select Torah study circle in Riga.
story_body: On 2 Cheshvan 5691, soon after returning to Riga from America, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Yehuda Leib Nimoitin announcing his decision to establish a Torah study circle in Riga for outstanding students of Torah and yiras shamayim. He wished to gather ten select students who would devote themselves wholly to Torah study according to set conditions.

title_en: Rayatz announces R' Ashurov's appointment as Rosh Yeshiva in Warsaw
summary_en: In his general letter of 19 Cheshvan 5691, the Rebbe announced R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov's appointment as Rosh Yeshiva in Warsaw.
story_body: On 19 Cheshvan 5691, in a general letter, the Rebbe Rayatz announced that he was sending R' Avraham Eliyahu Ashurov, described as a great Torah scholar of exceptional talent, to serve as Rosh Yeshiva in one of the divisions of Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw. However, this plan was apparently never carried out, as Ashurov remained in Riga.

title_en: R' Shmuel Zalmanov sends Rayatz overview of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
summary_en: R' Shmuel Zalmanov sent the Rebbe a detailed status report on Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at the start of the new term.
story_body: On 20 Cheshvan 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz with a general overview of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw at the start of the new term. He reported 29 new students admitted and 110 students in total studying across three divisions, detailing who was teaching nigleh and chassidus in each class and stressing the continuing need for an inner mashpia.

title_en: Rayatz writes Nimoitin that Riga study circle plan still not realized
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote Nimoitin that his desire to raise the level of Torah study had still not been realized.
story_body: On 14 Kislev 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote again to R' Yehuda Leib Nimoitin, noting that his wish for the good of the students and for raising the level of Torah knowledge had still not come to fruition. The plan to establish a Riga study circle was still encountering difficulties.

title_en: New executive committee elected at Anash gathering in Warsaw
summary_en: A general meeting of Anash in Warsaw elected an expanded executive committee for Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Following a general meeting of Anash held on Motzaei Shabbos Shemos and continued on Motzaei Shabbos Vaera, an expanded executive committee was elected to manage Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. The committee was reported in a letter dated 2 Shevat 5691 to the Rebbe's son-in-law Rashag, who had been placed in charge of the yeshiva's treasury. Members included R' Mendel Rotstein as honorary chairman and R' Shraga Feivish Zalmanov as chairman.

title_en: Hanhalla warns Rayatz of severe budget crisis at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw
summary_en: The yeshiva's management warned the Rebbe of a severe financial crisis threatening the institution.
story_body: On 22 Shevat 5691, the management of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw wrote a desperate letter to the Rebbe Rayatz describing the yeshiva's dire financial condition. The Great Depression had cut income from America, and they considered shrinking the institution by reducing students and staff. They requested guidance and that the Rebbe telegraph New York for emergency support.

title_en: Warsaw hanhalla again asks Rayatz for direction on reorganization
summary_en: The Warsaw management asked the Rebbe how to organize the yeshiva for the coming summer term amid financial uncertainty.
story_body: On 26 Nisan 5691, the management of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw again wrote to the Rebbe, awaiting direction on how to arrange the yeshiva for the coming summer term. The financial crisis left them uncertain how to proceed and they urgently sought the Rebbe's guidance.

title_en: Rayatz decides to transfer Warsaw advanced students to Riga
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote the Warsaw hanhalla announcing his decision to bring the advanced Ulam students to Riga.
story_body: In response to the hanhalla's questions in late Nisan 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz informed Warsaw that he had decided to establish the main Tomchei Tmimim near his residence in Riga. Around 30-35 advanced 'Ulam' students from Warsaw would be selected to move there, while the Warsaw branch would continue only as a preparatory mechina. R' Yehuda Eber was being dispatched to examine and select students.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber arrives in Warsaw to examine yeshiva students
summary_en: R' Yehuda Eber arrived in Warsaw to examine students for possible transfer to Riga.
story_body: On Monday 2 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber arrived in Warsaw, sent by the Rebbe Rayatz from Riga to examine the students of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw and select those suitable for transfer to a new Ulam being opened in Riga. He immediately began by testing the younger students.

title_en: R' Eber sends Rayatz first report on Warsaw student examinations
summary_en: R' Eber wrote to the Rebbe with detailed lists of students he had examined so far.
story_body: On 10 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on his progress examining students at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. He had finished testing the younger students in the shiurim taught by R' Naftali and R' Dovid, and had begun examining the older students of the 'Kibbutz' (advanced division), enclosing a detailed list.

title_en: R' Eber finishes examining Warsaw students and reports to Rayatz
summary_en: R' Eber finished examining all Warsaw students and sent the Rebbe a detailed analysis of the planned Riga transfer.
story_body: On 13 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe that he had examined all the students currently in Warsaw and that about 20 would be suitable to transfer to Riga. He recorded his disagreement with the hanhalla's plan to close the lower preparatory class, arguing that new students typically join the younger classes and that chassidic families in the area especially wished their sons to learn at Tomchei Tmimim.

title_en: R' Eber examines Tomchei Tmimim students at the Lodz branch
summary_en: R' Eber traveled to Lodz to examine students of the Tomchei Tmimim branch there.
story_body: From 17 to 19 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber, at the Rebbe Rayatz's direction, examined the students at the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Lodz. After completing the examinations, he returned to Warsaw.

title_en: R' Eber travels to Vilna to examine Tomchei Tmimim students there
summary_en: R' Eber traveled from Warsaw to Vilna to examine students at that branch of Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: On Sunday 23 Iyar 5691, R' Yehuda Eber traveled from Warsaw to the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Vilna to examine its students, continuing his survey of yeshiva students across the Polish branches at the Rebbe Rayatz's direction.

title_en: R' Eber writes Rayatz detailed final report on yeshiva students
summary_en: From Vilna on Isru Chag Shavuot, R' Eber sent the Rebbe a detailed final report on enrollment and faculty needs.
story_body: On Isru Chag Shavuot (7 Sivan) 5691, R' Yehuda Eber wrote in detail from Vilna to the Rebbe Rayatz, reporting that Warsaw had about 25 students in the Kibbutz, 27 in the older shiur, and 25 in the younger. He warned that two qualified teachers in nigleh and chassidus would urgently be needed if the planned student transfer to Riga did not proceed soon.

title_en: Rayatz departs Riga for tour of Polish yeshiva branches
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to visit the three Tomchei Tmimim branches in Poland.
