story_body: On 9 Tammuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga to visit the three branches of Tomchei Tmimim under his guidance in Poland: Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz. He arrived in Warsaw on 8 Tammuz, intending to make personal visits to the yeshivas and meet privately with students.

title_en: Rayatz spends Chag HaGeula 12-13 Tammuz with yeshiva in Warsaw
summary_en: The Rebbe spent Chag HaGeula in Warsaw with the Tomchei Tmimim community, delivering chassidus and meeting students.
story_body: On 12-13 Tammuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz celebrated his liberation festival with the Tomchei Tmimim community at the yeshiva in Warsaw. He delivered three maamarei chassidus and many sichos during his approximately two-week stay, and met privately in yechidus with virtually every student of the yeshiva.

title_en: Rayatz departs Warsaw to travel to Marienbad
summary_en: After approximately two weeks visiting the Warsaw yeshiva, the Rebbe departed for Marienbad.
story_body: On 22 Tammuz 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Warsaw to travel to Marienbad. His Warsaw stay had been devoted primarily to the yeshiva, with the visit lasting from 8 Tammuz through 22 Tammuz.

title_en: Rayatz describes purpose of his tour of three Polish yeshivas
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote describing his recent journey to visit the three Tomchei Tmimim branches in Poland.
story_body: On 5 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that on 9 Tammuz he had left Riga for Warsaw to visit the three yeshivas under his guidance in Warsaw, Vilna, and Lodz. The trip had given particular focus to meeting yeshiva students personally.

title_en: R' Zalmanov reports to R' Slonim on Rayatz's Warsaw visit
summary_en: R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to R' Azriel Zelig Slonim describing the Rebbe's recent two-week visit to Warsaw.
story_body: On 7 Menachem Av 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov wrote to R' Azriel Zelig Slonim about the Rebbe Rayatz's recent visit to Warsaw on his way to Marienbad. The Rebbe stayed two weeks, delivered three maamarim and many sichos, celebrated Chag HaGeula at the yeshiva, took interest in its state, and met privately with nearly every student.

title_en: Feigin writes Jacobson on Rayatz's reasoning for the Warsaw journey
summary_en: Secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote R' Yisrael Jacobson about the Rebbe's visit to Poland.
story_body: On 15 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe's secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote R' Yisrael Jacobson describing how the Rebbe Rayatz had chosen, en route to Marienbad, to visit Poland and especially the yeshiva. The Rebbe had said the situation could no longer continue without a yeshiva nearby, deciding either to transfer part of the yeshiva to Riga or to relocate his own residence to Warsaw.

title_en: Rayatz directs preparation of Tomchei Tmimim alumni list
summary_en: The Rebbe instructed R' Shmuel Zalmanov to compile a comprehensive list of all alumni from Tomchei Tmimim's first decade.
story_body: On 22 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Shmuel Zalmanov asking the hanhalla to compile a list of all students who had studied at Tomchei Tmimim over its first ten years, including where they were now and what they were doing. The aim, the Rebbe wrote to talmid R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum, was to identify alumni who could be placed as roshei yeshiva, mashpiim, and madrichim to spread Torah.

title_en: Zalmanov reports to Rayatz on alumni-tracking project progress
summary_en: R' Zalmanov reported he had begun sending circular letters to traceable alumni.
story_body: On 27 Menachem Av 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov replied to the Rebbe that he had begun the alumni project, sending each known alumnus a circular letter with detailed questions. He included a sample of the letter being sent.

title_en: Zalmanov updates Rayatz on slow alumni response, plans newspaper notice
summary_en: R' Zalmanov reported few alumni had yet responded; nearly 300 names were on file but many addresses were uncertain.
story_body: On 6 Elul 5691, R' Shmuel Zalmanov updated the Rebbe Rayatz on the alumni project, noting that responses had so far been few. The hanhalla had nearly 300 alumni names on file, though not all addresses were precise, and planned to publish a notice in newspapers to reach more former students.

title_en: Rayatz settles in Otwock at Shapira hotel for the month of Tishrei
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived from Riga in Otwock to remain there throughout the month of Tishrei.
story_body: In Elul 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Otwock from Riga, renting the Shapira hotel as a spacious residence and beis midrash for himself and his family. He instructed that the students of the Lodz yeshiva join him in Otwock for the entire month of Tishrei.

title_en: R' Menachem Mendel Schneerson farbrengs publicly for first time, in Otwock
summary_en: During Sukkos 5692 in Otwock, R' Menachem Mendel Schneerson (later the Rebbe) delivered his first public farbrengen.
story_body: On a night of Simchas Beis HaShoeiva during Sukkos 5692 in Otwock, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed his son-in-law R' Menachem Mendel Schneerson, then called the Ramash, to farbreng with the assembled community. Beginning at 8 PM and continuing until dawn, the Ramash opened on the mishna 'Hevei az kanamer' and astonished the entire crowd with the depth and brilliance of his Torah, drawing on Talmud, Midrash, Zohar, Kabbalah, and chassidic stories. From that moment Anash began to recognize his unique greatness in his own right.

title_en: Igud Talmidei HaTmimim alumni organization founded
summary_en: The Igud Talmidei HaTmimim alumni organization was founded in 5694 to unite graduates of Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: In 5694 (1934), three years after the Rebbe Rayatz had directed R' Zalmanov to compile a list of all Tomchei Tmimim alumni, the Igud Talmidei HaTmimim was founded. Its purpose was to unite the graduates of the yeshiva for joint efforts in spreading Torah, yiras shamayim, and the study of chassidus.

title_en: Yeshiva administration asks Rebbe to appoint R. Yehuda Eber as Rosh Yeshiva in Warsaw
summary_en: Members of the Warsaw yeshiva administration wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz asking that R. Yehuda Eber be appointed as mashgiach and rosh yeshiva for nigleh.
story_body: On 26 Nisan 5691, the leadership of Tomchei Temimim in Warsaw petitioned the Rebbe Rayatz to bring R. Yehuda Eber on as a leader of the nigleh studies. They believed he would greatly benefit the depth and quality of Talmud study at the yeshiva.

title_en: Decision to keep central yeshiva in Warsaw and expand it
summary_en: During Tishrei 5692 it was resolved that the central Tomchei Temimim yeshiva would remain in Warsaw and be expanded with a new mechina division.
story_body: After a plan to move the yeshiva closer to the Rebbe in Riga was abandoned, the decision was made during Tishrei 5692 to keep the central yeshiva in Warsaw and grow it. A preparatory mechina division for younger students was added, classes were enlarged, and the staff was expanded.

title_en: R. Yehuda Eber appointed Rosh Yeshiva of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw
summary_en: R. Yehuda Eber confirmed in a letter to R. Yisrael Jacobson that the Rebbe had appointed him as r"m and mashgiach over nigleh studies in Warsaw.
story_body: On 26 Tishrei 5692, R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson reporting his new appointment by the Rebbe Rayatz as r"m and mashgiach for nigleh studies at the Warsaw yeshiva. He also noted his expectation that the Rebbe himself would settle permanently in Warsaw.

title_en: Tomchei Temimim Warsaw opens 5692 school year with 120 students
summary_en: The 5692 academic year opened in Warsaw with 120 students: 50 in the main hall, 60 in two classes, and 10 in the newly opened mechina.
story_body: At the start of the 5692 school year, Tomchei Temimim Warsaw enrolled approximately 120 students. The faculty included R. Yehuda Eber as rosh yeshiva, R. David Teiblum as r"m, R. Baruch Friedman as mashpia, R. Shmuel Zalmanov as administrator, and R. Eliyahu Moshe Liss and R. Meir Glazman as Chassidus instructors.

title_en: Mechina preparatory division opens at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw
summary_en: On Sunday of Parshas Vayera 5692, formal studies began in the new mechina preparatory department with 10-11 young students.
story_body: The mechina division for younger students officially began learning on Sunday of Parshas Vayera. Only 10-11 students initially enrolled because word had spread late, but more were expected to join in the coming term.

title_en: R. Shmuel Zalmanov resigns from yeshiva administration in Warsaw
summary_en: R. Shmuel Zalmanov stepped down as administrator of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw at the start of Kislev 5693 to focus on his private business.
story_body: Having taken on private business obligations, R. Shmuel Zalmanov informed the Rebbe at the start of Marcheshvan 5693 that he could no longer manage yeshiva administration. From Rosh Chodesh Kislev he ceased most involvement, and the burden fell on R. Yehuda Eber until a new manager could be appointed.

title_en: Yeshiva Warsaw faces severe financial crisis at start of 5693
summary_en: R. Shmuel Zalmanov reported to the Rebbe on 5 Marcheshvan 5693 that the yeshiva treasury was empty and the administration was considering downsizing.
story_body: Facing crushing debts and humiliating creditor pressure, the yeshiva leadership concluded on Sunday before 5 Marcheshvan 5693 that they would have to reduce the institution's size. Not a single coin remained in the treasury, and they could not even begin to cover daily expenses.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz proposes dismissing R. David Teiblum to cut costs
summary_en: On 26 Tishrei 5693 the Rebbe suggested converting R. David Teiblum's class into a mechina under R. Shneur Zalman Gurary to save salary costs.
story_body: Facing the financial crunch, the Rebbe Rayatz proposed to the Warsaw administration that R. David Teiblum be released and his class be turned into a mechina taught by R. Shneur Zalman Gurary. The administration ultimately decided it was impossible to dismiss him mid-term and kept the arrangement unchanged.

title_en: R. Yehuda Eber appointed director of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw
summary_en: On 11 Iyar 5693 the Rebbe Rayatz formally appointed R. Yehuda Eber as overall director of the Warsaw yeshiva, in addition to his role as rosh yeshiva.
story_body: After R. Yehuda Eber visited the Rebbe in Riga during Nisan 5693, the Rebbe gave him authority over the yeshiva's entire operation, including budget and personnel. The formal appointment letter was issued on 11 Iyar 5693, empowering him to manage all aspects of the institution and to correspond with donors.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz relocates from Riga to Warsaw
summary_en: In the late summer of 5693 the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Riga to Warsaw to live in proximity to the central yeshiva.
story_body: After years of leading the movement from Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz moved to Warsaw in late summer 5693 to be near Tomchei Temimim. This ended the need for the lengthy written correspondence between the Rebbe and the yeshiva administration that had marked the previous years.

title_en: Founding of Kupat Bachurim student welfare fund in Warsaw
summary_en: The Kupat Bachurim fund supporting Tomchei Temimim students was established on 15 Av 5692.
story_body: On 15 Av 5692, a dedicated fund called Kupat Bachurim was founded to support the bachurim of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw. Its honorary chairman was R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson (the Rebbe's son-in-law), with R. Yechezkel Feigin as chairman.

title_en: Birth of R. Yosef Avraham Cohen (Friedman) in Rechitsa
summary_en: R. Yosef Avraham Cohen, later chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, was born in Rechitsa, Russia in 5668 under the name Yosef Avraham Friedman.
story_body: Yosef Avraham Friedman was born in Rechitsa in 5668 (1908). He would later cross into Poland, study at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, and become a key administrator of the yeshiva office.

title_en: R. Yosef Avraham Friedman smuggled across border to Poland
summary_en: In 5682 the future Tomchei Temimim secretary smuggled himself across the Soviet-Polish border and assumed the name Alter Kagan.
story_body: In 5682 (1922), Yosef Avraham Friedman illicitly crossed from Russia into Poland. He officially adopted the name Alter Kagan, though unofficially he continued to be known as Yosef Avraham Kagan.

title_en: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan emigrates from Poland to England
summary_en: At the start of 5699 R. Yosef Avraham Kagan left Warsaw for England, where he would settle permanently in London.
story_body: After years serving as chief secretary at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, R. Yosef Avraham Kagan departed for England at the start of 5699. He had become engaged to a young woman from England, and a farewell gathering was held before his journey.

title_en: Wedding of R. Yosef Avraham Kagan in London
summary_en: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan's wedding was held in London on 8 Tammuz 5699, after which he settled there permanently.
story_body: On 8 Tammuz 5699, R. Yosef Avraham Kagan, formerly chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, married in London. He lived in London for the rest of his life.

title_en: Death of R. Yosef Avraham Kagan
summary_en: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan, longtime chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw, passed away in 5737.
story_body: R. Yosef Avraham Kagan, who had served as chief secretary of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw before emigrating to London in 1939, died in 5737 (1977). He had lived out his life in London after his marriage there.

title_en: Severe financial deterioration at Tomchei Temimim Warsaw in summer 1938
summary_en: On erev Shabbat Parshat Shelach 5698, R. Yehuda Eber reported a dire financial situation and a collapsing administrative office.
story_body: By summer 5698, the yeshiva's secretariat was barely functioning. The chief secretary R. Yosef Avraham Kagan was preparing to leave for London, and his colleague R. Moshe Pinchas Katz had married and was no longer working. R. Yehuda Eber lamented to the Rebbe that income had collapsed and no suitable replacements were available.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes about move to Poland for sake of yeshiva
summary_en: On 26 Sivan 5693, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (later the Rebbe) expressing his hope to relocate to Poland to be near the yeshiva.
story_body: After years of failed plans to bring Tomchei Temimim closer to him (Riga in 1931, Otwock in 1931), the Rebbe Rayatz finally decided to move from Riga to Warsaw. In this letter he wrote of his 'innermost yearning' to dwell amid the tent and surroundings of Torah, identifying proximity to the yeshiva as the central motivation for the move.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Rosh Yeshiva to organize Warsaw move
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5693 the Rebbe wrote to Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber urging diligent preparations to relocate the yeshiva.
story_body: With the move to Warsaw finalized, the Rebbe instructed R. Yehuda Eber to seek a suitable courtyard with multiple apartments for the yeshiva and its officials. He emphasized that the relocation was specifically to spread Torah 'in the spirit of Tomchei Temimim of Lubavitch' — not a yeshiva that merely bore the name.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Warsaw and begins Tiku 5694 maamarim
summary_en: Beginning Rosh Hashana 5694, immediately upon arriving in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the Hemshech maamarim 'Tiku 5694'.
story_body: On Rosh Hashana 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz began delivering the long Hemshech 'Tiku' which concluded on Shabbos Parshas Toldos. Talmidim repeated the maamarim, and select students entered the Rebbe's room to chazer them before him. The Rebbe also wrote down the maamarim, which were then copied and studied by the talmidim.

title_en: Secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin reports Rebbe's recovery in Warsaw
summary_en: On 27 Tishrei 5694 the secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote that the Rebbe had returned to himself spiritually now that the yeshiva was near him.
story_body: Feigin reported that during the Yamim Noraim and Sukkos the Rebbe delivered deep Hemshech maamarim of nearly two hours, though it was beyond his strength. Students repeated the maamarim and selected ones entered the Rebbe to chazer them, evoking the atmosphere of Lubavitch twenty years earlier.

title_en: Feigin reports weekly maamarim and chazara in Warsaw
summary_en: On 5 Kislev 5694 Feigin wrote that the Rebbe was saying deep maamarim almost every Shabbos and the students were chazering them with him.
story_body: The secretary described how, with the Rebbe and yeshiva united in Warsaw, the atmosphere of pre-revolution Lubavitch was being restored. Students repeated the maamarim together and entered for chazara before the Rebbe, sometimes feeling as though the past twenty years had not intervened.

title_en: Rosh Yeshiva Eber introduces new written-exam method
summary_en: On 7 Tevet 5694 R. Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe on a new method of examining students with written questions.
story_body: Eber gave the talmidim five questions with about two weeks to answer them; more than ten students responded with mostly accurate answers. The youngest, such as 14-year-old Eliezer Feldberg and Yaakov Falkenfeld, produced especially well-ordered and clear replies. The Rosh Yeshiva planned to pause briefly to avoid pulling students from their regular shiurim.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz reports success of move to Poland
summary_en: On 3 Adar 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yitzchak Horowitz that the move to Poland was bearing good fruit in Torah and avoda.
story_body: The Rebbe summarized the results of relocating his residence to Poland, expressing satisfaction that students of the yeshivos were diligent in their studies. He saw it as fulfillment of the mission set by his father, the Rebbe Rashab.

title_en: Feigin describes Shabbos maamarim and Polish attendees
summary_en: On 9 Iyar 5694 R. Yechezkel Feigin described weekly Shabbos maamarim attended by anash, talmidim and many Polish Jews who had drawn close.
story_body: Feigin wrote that every Shabbos the Rebbe delivered maamarim during Kabbalas Shabbos as in Lubavitch days, students gathered in the morning for chazara, and after mincha talmidim and anash assembled in the Rebbe's beis hamedrash. Many local Polish Jews drew close in order to hear Chassidus.

title_en: Womens committee establishes yeshiva kitchen support
summary_en: On 16 Menachem Av 5694 R. Yehuda Eber reported on the Frauen Komitet, founded by Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, supporting the yeshiva kitchen.
story_body: The womens committee, headed by the Rebbe Rayatzs mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, hired a cook for 40 zloty a month to assist the existing helper. The Rebbetzin personally inspected the kitchen daily, and despite tight conditions almost all needy students were now eating proper meals.

title_en: Rosh Yeshiva examines all students in Warsaw
summary_en: On 15 Menachem Av 5694 R. Yehuda Eber reported he had examined all the preparatory and main yeshiva students with generally good results.
story_body: Eber reported that the spiritual state was good: he had tested the preparatory students and all the classes of the yeshiva. Most students of the yeshiva, particularly the third class, possessed relatively strong knowledge.

title_en: Yeshiva reaches nearly 200 students in winter 5695
summary_en: On 29 Marcheshvan 5695 R. Yehuda Eber reported nearly 200 students enrolled across the yeshivas departments.
story_body: The Rosh Yeshiva detailed enrollment: about 60 in the kibbutz, 30 in the great class, 29 with R. Dovid Teiblum, 23 with R. Zalman Gurary, and nearly 60 at the Zamenhof branch. He noted improvement in chazaras hamaamarim, with nearly all kibbutz students participating.

title_en: Yeshiva enrollment reaches 197 students
summary_en: On 26 Tevet 5695 the Rosh Yeshiva reported total enrollment of 197 students, up from roughly 155-160 the previous summer.
story_body: R. Yehuda Eber sent updated student lists for the hall, classes and branches, noting significant growth in the kibbutz and other departments. He prayed for the financial means to maintain them and thereby improve quality alongside quantity.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz and Tomchei Temimim relocate to Otwock
summary_en: In summer 5695 the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Warsaw to Otwock, and the central Tomchei Temimim yeshiva relocated with him.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz moved his residence to the nearby town of Otwock, and the yeshiva followed into a three-story building at Slowackiego 1. Initially considered temporary (as letterhead reflected), the move soon became permanent, opening the 'golden era' of Tomchei Temimim in Otwock that lasted four years until the war.

title_en: Shmuel Tzvi Fuchs enters Otwock yeshiva after bar mitzva
summary_en: At the end of Elul 5695, immediately after his bar mitzva, Shmuel Tzvi Fuchs arrived to study at Tomchei Temimim in Otwock.
story_body: Fuchs entered the first preparatory class, where nigleh was studied by day and Tanya at night. He would learn there until the outbreak of WWII at the end of 5699, and counted his Tishrei 5696 with the Rebbe as a central experience of his life.

title_en: Group photo of students in Otwock
summary_en: On 18 Tevet 5696 a group photograph was taken of Tomchei Temimim students in Otwock, including R. Moshe Beitch and R. Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel.
story_body: The photograph documents talmidim of Tomchei Temimim at Otwock during the yeshivas Otwock period, including R. Netta Denderowitz of Rika, R. Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel of Warsaw, R. Moshe Beitch of Swierze and R. Moshe Rudnier of Krasne.

title_en: Eber reports Otwock relocation and financial strain
summary_en: On 18 Tevet 5696 R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Yehuda Leib Horowitz in Boston about the move of much of the yeshiva to Otwock.
story_body: Eber described the new building amid a great forest in the best part of Otwock, housing the kibbutz and the two large classes (the two smaller remained in Warsaw as a branch). Hundreds of students were diligent, but the move and renovations had increased expenses while income shrank, exhausting the leaderships endurance.

title_en: Yeshiva refuses new students for summer 5696
summary_en: On 18 Iyar 5696 R. Yehuda Eber wrote that for the first time the yeshiva had publicly announced it would accept no new students due to capacity.
story_body: The Rosh Yeshiva reported it was the first time since Tomchei Temimims founding that they advertised in the press that no new talmidim would be accepted. Dozens of students from across Poland and abroad still came begging entry. The Rebbe Rayatz suffered greatly at having to refuse so many promising bochurim while other major yeshivos shrank to mere dozens of students.

title_en: Rabbi David Meir Rabinowitz visits yeshiva in Otwock
summary_en: On 29 Tammuz 5696 R. Yehuda Eber described the recent visit of Rabbi David Meir Rabinowitz of Boston to the yeshiva.
story_body: Rabinowitz, en route to Eretz Yisrael, stopped at Otwock with his son Peretz and other American travelers. Upon entering the hall where about 70 senior students were learning, he was so overcome with emotion that he sat speechless against the wall for some time. At his farewell gathering he cried out that he had never imagined Tomchei Temimim could be so elevated.

title_en: R. Dovber Garfinkel (Kornitzer) appointed mashgiach in Otwock
summary_en: In 5696 R. Dovber Kornitzer (Garfinkel) fled Russia and was immediately appointed by the Rebbe as general mashgiach and examiner.
story_body: Renowned for knowing Shas by heart and for unusual clarity of explanation, Kornitzer transformed the yeshiva atmosphere from the moment he arrived. He instituted Erev Shabbos chazara of maamarim in the forest surrounding the yeshiva, where chaburos of students sat at fixed tables among tall trees to repeat Chassidus before Kabbalas Shabbos.

title_en: Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky visits Tomchei Temimim
summary_en: During 5696 Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky (Chazon Yechezkel) visited Tomchei Temimim while passing through Poland.
story_body: Abramsky, dayan of the London Beis Din, deliberately detoured to visit the yeshiva and found there about 200 fine bochurim diligently learning Torah and yiras Hashem, all sustained by the yeshivas treasury. A year later, on Lag BaOmer 5697, he publicized this visit in a letter of support urging Jews everywhere to become regular supporters of the yeshiva.

title_en: Abramsky publishes letter of support for Tomchei Temimim
summary_en: On Lag BaOmer 5697 Rabbi Yechezkel Abramsky wrote a public letter calling on all Jews to support Tomchei Temimim regularly.
story_body: Drawing on his personal visit to the yeshiva the previous year, Abramsky testified that seeing is not the same as hearing, and that he found 200 bochurim shokdim on Torah and yiras Hashem. He signed as 'dayan of the Beis Din of London and the country' and promised Hashems blessing in all good for those who became fixed supporters.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz describes Pesach with talmidim in Otwock
summary_en: On 25 Nisan 5698 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (later the Rebbe) about Pesach spent with the talmidim and their teachers.
story_body: Though he had not said Chassidus on the first days, the Rebbe wrote that the Sedarim and Yom Tov meals passed pleasantly and unhurriedly, with talmidim of Tomchei Temimim and their teachers joining. They spent long hours delighting in the goodness of Hashem and in memories of earlier days.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva founded
summary_en: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was founded in Lubavitch.
story_body: In the year 5657 (1897), the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Lubavitch by the Rebbe Rashab. The 40th anniversary of this founding would later be marked in 1937 with a special issue of HaTamim dedicated to the history of the yeshiva.

title_en: First published list of Tomchei Tmimim graduates
summary_en: The first known list of Tomchei Tmimim graduates was published on 14 Tevet 5670.
story_body: On 14 Tevet 5670 (December 26, 1909), a list of Tomchei Tmimim graduates was published — the first such roster of alumni. It was later reprinted in 'MiBeit HaGenazim' and represents the earliest documented effort to catalog the yeshiva's students.

title_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik born in Minsk
summary_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik was born in Minsk on 19 Cheshvan 5673.
story_body: R. Mordechai Mentlik was born in Minsk on 19 Cheshvan 5673 (October 30, 1912). He later studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw from 1925, was selected to study in Riga in 1931, and became a maggid shiur in the preparatory program in 1934.

title_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz born in Poland
summary_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was born in Kintsk, Poland in 5673.
story_body: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was born in Kintsk, Poland in 5673 (1912-1913). He studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw from 1925 to 1933 and then served as a maggid shiur in the preparatory program in Warsaw and worked in the yeshiva office.

title_en: R. David Stockhamer arrives in United States
summary_en: R. David Stockhamer arrived in the US with his wife and three daughters around 5680.
story_body: Around 5680 (1919-1920), the chassid R. David Stockhamer arrived in the United States with his wife and three daughters and settled in Newark, New Jersey. He later became distressed at the lack of suitable chassidic young men for his daughters in America, leading him to consult the Rebbe Rayatz.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim founded in Warsaw
summary_en: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Warsaw in 5681.
story_body: In 5681 (1920-1921), the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was established in Warsaw, Poland. This Polish branch would later become the central yeshiva after the Rebbe Rayatz settled in Poland, growing to include multiple branches across Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz orders comprehensive alumni list
summary_en: On 18 Shevat 5684 the Rebbe Rayatz instructed R. Sholom Dovber Halevin to prepare a list of all Tomchei Tmimim students from 1897-1924.
story_body: On 18 Shevat 5684 (January 24, 1924), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Sholom Dovber Halevin requesting a comprehensive list of all yeshiva students from Tomchei Tmimim and its branches — Lubavitch, Zembin, Kovlitz, Horodishtz, Shchedrin, Romny, Cherson, Hebron, Kremenchug, Poltava, Warsaw, Kutaisi, Nevel, and Jerusalem — from 5657 to 5684. A mimeographed list was reportedly prepared in Rostov-Leningrad, though no copies have been found.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz orders Polish yeshivot alumni list
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz directed the preparation of an alumni list of the yeshivot in Poland in 5691.
story_body: In 5691 (1930-1931), the Rebbe Rayatz directed the preparation of a list of graduates of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshivot in Poland. Unlike the earlier lists, this one was apparently not intended for publication and remained an internal record.

title_en: Central yeshiva moves to Otwock
summary_en: The central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva relocated from Warsaw to Otwock in 5696.
story_body: In 5696 (1935-1936), the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva (with the older students) moved from Warsaw to Otwock, a resort town and known recuperative location near the Polish capital. Three lower classes remained in Warsaw, while the central yeshiva occupied several buildings in a healthful pine forest setting in Otwock.

title_en: R. Yehuda Eber writes about student Moshe Pinchas Katz
summary_en: On 29 Tammuz 5696, Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Avraham Ziskind about efforts to arrange entry papers for R. Moshe Pinchas Katz to the US.
story_body: On 29 Tammuz 5696 (July 19, 1936), Rosh Yeshiva R. Yehuda Eber wrote to R. Avraham Ziskind regarding their student Moshe Pinchas Katz, noting they were doing everything possible — and more than was within their means — to help him. The letter was part of efforts to arrange a shidduch with one of R. David Stockhamer's daughters and secure US entry papers.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim class photographs taken at Otwock
summary_en: At the beginning of 5697, class photographs were taken of all Tomchei Tmimim students and staff in Otwock and Warsaw.
story_body: At the beginning of 5697 (autumn 1936), class photographs were taken of every student of the yeshiva — both those in the main study hall and classes at Otwock and those in the preparatory program in Warsaw — along with every member of the yeshiva staff. The photo also included images of the yeshiva buildings in Otwock, which the yeshiva had entered at the beginning of 5696.

title_en: Warsaw rabbis sign support letter for yeshiva
summary_en: In autumn 5697, members of the Warsaw rabbinical council signed a letter of support for Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: On the Sunday of parshat Haazinu 5697 (autumn 1936), a portion of the rabbis of the Warsaw rabbinical council signed a letter of support for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva. A similar letter would be issued by the full council in Kislev 5698.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz proposes 40th anniversary HaTamim issue
summary_en: In early summer 5697, the future Rebbe (Ramash) proposed to his father-in-law that HaTamim's 12 Tammuz issue commemorate Tomchei Tmimim's 40th anniversary.
story_body: At the beginning of summer 5697 (1937), the future Rebbe (Ramash, the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law) wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz proposing that since summer marked the 40-year anniversary of Tomchei Tmimim's founding, the upcoming 12 Tammuz issue of HaTamim should be dedicated to the yeshiva's history with special material. He also urged that a list of all yeshiva students throughout the years be published in time for the jubilee.

title_en: HaTamim issue 7 published for 40th anniversary
summary_en: The 7th issue of HaTamim was dedicated to the 40th anniversary of Tomchei Tmimim's founding.
story_body: On 12 Tammuz 5697 (June 21, 1937), the 7th issue of HaTamim was published, dedicated to the 40-year jubilee of the founding of Tomchei Tmimim in 5657. The issue began a series of articles on the founding, purpose, development, and growth of the yeshiva, with promises of more letters and essays in future issues.

title_en: Opportunity to purchase yeshiva building arises
summary_en: At the beginning of Tishrei 5698, an opportunity arose to purchase the entire yeshiva building in Otwock.
story_body: At the beginning of Tishrei 5698 (autumn 1937), an opportunity arose to purchase the entire building housing the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Otwock. The building cost more than the Rebbe Rayatz's available means, and he decided to organize a special fundraising campaign among Chabad chassidim in the United States and the Land of Israel.

title_en: R. Feigin writes Tel Aviv Chabad about building purchase
summary_en: On 28 Tishrei 5698, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the heads of the Chabad community in Tel Aviv about the urgent need to purchase the yeshiva building.
story_body: On 28 Tishrei 5698 (October 3, 1937), secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the heads of the Chabad community in Tel Aviv urging quick action on the building purchase. He explained that the Rebbe Rayatz had departed from his usual practice and personally assigned set sums to each chassid and student as founding members of the campaign.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes Cramer about building purchase
summary_en: On 12 Cheshvan 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Chaim Shneur Zalman Cramer, chairman of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in the US, about purchasing the yeshiva building.
story_body: On 12 Cheshvan 5698 (October 17, 1937), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Chaim Shneur Zalman Cramer, chairman of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in the United States. He explained that for over a month he had decided that it was essential to purchase a building and courtyard for the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva, and that thank G-d a suitable opportunity had arisen.

title_en: Warsaw rabbis issue support letter for Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: On 10 Kislev 5698, the Council of Rabbis of Warsaw issued a letter of support for the yeshiva.
story_body: On 10 Kislev 5698 (November 14, 1937), members of the Council of Rabbis of Warsaw issued a letter of support praising Tomchei Tmimim as one of the most exalted Torah institutions in the world. They noted that they had personally tested many of the students, were amazed by their sharpness and erudition, and had granted them rabbinical ordination. The letter stated that seven branches of the yeshiva operated in Poland with nearly 700 students in total.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes about house and library near yeshiva
summary_en: On 3 Shevat 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson about the urgent need to purchase a residence and space for the library adjacent to the yeshiva.
story_body: On 3 Shevat 5698 (January 5, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson explaining the urgency of purchasing a residence for himself and the library, both for health reasons and for the inner workings of his activities. He stressed it must be adjacent to the yeshiva — courtyard next to courtyard — since he had moved from Riga to Poland only for the yeshiva's sake.

title_en: R. Feigin summarizes Rebbe Rayatz's chassidus discourses
summary_en: On 15 Shevat 5698, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Sholom Posner summarizing the Rebbe Rayatz's recent activities.
story_body: On 15 Shevat 5698 (January 17, 1938), secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to his brother-in-law R. Sholom Posner reporting that until 19 Kislev the Rebbe Rayatz had delivered chassidus on every Shabbat as usual, but only before a small group of about 20-30 yeshiva students who rotated each Shabbat. Feigin also noted that the Rebbe had spoken at the beginning of Kislev about the need to travel to a sanatorium to renew medical treatment.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes Ramash about transferring funds
summary_en: On 23 Shevat 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law in Paris about transferring 10,000 zloty for the yeshiva building.
story_body: On 23 Shevat 5698 (January 25, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (the future Rebbe, Ramash, in Paris) inquiring about the most economical way to transfer 10,000 zloty to his Warsaw account — whether by purchasing a bank check or direct transfer. Due to Polish currency restrictions, all support funds were routed to the Rebbe Rayatz through his son-in-law in Paris.

title_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik marries Gittel Stockhamer
summary_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik married Gittel Stockhamer on Isru Chag Shavuos 5698.
story_body: On Isru Chag Shavuos 5698 (7 Sivan, June 6, 1938), R. Mordechai Mentlik married Gittel Stockhamer, one of the daughters of R. David Stockhamer of Newark. The Rosh Yeshiva and the Rebbe Rayatz's secretaries — R. Yechezkel Feigin, R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein, and board member R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov — participated in the wedding and the sheva brachos.

title_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz marries Mindel Stockhamer
summary_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz married Mindel Stockhamer on 15 Sivan 5698 at the Rebbe's residence in Otwock.
story_body: On 15 Sivan 5698 (June 14, 1938), R. Moshe Pinchas Katz married Mindel Stockhamer at the building where the Rebbe Rayatz resided in Otwock — Prusa Street 6, as specified on the invitation. The Rosh Yeshiva, secretaries, and close friends of the groom participated in both the wedding and the sheva brachos.

title_en: R. Geleshrtein writes about new student Preger
summary_en: On 4 Iyar 5698, R. A.M. Gelershtein from Brisk wrote about a new candidate, Preger, seeking to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
story_body: On 4 Iyar 5698 (May 5, 1938), R. Avraham Mordechai Gelershtein of Brisk wrote to yeshiva secretary R. Yosef Avraham Kagan urging acceptance of the student Menachem Nachum Preger of Brisk, describing him as an outstanding talmid with fine character and talent. Preger was accepted, studied in Otwock until the war's outbreak, later escaped to Vilna and then Japan and Shanghai, and ultimately reached New York.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes Jacobson about sons-in-law visas
summary_en: On 18 Av 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote R. Israel Jacobson urging help to obtain US visas for the new sons-in-law of R. David Stockhamer.
story_body: On 18 Av 5698 (August 15, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson, director of Aguch in America, urging him out of inner love to help obtain US entry visas for both of R. David Stockhamer's new sons-in-law — R. Mordechai Mentlik and R. Moshe Pinchas Katz — so they could settle near him in Newark, 'a good place for a ben Torah.'

title_en: R. Feigin writes Jacobson about renewed building plans
summary_en: On 9 Tammuz 5698, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote R. Israel Jacobson that talks had resumed about purchasing the yeshiva building.
story_body: On 9 Tammuz 5698 (July 8, 1938), secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Israel Jacobson, director of Aguch in America, that after a long silence concerning the purchase of the yeshiva property — for various reasons the discussion had been suspended — by the Rebbe Rayatz's will, talks had been renewed to bring the purchase closer to fruition.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz on building purchase obstacle
summary_en: On 19 Tammuz 5698, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson about the obstacle to the building purchase.
story_body: On 19 Tammuz 5698 (July 18, 1938), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson that the obstacle to advancing the yeshiva building purchase was the lack of approved bylaws for Agudas Chabad from the US government and the Polish consul in New York. Only once these were approved could the building be purchased in Aguch's name.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes Ramash about renting Gelbfish building
summary_en: On 15 Iyar 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote his son-in-law about renting the Gelbfish building for the yeshiva.
story_body: On 15 Iyar 5699 (May 4, 1939), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to his son-in-law (Ramash) about a strong possibility of renting a spacious residence in the courtyard adjacent to his own home — the Gelbfish pension with about forty rooms and large halls. The plan required a two-year-plus lease at 8,000 zloty per year paid in advance, totaling nearly 18,000 zloty, to be financed from funds collected by R. M.D. — but a few months later the war erupted and all plans came to a halt.

title_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz writes about visa difficulties
summary_en: On 11 Adar 5699, R. Moshe Pinchas Katz wrote about his ongoing difficulties obtaining a US visa.
story_body: On 11 Adar 5699 (March 2, 1939), R. Moshe Pinchas Katz wrote to R. Yosef Avraham Kagan about the difficulty of obtaining a US visa. He had visited the consulate the previous week with an American yeshiva student, hoping that the citizen sponsor might receive favorable consideration, and the consul had promised a quick response, but the waiting was agonizing.

title_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz departs for United States
summary_en: On 7 Iyar 5699, secretary Nissan Mindel reported that R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was departing for London en route to the US.
story_body: On 7 Iyar 5699 (April 26, 1939), secretary Nissan Mindel wrote to R. Yosef Avraham Kagan in London that R. Moshe Pinchas Katz was departing that day for London on his way to America. R. Mentlik later confirmed on 23 Iyar (May 12) that he had received a telegram on Tuesday that his brother-in-law had arrived safely.

title_en: R. Mentlik to receive visa
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5699, secretary R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein wrote that R. Mordechai Mentlik would receive his visa the next day.
story_body: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5699 (August 15, 1939), secretary R. Moshe Leib Rotshtein wrote to R. Yosef Avraham Kagan that R. Mordechai Mentlik would receive his visa in practice the next day. With the war breaking out only weeks later, this was among the final pieces of correspondence from Otwock's yeshiva administration.

title_en: Final photograph of students learning at Otwock
summary_en: On 10 Av 5699, a photograph was taken of students learning at the Gelbfish pension, likely the last picture of Tomchei Tmimim students at Otwock.
story_body: On 10 Av 5699 (July 26, 1939), approximately one month before the outbreak of World War II, a photograph was taken at the Gelbfish pension showing yeshiva students learning sugyot together in the courtyard. R. Yosef Rodal sat at the center. The photograph was sent to R. Moshe Pinchas Katz, who had recently emigrated to America, and is likely the last image of Tomchei Tmimim students learning in Otwock.

title_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik arrives in United States
summary_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik arrived in the United States in Tishrei 5700.
story_body: R. Mordechai Mentlik arrived in the United States in Tishrei 5700 (September-October 1939), having received his US visa at the beginning of Elul 5699 just before the outbreak of war. He later served as the senior rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim in New York and was a member of the Aguch executive.

title_en: Achei Tmimim yeshiva founded in Newark
summary_en: R. Mentlik and R. Katz founded the Achei Tmimim yeshiva in Newark in 5702.
story_body: In 5702 (1941-1942), R. Mordechai Mentlik and R. Moshe Pinchas Katz — both living in Newark and commuting daily to their yeshiva work in New York — founded the Achei Tmimik yeshiva in Newark, New Jersey. They continued to reside in Newark until 5706, when they moved to New York.

title_en: R. Avraham Ziskind passes away
summary_en: R. Avraham Zushe Ziskind passed away in New York on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5727.
story_body: R. Avraham Zushe Ziskind passed away in New York on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5727 (April 11, 1967). After his marriage he had served as a shochet in New York, engaging extensively in halacha and chassidus, and in his final years headed the avreichim kollel attached to the Rebbe's secretariat.

title_en: R. Menachem Nachum Preger passes away
summary_en: R. Menachem Nachum Preger of Brisk passed away in 5741.
story_body: R. Menachem Nachum Preger passed away in 5741 (1980-1981). Originally from Brisk, he had been accepted to Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock in 5698, fled to Vilna at the war's outbreak, and was saved with the group of students who traveled to Japan, Shanghai, and eventually New York.

title_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz passes away
summary_en: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz passed away in New York on Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5746.
story_body: R. Moshe Pinchas Katz passed away in New York on Erev Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5746 (March 11, 1986). He had served as a gabbai of the 770 synagogue and a member of the executive of Agudas Chassidei Chabad, Vaad HaMesader, Vaad LeHafatzas Chassidus, Vaad HaMaamad, and Vaad Kupas Bachurim.

title_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik passes away
summary_en: R. Mordechai Mentlik passed away in New York on 25 Tishrei 5748.
story_body: R. Mordechai Mentlik passed away in New York on 25 Tishrei 5748 (October 18, 1987). He was the author of the work Amrei Mordechai and served as a member of the executive of Agudas Chassidei Chabad. Beginning when the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in New York and opened Tomchei Tmimim there, R. Mentlik served as the senior rosh yeshiva.

title_en: Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim report lists over 700 students across branches
summary_en: On 7 Tishrei 5699, the Yeshiva administration issued a report stating that over 700 students were enrolled across the central Yeshiva in Otwock, the preparatory school in Warsaw, and branches in various towns.
story_body: The letter from the Yeshiva leadership in early Tishrei 5699 (October 2, 1938) summarized the scope of Tomchei Tmimim under the previous Rebbe (Rayatz). It reported that the institution had become world-renowned, producing thousands of Torah scholars, and that more than 700 students were currently being educated and supported through the central yeshiva and its many branches.

title_en: Rashag named president of Tomchei Tmimim executive board
summary_en: Beginning in 5699, Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary (the Rashag), son-in-law of the Rebbe Rayatz, served as president of the Yeshiva's executive committee.
story_body: After a brief earlier involvement in 5691, the Rashag returned to active leadership of Tomchei Tmimim in 5699. Letters from this year, written on the Yeshiva's stationery, identify him as president of the executive board. By Adar 5699 he was taking part in all of the Yeshiva's operations, with all expenditures passing through him.

title_en: Rashag begins teaching Chassidus to Tomchei Tmimim students
summary_en: In the early months of 5699, the Rashag began regularly speaking with the Yeshiva students about Chassidic teachings.
story_body: Rabbi Yisrael Yaakov Yeber, the rosh yeshiva, reported at the start of the year that the Rashag had recently begun speaking with the talmidim in Chassidus. The Rashag came to regard one of the senior students, Mendel Tenenboim, as outstanding among the talmidim.

title_en: Wedding of Shlomo Zalman Hecht, son-in-law of Rabbi Jacobson
summary_en: On 3 Elul 5698, Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Hecht married the daughter of Rabbi Israel Jacobson in New York before traveling to study at the Otwock yeshiva.
story_body: Rabbi Israel Jacobson, head of Achei Tmimim in America, arranged that immediately after his daughter's wedding on 3 Elul 5698, the young couple would travel to Poland so the groom could study in Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock. This had been approved in advance by the Rebbe Rayatz, and the trip was made with great fanfare.

title_en: Feigin confirms plan for Hecht couple to travel to Otwock
summary_en: On 6 Elul 5698, the Rebbe's secretary Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin wrote to Rabbi Jacobson promising to help arrange his son-in-law's arrival in Otwock.
story_body: Following the Hecht wedding, secretary Feigin wrote that he would do everything possible to assist the young couple's transition to Poland and would press the Yeshiva administration to give special attention to the new student arriving from America.

title_en: Shlomo Zalman Hecht and wife arrive in Otwock
summary_en: By 12 Tishrei 5699, Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Hecht and his wife had arrived in Otwock to begin his studies at Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Rabbi Feigin reported to Rabbi Jacobson on 12 Tishrei 5699 that his daughter and son-in-law had arrived safely. Because they came right before Yom Tov, they initially stayed at a pension, but the Rebbe Rayatz advised them to find their own apartment for both material and spiritual reasons.

title_en: Hecht couple rents apartment near Rebbe's secretary in Otwock
summary_en: By 26 Tishrei 5699, the Hechts had rented an apartment in the same courtyard where Rabbi Feigin and the Rebbetzin lived in Otwock.
story_body: Following the Rebbe Rayatz's advice, the young couple moved out of the pension and rented an apartment in the courtyard where the Rebbe's secretary and the Rebbetzin also lived. The arrangement was deemed beneficial both for the wife, who would not be alone while her husband studied, and for the young couple's domestic guidance.

title_en: Jacobson writes Rebbe about two students preparing to travel to Otwock
summary_en: On 7 Cheshvan 5699, Rabbi Jacobson informed the Rebbe Rayatz that two students, Abraham Menachem Mendel Barnetzky and Dovber Levy, would soon travel to study at Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Jacobson described both students positively: Barnetzky as a deep, hard-working chossid, and the 17-year-old Levy as exceptionally gifted, a nephew of the chassid 'Reb Avraham Dov the Malach.' Levy had only joined Achei Tmimim months earlier but Jacobson believed he could become 'a beautiful vessel.'

title_en: Barnetzky and Levy arrive at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock
summary_en: On 17 Cheshvan 5699, the two American students Abraham Barnetzky and Dovber Levy arrived unexpectedly at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
story_body: The two students sailed on the Queen Mary shortly after Sukkos 5699 and arrived in Otwock without prior notice. Rabbi Feigin wrote to Jacobson that the administration had been unprepared and noted that American students could not be sustained on the same austere terms as the local talmidim, requiring special attention both materially and spiritually.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Jacobson to send Achei Tmimim students to Otwock
summary_en: On 12 Kislev 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote Rabbi Jacobson instructing him to send Achei Tmimim students to Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock as the foundation for a future American yeshiva.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz directed Jacobson 'to make efforts to send students from Achei Tmimim to the Tomchei Tmimim Yeshiva in Otwock,' adding that with God's help this would become the seed for establishing a yeshiva in their own country in the spirit of Tomchei Tmimim. This shaped subsequent travel plans for additional groups.

title_en: Jacobson outlines plan for new group of students to travel to Otwock
summary_en: On 9 Adar 5699, Rabbi Jacobson wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz detailing plans to send another group of American students to study at Otwock.
story_body: Jacobson's letter outlined which talmidim from Achei Tmimim were prepared to travel to Poland. The Rebbe Rayatz responded on 28 Adar that he was too busy to reply at length and would answer in due time, beginning a months-long planning process for the trip.

title_en: Feigin updates Jacobson on planning for second American student group
summary_en: On 4 Tammuz 5699, Rabbi Feigin conveyed the Rebbe's response that doubled the proposed group size and set the stay at two years.
story_body: Feigin wrote that the Rebbe Rayatz, comparing Jacobson's proposed five talmidim with what the Rebbe's own secretariat had suggested, was prepared for double that number, to study in Otwock for two years. Jacobson then began final arrangements to escort the group personally to Poland.

title_en: Feigin reports on Hecht's studies and difficulties of distance in Otwock
summary_en: On 17 Tammuz 5699, Rabbi Feigin updated Jacobson about his son-in-law's studies in Otwock, noting both progress and challenges.
story_body: Feigin wrote that although Hecht's learning was now well arranged, the physical distance between home and yeshiva remained difficult. Hecht traveled early each morning to the yeshiva, where he learned Chassidus and prayed before turning to nigleh.

title_en: Jacobson sets August departure date for next group to Otwock
summary_en: On 2 Menachem Av 5699, Rabbi Jacobson wrote to Rabbi Yehuda Leib Horowitz of Boston announcing his departure to the Rebbe Rayatz with a group of students.
story_body: Jacobson informed Horowitz that he would sail on Erev Shabbos Parshas Eikev, 19 Menachem Av (August 4, 1939), to travel to the Rebbe in Otwock with some of his talmidim. The original date was ultimately postponed.

title_en: Jacobson sails for Poland with six Achei Tmimim students on Île de France
summary_en: On 23 Menachem Av 5699 (August 8, 1939), Rabbi Jacobson set sail on the Île de France with six Achei Tmimim students bound for Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
story_body: The group included Mordechai Dov Altein, Meir Greenberg, Avraham Dovber Hecht, Yitzchak Kalodny, Zerach Gordon, and Mordechai Fisher, intending to study in Poland for two years. They traveled by train through France, Belgium, and Germany after disembarking, reaching Otwock at the start of Elul.

title_en: Six American students arrive at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Elul 5699, Rabbi Jacobson and the six American talmidim arrived in Otwock to begin their studies.
story_body: Met in Paris by the Rebbe's son-in-law (the future Rebbe), the group continued by train through Europe, arriving at the Yeshiva on Rosh Chodesh Elul. Rabbi Shmuel Dovid Reitchik was the first to engage them in learning, and they were tested in both nigleh and Chassidus by Rabbi Berel Kornitzer.

title_en: American students hear Maamar Shoftim and have first yechidus with Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: On 3 Elul 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered Maamar Shoftim and admitted the newly-arrived American talmidim to their first yechidus.
story_body: Two days after their arrival, on Friday 3 Elul (Parshas Shoftim), the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Shoftim v'shotrim titen lecha b'chol she'arecha,' which was then repeated by the chozer Rabbi Mordechai Mentlik before his own departure to America. That night a farbrengen was held in Shlomo Zalman Hecht's home led by Rabbi Yechezkel Feigin.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes son-in-law about Jacobson's arrival with students
summary_en: On 3 Elul 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote his son-in-law (the future Rebbe) that Rabbi Jacobson had arrived in Otwock with six new students.
story_body: The Rebbe wrote that he had been busy since Jacobson's arrival answering hundreds of letters the latter had brought from America. He also directed that two hundred copies of Rabbi Simpson's sefer be given to Jacobson to take back.

title_en: Jacobson holds farewell yechidus before returning to America
summary_en: On 14 Elul 5699, Rabbi Jacobson had yechidus with the Rebbe Rayatz before departing back to the United States from Poland.
story_body: During this final yechidus Jacobson asked what answer to give the parents of the talmidim he had escorted from America. The Rebbe replied that whatever would happen to all the talmidim would also happen to them, but added that as American citizens they could always escape to Riga.

title_en: World War II begins; Rebbe Rayatz directs American talmidim to Warsaw and Riga
summary_en: On 17 Elul 5699 (1 September 1939), with the outbreak of World War II, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed the American talmidim to leave Otwock for Warsaw and continue on to Riga before Shabbos.
story_body: On Friday morning the students heard the roar of aircraft and bombings begin. The Rebbe Rayatz called them in to yechidus, told them to travel calmly to Warsaw and then on to Riga 'to my Chassidim,' where Rabbi Mordechai Chefetz would arrange their studies in nigleh and Chassidus until the storm passed. Meir Greenberg was given a private mission to communicate with Mordechai Dubin in Riga regarding a Latvian visa for the Rebbe.

title_en: American talmidim arrive in Riga and cable Agudas Chabad
summary_en: On 20 Elul 5699, the group of American students arrived safely in Riga from war-torn Poland and cabled Agudas Chabad in New York.
story_body: After spending Shabbos in Warsaw with help from the Joint and the American consulate, the talmidim continued to Riga, where they sent a cable to Agudas Chabad in New York reading: 'Arrived safely Riga out of danger. Rabbi well Otwock.' The signatories were the three Hechts, Barnetzky, Levy, Kalodny, Gordon, Greenberg, Fisher, and Altein.

title_en: American talmidim study in Riga under Rabbi Itche Masmid
summary_en: Following their flight from Otwock, the American students remained in Riga to continue their studies through mid-Tishrei 5700.
story_body: During Chol HaMoed Sukkos the group decided to remain in Riga as long as possible to fulfill their original purpose of intensive study. Rabbi Yitzchak the Masmid taught them Likkutei Torah, another chossid taught them Tanya in the evenings, and Rabbi Mordechai Dubin paid for their lodging.

title_en: Zerach Gordon and Hecht couple arrive in Stockholm en route to New York
summary_en: On 19 Tishrei 5700, Zerach Gordon and Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Hecht and his wife arrived in Stockholm after a 36-hour sea voyage from Riga.
story_body: After a difficult ship journey, the small group reached Stockholm on the second day of Chol HaMoed Sukkos. From there they planned to continue to New York, separate from the remaining seven talmidim who left Riga later. In Stockholm they were assisted by Rabbi Yisrael Zuber, who arranged food, lodging, and a place to learn in the synagogue.

title_en: American talmidim return to New York from Stockholm
summary_en: On 22 Cheshvan 5700, the remaining seven American talmidim arrived back in New York after some weeks in Stockholm.
story_body: Following Zerach Gordon and the Hechts, the rest of the group sailed from Stockholm to America. They reached New York on 22 Cheshvan 5700, ending their abbreviated study mission in Europe.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes returned talmidim from Riga after escaping besieged Warsaw
summary_en: On 14 Teves 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the American talmidim from Riga after his escape from the siege of Warsaw.
story_body: The Rebbe described how during the siege he had worried about them, repeatedly asking the American consul in Warsaw for news. Only on reaching Riga did he learn that they had returned safely home, and he thanked God 'for His kindness endures forever.'

title_en: Mechina preparatory division founded at Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw
summary_en: Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw opened a new Mechina division for bar-mitzvah-age students at the start of 5692.
story_body: After deliberations through summer 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz decided in Tishrei 5692 to keep the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Warsaw and add a Mechina branch for younger students. Classes opened on Sunday of Parshat Vayera with 10–11 boys, supplementing the existing two shiurim for ages 14–17 and the senior Olam for self-learners. Initial enrollment was limited because the new program was announced late.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber reports founding of Mechina to the Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: On 28 Marcheshvan 5692 rosh yeshiva R' Yehuda Eber wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz confirming the Mechina had begun functioning.
story_body: R' Yehuda Eber's report described 10–11 boys learning in the new Mechina, attributing low initial numbers to short notice. He predicted growth in subsequent terms. By 20 Kislev there were 13 talmidim, and from 3 Tevet R' Moshe Chaim was teaching them Tanya daily.

title_en: R' Schneur Zalman Gourary appointed maggid shiur of upper Mechina class
summary_en: At the start of 5693 R' Schneur Zalman Gourary became maggid shiur for the upper Mechina class in Warsaw.
story_body: R' Yehuda Eber reported to the Rebbe Rayatz on 7 Marcheshvan 5693 that R' Schneur Zalman Gourary would teach the upper Mechina class while R' Moshe Meirowitz continued the lower class. The two Mechina classes at the Agudas Chabad shul on Dzika 8 had grown to about 50 students.

title_en: Third Mechina class added; classes split between Twarda and Zamenhof
summary_en: By 7 Tevet 5694 the Mechina had grown to three classes spread between Twarda and Zamenhof Street locations.
story_body: Class A learned at Twarda (Proste 10) and Classes B–C at Zamenhof 8. R' Yehuda Eber reported tighter admissions standards had slightly lowered numbers but expected the Twarda branch to grow. Around the same time R' Mordechai Mentlik joined the staff as maggid shiur for the youngest class.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz blesses founding of Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim
summary_en: On 28 Iyar 5694 the Rebbe Rayatz approved an alumni association of Tomchei Tmimim graduates.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz blessed the proposal from former students to form a network for Tomchei Tmimim alumni. Headed by R' Schneur Zalman Gourary, the Agudah set up offices at Moranowski 7/9 in Warsaw — the same address as the Rebbe's beit midrash. Its aims included disseminating Chassidus and helping members secure rabbinic, shochet, and commercial positions.

title_en: Founding convention of Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim in Warsaw
summary_en: About 100 alumni gathered at the Rebbe Rayatz's Warsaw beit midrash on 3 Tishrei 5695 to formally inaugurate Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim.
story_body: The convention drew Tmimim from Poland and abroad to the beit midrash at Moranowski 7/9. The assembly elected R' Shmaryahu Gourary as chairman and R' Schneur Zalman Gourary as director, with R' Moshe P. Katz as secretary. The agenda included Chassidic outreach, member assistance with placements, and a charter for the Agudah.

title_en: First issue of HaTamim journal printed in Warsaw
summary_en: The first issue of HaTamim, the Chabad journal of Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim, was completed at the end of Menachem Av 5695.
story_body: On 20 Menachem Av 5695 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote that HaTamim was ready for press. Its formal editors were R' Yechezkel Feigin and R' Yehuda Eber, with R' Shmuel Zalmanov as general editor, but in practice the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law (later the Rebbe) in Paris substantially edited and annotated the material. R' Schneur Zalman Gourary oversaw publication on behalf of the Agudah.

title_en: Main yeshiva moves from Warsaw to Otwock; Mechina remains in Warsaw
summary_en: At the start of 5696 the senior division of Tomchei Tmimim relocated to Otwock while the three Mechina classes stayed in Warsaw.
story_body: The Olam and two upper classes moved to Otwock, leaving roughly 60 Mechina talmidim in Warsaw under R' Schneur Zalman Gourary and R' Moshe Pinchas Katz. The Mechina initially stayed at the Agudas Chabad shul at Zamenhof 8, then later relocated to the Shmotkin family compound at Moranowska 32 when a third class was added.

title_en: Bar mitzvah of Shalom Dovber Gourary, grandson of the Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz farbrenged with Tomchei Tmimim talmidim in Otwock on 25 Shevat 5696 to mark the bar mitzvah of his grandson.
story_body: The celebration was held in the yeshiva hall at Otwock, drawing guests from Poland, Riga, Vienna and elsewhere. Sichos delivered at the farbrengen were later printed in Likkutei Dibburim vol. 2. A surviving photograph shows the Rebbe Rayatz at the head table with the bar mitzvah boy, his father R' Shmaryahu Gourary, and the Rebbe's secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin.

title_en: R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman appointed maggid shiur in Warsaw Mechina
summary_en: Around Pesach 5697 R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman, then about 18, was appointed maggid shiur in the Warsaw Mechina.
story_body: After three years in the Olam, R' Heshel Reizman was called in spring 5697 to teach the junior Mechina class alongside R' Schneur Zalman Gourary, who led the upper class. When Gourary later left the yeshiva, Reizman took over the upper class and R' Yitzchak Hendel filled the junior position. Reizman remained in his hometown of Suchedniow when WWII broke out and survived the war.

title_en: Publication of HaTamim journal halted by outbreak of WWII
summary_en: Publication of HaTamim ceased at the end of 5699 when WWII broke out, after eight issues had appeared.
story_body: From the first issue in late summer 5695 through the eighth issue in winter 5699, the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law in Paris had continued to substantively edit HaTamim under cover of named Warsaw editors. The outbreak of war in autumn 5699 ended the journal's run; Agudas Talmidei HaTmimim had also been publishing Likkutei Dibburim, the Megillas Yud-Tes Kislev, and a Tehillim compilation under R' Schneur Zalman Gourary's direction.

title_en: R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman passes away
summary_en: R' Yehoshua Heshel Reizman, former maggid shiur of the Warsaw Mechina, died on 10 Tevet 5769.
story_body: Born on 1 Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5678 in Wodzislaw and raised in Suchedniow, R' Heshel Reizman studied at Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw from 5692, taught in its Mechina from spring 5697, and survived WWII. He passed away on 10 Tevet 5769. A short biography appears at the start of his sefer Iyunim B'Ta'aniyos.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Otwock
summary_en: A preparatory branch of Tomchei Tmimim was founded in Otwock in 5686 (1926).
story_body: Founded by R. Meir Blizinski shortly after his wedding, the Otwock branch opened after Pesach 5686 with three classes meeting at Beis Medrash Rindorf. It served as a feeder yeshiva for the central Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw, but lasted only one year before closing in spring 5687 (1927) due to funding cuts.

title_en: R. Meir Blizinski marries on 1 Nisan
summary_en: R. Meir Blizinski married on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5686, the day he turned nineteen.
story_body: In a letter dated 13 Shevat 5737 to his grandson R. S. Heber, Blizinski recalled marrying on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5686 at age nineteen. Soon after, he moved to Otwock and resolved to establish a yeshiva there, which became the first Tomchei Tmimim branch outside Warsaw.

title_en: Otwock yeshiva opens after Pesach with three classes
summary_en: The Otwock yeshiva opened immediately after Pesach 5686 with three classes at Beis Medrash Rindorf.
story_body: R. Meir Blizinski enlisted a local bachur named Naftali Tzuker, who already had a small study group, and added two additional classes. Blizinski personally taught Tanya nightly to the upper class while shouldering most of the budget from his dowry savings and the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim leadership.

title_en: Warsaw leadership absorbs Otwock yeshiva as Tomchei Tmimim branch
summary_en: In Elul 5686, the Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim hanhalah visited Otwock and formally adopted the yeshiva as a branch.
story_body: R. Feivel Zalmanov, R. Zalman Shmuktin and R. Tzvi Gurary HY"D came to Otwock on a Shabbos in Elul 5686, informed the teachers the yeshiva was now Tomchei Tmimim Otwock, and planned to bring in around twenty out-of-town students. R. Chaim Meir Liss was sent as mashpia while Blizinski remained gashmi administrator handling salaries, lodging and meals.

title_en: Otwock branch closes after one year
summary_en: The Otwock branch closed before Pesach 5687 after the American Relief organization cut funding to Polish yeshivos.
story_body: By spring 5687 the Relief organization had stopped supporting Polish yeshivos, claiming Polish Jewry could sustain them itself. Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim could only fund a reduced two-class operation in Otwock with lowered salaries; Blizinski withdrew, and no Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva existed in Otwock until the central yeshiva relocated there in 5696 (1936).

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Vilna
summary_en: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Vilna in 5687 (1927).
story_body: The Vilna branch joined a growing network of provincial Tomchei Tmimim preparatory yeshivos feeding into the central yeshiva in Warsaw. It would become one of the longest-lasting and most prominent branches, eventually serving as the refuge point when Polish branches collapsed at the outbreak of WWII.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Lodz
summary_en: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Lodz in 5689 (1929).
story_body: Added to the growing network of provincial preparatory yeshivos, Lodz grew into one of the largest branches with two classes by 5695 and roughly 150 students before the war. It remained a central pillar of Chabad education in Poland until the Nazi invasion forced its collapse.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Chmielnik
summary_en: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Chmielnik in 5690 (1930).
story_body: Chmielnik joined Warsaw, Vilna and Lodz in the expanding Tomchei Tmimim provincial network. It remained active through the late 1930s and was repeatedly listed among the network's stable branches in official accountings.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branches founded in Patzanow, Riga, Kovel, Baranowicze
summary_en: Four new Tomchei Tmimim branches opened in 5692 (1932) in Patzanow, Riga, Kovel and Baranowicze.
story_body: While Patzanow became a stable long-term branch, the branches in Riga, Kovel and Baranowicze each lasted only one year. The 1932 expansion reflected the Frierdiker Rebbe's push to seed Chabad education across Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.

title_en: R. Yisrael Eber proposes new Otwock branch on 12 Sivan 5693
summary_en: On 12 Sivan 5693, Rosh Yeshiva R. Yisrael Eber reported a possible new Tomchei Tmimim branch in Otwock built on a local yeshiva ketana of 35 students.
story_body: Eber wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe describing a local Otwock yeshiva of about 35 students, previously funded by the late gvir R. Shlomo Goldberg, whose heirs would only give 400 zlotys monthly per his will. The local teachers proposed merging with Tomchei Tmimim provided the name retained a reference to Goldberg, but the plan ultimately did not materialize.

title_en: R. Yechezkel Feigin summarizes branch finances on 18 Shevat 5695
summary_en: On 18 Shevat 5695, secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R. Yisrael Jacobson detailing how the central yeshiva and branches were funded.
story_body: Feigin explained that the Warsaw kibbutz and top two classes ran on their own income, while four lower Warsaw classes plus the Vilna, Lodz and Patzanow branches were funded by the Rebbe's accounts. In times of severe shortage, R. Yehuda Eber would appeal directly to the Rebbe to prevent closures.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branches founded in Globoke and Raciaz
summary_en: Two new Tomchei Tmimim branches opened in Globoke and Raciaz in 5695 (1935).
story_body: The Globoke and Raciaz branches were added to the network as part of ongoing efforts to seed Chabad education across provincial Polish towns. Both appeared on the official 5695 list of branches published in HaTamim Vol. 1 that summer.

title_en: HaTamim Vol. 1 publishes 5695 branch list
summary_en: In Tammuz 5695 (June/July 1935), HaTamim Vol. 1 summarized the Tomchei Tmimim branches operating across Poland.
story_body: The summary listed branches in Vilna, Globoke, Lodz, Chmielnik, Patzanow and others. This published account served as the first widely circulated public record of the network's reach during the interwar period.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Chelm
summary_en: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Chelm in 5696 (1936).
story_body: Per the 5697 yeshiva calendar, the Chelm branch was organized in the summer of 5696. It would grow to about 100 students by the eve of WWII and was specifically named by the Frierdiker Rebbe in 5700 as a community whose students needed to be hurried to Vilna.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Dankera, Latvia
summary_en: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Dankera, Latvia, in 5697 (1937).
story_body: Dankera was one of two Latvian branches in the Tomchei Tmimim network. By Tishrei 5701 it had merged with the Livenhof (Livani) branch and relocated to Riga as the Polish branches collapsed under the German invasion.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe lists branches on 28 Nisan 5697
summary_en: In a letter dated 28 Nisan 5697, the Frierdiker Rebbe enumerated the cities hosting Tomchei Tmimim branches.
story_body: The letter (Igros Vol. 17, no. 6420) listed Warsaw, Otwock, Lodz, Vilna, Globoke, Chelm, Chmielnik and Patzanow as homes of Tomchei Tmimim branches. This contemporaneous list anchors the historical picture of the network at its peak.

title_en: HaTamim Vol. 7 publishes overview of Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: In Tammuz 5697, HaTamim Vol. 7 published a general overview of Tomchei Tmimim's development with the branch count for that year.
story_body: The piece reported that seven additional departments operated under the central yeshiva in Otwock-Warsaw, with hundreds of students across the network. It described the talmidim as G-d-fearing, talented and ready to be recognized as 'seed blessed by Hashem.'

title_en: Warsaw Rabbinical Committee letter of 10 Kislev 5698
summary_en: On 10 Kislev 5698, the Warsaw Vaad HaRabbanim wrote a letter of support emphasizing the seven branches and roughly 700 students.
story_body: The endorsement letter noted that seven branches operated under the Tomchei Tmimim banner with close to seven hundred students between the center and branches. Such rabbinical endorsements were essential to fundraising efforts during the difficult late-1930s economic climate.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branches founded in Kaluszyn, Lenchna, Stopnica
summary_en: Three new Tomchei Tmimim branches opened in Kaluszyn, Lenchna and Stopnica in 5698 (1938).
story_body: The 5698 expansion marked one of the last major growth waves before the war. Lenchna grew rapidly, reaching 75 students by the eve of war, while Kaluszyn would later be specifically mentioned by the Frierdiker Rebbe among the branches whose talmidim he rescued to Lithuania.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe writes about branch management on 18 Tammuz 5698
summary_en: In a letter of 18 Tammuz 5698, the Frierdiker Rebbe described the great effort required to run the yeshivos in Lodz, Vilna and the provincial yeshivos ketanos.
story_body: The letter (Vol. 4, no. 1042) testified to the personal toll of managing the network. It positioned the provincial yeshivos ketanos as central to the Rebbe's ongoing chinuch mission rather than peripheral satellites.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe writes on 25 Tammuz 5698 about Polish yeshivos ketanos
summary_en: On 25 Tammuz 5698, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that modest funding could establish many yeshivos ketanos in Poland.
story_body: He emphasized that no Polish city had organized Jewish chinuch outside of secular Tarbut schools and that small sums could fund roshei yeshiva for many new yeshivos ketanos. He cited the demonstrated success of existing Tomchei Tmimim preparatory branches as proof of concept.

title_en: US Vaad publishes Tomchei Tmimim branch list on 16 Elul 5698
summary_en: On 16 Elul 5698, the US-based Vaad LeHachzakas Yeshivos Tomchei Tmimim issued a letter listing the network's branches.
story_body: The American Vaad listed branches in Warsaw, Otwock, Vilna, Lodz, Chmielnik, Patzanow, Raciaz, Globoke, Stopnica and Chelm. The letter was part of fundraising efforts to support a network the founders rightly sensed was facing existential threats from the deteriorating European political situation.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Livenhof (Livani), Latvia
summary_en: A Tomchei Tmimim branch was founded in Livenhof (Livani), Latvia, in 5699 (1939).
story_body: The final pre-war branch opened in Livenhof shortly before the outbreak of WWII. By the start of 5701 (autumn 1940), Livenhof and Dankera merged and relocated to Riga as Polish branches collapsed and Latvia fell under Soviet control.

title_en: 5699 yeshiva calendar lists 9 Tomchei Tmimim branches
summary_en: The yeshiva's 5699 calendar listed nine branch departments across Poland and Latvia.
story_body: The published list named Vilna, Lodz, Chmielnik, Patzanow, Stopnica, Globoke, Chelm, Lenchna, Kaluszyn and Dankera (Latvia). This represented the network's largest documented extent just before its near-total destruction in WWII.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe transfers branches to Lithuania on 14 Tevet 5700
summary_en: In a letter of 14 Tevet 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe described relocating parts of the yeshiva from Otwock and Polish branches to Lithuania.
story_body: The letter (Vol. 5, no. 1136) recounted great effort and expense to evacuate portions of the central yeshiva in Otwock and the branches in Warsaw, Lodz, Kaluszyn and Chelm to Lithuania. A large portion of students nonetheless remained trapped in Poland after the German invasion.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe urges talmidim to relocate to Vilna on 3 Adar I 5700
summary_en: On 3 Adar I 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe urged talmidim from Chelm, Lodz and other branches to relocate to Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna.
story_body: The letter (Vol. 5, no. 1153) instructed the recipients to hurry along talmidim who had learned in the smaller branches in Chelm, Lodz and elsewhere to make their way to Vilna. From there, a group of 38 talmidim was ultimately rescued and brought to safety.

title_en: Livenhof and Dankera merge and relocate to Riga in 5701
summary_en: At the start of 5701, the Tomchei Tmimim branches in Livenhof and Dankera merged and moved to Riga.
story_body: As the war engulfed Eastern Europe and Latvia fell under Soviet control, the two Latvian branches consolidated in Riga. This merger marked the end of the dispersed pre-war Tomchei Tmimim network in the Baltic region.

title_en: R. Moshe Leib Rotstein reports on Tomchei Tmimim on 18 Elul 5702
summary_en: On 18 Elul 5702, secretary R. Moshe Leib Rotstein issued a report on Tomchei Tmimim listing the pre-war Polish branches.
story_body: The booklet 'Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch' described the network as having operated in Lodz, Vilna, Chelm, Patzanow, Chmielnik, Globoke, Kaluszyn and other cities. By the time of publication most of these communities and their yeshivos had been destroyed.

title_en: R. Meir Blizinski recounts Otwock founding in letter of 13 Shevat 5737
summary_en: On 13 Shevat 5737, R. Meir Blizinski wrote to his grandson R. S. Heber describing how he founded the Otwock branch in 5686.
story_body: The detailed memoir letter recounted his marriage on Rosh Chodesh Nisan 5686, his decision to establish a yeshiva in Otwock, the recruitment of Naftali Tzuker and R. Shlomo Tziley, and the eventual collapse of the branch in spring 5687. The letter became the primary first-person source for understanding the Otwock branch's brief existence.

title_en: Anash in Vilna write to Rebbe Rayatz proposing Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva
summary_en: On 13 Nisan 5687, Chabad chassidim in Vilna wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad asking his blessing to establish a Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in the Apatow Shul.
story_body: In early Nisan 5687, Anash of Vilna were inspired to found a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in their Apatow synagogue, modeled on the Warsaw yeshiva. A letter signed by the founding committee was sent to the Rebbe Rayatz in Leningrad, requesting his approval, guidance on selecting students, structuring nigleh and chassidus studies, and finding a suitable mashpia. The shaliach R' Lemil from Warsaw also assisted during a visit.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz blesses founding of Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Vilna
summary_en: On 27 Nisan 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz replied to the Vilna chassidim with joy and blessing for the new yeshiva, advising that the director be a Tomim familiar with the spirit of Lubavitch.
story_body: Responding to the founders' letter, the Rebbe Rayatz expressed great joy and confidence that students from surrounding regions would soon gather.
