He stressed that the director must be a former Tomchei Tmimim student deeply familiar with the institution's spirit, fully dedicated to admissions and supervising students with sharp insight and a firm hand.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva opens in Vilna at Apatow Shul
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5687, the Vilna branch of Tomchei Tmimim was inaugurated at the Apatow Shul on 21 Vilner Street with a festive opening assembly.
story_body: Following the Rebbe's blessing, the new yeshiva opened with a grand ceremony attended by congregants of both the Apatow and Kirzner Chabad shuls, along with the city's leading rabbis including the renowned Maggid of Vilna, Rabbi Menachem Kasovsky. Thirteen boys aged 14-15 had been gathered from surrounding shtetls; classes opened with Masechet Gittin under Rabbi Zeev Segal as first Rosh Yeshiva and R' Mordechai Leib Grossbein as mashgiach.

title_en: Vilna yeshiva reports rapid growth to Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: On 5 Sivan 5687, Vilna yeshiva leaders wrote to the Rebbe reporting over twenty students from surrounding towns and confirming Rabbi Zeev Segal as Rosh Yeshiva.
story_body: The Vilna directors reported that students were arriving daily from Disna, Dokshitz, Postov, Koretz and other towns, exceeding twenty in number. Rabbi Zeev Segal, formerly a Rosh Mesivta in Grodno, was appointed Rosh Yeshiva, and R' Mordechai Leib Grossbein was temporarily designated as mashpia in chassidus. Classes were divided by age into two levels studying Gemara with Tosafot.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrested in Leningrad by Soviet authorities
summary_en: On 15 Sivan 5687, the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested in Petersburg, beginning the chain of events leading to his exile, redemption, and departure from Russia.
story_body: Soon after responding to the Vilna founders, the Rebbe Rayatz was arrested in Petersburg on 15 Sivan and subsequently sent into exile. After his miraculous redemption, efforts began to extract him from Russia entirely. He eventually reached Riga at the end of Tishrei 5688.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz's train stops in Vilna en route to Latvia
summary_en: At the end of Tishrei 5688, after leaving Russia for Latvia, the Rebbe Rayatz's train briefly stopped in Vilna where he spoke with the Rosh Yeshiva and mashpia.
story_body: As the Rebbe Rayatz traveled from Russia to Latvia, his train passed through Vilna. The yeshiva's bochurim and administration eagerly awaited him at the station. The Rebbe stepped out onto the carriage steps and conversed with the Rosh Yeshiva and mashpia, but the brief stop did not permit longer interaction before the train continued to Riga.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Vilna yeshiva after Warsaw trip
summary_en: In Adar 5688, after visiting Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Vilna to visit the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva there.
story_body: Following his Warsaw visit during Adar 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz continued to Vilna to personally visit the young Tomchei Tmimim branch. The directors had previously requested he come and also pleaded for a qualified candidate to serve as combined Rosh Yeshiva, mashpia, and mashgiach.

title_en: Yechezkel Feigin reports first-year progress of Vilna yeshiva
summary_en: On 3 Iyar 5688, the secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote to R' Israel Jacobson summarizing the Vilna yeshiva's first-year growth to 28 students.
story_body: In a letter to R' Israel Jacobson dated 3 Iyar 5688, R' Yechezkel Feigin (secretary to the Rebbe Rayatz) reported that the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim had reached 28 students in its first year and that more were expected to join in the upcoming summer term.

title_en: R' Moshe Katzenelson, Vilna yeshiva committee member, passes away
summary_en: R' Moshe ben Eliezer HaKohen Katzenelson, formerly of Polotzk and a founding committee member of the Vilna yeshiva, passed away on 2 Nisan 5689.
story_body: R' Moshe Katzenelson was a member of the executive committee of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim from its founding, devoted to the institution with complete faith. Originally from Polotzk, he served on the management board until his passing on 2 Nisan 5689.

title_en: Vilna yeshiva committee appeals to Vaad HaYeshivot for aid
summary_en: On 4 Nisan 5689, the Vilna yeshiva committee wrote in Yiddish to the Vaad HaYeshivot describing their critical financial situation.
story_body: A letter from the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim committee, preserved in the Vaad HaYeshivot file at the YIVO archives, described the yeshiva's dire situation in the Apatow Shul where many poor children were being supported. The committee emphasized that despite the yeshiva's chassidic name, students of all orientations learned there, appealing for funds.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Zeligson, Vilna yeshiva co-founder, passes away
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman ben Avraham Aba Zeligson, a co-founder and supporter of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim, passed away on 25 Shevat 5690.
story_body: R' Shneur Zalman Zeligson prayed in the building that became the Vilna yeshiva before its founding and was among its founders. He later served as an examiner of the students and a supporter of the institution until his passing on 25 Shevat 5690, as recounted by his student R' Moshe Dreyzin.

title_en: Vilna yeshiva reports examination by R' Aryeh Leib Sheinin
summary_en: On 23 Shevat 5690, Vilna yeshiva administrators wrote to the Rebbe describing R' Aryeh Leib Sheinin's recent examination of the students.
story_body: R' Aryeh Leib Sheinin, rabbi of Dokshitz, visited the Vilna yeshiva and examined the students in their Torah, avodah, and conduct. So impressed was he that he urged the administration to expand beyond their current five classes by adding a higher division for advanced bochurim who would otherwise need to travel elsewhere.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz requests student rosters from Vilna yeshiva
summary_en: On 3 Nisan 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna yeshiva requesting detailed lists of students including names, hometowns, abilities, and class placement.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote asking the Vilna administration to send detailed rosters of all students - names, fathers' names, occupations, hometowns, length of study at the yeshiva, abilities, study habits, class placement, and the committee's plans for each student's upcoming year.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to R' Chaim Ozer Grodzensky on Vilna funding
summary_en: On 3 Nisan 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzensky requesting an increase in the Vaad HaYeshivot subsidy to the Vilna yeshiva from 25 to 50 shekels monthly.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote a warm letter to Rabbi Chaim Ozer Grodzensky thanking him for his support of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim and the Vaad HaYeshivot's monthly subsidy of 25 shekels. He requested that the subsidy be raised to 50 shekels monthly, expressing confidence that Rabbi Chaim Ozer would fulfill this request.

title_en: Vilna yeshiva confirms $100 stipend from Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: On 4 Tammuz 5690, the Vilna yeshiva administration formally acknowledged receipt of $100 from the Rebbe Rayatz covering the month of Sivan.
story_body: Beyond communal donations and the Vaad HaYeshivot subsidy, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a monthly stipend from Riga to support the Vilna yeshiva. The administration's signed receipt for $100 covering Sivan was preserved, demonstrating the ongoing financial lifeline from the Rebbe's office.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz sends $90 Tammuz subsidy to Vilna yeshiva
summary_en: On 7 Tammuz 5690, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a check for $90 to Vilna - the regular $100 monthly subsidy minus $10 toward the gemach.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna yeshiva committee enclosing a check for $90 - the standard monthly $100 stipend, with $10 deducted for the gemach (free-loan fund). This documented one example of the systematic monthly support the Rebbe provided from Riga.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz appoints R' Yehuda Eber Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna
summary_en: On 19 Marcheshvan 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna administration appointing R' Yehuda Eber as new Rosh Yeshiva.
story_body: Having rescued R' Yehuda Eber from Russia to Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz sent him to head the Vilna yeshiva. In his letter introducing the appointment, the Rebbe described R' Eber as one of the directors of Tomchei Tmimim in Russia, an outstanding talmid chacham of exceptional talent, still young in years.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber sends detailed report to Rebbe on Vilna students
summary_en: On Motzaei Shabbos Vayishlach 16 Kislev 5691, R' Yehuda Eber wrote a comprehensive report to the Rebbe Rayatz after examining all students in Vilna.
story_body: After his arrival as Rosh Yeshiva, R' Yehuda Eber individually examined every student and sent the Rebbe a detailed roster covering each student's abilities, diligence, and yiras shamayim. He noted that R' Yaakov Hochman, the mashpia, was dedicated to the students' conduct but had not been examining their progress; new procedures were instituted.

title_en: R' Chaim Shpreyreg, Vilna yeshiva committee member, passes away
summary_en: R' Chaim ben Yehuda Shpreyreg, a member of the Vilna yeshiva committee, passed away on 25 Kislev 5693.
story_body: R' Chaim Shpreyreg served on the founding executive committee of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim and was remembered with blessing for his contributions to the institution until his passing on 25 Kislev 5693.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber reports on Vilna yeshiva class restructuring
summary_en: On 1 Sivan 5691, R' Yehuda Eber wrote from Vilna detailing his reorganization of the yeshiva classes after returning from examining students in Warsaw and Lodz.
story_body: After visiting Warsaw and Lodz to examine students at the Rebbe Rayatz's request, R' Yehuda Eber returned to Vilna and immediately reorganized the classes. He reported that although the student count had decreased slightly from the winter, the qualitative level had improved. The preparatory class was disbanded, and not a single student was missing from his own advanced class or R' Zeev Segal's top class.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz visits Vilna yeshiva late at night
summary_en: In early Elul 5692, during his visit to Vilna, the Rebbe Rayatz made a late-night surprise visit to the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva to hear 'the voice of Torah.'
story_body: At the conclusion of his Vilna visit in early Elul 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz expressed his desire to visit the yeshiva at a late hour. Finding the students still learning at long tables with open gemaros, the Rebbe declared 'Hakol kol Yaakov - I wish to hear the sound of Torah.' The bochurim resumed learning aloud as the Rebbe walked among the tables gazing at each student before bestowing his blessing.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz refuses R' Eliyahu Weitz's resignation in Vilna
summary_en: On 13 Nisan 5694, the Rebbe Rayatz refused to accept R' Eliyahu Weitz's resignation from leading the Vilna yeshiva, fearing the institution would collapse.
story_body: R' Eliyahu Weitz, who bore the main burden of the Vilna yeshiva's leadership, wrote that he could no longer continue alone. The Rebbe Rayatz refused to accept his resignation, knowing it would mean the institution's destruction, and the same day wrote to Anash of Vilna chastising their cold attitude and pleading they actively support R' Weitz and the yeshiva.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz proposes R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal for Braslav branch
summary_en: On 27 Nisan 5694, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal inquiring whether he would accept a position as Rosh Yeshiva of a proposed Tomchei Tmimim branch in Braslav.
story_body: Discussions arose in spring 5694 about opening a new Tomchei Tmimim branch in Braslav. R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal was among the candidates proposed to lead it. Though the Braslav branch ultimately never opened, this exchange set the stage for his appointment as Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna the following year.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal appointed Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna
summary_en: After the Yamim Noraim of 5696, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal was appointed Rosh Yeshiva and director of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim by directive of the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: Following the Days of Awe in 5695, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal received instructions from the Rebbe Rayatz's secretariat to travel immediately to Vilna to take up the position of Rosh Yeshiva and director. Despite his youth, his scholarship was already renowned. He found roughly sixty students and worked to restore the discipline that had loosened since R' Spitz had departed. The third (top) class was led by Rabbi Israel Gustman.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal reports 33 Vilna yeshiva students
summary_en: On 24 Sivan 5696, director R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal reported to the Vilna Vaad HaYeshivot that the yeshiva had 33 students across three classes.
story_body: R' Oshpal submitted a formal report stating the yeshiva contained three classes: 15 in class A, 7 in class B, and 11 in class C. Of the 33 students, 7 were residents of Vilna while 26 came from other towns. A full roster of students with their ages was attached the following day.

title_en: WWII breaks out and Vilna Tomchei Tmimim temporarily closes
summary_en: With the outbreak of World War II in Elul 5699, the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva closed and its students were sent home.
story_body: When World War II broke out in Elul 5699, the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim shut down and dispersed its students to their homes. R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal returned to his family in Koretz. Shortly afterward, the yeshiva reopened as a refuge for displaced Warsaw Tomchei Tmimim students, with R' Oshpal returning to head it.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in America and opens Tomchei Tmimim in New York
summary_en: In late winter 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America and opened the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in New York, where R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal was appointed Rosh Mesivta.
story_body: Upon the Rebbe Rayatz's arrival in America at the end of winter 5700, he established the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in New York. R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, who had escaped to America during the war, was appointed Rosh Mesivta and educator, a position he held the rest of his life.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal becomes rabbi of Anshei Lubavitch of Boro Park
summary_en: From 5716, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal served as rabbi of the Anshei Lubavitch synagogue in Boro Park, New York.
story_body: Beginning in 5716, R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal served as rabbi of the Anshei Lubavitch of Boro Park synagogue. He also directed the Chevra Kadisha of Agudas Chabad, authoring the work 'Darchei Chesed' in that capacity.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal passes away in New York
summary_en: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, longtime Rosh Mesivta of Tomchei Tmimim and former Rosh Yeshiva in Vilna, passed away in New York on 12 Adar 5743.
story_body: R' Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, born in Svintzian in 5671, was among the earliest students of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim, later its Rosh Yeshiva, and eventually a longtime Rosh Mesivta at Tomchei Tmimim in New York. He served as rabbi of Anshei Lubavitch of Boro Park and director of the Agudas Chabad Chevra Kadisha until his passing on 12 Adar 5743.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch Łódź founded
summary_en: The Łódź branch of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch was founded on 17 Elul 5689.
story_body: According to the letterhead of the yeshiva, the Łódź branch of Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch was founded on 17 Elul 5689 (Sept 22, 1929) at Paludniowa 25. R. Zalman Schneersohn served as chairman and his son R. Dovber Yitzchok as director. The yeshiva initially operated with two divisions and grew steadily under the leadership of Lubavitcher chassidim in Łódź.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Chmielnik 'Toras Emes' founded
summary_en: The Chmielnik branch of Tomchei Tmimim, named 'Toras Emes,' was founded in the winter of 5690.
story_body: While visiting the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga during Tishrei 5690, Yosef Goldstein, a young shochet and former student of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw, was instructed to establish a branch in Chmielnik called 'Toras Emes.' Together with Avraham Zonstein he gathered about fifteen students, and the yeshiva quickly grew. By the time of its report, three rashei yeshiva taught roughly seventy students across four divisions.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz instructs founding of Chmielnik yeshiva
summary_en: During Tishrei 5690 the Rebbe Rayatz, in Riga, instructed Yosef Goldstein to establish a Tomchei Tmimim branch in Chmielnik.
story_body: When Yosef Goldstein traveled to the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga for the High Holidays of 5690, the Rebbe ordered him to found a branch of Tomchei Tmimim in his hometown of Chmielnik under the name 'Toras Emes.' Goldstein returned home, partnered with Avraham Zonstein of the Tmimim association, and the yeshiva was operational within weeks. The name 'Toras Emes' was retained at the Rebbe's insistence even though local authorities preferred the older 'Beis Yosef' designation.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz writes to Łódź students about study reports
summary_en: On 19 Cheshvan 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the talmidim of Warsaw, Vilna and Łódź expressing pleasure at their study reports.
story_body: In a letter dated 19 Cheshvan 5691 (Igros Kodesh vol. 2, no. 498), the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the talmidim of Tomchei Tmimim that he had taken great pleasure reading the lectures and study reports from Warsaw, Vilna and Łódź. The letter is the earliest extant reference to the Łódź branch in the Rebbe's correspondence. It documents the regular reporting system maintained between the branches and the Rebbe during his stay in Riga.

title_en: Połaniec branch of Tomchei Tmimim founded
summary_en: The Połaniec (Potshanov) branch of Tomchei Tmimim was founded at the start of 5692 with about 25 students.
story_body: At the start of 5692 (fall 1931), at the urging of the Rebbe Rayatz, a small yeshiva was opened in Połaniec as a branch of Tomchei Tmimim Warsaw. Beginning with about twenty-five students, the yeshiva grew to over sixty boys divided into five divisions, under the leadership of R. Moshe Aharon Morgel. He taught Gemara and some chassidus to the upper division, with public chassidus shiurim several times a week.

title_en: R. Yehuda Eber reports to Rebbe on Łódź yeshiva
summary_en: On 22 Iyar 5691 R. Yehuda Eber sent the Rebbe a detailed report on the 52 students of the Łódź yeshiva.
story_body: After being dispatched in Iyar 5691 to examine students in Warsaw, Łódź and Vilna, R. Yehuda Eber reported from Warsaw on 22 Iyar (May 9, 1931). He found 52 students at Łódź studying in two divisions, described their daily schedule, and praised the dedication of the Schneersohn brothers — particularly Dovber — who funded the yeshiva from their own pockets. He observed that the city was fertile ground for growth but financial strain limited expansion.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz commits monthly funding to Łódź yeshiva
summary_en: On 7 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz sent $50 to Łódź — $25 for yeshiva upkeep and $25 for R. Baruch Friedman's salary.
story_body: In a letter dated 7 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz enclosed two checks of $25 each to the directorate of Tomchei Tmimim Łódź. The first was on account of his pledge toward yeshiva expenses, and the second toward the salary of R. Baruch Friedman, who served as the mashpia from 5689 to 5692. The Rebbe requested immediate confirmation of receipt.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz leaves Riga for Warsaw to visit yeshivos
summary_en: On 9 Tammuz 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Warsaw to visit the three yeshivos under his direction.
story_body: As recounted in his letter of 5 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz departed Riga on 9 Tammuz to travel to Warsaw and inspect the three yeshivos in Warsaw, Vilna and Łódź under his administration. During his time in Warsaw in mid-Tammuz, students from the Łódź branch traveled to meet him and were received in yechidus.

title_en: Rebbe writes R. Yehuda Eber on Łódź yeshiva's future
summary_en: On 14 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote R. Yehuda Eber that the Łódź yeshiva must offer shiurim only, not a full study hall.
story_body: Writing on 14 Menachem Av 5691, the Rebbe Rayatz urged R. Yehuda Eber to spend several days in Łódź to evaluate the situation. He clarified that the Łódź branch was intended to host shiurim only, with no large independent study hall — that role being reserved for Warsaw. The letter reflects the structural division the Rebbe envisioned among the Polish branches.

title_en: R. Yitzchok Aryeh Mandelbaum sent to head Łódź yeshiva
summary_en: At the start of 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz sent R. Yitzchok Aryeh Mandelbaum to lead the Łódź yeshiva.
story_body: Early in 5692 (autumn 1931), the Rebbe Rayatz dispatched R. Yitzchok Aryeh Mandelbaum to Łódź to head the yeshiva. He arrived on the night of Sunday of Parshas Noach and immediately set about examining and organizing students into divisions. Although officially appointed only as ram, the burden of administration also fell on his shoulders since the Schneersohn brothers were occupied with their business.

title_en: R. Mandelbaum reports overcrowded conditions at Łódź
summary_en: On 8 Kislev 5692 R. Mandelbaum reported the Łódź yeshiva's financial state was dire despite excellent student progress.
story_body: In his report of 8 Kislev 5692, R. Mandelbaum described the yeshiva's grave financial situation: income was minimal relative to expenses and the Schneersohn brothers were covering shortfalls from their own pockets. Nonetheless, he was pleased with the students' diligence in both nigleh and chassidus, and reported that the yeshiva had earned a reputation among the yeshivos of Łódź.

title_en: Łódź yeshiva moves to Pomorska A41 building
summary_en: In Shevat 5692 the Łódź yeshiva moved to a larger building at Pomorska A41 with three divisions.
story_body: Beginning in Shevat 5692, the Łódź yeshiva relocated from Paludniowa 25 to spacious modern quarters at Pomorska A41. The new building featured central heating, hot water and modern facilities, and housed roughly fifty families including many chassidim. With the move, the yeshiva expanded to three divisions and grew to about one hundred students.

title_en: Rebbe presses Łódź for status updates
summary_en: On 3 Adar II 5692 the Rebbe Rayatz expressed surprise at receiving no updates from the Łódź yeshiva.
story_body: In a letter dated 3 Adar II 5692, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote with surprise that he had heard nothing of the Łódź yeshiva's situation since his recent travels and return. He demanded to know how his earlier instructions had been carried out and asked for a complete update on the current state of affairs.

title_en: R. Menachem Mendel Rozenmutter appointed head of Łódź yeshiva
summary_en: In 5694 R. Menachem Mendel Rozenmutter was appointed rosh yeshiva of Tomchei Tmimim Łódź.
story_body: In 5694 (1934), R. Menachem Mendel Rozenmutter, son-in-law of R. Dovber Moshe Shmotkin of Warsaw, was appointed rosh yeshiva of the Łódź branch. He refused to accept a salary, supporting himself from his candle factory; when the Rebbe heard this he was displeased, quoting 'a free doctor is worth nothing.' Rozenmutter was murdered in the Holocaust.

title_en: R. Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky sent to teach in Łódź
summary_en: In 5697 the Rebbe instructed R. Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky to leave Otwock and return to Łódź to teach.
story_body: Having studied in Otwock until 5697, R. Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky was instructed by the Rebbe to return to Łódź — this time as a teacher. He found a group of devoted chassidish bochurim and taught them nigleh and chassidus through 5699, ultimately managing the division during the final two years of the yeshiva's existence.

title_en: R. Morgel reports on Połaniec yeshiva to the Rebbe
summary_en: On 7 Tevet 5697 R. Moshe Aharon Morgel reported to the Rebbe on the expanded Połaniec yeshiva.
story_body: In his report of 7 Tevet 5697, R. Moshe Aharon Morgel informed the Rebbe Rayatz that the yeshiva had grown to approximately forty students divided into three divisions studying Bava Metzia, Bava Kamma, Yevamos and Shevuos with Rashi, Tosafos and select commentaries. After Maariv R. Yitzchok Pinchas, son of the tzaddik of Kinsk, taught a public Tanya chapter for laymen, youth and students of the third division.

title_en: Germans close Chmielnik yeshiva
summary_en: On Rosh Hashanah 5700 the Germans entered Chmielnik and outlawed study at the Toras Emes yeshiva.
story_body: With the German invasion on Rosh Hashanah 5700, study at the Chmielnik yeshiva was officially banned. Despite the prohibition, many students continued learning clandestinely in the women's section above the shul, and lessons persisted until the end of winter 5701. The clandestine yeshiva represents one of the documented cases of continued Torah study under Nazi occupation in occupied Poland.

title_en: Goldstein flees Chmielnik after Nazi search
summary_en: On Purim 5701, Nazi agents searched Yosef Goldstein's home in Chmielnik; he escaped with only his tefillin and a letter from the Rebbe.
story_body: On Purim 5701 (March 13, 1941), German agents came to seize Yosef Goldstein at his home in Chmielnik but did not find him, as he was praying in the beis midrash below. Realizing he had been informed upon — either over the yeshiva or his continued shechita work — he returned briefly, took only his tefillin (in which he had kept a 1933 letter from the Rebbe Rayatz), and fled the city. He credited that letter with miraculously saving him in the labor camps, escaping every Nazi search that followed.

title_en: HaTamim reports Tomchei Temimim activity in Chelm
summary_en: The journal HaTamim reports on a group of Tomchei Temimim Warsaw students active in spreading Torah and Chassidus among the youth of Chelm.
story_body: Issue 1 of HaTamim (Tammuz 5695) describes a cluster of Tomchei Temimim alumni in Chelm running Torah classes and a Chassidus shiur for members of Tzeirei Agudas Yisrael. The chief organizer is identified as Yaakov Yitzchak Rosenbaum, a Warsaw Tomchei Temimim student. This reporting laid the groundwork for the formal Chelm branch founded the next year.

title_en: Decision to found Achei Temimim yeshiva branch in Chelm
summary_en: At a post-Pesach gathering at Moshe Berland's home in Chelm, students returning from Tomchei Temimim Otwock resolved to open a local branch yeshiva.
story_body: After Passover 5696, students who had been home for the holiday from Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch in Otwock convened a farbrengen at the home of Moshe Berland. They decided to establish a yeshiva in Chelm as a branch of the Otwock yeshiva, to be named Yeshivas Achei Temimim Lubavitch. Yaakov Yitzchak Rosenbaum was elected chairman and Avraham Yitzchak Kornblit secretary.

title_en: Chelm yeshiva opens with 40 students
summary_en: In summer 5696 the new Achei Temimim branch in Chelm began operating with roughly forty students in two classes.
story_body: The yeshiva opened with about forty students, mostly local Chelm boys with some from surrounding towns. Avraham Goldman taught the lower class and Pesachya Meller the upper class. Local balebatim provided room and board for out-of-town students, while the Otwock central yeshiva sent a monthly subsidy for staff salaries.

title_en: 19 Kislev farbrengen at Chelm yeshiva
summary_en: Chelm's Achei Temimim yeshiva held a 19 Kislev seudah where the Rebbe Rayatz's general letter and a 1928 maamar were studied.
story_body: On 19 Kislev 5697 the Chelm branch hosted a celebration of the Chag HaGeulah starting at 7 PM, including students, hanhalah members and visiting avreichim. They read the Frierdiker Rebbe's klali letter and the parsha of the Chag HaGeulah, then learned the maamar 'Asarah Sheyoshvim' from 12 Tammuz 5688 during the seudah.

title_en: Chelm hanhalah confirms receipt of Rebbe's monthly stipend
summary_en: Rosenbaum and Kornblit wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe acknowledging his Kislev stipend, which alone covered two weeks of staff wages.
story_body: On 22 Kislev 5697 the Chelm yeshiva managers Yitzchak Yaakov Rosenbaum and Avraham Yitzchak Kornblit wrote the Frierdiker Rebbe thanking him for the monthly support, noting that they had no other source to pay the maggidei shiurim for the last two weeks. They also reported on the 19 Kislev farbrengen and asked the Rebbe to confirm Tanya study with the second class.

title_en: Chelm community grants land for new yeshiva building
summary_en: In 5699 the Chelm kehilla allotted land and Keren HaTorah pledged major funds to build a new yeshiva campus, plans aborted by the war.
story_body: By 5699 student numbers in the Chelm branch had outgrown its premises. Kornblit obtained a building site from the kehilla and a substantial pledge from Dr. Shmuel Deutschlander of Agudas Yisrael's Keren HaTorah. The outbreak of WWII cancelled all construction plans, and most Chelm Jews were later murdered.

title_en: Kaloszyn branch of Tomchei Temimim founded
summary_en: A Tomchei Temimim branch was founded in Kaloszyn in 5698, eventually growing to about 60 students under Leib Kremer.
story_body: The Kaloszyn branch yeshiva was established in 5698 (1938) under the leadership of Rabbi Leib Kremer, later director of Tomchei Temimim Montreal. According to a report in HaPardes it eventually enrolled around 60 students.

title_en: Shimon Goldman studies in Kaloszyn yeshiva
summary_en: At his bar mitzvah Shimon Goldman entered the Lubavitch yeshiva in Kaloszyn, where students were learning Masechet Pesachim.
story_body: In summer 5699 the 13-year-old Shimon Goldman from Siedlce began learning at the Lubavitch branch yeshiva in Kaloszyn, recalling Leib Kremer as menahel and the dayan's son as maggid shiur. The boys studied Masechet Pesachim and ate 'days' arrangements with local families. He later recorded his memories in Kfar Chabad magazine.

title_en: Kaloszyn yeshiva dispersed at outbreak of WWII
summary_en: After the German invasion of Poland, Rabbi Kremer dissolved the Kaloszyn yeshiva and sent out-of-town students home.
story_body: During the first week of the war the Kaloszyn yeshiva kept its learning schedule, but as the Wehrmacht's rapid advance became clear, Leib Kremer and the hanhalah declared an emergency. Unable to take responsibility for boys from other towns, they dispersed the yeshiva and sent students such as Shimon Goldman back to families like his in Siedlce.

title_en: Rebbe transfers yeshiva sections from Poland to Lithuania
summary_en: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 14 Kislev 5700 that he had succeeded, with great effort, in moving part of the yeshiva's Polish branches to Lithuania.
story_body: In a letter dated 14 Kislev 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe reported that with great toil and expense he had transferred to Lithuania part of the Tomchei Temimim sections from Warsaw, Lodz, Kaloszyn, Chelm and elsewhere. This move was part of the Chabad effort to preserve the yeshiva network as the Nazi occupation of Poland tightened.

title_en: Yeshivas Zichron Yosef founded in Dankra
summary_en: In 5696, after the Rogatchover Gaon's passing, a Chabad yeshiva named Zichron Yosef was opened in Dankra (Gostini), Latvia.
story_body: Following the death of the Rogatchover Gaon Yosef Rosen in 5696, the town of Dankra (also called Gostini) in Latvia established a Chabad yeshiva named Zichron Yosef in his memory. The yeshiva was run by the town rabbi, Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen, son-in-law of Refael Hakohen of Riga.

title_en: Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen becomes rabbi of Gostini
summary_en: Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen, born in Livani in 5644, took up his post as rabbi of Gostini on 11 January 1935.
story_body: According to the volume 'Latvia: Synagogues and Rabbis' (Riga 2005), Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen was installed as rabbi of Gostini on 11 January 1935 (26 Tevet 5695). The town had two Chassidic shuls and two for the misnagdim. He would soon lead the Chabad yeshiva there and serve as a key node in the Latvia branch network.

title_en: Rebbe urges importing Lithuanian students to Dankra
summary_en: On 8 Elul 5697 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Refael Hakohen of Riga that Dankra must bring students from Lithuania to ignite local Latvian youth.
story_body: In a letter of 8 Elul 5697 (Igrot vol. 4, no. 940) the Frierdiker Rebbe told Refael Hakohen, head of the Chabad community in Riga, that the Dankra yeshiva was obligated to import students from Lithuania to inspire 'feelings of love for Torah' among Latvian youth. This was part of his strategy of seeding new branches with veteran Tomchei Temimim talmidim.

title_en: Rebbe thanks Dubin and Westerman for Dankra donation
summary_en: On 3 Shevat 5698 the Frierdiker Rebbe acknowledged a gift from Westerman, arranged through Mordechai Dubin, for the Dankra mechina.
story_body: Six months after pushing for Lithuanian recruits, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Eliyahu Chaim Althoiz of Riga on 3 Shevat 5698 thanking him for news of a donation from the philanthropist Westerman for the Tomchei Temimim mechina in Dankra. The gift had been secured through the efforts of the Latvian parliamentarian Mordechai Dubin.

title_en: Rabbi Teitz of Livenhof requests teacher for the youth
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote on 6 Tevet 5691 considering sending Yaakov Landa to Livenhof to teach the local Tiferes Bachurim youth.
story_body: In winter 5691 Rabbi Avraham Binyamin Teitz of Livenhof asked the Frierdiker Rebbe to send a teacher for the town's young men. The Rebbe wrote to Yaakov Landa on 6 Tevet 5691 (Igrot vol. 2, no. 516) saying that Livenhof was unusual: even the local balebatim wanted to study, and Rabbi Teitz, while distinguished, was not an outgoing public figure.

title_en: Pinchas Mordechai Teitz founds Yavneh society in Livenhof
summary_en: In Sivan 5691 Pinchas Mordechai Teitz visited the Rebbe in Riga and reported on the new Yavneh society for youth Torah study.
story_body: During Sivan 5691 Rabbi Teitz's son Pinchas Mordechai Teitz visited the Rebbe in Riga and described the new association 'Yavneh' he had formed to organize the Livenhof youth around study of Tanach, Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, Mishnayos and Aggadah, and to strengthen mitzvah observance.

title_en: Rebbe blesses Yavneh society of Livenhof
summary_en: On 20 Sivan 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent a letter of blessing to the newly founded Yavneh society in Livenhof.
story_body: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 20 Sivan 5691 (Igrot vol. 17, no. 6289) expressing joy at Pinchas Mordechai Teitz's report of the founding of Yavneh in Livenhof. He blessed its members for success in their Torah learning program and prayed they would grow in numbers and become a model among Jewish youth.

title_en: Rebbe travels from Riga to Warsaw with R. Teitz
summary_en: During Tammuz 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe traveled from Riga to Warsaw, suggesting on the train to R. Teitz that Livenhof open a yeshiva.
story_body: In Tammuz 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe left Riga for Warsaw, riding the train together with Pinchas Mordechai Teitz. During the journey the Rebbe urged Teitz to expand the Yavneh learning groups and try to open a full yeshiva in Livenhof itself.

title_en: Rebbe inquires about Livenhof and Kreuzburg activity
summary_en: On 27 Av 5691 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote that he had heard only second-hand reports from Livenhof and Kreuzburg and requested a detailed update.
story_body: The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 27 Av 5691 (Igrot vol. 17, no. 6299) complaining that since leaving Riga at the start of Tammuz he had only heard fragmented news 'from afar' about Livenhof and Kreuzburg, and asked Pinchas Mordechai Teitz to send a detailed report on developments there.

title_en: Rebbe approves Livenhof yeshiva and reports 27 students
summary_en: On 25 Nissan 5692 the Frierdiker Rebbe encouraged founding a small yeshiva in Livenhof, soon reporting 27 talmidim.
story_body: In a Chol HaMoed Pesach letter dated 25 Nissan 5692 the Frierdiker Rebbe told Pinchas Mordechai Teitz that he had discussed strengthening Tiferes Bachurim/Yavneh with R. Chadakov and was thrilled at the possibility of founding a small yeshiva in Livenhof. A subsequent letter celebrated that, with mesirus nefesh, the yeshiva had already enrolled 27 students.

title_en: R. Teitz leaves Livenhof yeshiva for America
summary_en: After roughly one year leading the Livenhof yeshiva, Pinchas Mordechai Teitz left for the US in 5694 as Telz emissary.
story_body: Pinchas Mordechai Teitz ran the original Livenhof yeshiva for only about a year. In 5694 he traveled to the United States as a shaliach for the Telz yeshiva, married there, and was appointed rabbi of Elizabeth, New Jersey, leaving Livenhof without its founding director.

title_en: Tomchei Temimim branch reopens in Livenhof
summary_en: Around 5699 the Frierdiker Rebbe established a Tomchei Temimim branch in Livenhof, run together with the Dankra yeshiva by R. Berchen.
story_body: Approximately in 5699 the Frierdiker Rebbe founded a Tomchei Temimim branch in Livenhof, separate from R. Teitz's earlier yeshiva. Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen of Gostini directed both Latvian branches simultaneously, corresponding with the Rebbe about each.

title_en: Rebbe allocates $1200 between Dankra and Livenhof
summary_en: Now in the US, the Rebbe wrote on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5700 instructing how to split $1200 sent via Mordechai Chefetz between the two Latvian branches.
story_body: After arriving in America, the Frierdiker Rebbe managed to send $1200 to Mordechai Chefetz in Riga. On 1 Iyar 5700 he wrote (Igrot vol. 12, no. 4391) directing that R. Berchen receive 100 lats per month for the Dankra yeshiva and 50 lats per month, from Nissan onward, for the Livenhof branch.

title_en: R. Berchen reports founding Livani branch
summary_en: On Erev Shavuos 5700 Yeshaya Chanoch Berchen wrote the Rebbe that, after great effort, the Livani branch had been established with students from Riga and the region.
story_body: In an Erev Shavuos 5700 letter R. Berchen described how, after toil and travail, they finally succeeded in founding the small yeshiva in Livani, staffed by Tzvi Cohen and Shalom Ber Asherov who had relocated there. A planned Preili branch failed for lack of a teacher willing to relocate, and the Riga vaad had functionally collapsed. He confirmed receipt of $50 toward Livani.

title_en: Rebbe responds to Berchen on Latvian yeshivot
summary_en: On 5 Tammuz 5700 the Frierdiker Rebbe replied to Berchen with blessings for students, teachers and supporters of the Dankra and Livani branches.
story_body: Replying on 5 Tammuz 5700 (Igrot vol. 12, no. 4426), the Frierdiker Rebbe expressed great satisfaction at hearing news of the talmidim at Dankra and Livani. He asked Berchen to convey his brachos to the students for health and success in Torah, and to their teachers and supporters.

title_en: Latvian branches consolidate in Riga
summary_en: At the start of Tishrei 5701 the three Latvian branches (Riga, Dankra, Livenhof) merged in Riga as Dankra became untenable.
story_body: By Tishrei 5701 conditions in Dankra had become unbearable and the yeshiva relocated to Riga, where it joined the Livenhof branch and the Riga branch reopened in 5699. R. Berchen wrote the Rebbe on 6 Tishrei 5701 in coded language about his sons (the students) having left him for Riga to continue their studies, hinting at the move under Soviet censorship.

title_en: Rebbe orders weekly contact with European talmidim
summary_en: On 15 Kislev 5701 the Frierdiker Rebbe instructed Moshe Pinchas Katz to correspond weekly with Tomchei Temimim students in Vilna, Riga and Poland.
story_body: From New York, on 15 Kislev 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Moshe Pinchas Katz (Igrot vol. 5, no. 1310) instructing him to maintain weekly correspondence with Tomchei Temimim students still in Vilna, Riga and Poland, keeping them informed and gathering reports on their material and spiritual situations.

title_en: Rebbe obtains 127 US visas for European talmidim
summary_en: At the start of 5701 the Frierdiker Rebbe secured 127 US visas for top Tomchei Temimim talmidim across occupied Europe, including Latvia.
story_body: Early in 5701 the Frierdiker Rebbe arranged 127 visas to the United States for select Tomchei Temimim students across Nazi-occupied Europe, with a portion allocated to Latvia. Almost none were permitted to leave; most of the intended recipients perished in the Holocaust.

title_en: Jews of Dankra (Gostini) murdered by Nazis
summary_en: On Erev Tisha B'Av 5701 the Jewish community of Dankra (Gostini), including the yeshiva network families, was murdered by the Nazis.
story_body: According to 'Hashmadat Yehudim B'Latvia' p. 198, on Erev Tisha B'Av 5701 the Jews of Dankra/Gostini were killed by the Nazis. The Frierdiker Rebbe, lacking firsthand information, later asked in coded language on 23 Adar II 5703 about Himmelstein of Dankra and R. Berchen ('Refael's son-in-law'), seeking news of their fate.

title_en: Lentschna branch founded by Pesachya Meller
summary_en: After 5696 Pesachya Meller founded the Achei Temimim Lubavitch branch in Lentschna, where he also served as maggid shiur.
story_body: After leaving his post in Chelm in 5696, Pesachya Meller founded a new Achei Temimim Lubavitch yeshiva in Lentschna and served as its maggid shiur. It was listed in the 5699 yeshiva calendar and reported in HaPardes as having 75 students.

title_en: Stopnica branch of Tomchei Temimim active
summary_en: A Tomchei Temimim branch in Stopnica operated from 5696 through 5699, listed in official yeshiva calendars and US fundraising correspondence.
story_body: The Stopnica branch existed from 5696 until 5699 and is referenced in the yeshiva calendar for 5697, in a 16 Elul 5698 letter from the US Vaad LeHachzakas Tomchei Temimim listing active yeshivos, and in the 5699 yeshiva calendar. Beyond these mentions no further details are known.

title_en: Rebbe visits Warsaw and dispatches students to scout Polish-Volhynian towns
summary_en: During his summer 1931 visit to Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz spoke with select students about traveling through Poland and Volhynia to identify towns where additional Tomchei Temimim branches could be opened.
story_body: In mid-Tammuz 5691, while in Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz convened several senior students — including R' Shneur Zalman Gurary, R' Yosef Goldstein, R' Meir Glazman and R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum — and tasked them with surveying towns across Poland and the Volhynia region. Each was to assess where it would be feasible to establish new branches of the yeshiva. By mid-Av the students were reporting back, and the Rebbe responded with detailed instructions to each.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum proposes opening a yeshiva in Maciów
summary_en: In Av 5691, R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum wrote to the Rebbe relaying an offer from his hometown Maciów of a newly built, well-appointed building suited for a yeshiva.
story_body: Mandelbaum forwarded a letter from a young man in Maciów (Volhynia) describing a magnificent stone building, recently completed by a wealthy New York native in memory of his deceased daughter. The donor had built dormitory space, a dining hall, and apartments for the heads of the yeshiva, and pledged ongoing support. The local community urged that a Chabad yeshiva be founded there.

title_en: Rebbe sends R' Shneur Zalman Gurary to investigate Maciów yeshiva offer
summary_en: On 22 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe instructed R' Shneur Zalman Gurary to travel discreetly to Maciów to inspect the building offered for a new yeshiva.
story_body: After receiving Mandelbaum's report, the Rebbe wrote both to Mandelbaum and to Gurary on the same day. He asked Gurary to view the buildings, send a detailed description, and act quietly so that no rival groups would seize the opportunity. The Rebbe hoped that once full details were in hand, arrangements could be made to open a yeshiva there.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Gurary visits Maciów to inspect proposed yeshiva building
summary_en: On 5 Elul 5691, R' Shneur Zalman Gurary reported from Maciów after touring the proposed yeshiva building and meeting with the local committee.
story_body: Gurary described the structure in detail, sketching its layout since the town was too small for him to photograph or measure openly — a bearded bochur arriving in such a small town drew immediate attention. The local committee, prompted by Mandelbaum's letter forwarding the Rebbe's interest, had convened a meeting earlier that week and was actively considering the proposal. Gurary indicated that a formal letter from the committee to the Rebbe was forthcoming.

title_en: Maciów community committee formally proposes hosting a Chabad yeshiva
summary_en: On 7 Elul 5691 the rabbi, deputy rabbi, and seven committee members of Maciów's 'Yeshivat Talmud Torah' wrote to the Rebbe offering a hall in their new building for a thirty-student yeshiva.
story_body: Signed by Rabbi Shalom Shachna Cherniak, his deputy Rabbi Yosef Lashtshiver, and the seven committee members, the letter described how they had deliberately left the upper story of the building unfinished to prevent secularists from establishing schools there. They offered the Rebbe immediate use of a large, ornate hall sufficient for thirty students, and invited the Rebbe to take an active interest in establishing a major yeshiva in Volhynia at this site.

title_en: Maciów yeshiva proposal revived by R' Yitzchak Aryeh Mandelbaum
summary_en: On the 3rd day of Chol Hamoed Sukkot 5694, Mandelbaum again wrote to the Rebbe urging the founding of a yeshiva in Maciów to serve graduates of local cheders.
story_body: Mandelbaum warned that the largest cheder class in Maciów and surrounding towns was only beginning Gemara, and that students leaving without further Torah education risked drifting from religious life entirely. He committed to personally establishing a small yeshiva on his return home, teaching the local boys Gemara and Chassidus daily. The plan, however, did not materialize.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum appointed rabbi of Chabad community in Glubokoye
summary_en: In 5695 the Rebbe dispatched R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum to serve as rabbi of the Chabad community in Glubokoye.
story_body: After the Maciów initiative failed to advance, the Rebbe Rayatz reassigned Mandelbaum in 1935, sending him to lead the Chabad kehillah in Glubokoye. This appointment redirected Mandelbaum's communal work from the abandoned Volhynian yeshiva project to congregational leadership.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum sent on summer mission to Krakow
summary_en: In summer 5691 the Rebbe dispatched R' Yitzchak Mandelbaum to Krakow for an extended outreach visit to local bochurim.
story_body: Mandelbaum spent time in Krakow connecting with young men and exchanging letters with them. On returning he debriefed the Rebbe, who on 15 Menachem Av asked for fuller particulars — names, addresses, and any continuing correspondence — to follow up on these contacts.

title_en: Rebbe asks R' Yosef Goldstein to undertake a Krakow mission
summary_en: On 22 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe wrote to R' Yosef Goldstein asking whether he could accept a two- to three-week shlichus to Krakow.
story_body: Building on his Warsaw conversations about strengthening Tomchei Temimim alumni scattered across Polish towns, the Rebbe noted that Goldstein lived not far from Krakow and might be able to visit the city periodically. He inquired whether Goldstein had already acted on their discussion and whether his schedule allowed him to take on a focused Krakow mission of several weeks.

title_en: R' Mordechai Mentlik dispatched to Krakow for outreach work
summary_en: In late summer 5693 the Rebbe selected R' Mordechai Mentlik to spend weeks teaching the Chassidus circle of avreichim in Krakow.
story_body: On 14 Menachem Av 5693 the Rebbe wrote to Rosh Yeshiva R' Yehuda Eber proposing such a mission, offering to fund up to 100 zloty, and noting that the local circle led by R' Michael Zeligson studied Chassidus twice weekly. By 23 Av the Rebbe had settled on Mentlik and authorized an expanded budget of 125 zloty. The students later recalled this mission in a 18 Elul 5701 letter from Shanghai, when one of the avreichim from that Krakow circle resurfaced as a refugee in the Far East.

title_en: Rebbe sends R' Meir Glazman to survey yeshivas in Lvov and surroundings
summary_en: On 15 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe instructed R' Meir Glazman to broaden his Lvov mission beyond the Machzikei Lomdei Torah yeshiva to all local Torah institutions.
story_body: Responding to Glazman's first report from Lvov, the Rebbe expressed pleasure that he had grasped the broader purpose of the visit. The Rebbe asked him to identify every yeshiva, study circle, and shtiebel where Torah was learned in the city, to record names of contacts for future correspondence, and to extend his survey to the surrounding towns of the Lemberg region for another week.

title_en: Rebbe asks R' Yehuda Eber to map yeshivas of Polish Lithuania
summary_en: On 15 Menachem Av 5691 the Rebbe repeated his request that R' Yehuda Eber compile a list of yeshivas in Polish Lithuania with their locations and student counts.
story_body: The Rebbe had originally written the prior winter asking Eber, head of Tomchei Temimim in Vilna, to gather this information. Now he renewed the request, observing that Vilna was a natural base from which such intelligence could be assembled. The data was to feed his broader planning for Tomchei Temimim's expansion across Polish Lithuania.

title_en: R' Eliyahu Weitz proposes opening Tomchei Temimim branch in Braslau
summary_en: In winter 5694, R' Eliyahu Weitz, director of the Vilna yeshiva, wrote to the Rebbe proposing a new yeshiva ketana branch in Lithuanian Braslau.
story_body: Weitz suggested sending a particular individual to serve as rosh mesivta in Braslau. The proposal reached the Rebbe during the winter months and set off several months of consultation about whether the branch should be established and who should be appointed to lead it.

title_en: Rebbe encourages founding a Tomchei Temimim branch in Braslau
summary_en: On 13 Nissan 5694 the Rebbe wrote both to R' Eliyahu Weitz and to R' Shneur Aron of Braslau, urging immediate steps to establish a yeshiva ketana there.
story_body: To Weitz the Rebbe suggested that a Tomchei Temimim student would be a more suitable rosh mesivta than the candidate Weitz had proposed, and that the cost would be lower. To R' Shneur Aron the Rebbe described Braslau as urgently needing a yeshiva in the spirit of Tomchei Temimim and asked him to rally local Anash to bring the plan to fruition without delay, coordinating logistics through Weitz in Vilna.

title_en: Rebbe offers R' Yitzchak Dov Ber Ushpal the Braslau yeshiva leadership
summary_en: On 26 Nissan 5694 the Rebbe wrote to R' Yitzchak Dov Ber Ushpal of Korniec offering him the post of rosh yeshiva and educator at the planned Braslau branch.
story_body: After R' Shneur Aron of Braslau responded affirmatively, the Rebbe informed him that the candidate would be named the following week. The same day he wrote to Ushpal asking whether he could accept the appointment as rosh yeshiva and mechanech at the new Tomchei Temimim branch in Braslau. The Braslau branch never materialized; some months later Ushpal was instead sent to head the Vilna yeshiva.

title_en: WWII breaks out; German bombs fall on Otwock during yeshiva founding-day gathering
summary_en: On the eve of 17 Elul, after an all-night yeshiva-founding-day farbrengen, German bombs began falling on Otwock as the students returned from the mikveh.
story_body: Rabbi Dov had led the Tomchei Tmimim bochurim in a yeshiva-anniversary farbrengen through the night of 17 Elul. At dawn, walking back from the mikveh half an hour away, the students heard explosions they first mistook for Polish drills. By morning it was clear that Germany had invaded Poland, bombs had hit Jewish neighborhoods, and the Second World War had begun.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz travels from Otwock to Warsaw with family
summary_en: On the Tuesday after war broke out, the Rebbe Rayatz moved from Otwock to Warsaw with his family and inner circle.
story_body: After the German invasion, many bochurim had already fled toward Warsaw, hoping the capital would be safer from German bombardment. On Tuesday, 21 Elul, the Rebbe Rayatz himself followed with his family and close attendants, where they would remain under aerial bombardment for the next four months.

title_en: American Tomchei Tmimim students instructed to flee Poland
summary_en: On 17 Elul the Rebbe Rayatz directed American students in the Otwock yeshiva to escape via Warsaw, Riga, and Stockholm back to the United States.
story_body: Once war began, the Rebbe Rayatz told the American bochurim at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock to seek passage out of Poland alongside foreign diplomats and citizens. The mashpia R. Yisroel Eber distributed travel money. They escaped via Warsaw, Riga, and Stockholm, eventually returning to the United States.

title_en: About 20 Otwock students reach Vilna on foot
summary_en: By 10 Kislev, secretary R. Chaim Lieberman reported from Riga that some twenty Otwock bochurim had walked to Vilna.
story_body: After the Ribbentrop-Molotov partition of Poland, Tomchei Tmimim students began making their way north on foot across two borders to reach Vilna, which had just been transferred from Soviet to Lithuanian control. Writing from Riga to R. Yisroel Jacobson on 10 Kislev 5700, R. Chaim Lieberman reported that some twenty bochurim had already arrived in Vilna.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz instructs Warsaw students to escape to Vilna
summary_en: In early Kislev the Rebbe Rayatz directed Tomchei Tmimim students in Warsaw to smuggle across two borders to Vilna and re-establish the yeshiva there.
story_body: After the Soviets handed Vilna over to independent Lithuania, the Rebbe Rayatz saw an opening to save his yeshiva. In mid-Kislev he received bochurim including R. Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel for yechidus, blessed their escape, and pledged the funds needed to cross the German-Soviet and Soviet-Lithuanian borders. R. Shmaryahu Gourary handed each escapee 100-150 zlotys for travel and bribes.

title_en: Reitchik departs Warsaw after parting blessing from the Rebbe
summary_en: On the night of 18 Kislev R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik received the Rebbe's parting blessing and set out from Warsaw for Vilna.
story_body: R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik later wrote a detailed report of his escape route. After parting blessings from the Rebbe Rayatz on the night of 18 Kislev, his group farbrenged on 19 Kislev in Praga, then traveled to Siedlce. After many obstacles they crossed the German-Soviet border on the night of 26 Kislev and reached Slonim by 29 Kislev.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz rescued from Warsaw to Riga
summary_en: On 5 Tevet the Rebbe Rayatz escaped war-torn Warsaw and reached Riga, after four months under German aerial bombardment.
story_body: After four months in Warsaw under relentless German bombing, an elaborate international rescue effort brought the Rebbe Rayatz, his family, and close attendants safely to Riga on 5 Tevet 5700. From Riga he immediately turned to mobilizing American Chabad and the Joint Distribution Committee to fund the evacuation of his remaining students.

title_en: R. Yitzchak Dov Oshpal smuggled across border into Vilna
summary_en: At 4 a.m. on 7 Tevet, the head of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim branch crossed from Soviet-held Kornitz into Lithuania.
story_body: R. Yitzchak Dov Oshpal, head of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim branch, had fled to his home in Kornitz when war erupted. In Tevet 5700, his student Yosef Kaminetsky came as a special emissary from Vilna with funds and a US visa held for him by R. Chaim Ozer Grodzenski. At 4 a.m. on 7 Tevet, after enormous danger, Oshpal crossed the border into Lithuania, noting the event in his Mishnayos.

title_en: Rebbe writes from Riga seeking funds for student evacuation
summary_en: On 14 Tevet the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Yisroel Jacobson and to Dr. Leo Jung requesting urgent funds to evacuate remaining students from Poland to Lithuania.
story_body: Once safe in Riga, the Rebbe Rayatz immediately mobilized international Chabad and the Joint. In letters of 14 Tevet he reported having moved part of the central yeshiva from Otwock and branches from Warsaw, Lodz, Kaluszyn and Chelm to Lithuania, and pleaded for $4,000 from the Joint to rescue the remainder still in mortal danger in Poland.

title_en: Three Tomchei Tmimim bochurim reach Vilna after border crossing
summary_en: On the night of 29 Tevet, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik, R. Yosef Menachem Mendel Tannenbaum, and R. Menachem Zev Greenglas arrived in Vilna.
story_body: After zig-zagging through Slonim, Lida, Oshmany, Globoka, Postov and Sventzian, dodging border guards and changing currency twice, the group of bochurim crossed the second border on the night of 28 Tevet and reached Vilna the next night. They found Tomchei Tmimim already operating in the Apatow Kloiz with dozens of bochurim from Otwock.

title_en: Rebbe welcomes new Vilna arrivals and urges them to summon others
summary_en: On 8 Shevat the Rebbe Rayatz wrote from Riga blessing Greenglas, Tannenbaum and Reitchik on their arrival in Vilna and pressing them to urgently summon remaining students.
story_body: Receiving Greenglas's report that the three bochurim had reached Vilna, the Rebbe replied on 8 Shevat 5700 with effusive blessing and a pressing instruction: write at once to every remaining talmid scattered across Poland to come to Vilna without delay. He demanded a list of names contacted, warning that 'the time is exceedingly precious.'

title_en: List of 43 students at Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna compiled
summary_en: An archival roster dated 31 January 1940 (21 Shevat 5700) lists 43 bochurim studying at the re-established Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna.
story_body: Secretary R. Moshe Leib Rothstein compiled a detailed register of the bochurim who had reached Vilna, recording their origins, ages, and arrival dates, plus those still stuck at the border. A photograph of the 31 January 1940 list of 43 students survives in the archive. Most of those listed were later saved via Russia-Japan-China, though not all.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz cables New York demanding Joint funding for student rescue
summary_en: On 26 Shevat the Rebbe cabled Jacobson and Lavut, demanding pressure on the Joint to fund Pesach relief, evacuation of 200 students, and rescue of six rabbis' families.
story_body: After Tropper of the European Joint deferred his earlier appeal, the Rebbe Rayatz wired R. Yisroel Jacobson and R. Shmuel Levitin in New York on 26 Shevat 5700, itemizing $5,000 for Pesach aid, $4,000 to rescue 200 yeshiva students, and $5,143 to bring six rabbis and their families to the US. He instructed them to meet Rosen urgently and recruit Kramer and Dr. Jung to lobby the Joint.

title_en: Reitchik sends detailed escape report and rescue updates to the Rebbe
summary_en: On Motzaei Shabbat Ki Tisa, 15 Adar I, R. Shmuel Dovid Reitchik wrote the Rebbe a full account of his escape and the names of students still trapped at borders.
story_body: From Vilna, Reitchik catalogued his entire route to the Rebbe and reported on bochurim still stuck near borders in Oshmany, Lida and Sventzian, plus those rescued via Mendel Tenenbaum. He proposed sending an emissary back across the border to bring the remaining students and the chossid Chaim Meir Lis, and noted that the Vilna yeshiva had already drawn other bochurim attracted to Chassidus.

title_en: Greenglas reports widening rescue correspondence to the Rebbe
summary_en: On 19 Adar I, R. Menachem Zev Greenglas reported writing to scattered students across Poland urging them to reach Vilna at once.
story_body: Following the Rebbe's directive, Greenglas wrote from Vilna to bochurim in Sidlowice, Suchedniow, Chmielnik, Pociejow, and Lodz, naming specific talmidim to bring along. He also reported on shtot rabbanim who had hosted and fed Tomchei Tmimim students in Otwock during the war's opening months, including Rabbi Yechiel Yeshaya Weinberg of Yendrzejov.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz replies with welcome blessing to Reitchik in Vilna
summary_en: On 25 Adar I the Rebbe Rayatz responded to Reitchik's report with a Bruchim Habaim blessing and exhortation to succeed in learning.
story_body: Replying from Riga on 25 Adar I 5700 (Igros Kodesh vol. 14, letter 5261), the Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged Reitchik's safe arrival in Tomchei Tmimim, blessed him, and reminded him to follow the directives in the Rebbe's general letter to the students - to succeed in learning and become a G-d-fearing chossid and lamdan.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga for Stockholm en route to America
summary_en: At the end of Adar I 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz left Riga for Stockholm, continuing on to the United States.
story_body: After two months in Riga coordinating the rescue of his yeshiva students from Poland and Soviet-held territory, the Rebbe Rayatz left for Stockholm at the end of Adar I 5700. From Stockholm he continued onward to the United States, where he would arrive that spring and re-establish the center of Chabad.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz issues general letter pledging not to rest until students saved
summary_en: In a Nisan 5700 general letter, the Rebbe Rayatz publicly pledged to not rest until he had rescued every Tomchei Tmimim talmid still trapped in Poland.
story_body: Writing his klali letter in Nisan 5700 (Igros Kodesh vol. 5, letter 1181), the Rebbe Rayatz described in Yiddish the terror of being trapped under bombs in Warsaw with hundreds of his Tomchei Tmimim students. He declared his life-mission upon being rescued: to do everything in his power to save every dear talmid chacham still left behind in Poland.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz urges students to flee Poland for the Vilna yeshiva
summary_en: On 3 Adar I 5700, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote from Riga urging students to hurry to the Vilna yeshiva and to mobilize one another to escape Poland.
story_body: Still based in Riga before his journey to New York, the Rebbe Rayatz sent a letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 5, no. 1153) to one of the Tomchei Temimim students. He instructed each student to write to his peers in Poland — including those at the Chelm branch and other smaller yeshivot — to rouse them to come, to seek out missing students, and to push past every obstacle to reach the yeshiva.

title_en: Greenglass reports to Rebbe on students trapped in Poland
summary_en: On 10 Adar II 5700, the student Menachem Zev Greenglass wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz about fellow Temimim facing severe obstacles trying to reach Vilna.
story_body: Greenglass relayed letters from Yechezkel Shpiorvach of Kombin and Yitzchak Stulman of Bichawe, both of whom asked the Rebbe to arouse heavenly mercy on their behalf as they struggled to cross the closed Polish-Lithuanian border. His report was part of the steady stream of intelligence the Rebbe was receiving about scattered Tomchei Temimim students.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz in New York describes plight of European yeshivot
summary_en: On 17 Adar II 5700, shortly after arriving in New York, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to supporters that the situation of his European yeshivot was dire and some students still needed to be smuggled out of Poland.
story_body: Writing in Yiddish (Igrot Kodesh vol. 12, no. 4362), the Rebbe described how part of his students were already in Vilna while others remained in Poland and had to be brought across the border. The letter served as a discreet appeal for help in continuing the rescue effort from the safety of America.

title_en: Soviet Union occupies Lithuania during Shavuot
summary_en: On Shavuot 5700 the Soviets occupied Lithuania, fusing Vilna into the same Soviet bloc as Russian-held Poland and making border smuggling vastly harder.
story_body: With both eastern Poland and Lithuania now under Soviet rule, the smugglers who had been bringing Tomchei Temimim students into Vilna lost their motivation: any 'merchandise' they delivered would simply remain under the same Soviet authorities. The shift dramatically tightened the noose around the students still stranded in Poland.

title_en: Vilna Temimim send coded letter to Rebbe about arrested students
summary_en: On 19 Tammuz 5700, students in Vilna sent the Rebbe a heavily coded letter reporting Soviet arrests of Tomchei Temimim and renewed efforts to smuggle them out.
story_body: Disguising names and events as a commercial correspondence about 'merchants' and 'merchandise,' the students reported that Shmuel Arbis, Avraham Rayevski, and Shraga of Lodz had been imprisoned, while Yisrael Ratzer was in hiding. They feared the prisoners would be deported to Siberia and described how R. Yehuda Eber, then in Riga, had authorized resuming costly smuggling attempts despite tighter Soviet border controls.

title_en: R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis writes Rebbe about wife's plan to flee Poland
summary_en: On 7 Tishrei 5701, R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis informed the Rebbe that his wife Golda had registered to leave Biala for Vilna, fearing she might share his brother's fate of Siberian exile.
story_body: Lis, who served as mashgiach in the Vilna yeshiva, had left his wife Golda and daughters Rachel Miriam and Bluma behind in Biala. He worried that registering to cross into Soviet-held Lithuania could mean deportation to Siberia, as had happened to his older brother Chaim Meir. His family ultimately remained in Poland and perished in the Holocaust while he escaped via Shanghai to America.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz directs weekly correspondence with scattered Temimim
summary_en: On 15 Kislev 5701, the Rebbe Rayatz instructed R. Moshe Pinchas Katz to maintain a weekly written link with Tomchei Temimim students in Vilna, Riga, and Poland.
story_body: In Igrot Kodesh vol. 5, no. 1310, the Rebbe urged that the students report regularly on their physical and spiritual state and receive news in return, so a meaningful bond could be sustained across the war zone. The directive came just as mail between Europe and the United States was beginning to break down entirely.

title_en: R. Lis writes from Shanghai pleading for news of wife and children
summary_en: On 14 Cheshvan 5702, R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis wrote to the Rebbe from Shanghai begging for any word from his wife and children in Poland, after ten months of silence.
story_body: Having reached Shanghai with the rest of the Tomchei Temimim refugees, Lis appealed to the Rebbe to help locate his family and send whatever aid was possible, since he himself could do nothing from East Asia. The Rebbe responded (Igrot Kodesh vol. 6, no. 1604) with consolation and a prayer for good news, but Golda and the daughters never escaped — they perished in the Holocaust while Lis survived alone and continued on to America.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in Riga after escaping Warsaw
summary_en: On 5 Tevet 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in Riga after escaping Nazi-occupied Warsaw.
story_body: Following his dramatic rescue from Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz reached Riga on 5 Tevet 5700. From there he immediately began encouraging the Tomchei Tmimim students who had also fled to Vilna, urging them to maintain their studies. His arrival in Riga marked the start of a transitional period before his eventual emigration to the United States.

title_en: Rebbe writes to Vilna students about the yeshiva's transitional state
summary_en: On 20 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to the Vilna yeshiva students through R. Shmuel Zalmanov and R. Moshe Leib Rodstein.
story_body: Writing from Riga on 20 Tevet 5700, the Rebbe Rayatz acknowledged the temporary arrangements established for Tomchei Tmimim in Vilna and asked every student to understand that the yeshiva was in a state of transition and preparation. The letter was carried by R. Shmuel Zalmanov and R. Moshe Leib Rodstein, who were helping run the yeshiva-in-exile.

title_en: Rebbe urges Vilna students to greater diligence
summary_en: On 25 Shvat 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to three Vilna students urging them to greater diligence in study and avodah.
story_body: The Rebbe addressed Yosef Hakohen Bornstein (Portowicz), Menachem Zev Greenglass and Avraham Yitzchak Garfinkel, noting that while the yeshiva was reorganizing well, the spiritual impact expected of the students was not yet evident. He pressed them to strengthen both their study and their avodah shebalev.

title_en: Rebbe endorses the Hassidic-lineage students' union
summary_en: On 11 Adar I 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz endorsed the new union of Hassidic-lineage yeshiva students.
story_body: Responding to a letter dated 4 Adar I, the Rebbe approved the founding of an union of students of Hassidic lineage who were studying in the Lithuanian yeshivot of Kamenitz, Kletzk, Pinsk, Bialystok, Lomza, Ostrow-Brisk, Chachmei Lublin, Tomchei Tmimim and Slonim. He praised the new bylaws, the spiritual committee and the executive board, and emphasized that success would depend on the spiritual committee's commitment.

title_en: Group photo of Tomchei Tmimim students taken in Vilna
summary_en: On 17 Adar I 5700 (Feb 26, 1940), the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim students and faculty were photographed.
story_body: A series of group photographs of the Vilna Tomchei Tmimim students, mashgiach R. Eliyahu Moshe Lis, and administrators including R. Moshe Leib Rodstein, R. Shmuel Zalmanov and R. Yitzchak Dov Ber Ushpal were taken on 17 Adar I 5700. These photos are among the few surviving images of the yeshiva-in-exile in Vilna.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz departs Riga en route to the United States
summary_en: At the end of Adar I 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz set out from Riga to the United States.
story_body: Together with his family and secretaries R. Chaim Liberman, R. Chaim Mordechai Aizik Hodakov and R. Nissan Mindel, the Rebbe began his journey to America. On 27 Adar I 5700 he wrote en route to the Vilna students, asking the senior students in particular to take responsibility for every aspect of the yeshiva and to conduct it in the spirit of Tomchei Tmimim as it had been in Otwock.

title_en: Rebbe requests reports on the Hassidic yeshiva students' union
summary_en: On 9 Nissan 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz asked the union's leaders to send him details of their gatherings.
story_body: The Rebbe expressed pleasure at hearing of the students' gatherings and asked to be informed of the topics of the talks. He requested copies of meeting records, the names of students at each yeshiva, and the founding regulations along with any additions.

title_en: Rebbe encourages Avraham Tzvi Segal to join Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: On 13 Nissan 5700 the Rebbe encouraged Pinsk student Avraham Tzvi Segal in his desire to study at Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Responding to the Pinsk student's longing for a chassidic yeshiva, the Rebbe told him to thank Hashem for awakening such a desire and assured him that Hashem had arranged the opportunity to realize it at Tomchei Tmimim. Segal eventually became a student at the Vilna yeshiva and its union secretary.

title_en: Lag BaOmer farbrengen held at Tomchei Tmimim Vilna
summary_en: On Lag BaOmer 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch led a farbrengen at the Vilna yeshiva attended by local anash.
story_body: Mashpia R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch arranged that the Kerzner minyan announce the farbrengen, and over a minyan from each of the Kerzner and Apatow chassidim joined. At the gathering he repeated the maamar 'Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu Ba B'Trunya' of the Rebbe Rashab.

title_en: Rabbi Baruch reports to the Rebbe on Vilna yeshiva life
summary_en: On 23 Iyar 5700 R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch sent a detailed report to the Rebbe about Vilna yeshiva activities.
story_body: Baruch described a kiddusha rabba for new arriving students that ran until evening, the Lag BaOmer and Pesach Sheni farbrengens, and the system he had instituted for monitoring both nigleh and chassidus learning. At the time there were 26 students in the senior group.

title_en: Soviet army enters Vilna on Shavuot eve
summary_en: On Shavuot eve 5700, Soviet tanks rolled past the Vilna yeshiva's beis hamidrash as students recited Tikkun Leil Shavuot.
story_body: During the recitation of Tikkun Leil Shavuot, students heard the heavy chains of Soviet tanks moving on the main street opposite the yeshiva. The Red Army was occupying Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. A heavy dread fell over the Jewish community, especially Torah students, but the Soviets initially refrained from closing the yeshivot and allowed the Joint to continue supporting Jewish refugees.

title_en: Rebbe replies to Rabbi Baruch's Vilna yeshiva report
summary_en: On 14 Sivan 5700 the Rebbe responded with satisfaction to R. Baruch's detailed report on the Vilna yeshiva.
story_body: The Rebbe wrote that he greatly enjoyed the detailed account of the students and anash of Lithuania and asked to be kept informed of subsequent reports from anash. He blessed the students and confirmed that the arrangements Baruch had set in place at the yeshiva were excellent.

title_en: Rebbe asks union manager to send regular updates
summary_en: On 19 Sivan 5700 the Rebbe asked Avraham Tzvi Segal to write him regularly about the union's progress.
story_body: Writing to Segal, the Rebbe asked him to keep him informed regarding fellow students in and outside the union. He blessed all the students with success in study and yiras shamayim, that they should widen the borders of bnei Torah and illuminate the darkness of the world.

title_en: Rebbe writes Dr. Yang that yeshivot continue under Soviet rule
summary_en: On Erev Shabbat Shelach 5700 the Rebbe wrote to Dr. Yang that despite Soviet occupation, the Lithuanian and Latvian yeshivot remained intact.
story_body: The Rebbe reported receiving telegrams from Vilna and Riga indicating that, despite the entry of Soviet forces into Lithuania and Latvia, the situation of the yeshivot was unchanged and their continued operation had not been impaired. He confirmed the wellbeing of the yeshivot and 'our dear students.'

title_en: Vilna yeshiva students begin learning trades
summary_en: On 18 Tammuz 5700 senior Vilna students began learning trades including shechita, sofrus and milah.
story_body: R. Baruch reported that Yosef Weinberg, Gershon Chanovitz and Moshe Eliyahu Gerlitzky began learning poultry shechita (about six weeks of training, two hours daily). Menachem Zev Greenglass and Chaim Leib Praffs took up stam writing for four weeks, three hours daily, while Tzvi Fuchs began learning milah. Baruch approved these vocational studies given wartime conditions.

title_en: Rebbe approves vocational training for Vilna students
summary_en: On 17 Av 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz approved the Vilna students learning shechita, sofrus and crafts.
story_body: Writing to R. Baruch, the Rebbe endorsed Yosef Weinberg and Gershon Chanovitz's shechita studies and Menachem Zev Greenglass and Chaim Leib's stam studies. He suggested that if other students were similarly inspired, an 'artel' of craftsmen should be organized among the students, given the conditions of the time.

title_en: Rebbe directs Kollel Chabad funds to support Vilna yeshiva
summary_en: On 25 Av 5700 the Rebbe instructed that Kollel Chabad funds collected in Lithuania be redirected to the Vilna yeshiva.
story_body: Through coded language about a 'Ramban commentary,' the Rebbe arranged for monies collected in Lithuania for Kollel Chabad (Kupat Rabbi Meir Baal Hanes) to be given to R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch to support the Vilna yeshiva. The Rebbe undertook to remit equivalent funds to Kollel Chabad in Eretz Yisroel.

title_en: Menachem Zev Greenglass travels to Telz yeshiva
summary_en: On 15 Elul 5700 Menachem Zev Greenglass was sent to the Telz yeshiva on a mission for Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Sent by mashpia R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch, Greenglass traveled to Telz primarily to enroll a talented young orphan in the yeshiva there. While there he also studied with and held farbrengens with the local Hassidic-lineage students.

title_en: Chai Elul farbrengen at Telz led by Greenglass
summary_en: On Chai Elul 5700, Menachem Zev Greenglass led a Hassidic farbrengen in Telz attended by close to 30 students.
story_body: After mincha at the home of R. Tzvi Merkin, close to three minyanim of students gathered, including the son-in-law of Reb Elchanan Wasserman. Greenglass spoke about the chiddush of the Baal Shem Tov, sang Chabad niggunim including the niggun of the Alter Rebbe, and recited the maamar of Yom Tov Shel Rosh Hashana 5666.

title_en: Greenglass reports to Rebbe on Telz mission
summary_en: On 7 Tishrei 5701 Greenglass reported to the Rebbe in detail on his recent Telz mission.
story_body: Greenglass described placing the young orphan at the Telz yeshiva with the help of R. Tzvi Merkin and Yehuda Leib Mintz, the Chai Elul farbrengen he had led, and his shiur in Tanya chapter 29 with local Hassidic-lineage students. He also reported on a new student, Yehuda Leib Mintz, with whom he had begun studying maamarim.

title_en: Rabbi Yehoshua Isaac Baruch perishes in the Kovno Shoah
summary_en: On 9 Cheshvan 5702 R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch, mashpia of Tomchei Tmimim Vilna, was murdered in Kovno.
story_body: Before the Rebbe Rayatz left for America in winter 5700, R. Yehoshua Isaac Baruch had traveled from Vilna to Riga to take leave of him. The Rebbe's parting blessing — 'May Hashem help that we merit to meet again with Moshiach' — deeply troubled Baruch, who took it as a prophecy that they would not meet again before the redemption. He was murdered in the Kovno Holocaust on 9 Cheshvan 5702.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz rescued from Warsaw to Riga
summary_en: On 2 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz was rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw and arrived in Riga.
story_body: Having been trapped in Warsaw at the outbreak of World War II, the Rebbe Rayatz was extracted to Riga on 2 Tevet 5700. Once safe in Latvia he immediately turned to organizing the rescue of his Tomchei Tmimim students from Vilna to the United States, opening the long campaign that occupies this chapter.

title_en: Letter to Israel Jacobson urging rescue of 50 students
summary_en: On 14 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote to R. Israel Jacobson, head of Agudas Chabad in America, urging immediate effort to bring fifty Tomchei Tmimim students to the United States.
story_body: The Rebbe stressed that the matter touched the inner foundation of the yeshiva's future in America and asked that everything possible be done with speed. The letter (Igros vol. 5, no. 1133) opened a sustained correspondence with American Chabad activists about routes, visas and funding for the trapped Vilna students.

title_en: Letter to Chief Rabbi Herzog about Palestine certificates
summary_en: On 21 Tevet 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz clarified to Chief Rabbi Isaac Herzog that the five Palestine certificates were meant not for his own family but for endangered yeshiva students.
story_body: Rabbi Herzog had assumed the Rebbe's request for British Mandate certificates was for his own household and granted five. The Rebbe responded that he had requested them to distribute among those in real danger in Europe, and pressed for a larger allotment because of the dire situation he had personally observed in Poland.

title_en: Letter to R. Chaim Ozer requesting 100 Palestine certificates
summary_en: On Isru Chag Pesach 5700 the Rebbe Rayatz asked R. Chaim Ozer Grodzinski to allocate at least one hundred Palestine certificates for Lubavitch students and their teachers.
story_body: Hearing that R. Chaim Ozer was about to receive a batch of British certificates through Rabbi Herzog's intervention, the Rebbe wrote requesting that the committee under R.
