The bar mitzvah came soon after a difficult period in which his protests over class placement nearly resulted in expulsion from Tomchei Tmimim.

title_en: Conference of Chabad rabbanim and wealthy chassidim in Lubavitch
summary_en: In Marcheshvan 5669, prominent Chabad rabbanim and wealthy chassidim gathered in Lubavitch for an unusual conference referenced later by the Frierdiker Rebbe.
story_body: Around Parshas Vayera in Marcheshvan 5669, a notable assembly of senior Chabad rabbanim and wealthy chassidim convened in Lubavitch — alluded to by the Rayatz in a later sicha of Pesach 5694. The author saw R. David Tzvi Chen of Chernigov and R. Yaakov Mordechai Bezpalov of Poltava for the first time. The aliyos in shul that Shabbos required special direction from the Rebbe Rashab himself.

title_en: Passing of the Raza, elder brother of the Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: In the week of Parshas Vayera 5669, R. Zalman Aharon (Raza), elder brother of the Rebbe Rashab, passed away in Vitebsk.
story_body: The Raza, who lived in Vitebsk, passed away during the week of Parshas Vayera 5669. The family withheld the news from the elderly Rebbetzin Rivka, who was still alive. When she insisted on traveling to Vitebsk after a week without letters from her son, an elder of the town, R. Dovber 'Bere Avremkes,' gently told her there was no longer reason to go, and the horses were returned to the stable.

title_en: 19 Kislev farbrengen 5669 closed to younger students
summary_en: At the 19 Kislev 5669 farbrengen, the Rebbe Rashab spoke sharply against state-language primary schools being established in the Pale of Settlement.
story_body: The Tomchei Tmimim administration barred cheder-level students from attending the 19 Kislev 5669 farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab in the large zal. The Rebbe spoke with great bitterness against the founding of Russian-language 'shkoles' for Jewish children, condemning the initiative's patron Baron Horace Ginzburg, who had refused his plea to spare at least Lubavitch. The author later heard that the baron died around Purim that winter.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim branch founded in Babinovitch
summary_en: In 5669 a Tomchei Tmimim branch was established in Babinovitch as an intermediate stage between the Lubavitch cheders and the great hall.
story_body: In 5669 the yeshiva opened a branch in Babinovitch to bridge the gap between the cheder-level shiurim in Lubavitch and the senior bachurim of the large zal. R. Zev Wolf Levitin supervised the nigleh studies and R. Shlomo b. David Risin oversaw Chassidus. A separate group of bachurim continued learning in Horodishtch under R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin.

title_en: Cholera outbreak in the Vitebsk province
summary_en: During the summer of 5669, a cholera epidemic struck the Vitebsk region and nearby provinces, prompting government orders to drink only boiled water.
story_body: In the summer of 5669 the dreaded cholera 'dever' spread through the Vitebsk province and surrounding regions. The Russian authorities ordered that only boiled water be drunk throughout the affected provinces. Large cauldrons of boiling water were kept in the yeshiva at all times, and even the drinking barrel in the zal was filled exclusively from boiled water.

title_en: Rosh Hashanah prayers held in Great Hall at Lubavitch
summary_en: On Rosh Hashanah 5670 (1909), roughly 150 minyanim gathered for prayers in the Great Hall at Lubavitch.
story_body: In 5669 prayers had been held in the Small Hall, but in 5670 a much larger crowd—approximately 150 minyanim—prompted moving the High Holiday services to the Great Hall. During dancing on the second night of Rosh Hashanah after the chassidus discourse, the roof beams began to crack.

title_en: Great Hall at Lubavitch closed after roof beams cracked
summary_en: After dancing on the second night of Rosh Hashanah 5670 caused the roof beams to crack, the Great Hall at Lubavitch was closed.
story_body: During dancing on the second night of Rosh Hashanah 5670, the roof beams of the Great Hall began to give way. Immediately after Rosh Hashanah the hall was closed, and after Sukkot additional support beams were installed from floor to ceiling to brace the structure.

title_en: Simchat Torah farbrengen of Rebbe Rashab in Small Hall, 5670
summary_en: On Simchat Torah 5670 the Rebbe Rashab held a farbrengen in the Small Hall at Lubavitch, speaking emotionally about his father, the Rebbe Maharash.
story_body: Because the Great Hall was closed, the Simchat Torah daytime farbrengen took place in the crowded Small Hall, with the Rebbe Rashab entering through a door from the Maharash's adjoining room. He spoke at length and wept while recalling his father's Simchat Torah and 19 Kislev. Crushing pressure broke tables and benches; his elderly mother Rebbetzin Rivkah and his wife Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah came to plead with him not to overexert himself.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab promises 'Reid' and Maamar that became Kuntres HaAvodah
summary_en: On Simchat Torah 5670, unable to continue the farbrengen due to crowding, the Rebbe Rashab promised to deliver a 'reid' and maamar that later became Kuntres HaAvodah.
story_body: Overcome by heat and pressure of the crowd at the Simchat Torah 5670 farbrengen, the Rebbe Rashab stood and told the chassidim he would not release them until he gave them a 'reid' as Tomchei Temimim required, and a maamar. The discourse was eventually published in 5671 (1910/11) as Kuntres HaAvodah, though it was also called Kuntres 5669.

title_en: Tomchei Temimim branch moves from Bobinovich to Shchedrin
summary_en: At the beginning of 5670 (late 1909), the Tomchei Temimim branch in Bobinovich relocated to Shchedrin.
story_body: The branch served as an intermediate level between the chadarim and the main Lubavitch yeshiva, with roughly sixty students in three classes. The town's householders agreed that about forty students would be supported by hosting meals ('teg'), while twenty would be supported wholly or partly by the Lubavitch yeshiva fund. Students traveled from Lubavitch to Shchedrin after Sukkot 5670.

title_en: R. Zalman Dov of Dribin appointed Rosh Mesivta in Shchedrin
summary_en: R. Zalman Dov of Dribin, a noted Chabad scholar, was appointed Rosh Mesivta for the Tomchei Temimim branch in Shchedrin.
story_body: R. Zalman Dov, a great talmid of R. Tzvi Neta Gnessin of Pochep, was selected from among the outstanding learners of Chabad chassidim. R. Shaul Dov Zislin was chosen as mashpia and director of the Shchedrin branch.

title_en: R. Yehoshua Arsh begins teaching at Tomchei Temimim Lubavitch
summary_en: In the winter of 5670 R. Yehoshua Arsh was accepted for the first time as a Rosh Mesivta at Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch.
story_body: The memoirist studied that winter under R. Yehoshua Arsh, who had just been hired. The class learned tractate Kiddushin together with all of Tosafot over the course of the winter through Pesach, mastering the material thoroughly.

title_en: Move of Shchedrin students delayed; learning in Great Hall
summary_en: After Pesach 5670, students bound for Shchedrin were forced to remain in Lubavitch and learn in the Great Hall until after Shavuot.
story_body: Although the students were supposed to leave for Shchedrin after Pesach, the host town was not ready to receive them. They remained in Lubavitch, studying in the Great Hall under supervision of R. Yosef Friedman of Rogachov for nigleh and R. Moshe of Zembin for chassidus.

title_en: Examinations at Tomchei Temimim attended by Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: In spring 5670, examinations of younger students at Tomchei Temimim were conducted by senior bochurim, with the Rebbe Rayatz entering during the test.
story_body: The memoirist and his brother-in-law Alter Beilin were tested by R. Raphael Cohen of Germanovitch and R. Avraham Eli Plotkin in Ketubot 74b. The exam took place Friday morning of erev Shabbat, and the Rebbe Rayatz, then director of Tomchei Temimim, entered during the testing. The author notes the awe his presence inspired and that they passed successfully.

title_en: Author moves to Shchedrin branch after Shavuot 5670
summary_en: After Shavuot 5670, the memoirist relocated to the Shchedrin branch of Tomchei Temimim to continue his studies.
story_body: At Shchedrin he heard a shiur in nigleh from R. Moshe Mordechai Amrami (Poharelsky) of Pochep on tractate Bava Batra. The two classes were combined under R. Shaul Dov Zislin's direction, and the mashgiach for nigleh was R. Yaakov Baruch Krasik.

title_en: Rosh Hashanah 5671 journey from Shchedrin to Lubavitch
summary_en: For Rosh Hashanah 5671, the new Shchedrin students traveled together to Lubavitch despite the yeshiva refusing travel expenses.
story_body: Eighteen students obtained permission to travel only after depositing five rubles each for return travel. Joined by chassidim from Bobruisk-area towns, they rented a dedicated train car from Zlobin to Orsha and spent the journey singing chassidic niggunim. R. Shaul Dov Zislin led the lively farbrengen on the train, drawing curious onlookers from other cars.

title_en: Search for new Rosh Mesivta in Shchedrin in 5671
summary_en: In 5671 the Shchedrin branch searched for a new Rosh Mesivta but could not find a suitable candidate.
story_body: Among the candidates was Nachum Eliezer of Paritch, a brilliant scholar with semicha from the Rogatchover Gaon. Although he delivered two impressive shiurim, he was not hired due to a health concern. Several other candidates were tried unsuccessfully.

title_en: Tomchei Temimim Tomchei Tmimim founds Toras Emes yeshiva in Hebron
summary_en: In summer 5671, the Rebbe Rashab announced the founding of a yeshiva in Eretz Yisrael, dispatching R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin with students to Hebron.
story_body: After Shavuot 5671 (1911) it became known that the Rebbe Rashab was establishing a yeshiva in the Holy Land, choosing Hebron as its location. R. Shlomo Zalman Havlin traveled with five selected students—R. Yechezkel Feigin, R. Alter Simchovich, R. Hillel of Pochep, R. Yisrael Zalman of Yanovich, and R. Tzvi Katzav of Hadiach—along with three volunteers who joined them.

title_en: Author begins learning at Great Hall Lubavitch, 5672
summary_en: For Rosh Hashanah 5672 (fall 1911) the memoirist's class moved to learn in the Great Hall at Lubavitch.
story_body: R. Shilem Koratin was appointed mashgiach for chassidus that winter, with R. Yaakov Baruch Krasik supervising nigleh and R. Shmuel Gronem Esterman serving as mashpia. They learned Derech Mitzvotecha until R. Gronem fell ill with eye trouble and had to travel for extended treatment, after which the students learned on their own from the Rebbe Rashab's maamarim.

title_en: Passing of R. Michoel Bliner, mashpia of Tomchei Temimim
summary_en: R. Michoel Bliner, mashpia at Tomchei Temimim, passed away on Motzaei Shabbat 28 Cheshvan 5672 in Lubavitch.
story_body: On Yom Kippur 5672 R. Michoel had asked to be brought into the Great Hall where the Rebbe Rashab prayed, with his bed placed against the wall between the hall and the second room. The Rebbe Rashab spoke with him on Yom Kippur, discussing whether he was permitted to forgo fasting, though he chose to fast anyway. The Rebbe Rashab attended the funeral that Motzaei Shabbat through deep mud, and the Rebbe Rayatz carried the bier, losing a galosh in the mire en route to the cemetery.

title_en: Older bochurim assigned to learn Chassidus with younger students at Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: A new study arrangement at Tomchei Tmimim paired senior bochurim with younger students to deepen their Chassidus learning.
story_body: At the start of 5673, after the mashpia R. Shilem Kuratin suspected that several students were not committing themselves to learning Chassidus, a new arrangement was instituted in Tomchei Tmimim. A few of the senior bochurim were paired with younger students to study Chassidus together. The author was assigned to R. Nota Pinski.

title_en: Group of lax students expelled from Tomchei Tmimim, most readmitted
summary_en: Students dismissed from Tomchei Tmimim for laxity in seder were mostly readmitted after pleading and commitments to improve.
story_body: During 5673 a group of students grew lax with seder, rushing through tefillah in 35–40 minutes after Chassidus shiur to get to nigleh learning. R. Shilem Kuratin spoke with the Rebbe Rashab, who said he preferred dozens of proper students to hundreds of indifferent ones. The students were expelled, and after a week or more of pleading and promises most were readmitted, though one left Lubavitch entirely.

title_en: Author's first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: The author entered his first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab, who guided him on tefillah b'peirush hamilos.
story_body: In the winter of 5673 the author entered his first yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab, marking his entry among the bochurim devoted to inner avodah. He had prepared with intense Krias Shema al hamita and committed to at least six hours of Chassidus study daily plus extended tefillah. The Rebbe instructed him to daven b'peirush hamilos and to connect the themes of Pesukei D'Zimra and Birchos Yotzer, which would open the heart.

title_en: 19 Kislev 5673 farbrengen and maamar with Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab led a marathon 19 Kislev celebration with the four-levels sicha, a 40-minute niggun, and a maamar from the Hemshech Tarav.
story_body: 19 Kislev 5673 fell on a Friday, with the main celebration and meal held Motzei Shabbat in the great hall. The Rebbe Rashab came at about 10 PM and delivered the famous two-hour sicha on the four levels of tzaddik, yashar, tamim, and chassid, followed by the niggun for forty minutes and the 19 Kislev maamar from the Hemshech Tarav. He spoke of being an etzem unaffected by higher or lower, and said that leaving Lubavitch (for medical travel abroad) was "like separating from life" since his whole vitality was speaking Chassidus.

title_en: Maamar on Kabbalas Shabbos of 10 Teves 5673
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab delivered a maamar at Kabbalas Shabbos of 10 Teves, with students listening from outside the window in the snow.
story_body: 10 Teves 5673 fell on Friday erev Shabbos. The Rebbe Rashab davened Kabbalas Shabbos at home, and announced that students could eat something and then he would deliver a maamar. The doors were closed by the time the author and others returned; they stood outside the window in the bitter cold and snow listening to the maamar delivered b'kol ram, and R. Shimshon Vitebsker was let in mid-maamar through a chain of doors opened by the Rayatz's daughter Chana.

title_en: Chol HaMoed Pesach 5673 Rayatz farbrengen in the Raza's rooms
summary_en: The Rayatz farbrenged with senior bochurim Chol HaMoed Pesach 5673, teaching that each day must surpass the previous.
story_body: During Chol HaMoed Pesach 5673 the Rayatz farbrenged with the senior bochurim in the rooms of the RaZ"A (R. Zalman Aharon). He told how the Rashbatz had once made him pay six kopecks for whiskey and two for cake to hear a chassidishe vort, then delayed telling it: the parable of the wagon driver's apprentice who, after a fast on 17 Tammuz, said "today is not yesterday" — meaning each day must be better than the last.

title_en: Simchas Torah 5673 Rayatz farbrengen with the Tzarske familye remark
summary_en: The Rayatz farbrenged Simchas Torah 5673 and dubbed R. Shilem and R. Elchanan Dov a "royal family" not to be touched.
story_body: On Simchas Torah the Rayatz farbrenged in the same apartment, in the room of R. Nachman the meshares (then occupied by R. Shlomo Leib Eliezerov). R. Elchanan Dov Morozov made a witty barb at R. Shilem, who quoted "sent forth his hand against him." The Rayatz responded by calling them "tzarske familye" (royal family), and someone added in Russian: "He will lie many klaftern deep, but tzarske familye — don't touch the royal family."

title_en: Zhuravichi delegation to Rebbe Rashab over land sold to non-Jews
summary_en: A delegation from Zhuravichi petitioned the Rebbe Rashab to intervene after chassidim sold the town's pastureland.
story_body: In summer 5673 the author's father came with R. Zev Brulin, secretary of the Zhuravichi kehilla, on a special mission to the Rebbe Rashab. The wealthy chassidim R. Shmuel Trainin of Petersburg and R. Yehoshua Rosenkin of Mogilev had bought the courtyard and land surrounding Zhuravichi from non-Jewish landowners and were now reselling it, leaving the town with no pasture for its cattle; the delegation asked the Rebbe to intervene on behalf of the town's poor.

title_en: Author's sister Sasha Hinde emigrates to the United States
summary_en: The author's sister emigrated to the United States in summer 5673, prompting a yechidus over travel home.
story_body: In summer 5673 the author's sister, Mrs. Sasha Hinde, traveled to the United States. The father asked the Rebbe Rashab for permission for the author to come home from yeshiva to bid her farewell, but the Rebbe questioned the trip in the middle of zman. During the same yechidus the author received approval to begin laying Rabbeinu Tam tefillin upon turning 18 that Kislev.

title_en: Rostov delegation brings 12 students to Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: The Rostov kehilla, beyond the Pale of Settlement, sent 12 children to train at Tomchei Tmimim as future klei kodesh.
story_body: In 5674 a delegation came from the Rostov-on-Don kehilla to evaluate the yeshiva. Since Rostov was beyond the Pale of Settlement, the community lacked shochtim, rabbanim, mohalim and other religious functionaries, so they decided to send their children to be trained as future klei kodesh. After visiting several yeshivos, they were impressed by Lubavitch and enrolled twelve students, hiring R. Moshe Rosenblum as their melamed.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab travels abroad for health reasons, early Kislev 5674
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab left Lubavitch for medical treatment abroad in early Kislev 5674, returning only after Pesach.
story_body: Due to his weakened health, the Rebbe Rashab left for abroad around the week of Parshas Vayetzei, in the beginning of Kislev 5674, so that he was not in Lubavitch for 19 Kislev that year. Wealthy chassidim later traveled to be with him for Purim 5674. He did not return to Lubavitch until after Pesach 5674.

title_en: Bris milah of R. Shilem Kuratin's son on 19 Kislev 5674
summary_en: Shneur Zalman, son of R. Shilem Kuratin, had his bris on 19 Kislev 5674 with the Rayatz as sandek.
story_body: A son was born to the mashgiach R. Shilem Kuratin, with the bris milah held on 19 Kislev 5674. The child was named Shneur Zalman, and the Rayatz was honored with sandekaus. The Rebbe Rashab was abroad that year, so the 19 Kislev celebrations were led by mashpi'im and anash.

title_en: Hidden Chanukah farbrengen at a tinsmith's house, Nun Hei of Chanukah 5674
summary_en: R. Shmuel Gronem held a hidden farbrengen for 30 bochurim on the 5th night of Chanukah 5674 and taught a new niggun.
story_body: On the 5th night of Chanukah 5674 a secret farbrengen was held with R. Shmuel Gronem Esterman. Because doctors had forbidden him whiskey due to eye trouble, the gathering was kept hidden; the talmid Yitzchak Raskin had bought a menorah at a tinsmith's workshop near Chochlukeh Street and arranged to use the place. About thirty bochurim attended; R. Gronem taught them the niggun "Mipnei mah yarda haneshama" and spoke discreetly about shemiras habris.

title_en: Passing of Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Maharash, 10 Shevat 5674
summary_en: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Maharash, passed away in Lubavitch on 10 Shevat 5674 while her son was in Menton.
story_body: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Rebbe Maharash, passed away on Friday morning, 10 Shevat 5674. She had caught a cold earlier in the week, which developed into pneumonia; Dr. Lieberman of Vitebsk was summoned, and on Thursday night R. Nachum Glass traveled to Vitebsk to bring oxygen, but she died that Friday morning. The Rebbe Rashab was in Menton at the time and the Rayatz led the levaya, choosing a plot opposite the ohel of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Maharash, conditional on the Rebbe Rashab's approval.

title_en: Rayatz travels abroad to console his father after Rebbetzin Rivka's passing
summary_en: The Rayatz left for Germany after Shabbos to console his father, who ordered round-the-clock learning in his mother's room.
story_body: On Motzei Shabbos following the levaya, the Rayatz traveled to Germany to comfort his father the Rebbe Rashab and to report on the funeral arrangements. When someone pointed out that his hat was not properly placed, he replied that he never paid attention to such things, certainly not now. From abroad the Rebbe Rashab sent a telegram instructing that ten bochurim study around the clock for the entire shloshim in his mother's room.

title_en: Purim 5674 farbrengen abroad with wealthy chassidim
summary_en: Wealthy chassidim traveled abroad for a long Purim 5674 farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: For Purim 5674, while the Rebbe Rashab was still abroad for medical treatment, wealthy chassidim of anash traveled to be with him. There was a long farbrengen with wondrous teachings. The Rebbe returned to Lubavitch only after Pesach 5674.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab returns to Lubavitch after Pesach 5674
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab returned to Lubavitch after Pesach 5674 and resumed his Tarav Hemshech on Shavuos.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab returned to Lubavitch after Pesach 5674, ending the absence that had begun the previous Kislev. On Shavuos he resumed delivering the Hemshech that he had begun on Shavuos Tarav ("BeSha'a SheHikdimu"), continuing without break until Shabbos Parshas Vayera 5676.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab resumes Hemshech Tarav on Shavuos 5674
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab resumed his Hemshech Tarav on Shavuos 5674 with maamarim on tohu and tikkun.
story_body: On Shavuos 5674 the Rebbe Rashab resumed delivering the Hemshech he had begun on Shavuos Tarav ("BeSha'a SheHikdimu"). The maamarim of summer 5674 dealt with the themes of tohu and tikkun, offering deep and luminous explanations. The series continued without interruption until Parshas Vayera 5676.

title_en: Shabbos Beha'aloscha 5674 at the Zaalshe dacha
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab at the Zaalshe dacha spoke on the root of middos above seichel on Shabbos Beha'aloscha 5674.
story_body: On Shabbos Parshas Beha'aloscha 5674 the author was at the Rebbe Rashab's summer dacha at Zaalshe. The Rebbe spoke about the root of the middos that transcends the intellect. The author would visit Zaalshe again that summer for Parshas Pinchas and Parshas Ki Setze.

title_en: Shabbos Pinchas 5674 at the Zaalshe dacha
summary_en: A Shabbos at the Zaalshe dacha on Parshas Pinchas 5674 drew the mashgiach and prominent guests from Warsaw.
story_body: On Shabbos Parshas Pinchas 5674 the author was again at Zaalshe, joined by R. Shilem Kuratin the mashgiach on Chassidus and guests including the maskil R. Pesach Frenkel and the tamim R. Shraga Feivish Zalmanov of Warsaw-Klimovich, son-in-law of R. Yosef Yuzik Horowitz of Warsaw.

title_en: Outbreak of World War I and Rebbe Rashab's prophecy of a long war
summary_en: At the outbreak of WWI the Rebbe Rashab predicted a long, mutually destructive war and told chassidim to keep their businesses running.
story_body: At the start of Elul 5674 several wealthy chassidim came to Zaalshe to ask the Rebbe Rashab's advice as World War I broke out. They assumed Russia would quickly be forced to seek peace against Germany and considered halting their business. The Rebbe told them to continue their commerce, saying the war would be long, in his words: "einer vet dem andern einshlingen un vet zikh mit im derverger" (one will swallow the other and choke on him together).

title_en: Last maamar of Hemshech Tarav: Shabbos Vayera 5676 "Cholas Ahava"
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab delivered the closing maamar of Hemshech Tarav on Shabbos Vayera 5676, the day before leaving Lubavitch.
story_body: On Shabbos Parshas Vayera 5676 the Rebbe Rashab delivered the maamar on the inyan of "cholas ahava," the final maamar of the Hemshech that had begun on Shavuos Tarav. The next day, Sunday Parshas Chayei Sara, the Rebbe and his entire household relocated from Lubavitch.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab relocates from Lubavitch with his family
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab left the town of Lubavitch with his entire family the day after Shabbos Vayera 5676.
story_body: On Sunday Parshas Chayei Sara 5676, the day after delivering the closing maamar of his great Hemshech, the Rebbe Rashab departed Lubavitch with his entire family. The town of Lubavitch had been the Rebbes' seat since the Mitteler Rebbe; the departure marked the end of the Lubavitch era as the front lines of WWI advanced.

title_en: Passing of Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah, 13 Shevat 5702, in the United States
summary_en: Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah passed away in the United States on 13 Shevat 5702 in the same manner as Rebbetzin Rivka.
story_body: Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah, wife of the Rebbe Rashab and mother of the Rayatz, passed away on Shabbos morning 13 Shevat 5702 in the United States. As her mother-in-law Rebbetzin Rivka had decades earlier, she asked her attendant for a siddur, davened, and handed it back; when the attendant turned to put it away she had already passed. The Rayatz was in Chicago on klal matters at the time, mirroring the Rebbe Rashab's absence at the petira of his own mother.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab begins Rosh Hashanah discourse on divine unity
summary_en: On Rosh Hashanah 5675 the Rebbe Rashab opened a new chassidic discourse explaining 'one' from below upward and from above downward.
story_body: At the start of 5675 the Rebbe Rashab began expounding the concept of divine unity in both directions during the Tishrei maamarim. When chozrim asked for elucidation he replied enigmatically that 'the ends and the edges do not yet come together.' Only mid-winter, in the course of further chazara, did he indicate that the matter had now been clarified.

title_en: Wartime shortage of Calabrian etrogim in Lubavitch
summary_en: Because of the war the Rebbe Rashab could not obtain Calabrian etrogim for Sukkot 5675, receiving only three from Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: The outbreak of World War I cut off the usual supply of Calabrian etrogim. Three presumed non-grafted etrogim were brought from the Holy Land by R' Shneur Zalman Havlin, who had returned to Lubavitch that summer and was stranded by the war. The Rebbe Rashab was so distressed by the lack of Calabrian etrogim that he developed fever and facial swelling and did not attend shul on the first days of the festival.

title_en: Tzarist conscription of yeshiva students intensifies
summary_en: After Sukkot 5675 the Russian army began calling up successive age cohorts, including many yeshiva students.
story_body: Following Sukkot 5675 the standard call-up of 21-year-olds was followed by ever-younger classes as the war intensified. Most Tomchei Tmimim students were drafted, and many of those discharged could not return to Lubavitch. The campaign reshaped the yeshiva's enrollment for the rest of the war.

title_en: Twenty-year-olds called up for Russian military service
summary_en: In January 1915 the Russian army summoned men born twenty years earlier to military service.
story_body: As the war ground on, Russia expanded conscription downward through the age groups. January 1915 brought the call-up of twenty-year-olds, many of them yeshiva students at Tomchei Tmimim. The yeshiva ranks thinned dramatically as the draft progressed.

title_en: Nineteen-year-olds drafted; author called to register
summary_en: In May 1915 men born in 1896 were summoned for army service; the author registered and received a one-year deferment.
story_body: By May 1915 the Russian military extended the draft to nineteen-year-olds belonging to the 1916 conscription class. The author traveled home, presented himself, received a one-year exemption, and returned to Lubavitch for the summer. The conscription pattern foreshadowed yet younger cohorts being called later that year.

title_en: Eighteen-year-olds drafted into the Russian army
summary_en: In August 1915 the Russian army called up eighteen-year-olds belonging to the 1917 class.
story_body: The widening draft reached the eighteen-year-old cohort by August 1915, followed soon after by the 1918 class. The cumulative effect emptied much of Tomchei Tmimim of its students. The yeshiva struggled to retain a viable learning population.

title_en: Secret farbrengen with R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin before draft
summary_en: Students arranged a clandestine farbrengen with R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin before fellow student Shmuel Kadish Bertanovsky departed for the draft.
story_body: When Shmuel Kadish Bertanovsky had to leave Tomchei Tmimim to present himself for conscription, the author and a few others arranged a covert gathering. Government liquor shops were shut by wartime decree, so Moshe Gurary paid two roubles for a single bottle of kummel. R' Havlin spoke of how Chabad chassidus brings the soul's innermost essence into revealed expression through the intellect and emotions, and the farbrengen lasted from late Thursday night until six in the morning.

title_en: 19 Kislev farbrengen 5675 in Lubavitch
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5675 the Rebbe Rashab held the Chag HaGeulah farbrengen in the large hall and spoke of events in the World of Truth.
story_body: The annual 19 Kislev celebration in 5675 took place in the great hall at Lubavitch. The Rebbe Rashab discussed matters unfolding in the World of Truth; R' Moshe of Zembin asked 'what will become of us?' and the Rebbe responded that one should hold tight to his gartel. Wartime scarcity forced the gathering to make do with unfamiliar liquors, and the Rebbe ended the farbrengen when his wife came to ask that they cease searching for more.

title_en: Inheritance farbrengen for the Horowitz heirs in Lubavitch
summary_en: In Shevat 5675 the heirs of the wealthy R' Yosef Yozik Horowitz held a farbrengen in Lubavitch after settling the inheritance.
story_body: Sons, sons-in-law and a grandson of the late R' Yosef Yozik Horowitz, who had held a monopoly on button sales, came to Lubavitch to divide his estate before the Rebbe Rashab. Once arrangements were finalized they hosted a farbrengen on Thursday night at the home of R' Michael Katzenelnbogen, attended by mashpi'im, melamdim and select students. R' Moshe of Zembin and the Rashbatz debated the relative spiritual stature of the Rebbe Rashab, with R' Yitzchak Magidson defusing tension through niggun.

title_en: Passing of R' Moshe of Zembin in Lubavitch
summary_en: R' Moshe of Zembin passed away in Binyamin's Shtibel in Lubavitch on the Friday after the inheritance farbrengen in Shevat 5675.
story_body: On the morning after the all-night Horowitz farbrengen, R' Moshe of Zembin went to the mikveh and felt unwell. He was brought into the nearby Binyamin's Shtibel, where R' Dovber Shmotkin obtained medicine from Yehoshua's pharmacy that briefly revived him. He died there before Shabbos; the Rebbe Rashab cancelled the planned chassidus and asked whether any further attempts at resuscitation could be made, and the levaya was held on Motzaei Shabbos.

title_en: Wife of R' Elchanan Dov Morozov dies in childbirth
summary_en: The wife of R' Elchanan Dov Morozov died during childbirth in winter 5675 for lack of available physicians.
story_body: In the winter of 5675 the wife of R' Elchanan Dov Morozov, sister of the noted tamim R' Avraham Dovid of Klimavichi, died in childbirth. The Rebbe Rashab attributed her death to the dictum 'there are those who perish without judgment,' since adequate medical care was unavailable in the small town at the moment of need.

title_en: Purim 5675 farbrengen at the Rebbe Rashab's home
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab held a Purim 5675 farbrengen in his dining room, said chassidus, and davened maariv after midnight.
story_body: Purim 5675 began with a small gathering at the Rebbe's table where he discussed knowledge and free will, including whether gentiles possess true bechirah. As the night progressed the entire chassidic community joined and the Rebbe delivered a maamar. Maariv was davened at roughly 1:45 a.m., the latest the author had ever witnessed.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab denounces Kaiser Wilhelm at Simchas Torah farbrengen
summary_en: On Simchas Torah 5676 the Rebbe Rashab spoke harshly of Germany and Kaiser Wilhelm, calling them Amalek.
story_body: At the pre-hakafos farbrengen in his home on Simchas Torah 5676 the Rebbe Rashab spoke at length about Germany and Kaiser Wilhelm. He declared that he had known the Kaiser for thirty-one years, that he was Amalek whose end is destruction, and contrasted the Germans as 'apikorsim Amalekim' with the French and Africans. The farbrengen ran through the night and the hakafos that evening were not held.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab and family leave Lubavitch for the south
summary_en: On Sunday 16 Cheshvan 5676 the Rebbe Rashab and his family departed Lubavitch for safer territory deeper in Russia.
story_body: With the German army nearing Belarussia and Russian authorities seizing Jewish leaders as hostages near the front, the Rashab was forced to leave Lubavitch. Preparations had begun after Sukkot with wooden crates built for the seforim, and on Parshat Vayera he delivered a discourse on the levels of cholat ahavah. On 16 Cheshvan he departed; he stopped in the city of Ariel for several weeks before settling in Rostov-on-Don in the Cossack region.

title_en: Scarlet fever epidemic strikes Lubavitch
summary_en: A scarlet fever epidemic struck children in Lubavitch in winter 5676, killing a yeshiva student and others.
story_body: During the winter of 5676 scarlet fever spread through Lubavitch and children died daily, a calamity locals linked to the homemade liquor production prompted by the government ban. The town rav, R' David Yaakovson, declared a ban on the illicit distilling. One yeshiva student from Homel named Aharon died; his fellow students sat with him around the clock and buried him in Lubavitch.

title_en: Passing of R' Moshe Rosenblum in Rostov
summary_en: The scribe and chassid R' Moshe Rosenblum, who departed Lubavitch with the Rebbe, passed away on 2 Nisan 5680 in Rostov.
story_body: R' Moshe Rosenblum, a distinguished sofer and yerei shamayim, accompanied the Rashab's exile from Lubavitch in 5676. As they left the town he expressed hope to be reunited soon, and the Rebbe replied that he hoped it would be by Pesach. In the event Rosenblum remained in Rostov and died there on 2 Nisan 5680.

title_en: Author arrested as draft evader in Chernigov
summary_en: In mid-Elul 5676 the author was jailed in Chernigov as a deserter after presenting irregular papers during a mobilization.
story_body: On the Rebbe Rashab's advice the author traveled to Chernigov to seek help from the Rabbi Dovid Tzvi Chen rather than register as a rabbi near Zhuravichi. A surprise mobilization led the local police to demand his documents, which were not in order, and he was held with army deserters for four days. Through the intervention of communal leader R' Mordechai Polai he was released on Shabbos afternoon and brought before a fresh medical board which granted him a white discharge ticket.

title_en: Rosh Hashana 5677 with the Rebbe Rashab in Slavyansk
summary_en: The author and many Tomchei Tmimim students traveled to the Rebbe Rashab in the seaside resort town of Slavyansk for Rosh Hashana 5677, defying an order from the Rayatz that students not come.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab had summered in Slavyansk in 1916 and remained there through Rosh Hashana. The Rayatz, then yeshiva director, had instructed that no student travel for the chag, but nearly all the older bochurim came anyway. The students lodged in vacated summer cottages and subsisted largely on stale black bread and tea, while important guests were hosted at the Rebbe's table. A newly built local mikveh cracked overnight, forcing the Rebbe to walk to the town mikveh on Rosh Hashana morning.

title_en: Sukkot 5677 at the Rebbe Rashab's court in Rostov
summary_en: After Rosh Hashana the students traveled from Slavyansk to Rostov for Sukkot 5677, despite a directive against it; Calabrian etrogim were scarce and they lodged with the Gertzulin family alongside Novardok mussar students.
story_body: The Tomchei Tmimim students received return tickets after Rosh Hashana but were warned not to go on to Rostov; the author and several others went anyway. Calabrian etrogim, the chassidic standard, were in short supply because of the war. The students were hosted by the family of Mordechai Gertzulin and his mother Chana, where they also encountered Novardok mussar students for the first time and debated their approach to prayer. Lacking means to set up a sukkah at their first lodging, they built one at a Rostov house used by Tomchei Tmimim students from that city.

title_en: Simchat Torah farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
summary_en: On Simchat Torah 5677, under wartime restrictions, seven Tomchei Tmimim students who had stayed behind to review the Rebbe Rashab's maamar were warmly received at his clandestine farbrengen and unusually invited to say l'chaim.
story_body: Wartime conditions had been declared: no public gathering was to take place at the Rebbe's home, and infractions risked being shot on sight. After the hakafot the gabbai R' Elchanan Dov Morozov quietly announced that everyone should go home and that there would be no farbrengen. Seven bochurim — including the author, R' Yisrael Feigin, and Zalman Dovid Michelin — stayed behind to chazer the maamar. When they later climbed to the upper floor, they found the Rebbe Rashab seated with chassidim; he had a table brought for them, waited for each to wash and make hamotzi, and invited each one to say l'chaim — an honor previously unheard of for students.

title_en: Author leaves Chernigov for new Tomchei Tmimim branch in Kherson
summary_en: Around 19 Kislev 5677 the author received word from the Rebbe Rashab, via R' Shmuel Zalman Havlin, to relocate from Chernigov to a newly founded Tomchei Tmimim branch in Kherson.
story_body: While studying under the Rad'tz, R' Dovid Tzvi Chen, in Chernigov, the author received instructions just before 19 Kislev 5677 directing him and four classmates to join a new Tomchei Tmimim branch opening in Kherson. The discipline among the talmidim was such that no one questioned the move — the author packed up immediately. R' Tzvi Gottlieb of Kovno served as rosh mesivta in Kherson; there was no mashpia yet. Local supporters, including R' Yisrael Tchertok and the Bezpalov brothers (sons of the rav of Poltava), housed and fed the students generously.

title_en: Mother of Shmuel Kadish Bartnovsky dies before Pesach
summary_en: Before Pesach 5677 the mother of the author's classmate Shmuel Kadish Bartnovsky passed away; the author accompanied him as far as Nikolaev before returning to Kherson and home for the chag.
story_body: While the author was studying in the Kherson yeshiva, his close friend Shmuel Kadish Bartnovsky lost his mother in the weeks leading up to Pesach 5677. The author traveled with him to Nikolaev to accompany him in his grief, then returned to Kherson and made his way home for Pesach. He returned to Lubavitch after the chag with his younger brother Shlomo Tzvi, who was to study there.

title_en: February Revolution topples Tsar Nikolai II
summary_en: At the end of winter 5677, while the author was learning in Kherson, the Russian Revolution removed Tsar Nikolai II and the Provisional Government took power.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab responded with three open letters: one congratulating the Provisional Government, one urging chassidim to purchase shares in the new state loan, and one calling on chassidim and observant Jews to organize for upcoming communal elections now that Jews enjoyed full civil rights. He quipped that 'our God-fearing brothers excel at sluggishness.' Religious and Torah-aligned political parties began forming across Russia in response.

title_en: Author returns to Lubavitch and revives Kupat Bachurim
summary_en: After Pesach 5677 the author returned to Lubavitch with his brother Shlomo Tzvi and, finding the yeshiva impoverished by war and revolution, refounded the Kupat Bachurim society to support hungry students.
story_body: Train service had broken down, so the author traveled via Mohilev by steamboat to Orsha and onward by wagon. He found Lubavitch sharply diminished — the Rav's home in ruins, R' Zalman Fradkin visibly hungry when he came to the bochurim's dining hall, students rationed roughly two litras of bread per day. Shabbos challot were now baked small and of plain wheat flour. The author convened the older talmidim and refounded the Kupat Bachurim mutual aid society, writing to married Tomchei Tmimim alumni in scattered towns for help and securing supplemental support for the neediest students.

title_en: Summer 5677 fire devastates Lubavitch
summary_en: A fire swept through Lubavitch in the summer of 1917, destroying the author's quarters along with his seforim and writings and two cabinets of seforim belonging to R' Elchanan Dov Morozov in an adjacent house.
story_body: The alarm bell rang while the author was at the mikveh together with R' Avraham Dovid Poizner of Klimovich. They misjudged the direction of the fire and ran first to Poizner's home to rescue his Vilna Shas, hauling the seforim to dry ground at the riverbed. When the author reached his own lodgings at the home of R' Michael Katzenelenbogen, the roof was already alight; his brother Shlomo Tzvi was guarding their bedding. Several bochurim had tried to salvage furnishings but most was lost, including the author's books and writings and two large cabinets of seforim belonging to R' Elchanan Dov Morozov in the neighboring house.

title_en: Author returns to Chernigov to seek draft exemption
summary_en: At the end of summer 5677 the author returned to Chernigov when Russia recalled even fully exempt 'white-ticket' men to the army, traveling to Nezhin to consult R' Menachem Mendel Chen about his father's status as a shochet.
story_body: As the war ground on, the Russian government broadened conscription to include men previously released with white tickets. The author's father, fearing he would be called up despite serving as a shochet, sent his son to Nezhin to consult R' Menachem Mendel Chen, son of the Rad'tz, who had connections that might secure an exemption. The author spent a day there and was deeply impressed when the rav sat down at eleven at night to learn a sugya from mishna through Tosfos, explaining each word as if teaching a small child. The author was ultimately exempted again 'through the upper channels.'

title_en: Rad'tz Chen quietly dissolves Chernigov Jewish party assembly
summary_en: When a public Chernigov assembly meant to elect delegates for a religious Jewish party (likely Netzach Yisrael) drifted from observant aims, R' Dovid Tzvi Chen quietly maneuvered to dissolve it.
story_body: Under the Provisional Government, plans were underway for a national Jewish assembly in Kharkov to elect a council overseeing religious and educational affairs, and parties of every stripe were sending emissaries to local towns. A visiting rabbi came to Chernigov on behalf of a religious party — the author recalls it being called Netzach Yisrael or similar — and the Rad'tz himself attended the public meeting. Sensing during the speeches that the gathering did not in fact reflect truly observant priorities, the famously otherworldly Rad'tz acted with quiet practical wisdom and dissolved the assembly, and no delegates were chosen for that faction.

title_en: Bolsheviks overthrow Kerensky and ban Jewish religious parties
summary_en: The Bolshevik seizure of power dissolved the Provisional Government and annulled the religious Jewish parties and societies that had organized after the February Revolution.
story_body: Throughout 1917, in the freedom that followed the February Revolution, chassidim and other observant Jews had been organizing politically, urged on by the Rebbe Rashab, to win representation in the new communal structures. The planned all-Russian Jewish assembly never met. The Bolshevik overthrow of Kerensky's government ended these efforts entirely: the new regime invalidated the religious parties and disbanded the societies that had taken shape under the Provisional Government.

title_en: Yeshiva students travel to Rostov for Rosh Hashana with Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: All the bochurim of the great hall traveled from Lubavitch to Rostov to be with the Rebbe Rashab for Rosh Hashana 5678.
story_body: For Rosh Hashana 5678 the entire student body of the main study hall traveled to Rostov to spend the High Holy Days with the Rebbe Rashab. The narrator stayed with his previous host R' Mordechai Gertzulin on Staraya Pochtovaya 122. This was part of an established pattern of Tomchei Temimim students gathering with the Rebbe for major holidays.

title_en: Spanish flu epidemic strikes Chabad community in Rostov
summary_en: A devastating Spanish flu epidemic struck during Rosh Hashana 5678 in Rostov, incapacitating roughly forty people who could not attend the Rebbe's services.
story_body: The Spanish flu, accompanied by severe vomiting and diarrhea, swept through Rostov during Rosh Hashana 5678. The narrator himself was struck on the first night of the holiday. About forty people were unable to attend the Rebbe Rashab's Torah reading and shofar blowing, lying instead in the lower quarters of the building.

title_en: R' Zev Wolf Bronstein dies in Spanish flu epidemic
summary_en: R' Zev Wolf Bronstein, father of the Bronstein brothers of Cherkassy, succumbed to the Spanish flu between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur 5678.
story_body: The epidemic claimed R' Zev Wolf Bronstein during the Ten Days of Repentance in 5678. He was the father of the well-known Bronstein brothers of Cherkassy — Chaim Ezra, Nosson, Mordechai, and Hershka — and later father-in-law of R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman, who became a mashpia in Tomchei Temimim Lod.

title_en: Calabrian etrog mix-up at Rebbe Rashab's home on Sukkos
summary_en: During Chol Hamoed Sukkos 5678 the Rebbe Rashab's personal Calabrian etrog was mistakenly handed to Pesach Wolf of Zhitomir, prompting a halachic discussion.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab had several Calabrian etrogim that Sukkos, designating one for the chassidim to use for the blessing. When Pesach Wolf arrived mid-Chol Hamoed from Zhitomir, the attendant R' M.M. mistakenly brought him the Rebbe's own etrog. This sparked a subsequent halachic discussion about whether the blessing had been fulfilled or had to be repeated.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab's Simchas Torah farbrengen on lengthy prayer
summary_en: An exceptional Simchas Torah 5678 farbrengen in Rostov centered on the necessity of avodah and lengthy prayer, lasting until late at night.
story_body: The Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah farbrengens of 5678 in Rostov were extraordinary, all focused on the imperative of avodah and lengthy davening — the core mission of Lubavitch. Sichos from the farbrengen are preserved in transcripts and the printed Toras Shalom. The Rebbe also engaged Polish chassidic refugees of Ger and Alexander who were present, and the daytime farbrengen continued until near midnight with dancing through the house.

title_en: Bolshevik October Revolution begins, sparking Russian civil war
summary_en: At the start of 5678 the Red Revolution erupted in Russia, triggering shortages, civil war, and German advances into Jewish areas.
story_body: The Bolshevik Revolution at the start of 5678 unleashed widespread shortages of food and goods across Russia and ignited civil war. With the Russians ceasing combat, German forces advanced rapidly into the Jewish heartland of the western empire. The crisis directly threatened Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch, prompting plans to relocate the yeshiva.

title_en: Tomchei Temimim shiur students relocated to Oryol
summary_en: The younger shiur students were transferred from Lubavitch to Oryol amid worsening conditions and German advances during 5678.
story_body: As the financial and security situation in Lubavitch deteriorated under the new Bolshevik regime, the yeshiva's junior shiur students were sent to Oryol. There they were hosted by the shochet R' Yaakov Pantelyev and supported by the wealthy chassid Mr. Shmulevitch. Three older bochurim — Shmuel Chaim Shechtman of Zlobin, Abba of Bolhakov, and apparently R' Yisrael Zuber — accompanied them.

title_en: Yeshiva fundraisers depart Lubavitch on night of 13 Adar
summary_en: On the night of 13 Adar 5678 the narrator and R' Leib Krasik left Lubavitch for Moscow as part of an emergency fundraising mission to save the yeshiva.
story_body: With Tomchei Temimim collapsing financially, senior figures were dispatched to Russia's major Jewish centers. R' Shilem Kuratin went to Petersburg, R' Eliezer Kaplan to Vitebsk and Nevel, and the narrator with R' Leib Krasik were sent to Moscow. They read the megillah on the eve of 13 Adar and boarded the train that night, planning to daven and read megillah again in Moscow.

title_en: Eighteen thousand rubles raised in Moscow for Tomchei Temimim on Purim
summary_en: On Purim day 5678 the magnate R' Zalka Persitz and R' Baruch Shalom Kahan helped raise 18,000 rubles in a single day in Moscow for the yeshiva.
story_body: After arriving in Moscow on Purim eve and being hosted at R' Baruch Shalom Kahan's home, the fundraisers were taken the next morning to the office of the magnate R' Zalka Persitz. Through phone calls throughout the day they collected 18,000 rubles. The emissaries sewed 9,000 rubles into each of their garments and returned to Lubavitch.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab delivers maamar 'Hachodesh Hazeh' in Rostov
summary_en: On Shabbos Parshas Hachodesh 5678 the Rebbe Rashab said the maamar 'Hachodesh Hazeh' in Rostov, before a yechidus with the visiting emissary.
story_body: Following his fundraising trip to Moscow, the narrator traveled to Rostov to ask the Rebbe Rashab's guidance on the future of Tomchei Temimim. He arrived before Shabbos Parshas Hachodesh 5678 and heard the Rebbe deliver the maamar 'Hachodesh Hazeh' that Shabbos. Motzaei Shabbos he had a forty-minute yechidus in which the Rebbe gave his ruling that the students should remain in Lubavitch.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab rules yeshiva should remain in Lubavitch
summary_en: In a Motzaei Shabbos yechidus in Rostov, the Rebbe Rashab ruled that despite German advances Tomchei Temimim students should stay in Lubavitch.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab gave three reasons in yechidus: he believed the Germans would not capture Lubavitch; even if captured the area would not be fully controlled, allowing small group study; and even at worst the border would be porous enough to cross. He concluded that relocating Lubavitch itself was impossible — 'the light will be missing' — and a telegram was sent to halt the evacuation. By then it was too late and most students had already left.

title_en: Twelve Tomchei Temimim students arrested as suspected spies in Poltava
summary_en: Twelve Lubavitcher bochurim en route from Lubavitch to Kremenchug were arrested at Poltava station on suspicion of espionage and nearly executed.
story_body: Rumors reached Kremenchug on a Friday that twelve Tomchei Temimim students had been killed at Poltava station. In fact they had been detained as suspected spies — triggered by Zalman Birnbaum's Polish-style cap and rapid movements. R' Tzvi Gurary used his military contacts to telephone the Poltava war chief, and R' Mordechai Aharon Friedman traveled by military train to obtain rabbinic guarantees from R' Duber Greenpress and R' Eliyahu Akiva Rabinowitz that freed them.

title_en: 13 Nissan farbrengen at the Gurary shul in Kremenchug
summary_en: A farbrengen was held on 13 Nissan 5678 in the Gurary shul of Kremenchug, led by R' Elchonon Dov Morozov.
story_body: While stranded in Kremenchug arranging accommodations for the shiur students, the narrator attended a 13 Nissan farbrengen in the Gurary synagogue. R' Elchonon Dov Morozov was the principal speaker, with the meshulach R' Yechiel Halperin and others present. The gathering was part of the consolidation of the Tomchei Temimim community in its new wartime home.

title_en: Acharon shel Pesach farbrengen at R' Tzvi Gurary in Kremenchug
summary_en: On Acharon shel Pesach 5678 a farbrengen was held at R' Tzvi Gurary's home in Kremenchug, lasting late into the night.
story_body: The narrator spent Pesach 5678 in Kremenchug as a guest of R' Nosson Gurary, whose home was open to all. On the last day of Pesach the local chassidim gathered at R' Tzvi Gurary's house for a farbrengen that extended until late at night, even as 10,000 dollars was being raised for Tomchei Temimim per the Rebbe Rashab's instruction.

title_en: Germans capture Lubavitch region just before Pesach
summary_en: German forces entered the Lubavitch area immediately before Pesach 5678, cutting civilian rail travel and isolating the town.
story_body: Following the Brest-Litovsk treaty, German forces advanced into the area encompassing Lubavitch right before Pesach 5678. Civilian rail traffic was halted — only military trains ran — preventing the narrator from returning from Kremenchug. The occupation persisted through the summer, with German authorities installing local Ukrainian rulers under their suzerainty.

title_en: Ten thousand dollars raised in Kremenchug for Tomchei Temimim
summary_en: Per the Rebbe Rashab's directive, ten thousand dollars was collected in Kremenchug during spring 5678 for the yeshiva.
story_body: Following the narrator's return from Rostov, the Kremenchug chassidim raised the 10,000 dollars the Rebbe Rashab had mandated to sustain Tomchei Temimim. The daughters of R' Nosson Gurary — Perla and Leah — personally whitewashed the walls and scrubbed the floors of the new yeshiva quarters in preparation for the students.

title_en: Narrator returns to Lubavitch from Kremenchug around Rosh Chodesh Iyar
summary_en: Around Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5678 the narrator carried 10,000 rubles back to Lubavitch, crossing the German–Russian border on foot at Orsha at night.
story_body: Around Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5678 the narrator left Kremenchug for Lubavitch with 10,000 rubles hidden in his stockings. At Orsha he had to walk roughly three miles between the German and Russian customs posts in the dark, assisting an elderly Jewish woman who could not keep pace. He arrived in Lubavitch via Krasna in the morning.

title_en: Farewell farbrengen at R' Shmuel Gronem on Shabbos Mevorchim Elul
summary_en: On Shabbos Mevorchim Elul 5678, before leaving Lubavitch, a farewell farbrengen was held at R' Shmuel Gronem's home with wine from the Rebbe's cellar.
story_body: Before evacuating Lubavitch the remaining bochurim and senior figures held a final farbrengen at the Rashag's home on Shabbos Mevorchim Elul 5678. They drew bottles of wine from the cellar of the Rebbe Rayatz's father-in-law R' Avraham. The atmosphere of taking leave of Lubavitch — even with hope of return — was overwhelming, despite reassuring news from Kremenchug and Rostov.

title_en: Tomchei Temimim center relocates from Lubavitch to Kremenchug
summary_en: Near Elul 5678 the final group left Lubavitch via Bryansk and a night border crossing to reach Kremenchug, ending the yeshiva's presence in Lubavitch.
story_body: After hiding the Rebbe's household vessels in a deep cellar, the last twelve bochurim and senior families departed Lubavitch via Rudnia toward Bryansk. From Klintsy they used peasant wagons through a neutral zone, paying off Russian soldiers and German border guards along the way. After bribery, beatings, and a tense night in no-man's land, they reached Gomel and continued to Kremenchug — formally ending the yeshiva's residence in Lubavitch.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim students travel to Rostov for Rosh Hashanah 5679
summary_en: All the Tomchei Tmimim students traveled to Rostov to spend Rosh Hashanah 5679 with the Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: The chassidim prayed in the Shaalash, a wooden structure built in the courtyard of the Rebbe Rashab's home on Bradsky Pereulok 44 in Rostov, which he had purchased after the move from Lubavitch. R' Yechiel Halpern served as chazzan. This was the first Rosh Hashanah of the Tomchei Tmimim student body following the relocation from Kremenchug for the chag.

title_en: Wedding of Chaim Kavash officiated by the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
summary_en: Between Yom Kippur and Sukkot 5679, R' Chaim Kavash of Vyetka married a relative of Rebbetzin Sterna Sarah, with the Rebbe Rashab serving as mesader kiddushin.
story_body: The Rebbe Rashab stood at the entrance of the Shaalash while the chuppah was held in the courtyard. For the bracha of 'Asher Bara' he honored a religious German army officer who was lodging in the Rebbe's home. Witnesses noted that during the blessings the Rebbe held his hands raised, fingers spread above his eyebrows.

title_en: Calabrian etrog identified by the Rebbe Rashab on Erev Sukkot 5679
summary_en: On Erev Sukkot 5679 the Rebbe Rashab studied a single etrog brought from Calabria for about two hours before confirming its origin.
story_body: The etrog was sent by R' Shmuel Gurary and delivered by R' Dovber Ganzburg of Odessa amid wartime disruption of supply routes. Throughout Sukkot the Rebbe permitted every chassid to bless the etrog but allowed no one — not even his son the Rayatz — to perform na'anuim with it, and asked each person whether their hands were dry. He sat in the sukkah from 6 to 10 a.m. each day attending to the chassidim.

title_en: Simchat Torah 5679 farbrengen with the Rebbe Rashab in Rostov
summary_en: On the night of Simchat Torah 5679 the Rebbe Rashab attended kiddush at the home of his son the Rayatz before hakafot, delivering rare personal remarks.
story_body: The Rebbe spoke about Moshiach coming through wealthy supporters and about the founding of Tomchei Tmimim, declaring 'I am a sichli' and that he would not be moved by externalities. When he discussed connection to the House of David he turned to the Rayatz and said 'Yitzchak, hear this — it concerns you.' Hakafot were not held that night, and the Rebbe Rashab uncharacteristically danced with the assembled chassidim, something he had previously done only with his son.

title_en: Author's final yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: After Sukkot 5679 the author entered for what would be his final yechidus with the Rebbe Rashab, presenting two shidduch proposals.
story_body: He raised concerns about premature deaths in the family of the proposed bride suggested by his future brother-in-law R' Aharon Eliezer Zeitlin. The Rebbe Rashab repeated three times 'nito vos tzu choshesh zein' — there is nothing to fear — and closed with 'Hashem should protect you from everything,' the last words the author would ever hear from him in person.

title_en: 19 Kislev 5679 farbrengen in Rostov
summary_en: The 19 Kislev 5679 farbrengen was held in Rostov with R' Shaul Dov Zislin repeating a maamer 'Devash V'chalav Tachas Leshonech.'
story_body: Chassidim of Kremenchug including R' Shmuel Kuratin tried to travel to Rostov for the chag but could not obtain train tickets and had to return home as the rail network was in disarray. Witnesses recalled that as R' Shaul Dov Zislin chazered the maamer 'honey and milk flowed from his mouth.'

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim opens a branch in Charol
summary_en: After Pesach 5679 the Kremenchug branch of Tomchei Tmimim sent a contingent of its shiurim students to establish a class in the town of Charol.
story_body: The author traveled to Charol ahead of the move to arrange housing for the students and confer with the local rabbinate. He stayed with R' Shmuel Gurary, the town's dayan, while R' Moshe Madayevsky served as rav. The move was driven by the worsening shortages and disorder around Kremenchug.

title_en: Ukrainian pogroms of 5679–5680 kill roughly 300,000 Jews
summary_en: During 5679 and 5680 anti-Jewish pogroms by White Army, Petliura, and Makhno forces killed approximately 300,000 Jews across Ukraine.
story_body: Rival armies competing for control of Ukraine after the German withdrawal openly permitted their soldiers to attack Jewish communities. Kremenchug suffered an incursion by Petliura's troops for about a week, with house searches and several casualties; chassidim hid in cellars. Later the Makhnovist forces, who had killed R' Menachem Mendel of Bobruisk in Yekaterinoslav, besieged Kremenchug from across the Dnieper at Kraukov until Red Army artillery drove them back across the bridge.

title_en: Author's tenaim signed on 16 Tammuz 5679 in Zhuravichi
summary_en: On the night of 16 Tammuz 5679 the author's engagement to the daughter of R' Yehoshua Heshel Levin was finalized in Zhuravichi.
story_body: The father-in-law-to-be traveled to the author's parents in Zhuravichi for Shabbat 14 Tammuz, and the kishrei hatena'im were arranged after Shabbat. The kallah was not present, remaining in Gomel; a dowry of ten thousand rubles was committed, though the currency was already badly devalued by the upheaval.

title_en: Author's wedding on 8th day of Chanukah 5680 in Belitsa
summary_en: On the eighth day of Chanukah 5680 the author married in Belitsa near Gomel, amid acute famine and political collapse.
story_body: The original tenaim date had been advanced once his future brother-in-law saw the father-in-law's failing health and the spreading famine. The author's mother brought three or four pounds of meat, an uncle obtained a small amount of wheat flour for challos, and a brother-in-law procured a pound of sugar. About ten chassidim joined for sheva brachos on Shabbat, where the author began to chazer a maamer but stopped midway, overwhelmed by the surrounding conditions.

title_en: Father-in-law R' Yehoshua Heshel Levin passes away
summary_en: The author's father-in-law R' Yehoshua Heshel Levin passed away on 28 Tevet 5680.
story_body: He had long suffered from a debilitating leg ailment but could no longer travel to therapeutic spas because of the civil war. After the wedding his son brought him from Gomel to Belitsa, where he was bedridden until his death several weeks later. The author was then beginning to peddle small quantities of salt and tobacco between cities to support his family.

title_en: Passing of the Rebbe Rashab on 2 Nissan 5680
summary_en: Rabbi Sholom DovBer Schneersohn, the fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 2 Nissan 5680 in Rostov.
story_body: The news reached the author in Gomel only on Erev Shabbat Parshat Shemini, when R' Akiva Trachtenberg told him at a cobbler's shop and he returned home weeping. That Shabbat the Gomel chassidim gathered at the Lubavitch shul for Mincha, where elders including R' Shlomo, R' Moshe and R' Shneur Zalman Tomarkin and R' Aharon Eliezer Zeitlin declared the Rebbe Rayatz as successor, danced together, and resolved to write a collective letter of hiskashrus.

title_en: Birth of the author's daughter Sarah on 19 Kislev 5681
summary_en: The author's eldest daughter Sarah was born on 19 Kislev 5681 in Gomel.
story_body: She arrived during the height of the post-civil-war famine, as Ukrainian refugees lay swollen with hunger in the streets and Jews in Gomel were reduced to eating bran, oil-seed residue, and potato peels. The rabbinate permitted kitniyos that Pesach because of the shortages, and the family relied on supplies the author hauled back and forth from the village of Zhuravichi.

title_en: Decision to found Tomchei Tmimim branch in Homel
summary_en: On Simchat Torah 5682, Chabad chassidim gathered in Homel resolved to establish a local branch of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
story_body: Travel to the central yeshiva in Lubavitch had become unsafe under the new Soviet regime, leaving students wandering with no stable place to study. At a Simchat Torah gathering in the home of R' Shmuel Biale 'der zeiger macher,' the chassidim of Homel decided to open their own branch of Tomchei Tmimim. They wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz requesting permission and a rosh yeshiva, and he approved, granting the new institution the name 'Tomchei Tmimim of Lubavitch in Homel.'

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva opens in Homel
summary_en: On Chanukah 5682, the Homel branch of Tomchei Tmimim opened with R' Yechezkel Feigin as rosh yeshiva and a single student.
story_body: After receiving the Rebbe Rayatz's approval, the Homel chassidim engaged R' Yechezkel Feigin — who had recently moved from Kremenchug to his mother-in-law's home — to serve as rosh yeshiva, with his salary paid in flour because of the famine. The yeshiva opened on Chanukah in the Babushkin shul, the only synagogue willing to host the students out of fear they would break the windows and benches. For its first three weeks the only student was Hillel Sklyar, son of R' Avraham Yaakov Sklyar of Zlobin.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Homel adds assistant rosh yeshiva
summary_en: At the beginning of Adar 5682 the growing Homel yeshiva engaged Rabbi Yosef Baruch as assistant rosh yeshiva.
story_body: Students gradually streamed into the Homel branch of Tomchei Tmimim, and by the start of Adar a second teacher was needed. Rabbi Yosef Baruch was hired as assistant to R' Yechezkel Feigin, and the student Meir Shor of Padobranka was appointed deputy mashgiach. Although other shuls now offered space, the chassidim remained at the Babushkin shul on grounds of hazakah and were granted permission to set up long study tables throughout the building.

title_en: Confrontation between Tomchei Tmimim and Novardok yeshivas in Homel
summary_en: Shortly before Purim 5682, Novardok students confronted the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Homel over students who had transferred from their school.
story_body: Novardok students had been founding small yeshivas across Soviet Russia, including one in Homel, but their unstructured curriculum and idiosyncratic mussar exercises — recording 'peulos' of humility such as asking shopkeepers for absurd goods — caused many students to transfer to the better-ordered Tomchei Tmimim. Two senior Novardok students, including Meir of Brisk, demanded that R' Yechezkel Feigin return their students or cease teaching. The author and Feigin physically escorted them out, and the matter was later argued with R' Avraham Yafen, then rosh yeshiva of Novardok in Homel.

title_en: Soviet decrees against religion intensify in the Homel region
summary_en: After Pesach 5682 the Soviet authorities launched their first organized campaign of decrees against yeshivas and chadarim in the Homel area.
story_body: Following Passover, the Bolshevik regime escalated its persecution of religious institutions, issuing decrees aimed at closing yeshivas and chadarim. The chassidim, not yet familiar with Soviet tactics, were caught off guard as the authorities convened public meetings to attack religion and recruited informers — including former servants of rabbis — to act against the community.

title_en: Rabbi Rafael Mordechai Barshansky arrested in Homel
summary_en: Rabbi Rafael Mordechai Barshansky was jailed after publicly defending religion at a Soviet-organized debate in Homel.
story_body: When Soviet authorities convened a public assembly to attack religion, Rabbi Rafael Mordechai Barshansky — a powerful preacher — rose to refute them. Unable to defeat him in open debate, the authorities trumped up charges, with one of his former servants among the judges, and imprisoned him. After great efforts he was freed and subsequently emigrated to America.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz makes first return visit to Lubavitch
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5682, the Rebbe Rayatz visited Lubavitch for the first time since assuming the leadership of Chabad.
story_body: After travel restrictions were lifted, the Rebbe Rayatz traveled to Lubavitch on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul, delivering a maamar in the brick shul — the other synagogues having burned — and praying at the Ohel before departing for Moscow with R' Shmuel Aba Dulitzky. A delegation from Homel led by the author met him on the platform at the Krasna station, and the author received a yechidus on the train. The Rebbe likened his renewed journey to Lubavitch to a horse finally breaking loose from its tether, signifying the renewal of the bond with the town since he had assumed the nesius.

title_en: Yechidus in Rostov on emigration to America
summary_en: During Shavuot 5683 the Rebbe Rayatz, then residing in Rostov, advised the author to consider emigrating to America.
story_body: The author traveled to the Rebbe Rayatz in Rostov for Shavuot 5683, where the Rebbe delivered chassidus and R' Yechezkel Feigin served as chozer at the chazarah following Shacharis. In a yechidus after the holiday, after noting that his parents and siblings had already emigrated to the United States, the author received the Rebbe's answer that going to America was 'very right, one must travel, do not be ashamed.'

title_en: Chofetz Chaim passes through Homel en route to Poland
summary_en: Around 5683, when Polish nationals living in Russia were granted permission to return to Poland, the Chofetz Chaim passed through Homel and lodged with R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria.
story_body: When the Soviets permitted Polish nationals residing in Russia to return home, the Chofetz Chaim left the town of Snovsk, where he had been living with his students, and made his way toward Poland. En route he passed through Homel, staying as a guest in the home of R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria. This was the only time the author met him, describing him as 'a very pious Jew.'

title_en: Soviet authorities impose a kehilla council on Homel
summary_en: During 5683 the Soviet authorities compelled Homel's Jews to form an official community council, with R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria chosen as chairman.
story_body: As anti-religious decrees mounted — synagogues being seized through forced signature campaigns and mikvaot closed under hygienic pretexts — the government ordered the Jews of Homel to establish a community council. R' Shmuel Yitzchak Luria was elected chairman and worked closely with the younger tmimim, defying the protests of older communal figures. Through their efforts a new mikveh was built, and the Rebbe Rayatz sent Luria a long letter pledging support from his vast network of institutions despite carrying personal debts of tens of thousands of dollars.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz uproots from Rostov to Leningrad
summary_en: At the beginning of summer 5684, the Rebbe Rayatz was forced to leave Rostov and settled in Leningrad.
story_body: Mounting Soviet pressure forced the Rebbe Rayatz to uproot his household from Rostov and move to Leningrad (formerly Petrograd) at the start of summer 5684. By that point the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was situated in Kharkov, with R' Yechezkel Feigin serving as mashgiach and director.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim central yeshiva operates in Kharkov
summary_en: By 5684 the central Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was based in Kharkov under the direction of R' Yechezkel Feigin.
story_body: Following the dispersion of Tomchei Tmimim under Soviet pressure, the central yeshiva relocated to Kharkov by 5684. R' Yechezkel Feigin, who had earlier been called from Homel to lead the institution in Poltava, now served as mashgiach and manager of the Kharkov yeshiva, dispatching emissaries such as R' Shneur Gorelik and R' Yisrael Matmid to fundraise across the region.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Zalman Posner murdered by anti-Bolshevik bands
summary_en: R' Yitzchak Zalman Posner of Karop was killed together with twelve other Jews when anti-Bolshevik bandits seized a riverboat near Makoshin station.
story_body: R' Yitzchak Zalman Posner — father of R' Shalom Posner — was a regular guest of the author in Homel, traveling there roughly every two weeks to purchase wares for his store in Karop in Chernigov province. After refusing the author's invitation to stay for Shabbos so he could return for an unusual second trip the following week, he set out by train to Makoshin and then by riverboat. On Friday morning anti-Bolshevik bands boarded the boat and murdered thirteen Jews on board, claiming they were Bolsheviks, then dumped the bodies into the river. His mother in America was never informed of his death.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn considers Chicago rabbinate
summary_en: During 5684 R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn deliberated whether to accept a call from Chicago to serve as a Chabad rabbi in America.
story_body: R' Shneur Zalman Schneersohn — son of the Retziter Rebbe and a senior great-grandson of the Alter Rebbe — received papers from Chicago inviting him to serve as rabbi and Chabad leader there, with an apartment and a gabbai already prepared. R' Chaim Eliezer Bichovsky urged him to accept, citing a tradition that chassidus would spread in the lower hemisphere before the coming of Mashiach; his brother R' Chaim Schneersohn of Bremen advised him instead to settle in Eretz Yisrael. The author, consulted on the matter, also recommended America, noting that the wave of emigrants from Russia in those years consisted largely of Torah-observant Jews seeking religious freedom.

title_en: Author travels to Leningrad for Rosh Hashanah 5685
summary_en: Despite financial hardship, the author borrowed money and traveled from Homel to Leningrad to spend Rosh Hashanah with the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: The author's financial situation was strained, so he borrowed funds collected for ma'amad after R. Yosef the temimid's departure and bought a train ticket to Leningrad. His wife baked challahs and roasted two chickens for the journey. He stopped in Neveil to visit his brother-in-law R. Meir Simcha Chen and to see the famous chassidic town for the first time, lodging with relatives near the Rebbe.

title_en: Erev Rosh Hashanah encounter with Elye Chaim Althaus in Leningrad
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Hashanah at the Rebbe Rayatz's apartment in Leningrad, the author was awakened to chassidic responsibility by R. Elye Chaim Althaus.
story_body: After Selichos and Shacharis, the author entered the Rebbe's apartment at Machovaya 12 and was shocked to find the prayer hall unprepared with no benches set up. When he asked R. Elye Chaim Althaus about it, Althaus repeated the question back to him, awakening the author to the fact that he himself bore responsibility for the Rebbe's house. The author said this moment 'made him ten years older.'

title_en: Thirty minyanim of Temimim gather for Rosh Hashanah 5685 with the Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: Approximately thirty minyanim of Temimim, mostly Tomchei Temimim students, traveled to Leningrad for Rosh Hashanah 5685 with the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: Around thirty minyanim of Temimim, the overwhelming majority students of Tomchei Temimim, came to Leningrad to be with the Rebbe Rayatz for Rosh Hashanah. Even R. Leib Bagad, a balebatish figure from Lubavitch generally distant from chassidus, prayed there and embraced the visiting Temimim like brothers. The warmth and bond among the visitors was deeply felt throughout the holiday.

title_en: Temimim assembly resolves to send students from Russia to America
summary_en: After Rosh Hashanah 5685, an assembly of Temimim in Leningrad decided to send representatives abroad to help bring more students out of Russia.
story_body: Following Rosh Hashanah, the Temimim convened and resolved by majority vote that they must campaign to leave Russia, sending one or two emissaries to foreign countries who would then help bring additional students from Russia to safety. The author was the only one at the assembly preparing to travel to America, and the responsibility for the American mission was placed on him. The decisions were submitted to the Rebbe Rayatz.

title_en: Author secures Soviet exit visas for the Gurary family in Homel
summary_en: During winter 5685 the author arranged Soviet exit visas in Homel for the Gurary family, including the widow and children of R. Tzvi Hirsch Gurary.
story_body: R. Shmarya Gurary asked the author whether he could arrange foreign-travel passports through Homel for the family of R. Tzvi Hirsch Gurary, offering 250 rubles (25 chervontses). After Nochum Gurelnik came to verify the possibility, R. Nosson Gurary brought the family to Homel, where they were registered in residents' household books. By winter's end the author had obtained exit permits for R. Tzvi's entire family, for R. Nosson's wife Esther, and for R. Shmarya Gurary.

title_en: GPO agents search author at Homel train station after Purim
summary_en: In the week after Purim 5685 the author was detained and searched by GPO agents while boarding a train in Homel for Leningrad.
story_body: As the author boarded a train in Homel headed to Leningrad in the week after Purim, two GPO agents signaled him to follow them. They led him to their building next to the station and searched his clothing, body, and belongings. Among the searchers was a man who himself had smuggled goods for him from Minsk, but they found nothing and he managed to catch his scheduled train.

title_en: Author arrives in Leningrad on 21 Adar to seek audience with the Rebbe
summary_en: The author arrived in Leningrad on Tuesday 21 Adar 5685, traveling on behalf of R. Yisrael Magidsohn and to seek the Rebbe's guidance on his own emigration.
story_body: The author arrived in Leningrad on Tuesday, 21 Adar. The Rebbe Rayatz was not present, having traveled to Moscow, and only returned home the following day, Wednesday. The author was traveling both as an emissary for R. Yisrael Magidsohn, who feared GPO surveillance after a search at his government workplace, and to receive the Rebbe's guidance on his own preparations to leave Russia.

title_en: Yechidus appoints author mashpia in Homel and emissary to Rostov
summary_en: On Thursday night after 21 Adar 5685 the Rebbe Rayatz instructed the author to serve as mashpia in Homel and to travel to Rostov for the 2 Nisan yahrzeit.
story_body: In Thursday night yechidus the author first presented R. Yisrael Magidsohn's situation and then his own, and the Rebbe told him to begin preparations for the journey to America. The Rebbe also asked him to serve as mashpia in Homel for 40 rubles per month until his departure, regardless of his daytime occupation. Finally the Rebbe appointed him as emissary to travel to Rostov for the Rebbe Rashab's yahrzeit on 2 Nisan, which fell that year on Friday.

title_en: Second yechidus: pidyonos and instructions for the Rostov Ohel
summary_en: On Sunday before his trip the Rebbe Rayatz gave the author pidyonos to place at the Rebbe Rashab's Ohel and detailed instructions for handling the Rebbe's personal pidyon.
story_body: At 6pm Sunday yechidus the Rebbe summarized the Shabbos maamar and gave the author a bundle of pidyonos to place at the Ohel. He instructed that his own pidyon be read only once, only at the Ohel, never copied or shown to anyone, with no leniency. The Rebbe also sent the author to his mother, Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah, who gave him a pidyon and details about their former Rostov home at Bradsky Pereulok 44.

title_en: Author makes pilgrimage to Rostov Ohel for 2 Nisan yahrzeit
summary_en: On Friday 2 Nisan 5685 the author visited the Rebbe Rashab's Ohel in Rostov as the Rebbe Rayatz's emissary, marking the fifth yahrzeit.
story_body: Arriving in Rostov the author felt the city's emptiness, no longer the holy place that had drawn him in earlier years. He prayed Maariv with the local Temimim in the Rebbe's former home, where the absence of the tzaddik cried out from every corner.
