On Friday, the yahrzeit, he went to the Ohel and carried out the Rebbe Rayatz's instructions precisely, remaining in Rostov for Shabbos before returning home.

title_en: R. Israel Jacobson receives Soviet exit papers in Homel
summary_en: On 15 Sivan 5685, Jacobson received his Soviet passport and set out from Homel with his family for Moscow en route to America.
story_body: Jacobson's parents in America had sent him a rabbinic invitation from a synagogue in their Brooklyn neighborhood, which the U.S. consul in Riga needed to verify before issuing a visa. With the passport in hand, he boarded a carriage to the train station with his wife and daughters Chaya Sara and Rachel Dvasha, and was seen off at the station by Anash including his brother-in-law R. Aharon Eliezer and R. Zalman Chasdan. He traveled with French Line, hoping the company would extend him credit toward Riga since he still lacked the full ticket fare.

title_en: Jacobson granted yechidus with Rebbe Rayatz in Moscow
summary_en: During his six-week stay in Moscow awaiting payment of his American steamship ticket, Jacobson received yechidus and a parting blessing from the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: The Rebbe Rayatz visited Moscow while Jacobson was lodged in the Abramov family's apartment. The yechidus was held at the home of one of the Tmimim—either the shochet R. Chaim Zalman Gordon or R. Shimon Yaakobson—with Sender Rappaport, son-in-law of Shimon Yaakobson, managing entries and exits. The local circle of Anash and Tmimim included craftsmen and stocking-makers but also pnimi'usdike chassidim with deep grasp of Chassidus, gathering Shabbos mornings for two hours of Chassidus study followed by avoda-style davening.

title_en: Jacobson delivers maamar at bris of Chaim Eliezer Horowitz in Moscow
summary_en: Jacobson repeated the Rebbe Rashab's maamar 'Hareini Es Mareich' in Yiddish at the bris of Tomim Chaim Eliezer 'Velizer' Horowitz in Moscow.
story_body: During his Moscow stay he was honored to chazer Chassidus at the bris. Accustomed in Homel to chazering in Yiddish so that the balebatim could understand, he did the same in Moscow—drawing critique from the Moscow Tmimim, who considered the audience refined enough for Chassidus in Loshon HaKodesh and remarked that he was 'translating' Chassidus.

title_en: Jacobson family crosses Soviet–Latvian border at Sebezh
summary_en: At the end of Tammuz 5685, Jacobson and his family escaped Soviet Russia by train through Sebezh into Latvia.
story_body: The crossing came at sunset, and only when Latvian officials and railway staff boarded the train did the family begin to grasp that they were physically out of the Soviet Union. Even then the dread of being seized back on some pretext lingered—it could not yet be felt in the heart that the escape from Bolshevik rule was real.

title_en: Jacobson family arrives in Riga
summary_en: The Jacobson family arrived in Riga on Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av 5685, beginning a near five-month wait for an American visa.
story_body: French Line first lodged them in an emigrant hotel and then moved them to a quarantine residence required for travelers transiting Latvia for overseas voyages. The U.S. consul in Riga—since Washington did not yet recognize the Soviet government—required at least six weeks to verify the authenticity of the Brooklyn shul's invitation before considering a visa.

title_en: Daughter Chaya Sara hospitalized with scarlet fever in Riga
summary_en: Jacobson's four-and-a-half-year-old daughter Chaya Sara fell ill with scarlet fever in early Elul 5685 and was confined to a Riga municipal hospital for six weeks.
story_body: The American consul, on hearing of the contagion, warned that any entry to the consulate within three months would permanently void the visa. The municipal hospital had little warmth for Jewish refugees, so the parents could only visit at a window each day—including on Rosh Hashanah—bringing a hard-to-find orange and listening to their daughter beg to be taken home.

title_en: Simchat Torah farbrengen with Riga Tmimim
summary_en: On Simchat Torah 5686, Jacobson farbrenged in Riga with the local Tmimim and R. Mordechai Dubin, with hakafos running late into the night.
story_body: The gathering included R. Mordechai Chefetz Hy"d, his brother R. Michoel Leib Hy"d, R. Tzvi Gor (son-in-law of the chazan R. M.M. Volosov), R. Yaakov Horowitz of Liepaja Hy"d, and R. Mordechai Dubin. The Riga Tmimim had also received the Rebbe Rayatz's Rosh Hashanah 5686 maamarim, which Jacobson learned with the local chavurah during his five-month stay.

title_en: Jacobson departs Riga for America on 19 Kislev
summary_en: After his visa came through, Jacobson left Riga on motzaei Shabbat 19 Kislev 5686, taking leave during R. Mordechai Chefetz's 19 Kislev seudah.
story_body: Mid-seudah at the shochet R. Mordechai Chefetz's home, Jacobson received parting blessings from his friends and set out via Kovno, Königsberg, Berlin, Paris, and Le Havre. A planned reunion in Berlin with his friend Alter Beilin—who held his own American visa and would later become his brother-in-law—failed because Beilin's departure was on a different schedule and neither yet knew how to easily locate the other in a foreign city.

title_en: Jacobson family boards SS Paris at Le Havre
summary_en: On the sixth night of Chanukah 5686, Jacobson and his family boarded the SS Paris at Le Havre for the Atlantic crossing to America.
story_body: After about a week in Le Havre, the family embarked on Wednesday, the sixth Chanukah candle. The ship took on additional passengers via tender at an English coast before heading into open sea; Jacobson's wife was bedridden with seasickness from that stop onward, and elder daughter Chaya Sara also suffered, while a Friday-evening storm sent waves cresting over the ship's roof.

title_en: Jacobson family arrives in America at Ellis Island
summary_en: The Jacobson family reached the American shore on Tuesday 5 Tevet 5686 and were processed at Ellis Island.
story_body: After the stormy Atlantic crossing on the SS Paris, the ship docked on 5 Tevet. All the passengers, Jacobson and his family among them, were transferred to Ellis Island for immigration processing—closing out a journey from Homel that had taken roughly six months by way of Moscow, Riga, Kovno, Königsberg, Berlin, Paris, and Le Havre.

title_en: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrives in America at Ellis Island
summary_en: R' Yisrael Jacobson arrives at Ellis Island with his family and is processed by immigration officials before entering New York City.
story_body: Arriving with his wife and two children, Jacobson was held at Ellis Island where his daughter Rachel Dvasha (age 1.5) was secretly coming down with measles that went undetected by the inspectors. After questioning about his finances (he had only one dollar) and rabbinic duties, the synagogue representatives Mr. Benjamin (president), Mr. Siegel (secretary), and his uncle Yosef Hillel came to vouch for him. The next Thursday morning they took the Third Avenue elevated train into Manhattan, passing through Wall Street which his uncle described as the richest place in the world.

title_en: Sponsoring synagogue closes immediately after Jacobson's arrival
summary_en: The small storefront synagogue that filed immigration papers to bring Jacobson to America closes the Sunday after his first Shabbos.
story_body: The synagogue that had submitted the official request papers to bring Jacobson to America met in a rented storefront established by a small group of men. The Shabbos after his arrival he prayed there, but the very next day the synagogue closed permanently. This made clear that the shul had been founded specifically as a vehicle of divine providence to bring him to America.

title_en: Jacobson accepted as rabbi of Anshei Bobruisk in Brownsville
summary_en: After a two-week trial period, R' Yisrael Jacobson is hired as rabbi of the Anshei Bobruisk synagogue at 228 Christopher Street in Brownsville.
story_body: Through the advocacy of fellow Zhuravichi townspeople including R' Zev Chaikin, and after R' Memel Lukshin spoke with R' Shneur Zalman Chavkin (deputy chair of the Brownsville branch), Jacobson was given a two-week trial period and then hired as rabbi. The parent society in Manhattan opposed hiring a rabbi due to one maskil member's objection, so his salary was paid directly by individual congregants and the Mishnayos study society rather than the official society. Members who initially opposed him gradually came to embrace him, attending his home and shul on Yud-Tes Kislev, Purim, and other festive days.

title_en: Hilula farbrengen for Rebbe Rashab with Basi LeGani maamar
summary_en: Anash gather at Tzemach Tzedek shul on 184 Henry Street for the Rashab's yahrzeit, where Jacobson delivers a Basi LeGani maamar sent from Russia by the Rayatz.
story_body: Following instructions from the Rayatz, Anash held a farbrengen on 2 Nissan at the Tzemach Tzedek synagogue at 184 Henry Street to mark the yahrzeit of his father, the Rebbe Rashab. As a guest, Jacobson was honored to deliver chassidus and repeated the maamar 'Basi LeGani,' which the Rayatz had sent from Russia specifically to be studied by Anash on the yahrzeit that year. The maamar was very well received, and Anash from Brownsville subsequently began coming to Jacobson's own shul for Seudah Shlishis.

title_en: Jacobson moves into apartment at 204 Christopher Street
summary_en: Shortly before Passover, R' Yisrael Jacobson rents an apartment at 204 Christopher Street near his Brownsville synagogue.
story_body: Around Passover, Jacobson moved into an apartment at 204 Christopher Street near the Anshei Bobruisk synagogue, and later relocated to 276 Christopher Street. His father warned him that questions of kashrus on poultry — especially 'pakin' blemishes in the intestines — would arise before Pesach, particularly in Brownsville, which was then called 'the Jerusalem of America.' His father came frequently in those days to support him through the first such she'eilos.

title_en: Jacobson becomes baal tokea at Anshei Bobruisk
summary_en: Before the month of Elul, the Anshei Bobruisk congregants ask Jacobson to serve as their baal tokea, beginning a 24-year tenure in that role.
story_body: Before Elul 5686, the congregants asked Jacobson to serve as their baal tokea, despite his protest that he had almost never blown the shofar before. After practicing and finding the task within his ability, he purchased a new shofar. He went on to serve as the shul's baal tokea for twenty-four years, until he eventually left the position.

title_en: R' Elimelech Siminawski first travels to America
summary_en: R' Elimelech Siminawski of Sosnitsa was in America for the first time at the beginning of 5640 (autumn 1879).
story_body: R' Elimelech Siminawski traveled from Sosnitsa to America at the start of 5640, during the wave of departures triggered by Russian pogroms. He later recounted that the Rebbe Maharin of Nezhin, when asked whether one should flee to America, replied that if there were any place to escape from the Holy One he would flee there himself. His testimony helped frame the early Chabad community's ambivalent view of the chasidim who emigrated west.

title_en: R' Dovid Shifrin departs for America with Rebbe Rashab's notice
summary_en: Around 5660, R' Dovid Shifrin came to inform the Rebbe Rashab of his planned move to America, though not to ask permission.
story_body: Around 5660, before leaving for America, R' Dovid Shifrin of Pleshchenitsy (resident in Zembin) visited the Rebbe Rashab and said, 'Rebbe, I am going to America' — explaining that he had not come to ask permission, since his sons were already there and his ticket was bought, but that he did not want to be like a student who flees the cheder without telling his teacher. Shifrin became the central organizer of anash in America without title, office, or formal role, operating purely on personal bonds of chasidic brotherhood.

title_en: R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum travels to America for Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: Around 5673, R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum obtained the Rebbe Rashab's reluctant permission to travel to America, ostensibly to fundraise for Tomchei Tmimim.
story_body: Approximately in 5673, R' Shneur Zalman Rosenbaum traveled to America under the pretext of raising funds for Tomchei Tmimim. A letter later shown to the author from R' Yehoshua Kastrol in Trieste characterized the move as Rosenbaum's personal wish to reach America, for which he had persuaded the Rebbe Rashab to consent. The dating is anchored by the fact that the parallel Toras Emes yeshiva was founded just after Sukkos 5672.

title_en: Agudas Chasidei Chabad founded in the United States
summary_en: Agudas Chasidei Chabad of America was established in summer 5684 following the Rebbe Rayatz's directives.
story_body: In summer 5684 Rabbi Mendel Leib Lukshin of Krivoyrog reached America carrying lengthy guidance from the Rebbe Rayatz, with whom he had spoken at length in Rostov about establishing the new society. The office was set up behind a partition in the back of the Kremer brothers' wholesale trouser shop at 687 Broadway. R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer accepted the presidency at R' Dovid Shifrin's invitation, while Shifrin served as organizer and secretary.

title_en: Tmimim emigration pact made on Rosh Hashana 5685
summary_en: On Rosh Hashana 5685 the Tmimim resolved that every alumnus who reached the West would work to bring out his fellows from Russia.
story_body: Gathered for Rosh Hashana 5685, the chevrah of Tomchei Tmimim alumni committed that anyone who succeeded in leaving Soviet Russia for another country must labor on behalf of fellow Tmimim trying to follow. This compact shaped the rescue work of Agudas HaTmimim through the next decade. The author later operated under this mandate to secure visa affidavits and travel funds for many comrades — work which became sharply harder after the Rebbe Rayatz's 1929 American visit.

title_en: Funeral of R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer; presidency passes to his sons
summary_en: At his graveside on 6 Iyar 5685, the sons of R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer pledged to continue his work in Agudas Chasidei Chabad.
story_body: At the cemetery on 6 Iyar 5685, before R' Moshe Eliezer Kremer was lowered into the grave, R' Mendel Leib Lukshin halted the burial to extract a handshake commitment from the sons that they would continue their father's work as leaders of Agudas Chasidei Chabad. As eldest, R' Chaim Zalman Kremer (CHZK) thereby inherited the presidency. The agudah's office remained behind the family's wholesale trouser shop on Broadway.

title_en: Agudas HaTmimim founded in Manhattan on Motzei Shabbos Shemini
summary_en: On Motzei Shabbos Shemini 5686, Tomchei Tmimim alumni in America met at R' A. Simpson's home and founded Agudas HaTmimim.
story_body: On the night of Saturday parshas Shemini 5686, the Tomchei Tmimim alumni then in America assembled at R' A. Simpson's residence at 137 W. 116th Street in New York and formally established Agudas HaTmimim. R' Yitzchak Sneiderman and the shochet R' Avraham Ram joined the society. Its early meetings focused on supporting Maamad Beis Chayeinu (sending one thousand dollars in one campaign), securing affidavits to bring Tmimim from Russia, and founding a properly observant cheder.

title_en: Elul 5686 Agudas HaTmimim meeting commits funds to print Likkutei Torah
summary_en: In Elul 5686 the author convened Agudas HaTmimim at his home; members pledged to raise the funds needed to reprint Likkutei Torah in Warsaw.
story_body: After receiving word from Warsaw that Likkutei Torah could be reprinted there for roughly six hundred dollars, the author hosted a meeting of Agudas HaTmimim in Elul 5686. Members pledged sums proportionate to their means — some five dollars, some ten. The amount still fell short of even a down payment, and serious progress only came months later with the Tevet seudah.

title_en: Alter Rebbe yahrzeit seudah on 24 Tevet 5687 launches Likkutei Torah reprint
summary_en: On 24 Tevet 5687 the author held a seudah for the Alter Rebbe's hilula at which several hundred dollars were raised to begin printing Likkutei Torah.
story_body: On 24 Tevet 5687 the author convened a seudah at his home in honor of the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit; after delivering a maamar, he spoke before bentching about the Alter Rebbe, Likkutei Torah, and the Warsaw yeshiva's offer. Donors pledged on the spot in amounts of $25 and $50, raising several hundred dollars and finally enabling the print run. Total printing costs eventually reached over $800.

title_en: Likkutei Torah reprint completed in Warsaw by Agudas HaTmimim of America
summary_en: The Likkutei Torah reprint, sponsored by Agudas HaTmimim of America, was completed in 5688.
story_body: One thousand copies were printed; five hundred were given as a gift to Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and five hundred were shipped to America, bound, and sold for five dollars the set. The title page credited Agudas HaTmimim of America (the alumni of Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch) as sponsor, with the final volume listing every contributor. The printing significantly lifted the morale of anash in America.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz's first visit to the United States
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz visited the United States for the first time at the end of 5689.
story_body: At the close of 5689 the Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America for his first visit, traveling among Jewish communities including St. Louis, where he received $600 from R' Shaul Dovber Zislin's brother toward Zislin's rescue from Russia. After this visit obtaining Soviet exit permits became markedly harder, and the author's rescue work in subsequent years yielded fewer successes. The Rebbe's response to one rescue request was that supernatural intervention would be required to bring the family out.

title_en: R' Eliyahu Nochum Shklyar reaches America from Eretz Yisroel
summary_en: R' Eliyahu Nochum Shklyar arrived in America between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur 5690 with his wife and eldest daughter.
story_body: After leaving Russia for Eretz Yisroel and marrying there, R' Eliyahu Nochum Shklyar wished to join his father in America; the author persuaded the family to sponsor him by promising he would find a livelihood. Shklyar arrived between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur 5690 with his wife and eldest daughter Yehudis. A few days after Sukkos, the author placed him as shochet at the slaughterhouse where his uncle R' Yeshaya Jacobson was head shochet — a post he held for many years.

title_en: R' Aharon Eliezer Tzeitlin arrested on first night of Sukkos 5698
summary_en: R' Aharon Eliezer Tzeitlin, shochet in Mozhaysk and the author's brother-in-law, was arrested on the first night of Sukkos 5698 and exiled to Siberia.
story_body: Serving as shochet in Mozhaysk and operating a clandestine synagogue from his home, R' Aharon Eliezer Tzeitlin was seized by Soviet authorities on the first night of Sukkos 5698. He was deported to Siberia, where, weak in health, he died in his place of exile. The author had earlier exhausted himself attempting to bring Tzeitlin and his family to America; in 1929 the Rebbe Rayatz had told the author that only supernatural intervention could bring them out.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in the United States for the second time
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz arrived in America for the second time on 9 Adar Sheni 5700, this time to remain.
story_body: Having been extricated from Nazi-occupied Warsaw, the Rebbe Rayatz landed in America on 9 Adar Sheni 5700, beginning the era in which Lubavitch's center moved permanently to the United States. A small remaining stock of the 1928 Likkutei Torah reprint was still available on his arrival. Unlike his 1929 visit, this arrival marked permanent settlement and the relocation of the movement's leadership.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz speaks on mesirus nefesh of Avraham Avinu vs. Rabbi Akiva
summary_en: On Simchas Torah 5687 in Russia, the Frierdiker Rebbe explained to R' Yechezkel Feigin the distinction between Rabbi Akiva's and Avraham Avinu's approaches to mesirus nefesh.
story_body: Just after Simchas Torah 5687, R' Yechezkel Feigin wrote to the author conveying what the Frierdiker Rebbe had told him: Rabbi Akiva sought mesirus nefesh as an opportunity to fulfill the verse, whereas Avraham Avinu sought to publicize Hashem's existence in the world — accepting prison or being thrown into a furnace only as incidental consequences of that mission. The statement framed the Rebbe's own underground work in Soviet Russia and foreshadowed his arrest months later.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe arrested by Soviet authorities in Leningrad
summary_en: In 5687, the Frierdiker Rebbe was arrested in Soviet Russia for his clandestine work to strengthen Yiddishkeit, an event that reverberated through Chabad communities worldwide.
story_body: News of the arrest reached America only with significant delay. American Chassidim were caught off-guard and largely unaware of the mortal danger — they had not lived under the Soviet terror firsthand. Attorney Mr. Kramer turned to Washington through Senator Borah, who carried influence with the U.S. government and across the Atlantic, to seek the Rebbe's release.

title_en: American Chassidim lobby for Rebbe Rayatz's release
summary_en: Agudas Chassidei Chabad in America organized advocacy and fundraising to free the imprisoned Frierdiker Rebbe, working through Senator Borah in Washington.
story_body: Once word of the arrest arrived in the U.S., the chevra gathered to plan a response. Attorney Kramer engaged Senator Borah, an influential American politician whose voice carried weight even abroad. The American community's organized strength was weak, however, and the fundraising effort fell short of the urgency — Avraham Dov Levin der Malach even denied the whole story, reasoning that anything printed in the newspapers must be false.

title_en: R' Mordechai Dubin secures Rebbe Rayatz's exit visa via Latvian parliament
summary_en: R' Mordechai Dubin used Latvia's swing vote on recognizing the Soviet government to negotiate the Frierdiker Rebbe's release from Russia together with his manuscripts and library.
story_body: Newly independent Latvia operated as a democratic parliament whose vote on Soviet recognition was finely split. R' Mordechai Dubin, an Agudas Yisroel delegate with influence over several non-Jewish parliamentarians, traveled to Russia and promised that if the Rebbe were permitted to leave, he would help deliver Latvian recognition. After the Rebbe insisted at the Ohel in Rostov that he would not leave without his ksavim and seforim, Dubin returned and secured that concession as well.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe departs Soviet Russia after Sukkos
summary_en: Immediately after Sukkos 5688, the Frierdiker Rebbe and his family left Soviet Russia for Riga, Latvia, ending months of danger that followed his arrest and release.
story_body: After the events of Tishrei 5688 in Leningrad, the Frierdiker Rebbe and his household departed Russia just after Sukkos. The exit had been arranged through R' Mordechai Dubin's leverage in Latvian parliament, with permission also granted to bring the Rebbe's manuscripts and library out of the country. American Chassidim received news of the journey only later, in stages.

title_en: Brooklyn Chassidim wire $4,000 to Riga for the Rebbe's resettlement
summary_en: On Erev Shabbos Parshas Bereishis 5688, the author insisted on immediately telegraphing $4,000 to Riga to fund the Rebbe's exit from Russia despite communal hesitation.
story_body: Gathered in the Agudas Chassidei Chabad office in the Kramer brothers' factory, the author and R' A. Simpson — with Rabbi Lookstein's qualified support — pressed for an immediate $4,000 wire to R' Mordechai Dubin in Riga. The Kramer brothers initially balked at so large a sum and proposed delay, offering only $1,000, then $1,500. The author refused to leave the factory until the full sum was sent; by day's end the money was wired, and by Monday word arrived that the Rebbe and his family had reached Riga.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe arrives in Riga, Latvia
summary_en: Word reached American Chassidim that the Frierdiker Rebbe and his family had arrived safely in Riga, accompanied by his secretary R' Yechezkel Feigin.
story_body: On the Monday following the $4,000 wire transfer, news came that the Rebbe and his household had reached Riga. He was accompanied by his secretary and gabbai R' Yechezkel Feigin, who from Riga maintained an active correspondence with the author about day-to-day matters of the chatzer. Riga would serve as the Rebbe's primary residence for the next several years.

title_en: R' Shmuel Schneiderman, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky, and Chazzan Shmuel Kantroff arrive in USA
summary_en: Over the years 5686–5688, several Lubavitcher Tmimim including R' Shmuel Schneiderman, R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky, and Chazzan Shmuel Kantroff arrived in America.
story_body: During the period 5686–5688, a small wave of Tmimim reached the United States. R' Schneiderman settled in Philadelphia and remained there until his passing in 5715. Chazzan Kantroff moved between several towns before settling in Brooklyn, and R' Shlomo Aharon Kazarnovsky took a rabbinic position in Rochester before eventually being recruited as secretary and director of Agudas Chassidei Chabad.

title_en: Author begins importing Calabria esrogim to North America
summary_en: At the start of 5688, the author launched what would become a multi-decade enterprise of importing Calabria esrogim to America for Sukkos.
story_body: After Shavuos 5687 the author wrote to Tomchei Tmimim in Warsaw and to R' Yechezkel Feigin in Riga, asking them to ship ten Calabria esrogim to America in time for Sukkos 5688. Six were taken by named recipients, four remained unsold because of cosmetic flaws. By 5689 he was importing twenty in individual cardboard boxes, and the operation grew from there — he later credited himself as the first to bring Calabria esrogim to the Western Hemisphere.

title_en: R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin and R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin arrive in USA from Yeshivas Toras Emes
summary_en: At the end of Iyar 5688, R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin and R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin reached America to establish a dedicated fundraising office for Yeshivas Toras Emes of Eretz Yisroel.
story_body: Stopping in Riga en route to receive the Frierdiker Rebbe's guidance, the two arrived in Hoboken at the end of Iyar to set up an independent office for Toras Emes — separate from Agudas Chassidei Chabad. Tension arose with Agudas Chassidei Chabad's chairman R' Chaim Zalman Kramer, who lobbied them to channel all fundraising through the existing umbrella. After weeks of negotiation and a marathon overnight meeting that briefly produced a tentative agreement, Havlin instead rented his own offices on Blake Street and later on Henry Street, installing R' Mordechai Gruner to manage it.

title_en: Shavuos kiddush in Brooklyn unites Lubavitcher community around Toras Emes
summary_en: On Shabbos of Shavuos 5688, the author hosted a kiddush in Brownsville that drew local shtieblach into the cause of Yeshivas Toras Emes.
story_body: Shavuos 5688 fell on Friday and Shabbos. The author hosted a kiddush with cholent at his home, inviting his own shul's mispallelim and several minyanim of Anash from Brownsville — then considered 'the Yerushalayim of America.' R' Shlomo Zalman Havlin's warmth captivated the crowd, and fundraising drives for Toras Emes were soon organized in several local shuls including the Lubavitcher shtibel on Watkins Street under Rav Tzvi Hirsch Dachowitz.

title_en: Ma'amad committee founded under R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin in USA
summary_en: In summer 5688, a dedicated ma'amad committee was established under Agudas Chassidei Chabad to support the Frierdiker Rebbe's household, with R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin as chairman.
story_body: R' Yechezkel Feigin had written from Riga that Havlin and Rivkin would be enlisted to revive ma'amad fundraising in America. Because the Rebbe's household in Riga was under genuine financial strain — only about $300 per month was reaching him — Agudas Chassidei Chabad created a special ma'amad department chaired by R' Rivkin, with the tomim R' Elchonon Fogelman as a board member. A circular was sent to Anash, and the idea that ma'amad was its own primary obligation — not merely a line in the Agudah budget — began to take hold.

title_en: Maamar 'HaYom Haras Olam' in Yiddish received for printing in America
summary_en: In Elul 5688, the Frierdiker Rebbe's Yiddish ma'amar 'HaYom Haras Olam' arrived in America for printing and distribution, sponsored by R' Menachem Mendel Kunin.
story_body: The shochet R' Menachem Mendel Kunin — described as an exceptionally generous supporter of Lubavitch — personally underwrote the printing of the ma'amar. Its appearance in America was felt as a stirring of renewed Lubavitcher spirit among Anash, signaling that the warmth of the chatzer was reviving on American soil even as the Russian community had been shattered.

title_en: R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin appointed spiritual director of Yeshiva Torah Vodaas
summary_en: After Sukkos 5689, R' Moshe Dovber Rivkin became menahel ruchni of Yeshiva Torah Vodaas after R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz stepped down from that role.
story_body: R' Yeshaya Binush Tarshish approached the author with news that Torah Vodaas needed a new menahel ruchni following R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz's resignation from that position. The author and Rav Nissan Telushkin advocated for R' Rivkin, who at the time was floundering in an ill-defined ma'amad role. Rivkin was a natural fit — a scholar with yeshiva administrative experience — and his appointment came as Torah Vodaas stood on the threshold of major growth.

title_en: Tmimim raise emergency ma'amad funds after telegram from R' Feigin
summary_en: In mid-winter 5689, an urgent telegram from R' Yechezkel Feigin in Riga prompted twelve Tmimim to pledge emergency ma'amad funds at a meeting at R' Rivkin's home.
story_body: Roughly twelve Tmimim gathered at R' Rivkin's house, each pledging no less than $100 — except two who pledged $50, and R' Gershon Simpson who gave $150. The author himself took out a gmach loan he planned to repay $20 per week, though Providence enabled him to repay it sooner. One Tomim publicly demanded all give at least $100 yet ultimately contributed nothing himself and left angry with the author — an episode the author cites to illustrate how strained the Tmimim's finances were.

title_en: R' Shmuel Schneiderman passes away in Philadelphia
summary_en: R' Shmuel Schneiderman, who had arrived in America in the late 5680s and settled in Philadelphia, passed away there in 5715.
story_body: R' Schneiderman was among the small group of Tmimim who reached the United States during 5686–5688. He made his home in Philadelphia and remained there for the rest of his life, until his passing in 5715. His arrival had been part of the early wave that gradually rebuilt a Lubavitcher Tmimim presence in America during the years following the First World War.

title_en: Jacobson receives letter about Rebbe Rayatz's planned visit to America
summary_en: R. Yisrael Jacobson receives a letter from R. Yechezkel Feigin announcing that the Rebbe Rayatz plans to visit America the following summer.
story_body: In Shevat 5689 (early 1929), R. Yisrael Jacobson received a letter from the Rebbe Rayatz's secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin, informing him that the Rebbe was preparing to travel to the United States that summer on behalf of Russian Jewry. The letter sparked the first wave of preparations among Anash, who were astonished at the prospect but did not initially dare to formally invite the Rebbe themselves. Jacobson notes that it was the Rebbe's own self-sacrifice for Russian Jewry that ultimately drove him to undertake the difficult journey.

title_en: R. Feigin and Chaim Lieberman arrive in New York to prepare for Rebbe's visit
summary_en: Roughly a week before the Rebbe Rayatz's arrival, his secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin and Chaim Lieberman travel to New York to coordinate the visit.
story_body: In early Elul 5689, about a week before the Rebbe Rayatz himself was due to arrive, his secretary R. Yechezkel Feigin and Chaim Lieberman came to America to help organize the visit. They joined the ongoing debate over where the Rebbe would lodge, but no consensus emerged. By default the Rebbe was initially housed at R. Eliyahu Simpson's new apartment above a shul in Boro Park.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz arrives in America at New York Harbor
summary_en: On Wednesday, 13 Elul 5689 (September 18, 1929), the Rebbe Rayatz arrives at New York Harbor for his historic first visit to the United States.
story_body: Through the intervention of attorney Yekusiel Kremer, the Rebbe and his entourage were transferred at sea onto a small government vessel at South Ferry, sparing him the ordinary immigration disembarkation. A welcoming delegation that included R. Mordechai Lipa Lokshin, the Kremer brothers, Judge Philip Kleinfeld, and R. Shmuel Eliezer Nelson boarded the cutter to greet him. Despite a torrential downpour and an under-organized reception, the Rebbe was escorted through Manhattan by motorcycle police to R. Eliyahu Simpson's home in Boro Park, where he gave brief opening remarks ("Sadna de'ar'a chad hu") from the balcony.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz delivers maamar 'Hashkifa' on first Shabbos in America
summary_en: On Shabbos Parshas Ki Tavo, days after arriving in America, the Rebbe Rayatz delivers the maamar 'Hashkifa' at R. Eliyahu Simpson's Boro Park shul.
story_body: Just three days after disembarking in New York, the Rebbe Rayatz delivered the maamar 'Hashkifa Mim'on Kodshecha' on Shabbos Parshas Ki Tavo 5689. The maamar was later printed. It was given at R. Eliyahu Simpson's Boro Park shul, located below the apartment where the Rebbe was lodged during his first week in the United States.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe leads Rosh Hashana prayers at Anshei Lubavitch shul, Brownsville
summary_en: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn led the High Holy Day services at Beis Hamedrash Anshei Lubavitch, 195 Watkins Street, during his first visit to America.
story_body: Because the Rebbe's Crown Heights apartment was too small for the anticipated crowd, anash chose the large Anshei Lubavitch shul in Brownsville for his Yamim Noraim prayers. Rosh Hashana night prayers stretched many hours with weeping that listeners would never forget. The Rebbe stayed in the home of Dr. Akin on Stone Avenue, secured through community askan Aaron Siminovsky.

title_en: Famous Simchat Torah 'Eimasai Kaasi Mar' sicha and Stephen Wise visit
summary_en: During the Rebbe's first American Simchat Torah, Rabbi Stephen Wise visited and the Rebbe delivered the historic 'Eimasai Kaasi Mar' sicha later printed in three pamphlets.
story_body: Hakafos continued until dawn, and at the daytime meal the Rebbe was about to begin his sicha when Reform leader Rabbi Stephen Wise arrived to greet him. Yiddish journalists who were present struggled to capture the deep content; R. Chaim Lieberman, the Rebbe's secretary, stood behind him and transcribed the talk in pencil, later recopying it in ink. The sicha was published in a second edition in 5697 (1937) in three pamphlets.

title_en: Bar mitzvah of Meir Greenberg sparks beard-removal campaign in Crown Heights
summary_en: At the early-Cheshvan bar mitzvah of Meir Greenberg, the boy's father Yehoshua Falk had yechidus, prompting the Rebbe's sharp rebuke over American beard removal.
story_body: The author urged the bar mitzvah boy's father to seek the Rebbe's blessing; the father had removed his beard with depilatory cream as was then standard practice. After the visit the Rebbe scolded the author that a beardless Jew was attending his shul, demanding to know how he could eat his bread under such circumstances. This conversation launched a sustained effort to convince Crown Heights congregants to stop removing their beards.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe spends 19 Kislev in Philadelphia
summary_en: The Rebbe celebrated 19 Kislev 5690 in Philadelphia, drawing the Feder family back to observance.
story_body: On his cross-country American tour the Rebbe visited Philadelphia for Yud Tes Kislev. Among those drawn closer was the family of Michael Feder of Nevel, Vitebsk, who kashered their home. Their son Henry began putting on tefillin and briefly worked in the office handling the Rebbe's American visit.

title_en: Rebbe leads amud prayers in Crown Heights for Rebbetzin Rivka's yahrzeit
summary_en: On Shabbat 10 Shevat 5690 the Rebbe davened before the amud for the yahrzeit of his grandmother Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Rebbe Maharash.
story_body: Michael Feder traveled from Philadelphia and spent the entire Shabbat at the Rebbe's home to ease the test of Shabbat observance, davening near the Rebbe with hot tears streaming down. The Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of Rebbe Maharash, had passed away on Friday 10 Shevat 5674.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe spends Pesach in Chicago
summary_en: On his American tour the Rebbe celebrated Pesach in Chicago, drawing thousands to greet him.
story_body: As part of the Rebbe's extensive travel across the United States he visited Chicago for Pesach 5690. In every city he visited, thousands and sometimes over ten thousand Jews came to meet him at the train station. He inspired many families and communities to draw closer to Yiddishkeit.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe spends Shavuot in the Bronx
summary_en: The Rebbe celebrated Shavuot 5690 in the Bronx, praying and delivering a maamar at the East 172nd Street mikveh shul.
story_body: On Shavuot the Rebbe prayed in the synagogue attached to the mikveh at 172 East and delivered a maamar. During his US visit he also delivered chassidus on weekdays, including a Tuesday parshat Toldot maamar at Beis Knesses Tzemach Tzedek on Marcy Street in Brooklyn that drew an estimated five thousand people.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe departs America aboard the ship Bremen
summary_en: On 21 Tammuz 5690 Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn left the United States after his historic ten-month visit, sailing on the ship Bremen.
story_body: Before departure the tmimim gathered at the Rebbe's hotel expecting a farbrengen. The Rebbe prolonged his prayers until 5pm and then delivered over an hour of sharp rebuke. A large crowd including delegations from many cities came to the port to see him off, where the Rebbe addressed them with words of farewell and encouragement.

title_en: Founding of Agudas Chassidei Chabad branches in New York neighborhoods
summary_en: During his American visit the Rebbe convened anash leaders, drafted the bylaws of Agudas Chassidei Chabad, and established neighborhood branches across greater New York and other cities.
story_body: The Rebbe summoned the chief Chabad askanim and met with them several times in his quarters to draft the agudah's constitution. Greater New York was divided into neighborhoods with appointed gabba'im and ledger books, and the Rebbe wrote a personal blessing in his own hand at the head of each branch's book. At the Rebbe's request Shmuel Hein was appointed secretary of the agudah.

title_en: Vaad formed to bring the Frierdiker Rebbe to settle in America
summary_en: Before the Rebbe's summer 1930 departure, anash formed a committee chaired by Max (M.M.) Halbreich to bring the Rebbe to settle permanently in America.
story_body: An awakening grew among anash in summer 5690 that the Rebbe should immigrate to the United States. A vaad was chosen with Max Halbreich, brother and son-in-law of Chaim Halbreich, as chairman and R. Nissan Telushkin among its energetic activists, and funds were raised. The Rebbe would later write on 18 Cheshvan 5691 that he did not intend to settle in America.

title_en: Simchat Torah 5691 sicha and 'Pratz Klub' disruption attempt
summary_en: At the Simchat Torah 5691 gathering the Rebbe delivered sharp words to a crowd that included secularists, while members of the 'Pratz Klub' attempted to sabotage the meeting.
story_body: The printed sicha records the Rebbe's pointed remarks to the assembled, some of whom were freethinkers. During the gathering the electric lights were briefly extinguished and reignited; the disruptors had actually intended to cut the electric wires. The Rebbe later remarked that at the moment of speaking he did not understand what was forcing the content out of him.

title_en: R. Yechezkel Feigin tells Rebbe about 'Pratz Klub' plot
summary_en: On Friday 25 Tishrei 5691 R. Yechezkel Feigin entered the Rebbe to disclose that the 'Pratz Klub' had come with malicious intent at the Simchat Torah gathering.
story_body: Feigin had initially withheld the information about the disruption attempt and the planned cutting of the electric wires. When he finally told the Rebbe, the Rebbe responded that now he understood what had compelled him to deliver the pointed words he had spoken at the gathering.

title_en: Rebbe writes that he will not settle permanently in America
summary_en: In a letter dated 18 Cheshvan 5691 the Rebbe informed anash that he did not plan to immigrate permanently to the United States.
story_body: Despite the vaad's efforts to bring him to settle in America, the Rebbe wrote that this was not his intention. He later explained to the author in Elul 5699 that the manner of his American visit had been that of a public askan, an area in which he had skill and success but which was not his true work — his work was chassidim and chassidus.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe delivers 19 Kislev 5691 maamar on divine influx
summary_en: On 19 Kislev 5691 the Rebbe delivered a maamar teaching that divine influence to the souls of Israel flows from the Name Havayah by way of overriding nature.
story_body: R. Yechezkel Feigin reported the content of the maamar to the author in a letter from Kislev 5691. The Rebbe taught that the spiritual influence to neshamot Yisrael is drawn from the name Havayah via meavir ha-teva — overriding the natural order.

title_en: Tmimim begin chassidus shiurim that seed Achei Tmimim
summary_en: At the start of 5692 the tmimim Avraham M.M. Baranetzki, Yitzchak Kalodny, and Tzvi Schechter began joining the author's chassidus shiurim for yeshiva students.
story_body: The three initially found the lessons difficult and came only to socialize, but after a few weeks of informal gatherings they returned to the formal Tanya study. They were later joined by Mordechai Altein, Yitzchak Matashin, Mordechai Fischer, and Zerach Gordon, laying the foundation for the Achei Tmimim organization.

title_en: R. Yochanan Gordon immigrates to America from Dokshitz
summary_en: In 5692 the tamim R. Yochanan Gordon, shochet of Dokshitz, immigrated to America with his family including sons Nissan and Sholom Dovber.
story_body: On arrival R. Yochanan replaced his sons' Russian-style caps with American hats. When Sholom Dovber was embarrassed to enter the author's home wearing the new hat during Chol Hamoed Pesach, the author explained how garments of honor change with time and place, citing teachings from both the Rebbe Rashab and the Rebbe Rayatz on the matter.

title_en: Author's second visit to the Frierdiker Rebbe in Elul 5699
summary_en: In Elul 5699 the author visited the Rebbe for a second time and discussed the question of the Rebbe's settling in America.
story_body: The author delivered 213 pidyonot and regards from individuals and communal matters. The Rebbe explained that although people had approached him about moving to the United States, he had not held by the idea because the mode of his earlier American visit had been that of a public askan rather than reflecting his true purpose with chassidim and chassidus.

title_en: Passing of Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of the Rebbe Maharash
summary_en: Rebbetzin Rivka, wife of Rebbe Maharash, passed away on Friday 10 Shevat 5674.
story_body: The Rebbetzin's yahrzeit on 10 Shevat is observed by the Frierdiker Rebbe leading prayers before the amud. The date is referenced in the narrative of the Frierdiker Rebbe's 10 Shevat 5690 prayers in Crown Heights, when Michael Feder traveled from Philadelphia to be present.

title_en: Expansion of Chassidus study program for yeshiva students in Brooklyn
summary_en: The author expanded a Chassidus study program for yeshiva students into multiple weekly sessions of Tanya and maamarim.
story_body: Beginning with a Motzaei Shabbat Tanya class accompanied by stories of Lubavitch, the program grew to weekday classes on maamarim received from Europe and on Likutei Dibburim. The author also traveled twice weekly to the Division Ave Shtibel in Williamsburg to teach students. Participants included Avraham M.M. Barnetzki, Meir Greenberg, Menachem Mendel Feldman, and Yitzchak Kaladny.

title_en: Shavuos farbrengen with yeshiva students sparks public scandal
summary_en: A Shavuos farbrengen at the author's home where bochurim tasted mashke for the first time provoked a public outcry in Brownsville.
story_body: At the gathering R' Yochanan Gordon and his brother R' Yitzchak Yaakov Gordon participated; the boys, seated on the floor, were given mashke two or three times. News quickly spread that 'R' Yisroel Jacobson had gotten the boys drunk,' causing an uproar throughout Brownsville and the Williamsburg yeshiva. Parents from non-Chabad backgrounds began visiting the author's home to understand his influence on their sons.

title_en: R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz turns against Chabad influence at Torah Vodaas
summary_en: Torah Vodaas head R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, alarmed at growing Chabad influence on his students, attached a group of them to R' Chaim Avraham Dov Levin (the Malach).
story_body: After introducing Kuzari, Chovos Halevavos, Noam Elimelech and Tanya into Torah Vodaas, Mendlowitz objected to the author 'turning students into Lubavitcher chassidim.' He led a group of students, joined by several baalei batim, to R' Chaim Avraham Dov Levin — the Malach — who served as rav in the Nusach Ha'ari shul in the Bronx. R' Moshe David Rivkin was later sent to ask the author to stop teaching Chassidus to the students.

title_en: Malach's students leave Torah Vodaas to found Yeshivas Nesivos Olam
summary_en: Students of the Malach broke away from Torah Vodaas to establish a separate yeshiva called Nesivos Olam.
story_body: Adopting distinctive external practices — long coats, large tzitzis, no ties, unfolded hat brims, and learning only from Slavita and Zhitomir Talmud editions — the Malach's students openly clashed with Torah Vodaas. They eventually left and founded Nesivos Olam, drawing major support from R' Ben Tzion Weberman (formerly a pillar of Torah Vodaas) and the wealthy R' Avraham Yaakov Katz.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Hamasmid Horowitz arrives in USA as Rebbe's shadar
summary_en: The renowned chassid R' Yitzchak Horowitz (Hamasmid) arrived in America as a shadar of the Rebbe Rayatz before Rosh Hashana 5694.
story_body: Coming on a mission related to Maamad (financial support for the Rebbe), he lodged at the author's home during his stay. After his visit he returned to Riga and corresponded with the author. His presence helped consolidate Chabad activity in New York.

title_en: Passing of R' M.M. Lukshin, head of Agudas Chassidei Chabad
summary_en: R' M.M. Lukshin, head of Agudas Chassidei Chabad in America, passed away in Cheshvan 5694.
story_body: His death left a leadership gap in the American Chabad organization at a pivotal moment when student activities in Brooklyn were expanding. The author was simultaneously organizing a dedicated High Holidays minyan for his students.

title_en: Separate Yamim Noraim minyan organized for Chabad students in Brooklyn
summary_en: A dedicated High Holidays minyan was established for select chassidim and the author's students at the Bikur Cholim hall on Osborne Street.
story_body: R' Yochanan Gordon served as the baal tefillah and baal tokea. Separate hakafos were held on Simchas Torah after those at the author's main shul. The success of this arrangement led to the idea of a year-round dedicated minyan for the students.

title_en: Permanent students' minyan established at Toras Mitzion in Brownsville
summary_en: With help of R' Aba Rivkin, a permanent Shabbos minyan for the author's students was established at the Toras Mitzion building.
story_body: Initial Shabbatos sometimes lacked a full minyan and R' Yochanan Gordon complained about the difficulty. Over time the minyan grew and moved to the Anshe Ozaritz shul at 885 Hopkinson Ave. Eventually the minyan flourished with multiple minyanim attending Shabbos services and influence spread further into the yeshiva world.

title_en: Founding of Mesivta R' Chaim Berlin after Chabad-led plan is blocked
summary_en: An attempt to establish a Chabad-led mesivta at the Stone Ave Talmud Torah was preempted by local rabbanim who founded Mesivta R' Chaim Berlin instead.
story_body: Parents from R' Chaim Berlin's yeshiva had approached the author to start a high school division combining limudei kodesh with secular studies, and R' Yitzchak Shmidman of Yeshivas Toras Chaim had pledged support. Brownsville and East New York rabbanim, fearing Lubavitch influence, secretly approached the young R' Yitzchak Hutner and the Stone Ave Talmud Torah baalei batim. They opened what became known as Mesivta R' Chaim Berlin with Hutner as Rosh Mesivta.

title_en: Author becomes director of Yeshivas Toras Emes in Boro Park
summary_en: After Chabad chassidim were invited into the leadership of Yeshivas Toras Emes in Boro Park, the author entered as director at the start of 5697.
story_body: He brought in R' Yosef Dov Castel as Rosh Mesivta of the upper division, R' Yissachar Frankel for the Gemara class, and R' Nachman Mandel as a teacher. The yeshiva's spiritual standard rose substantially and Brownsville parents sent their sons there. However, Anash failed to engage with the yeshiva's leadership, the finances deteriorated under fundraiser R' Baruch Karf, and the author eventually withdrew when salaries went unpaid.

title_en: Author departs USA on Queen Mary to visit Rebbe Rayatz in Europe
summary_en: On 28 Tammuz 5697 the author sailed from the USA on the Queen Mary to visit the Rebbe Rayatz at Perchtoldsdorf near Vienna.
story_body: Almost all his students gathered at the dock to see him off. He carried a list of 213 students learning Chassidus and brought pidyonos from each one. He also planned to visit the yeshiva at Otwock during the trip.

title_en: Author meets Rebbe Rayatz at Perchtoldsdorf near Vienna
summary_en: The author met the Rebbe Rayatz at his Austrian retreat to report on the 213 students learning Chassidus in America.
story_body: The Rebbe took deep interest in the students; when asked which maamarim to teach them, he answered 'whatever you learn with them — the main thing is the embroidery (ushibatzta).' The Rebbe also remarked on R' D.M. Rabinowitz's unsanctioned trip to Eretz Yisrael saying 'Grandfather would command, Father would say, and I say as it comes out — but one must obey.' Before parting, the Rebbe instructed the author to write down everything he saw and heard on the journey.

title_en: Author visits Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Otwock
summary_en: During his European trip the author visited the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva at Otwock, Poland.
story_body: The visit gave the author a direct view of the yeshiva's mashpi'im and study atmosphere. This experience later shaped his decisions about sending American students to study there.

title_en: Author departs Vienna at end of European visit
summary_en: The author left Vienna on 2 Elul 5697 after his visit with the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: He proceeded to Paris en route home, arriving there the following day. His journey would later resonate with the Rebbe's letter to R' D.M. Rabinowitz about the spiritual significance of arriving in America.

title_en: Author arrives in Paris en route home from Rebbe
summary_en: On 3 Elul 5697 the author reached Paris and visited R' Shneur Zalman Schneerson.
story_body: R' Schneerson informed him that R' D.M. Rabinowitz had been in Paris hoping to meet him and convey regards from the Rebbe Rayatz, but had been forced to leave for Marseille to catch his ship to America. The author's own ship would depart Le Havre the following day.

title_en: Author returns to New York from European trip
summary_en: The author arrived in New York on 10 or 11 Elul 5697 after his visit with the Rebbe Rayatz in Vienna.
story_body: On returning he immediately arranged through Agudas Chassidei Chabad secretary Asher Hershman to monitor newspapers for the arrival of R' D.M. Rabinowitz's Dollar Line ship. Upon his return, the regular Chassidus study sessions and farbrengens strengthened and more students joined.

title_en: R' D.M. Rabinowitz arrives in USA on Chai Elul
summary_en: R' Dovid Meir Rabinowitz arrived in New York from Eretz Yisrael on Chai Elul 5697 (the Baal Shem Tov's birthday).
story_body: Delayed a week by a maritime workers' strike, he understood the Rebbe Rayatz's earlier letter — which had said his date of arrival would be propitious — as a hint to the spiritual significance of Chai Elul. He convened a farbrengen with Anash that day at the Broadway Central Hotel to fulfill the Rebbe's allusion. The letter cited tradition that on Chai Elul the Baal Shem Tov spoke Torah publicly before his students.

title_en: Shadar R' Mordechai Chefetz arrives in America
summary_en: R' Mordechai Chefetz, sent by the Rebbe Rayatz, arrived in the USA in early Adar 5698 to warm up Anash.
story_body: Stationed at the author's home at 494 Stone Ave for about twelve weeks, his farbrengens drew students and bochurim from major New York yeshivos and sometimes lasted until just before dawn. R' Yisroel Jacobson Feigin's letter of 21 Shevat 5698 conveyed the Rebbe's praise of Chefetz as a 'penimi who remembers the past with fine inner sensitivity.' His visit substantially elevated the reputation of Lubavitch among yeshiva students.

title_en: Engagement of Chaya Sarah Jacobson to R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht
summary_en: The engagement (kishurei tnaim) of the author's eldest daughter Chaya Sarah to R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht took place on 3 Nissan 5698.
story_body: Immediately after the tnaim, Hecht stopped removing his beard, an act that made a strong impression on the students. That summer R' Yitzchak Kaladny also stopped shaving his beard. The simcha was infused with a Chassidic atmosphere.

title_en: Wedding of Chaya Sarah Jacobson and R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht
summary_en: The wedding of the author's daughter Chaya Sarah to R' Shlomo Zalman Hecht took place on 3 Elul 5698 with the Rebbe Rayatz's blessing.
story_body: The Rebbe had agreed that after the seven days of feasting the couple would travel to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock. Their departure together with other American students became a milestone in Chabad outreach. The wedding was thus a turning point in the American student movement.

title_en: American bochurim travel to Tomchei Tmimim Otwock to study
summary_en: Right after Sukkos, around Parshas Lech Lecha 5699, the author's son-in-law, daughter, and bochurim Avraham M.M. Barnetzki and Dovber Levy sailed on the Queen Mary to study at Tomchei Tmimim in Otwock.
story_body: R' Dovber Levy, an American-born great-nephew of the Malach, had transferred to the author's circle and wanted to study in Europe; the author personally covered the shortfall in his fare. R' Aryeh Leib Gellman of Mizrachi, who sailed with them, later returned praising the bochurim's stringent yiras shomayim aboard ship, including their refusal to daven in a shul without a mechitza. The departure boosted morale among the remaining students in New York.

title_en: Author's second trip to Rebbe Rayatz in Otwock with six students
summary_en: In late summer of 5699, the author traveled to Otwock, Poland with six chosen Achei Tmimim students to study at Tomchei Tmimim and have yechidus with the Frierdiker Rebbe.
story_body: On the eve of World War II, the author led a group of six of his best students from Achei Tmimim to Europe, where the Frierdiker Rebbe then resided in Otwock, Poland and the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva was located. The trip required complex arrangements, especially convincing parents who saw the plan as extreme and dangerous. During their first yechidus, prepared for over a long spiritual period, the Rebbe told the author that if he came to America it would be solely to function as Nasi of Chabad and spread the Alter Rebbe's teachings.

title_en: Winter devoted to rescuing Rebbe Rayatz from Nazi-occupied Warsaw
summary_en: The entire winter of 5700 was devoted to rescuing the Frierdiker Rebbe, his family, and entourage from Nazi-occupied Warsaw.
story_body: After the German invasion of Poland, the winter of 5700 (1939–1940) was consumed by coordinated efforts to extract Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, his family, and his entourage from occupied Warsaw. A dedicated book documenting the events and testimony of those days is being prepared for publication. The rescue effort drew on diplomatic, logistical, and financial mobilization across the Chabad network.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe arrives in the United States
summary_en: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn arrived in America in the winter of 5700, opening a new chapter of Chabad activity in the United States.
story_body: After being rescued from Nazi-occupied Warsaw, the Frierdiker Rebbe reached the United States in the winter of 5700. His arrival mobilized the author, who immediately took on intensive new responsibilities: mashpia at central Tomchei Tmimim, chairman and director of Beis Rivkah and its New York branches, general gabbai of the Chevra Kadisha, rav of the Lubavitch community in New York, organizer of the Tomchei Tmimim branch in Newark, and founder and mashpia of the Hadar HaTorah yeshiva for newly observant students.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe's earlier American visit on eve of Wall Street crash
summary_en: The Frierdiker Rebbe's prior visit to America took place just before the Wall Street stock market crash, with hundreds of thousands of dollars raised for Soviet Jewry.
story_body: Recalling his earlier American visit during the 5699 yechidus, the Frierdiker Rebbe explained that his previous trip had been for the sake of general Jewish life and that he succeeded in that goal, with thanks to G-d. He raised several hundred thousand dollars to aid the Jews of Russia, on the very eve of the Wall Street stock market collapse, with his very presence stirring American Jewry to support his far-reaching activities. His deeper aim, however, had been spiritual: to awaken a feeling of teshuvah in the hearts of American Jewry.

title_en: Passing of the author on 17 Sivan 5735
summary_en: The author of the memoir, a longtime mashpia and Chabad activist in New York, passed away on 17 Sivan 5735 after 35 years of intensive sacred work following the Frierdiker Rebbe's arrival in America.
story_body: Across the 35 years between the Frierdiker Rebbe's arrival in America and his own passing, the author served as rav in the Brownsville community, member of the Agudas Chassidei Chabad leadership, and dealer in Calabrian etrogim. After 5700 he took on additional roles as mashpia at central Tomchei Tmimim, head of Beis Rivkah, general gabbai of the Chevra Kadisha, rav of the Lubavitch kehilla in New York, organizer of Tomchei Tmimim in Newark, and founder and mashpia of Hadar HaTorah. He maintained this vigorous, multi-front work until his final day.

title_en: Di Yiddishe Heim issue 64 publishes author's Otwock memoir
summary_en: Issue 64 of Di Yiddishe Heim, summer 5735, carried the author's English-language account of his 1939 trip to the Frierdiker Rebbe in Otwock, appearing days before his passing.
story_body: In the summer 5735 issue of Di Yiddishe Heim, on page 5 of the English section, the author published his own account of leading six students from Achei Tmimim to the Frierdiker Rebbe in Otwock on the eve of World War II. The piece appeared only days before his passing on 17 Sivan 5735. It preserved both the practical narrative of the journey and the Rebbe's words during their yechidus about his future plans for America.

title_en: Birth of M. Schusterman in Zlobin
summary_en: M. Schusterman was born on Friday, Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5674 in Zlobin to Eli son of Achiezer and Rachel daughter of Aharon Tzvi Hirsch.
story_body: Schusterman was born in the town of Zlobin, situated between Homel, Bobruisk, Rogachov, and the Volhynian district. His mother related that there was a solar eclipse on the day of his birth. The birth came three weeks after the outbreak of World War I on Tisha B'Av.

title_en: Outbreak of World War I on Tisha B'Av
summary_en: World War I began on Tisha B'Av 5674, three weeks before Schusterman's birth.
story_body: The First World War broke out on the ninth of Av 5674. Schusterman notes this in his memoir as a marker for his birth date, which came three weeks later in the town of Zlobin in White Russia.

title_en: Rabbi Moshe Axelrod leaves Zlobin for Suraz
summary_en: Rabbi Moshe Axelrod, the young Chasidic rabbi of Zlobin, left in 5687 to accept the prestigious rabbinate of Suraz.
story_body: Axelrod had filled the position of his brother-in-law Rabbi Menachem Mendel Dubrawsky in Zlobin. The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a letter of blessing upon his acceptance of the Suraz rabbinate, noting that 'from of old, men of name have sat there.' His departure opened the way for Rabbi Yerachmiel Binyaminson to come to Zlobin.

title_en: Rabbi Binyaminson accepts the Zlobin rabbinate
summary_en: Rabbi Yerachmiel Binyaminson came from Shtchedrin to serve as rabbi of Zlobin after gaining the elder rabbi's consent, ending factional strife in the town.
story_body: Binyaminson refused to enter a town divided by factional 'sides.' He first visited the elder Rabbi Wilda for his blessing, declaring he would not come if opposed. The elder rabbi agreed, the factions dissolved, and the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote praising the peace established (Sefer HaMaamarim 5687, supplement p. 269). Schusterman's father served as matchmaker for the arrangement.

title_en: Founding of the small Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Suraz
summary_en: Rabbi Moshe Axelrod founded a small yeshiva in Suraz upon assuming the rabbinate there, drawing seven students from Zlobin plus three locals.
story_body: Schusterman's father brought seven twelve-year-old students from Zlobin, including the author, and arranged their lodging and meals. Three additional local students brought the total to ten. Rabbi Yeshaya Alewski, the shochet, served as magid shiur teaching Gemara Gittin. Axelrod insisted the boys read Torah publicly despite being below bar mitzvah age.

title_en: Arrest and release of the Frierdiker Rebbe
summary_en: The Frierdiker Rebbe was arrested and released during the summer of 5687.
story_body: Schusterman recalls that the arrest and release of the Rebbe occurred during the summer of 5687, while he was studying in Suraz. The Suraz community was unaware of events at the time; Rabbi Axelrod may have known but feared to publicize it, as the Yevsektzia had begun operating in Suraz as well.

title_en: Death of Schusterman's sister Shayna in scarlet fever epidemic
summary_en: Schusterman's married sister Shayna (Sanya) died on 25 Menachem Av 5687 after five days of illness during a scarlet fever epidemic in Zlobin.
story_body: Scarlet fever swept Zlobin, with virtually no household spared. Shayna left a two-year-old son named Achiezer, who was later reported lost in the war. Rabbi Binyaminson's adopted son Alterke also died in the epidemic, as did Chaim, son of the melamed R' Shalom Horowitz, on his thirteenth birthday on Rosh Hashanah.

title_en: Bar mitzvah of M. Schusterman in Suraz
summary_en: Schusterman became bar mitzvah on Erev Rosh Chodesh Elul 5687 in Suraz, where he was studying at the small yeshiva.
story_body: After Shacharit at the 'rabbi's minyan' a bottle of liquor was placed on the table. Rabbi Axelrod called on the boy to deliver a drasha on tefillin from the verse 'V'shamarta es ha-chukah ha-zos l'mo'adah.' There were no invitations, no dinner, and no chair-lifting — only the minyan's congregants saying 'l'chaim.'

title_en: Closure of Tomchei Tmimim branch in Romen
summary_en: The Tomchei Tmimim branch in Romen was disbanded in 5689, forcing students including Schusterman to return home.
story_body: Schusterman had traveled to Romen to study at the yeshiva but had to return when it closed. The rosh yeshiva, Rabbi Yaakov ('Yana') Gurary, a local of Romen, was left without a position. Some townspeople proposed he assume the vacant rabbinate previously held by Rabbi Chaim Shneerson (grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek), but Rabbi Binyaminson — when offered the post — withdrew upon seeing factions form.

title_en: Author moves to Moscow to learn the retouching trade
summary_en: In Elul 5698 the author left his hometown Zlobin and settled in Moscow to learn photo-retouching and to be able to daven with a minyan for the approaching High Holidays.
story_body: In Zlobin it was impossible to daven with a minyan on the Yamim Noraim, so the author moved to Moscow, found temporary lodging in the Marina-Roshcha neighborhood near the shul, and began studying retouching. R' Zusya Paz, the chassidic shamash of the Marina-Roshcha synagogue who had known him from Surazh years earlier, welcomed him warmly. Hearing that a shidduch had been proposed for him, R' Zusya immediately said, 'Don't even think about a shidduch — I have one for you,' meaning his niece in Shumyachi.

title_en: Father buys an apartment in Cherbinov ahead of the wedding
summary_en: In Tishrei 5700 the author's father came to Moscow and bought him a 20-square-meter apartment in the Cherbinov settlement, about an hour by tram from the Marina-Roshcha synagogue.
story_body: Moscow's housing shortage was so severe that many bochurim could not marry. The father's finances had improved, so he came in Tishrei 5700, purchased the small apartment, and bought the essential furniture. The author would later travel into Moscow only rarely, working from home on retouching jobs.

title_en: Civil registration of the marriage in Moscow
summary_en: On 1 April 1940 the author and his fianceé entered a Soviet registry office and registered her as his wife so she could gain residency rights in Moscow.
story_body: Without a Moscow residence permit, the bride-to-be had to drift among relatives, and anyone caught without papers was deported from the city within 24 hours. Because the author held a permit for his apartment in Cherbinov, the couple went to the registry office on 1 April 1940 and registered her legally as his wife. Only later did the idea of an actual wedding crystallise in her mind.

title_en: Tena'im in the author's Cherbinov apartment
summary_en: On the night of 4 Nisan 5700, ten chassidim gathered in the author's Cherbinov apartment for the formal tena'im, with his father representing the chosson and the bride's uncles R' Zusya and R' Chaim Chanye Paz representing the kallah.
story_body: The seasoned businessman father insisted the matter not be left hanging in mid-air, saying, 'Let the child have a name.' R' Zusya brought ten men from the shul — among them R' Sa'adia Liberov and his brother R' Chaim Chanye Paz of Klimovichi — to Cherbinov, and the tena'im were signed on the night before 4 Nisan 5700. The father then returned to Zlobin together with the author's sister Esther.

title_en: Wedding of the author at the Marina-Roshcha synagogue, Moscow
summary_en: On 9 Tammuz 5700 the author married Henya Chasha Fradkin of Shumyachi, with kabbalas panim and chuppah held at the Marina-Roshcha synagogue and the meal in a neighbour's house next door.
story_body: The principal mechutanim from the bride's side were her mother Feigl, her brother Gershon, and her uncle R' Zusya the shamash with his daughter. R' Yakov 'Yana' Goray of Romen and R' Shmarya Sasonkin (Batumer), who had fled Leningrad, were among the chassidim who attended. Because of the Soviet climate of fear, no invitations were sent and no photographs were taken.

title_en: Underground Yud-Beis Tammuz farbrengen during the author's sheva brachos
summary_en: Because Yud-Beis Tammuz 5700 fell within the author's sheva brachos, his home in Cherbinov became the disguised venue for a clandestine Chag HaGeulah farbrengen led by R' Nissan Nemenov and attended by R' B-Z Shemtov, R' Dovid Bravman and many others.
story_body: With public farbrengens impossible, R' Zusya the shamash quietly redirected anyone asking where to celebrate Yud-Beis Tammuz to the author's home, since the sheva brachos provided a cover for the NKVD. Chassidim arrived from the tram carrying a suitcase of mashke and farbeisen; the house and courtyard filled, and they danced 'Veharikosi lochem brocho' so vigorously that the floor began to creak. R' Yona Cohen broke up the gathering at dawn so that participants could leave individually — a neighbour across the lane worked for the NKVD.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim bochurim arrested in Kursk
summary_en: In late Av or early Elul 5700 the NKVD arrested all the bochurim of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Kursk, including the author's brother-in-law Gershon Fradkin.
story_body: Coming to daven at the Marina-Roshcha shul, the author was told by R' Zusya that the entire Kursk yeshiva had been seized. During the search of Gershon's lodgings the NKVD had found a postcard addressed to the author's Cherbinov apartment and taken it with them. The author's mother-in-law rushed to Kursk to plead for Gershon, his wife went to Shumyachi to nurse her ailing father, and the author himself fled to his parents in Zlobin to wait out the Yamim Noraim.

title_en: Gershon Fradkin released from solitary confinement in Kursk
summary_en: In Cheshvan 5701 Gershon Fradkin returned to Moscow after being released from solitary confinement in Kursk, where he had spent all of Tishrei.
story_body: Gershon had been the last bochur to arrive in Kursk before the mass arrest and had 'not yet had time to sin much,' so the NKVD released him alone. He spent all of Tishrei — Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Simchas Torah — in the 'Kamera Adinochka' solitary cell, and told the author he had even worked out without pencil or paper on what date Yom Kippur would fall the following year. The imprisonment damaged his lungs and he travelled back to Shumyachi to recuperate.

title_en: Germany invades the USSR; the bride's family flees Shumyachi
summary_en: When Germany attacked the Soviet Union in the summer of 5701, the author's wife's family — her parents R' Zusman and Feigl and her brothers Gershon and Nechemia — abandoned Shumyachi and fled eastwards, only to be overtaken by the Wehrmacht and murdered.
story_body: Gershon, the same brother who had been freed from Kursk, ultimately perished with the rest of his family, while the Tomchei Tmimim bochurim who had remained in NKVD captivity — including R' Yehoshua Raskin of London — survived their sentences and went on to rebuild families in Israel. The author writes that 'the ways of Hashem are hidden from us.' His wife Henya was the sole survivor of the entire Fradkin–Paz family.

title_en: Author arrives in Samarkand and joins an underground minyan
summary_en: On the last Shabbos of Elul 5701 the author reached the old city of Samarkand, joined the Lubavitcher refugees who had already escaped Leningrad, and attended the secret Torah reading hosted by R' Aizik Karasik.
story_body: R' Yeshaya Hofin helped him rent an upstairs room in a tupik near the Mahalla market and warned that Lubavitcher chassidim feared to daven in the Bukharan synagogue. The author was let into the underground minyan in time for the last Shabbos of Elul. Because his landlady also possessed a sefer Torah, he and R' Aizik agreed to alternate Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur services between their homes, with the strict condition that only ten men attend.

title_en: Polish refugees crash the Yom Kippur minyan in Samarkand
summary_en: On Erev Yom Kippur 5702 Polish-Jewish refugees newly released from Siberia overheard 'Kol Nidrei' from R' Aizik Karasik's courtyard in Samarkand and forced their way in, far overflowing the planned ten-man minyan.
story_body: After Stalin made peace with the Polish government-in-exile in 1941 he released his Polish-citizen prisoners from Siberia, and thousands drifted south into the warm Central Asian republics, including Samarkand. Wandering from courtyard to courtyard in search of a Kol Nidrei, they began pounding on R' Aizik's gate until it opened and the house filled. Frightened by the exposure, R' Aizik refused to host the following day, and the worshippers returned to the author's apartment to complete Yom Kippur.

title_en: Nazi murder of the Jewish women of Shumyachi and surrounding shtetlach
summary_en: On 28 Adar 5702 the Nazis murdered the Jewish women gathered from Shumyachi, Klimovichi, Potsep and surrounding shtetlach, including the author's mother-in-law Feigl bas R' Moshe Leib Paz.
story_body: After the war the author learned that the Germans had concentrated the Jews of the surrounding shtetlach in a single killing site, murdering the women on 28 Adar 5702. The author's wife Henya was the sole survivor of the entire Fradkin–Paz family; the children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren they raised are credited to the merit of these kedoshim.

title_en: Nazi murder of the Jewish men of Shumyachi and surrounding shtetlach
summary_en: On 29 Adar 5702 the Nazis murdered the Jewish men of the Shumyachi region, including the author's father-in-law R' Zusman b'r Gershon Fradkin and his sons Gershon and Nechemia.
story_body: A day after killing the women, the Germans murdered the men of the gathered community. R' Zusman, the Shumyachi shochet and bodek who had also served as acting rav after R' Tzvi Edelstein left for Eretz Yisrael, had refused earlier suggestions to move to Moscow, saying that without him the townspeople would be forced to eat treif. He, his two young sons and the rest of the men were murdered on 29 Adar 5702.

title_en: Author crosses the Russian border, leaving the Soviet Union
summary_en: On 15 Av 5706 the author and his family crossed the border out of Russia — 'the homeland and cradle of Chabad' — beginning a year-and-a-half journey westward that would end in America.
story_body: After the war an organised effort smuggled Lubavitcher chassidim out of the Soviet Union via Poland. The author crossed the border on 15 Av 5706 and reached America on 18 Adar Sheni 5708. He contrasts the eighteen-month exodus with the twelve-hour Moscow-to-New-York flights available to Soviet Jews leaving in 5752.

title_en: Author and family arrive in Paris under the Joint and the Lubavitch Refugee Bureau
summary_en: Just before Shavuos 5707 the author and his family arrived in Paris, where the Joint and the Frierdiker Rebbe's Refugee Bureau (headed by R' B. Gorodetzky with R' Rafael Wilshansky as secretary) took charge of their care.
story_body: After temporary housing at the Hotel La Chapelle, the family was moved to a sub-divided room in a former noble château in Sèvres, where more than ten refugee families lived together. During his stay in Paris the author received hagahah and kabbalah for shechting poultry, having begun sharpening knives back in Pocking, and shechted in the Pletzl market alongside R' Betzalel Wilshansky.

title_en: Author arrives in the United States aboard the SS Sobieski
summary_en: On 18 Adar Sheni 5708 the author's family disembarked from the Polish liner SS Sobieski in New York, completing a year-and-a-half journey from the Soviet Union.
story_body: Knowing he would be at sea for Purim, the author bought a kosher Megillas Esther in Paris and read it aboard the ship. The American visa that brought him over came not from Tomchei Tmimim but from Telz Yeshiva of Cleveland — one of the six 'professor' visas allotted to Telz was redirected to the 'Lubavitcher,' thanks to the intervention of Freidel Stein (née Sacks), niece of his wife and wife of Telz mashgiach R' Chaim Stein.

title_en: Author's first Shabbos at 770 Eastern Parkway
summary_en: On his first Shabbos in New York the author walked over an hour from East New York to 770 Eastern Parkway, where he was admitted to the Frierdiker Rebbe's upstairs cabinet for kri'as haTorah.
story_body: The sefer Torah was carried up from the ground-floor shul to the Rebbe's second-floor study, where the leining took place on his writing desk before a tiny minyan. As a newly-arrived refugee the author was let in, wearing a heavy hand-spun woollen tallis from Russia that looked like a winter blanket. The gabbai R' Yochanan Gordon later told him the Rebbe could not stop looking at the tallis throughout the reading; the author kept it as a memento of 'what anash wore in the land of Egypt.'

title_en: Author studies Tanach and dikduk with R' Itshe Matlies in Zlobin
summary_en: Through the winter of 5688 in Zlobin, the author studied Tanach and Hebrew grammar with the veteran melamed R' Itshe Matlies (Riskin) by night to train as a precise baal koreh.
story_body: By day he learned Gemara with Rabbi Benyaminson, and in the evenings R' Itshe taught him Yirmiyahu and dikduk. Toward the end of the term R' Itshe drilled him word-by-word through the opening chapters of Shemos, demanding on which letter the trop fell and why. Half a century later the author still retained the rules of mileil and milra he had learned then.

title_en: Romen Tomchei Tmimim shut down just as the author arrives
summary_en: In the summer of 5688 the author travelled to Romen to learn in Tomchei Tmimim, only to discover on arrival that the underground yeshiva had just been broken up by Soviet pressure.
story_body: The Yevsektsiya was systematically destroying the remaining small yeshivos by arresting or hounding the magidei shiur, since the young bochurim themselves could not be jailed. Romen, a major chassidic centre, still hosted a functioning Tomchei Tmimim, so the author travelled there with Rabbi Benyaminson, who was also exploring a rabbinic post in the town. They arrived to find the yeshiva already dispersed, and the author returned to Zlobin to continue learning with Rabbi Benyaminson through the summer.

title_en: Stalin deports tens of thousands of Polish Jews to Siberia
summary_en: After the Soviet army occupied eastern Poland in 1939, Stalin seized thousands of Polish Jews and deported them to forced-labour camps in Siberia.
story_body: Many of the deportees perished from hunger, illness and cold. Two years later, when Hitler turned on the USSR, Stalin made peace with the Polish government-in-exile and released the surviving Polish citizens — who poured southward into the warm Central Asian republics, including Samarkand, where they would later collide with Lubavitcher refugees at clandestine Yom Kippur minyanim.

title_en: Chofetz Chaim's yeshiva relocates to Shumyachi during the revolution
summary_en: Between 1917 and 1920, as Jews from Latvia, Lithuania and Poland were resettled into Belarus and Ukraine, the Chofetz Chaim and his yeshiva ended up in Shumyachi, where the author's future father-in-law R' Zusman Fradkin became close to him.
story_body: The upheavals of the Russian Revolution displaced great Torah institutions along with their host communities. R' Zusman Fradkin, the Shumyachi shochet and acting rav, drew close to the Chofetz Chaim during this period and received from him, even though R' Zusman himself had learned in Slobodka and was a Chabad chassid by inclination.
