title_en: Author travels alone from Lipovets to study at the Kiev cheder katan
summary_en: After Pesach 5687 the 14-year-old author traveled by wagon and train from Lipovets to Kiev to learn in the underground cheder katan run by R' Yaakov der Beker under R' Benyamin Gorodetzky.
story_body: Reaching the Podol address of R' Shlomo Telingator (already departed for Eretz Yisrael), he was guided to Morgenstern's yeshiva, which refused him as underage at 14. He was instead accepted into the small Lubavitch yeshiva ketana effectively run by R' Yaakov der Beker, with Rabbi Benyamin Gorodetzky overseeing it from the Chabad shul on Shchekavitskaya St. R' Yaakov Konotoper served as his maggid shiur, teaching Perek HaMafkid.

title_en: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn freed from Soviet imprisonment
summary_en: Following the Frierdiker Rebbe's release on 12 Tammuz 5687, R' Benyamin Gorodetzky began showing his portrait at the Chabad shul in Kiev and urging Jews to behold it.
story_body: The author, then learning at the Kiev cheder katan, observed Rabbi Gorodetzky displaying a photograph of the Rebbe Rayatz to local balebatim and telling them it was a mitzvah to gaze upon him. He did not yet grasp the full significance, but the timing — soon after Yud-Beis Tammuz — places it just after the Rebbe's release from Soviet prison. The episode marks his earliest known exposure to the Frierdiker Rebbe.

title_en: Underground learning in Kiev's upper shiur during winter 5688
summary_en: In winter 5688 the author was promoted to the higher class at the Kiev cheder katan and the shiur began meeting clandestinely in shuls and private homes.
story_body: Fear of arrest forced the small class to learn in hiding, sometimes in a large shul where the bitter cold made the boys' toes burn, and other times crammed onto a bed in the tiny room of R' Zalman Levin of Kursk. From then on R' Zalman Levin reviewed the shiur with the author, materially strengthening his Gemara study. The author writes that this period brought him to feel the meaning of 'Torah is upheld only by one who kills himself for it,' and that it eventually opened the door to Tomchei Temimim in Vitebsk.

title_en: First 19 Kislev farbrengen at the Kiev yeshiva ketana
summary_en: Young students in Kiev held their first 19 Kislev farbrengen at the urging of R' Binyamin Gorodetzky.
story_body: R' Binyamin Gorodetzky asked the author to collect money from the boys of the underground yeshiva ketana in Kiev to organize a 19 Kislev gathering. The resulting farbrengen was the author's first participation in a Chag HaGeulah celebration, held quietly as Soviet surveillance of the yeshiva was beginning to tighten and synagogues were being closed across Russia.

title_en: Author arrives at Tomchei Tmimim Vitebsk on Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5688
summary_en: After Pesach 5688 the author traveled without authorization from Kiev to Vitebsk to join the underground Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
story_body: Together with Avrahmaleh Kvash and Dovid Green of Kaminetz, the author defied warnings and boarded a train to Vitebsk, the major rail hub serving the Tomchei Tmimim network in Polotsk and Nevel. He arrived on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Iyar and was hosted at the home of R' Berel Yaffe, where he saw for the first time large numbers of religious boys with payos and Lubavitcher tzitzis, writing home that he had reached 'Eretz Yisrael'.

title_en: R' Yitzchok Matmid leads Lag B'Omer 5688 farbrengen in Vitebsk
summary_en: R' Yitzchok Matmid interrupted the Vitebsk shiur on Lag B'Omer 5688 and farbrenged at the home of R' Chaim Shmuel of Lubavitch.
story_body: During his stay in Vitebsk's Kleiner Zeit, R' Yitzchok Matmid told R' Avraham Mayorer mid-shiur that the lesson must be shortened so a farbrengen could be held. The gathering took place at the home of R' Chaim Shmuel of Lubavitch, the shamash of the shul where the senior 'par zich' bochurim also took their meals.

title_en: R' Yehuda Eber tests Vitebsk Tomchei Tmimim students in Elul 5688
summary_en: In Elul 5688 R' Yehuda Eber examined the Vitebsk talmidim and grouped the youngest top boys into a new advanced shiur.
story_body: During Elul review the rosh yeshiva R' Yehuda Eber came to Vitebsk to test the bochurim, with R' Avraham Mayorer and the mashgiach deciding in advance how to combine them into examination groups. The author was tested alongside Avrahmaleh Kvash, Meir Zarchi, Yosef Sushtarvitz, and Shimon Shtilerman, the youngest and most capable bochurim, and the group was earmarked to form a new advanced class for the coming winter.

title_en: R' Yechezkel Himmelstein flees Polotsk to Vitebsk for Rosh Hashanah 5689
summary_en: After Soviet authorities closed the Polotsk mikveh, rosh metivta R' Yechezkel Himmelstein came to Vitebsk for Rosh Hashanah 5689.
story_body: The closure of the mikveh in Polotsk forced its rosh metivta R' Yechezkel Himmelstein to relocate to Vitebsk for the Yamim Noraim. He prayed together with the Tomchei Tmimim bochurim in the Zaranover shul, an early sign of how Soviet pressure was beginning to splinter the yeshiva network.

title_en: Soviet raid scatters Tomchei Tmimim central yeshiva in Nevel
summary_en: Mid-winter authorities came to arrest the Nevel yeshiva and kollel staff, scattering its classes across Leningrad, Vitebsk, and Yekaterinoslav.
story_body: Nevel had been the heart of the Tomchei Tmimim network in Russia, housing R' Nissan Nemenov, R' Zalman Kornitzer, R' Yehuda Eber's shiur, and R' Shmuel Levitin's kollel for rabbinical students. When the GPU came to arrest everyone, the entire institution dispersed: the middle and part of the youngest class went to Leningrad with R' Nissan Nemenov, the senior class transferred to Vitebsk, and R' Yehuda Eber's shiur passed through Vitebsk on its way to Yekaterinoslav.

title_en: Polotsk yeshiva shut down and R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman exiled to Poltava
summary_en: Shortly after Nevel, Soviet authorities raided Tomchei Tmimim in Polotsk and exiled R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman to Poltava.
story_body: Soon after the Nevel raid, the GPU moved against the Polotsk branch of Tomchei Tmimim, arresting its students and administrators. R' Shlomo Chaim Kesselman was singled out and exiled to Poltava, while the rest of the bochurim fled, most routing through Vitebsk because of its central rail position.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz reveals Simchat Torah 5691 directive to memorize 12 chapters of Tanya
summary_en: On Simchat Torah 5691 the Rebbe Rayatz in Riga disclosed a directive to memorize the first 12 chapters of Tanya including the Hakdama.
story_body: A letter from R' Yehuda Eber in Riga reached Vitebsk in the winter of 5691 reporting that on Simchat Torah the Rebbe Rayatz had revealed a 'secret': everyone must memorize the first 12 chapters of Tanya together with the introduction. The directive spread immediately through the underground network, and chassidim and bochurim across Russia began learning Tanya baal peh.

title_en: GPU closes Vitebsk Tomchei Tmimim before Purim 5691
summary_en: Before Purim 5691 the GPU raided the Vitebsk yeshiva, identifying students by their long thin Lubavitcher tzitzit and round yarmulkes.
story_body: Soviet agents entered the Kleiner Zeit shul where the bochurim were learning and arrested them along with two adult Jews present. A GPU investigator examined the prisoners' headcoverings and tzitzit: the older balei-batim whose flat yarmulkes and short, thick tzitzit looked different were released, while the boys with round yarmulkes and long thin tzitzit were identified as Lubavitchers. They were released that night but the yeshiva had effectively been broken.

title_en: Arrest of R' Eliyahu Far, shochet Tzvi Zarchi, and Vitebsk Zal bochurim
summary_en: Around the closure of the Vitebsk yeshiva, the GPU arrested the senior Zal bochurim and chassidim R' Eliyahu Far and shochet Tzvi Zarchi.
story_body: In Zarutchei the GPU arrested the older bochurim of the Zal, including Michael Teitelbaum, Herzl Minkowitz, and Avraham Aharon Chen. Soon after, they took the chassid R' Eliyahu Far and the shochet R' Tzvi Zarchi, father of Meir Zarchi. Most of the remaining rabbis and prominent chassidim fled, leaving only the suspected collaborator Goldberg as the Russian rav.

title_en: GPU misreads coded letter on Vitebsk visa list for 15 bochurim
summary_en: A coded letter from R' Yehuda Eber requesting Riga visas for 15 bochurim was deciphered by the GPU after an elderly chassid explained the abbreviation.
story_body: Shortly before Purim 5691 the Vitebsk hanhala received word from R' Yehuda Eber that visas were being arranged in Riga for 15 bochurim, with the message written in tiny letters as '15 ס.' to disguise the request. The hanhala understood that 'ס' stood for 'simanim' meaning bochurim, but when the GPU showed the letter to imprisoned balei-batim and an elderly chassid foolishly explained the code, the gentile investigator triumphantly identified the plot. The chassidim involved were held in prison for a long time.

title_en: Vitebsk chassidic prisoners fast nine days through Pesach 5691
summary_en: The arrested Vitebsk chassidim, including R' Eliyahu Far's daughter, fasted nine days through Pesach 5691 rather than eat chametz.
story_body: All the imprisoned Vitebsk chassidim, including the daughter of R' Eliyahu Far who later became the wife of R' Michael Lipsker, refused to eat chametz in their cells during Pesach. For nine days they subsisted on a single piece of sugar daily rather than violate the holiday, even as the rest of the Vitebsk yeshiva infrastructure collapsed around them.

title_en: 12 Tammuz 5691 farbrengen with R' Binyamin of Minsk in Kiev's Dimievka
summary_en: After fleeing Vitebsk, the author attended a warm 12 Tammuz farbrengen led by R' Binyamin of Minsk at the Kiev Tomchei Tmimim in Dimievka.
story_body: Following the breakup of the Vitebsk yeshiva, the author and his chavrusa R' Michael Rapoport regrouped in Kiev for Shabbat 12 Tammuz before continuing on to Baku. The senior bochur R' Binyamin of Minsk, the mashpia of the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Dimievka, led a warm farbrengen with the bochurim, providing a moment of spiritual encouragement amid the ongoing Soviet repression.

title_en: Chabad students arrive in Kutaisi to establish underground yeshiva
summary_en: A group of Chabad yeshiva students reaches Kutaisi, Georgia just before Erev Tishah B'Av after a difficult journey from Kiev via Baku.
story_body: After traveling from Kiev to Baku and finding it unsuitable for study, the students continued to Kutaisi. They arrived shortly before Erev Tishah B'Av and were warmly welcomed by local Georgian Chabad chassidim, many of whom had previously studied at Tomchei Tmimim in Vitebsk, Nevel, or Lubavitch. The community helped fund their settlement so a yeshiva could be re-established in the city.

title_en: Author and Mikhal Rapoport arrested at Gori, Stalin's birthplace
summary_en: While riding the train past Gori, Stalin's birthplace, the author and Mikhal Rapoport were detained by the GPU and briefly jailed.
story_body: Although they had safely passed major cities like Rostov, Baku, and Tbilisi, the GPU seized them in the small town of Gori because the local secret police were unusually aggressive in Stalin's hometown. They were locked up with a violent Georgian prisoner and demanded their tefillin from the guards in the morning. They were eventually released in Tbilisi after intervention.

title_en: Underground Rosh Hashanah minyan in Kutaisi for 5692
summary_en: Anash and tmimim gathered in R. Yosef's home in Kutaisi for a Rosh Hashanah minyan praying with the devotion of pre-revolutionary Vitebsk.
story_body: On Rosh Hashanah 5692 the students held a private minyan in the home of R. Yosef, brother of Chacham Yitzchak who had studied in Lubavitch. R. Eli Chaim the shochet led prayers with tears and dveikut. On motzaei Rosh Hashanah the maamar 'Hashem yechatu merivav' from 5689 was reviewed.

title_en: R. Zalman Levitin arrives in Kutaisi to head the underground yeshiva
summary_en: Mid-winter R. Zalman Levitin (the Haditcher) reached Kutaisi and reorganized the underground yeshiva with strong leadership.
story_body: In mid-winter R. Zalman 'the Haditcher' Levitin joined the Kutaisi group and began guiding them in chassidus, teaching Shoresh Mitzvas HaTefillah, Haamanas Elokus, and chapters of Derech Mitzvosecha before moving them on to Hemshech 5659 with required memorization. He raised funds and ran the yeshiva with a firm hand, drawing additional bochurim including Moshe Rexin, Ze'ev Zalmanov, and Avraham Kievman.

title_en: 12 Tammuz 5692 farbrengen at the Liebov family home in Kutaisi
summary_en: The growing Kutaisi Chabad community marked the chag hageulah of 12 Tammuz 5692 with a farbrengen at the home of R. Yisrael Liebov's father.
story_body: By summer 5692 the Liebov family and additional Anash households had moved to Kutaisi, turning the city into a small Chabad settlement. The chag hageulah of 12 Tammuz was celebrated in the home of R. Yisrael Liebov's parents, a gathering that knit together the underground yeshiva students and the established families.

title_en: Shabbat Teshuvah 5693 spent stranded at Rioni train station
summary_en: Sent to Baku by R. Zalman Levitin, the author and Shlomo Matusov returned late and were forced to spend Shabbat Teshuvah 5693 at the Rioni station.
story_body: Rumors of an imminent crackdown caused the mashpia to send the author and Shlomo Matusov to Baku, but they could not stay there. Returning on a delayed train they arrived at the Rioni junction just before sunset on erev Shabbat Teshuvah and could not travel the last quarter-hour leg to Kutaisi. They guarded their belongings, davened, and made kiddush on borrowed bread at the station until motzaei Shabbat.

title_en: Simchat Torah 5693 farbrengen at the Liebov home in Kutaisi
summary_en: The Kutaisi underground community held the Simchat Torah 5693 farbrengen at the Liebov home and prayed all Shabbatot at Bas-Sheva Lipsker's home.
story_body: On Simchat Torah 5693 a farbrengen was held in the Liebov family home, and the weekly Shabbat minyan and learning were hosted by Rebbetzin Bas-Sheva Lipsker, mother of the Lipsker family. The hidden community continued to function despite the rising danger and persistent fears of arrest.

title_en: Three students dispatched from Kutaisi to Kulashi for 19 Kislev 5693
summary_en: Fearing arrests in Kutaisi, R. Zalman Levitin sent the author, Yitzchak Hakohen Shtetin, and Avraham Kievman to Kulashi around 19 Kislev 5693.
story_body: As the GPU crackdown intensified, the Haditcher dispersed students to lower-profile locations. The three were warmly received in Kulashi and learned in a tiny shul lit by a single kerosene lamp. Avraham Kievman was an extreme masmid who balanced his oil lamp by the clock so he could rise at 5 a.m. and continue until past midnight.

title_en: Kulashi students arrested by drunk Communist officials at night
summary_en: A drunk Georgian Communist council head, a GPU agent, and other officials spotted lamplight in the Kulashi shul and arrested the three sleeping bochurim.
story_body: Walking home after a drinking party in Shevat 5693, the local officials noticed the elevated lamp glowing in the closed shul and burst in to arrest the students. They were held overnight in freezing police cells where local women came in the morning to weep at seeing them through the cracks, then transferred to the district prison in Samtredia where the warden slapped the tall author across the face on arrival.

title_en: Author's father Ephraim Shmuel passes away on 15 Shevat 5693
summary_en: While back in Kutaisi after his escape from Samtredia prison, the author received a telegram that his father Ephraim Shmuel had died on 15 Shevat 5693.
story_body: After being put on a transport to Ukraine, the author escaped at Sharafan station by hiding inside an iron staircase and Georgian Jews smuggled him back to Sachkhere. Back in Kutaisi a telegram arrived informing him that his father Ephraim Shmuel had passed away on 15 Shevat, and he sat shiva in the Kutaisi shul.

title_en: Mass arrest of Anash and yeshiva students on Erev Pesach 5693 in Kutaisi
summary_en: On Erev Pesach 5693 many Kutaisi Anash and yeshiva students were arrested, including the mashpia R. Zalman 'Haditcher' Levitin.
story_body: The Soviet authorities swept through Kutaisi just before Pesach 5693, seizing many chassidim and bochurim along with the yeshiva's mashpia, director, and mentor R. Zalman Levitin. The older bochurim were already imprisoned by the NKVD in Batumi. Any students who remained free had no choice but to flee.

title_en: Author smuggles shemurah flour by train from Georgia to Kiev
summary_en: Fleeing the Pesach 5693 arrests, the author traveled by rail to Kiev carrying shemurah flour from harvest-time despite repeated NKVD inspections.
story_body: He boarded the train carrying flour that was shemurah from the time of cutting, a stricter standard than what was available in Kiev. The flour bundle was searched multiple times during the multi-day journey but he reached Kiev safely. The matzot baked from his flour were divided among all ten bochurim of the Kiev yeshiva for the sedarim.

title_en: Holodomor famine grips Ukraine while Kiev yeshiva learns 5693
summary_en: A devastating Stalin-imposed famine struck Ukraine in 5693 even as the harvest was strong, forcing yeshiva students to scheme to get bread.
story_body: Although 5693 was a year of abundant harvest, Stalin's decrees caused mass starvation in Ukraine. Yeshiva students stood in bread lines for days, taking multiple places in the queue to feed the chevra. The young Jewish father-and-son bakers serving bread quietly risked their own safety by repeatedly handing out loaves to the bearded bochurim.

title_en: Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5693 farbrengen at R. Zalman Moshe in Ilyinka
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5693 the author traveled from Moscow to Ilyinka with R. Dovber Gurevitch to farbreng at R. Zalman Moshe Yitzchaki's home.
story_body: Having arrived in Moscow at the end of Sivan to raise funds for the Kiev yeshiva, the author joined R. Dovber Gurevitch on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz for a major farbrengen in Ilyinka. R. Yaakov Gurkov of Kharkov attended as well. R. Zalman Moshe explained that the simcha of preparation for 12 Tammuz must begin already on Rosh Chodesh.

title_en: 12 Tammuz 5693 farbrengen in Malachovka with new maamar from Rayatz
summary_en: Anash gathered in Malachovka for 12 Tammuz 5693 received the maamar 'Nasata Lirei'echa Nes Lehisnoses' from the Frierdiker Rebbe.
story_body: An exceptional farbrengen brought together R. Zalman Moshe Yitzchaki, R. Shmuel Levitin, R. Shmuel Aba Dolitzky, and many younger Anash. The newly arrived maamar 'Nasata Lirei'echa Nes Lehisnoses' from the Frierdiker Rebbe was studied at length and Anash drank substantial mashke in celebration.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe plans to relocate from Riga to Warsaw, 12 Tammuz 5693
summary_en: A letter from R. Yehuda Eber read at the Malachovka 12 Tammuz 5693 farbrengen announced the Frierdiker Rebbe's intent to move from Riga to Warsaw.
story_body: R. Shmuel Levitin read aloud a letter from R. Yehuda Eber reporting that the Frierdiker Rebbe planned to relocate his residence from Riga to Warsaw and required $1,500 for the move. The Rebbe requested that the relocation expenses be covered by the Moscow-area Anash, which they apparently quietly fulfilled.

title_en: R. Mordechai Leizer Lapatovsky visits Kiev yeshiva for Sukkot 5694
summary_en: During Tishrei 5694, especially Sukkot, R. Mordechai Leizer Lapatovsky came from nearby Zhitomir to farbreng with the Kiev yeshiva students.
story_body: R. Mordechai Leizer Lapatovsky, brother-in-law of R. Yona Cohen and R. Eli Chaim Roitblat, traveled from Zhitomir to Kiev to spend Sukkot with the underground yeshiva. He farbrenged with the bochurim in a spirit of mesirus nefesh and shared eyewitness stories of avodah from Lubavitch.

title_en: Kiev yeshiva students arrested by NKVD agents after Simchat Torah 5694
summary_en: After Simchat Torah and Shabbat Bereishit 5694, two disguised NKVD agents entered the Kiev yeshiva's ezras nashim and arrested the bochurim.
story_body: Two clean-shaven, fashionably dressed agents quietly entered the upstairs ezras nashim where the yeshiva learned, tested the two youngest bochurim on their gemara, then announced they were under arrest with police already at the door. The author escaped through the women's gallery windows while others were taken to NKVD headquarters; a sympathetic Jewish interrogator later returned most papers but denied them Kiev passports and warned them to flee.

title_en: Avraham Padabranker studied at the Lithuanian yeshiva in Kiev
summary_en: Avraham Padabranker learned at the Lithuanian yeshiva in Kiev led by Rabbi Morgenstern under Rabbi Mattasov of Podol.
story_body: In 5687 (1926/27), Avraham Padabranker studied in Kiev at the Litvish yeshiva. The Rosh Mesivta was Rabbi Morgenstern, who served under the leadership of Rabbi Mattasov, the chief rabbi of Podol. Years later he was encountered in Chernigov, having held onto some connection to Yiddishkeit unlike many of his peers who broke under Soviet pressure.

title_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin began service in Tomchei Tmimim Vitebsk
summary_en: After Pesach 5688, Yisrael Yehuda Levin began his work in the underground Tomchei Tmimim in Vitebsk together with the bachur Avraham Kvashe.
story_body: After Pesach in 5688 (spring 1928), Yisrael Yehuda Levin began serving in the clandestine Tomchei Tmimim network in Vitebsk alongside the bachur Avraham Kvashe (later in Riga). He worked there for the entire stretch of that period before later moving on to similar work in Kiev. This was during the era of intense Soviet persecution of religious education.

title_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin in Pereyaslav after fleeing Vitebsk
summary_en: After fleeing Vitebsk, Yisrael Yehuda Levin spent time in Pereyaslav and befriended the town rabbi, Yehoshua Zelig Diskin.
story_body: In 5691 (1931), after escaping from Vitebsk, the author settled for a time in Pereyaslav. There he became close with the rav demata, Rabbi Yehoshua Zelig Diskin, a great scholar of noble character, with whom he later corresponded. Rabbi Diskin wrote on his behalf to Chief Rabbi Avraham Yitzchok Kook in Eretz Yisrael, helping to set in motion paperwork for emigration to the Holy Land.

title_en: Extraordinary 19 Kislev farbrengen in Malachovka
summary_en: A remarkable Chag HaGeulah farbrengen was held in Malachovka outside Moscow, attended by many senior Chassidim hiding from Soviet authorities.
story_body: On 19 Kislev 5694 (December 7, 1933), an extraordinary farbrengen took place in the Malachovka shul. Many anash and elder Chassidim gathered there because the area was quiet in winter — Moscow officials had returned to the city and vacated their dachas. The farbrengen lasted several nights; at one point Rabbi Shmuel Levitin stood on the table with his long peyot loose over his face and sang 'Az der Rebbe iz do, iz doch hoderes vehaemunah uday do' — a moment that pierced the author's heart given his personal and the broader circumstances.

title_en: Purim farbrengen at Reb Elchanan Morozov in Leningrad
summary_en: Chassidim farbrenged at Reb Elchanan Morozov's home in Leningrad on Purim 5694, then continued at Reb Shmuel Nemotin's home.
story_body: On Purim 5694 (around March 1, 1934), Chassidim farbrenged at the home of Rabbi Elchanan Morozov in Leningrad. They later continued at the home of Rabbi Shmuel Nemotin, where a large farbrengen was held with long tables — Rabbi Chaikel Chaikin had just become engaged to his daughter. Rabbi Peretz Mochkin spoke, with prominent participants including Rabbi Baruch Shifrin, Rabbi Menashe Althaus, and Rabbi Michael Dvorkin (who was preparing to emigrate to Riga).

title_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin returned from Leningrad to Moscow for Pesach
summary_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin returned from Leningrad to Moscow on Erev Pesach 5694 after about a month with Chassidim in Leningrad.
story_body: On Erev Pesach 5694 (March 30, 1934), the author returned from Leningrad to Moscow and back to Malachovka. He had spent roughly a month in Leningrad, lodging with Rabbi Yitzchok Raskin and attending farbrengens and Shabbos seudos at the home of Rabbi Elchanan Morozov. Hosting unregistered Chassidim in Leningrad was literal mesirat nefesh given Soviet surveillance.

title_en: 13 Nissan farbrengen at Reb Zalman Moshe's home in Moscow
summary_en: On the yahrtzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek, a small farbrengen took place late at night at Reb Zalman Moshe's home in Moscow.
story_body: On the night of 13 Nissan 5694 (March 29, 1934), the yahrtzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek, the author overcame his exhaustion and went late at night to Reb Zalman Moshe's home. Soon afterwards, Rabbi Berel (Garfinkel) Kornitzer — the pride of the Rostov tmimim — arrived on a mission from Rabbi Zalman Schneersohn regarding communal finances, followed by Reb Yaakov Maskalik (Yaakov Zhuravitzer) who had come specifically to farbreng. The three sat down to farbreng and the author listened from the side.

title_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin wrote to Rebbe Rayatz requesting blessing for exit visa
summary_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin wrote to the Frierdiker Rebbe in Riga requesting a blessing as he applied for an exit permit from Soviet Russia.
story_body: On Erev Shabbat Parshat Shemini, 28 Nissan 5694 (April 13, 1934), Yisrael Yehuda ben Ephraim Shmuel Levin wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz from Moscow. He asked for arousal of mercy from on high so that the Soviet officials granting exit permits would look favorably on his case and issue him travel documents. The letter was preserved in the archive of the Rebbe Rayatz's correspondence at the library of Agudas Chasidei Chabad.

title_en: Passing of R. Ephraim Shmuel Levin
summary_en: R. Ephraim Shmuel Levin, father of the chassid Yisrael Yehuda Levin, passed away on 15 Shevat 5693.
story_body: On 15 Shevat 5693 R. Ephraim Shmuel Levin passed away, leaving his wife Leah Beila a widow with three daughters and two sons. The author's brother Yosef and sister Sara Yehudit were studying in Kharkov to become a doctor and nurse, while the family pressed the author to abandon yeshiva study and find work. This bereavement and family pressure would later push the author to write to the Rebbe Rayatz for guidance and support.

title_en: Underground Malakhovka farbrengen reorganizes bochurim's nigleh learning
summary_en: A summer 5694 farbrengen in Malakhovka assigned R. Refael Cohen of Nevel to teach nigleh to the bochurim.
story_body: In the summer of 5694 (1934) a chassidic farbrengen was held in the Malakhovka shul where it was decided that R. Refael Cohen of Nevel would begin teaching the bochurim nigleh. R. Pinchas Schreiber (Pinye Rakshiker) regularly taught them Hemshech 5666, while R. Elchonon Morozov occasionally taught a maamar. The group included future Lubavitcher figures like R. Shlomo Matusof, R. Meir Zarchi, R. Michoel Teitelbaum and R. Mendel Morozov, who later joined from Malakhovka.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz sends Torgsin dollars to Levin family in USSR
summary_en: In summer 5694 Rebbe Rayatz sent seven dollars in Torgsin coupons to support Yisrael Yehuda Levin and his widowed mother.
story_body: Hiding in a corner of the Marina Roshcha shul yard, the author wrote a desperate letter to the Rebbe Rayatz describing his hunger, persecution, and his family's pressure to abandon yeshiva study. To his surprise he received a reply enclosing three dollars for himself and four for his mother, with a blessing that Hashem strengthen his siblings' resolve. The dollars arrived as Torgsin coupons—redeemable in the Soviet hard-currency stores—allowing him to buy rice, oranges and other unobtainable goods to send home.

title_en: 12 Tammuz farbrengen in Malakhovka marks year since author's arrival
summary_en: On 12 Tammuz 5694 the author returned from Moscow to Malakhovka for a farbrengen marking a year since first arriving there.
story_body: On 12 Tammuz 5694 (June 25, 1934)—the anniversary of the Rebbe Rayatz's liberation from Soviet imprisonment—the author returned from Moscow to Malakhovka, completing a full year since first arriving in summer 5693. A farbrengen was held in the Malakhovka shul. He resumed sleeping and learning there, joined by a growing number of Anash families and bochurim fleeing intensifying decrees throughout the country.

title_en: Anash expand prayer arrangements in Malakhovka for Tishrei 5695
summary_en: For Tishrei 5695 the Malakhovka Anash community rented a separate prayer hall to handle the growing crowd of chassidim and bochurim.
story_body: By Tishrei 5695 (Fall 1934) the influx of Anash families and yeshiva bochurim to Malakhovka had grown so large that a separate prayer hall had to be rented for the High Holidays. The main shul served the general religious public while the new venue hosted only Anash and yeshiva bochurim, recreating the prayer atmosphere of pre-revolution Lubavitch. Sukkos and Simchas Torah were celebrated with extraordinary farbrengens.

title_en: Mashpi'im assigned Chassidus shiurim with Malakhovka bochurim after Simchas Torah
summary_en: After Simchas Torah 5695 the Malakhovka Anash organized that each mashpia would teach Chassidus to several bochurim.
story_body: Following the Simchas Torah 5695 farbrengens (October 1934), a planning meeting of Anash activists assigned each mashpia to learn Chassidus with a small group of bochurim. The author and R. Shlomo Matusof were assigned to study with R. Nissan Nemenov, who traveled almost daily from Ilinka to teach them Hemshech 5664. Bochurim were also boarded with Anash families—the author lodged with R. Zalman Alpert (Zalman Kornitzer).

title_en: Leah Beila Levin writes Rebbe Rayatz after being injured in food line
summary_en: On Tuesday of Parshas Yisro 5695 the author's mother Leah Beila wrote the Rebbe Rayatz describing her injury when a non-Jew pushed her in a food queue.
story_body: On Tuesday of Parshas Yisro 5695 (around January 22, 1935), Leah Beila Levin—widow of R. Ephraim Shmuel and mother of the author—wrote a letter to the Rebbe Rayatz, now preserved in the archives. She described being shoved by a non-Jew while waiting on a sidewalk in a Soviet food queue, falling and gashing her head open and requiring stitches. She wrote of her hope for redemption and ascribed her survival to the merit of her orphaned children.

title_en: Purim 5695 farbrengen at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home
summary_en: On Purim 5695 R. Elchonon Morozov led a farbrengen at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home with R. Yonah Cohen.
story_body: The Purim 5695 farbrengen at R. Zalman Kornitzer's home was led by R. Elchonon Morozov and joined by R. Yonah Cohen, a fervent singer who drank heavily and led niggunim while R. Elchonon spoke. R. Elchonon expounded that the Rebbe Rayatz is 'Avinu Malkenu'—just as the Alter Rebbe was Atzmus, so too the present Rebbe—and that, unlike the Alter Rebbe's chassidim, the Rayatz's chassidim include those who never saw him yet bind themselves to him with mesirus nefesh. The drasha left a deep impression on the bochurim present.

title_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin arrested at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home
summary_en: The author and Avraham Kievman were arrested at R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home for residing within 100 km of Moscow without registration.
story_body: Soon after Purim 5695, Soviet detectives raided R. Zalman Kornitzer's Malakhovka home in the night and arrested the author and Avraham Kievman, who were sleeping there unregistered within the forbidden 100-kilometer Moscow zone. They were jailed in Lyubertsy in a cell with thieves and murderers; the criminals plucked hairs from Kievman's red beard, breaking his spirit. After several days they were released on signing a pledge that a second offense would mean two years of exile.

title_en: Second arrest at Malakhovka shul with Shimshon Charitonov
summary_en: After Pesach 5695, NKVD detectives raided the Malakhovka shul at night and arrested the author together with Shimshon Charitonov.
story_body: After Pesach 5695 the author resumed sleeping in the Malakhovka shul together with Shimshon Charitonov. In a midnight raid, detectives shone flashlights and burst through the door, taking both bochurim to the Lyubertsy police. At dawn the author quickly donned tefillin and prayed, then persuaded the police chief—through humor and a misfiled prior pledge—to release them. R. Yaakov Maskalik later comforted him by recounting the Tzemach Tzedek's blessing of 'mice' that ate incriminating court papers.

title_en: Yisrael Yehuda Levin mails photograph to Rebbe Rayatz from Moscow
summary_en: On Erev Shabbos Emor 7 Iyar 5695, the author photographed himself in Moscow and mailed his picture to the Rebbe Rayatz with a request for blessing.
story_body: Hearing while in prison that the Rebbe Rayatz had asked chassidim to send him their photographs, the author resolved to comply once freed. On Friday 7 Iyar 5695 (May 10, 1935) he entered a Moscow photo studio, urging them to finish before Shabbos, and just before sunset received the prints and mailed them at the post office. His accompanying letter asked the Rebbe to arouse mercy for 'Yisrael Yehuda ben Leah Beila' that he merit to see the Rebbe face to face, and listed R. Chaim Ezra Bronstein as his return address.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz replies to Yisrael Yehuda Levin's photograph
summary_en: On 16 Sivan 5695 Rebbe Rayatz replied to the author's photo letter, blessing him and sending regards to his friends and relatives.
story_body: On 16 Sivan 5695 (around June 18, 1935), the Rebbe Rayatz replied to the photograph and letter the author had sent the previous month. The Rebbe wrote that he had enjoyed seeing the photograph, asked the author to convey greetings to his friends and relatives, and blessed him with Hashem's help. In the darkness of those Soviet years, the letter and blessing gave the author considerable joy and encouragement.

title_en: Elul 5695 NKVD sweep of Malakhovka thwarted by R. Zalman Kornitzer
summary_en: In early Elul 5695 the NKVD came to round up Anash in Malakhovka; R. Zalman Kornitzer warned the targeted families and many escaped.
story_body: At the start of Elul 5695 (late August 1935), NKVD investigators came to R. Zalman Kornitzer (Alpert) demanding 'Zalman Kornitzer'—which he denied, giving his legal name Alpert. While held at the village council he overheard officers reading a list of Anash to arrest: Shmuel Leib Paritzer (R. Shmuel Levitin), Shlomo Chaim Palatzker (Kesselman), Avraham Mayarer (Dreizin) and others. After being released he raced to warn each family on the list, saving many from arrest; investigators had tricked two captured boys into naming Anash, mistaking nicknames for surnames. R. Yonah Cohen then took it upon himself with mesirus nefesh to care for the bochurim and Anash children, receiving the Rebbe's blessing to be strong in this work.

title_en: Israel Yehuda's military exemption via glasses ruse on 11 Tishrei
summary_en: Israel Yehuda received a full Red Army exemption at his Yegoryevsk induction by feigning poor eyesight on the advice of the Rebbe Rayatz.
story_body: Facing conscription that endangered observant Jews, Israel Yehuda wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz and consulted senior Tmimim including R' Nissan Nemanov and R' Yaakov Maskalik. After receiving the Rebbe's directive to wear glasses, he obtained reading glasses at the Semashko clinic and on 11 Tishrei 5696 deliberately misread the eye chart, securing a complete exemption rather than the conditional one given to two other Anash bochurim that day.

title_en: Tishrei 5696 holiday minyanim in Moscow under Soviet surveillance
summary_en: During Tishrei 5696, Anash held clandestine High Holiday and Sukkot minyanim in Moscow, including a Shmini Atzeret farbrengen held adjacent to Butyrka prison where many Chassidim were jailed.
story_body: On Hoshana Rabbah and Simchat Torah, Israel Yehuda traveled to the Marina Roshcha synagogue, where the sharp-minded R' Mendel Leib Yaakobson unexpectedly joined the hakafot. Fearing arrest, on Shmini Atzeret the group gathered at the home of a friendly Lithuanian Jew situated directly next to the Butyrka prison, holding a heartfelt farbrengen with R' Melech Kaplan while their imprisoned brethren sat just meters away.

title_en: Israel Yehuda relocates to Voronezh to study under R' Betzalel Wilshansky
summary_en: After Tishrei 5696, Israel Yehuda traveled to Voronezh at R' Yonah Cohen's direction to learn under the influence of R' Betzalel Wilshansky alongside other older bochurim.
story_body: R' Yonah Cohen sent the older bochurim approaching marriage age to receive guidance from R' Betzalel Wilshansky in Voronezh. Israel Yehuda joined Michoel Teitelbaum, Shaul Prafoisker (Steinbach), and Shalom Wilenkin there to learn, while also tutoring R' Betzalel's twelve-year-old son Folka (later R' Refoel Wilshansky).

title_en: Yezhovshchina terror disrupts underground yeshiva networks
summary_en: The Yezhovshchina purges of 5697 brought mass street arrests and Siberian exile, forcing Israel Yehuda to flee Voronezh temporarily.
story_body: During the height of Stalin's Great Terror in 5697, the NKVD arrested people directly off the streets and deported them to Siberia, creating a 'terrible fear' Israel Yehuda could no longer endure. He fled to Moscow before Purim to consult R' Yonah Cohen, returning to Voronezh only for Passover, where the group baked matzot with utmost stringency under R' Betzalel Wilshansky's supervision.

title_en: Israel Yehuda dispatched to teach underground yeshiva in Krivoy Rog
summary_en: R' Yonah Cohen sent Israel Yehuda to Krivoy Rog to instruct a group of young Anash boys in an underground yeshiva housed at R' Yoel Itkin's home.
story_body: Following a clandestine meeting at R' Zalman Pruss's home in Moscow, R' Yonah Cohen organized the dispatching of older bochurim to teach groups of four boys per location, reportedly on the Rebbe's instruction. Israel Yehuda took over from Michoel Teitelbaum in Krivoy Rog, teaching Perek Shnayim Ochzin to boys including Leibke Mochkin, Yoel Duchman, Mendel Raskin, and Yehoshua Katzenelenbogen-Raskin at R' Yoel Itkin's home, which served the cause with extraordinary mesirat nefesh.

title_en: Israel Yehuda visits R' Levi Yitzchak Schneerson in Dnepropetrovsk
summary_en: While fundraising for the Krivoy Rog yeshiva, Israel Yehuda visited Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson in nearby Dnepropetrovsk.
story_body: Traveling to Dnepropetrovsk to raise funds for the underground yeshiva, Israel Yehuda came to the home of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, the future Lubavitcher Rebbe's father. The Rebbetzin Chana directed him to the synagogue, where he found Rabbi Levi Yitzchak sitting and praying.

title_en: Rosh Hashanah and Sukkot 5698 minyan in Krivoy Rog
summary_en: For Tishrei 5698, R' Mikhoel Rapoport joined the Krivoy Rog group to establish a clandestine High Holiday minyan at R' Yoel Itkin's home.
story_body: Fearing exposure at the main synagogue where a chazzan from Kremenchug officiated, the group organized their own minyan at R' Yoel Itkin's home. On Simchat Torah they secretly observed the synagogue hakafot and saw the visiting young chazzan from Dnepropetrovsk dancing to Chabad niggunim, later learning he was among Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's students at the local technicum.

title_en: Israel Yehuda's engagement to Itta Devorah Gurkov of Kharkov
summary_en: In Shvat 5698, Israel Yehuda entered into tnaim with Itta Devorah, daughter of R' Meir Gurkov of Kharkov.
story_body: Despite warning his kallah that he could be arrested at any moment, Itta Devorah was undeterred since she too was prepared for arrest because of her commitment to Yiddishkeit and Chabad. The match represented a partnership ready to bear the cost of religious life under Soviet persecution.

title_en: Wedding of Israel Yehuda and Itta Devorah Gurkov on 5 Nissan
summary_en: Israel Yehuda married Itta Devorah Gurkov on 5 Nissan 5698 in Kharkov.
story_body: The wedding took place under the shadow of constant NKVD danger. Around the same time, R' Yonah HaKohen of Poltava sent flour for shemurah matzah for the entire Passover holiday from Hadiach, and a particularly fine talit gadol made by the righteous converts of Voronezh as a wedding gift, which Israel Yehuda treasured and used for decades.

title_en: Berdichev underground yeshiva raided, 12 students and Rosh Yeshiva arrested
summary_en: The NKVD arrested 12 students of the Berdichev underground yeshiva along with their Rosh Yeshiva R' Moshe Korolevitzer (Rubinson).
story_body: Following the Berdichev arrests, the remaining students in Krivoy Rog fled to Kutaisi in Georgia. Around the same time the Kursk yeshiva was also shut down and its students dispersed; several young learners including R' Zalman Levin and R' Dovber Kiubman made their way to Kharkov, where Israel Yehuda and Michoel Teitelbaum sheltered and taught them.

title_en: NKVD arrests R' Meir Gurkov in Kharkov on Shushan Purim
summary_en: On Shushan Purim 5699 the NKVD searched R' Meir Gurkov's home and arrested him along with three other Anash, following the arrival of informer David Itze in Kharkov.
story_body: After the informer David Itze appeared in Kharkov and lodged with R' Meir Gurkov, the family realized danger and Gurkov briefly hid at his son-in-law Israel Yehuda's apartment on the city's outskirts. On Shushan Purim 5699 the NKVD raided Gurkov's home, arresting him and three other Anash members under harsh conditions and interrogating their sons; the fear was so severe that family members could not look one another in the eye.

title_en: Birth of Ephraim Shmuel son of Israel Yehuda on Tisha B'Av
summary_en: Israel Yehuda's son Ephraim Shmuel was born on 9 Av 5699 in Kharkov and was given a brit milah with a minyan of ten men.
story_body: The boy was named for Israel Yehuda's father. Despite the danger of gathering openly, a minyan was assembled for the brit. R' Betzalel Wilshansky later fled Voronezh and joined the family in Kharkov around this period.

title_en: German invasion of the Soviet Union begins Operation Barbarossa
summary_en: On 22 June 1941 Germany invaded the USSR, prompting Israel Yehuda and Michoel Teitelbaum to seek papers to flee Kharkov, though others delayed evacuation.
story_body: When the war began, Israel Yehuda and Michoel Teitelbaum urged immediate efforts to obtain documents and leave Kharkov, but they were not heeded. As the front approached and German bombardments intensified, the families ultimately chose to wait through the High Holidays and Shabbat Bereishit before departing.

title_en: Israel Yehuda's family flees Kharkov amid German bombing after Shabbat Bereishit
summary_en: After Shabbat Bereishit 5702 Israel Yehuda fled Kharkov by freight train with his family, Michoel Teitelbaum, and the elder R' Avraham Katzenelson as the Germans bombed the city.
story_body: The night before departure a massive German bombardment partially destroyed their building; the families wrote a pidyon nefesh to the Rebbe during the raid. With the main Kharkov station destroyed and only the freight terminal operating, Israel Yehuda was nearly stranded with his belongings until two passing gentile laborers agreed to carry his bundles down the hill for thirty rubles. The train was bombed en route, but the group survived by remaining inside rather than running into the open.

title_en: Israel Yehuda's family arrives in Kzyl-Orda en route to Samarkand
summary_en: On Shabbat Mevarchim Kislev 5702, Israel Yehuda's family reached Kzyl-Orda in Kazakhstan during the wartime evacuation toward Samarkand.
story_body: The journey took the family first to Saratov, where they sheltered with the distinguished R' Yaakov Yitzchak Karasik, who advised them that the evacuation already amounted to leaving the country since everyone was heading to Samarkand. Boarding another train, they reached Kzyl-Orda for Shabbat Mevarchim Kislev, finding bitter cold nights, hot days, and severe hunger.

title_en: Israel Yehuda Leib Levin's family arrives in Samarkand
summary_en: Israel Yehuda Leib Levin and his family arrived in Samarkand in Kislev 5702 amid wartime overcrowding, disease, and famine.
story_body: After fleeing wartime Russia, the Levin family reached Samarkand in Kislev 5702 (late 1941). They found the city packed with newly released Polish deportees, swept by disease and starvation, with people collapsing dead in the streets daily. There was no place to settle and medicines were nearly impossible to obtain.

title_en: Death of Levin's son Ephraim Shmuel in Samarkand hospital
summary_en: Ephraim Shmuel, two-and-a-quarter-year-old son of Israel Yehuda Leib Levin, died in a Samarkand hospital on erev Shabbat 9 Kislev 5702.
story_body: On erev Shabbat 9 Kislev 5702, Levin's wife brought their two-and-a-quarter-year-old son Ephraim Shmuel to a Samarkand hospital, where he died — almost no one who entered the hospital in those days came out alive. The couple themselves carried his body several kilometers to the cemetery after Shabbat. Crushed, Levin prayed only that he not lose his faith and his bond with the Rebbe.

title_en: Tu BiShvat farbrengen launches Samarkand Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: At a Tu BiShvat 5702 farbrengen at R' Yehoshua Karf's home, Michael Teitelbaum proposed founding a Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Samarkand.
story_body: On Tu BiShvat 5702 the chassidim gathered at R' Yehoshua Karf's home, where Michael Teitelbaum urged arousing mercy for Anash and called for starting a Tomchei Tmimim in Samarkand. They began with three boys — Sholom Levertov, Zelig Katzman, and Heishke Dobrawski — each chassid pledging to feed and teach them on assigned days. The yeshiva soon expanded greatly once R' Mendel Futerfas and R' Abba Pliskin arrived to hire teachers and run it.

title_en: Yarn-trade livelihood begins after Purim 5702
summary_en: After Purim 5702, Levin began trading yarn with Bukharian Jews in Samarkand, suddenly earning 1,400 rubles and easing the family's hunger.
story_body: After Purim 5702 a stranger left yarn at Levin's home; that same day a Bukharian Jew offered to buy it at double the price. Reciting Tanya by heart to calm his fear of walking the streets without papers, Levin delivered seven kilos and earned 1,400 rubles in one transaction. From then on his livelihood eased, and he partnered with R' Pinchas Levitin in buying a wooden weaving machine.

title_en: Levin and Teitelbaum smuggle a letter to the Rebbe
summary_en: On Sunday of Parshat Bamidbar 5703, Israel Yehuda Levin and Michael Teitelbaum sent a joint Yiddish letter to the Rebbe via R' Leib Cohen.
story_body: After years cut off from the Rebbe, an opening to write through Eretz Yisrael appeared in 5703. On the first day of the week of Bamidbar, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum jointly wrote a Yiddish letter — Teitelbaum opening, Levin closing — and gave it to R' Leib Cohen for transmission. Cohen, who did not know the writers, forwarded it with a note that it had come from Samarkand via Mrs. A. Dvoskin (Teitelbaum's wife).

title_en: Levin hides from Red Army search in wall cavity
summary_en: In summer 5703, Levin hid inside a wall cavity while Red Army search parties broke into his home looking for draft evaders.
story_body: During a summer 5703 sweep for army draft evaders, Levin hid in a wall cavity behind a curtain, reciting the maamar D"H Dirshu 5690 to himself. Soldiers broke the lock, searched the room, and one peered straight through the curtain crack but did not see him. A second search party was told 'we already checked here' and left — Levin and his wife celebrated their open miracle.

title_en: Levin obtains false Polish-refugee papers as Naftali Batt
summary_en: After abandoning a military medical exam in summer 5703, Levin received forged Polish-refugee papers — eventually under the name Naftali Batt.
story_body: Summoned to a military medical exam, Levin slipped out before being seen and fled home without his papers. R' Waldman, a Polish Jew, supplied him with documents from a Polish refugee who had died in Siberia; when those wore out, Waldman brought new papers in the name Naftali Batt. Under that identity Levin lived hidden in Samarkand for several years, unable even to speak the Polish his papers claimed as his mother tongue.

title_en: Levin's sister Freida traced through Soviet bureau
summary_en: In summer 5703, Levin's wife traced his sister Freida to a camp near Stalingrad through a new Soviet missing-persons bureau.
story_body: Hearing in summer 5703 that a Soviet office had opened to trace people lost since the war began, Levin's wife inquired about his family and learned that his sister Freida was in a camp near Stalingrad. Sharing the surname Levin, she presented herself as Freida's sister-in-law and obtained her travel papers. Freida joined them in Samarkand and helped run the household weaving operation.

title_en: Rebbe's response letter to Levin written in Brooklyn
summary_en: On 24 Nissan 5704 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a response from Brooklyn blessing Levin with healthy offspring and good livelihood.
story_body: On 24 Nissan 5704, the Rebbe — through R' Moshe Gurary — answered Levin's smuggled letter from Brooklyn, blessing him with 'zera chaya vekayama' and good parnassah in both material and spiritual matters. The letter never reached Levin in Russia; only forty years later did he discover in the archive that the Rebbe had blessed him before his children were born. He saw in this the hidden providence behind his eventual escape from Russia.

title_en: Levin matches his sister Freida with R' Asher Sasonkin
summary_en: In Tammuz 5704, Levin arranged the marriage of his sister Freida to R' Asher Sasonkin, who began running a bread-distribution kiosk.
story_body: In Tammuz 5704 Levin matched his sister Freida with R' Asher Sasonkin in Samarkand. He rented them an apartment, and Sasonkin took a job distributing bread at a kiosk, giving the new household a steady livelihood.

title_en: R' Meir Gurkov released and arrives in Samarkand
summary_en: In summer 5704, Levin's father-in-law R' Meir Gurkov was released and arrived in Samarkand with his wife Feiga Rivka.
story_body: Levin's father-in-law R' Meir Gurkov was released from Soviet detention in summer 5704 and made his way to Samarkand with his wife Feiga Rivka. The couple rented an apartment in the city, rejoining the family circle there.

title_en: Itta Devorah Levin survives typhus at home in Samarkand
summary_en: In winter 5705 Itta Devorah Levin contracted brushnoi typhus and recovered at home rather than risk hospitalization.
story_body: In winter 5705 Itta Devorah Levin fell ill with brushnoi typhus; with Soviet hospitals nearly a death sentence, she was nursed at home and slowly recovered. Left weakened, she moved to her parents' home to convalesce, and the family changed apartments. The couple poured out prayers for healthy children, fulfilling 'horidi kanachal dimah.'

title_en: End of WWII celebrated by Samarkand chassidim
summary_en: On 5 Sivan 5705 (May 17, 1945) Levin and Michael Teitelbaum farbrenged in Samarkand to mark the end of the war.
story_body: When news arrived on 5 Sivan 5705 that the war was over, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum sat together drinking l'chaim in great joy. Others mocked their celebration — they had profited from valid wartime travel papers — but Levin gave thanks that the bloodshed of Jews had ended and that he might now leave the house openly and resume contact with the Rebbe.

title_en: R' Yonah Cohen visits Tashkent fertility doctors with Levin's wife
summary_en: In winter 5706 R' Yonah Cohen brought Levin and Teitelbaum's wives from Samarkand to Tashkent specialists, hosting them for a month.
story_body: Childless after years of marriage, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum confided in their friend R' Yonah Cohen of Tashkent. Himself childless, R' Yonah declared he would do everything in his power for them: he hosted both wives at his Tashkent home for a month in winter 5706 and personally escorted them to leading specialists.

title_en: Shabbos Chanukah 5706 farbrengen on emigration plans
summary_en: On Shabbos Chanukah 5706, senior chassidim gathered at Levin's home and argued against his plan to leave Russia.
story_body: On Shabbos Chanukah 5706, Rabbis Nachum Sasonkin, Dov Chen, and other senior chassidim gathered at Levin's home for a farbrengen and challenged Levin and Michael Teitelbaum's plan to apply for exit papers. Teitelbaum, well into the mashke, retorted that those whose lives were comfortable in Russia could stay where they were — he and Levin, whose lives were bitter both materially and spiritually, would do everything in their power and trust in Hashem to help them.

title_en: Levins submit OVIR exit applications via Polish identity
summary_en: In mid-winter 5706 the Levins submitted exit applications to OVIR, doctoring Itta Devorah's passport to match Naftali Batt's Polish identity.
story_body: Hearing that Polish refugees could repatriate and possibly continue on to American-occupied Germany, Levin and Michael Teitelbaum applied to OVIR in mid-winter 5706. To register his wife under the Polish name Naftali Batt, Levin tore numbered pages from her passport that recorded her maiden name Gurkov; the clerk did not notice and stamped her marriage to 'Batt.' A subsequent midnight visit from NKVD-linked questioners about the application terrified them but did not stop them.

title_en: R' Yonah Cohen's farewell blessing to Levin
summary_en: Shortly before Levin's 5706 departure, the martyred R' Yonah Cohen came to bless him and asked to be remembered.
story_body: Before Levin left Samarkand, R' Yonah Cohen — later martyred — came to his home, kissed him, and said: 'Hashem should help you with what you need; remember me. You will succeed.' Levin recalled the visit as 'cold water on a weary, thirsty soul.'

title_en: Levin family departs Samarkand on echelon no. 3
summary_en: On 4 Sivan 5706 (June 3, 1946) the Levins left Samarkand on echelon no. 3, repatriating to Poland under Polish-refugee papers.
story_body: After receiving their OVIR exit permits, the Levins were assigned to echelon no. 3, departing Samarkand on Monday 4 Sivan 5706 / June 3, 1946. They traveled with many Polish-refugee families rather than risk solo train travel, gambling on a chance — however slim — to escape Russia and reach the Rebbe.

title_en: Chabad refugees board freight train out of Samarkand (Eshelon No. 3)
summary_en: On 4 Sivan 5706, Chabad refugees loaded their belongings and boarded Eshelon No. 3, a windowless freight train, departing Samarkand toward Poland.
story_body: After waiting on the tracks most of the day, the refugees were finally permitted to board the freight train in the late afternoon. For the narrator it was the first time leaving Samarkand, where fear of the Soviet authorities had kept him indoors for years. The departure marked the start of the post-war 'Eshelonim' escape from the USSR using forged Polish papers.

title_en: Refugees immerse in roadside puddle on Erev Shavuot mid-journey
summary_en: On 5 Sivan 5706, Erev Shavuot, the narrator and R. Michoel Teitelbaum jumped from the halted train into a muddy roadside puddle to immerse themselves in honor of the festival.
story_body: The freight train suddenly stopped beside a field with a muddy puddle nearby. Seizing the opportunity, the two chassidim climbed down and immersed quickly before the train moved on. It was exactly one year since they had celebrated the end of the war together in Samarkand.

title_en: Eshelon train halted near Tambov, refugees fear deportation to Siberia
summary_en: On 15 Sivan 5706 the train stopped for hours near Tambov on a route that could lead either to Poland or to Siberia, triggering deep anxiety among the passengers.
story_body: Rumors spread that earlier eshelonim were still circling within Russia and that the passengers might be diverted to Siberia. After a long wait the train suddenly resumed moving, and by the next day they could see it was headed via Kursk toward Ukraine and Poland. A later remark attributed by the narrator to an American general framed Stalin's decision to release the Jews as a miracle.

title_en: Eshelon No. 3 crosses Dnieper at Darnitsa, route to Poland confirmed
summary_en: On 17 Sivan 5706 the train crossed the long Dnieper bridge by Darnitsa near Kiev, definitively confirming that the refugees were being routed to Poland.
story_body: After a long halt near Darnitsa the train began moving across the Dnieper, and the passengers realized for certain they were on the road to Poland rather than Siberia. The narrator silently thanked God for being granted to see the journey 'from narrowness to expanse.' Further west they were shown mounds where Germans and Ukrainians had buried murdered Jews alive.

title_en: Refugees reach the old Russian-Polish border
summary_en: Around 18 Sivan 5706 the eshelon reached the pre-war Russian-Polish border, a moment the narrator had awaited for twelve years since the Frierdiker Rebbe's 1934 reply.
story_body: The narrator had been refused exit permits in 5694 (1934) despite the Rebbe's instructions to apply, and again the same summer. Now, after twelve years, the train passed the red-and-white striped border posts of the old border at about 11 a.m. He privately thanked God but hid his joy until they were beyond Russian territory.

title_en: Banderite raiders attempt to attack Eshelon No. 3 in western Ukraine
summary_en: During a night halt by a forest in western Ukraine, Banderite raiders tried to break into the refugees' freight car before being driven off until morning.
story_body: Rumors said the train drivers cooperated with Banderite bandits, halting at forests so that the cars could be looted; Eshelon No. 2 had already been robbed in this way. R. Michoel Teitelbaum bolted the door from inside and beat off the attackers' fingers with empty bottles until dawn broke and the train moved on. The car had no windows because it was a freight and livestock wagon.

title_en: Eshelon No. 3 crosses into Poland at Przemyśl
summary_en: On about 20 Sivan 5706 the refugees crossed the new Russian-Polish border into Przemyśl after exchanging rubles for złoty at the Soviet bank.
story_body: Soviet officials forced an unfavorable ruble-to-złoty rate at the border but the narrator and R. Michoel refused to risk delay and exchanged everything they had. Border guards merely called out names from a list without searching the cars, allowing undocumented young women hidden in the wheat fields to slip aboard. Once in Przemyśl Polish merchants paid three złoty per ruble, and the refugees realized they were finally out of Russia.

title_en: Lubavitcher refugees arrive in Łódź
summary_en: On Thursday, 21 Sivan 5706, the eshelon reached Wrocław and the Anash refugees continued by hired rail car to Łódź, settling at 42 Zachodnia Street.
story_body: At Wrocław German and Polish locals warned that many Jews had survived, and the refugees grasped that danger still lay ahead. Bribed Polish officials let them disembark, and Anash who had arrived earlier hired a truck to bring them to 42 Zachodnia Street, where the Lubavitch refugees from Russia lodged together. A va'ad of Anash in Łódź coordinated relief, likely with Joint Distribution Committee aid, and began arranging onward travel out of Poland.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe writes letter endorsing Rabbi Eliezer Silver
summary_en: On 27 Iyar 5706 the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote a letter (Igros Kodesh vol. 9 p. 128) instructing the refugees in Łódź to honor the visiting Rabbi Eliezer Silver.
story_body: The letter reached the Anash refugees in Łódź a day or two before Rabbi Silver's visit and resolved their hesitation about how to receive a non-chassidic American rav. The Rebbe praised Silver's self-sacrifice in saving Jews and ranked him above factional politics. Receiving the letter after years of severed contact was experienced as the first overt miracle the refugees saw from the Rebbe after leaving Russia.

title_en: Rabbi Eliezer Silver reception in Łódź; Frierdiker Rebbe's letter read aloud
summary_en: On Friday, 29 Sivan 5706 (Erev Shabbos Korach), American Chief Rabbi Eliezer Silver was received by the religious parties in Łódź, and R. Benyamin Gorodetzky read the Frierdiker Rebbe's letter publicly.
story_body: Held in the Agudath Israel secretariat at 66 Zachodnia Street, the reception included delegates from Agudah, Poalei Agudah, Mizrachi and Hapoel Hamizrachi. When R. Benyamin Gorodetzky rose with the Rebbe's letter, Rabbi Silver also stood out of respect, forcing the entire assembly to rise — a public win for the small Lubavitch contingent. At Mincha afterward Silver crossed the synagogue to greet Gorodetzky beside the Aron Kodesh, demonstratively honoring Chabad before the other delegates.

title_en: Rabbi Eliezer Silver's drasha in Łódź on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz
summary_en: On Shabbos Parshas Korach, 1 Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5706, Rabbi Eliezer Silver addressed a large crowd in Łódź, praising the Frierdiker Rebbe as the hidden source of the refugees' mesirus nefesh.
story_body: Silver compared the chassidim's spiritual endurance under Soviet persecution to a flourishing tree in the desert whose water comes from a distant hidden spring — the Rebbe. He added that the Rebbe was likewise working with mesirus nefesh in the United States, and that he himself was strengthened by him. He then held a separate private meeting with the small Anash group in honor of the Rebbe, and afterward began advocating for Polish passports to Prague for them.

title_en: R. Levin's group leaves Lodz for Katowice on Bricha escape route
summary_en: R. Yisrael Yehuda Levin and his Chabad group depart Lodz for Katowice on 10 Menachem Av as part of the Bricha escape effort.
story_body: After finally receiving passports, Levin and a Chabad group left Lodz for Katowice on 10 Menachem Av 5706. Upon arrival they were asked not to appear on the streets with long beards. Mikhael Teitelbaum departed separately via Stettin, while Levin remained with the main group to travel by train toward Prague.

title_en: Levin's group reaches Prague; Rebbe sends R. Yisroel Jacobson
summary_en: On 17 Menachem Av the group reaches Prague where R. Yisroel Jacobson, sent specially by the Frierdiker Rebbe, awaits them.
story_body: After a polite border check by Czech police, the Warsaw–Prague express reached Prague on Wednesday, 17 Av 5706. R. Yehuda Chitrik told Levin the verse 'I bore you on eagles' wings' was being fulfilled. The Frierdiker Rebbe had dispatched R. Yisroel Jacobson from America specifically to receive them and arrange their onward journey.

title_en: Levin prays at the Maharal's grave in Prague
summary_en: On 18 Av the refugees daven in the Maharal's synagogue and Levin visits his grave to plead for children.
story_body: On Thursday Parshat Ekev, 18 Menachem Av 5706, the Chabad refugees went into Prague to daven at the Altneuschul. Afterward Levin and his wife Itta Devorah visited the adjacent graves of the Maharal of Prague and his righteous wife to beg for healthy offspring.

title_en: Friday-night farbrengen with R. Yisroel Jacobson in Prague camp
summary_en: On 19 Av 5706 the Rebbe's emissary leads a Friday-night farbrengen in the Prague refugee camp.
story_body: On Erev Shabbat Ekev, 19 Av 5706, bottles of mashke were brought to the camp from the city. At the Friday-night meal R. Yisroel Jacobson farbrenged with the group — Levin's first time experiencing a personal emissary of the Rebbe at a tisch. Jacobson, who otherwise ate only food brought from America, accepted chicken that Itta Devorah had koshered in Katowice once told her father was R. Meir Gorkov, and blessed her with offspring.

title_en: Rabbi Herzog addresses refugees at Maharal's Prague synagogue
summary_en: On 21 Av Chief Rabbi Herzog speaks in Prague urging refugees to make aliyah to Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: On Sunday Parshat Re'eh, 21 Menachem Av 5706, the Chabad group returned to the Altneuschul. Rabbi Yitzchak Halevi Herzog, Chief Rabbi of Eretz Yisrael, spoke on Parshat Re'eh and called on all to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael. Litvish yeshiva talmidim Levin knew from Samarkand and other Polish refugees were also present.

title_en: First attempted Czech–German border crossing repulsed by U.S. MPs
summary_en: On 28 Av the group is driven from Asch to the border but turned back at gunpoint by American MPs.
story_body: After Shabbat in Asch the Chabad group was driven by Bricha guides to the U.S.-zone border on Sunday Parshat Shoftim, 28 Av 5706. The original guards had been replaced and U.S. Military Police forced them — including pregnant women such as R. Pinchas Schreiber's daughter — back onto the truck. They returned to Asch and soon moved to a former Wehrmacht camp closer to the frontier to wait for another attempt.

title_en: Night march through forest into U.S.-occupied Germany
summary_en: On 6 Elul Bricha guides lead the group at night through a forest toward the U.S. zone under MP gunfire.
story_body: On Monday Parshat Ki Seitzei, 6 Elul 5706, Bricha activists trucked the group to a stable beside a forest. After dark a guide led them into the woods; jeeps of U.S. Military Police fired into the trees on hearing rustling, forcing them to lie still. The guide briefly led them toward the Soviet zone before correcting course; they walked nearly all night.

title_en: Levin's group reaches UNRRA camp at Rehau
summary_en: On 7 Elul 5706 the group slips into the UNRRA gate at Rehau, escaping pursuing U.S. MP jeeps.
story_body: At dawn the guide ordered them onto the road; Itta Devorah ran ahead and reached the UNRRA gate first on 7 Elul 5706 (Parshat Ki Seitzei). Once inside they were protected from being returned to Czechoslovakia by UNRRA jurisdiction. An MP jeep — driven by the same officers from the earlier turn-back — passed moments later but could not enter UNRRA territory. The next day a Jewish woman ran in reporting that 150 refugees just behind them had been seized by MPs.

title_en: R. Chaikel Chaikin escorts Levin's group to Hof DP camp
summary_en: On 9 Elul R. Chaikel Chaikin arrives by truck and brings the group from Rehau to the larger Hof DP camp.
story_body: On Thursday Parshat Ki Seitzei, 9 Elul 5706, R. Chaikel Chaikin — already settled at Hof — drove out to fetch them. Hof was further from the border and considered safer. The group spent Shabbat Parshat Ki Seitzei (11 Elul) there before moving on.

title_en: Chabad refugees settle at Waldstadt Pocking DP camp
summary_en: After Shabbos the Chabad refugees move to Waldstadt 'Pocking', a forested DP camp of 7,000 Jews near Munich.
story_body: Following Shabbat at Hof the group moved to Waldstadt Pocking, a sprawling DP camp of about 7,000 Jews not far from Munich. Two blocks were assigned temporarily, with a permanent Lubavitcher corner — one room per family — promised within days. Pocking would become the main Chabad refugee hub in occupied Germany.

title_en: R. Nissan Nemanov organizes Anash vaad at Pocking
summary_en: On 15 Elul 5706 R. Nissan Nemanov convenes an assembly and appoints a Chabad vaad including Mikhael Teitelbaum.
story_body: On Wednesday Parshat Ki Tavo, 15 Elul 5706, R. Nissan Nemanov gathered the Lubavitchers in Pocking and, with general consensus, established a vaad to run their communal affairs. Mikhael Teitelbaum, reunited with Levin at Pocking, was included among the appointees. The community was filled with joy at having reconstituted itself in safety.

title_en: R. Nissan Nemanov leads Chai Elul farbrengen in Pocking
summary_en: On Shabbos Chai Elul 5706 R. Nissan Nemanov farbrengs in the Agudah shul at Pocking with singing and dancing.
story_body: On Shabbat 18 Elul 5706 R. Nissan Nemanov held a joyous farbrengen in the Agudah synagogue at Pocking. The broken refugees in the camp could not understand the Lubavitchers' jubilation at having escaped Russia; one was overheard calling them 'a meshugene Agudah.' R. Nemanov soon arranged daily shiurim and rebuilt a yeshiva structure with melamdim.

title_en: R. Levin receives first letter from Frierdiker Rebbe at Pocking
summary_en: On 23 Shevat 5707 Levin receives a welcome and blessing letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe via the Paris lishka.
story_body: After Levin and others demanded the camp leadership find a way to reestablish direct contact with the Rebbe, the Paris lishka began conveying letters. The Frierdiker Rebbe wrote to Levin on 23 Shevat 5707 with a 'baruchim haba'im' blessing for him and his wife and wishes for success in material and spiritual matters. Levin had waited for such a letter throughout the entire flight from Russia.

title_en: Rashag and R. Benyamin Gorodetzky visit Pocking before Pesach
summary_en: Before Pesach 5707 the Rashag and R. Benyamin Gorodetzky visit Pocking with letters and maamarim from the Rebbe.
story_body: Before Pesach 5707 R. Benyamin Gorodetzky and the Rashag came from the Rebbe to Pocking. The Rashag held a Shabbat farbrengen with anash; afterward R. Shlomo Matusof delivered a letter from the Rebbe rebuking Levin's preoccupations and urging him to immerse in study. They also brought freshly copied maamarim of the Rebbe from that year.

title_en: R. Levin receives Rebbe's letter dated 27 Nissan 5707
summary_en: Letter dated 27 Nissan 5707 from the Frierdiker Rebbe to Levin blessing his health and that of his family.
story_body: Through the Paris office Levin received a letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe dated 27 Nissan 5707, blessing his health and that of his household along with success in their material and spiritual needs. This was part of a series of letters now flowing between Pocking and the Rebbe via the Paris lishka.

title_en: R. Chaim Asher brings Rebbe's letters to Pocking on Lag B'Omer
summary_en: On Lag B'Omer 5707 R. Chaim Asher arrives from Paris with replies from the Frierdiker Rebbe.
story_body: On Lag B'Omer 5707 R. Chaim Asher came from Paris bearing further letters from the Rebbe in response to those sent after the first 'baruchim haba'im' batch. Levin then wrote again pleading for mercy on his sister Frayde Meni Sosonkin, her husband Asher (son of R. Shmaryahu Sosonkin of Batum) and their daughter Chava, who remained stranded in Lvov.

title_en: Pocking Shavuos memorial morphs into Lubavitch chinuch drive
summary_en: On Shavuos 5707 Levin and Mikhael Teitelbaum convert a yizkor assembly into a Lubavitch education drive.
story_body: Acting on a rebuke from the Ramash that Pocking's Lubavitchers were sitting idle while DP children went untaught, Levin and Mikhael Teitelbaum independently summoned all 7,000 refugees on Shavuos 5707 to a 'memorial' at the Chabad shul. R. Avraham Eliyahu Plotkin and R. Yisrael of Nevel delivered fiery drashos linking Dovid HaMelech to the chinuch of children. After a stormy split between Mizrachi and Cherut factions, an agreement emerged: Lubavitcher melamdim would supplement the camp's secular schools with Torah hours, planting decades of warmth toward Yiddishkeit in Pocking-raised children.

title_en: Rebbe's letter dated 29 Sivan 5707 reaches R. Levin
summary_en: On 29 Sivan 5707 the Frierdiker Rebbe answers Levin's plea for the Sosonkin family stranded in Lvov.
story_body: Replying via the Paris office, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 29 Sivan 5707 invoking blessings on the family members in Levin's earlier letter — his sister Frayde, her husband Asher Sosonkin, and their daughter Chava — who remained in the Soviet Union. The Rebbe blessed them with refuah, deliverance from hardship, and reunion with anash in the Rebbe's presence.

title_en: Birth of Sterna Sarah Levin in Pocking DP camp
summary_en: On 24 Elul 5707 Itta Devorah Levin gives birth to a daughter, Sterna Sarah, at Pocking.
story_body: On 24 Elul 5707 Itta Devorah Levin gave birth to a daughter — Sterna Sarah — while still in Pocking awaiting visas. The yeshiva's cooks prepared a large and lengthy kiddush, with much mashke and a farbrengen lasting until evening. R. Avraham Mayor was so joyful he rolled along the benches.

title_en: Rebbe writes about Levin's ailing daughter
summary_en: On 5 Kislev 5708 a letter in the Rebbe's name responds to news of the infant Sterna Sarah's illness.
story_body: In early winter 5708 Levin's infant daughter took ill and he wrote to the Rebbe. The reply, dated 5 Kislev 5708 and sent in the Rebbe's name, conveyed mazal tov on her birth and a blessing to raise her to Torah, chuppah and good deeds amid material and spiritual ease.

title_en: Levin family receives French visa and moves toward Paris
summary_en: After Pesach 5708 Levin receives a visa to Paris arranged by his in-laws R. Meir and Fayge Rivka Gorkov.
story_body: After Pesach 5708 the long-delayed visa to France finally came through. Levin's in-laws R. Meir Gorkov and Fayge Rivka Gorkov, already in Paris, had pushed the paperwork while Mikhael Teitelbaum waited on a U.S. visa. The Levins relocated from Pocking to Bezancourt outside Paris.

title_en: Rebbe's welcome letter to R. Levin on arrival in Paris
summary_en: On 21 Sivan 5708 the Rebbe writes 'baruchim haba'im' to R. Levin on his arrival in Paris.
story_body: On Levin's arrival in Paris the Frierdiker Rebbe sent a personally signed welcome letter dated 21 Sivan 5708. The Rebbe blessed him and his family with health, a comfortable livelihood and immersion in Torah and avodah in their new home.

title_en: Rebbe asks Levin to consult elder chassidim about employment
summary_en: On 29 Sivan 5708 the Rebbe directs Levin to consult senior chassidim about his employment.
story_body: Idle in Bezancourt with no parnasa, Levin asked the Rebbe what work to pursue. The reply, dated 29 Sivan 5708, instructed him to consult senior anash and report back their advice. R. Yisrael Noach and other elders subsequently advised him to take up melamdus.

title_en: Rebbe endorses melamdus as Levin's path in Paris
summary_en: On 21 Av 5708 the Rebbe endorses Levin's plan to support himself teaching the children of Parisian Jews.
story_body: Replying to Levin's report on the elders' counsel, the Frierdiker Rebbe wrote on 21 Av 5708 strongly endorsing his becoming a melamed. He blessed him with the gift of teaching, influence over students in conduct and chassidic ways, and ample parnasa. Levin then began traveling from Bezancourt into Paris, using addresses given by R. Zalman Serebryanski, to teach Sephardi 'patrons' who had never before encountered a Torah tutor.

title_en: Levin reports on Paris kiruv work to the Rebbe
summary_en: On 11 Elul 5708 Levin reports to the Rebbe on tutoring eight Parisian children, including putting on tefillin.
story_body: Levin wrote on 11 Elul 5708 that he was traveling daily from Bezancourt into Paris to teach the children of French Jewish 'patrons' who spoke only French. He had grown his roster from one student to eight, teaching kamatz alef and laying tefillin. He described coaxing reluctant students to don a hat and tefillin and distributing French-language Merkos pamphlets in the homes.

title_en: Birth of R. Shalom DovBer Levin in Paris
summary_en: On 27 Elul 5708 Itta Devorah Levin gives birth in Paris to a son, the future Chabad librarian R. Shalom DovBer Levin.
story_body: On 27 Elul 5708 in Paris Itta Devorah Levin gave birth to a son. He was named Shalom DovBer — the future longtime director of the Chabad Library at 770.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe's Rosh Hashanah blessing letter to Levin
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Hashanah 5709 the Frierdiker Rebbe sends Levin a kesiva v'chasima tova blessing.
story_body: On Erev Rosh Hashanah 5709 the Frierdiker Rebbe sent Levin a personally signed blessing. The letter wished him and his family a kesiva v'chasima tova and a sweet new year in both material and spiritual realms.

title_en: Rebbe's bris mazal-tov letter for Shalom DovBer Levin
summary_en: On 25 Tishrei 5709 the Rebbe writes congratulating Levin on the bris of his son Shalom DovBer.
story_body: Following the bris of his newborn son, Levin received a letter dated 25 Tishrei 5709. In it the Frierdiker Rebbe wished him mazal tov on entering his son into the covenant of Avraham Avinu and blessed him to raise the child to Torah, chuppah and good deeds amid expansiveness in body and spirit.

title_en: Levin opens cheder for Anash children in Bezancourt
summary_en: On 18 Kislev 5709 Levin reports to the Rebbe that he has begun teaching the young children of Anash in Bezancourt.
story_body: On 18 Kislev 5709 Levin wrote to the Rebbe that he had now established himself fully as a melamed. In addition to his outreach work with Parisian families, he was teaching the small children of Anash families living in Bezancourt — laying the seeds of an Anash cheder for the postwar French community.

title_en: Rayatz instructs R' Yisrael Yehuda Levin to travel to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: On 19 Shevat 5709 the Rayatz wrote to Yisrael Yehuda Levin advising him to travel to Eretz Yisrael and to consult the Vaad HaMesader of Anash in Tel Aviv.
story_body: Levin had written asking the Rebbe Rayatz where to go after leaving Europe. The Rebbe's secretariat replied on 19 Shevat 5709 directing him to Eretz Yisrael, where he should contact Rabbi R. S. D. Zislin and R. M. Gurary of the Vaad HaMesader of Anash and Tmimim in Tel Aviv. The letter set the direction for Levin's emigration after the war.

title_en: Rayatz blesses Levin's aliyah plans for Nissan 5709
summary_en: On 11 Nissan 5709 the Rayatz wrote Levin to proceed with his journey to Eretz Yisrael with his family and to settle in agriculture or poultry-raising.
story_body: As a large group of Chassidim prepared to sail from Europe, Levin informed the Rebbe of his plans. The Rayatz responded on 11 Nissan 5709 with blessings for safe travel and a successful settlement, suggesting agricultural work or chicken farming as a livelihood.

title_en: Farbrengen near Marseille on the eve of departure
summary_en: On Motzaei Shabbat Parshat Emor 5709, R' Peretz Mochkin came to the group of Chassidim waiting by the sea near Marseille and held a farbrengen.
story_body: Levin and a group of Chassidim, including R' Shlomo Chaim, gathered by the sea near Marseille to board a ship to Eretz Yisrael. On Motzaei Shabbat Parshat Emor R' Peretz Mochkin joined them and led a farbrengen the night before they sailed.

title_en: Levin's group sails from Marseille to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: On Sunday of Parshat Behar 5709, Levin and his family set sail from near Marseille to Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: After the Motzaei Shabbat farbrengen, the group boarded their ship on Sunday of Parshat Behar 5709 and began the voyage to Eretz Yisrael, marking the start of a new chapter for the post-war emigrants.

title_en: Rayatz welcomes Levin's arrival in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: On 27 Menachem Av 5709 the Rayatz responded to Levin's report of safe arrival in Eretz Yisrael and his settlement in Kfar Sefaria.
story_body: Levin wrote to the Rebbe Rayatz on 16 Av 5709 reporting that he had reached Eretz Yisrael and settled in Kfar Sefaria, where he worked irrigating orchards. The Rebbe's reply, dated 27 Menachem Av, blessed the family with material and spiritual sustenance. The signature notably emphasized the letter yud, a usage Rayatz adopted from Shevat 5709 onward.

title_en: Rayatz sends New Year blessing letter for 5710
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Hashana 5710 the Rayatz wrote Levin a New Year blessing letter for a good and sweet year.
