title_en: Rebbe Rashab delivers maamar on yahrtzeit of Rebbetzin Rivkah in Rostov
summary_en: On the yahrtzeit of his mother Rebbetzin Rivkah, the Rebbe Rashab delivers the maamar 'Vayehi Beshalach Pharaoh' in Rostov.
story_body: On Shabbat 10 Shevat 5676, parshat Beshalach, the Rebbe Rashab marked the yahrtzeit of his mother, the Rebbetzin Rivkah. He delivered the maamar beginning 'Vayehi Beshalach Pharaoh,' a brief notation of which appears in the Rayatz's short daily diary for that year.

title_en: Rayatz begins composing his account of the move to Rostov
summary_en: In Rostov the Rayatz begins writing his detailed reshimah recounting the family's evacuation from Lubavitch via Orel.
story_body: Starting on 2 Adar I 5676 in Rostov, the Rayatz set down a meticulous record of the decision to leave Lubavitch, the journey, the first reception in Rostov, the apartment search, the inaugural Yud-Tes Kislev farbrengen in the new home, and the troubles with the landlord. The composition continued through Purim Katan of that same year.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab's Purim Katan maamar in Rostov
summary_en: Over Shabbat Purim Katan in Rostov the Rebbe Rashab delivers the maamar 'Ve'ahavta et Havayah.'
story_body: For Shabbat Purim Katan 5676 Rabbi Y.Y. of Kremenchug came to Rostov, and R. Tzvi Gurary, who had planned to leave Thursday night, stayed on to spend Shabbat with the Rebbe Rashab. The Rebbe delivered the maamar 'Ve'ahavta et Havayah Elokecha,' which was preserved in a separate written record.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab writes blessing to mother from Slavyansk
summary_en: Rebbe Rashab penned a handwritten note to a mother, blessing her son to walk in the good and upright path.
story_body: While residing in Slavyansk during the upheavals of World War I, Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch wrote a brief handwritten response to a mother who had sought his blessing. He acknowledged receipt of her letter and prayed that G-d grant her son a good heart to walk in the good and upright way. The note is dated Monday of the week of Parshat Re'eh, 5677.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab gives Mazal Tov gift on 19 Kislev 5680
summary_en: On the Chag HaGeulah of 19 Kislev 5680, Rebbe Rashab distributed a banknote inscribed with a Mazal Tov blessing.
story_body: On 19 Kislev 5680, the festival commemorating the Alter Rebbe's liberation, Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch presented a banknote bearing the inscription 'Mazal Tov, 19 Kislev 5680' to a chassid. The annotation in the margin was recorded by his secretary, Rabbi Elchonon Dov Marozov. This was one of the final such gifts of the Rebbe Rashab's life, given mere months before his passing.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab distributes banknotes on Sukkot 5680
summary_en: Rebbe Rashab gave out banknotes as gifts and segulot during Sukkot 5680, his final Sukkot.
story_body: On Sukkot of 5680, Rebbe Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch distributed banknotes either as gifts or as a segulah (spiritual remedy). The dates were inscribed in the margins by his secretary, Rabbi Elchonon Dov Marozov. This was the Rebbe Rashab's final Sukkot before his passing on 2 Nissan 5680.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz secludes himself during mourning for his father
summary_en: Following the passing of his father Rebbe Rashab, Rebbe Rayatz sat secluded in his room, alone with his Creator.
story_body: After Rebbe Sholom DovBer passed away on 2 Nissan 5680, his son Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak entered a period of intense seclusion. As he later described in his letters, from the first day he felt as a man struck by thunder, finding no rest except in his thrice-daily prayers, and remaining closed in his room without speaking. This period of withdrawal and inner reckoning shaped his early nesius.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz compiles inventory of his father's manuscripts
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz compiled a detailed list of the maamarim, chozrim, and letters left by his father Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: On 19 Mar-Cheshvan 5681, during his year of mourning for his father, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak compiled a detailed catalogue of every Chassidic maamar that remained in his father Rebbe Rashab's own handwriting. He also recorded the names of the chozrim who transmitted maamarim delivered orally, and summarized the collection of letters left behind. The list was later printed at the end of Kuntres Chanoch LaNaar.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz draws the Menorah of Chassidus
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz drew a seven-branched menorah summarizing the seven generations of Chassidic leadership from the Baal Shem Tov to his father.
story_body: During his year of mourning, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak drew a seven-branched Menorah of Chassidus for himself, each branch dedicated to one of the founders of Chassidus and the Rebbeim of Chabad across the seven generations. Each Rebbe was inscribed with his name, years of leadership, yahrtzeit, and in some cases burial location. The drawing was framed by verses about the seven lamps illuminating Israel and the soul of man standing on four pillars: love, feeling, knowledge, and faith.

title_en: Letter to Rabbi Tzirelson of Ludmir on Eretz Yisrael fundraising
summary_en: Secretary Yaakov Kapil Zeliksohn wrote to Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Tzirelson of Ludmir regarding Eretz Yisrael fundraising.
story_body: On 20 Adar 5667, writing on the Rebbe Rayatz's stationery from Lubavitch, secretary Yaakov Kapil Zeliksohn sent a postcard to Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Tzirelson, rabbi of Ludmir (Vladimir-Volynsky). The letter urged Tzirelson to follow the model of the Kovel community in collecting Ramban funds for the Anash community in Hebron. At that time the future Rebbe Rayatz served as director of Tomchei Temimim and chairman of the Hebron Vaad.

title_en: Wedding of Rebbe Rayatz and Rebbetzin Nechama Dina
summary_en: Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak married Rebbetzin Nechama Dina on 13 Elul 5657.
story_body: On 13 Elul 5657, Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, son of Rebbe Rashab and the future sixth Rebbe of Lubavitch, married Nechama Dina, daughter of Rabbi Avraham Schneersohn of Kishinev. The date would later be commemorated annually with gifts and blessings exchanged between the couple. The anniversary became significant in Chabad lore and was marked publicly fifty years later in 5707.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz gives 50th anniversary gift to Rebbetzin Nechama Dina
summary_en: On their 50th anniversary, Rebbe Rayatz gifted Rebbetzin Nechama Dina a new coat with $500 from their joint fund, and the future Rebbe gifted her a printed copy of Sefer HaZichronot.
story_body: On 13 Elul 5707, marking fifty years since their wedding, Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak wrote a brief Yiddish note to his wife wishing many long, healthy, content years, nachas from their children, and all good both materially and spiritually. He gifted her a new coat funded by $500 from 'our joint fund,' to be worn in health and with a joyful heart. The future Rebbe (then Ramash) gifted Rebbetzin Nechama Dina a printed copy of Rebbe Rayatz's Sefer HaZichronot, which he had brought to press that same year.

title_en: Sasonkin writes from Rostov to Axelrod in Zembin
summary_en: Secretary Nochum Shmaryahu Sasonkin wrote from Rostov to Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod with fundraising directives for Tomchei Temimim.
story_body: On 13 Sivan 5681, writing from Rostov-on-Don, Rebbe Rayatz's secretary Nochum Shmaryahu Sasonkin wrote to the recently married Axelrod in Zembin. He acknowledged a letter from Axelrod's father in America and directed Axelrod to urge his father to mobilize donations to Tomchei Temimim through newspaper appeals. He listed contacts in Vienna, Iași (Romania), Warsaw, and Riga who could relay funds, noting that foreign currency would be worth two thousand times more in their home country.

title_en: Marozov writes to Axelrod in Baltimore
summary_en: Secretary Elchonon Dov Marozov wrote to Axelrod in Baltimore acknowledging a donation and reflecting on the spiritual oppression in Soviet Russia.
story_body: On 2 Iyar 5685, secretary Elchonon Dov Marozov acknowledged receipt of three shekalim from a donor through Axelrod, who had by then emigrated to Baltimore. Marozov described how despite difficult material conditions in Soviet Russia they had celebrated Pesach with joy, lamenting that no acquaintance had bread or peace of mind. He praised Axelrod for having escaped 'the darkness here where the air is full of heresy and apostasy, enforced with a strong hand.'

title_en: Announcement of Rebbe Rayatz's return from Kostroma exile
summary_en: Secretary Shneur Zalman Schneersohn announced to Axelrod that the Rebbe Rayatz had safely returned home from Kostroma exile.
story_body: On 15 Tammuz 5687, secretary Shneur Zalman Schneersohn wrote with the long-awaited news that 'today is the day we hoped for — our holy father returned home in peace and success.' This announced Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak's release from his Kostroma exile, following his arrest by Soviet authorities, death sentence, and dramatic redemption on 12-13 Tammuz. The release would soon be commemorated annually as Chag HaGeulah.

title_en: Feigin writes to Axelrod about the custom of mother's name in pidyon
summary_en: Secretary Yechezkel Feigin confirmed to Rabbi Axelrod the established custom of writing the mother's name in a pidyon nefesh.
story_body: On 6 Tevet 5689, secretary Yechezkel Feigin confirmed receipt of Axelrod's pidyon nefesh and his five-shekel check. He clarified that the established practice is to write the mother's name in a pidyon, citing both the Rebbe Rayatz's statement that the Rebbeim had always written the mother's name and a tradition from Rabbi Hillel of Paritch that in a pidyon one writes the mother's name while in a tzettel one writes the father's name.

title_en: Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod emigrates to Baltimore
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod emigrated from Soviet Russia to the United States, settling in Baltimore.
story_body: In 5684 Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod, a noted Tomchei Temimim alumnus who had been living in Zembin since 5681, emigrated from Soviet Russia to America and settled in Baltimore. He would serve as a rabbi there for nearly three decades. His departure was later praised by Rebbe Rayatz's secretary Marozov as an escape from the spiritual darkness of Soviet life.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod in Baltimore
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod, prominent chassid and Tomchei Temimim alumnus, passed away in Baltimore on 4 Adar 5712.
story_body: On 4 Adar 5712 the famed chassid Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Axelrod passed away in Baltimore. He had studied at Tomchei Temimim from 5666 to 5681, married and lived in Zembin from 5681 to 5684, and then emigrated to Baltimore where he served as a rabbi for the remaining decades of his life. His correspondence with the secretariat of Rebbe Rayatz preserves important historical material from the Rostov, Riga, and Otwock periods.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz falls ill with heart disease
summary_en: Beginning in late Tishrei 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz began suffering fatigue and pains around the heart, marking the onset of a serious heart illness.
story_body: Already at the end of Tishrei 5705 (October 1944), Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn began to feel fatigue, agitation and pains around the heart. Dr. Wilder visited him almost daily, several times together with the cardiologist Dr. Dressler. They prescribed medication and ordered him to rest, though the Rebbe continued his writing, correspondence, and reception of visitors as much as possible.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz directs Anash that he can no longer receive visitors
summary_en: On 21 Marcheshvan 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz issued a general directive to Anash that, per his doctors, he must rest from receiving people and could communicate only in writing.
story_body: On 21 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a general directive (printed in Igrot Kodesh vol. 8, letter 2,535) informing Chassidim that his doctors had ordered him to cease in-person audiences. He explained that he was suffering chest pain requiring full rest, yet noted that the demands of spreading Torah, fear of Heaven, and proper chinuch required tenfold more strength than before.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz suffers heart attack
summary_en: On 26 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz suffered a heart attack and remained bedridden for approximately three weeks.
story_body: On 26 Marcheshvan 5705 (12 November 1944) the Rebbe Rayatz suffered a heart attack. He lay bedridden in serious condition for roughly three weeks, during which time he did not write in his diary at all. Drs. Wilder and Dressler attended him throughout the recovery.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz publishes thanksgiving letter for recovery
summary_en: On 24 Kislev 5705, beginning to recover, the Rebbe Rayatz wrote a general letter thanking God and Anash for prayers during his illness.
story_body: On 24 Kislev 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz, beginning to regain strength, composed a public letter (Igrot Kodesh vol. 8, letter 2,548) thanking God for His great kindness and Anash for their prayers and blessings, which he credited with raising him from three weeks of severe suffering. Even then, he was confined to bed by day and forbidden from returning to the yechidus room.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz returns to study after six-week heart illness
summary_en: On 7 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz returned to his yechidus room for the first time after roughly six weeks of illness.
story_body: On 7 Tevet 5705 (23 December 1944), after about six weeks of heart illness, the Rebbe Rayatz returned to his study for the first time, reading books although still feeling weak. He prayed for strength to resume spreading Torah with fear of Heaven, strengthening institutions, kosher education, guiding Anash, and editing his memoir manuscripts.

title_en: Cold passes; Rebbe Rayatz resumes yechidus on 26 Tevet
summary_en: On 26 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz, his cold and fever having passed, received people in yechidus, including the principal of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Montreal.
story_body: On 26 Tevet 5705 the cold, nasal congestion and fever the Rebbe had been suffering finally passed. That evening he received Rabbi R. Sh. L. about the administration of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in Montreal, and also Rabbi Kramer, the principal of that yeshivah.

title_en: Founding meeting for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Lubavitch Chicago
summary_en: On 28 Tishrei 5705 a meeting with Chicago donors raised $25,000 in two-year loans toward purchasing a building for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Lubavitch in Chicago.
story_body: On 28 Tishrei 5705 (15 October 1944) Mr. Pinchas Rismann, Mr. and Mrs. Yechezkel Liesner, Mr. Palmer, Rabbi Rodstein, Rabbi Predmesky and the Rebbe's son-in-law Rashag met with the Rebbe Rayatz about establishing Yeshivat Achei Tmimim in Chicago. The Liesners pledged a $15,000 two-year loan, with Rismann and C. S. Palmer each adding $5,000, all earmarked to purchase a building for the new yeshivah.

title_en: Assembly on reviving Chassidic communities in America
summary_en: On 29 Tishrei 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz convened an assembly of Anash on reviving Chassidic communities, organized around shul congregants, scattered Anash, and Chassidic lineage families.
story_body: On the evening of 29 Tishrei 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz convened an assembly of Anash that he had summoned regarding the revival of Chassidic communities in the present generation. The discussion was framed around three categories: regular congregants of Anash shuls, individual Anash who pray in other shuls, and descendants of Chassidic families — with a coordinating committee to be selected.

title_en: Suitable building identified in Chicago for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim
summary_en: On 5 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz was told that a large, suitable building had been identified in Chicago to house the new Achei Tmimim Lubavitch yeshivah, with purchase planned the next day.
story_body: On the evening of 5 Marcheshvan 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law Rashag informed him that contacts in Chicago had reported finding a large, suitable building for Yeshivat Achei Tmimim Lubavitch and intended to purchase it the next day. The development came less than two weeks after the founding fundraising meeting on 28 Tishrei.

title_en: Mindel project to compile English booklet on Chabad communal work
summary_en: On Motzaei Shabbat Lech Lecha 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz began dictating, to son-in-law Ramash and R. Nissan Mindel, material on the communal and economic activity of the Chabad Rebbes for an English-language booklet.
story_body: From Motzaei Shabbat Lech Lecha, 11 Marcheshvan 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz began quietly relating to his son-in-law Ramash (the future Rebbe) and to Nissan Mindel an account of the communal activity — especially economic — of the Mitteler Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, the Maharash, and the Rashab through 5661. Ramash relayed the words to Mindel, who took notes; their stated aim was to compile and print a Chabad-leadership communal-activity booklet in English.

title_en: Birthday of the Rebbe Rashab recalled in 1944 diary
summary_en: The Rebbe Rashab, fifth Lubavitcher Rebbe, was born Monday Chaye Sarah, 20 Marcheshvan 5621, at 9 AM.
story_body: In his 5705 diary the Rebbe Rayatz noted that 20 Marcheshvan was the birthday of his father, the Rebbe Rashab, who was born on Monday of parashat Chaye Sarah, 20 Marcheshvan 5621 (5 November 1860), at the ninth hour of the morning. The Rayatz recorded a dream that night in which his father appeared in Shabbat garments on the 84th anniversary of his soul's descent.

title_en: Roosevelt elected to a fourth term as US President
summary_en: Diary entry of 22 Marcheshvan 5705 records that Franklin D. Roosevelt had been elected US President for a fourth term.
story_body: Writing on 22 Marcheshvan 5705 (8 November 1944), the Rebbe Rayatz recorded that it had become known that Mr. F. D. Roosevelt had been elected President of the United States for the fourth time. The previous day's diary entry — written on US election day, 21 Marcheshvan / 7 November 1944 — had noted the day's significance.

title_en: Rayatz sends congratulatory letter to President Roosevelt
summary_en: On 23 Marcheshvan 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz drafted a letter of blessing to President Roosevelt on his re-election and asked R. Nissan Mindel to translate it into English.
story_body: On 23 Marcheshvan 5705 (9 November 1944), although feeling unwell, the Rebbe Rayatz composed a letter of blessing to the newly re-elected President Roosevelt. He gave the draft to Nissan Mindel to translate into English so that it could be sent in the language of the country.

title_en: Yahrzeit of Rebbetzin Yocheved bat Leah
summary_en: The Rebbe Rayatz's mother-in-law, Rebbetzin Yocheved bat Leah, passed away on 16 Marcheshvan 5680.
story_body: The 5705 diary records that 16 Marcheshvan was the yahrzeit of the Rebbe Rayatz's mother-in-law, Rebbetzin Yocheved bat Leah, who passed away on 16 Marcheshvan 5680 (9 November 1919). The Rebbe marked the day by preparing a Yiddish maamar on 'Hayta li dim'ati' for the Kriah V'Kedushah journal.

title_en: Birth of Rebbetzin Sheina, daughter of Rebbe Rayatz
summary_en: Rebbetzin Sheina, youngest daughter of the Rebbe Rayatz, was born on the night of Shabbat Shemot, 21 Tevet 5664.
story_body: The 5705 Motzaei Shabbat Shemot diary entry records the birth of the Rebbe Rayatz's daughter Sheina forty-one years earlier, on the night of Shabbat Kodesh Shemot 5664 (January 1904), at the twelfth hour of the night. The Rebbe spent three hours that night reconstructing every detail of her birth in his memory, then wept over not knowing where Sheina and her husband Menachem Mendel — son of his cousin Chaya Mushka — then were, and prayed for their safety among the rest of Israel.

title_en: Maamar Mai Chanukah written for Kriah V'Kedushah Kislev issue
summary_en: On 15 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz wrote the maamar 'Mai Chanukah' for the delayed Kislev issue of the Yiddish journal Kriah V'Kedushah.
story_body: Because of the Rebbe Rayatz's illness, the monthly Yiddish journal Kriah V'Kedushah had not appeared during Kislev. On Sunday 15 Tevet 5705 he wrote the maamar 'Mai Chanukah' for the Kislev issue and sent it to Mr. L. The Tevet issue maamar, 'Ki Ner Mitzvah V'Torah Or,' followed the next day, 16 Tevet.

title_en: Editing of Likkutei Dibburim from 5700 begun
summary_en: On 17 Tevet 5705, at his son-in-law Ramash's prompting, the Rebbe Rayatz began reviewing his 5700 sichot starting from his arrival in America, in preparation for printing.
story_body: On 17 Tevet 5705 (2 January 1945) the Rebbe Rayatz began going through transcripts of sichot from 5700, starting from the day of his arrival in the United States, in order to prepare them for publication. The project — eventually published as part of Likkutei Dibburim — was undertaken at the urging of his son-in-law Ramash (the future Rebbe).

title_en: Pledge of $8,000 to print Tzemach Tzedek
summary_en: On 19 Tevet 5705 Mr. Elchanan Glazer pledged $8,000 in his ailing father's name toward the printing of the Tzemach Tzedek's writings.
story_body: On 19 Tevet 5705 (4 January 1945) the Rebbe Rayatz received Mr. Elchanan Glazer, whose father Mr. Yisrael Glazer was ill. He promised to give $8,000 — the estimated cost of printing the Tzemach Tzedek's works — toward that project. The Rebbe prayed that the pledge would quickly come to fruition.

title_en: Chevrei Adei-Ad organization launched
summary_en: On 22 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz drafted founding letters for the Chevrei Adei-Ad institution and invited rabbis Silver, Dushavitz and Telushkin to join its Torah council.
story_body: On 22 Tevet 5705 (7 January 1945) the Rebbe Rayatz prepared the founding letters for the new institution Chevrei Adei-Ad: a general circular announcing its establishment, a supplementary letter to Rabbi Mordechai Mentlik regarding the administrative board, and individual letters to Rabbis Silver, Dushavitz and Telushkin inviting them to serve on its Torah council.

title_en: Rayatz receives Massechet Chagigah at Machaneh Israel Siyum HaShas
summary_en: At the Siyum HaShas of Machaneh Israel held the night of 23 Tevet 5705, the Rebbe Rayatz took Tractate Chagigah as his portion in the chalukat haShas.
story_body: On Tuesday 24 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz recorded that, at the previous night's chalukat haShas of Machaneh Israel, he had taken Massechet Chagigah as his portion. He prayed that God enlighten his eyes and heart in Torah and bless his work in all Torah and charitable institutions, despite the cold and head pains he was then suffering.

title_en: Reception of Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kramer of Montreal Tomchei Tmimim
summary_en: On 22 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz received Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kramer, principal of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim in Montreal, who reported on the state of the yeshivah and its branches.
story_body: On the evening of 22 Tevet 5705 the Rebbe Rayatz received Rabbi Aryeh Leib Kramer, principal of Yeshivat Tomchei Tmimim Lubavitch in Montreal and its branch ketanot yeshivot. Kramer reported in detail on the yeshivah's physical and spiritual state, and the Rebbe urged him to establish Beit Rivka, a school for girls aged 15–18 to be trained as teachers, alongside Beit Sarah for younger girls.

title_en: Wedding of Chava, daughter of Rabbi Y. Jacobson
summary_en: The wedding of Chava (daughter of Rabbi Y. Jacobson) took place on 5 Kislev 5709 with a classic chassidic celebration.
story_body: On 5 Kislev 5709, the daughter of Rabbi Yaakov Yehuda Jacobson was married. The Rebbe Rayatz's daughter Chana attended and described it as a genuine first-class chassidic simcha, with men and women dancing in two separate halls and the Tomchei Tmimim students enlivening the celebration with love and friendship.

title_en: Aaron Dingol of The Day reports on Chabad refugee work in Paris
summary_en: Mr. Dingol, editor of The Day newspaper, reported to Rebbe Rayatz on his tour of European refugee centers, noting Chabad's prominent role.
story_body: On 9 Tevet 5709, Mr. Aaron Dingol, editor of the Yiddish daily Der Tog, visited Rebbe Rayatz and reported on his tour of post-war refugee camps. He described how most rabbis, shochtim and teachers there were affiliated with Lubavitch, and detailed the orderly Chabad institutions in Paris including Bais Rivka and Bais Sara schools serving Lubavitch refugees.

title_en: Klausenberger Rebbe asks Rayatz how to relate to Israel's declaration
summary_en: The Klausenberger Rebbe inquired in the name of Agudas HaAdmorim how to respond to the proclamation of the State of Israel.
story_body: On 17 Shevat 5709, the Klausenberger Rebbe approached Rebbe Rayatz on behalf of Agudas HaAdmorim with the question of how the Rebbes should relate to the recent declaration of the State of Israel. Rayatz replied that the matter was very serious and would have to be resolved by the senior Rebbes, and that he would give his opinion only after receiving their written, signed question.

title_en: Mr. Palmer reports on visit to Paris and Eretz Yisrael refugee camps
summary_en: Mr. Palmer delivered a detailed multi-hour report on his fact-finding mission to Chabad communities and refugee camps.
story_body: On 17–18 Shevat 5709, Mr. Palmer (R.Ch.S.) presented Rebbe Rayatz with a lengthy report (six to nine hours over two days) on his visit to Chabad communities in Paris and refugee camps in Eretz Yisrael. He expressed amazement at the state of hiskashrus among anash, and Mr. Broida marveled at the closeness shown to children and at the diligent learning of the Tomchei Tmimim students.

title_en: Eight Tmimim approved to train as shochtim under R. Gordon
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz approved a list of eight Tmimim to study shechita knife-setting under shochet Rabbi Gordon.
story_body: On 23 Shevat 5709, Rebbe Rayatz recorded the names of eight Tomchei Tmimim students approved to study the craft of setting the shechita knife under shochet Rabbi Gordon at a cost of $25 per student, meeting daily at 4pm. The Rebbe arranged loans through his sons-in-law for the purchase of knives and sharpening stones, blessing the students that they should become skilled and disseminate proper chinuch in their future posts.

title_en: Rabbi Raichik dispatched as shliach to central locations
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz gave Rabbi Raichik and his wife a blessing for their shlichus, with arrangements made by Rabbi M.M. Schneerson.
story_body: On 23 Shevat 5709, Rebbe Rayatz blessed Rabbi Raichik and his wife for their journey on shlichus. The terms of his work were arranged by the Rebbe's son-in-law Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson (the future Rebbe), who organized his deployment to central locations.

title_en: Rayatz sends blessing letter to Shanghai refugees bound for Israel
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Adar, Rebbe Rayatz sent a blessing letter to Chabad refugees traveling from Shanghai to Eretz Yisrael via the US.
story_body: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5709, Rebbe Rayatz dispatched a letter of blessing to Chabad refugees traveling from Shanghai to Eretz Yisrael via America. The letter was drafted on the suggestion of his son-in-law Rabbi M.M. Schneerson and delivered through Rabbi Ashkenazi and Rabbi Chadakov. Rabbi Chadakov later reported that the emissaries and letter generated great emotional impact and brought hearts closer.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz becomes a citizen of the United States
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz was sworn in as a US citizen at his home in Brooklyn before Judges Reifel and Kleinfeld.
story_body: On Thursday 16 Adar 5709 (parashas Ki Sisa), Rebbe Rayatz became a citizen of the United States. The ceremony took place at his home with Judges Reifel and Kleinfeld officiating, witnessed by Rabbi Kazarnovsky, attorney Yekusiel Kramer, and Rabbi Chadakov; the proceedings were organized by his son-in-law the future Rebbe. The Rebbe expressed hope that the citizenship would bring health and success to him, his family, and his work in spreading Chassidus and strengthening Judaism.

title_en: Rayatz writes Henry Morgenthau requesting aid for Chabad aliyah colonies
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Henry Morgenthau seeking £100,000 to settle 100 Chabad refugee families in Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: On 6 Nissan 5709, Rebbe Rayatz wrote to Mr. Henry Morgenthau requesting that £100,000 (Eretz Yisrael pounds) be allocated to establish colonies for 100 Chabad refugee families, with £2,000 needed per family. Half would come from local Israeli institutions on the guarantee of Zalman Shazar (Rubashov), and half from Agudas Chassidei Chabad. The letter was composed in Hebrew by the future Rebbe and translated to English by Mr. Mindel.

title_en: Morgen Zhurnal article on R. Gorodetzky's Paris refugee work
summary_en: The Morgen Zhurnal newspaper published an article on Rabbi Benjamin Gorodetzky's refugee work outside Paris.
story_body: On 27 Sivan 5709, the Morgen Zhurnal carried an article about the work of Rabbi Benjamin Gorodetzky in Paris arranging temporary housing for refugees in special homes around Paris and organizing their emigration to Eretz Yisrael and other countries. His operation included partnership with the Joint Distribution Committee for refugee resettlement.

title_en: Rashag returns to New York from Eretz Yisrael via Paris
summary_en: Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law Rashag flew in from Paris after visiting Eretz Yisrael, praising the spiritual state of anash.
story_body: On 7 Tammuz 5709 at 5pm, Rebbe Rayatz's son-in-law Rabbi Shmaryahu Gurary (Rashag) arrived by airplane from Paris on his return from Eretz Yisrael. He extolled the spiritual state of anash in general and the refugees in particular, expressing astonishment at their devotion to Chassidus and to avodas hatefillah.

title_en: Yud-Beis Tammuz farbrengen marking entry into Rayatz's 70th year
summary_en: A Yud-Beis Tammuz Chag HaGeulah farbrengen took place marking the start of Rebbe Rayatz's 70th year.
story_body: On 14 Tammuz 5709 at 6pm, a farbrengen was held in honor of the Chag HaGeulah and Rebbe Rayatz's entry into his 70th year. The Rebbe delivered an extended sicha — over an hour long — on avodah, the ways of Chassidus, and avodas hatefillah, and recorded that he would later arrange it in writing.

title_en: R. Avraham David Lavut, Rabbi of Nikolayev, passes away
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham David Lavut, Rabbi of Nikolayev, passed away in 5650, having designated his grandson to succeed him.
story_body: In 5650 (1890), Rabbi Avraham David Lavut, who had served as Rabbi of Nikolayev, passed away. Before his passing he instructed the heads of the community that his grandson Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky should fill his place. Yanovsky thereupon assumed the Nikolayev rabbinate, a post he would hold until his own passing in 5693.

title_en: R. Meir Shlomo Yanovsky becomes Rabbi of Nikolayev
summary_en: Rabbi M.S. Yanovsky, grandfather of the Rebbe, assumed the Nikolayev rabbinate in 5650.
story_body: In 5650 (1890), Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky succeeded his grandfather Rabbi Avraham David Lavut as Rabbi of Nikolayev, on Lavut's deathbed instruction. He held the position until his death on 23 Elul 5693 (1933), after which his son-in-law Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (uncle of the Rebbe) succeeded him.

title_en: Marriage of R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson and Rebbetzin Chana
summary_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Rebbe, married Rebbetzin Chana in summer 5660.
story_body: In the summer of 5660 (1900), Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Rebbe, was married to Rebbetzin Chana (Yanovsky). The date is documented in a letter of Rebbe Rashab (Igros Kodesh vol. 3, letter 656). It is suggested that during the years 5658–5660 he may have briefly studied at Lubavitch.

title_en: R. Levi Yitzchak Schneerson appointed Rabbi of Yekaterinoslav
summary_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was accepted as Rabbi of Yekaterinoslav in 5669, when the Rebbe was seven years old.
story_body: In 5669 (1908–1909), Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Rebbe, was accepted as Rabbi of Yekaterinoslav. The Rebbe, born in Nikolayev, was seven years old at the time of the move. In subsequent years he would travel back to Nikolayev at the end of each summer to stay several weeks with his maternal grandparents.

title_en: R. Meir Shlomo Yanovsky writes pre-Rosh Hashanah letter to grandchildren
summary_en: Rabbi M.S. Yanovsky and his wife Rachel wrote a Rosh Hashanah blessing letter from Nikolayev to their grandchildren in Riga.
story_body: On 24 Elul 5690 (Sept. 17, 1930), Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky and Rebbetzin Rachel wrote from Nikolayev to their grandchildren — the future Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, and Rebbetzin's brother Yisrael Aryeh Leib. They expressed longing to see them, asked for letters in return, and gave their Rosh Hashanah blessings; this was one of the last letters before Yanovsky's passing three years later.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky, Rabbi of Nikolayev
summary_en: Rabbi M.S. Yanovsky, grandfather of the Rebbe and Rabbi of Nikolayev for 43 years, passed away on 23 Elul 5693.
story_body: On 23 Elul 5693 (Sept. 14, 1933), Rabbi Meir Shlomo Yanovsky, the Rebbe's maternal grandfather and longtime Rabbi of Nikolayev, passed away. He had served the community since 5650, succeeding his grandfather Rabbi Avraham David Lavut. After his passing, his son-in-law Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (uncle of the Rebbe) succeeded him in the rabbinate.

title_en: Sefer HaTmimim first edition published
summary_en: The first edition of Sefer HaTmimim, listing alumni of Tomchei Tmimim, was published at the beginning of 5750.
story_body: At the beginning of 5750 (late 1989), the first edition of Sefer HaTmimim was published, recording students of the Lubavitch yeshiva Tomchei Tmimim. Shortly afterward additional names were uncovered from a 5670 Vaad Agudas HaTmimim membership roster, leading to a second expanded edition published in 5751 that included the previously missing names.

title_en: Aguda Tmimim membership flyer arrives at the Library
summary_en: A 5670 flyer listing the members of Vaad Aguda Tmimim was acquired by the Lubavitch Library on Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5750.
story_body: On Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5750, a flyer was brought to the Lubavitch Library showing that already in 5670 a printed list of Tmimim had been prepared. The list contained only members of the Vaad Aguda Tmimim — alumni of Tomchei Tmimim from 5657 to 5670 who had married before 14 Teves 5670 — and notably included the Rebbe's father Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson and his two brothers, prompting the Rebbe's later acknowledgment 'I have seen and thank you.'

title_en: Rabbi David Tzvi Hirsch Chen (the Radatz) passes away in Jerusalem
summary_en: The Radatz, rabbi of Chernigov and grandfather of the poet Zelda, died on 24 Kislev 5686 in Jerusalem and was buried on the Mount of Olives.
story_body: Rabbi David Tzvi Hirsch Chen, known as the Radatz, served as rabbi of Chernigov before emigrating to the Land of Israel and settling in Jerusalem. Less than a year after his aliyah he passed away on 24 Kislev 5686. He was buried on the Mount of Olives, leaving behind his daughter Rachel and granddaughter Zelda.

title_en: Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn passes away in Jerusalem
summary_en: Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn, uncle of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and rabbi of Shiroka, died on 7 Shevat 5686 in Jerusalem.
story_body: Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn was the brother of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn and served as rabbi of Shiroka before fleeing to Chernigov during the Russian Revolution. He later made aliyah with his father-in-law the Radatz but died on 7 Shevat 5686 in Jerusalem, less than a year after arriving. He was buried on the Mount of Olives, survived by his wife Rachel and daughter Zelda.

title_en: Rayatz writes condolence letter on the passing of Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn
summary_en: The Rayatz wrote a letter of consolation from Leningrad on 4 Iyar 5686 to Rebbetzin Rachel Schneersohn after her husband's passing.
story_body: Upon learning of the death of his relative Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn, the Rayatz wrote a condolence letter on 4 Iyar 5686 to the widow Rebbetzin Rachel. He noted that he had not shared the news with his mother Rebbetzin Shterna Sarah to spare her grief, and offered prayers and blessings for the family's wellbeing.

title_en: Levi Yitzchak and Chana Schneersohn write to Rachel Schneersohn after Rebbe's wedding
summary_en: In Adar I 5689 Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and Rebbetzin Chana wrote from Dnepropetrovsk to their sister-in-law Rachel acknowledging her mazel tov for the Rebbe's wedding.
story_body: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneersohn and Rebbetzin Chana wrote from Dnepropetrovsk (Yekaterinoslav) in Adar I 5689, thanking Rachel and Zelda for their congratulations on the wedding of their son the Rebbe. Levi Yitzchak explained that they had been unable to attend the wedding for various reasons and described arranging financial support to be sent to Rachel through Rabbi Lakshin.

title_en: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn writes from Nikolaev on erev Yom Kippur
summary_en: On erev Yom Kippur 5694 Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn of Nikolaev wrote to Rachel Schneersohn mentioning the recent passing of his father-in-law.
story_body: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, rabbi of Nikolaev and uncle of Zelda, wrote on erev Yom Kippur 5694 to his relative Rachel. He shared that his father-in-law had passed away one week before Rosh Hashanah of that year and offered New Year blessings for her and her daughter Zelda.

title_en: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn visits his mother's grave in Kiev
summary_en: Around Parshat HaChodesh 5694 Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn wrote from Nikolaev describing a recent pilgrimage to his mother's grave in Kiev.
story_body: In a letter dated erev Shabbat Parshat HaChodesh 5694, Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn told Rachel that he had recently visited and prayed at his mother's grave in Kiev. He noted that his mother's yahrzeit had just passed and asked her merit to protect the family.

title_en: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin flee Paris on erev Shavuot
summary_en: On erev Shavuot 5700 the Rebbe and Rebbetzin fled Paris for Vichy as the Nazis advanced into France.
story_body: With Nazi forces overrunning France, the Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka escaped from Paris on erev Shavuot 5700. They traveled to Vichy where they remained for several months attempting to secure American immigration papers. The flight began a year of wandering across France that would not end until their arrival in New York in Sivan 5701.

title_en: Rayatz sends telegram to Barcelona about Schneersohn rescue file
summary_en: In late Shevat 5701 the Rayatz cabled Barcelona from Brooklyn asking what more could be done to expedite the Schneersohn rescue file.
story_body: As efforts to extract his son-in-law the Rebbe from France dragged on, the Rayatz sent a telegram from Brooklyn to Barcelona in late Shevat 5701. He requested detailed information about what additional steps were needed to advance the Schneersohn file. A parallel telegram was sent to Marseille at the same time.

title_en: Rayatz sends follow-up telegram to Barcelona on Schneersohn file
summary_en: In early Adar 5701 the Rayatz sent a second telegram from Brooklyn to Barcelona requesting an update on the status of the Schneersohn file.
story_body: Continuing his frantic efforts to free the Rebbe from Nazi-occupied Europe, the Rayatz sent another telegram from Brooklyn to Barcelona in early Adar 5701. The cable simply requested the current status of the Schneersohn rescue file. These telegrams reflect the extraordinary length of the bureaucratic process that ultimately led to the Rebbe's escape.

title_en: US Embassy in Marseille confirms passage from Lisbon to New York
summary_en: On 21 Adar 5701 the American Embassy in Marseille confirmed it had arranged travel for Menachem Mendel and Chaya Mushka Schneersohn from Lisbon to New York.
story_body: After months of effort, the American Embassy in Marseille notified the Schneersohns on March 20, 1941 (21 Adar 5701) that its Lisbon office had arranged their passage from Lisbon to New York no later than July 15, 1941. An advance payment of 840 US dollars was required and the cable was transmitted from Lisbon four days later on March 24.

title_en: The Rebbe and Rebbetzin arrive in New York
summary_en: On 28 Sivan 5701 the Rebbe and Rebbetzin reached New York after their year-long flight from Nazi-occupied Europe.
story_body: After fleeing Paris in June 1940, spending months in Vichy, Nice and Marseille obtaining papers, and crossing through Lisbon, the Rebbe and Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka arrived safely in New York on 28 Sivan 5701. Their arrival concluded a perilous year-long escape from Europe coordinated by the Rayatz through American diplomats and rescue networks. The date is commemorated annually in Chabad as a day of gratitude.

title_en: Israel Aryeh Leib Schneersohn writes to his mother after her arrival in the US
summary_en: On 4 Tammuz 5707 the Rebbe's brother Israel Aryeh Leib wrote to his mother Chana after she escaped the Soviet Union and reached the United States.
story_body: Following the dramatic rescue of Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn from the Soviet Union and her arrival in the United States in summer 5707, her younger son Israel Aryeh Leib wrote her a warm letter on 4 Tammuz 5707. He expressed relief that her ordeal of waiting and travel had ended and asked after her health and her injured leg. He sent photographs of his daughter Dalia and looked forward to a reunion with his mother and brother.

title_en: Israel Aryeh Leib Schneersohn passes away
summary_en: The Rebbe's younger brother Israel Aryeh Leib Schneersohn passed away on 13 Iyar 5712.
story_body: Israel Aryeh Leib Schneersohn, the Rebbe's younger brother, passed away on 13 Iyar 5712. His death was concealed from his mother Rebbetzin Chana out of concern that the news would harm her health. For the next twelve years the Rebbe personally added a few lines signed 'Leib' to the bottom of letters his sister-in-law Gania sent to Rebbetzin Chana to maintain the disguise.

title_en: Anash of Jerusalem petition the Rebbe to visit Israel
summary_en: In Iyar 5713 Chabad chassidim in Jerusalem signed a formal petition pleading with the Rebbe to visit the Holy Land.
story_body: In Iyar 5713 the community of Anash in Jerusalem composed and signed a heartfelt petition imploring the Rebbe to make a visit to the Land of Israel. Citing the historic bond between Rebbe and chassid and noting that only a select few could afford to travel to Brooklyn, they begged him to come strengthen the community and its institutions in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, Lod, Safed and elsewhere. Roughly three hundred signatures from across Israel and France were collected in total.

title_en: Rabbi Alexander Yudasin and Tel Aviv shul gabbaim petition the Rebbe
summary_en: On erev Shabbat 9 Iyar 5713 Rabbi Alexander Yudasin and the gabbaim of several Tel Aviv synagogues signed a letter inviting the Rebbe to visit Israel.
story_body: Rabbi Alexander Yudasin, former head of the Krivoy Rog beis din, joined with gabbaim of the Chabad shul, Beis Hamedrash Perushim in Neve Tzedek, the Shas chevra, Kahal Chassidim in Neve Shalom and other Tel Aviv synagogues in signing a petition to the Rebbe on 9 Iyar 5713. They pleaded for him to visit the Holy Land to illuminate the present era, invoking the Talmudic blessing 'blessed is your coming in peace.'

title_en: Anash of France petition the Rebbe to visit
summary_en: Chabad chassidim in France submitted a petition asking the Rebbe to visit, received by the Rebbe on 12 Tammuz 5713.
story_body: Anash in France, many of them refugees who had escaped the Iron Curtain, submitted a petition begging the Rebbe to travel abroad to visit them. They wrote that most chassidim of the past several decades knew the Rebbe only through hearsay and pleaded for a face-to-face encounter. The Rebbe noted in his own handwriting that the petition was received on 12 Tammuz 5713.

title_en: Rebbe responds to invitations to visit Israel and France
summary_en: On 13 Elul 5713 the Rebbe wrote a formal response to the invitations from Anash, citing concealments preventing the visit.
story_body: Responding to the petitions of Anash in Israel and France, the Rebbe wrote on 13 Elul 5713 acknowledging their invitation to visit. He explained that material and spiritual concealments and obstacles prevented him from fulfilling the desired visit, and prayed that God would remove them so they could meet in abundance of joy. He enclosed the newly published Kuntres for Chai Elul and offered blessings for the new year. The response was published in Igrot Kodesh vol. 7.

title_en: Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn passes away
summary_en: Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn, mother of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 6 Tishrei 5725.
story_body: Rebbetzin Chana Schneersohn, mother of the Lubavitcher Rebbe and widow of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, passed away on 6 Tishrei 5725. With her death ended the twelve-year concealment of her younger son Israel Aryeh Leib's earlier passing, which had been hidden from her to protect her health.

title_en: Rebbe writes to Zelda about her mother's tombstone inscription
summary_en: On 9 Shevat 5725 the Rebbe wrote to the poet Zelda regarding the inscription for her mother Rachel's tombstone.
story_body: Following the passing of Rebbetzin Rachel Schneersohn in 5725, the Rebbe wrote on 9 Shevat 5725 to her daughter, the poet Zelda Mishkovsky, regarding the wording of the matzeva. The letter was later published in Igrot Kodesh vol. 23, letter 8934.

title_en: Rebbe writes condolence letter to Zelda upon her husband's passing
summary_en: On 21 Menachem Av 5730 the Rebbe wrote a letter of consolation to Zelda following the death of her husband Chaim Mishkovsky.
story_body: After the passing of Chaim Mishkovsky in 5730, the Rebbe wrote a letter of consolation to his widow Zelda on 21 Menachem Av of that year. In the letter the Rebbe expressed personal interest in every detail of how she would arrange her life going forward, noting that only a few remained of their family in this generation. The letter was published in Igrot Kodesh vol. 26, letter 9955.

title_en: The poet Zelda Mishkovsky-Schneersohn passes away
summary_en: Zelda Schneersohn Mishkovsky, the celebrated Hebrew poet and cousin of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, passed away on 27 Nissan 5744.
story_body: Zelda Schneersohn Mishkovsky, the renowned Hebrew poet and only child of Rabbi Shalom Shlomo Schneersohn and Rachel Chen, passed away on 27 Nissan 5744. Childless, her literary estate including correspondence from the Rebbe and his father Rabbi Levi Yitzchak was scattered after her death. Years later, photocopies of these family letters were transmitted to the Chabad library.

title_en: Rebbe launches Mivtza Tefillin during Six-Day War
summary_en: In Iyar 5727 the Lubavitcher Rebbe announced the worldwide Mivtza Tefillin campaign in connection with the Six-Day War and the ensuing victory.
story_body: In Iyar 5727 (May 1967), in the lead-up to and aftermath of the Six-Day War, the Rebbe declared Mivtza Tefillin — a global initiative urging volunteers to help Jewish men, including many entirely unaffiliated, don tefillin. The campaign quickly became one of the Rebbe's signature mivtzaim, but also drew halachic and ideological questions from various rabbinic circles over the summer of 5727.

title_en: Rebbe defends Mivtza Tefillin at Shabbat Bereishit 5728 farbrengen
summary_en: At the Shabbat Bereishit 5728 farbrengen the Rebbe systematically answered the questions and objections raised against Mivtza Tefillin.
story_body: After receiving numerous queries and challenges to Mivtza Tefillin during the summer, the Rebbe devoted his Shabbat Bereishit 5728 farbrengen (Oct 28, 1967) to addressing them publicly. The edited sicha was printed as its own kuntres opening 'בהיות שהגיעו אלי כמה שאלות וטענות בנוגע לההתעוררות דמבצע תפלין' and was later reprinted in Likkutei Sichot vol. 6 p. 271ff.

title_en: Rebbe responds to Agudat Yisrael attack on Lubavitch
summary_en: At his Shabbat Toldot 5728 farbrengen the Rebbe responded to a speaker at the Agudat Yisrael annual convention who attacked him and Lubavitch.
story_body: Around the time of the annual Agudat Yisrael leadership convention, one of the speakers publicly attacked the Rebbe and the Lubavitch movement, drawing a comparison to Yitzchak Avinu who loved Esav 'because there was trapping in his mouth.' The Rebbe responded at the Shabbat Toldot 5728 farbrengen (Dec 2, 1967) and at subsequent gatherings, as later published in Sichot Kodesh p. 179ff.

title_en: Rabbi Yitzchak Hutner writes Rebbe questioning Mivtza Tefillin halacha
summary_en: Rabbi Yitzchak Hutner wrote the Rebbe arguing that Mivtza Tefillin volunteers must tell recipients that parshiyot lie inside the batim, else it is mit'asek.
story_body: After reading the Rebbe's Shabbat Bereishit kuntres, Rabbi Yitzchak Hutner — Rosh Yeshiva of Chaim Berlin and author of Pachad Yitzchak — sent his first letter to the Rebbe on Or L'Yom Bet of Parshat Vayeshev 5728. Citing the Ra'ah on one who eats matzah without knowing it is matzah, he argued that many 'tinokot shenishbu' approached by mivtza volunteers had no idea anything was inside the batim, and that without such knowledge the act constituted mit'asek rather than fulfillment of the mitzvah.

title_en: Rabbi Hutner sends apology letter after Agudat Yisrael convention reports
summary_en: Hearing of the Agudat Yisrael convention attack on the Rebbe, Rabbi Hutner wrote to clarify he had not attended and to apologize if his earlier letter caused pain.
story_body: On Yom Rishon of Parshat Vayechi 5728 (Jan 7, 1968), Rabbi Hutner wrote a second letter to the Rebbe after hearing from Rabbi Zalman Gurary about the recent Agudat Yisrael convention and its attacks on the Rebbe. He stressed that he had never attended any such convention, that his earlier halachic letter was strictly private and personal, and asked forgiveness if it had caused any pain — while noting that the Torah content itself was not subject to retraction.

title_en: Rabbi Hutner asks Rebbe to clarify objection to his first letter
summary_en: Concerned by the Rebbe's silence, Rabbi Hutner sent a brief note on 16 Tevet 5728 asking him to identify the precise nature of any objection.
story_body: On 16 Tevet 5728 (Jan 17, 1968), Rabbi Hutner sent a very short third letter to the Rebbe, asking that he do him the kindness of pointing out the nekudat ha-hakpadah — the precise point of objection — to his original Mivtza Tefillin letter. This brief note appears to have prompted the Rebbe's lengthy detailed reply two days later.

title_en: Rebbe sends detailed halachic reply to Rabbi Hutner on tefillin
summary_en: On Erev Shabbat 18 Tevet 5728 the Rebbe wrote a lengthy halachic reply to Rabbi Hutner rejecting the mit'asek concern.
story_body: On Erev Shabbat 18 Tevet 5728 (Jan 19, 1968), the Rebbe wrote his major reply in the exchange, drafting it by hand directly on Rabbi Hutner's letter. He marshaled counter-proofs from tefilah (the Rambam's 'as if standing before the Shechinah'), korbanot, etrog and matzah, arguing that 'ein la-davar sof' if one demands knowledge of every halachic detail, and that general awareness of tefillin as a special mitzvah-object suffices. The handwritten draft was typed by the mazkirut and re-edited again in the Rebbe's own hand.

title_en: Rabbi Hutner replies restating his halachic position to Rebbe
summary_en: On Thursday of Parshat Va'era 5728 Rabbi Hutner thanked the Rebbe but insisted that absent knowledge of the parshiyot, Mivtza Tefillin recipients are mit'asek.
story_body: On Yom Hamishi of Parshat Va'era 5728 (Jan 25, 1968), Rabbi Hutner wrote back, opening with thanks for the Rebbe's reply but maintaining his original position. He insisted his argument was ikar ha-din and not a mere chashash, brought further proofs from Responsa Rabbi Akiva Eiger §8, the Chavat Daat, and Tosafot Shabbat 11, and concluded that without awareness of the parshiyot the brachah would be in vain.

title_en: Rebbe sends second halachic reply to Rabbi Hutner on tefillin
summary_en: On 8 Shevat 5728 the Rebbe wrote his second reply to Rabbi Hutner, distinguishing mistaken knowledge from absence of knowledge.
story_body: On 8 Shevat 5728 (Feb 7, 1968), the Rebbe responded a second time, opening by noting that Rabbi Hutner had not addressed his core proofs from tefilah and korban. He drew a sharp distinction between mistaken knowledge ('kasavur she'hu basar') as in the Shulchan Aruch HaRav on matzah, versus mere absence of knowledge, and added new chiddushim from the Alter Rebbe's pesakim on tefillin.

title_en: Rabbi Hutner sends third letter defending his position to Rebbe
summary_en: On 13 Shevat 5728 Rabbi Hutner sent his third and final letter, restating his arguments and adding a story about tinokot shenishbu extending both hands.
story_body: On 13 Shevat 5728 (Feb 12, 1968), Rabbi Hutner sent his third reply, opening with thanks for 'a second utterance' from the Rebbe while reiterating his prior reservations. He elaborated his mit'asek argument with proofs from Rabbi Akiva Eiger §8, the Chavat Daat, the Alter Rebbe's Kuntres Acharon on safek p'sik reisha, and Tosafot Shabbat 11. In a postscript he relayed Rabbi Zalmanov's recent report of seeing tinokot shenishbu offering both hands for tefillin — illustrating, in his view, how complete their unfamiliarity could be.

title_en: Rebbe's 70th birthday marked by greetings from Israeli leaders
summary_en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson reached the age of seventy on 11 Nissan 5732, drawing greetings from leading rabbis, government ministers, Knesset members, generals, and public figures in Israel.
story_body: On 11 Nissan 5732 (25 April 1972), the Rebbe turned seventy, an occasion that drew formal written blessings from across Israeli society. Greeters included President Zalman Shazar, Rabbis Ovadia Yosef, Shlomo Goren and Moshe Zvi Neria, Foreign Minister Abba Eban, Minister Shimon Peres, Religious Affairs Minister Zerach Warhaftig, IDF Chief of Staff David Elazar, Generals Ariel Sharon and Rechavam Zeevi, Jerusalem Mayor Teddy Kollek, future President Ephraim Katzir, and poets Avraham Shlonsky and Uri Tzvi Greenberg. The collected blessings were assembled into 'Sefer HaBrachot LiShnat HaShivim' (The Book of Blessings for the Year of Seventy).

title_en: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar born in Fez
summary_en: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, future head of the rabbis of Fez, was born in Fez (5415).
story_body: Yehuda ibn Attar was born in Fez (פאס) in the Hebrew year 5415 (1655). He would become the leading halachic authority of Moroccan Jewry, known by Moroccan Jews as 'Arbi Alkabir' (Our Great Rabbi). His family pedigree traced through generations of Fez scholars: his father R. Yaakov, grandfather R. Avraham, and great-grandfather R. Yaakov.

title_en: Marriage of Shi'acha bat Yehuda ibn Attar to Shem Tov ben Avraham
summary_en: Shi'acha, daughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, married her cousin Shem Tov ben Avraham in Fez on 17 Cheshvan 5472.
story_body: On Friday, 17 Cheshvan 5472 (Nov 7, 1711), Shi'acha bat Yehuda ibn Attar married Shem Tov, son of her uncle Avraham ibn Attar, in Fez. The wedding was recorded in the marriage register of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Ya'abetz). The match kept the ibn Attar family lineage close, with Shi'acha marrying her first cousin.

title_en: Marriage of R. Shmuel ben Yosef ibn Attar
summary_en: R. Shmuel, son of Yosef ibn Attar (brother of Rabbi Yehuda), was married on 26 Cheshvan 5473 in Fez.
story_body: On Friday, 26 Cheshvan 5473 (Nov 5, 1712), Shmuel ben Yosef ibn Attar — a nephew of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar — was married. The event was registered in Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur's marriage records. This entry reveals that Rabbi Yehuda had a previously unrecorded brother named Yosef who had three sons: Shmuel, Yaakov, and Yitzchak.

title_en: Marriage of Rivka bat Oved ibn Attar to Shmuel ben Nachmosh
summary_en: Rivka, granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, married Shmuel ben Nachmosh ben Mayara on 17 Kislev 5473.
story_body: On Friday, 17 Kislev 5473 (Dec 6, 1712), Rivka bat Oved — a granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar through his son Oved — was married to Shmuel ben Nachmosh of the Mayara family in Fez. The marriage was registered in the records of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Ya'abetz).

title_en: Marriage of Miriam bat Yaakov ibn Attar
summary_en: Miriam, daughter of R. Yaakov (Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar's nephew), was married on 20 Tevet 5478.
story_body: On 20 Tevet 5478 (Jan 12, 1718), Miriam bat Yaakov ben Yosef ibn Attar was married. The match was recorded in the Ya'abetz's marriage register. Yaakov was a son of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar's brother Yosef, making Miriam a grandniece of the head rabbi of Fez.

title_en: Letter on drought and tax oppression in Fez community
summary_en: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar wrote to Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur in 5485 lamenting severe drought and oppressive tax extraction from the Fez community.
story_body: In the year 5485 (1725), Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar wrote anguished letters to Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur, then serving as rabbi in Meknes. He described the dire situation in Fez: severe drought, Torah scholars imprisoned by the local governor for three days over debts, and a punishing communal tax of 500 ounces per seventy households in the Mellah. He wrote in tears, fearing violence between debtors and oppressors.

title_en: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar adjudicates dilapidated property dispute
summary_en: On 25 Tammuz 5486, Rabbi Yehuda of Fez wrote to the Meknes beit din about an endangered building requiring urgent demolition and rebuilding.
story_body: On 25 Tammuz 5486 (July 25, 1726), Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar wrote from Fez to the rabbis and leaders of Meknes regarding the case of Shlomo Ag'iani and Yosef Abuzaglu over the property known as 'Dar Mawlana' purchased from the royal court. A previous letter from him in the same period addressed an upper-story building in the 'Dar Bunfad' courtyard that had become structurally dangerous and required immediate sale or repair authorization.

title_en: Marriage of R. Yom Tov ben Yitzchak ibn Attar
summary_en: R. Yom Tov, son of Yitzchak ibn Attar, was married on 13 Adar 5491 in Fez.
story_body: On 13 Adar 5491 (~March 2, 1731), Yom Tov ben Yitzchak ibn Attar was married. The wedding was recorded in the Ya'abetz's marriage register in Fez. Yitzchak was a son of R. Yosef ibn Attar, brother of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar.

title_en: Marriage of Dona bat Oved ibn Attar to Avraham
summary_en: Dona, granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, married Avraham ben Chaim Shem Tov on 20 Elul 5491.
story_body: On 20 Elul 5491 (~September 22, 1731), Dona bat Oved ibn Attar — a granddaughter of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar — was married to Avraham, son of Chaim Shem Tov ben Avraham ibn Attar. Like her aunt Shi'acha a generation earlier, Dona married within the extended ibn Attar family. The marriage was inscribed in the Ya'abetz's register.

title_en: Second marriage of R. Oved ibn Attar, son of Rabbi Yehuda
summary_en: R. Oved ibn Attar, son of Rabbi Yehuda, took a second wife on 18 Av 5494 in Fez.
story_body: On the night of Tuesday, 18 Av 5494 (~July 19, 1734), Rabbi Oved ibn Attar — son of the late Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar — was married for the second time. The wedding entry refers to Rabbi Yehuda with the honorific 'savah de-mishpatim' (elder of judgments) and as a 'hasid,' 'light of Israel,' indicating Rabbi Yehuda had already passed away (he died in 5493).

title_en: Marriage of R. Yosef ben Yitzchak ibn Attar
summary_en: R. Yosef, son of Yitzchak ibn Attar, was married on 8 Tishri 5495 in Fez.
story_body: On 8 Tishri 5495 (~October 5, 1734), Yosef ben Yitzchak ibn Attar was married. The Ya'abetz's marriage register in Fez recorded the event. Like his brother Yom Tov who married three years earlier, Yosef was a grandnephew of the late Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar through Yehuda's brother Yosef.

title_en: Death of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar of Fez
summary_en: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, the head of Fez's rabbis known as 'Arbi Alkabir,' died in 5493 (1733).
story_body: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar passed away in the Hebrew year 5493 (1733), having served as the leading rabbinical authority of Fez and one of the most revered figures of Moroccan Jewry. Honored by Moroccan Jews as 'Arbi Alkabir' (Our Great Rabbi), he left behind a rich corpus of responsa and a network of correspondence with Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur of Meknes.

title_en: Marriage of R. Yehuda ben Oved ibn Attar, grandson of Rabbi Yehuda
summary_en: R. Yehuda ben Oved, grandson and namesake of Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar, was married on 24 Cheshvan 5516.
story_body: On Wednesday, 24 Cheshvan 5516 (~November 8, 1755), Yehuda ben Oved ibn Attar was married. He was a grandson and namesake of the renowned Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar of Fez, who had died over two decades earlier. The marriage was recorded in the Ya'abetz's register, which referred to his late grandfather as 'the great rabbi, the wondrous of the Sanhedrin, elder of judgments.'

title_en: Birth of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Yaavetz) in Meknes
summary_en: Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur, known as the Yaavetz, was born on Shabbat 27 Iyar 5433 in Meknes, Morocco.
story_body: Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur, later known as the Yaavetz and one of Morocco's preeminent halachic authorities, was born on Shabbat, 27 Iyar 5433 (May 1673), in Meknes. He was the son of Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur. Strikingly, on the day of his circumcision (5 Sivan 5433) the renowned Land of Israel emissary Rabbi Elisha Ashkenazi passed away in Meknes, evoking the Talmudic image of one sun rising as another sets.

title_en: Ibn Tzur family relocates from Meknes to Fez
summary_en: A 5443 book-purchase notation suggests the Yaavetz's father moved the family from Meknes to Fez when Yaakov was about ten.
story_body: Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur, father of the Yaavetz, relocated his family from Meknes to Fez during the Yaavetz's youth. A note in a 1559 Riva di Trento Mishnayot volume — now preserved in the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad — records his father purchasing it in Fez in 5443 (1683), suggesting the move took place when Yaakov was roughly ten years old. The Yaavetz would spend most of his life in Fez.

title_en: Yaavetz begins serving in a Fez synagogue as shaliach
summary_en: From 5448, the Yaavetz served as shaliach for sacred matters in a Fez synagogue, reading Torah and delivering sermons.
story_body: From 5448 (1688), the young Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur served as 'shaliach for every matter of holiness' in a Fez synagogue, including Torah reading and weekly sermons on halacha, aggadah, and ethics. His later rabbinic appointment letter (1697), preserved in the Ibn Tzur archive at the Agudat Chasidei Chabad library, lavishly praises his cantillation and preaching during these years.

title_en: Yaavetz appointed scribe of the Fez beit din at age 20
summary_en: In 5453, at age 20, the Yaavetz was appointed scribe of the Fez beit din under Rabbis Vidal Tzarfati and Menachem Serero.
story_body: In 5453 (1693), at age twenty, Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur was appointed scribe (sofer beit din) of the Fez rabbinical court led by Rabbis Vidal Tzarfati and Menachem Serero. He later recorded that during this period he visited the court rabbis two or three times daily, presenting his halachic questions and observing their adjudication. An archive document from 5459 still bears his signature with the title 'sofer.'

title_en: Fez synagogue formally installs Yaavetz as permanent rabbi
summary_en: In 5457 the members of his Fez synagogue signed a binding rabbinic appointment for the Yaavetz and his descendants in perpetuity.
story_body: In 5457 (1697) the congregation of the Yaavetz's Fez synagogue ratified a sweeping rabbinic appointment installing him as their permanent leader, with the position to pass to his descendants 'until the coming of Messiah.' The signed contract — which also turned over three Torah scrolls and the entire synagogue endowment to his discretion — is preserved in the Ibn Tzur archive at the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad.

title_en: Yaavetz elevated to dayan of Fez after Rabbi Vidal Tzarfati's death
summary_en: Following Rabbi Vidal Tzarfati's death in 5464, the Yaavetz was promoted to dayan of the Fez beit din.
story_body: After Rabbi Vidal Tzarfati's passing in 5464 (1704), Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur was appointed to fill his seat as dayan on the Fez rabbinical court. He served alongside his teacher Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar (the Maharibav) and Rabbi Shmuel Tzarfati, marking his ascension to the senior tier of Moroccan poskim. He would later author the influential responsa work Mishpat u'Tzedakah B'Yaakov.

title_en: Birth of Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, son and future successor
summary_en: Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, the Yaavetz's son and eventual successor, was born on 3 Shevat 5466.
story_body: Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur was born on Monday, 3 Shevat 5466 (January 1706) in Fez. He was one of seventeen children born to the Yaavetz, of whom only he and his brother Reuven survived their father. He would eventually inherit his father's rabbinic mantle and continue the family's marriage-registration pinkas, now preserved as MS 1605 in the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad.

title_en: Yaavetz moves from Fez to Meknes to head the community
summary_en: Between Iyar and Menachem Av 5478, the Yaavetz relocated from Fez to Meknes, where he was received as 'head and dignitary' of the community.
story_body: Between Iyar and Menachem Av of 5478 (spring–summer 1718), Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur left Fez and settled in Meknes, where the community received him as 'head and dignitary.' A 13 Menachem Av letter from Jerusalem emissary Rabbi Yom Tov Crispo expresses joy at the news of his installation. He would remain in Meknes for roughly eleven years.

title_en: Rabbi Menachem Sirero, son-in-law of the Yaavetz, dies young
summary_en: Rabbi Menachem Sirero, husband of the Yaavetz's daughter Azi Bueno, died in Cheshvan 5479 at about 26 years old.
story_body: Rabbi Menachem Sirero, son-in-law of the Yaavetz, passed away in Cheshvan 5479 (autumn 1718). Born in 5453, he was only about twenty-six. The Yaavetz had inscribed Sirero's marriage to his daughter Azi Bueno in his own hand on 8 Adar in the family marriage-records register.

title_en: Crispo dedicates 'Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah' to the Yaavetz
summary_en: On 25 Tammuz 5482 in Alexandria, Jerusalem emissary Yom Tov Crispo purchased and dedicated 'Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah' to the Yaavetz.
story_body: On 25 Tammuz 5482 (July 1722), Rabbi Yom Tov Crispo — a Jerusalem emissary returning from Morocco — purchased the volume 'Shiyarei Knesset HaGedolah' in Alexandria and inscribed it as a gift to the Yaavetz. Earlier letters from Crispo (7 and 12 Marcheshvan 5482) record that he had also sent two other rare volumes, 'She'elot u'Teshuvot Bach' and 'Ginat Veradim,' at the Yaavetz's request. Several of these volumes are today held in the Library of Agudat Chasidei Chabad.

title_en: Fez community begins effort to bring the Yaavetz back from Meknes
summary_en: During Hanukkah 5487, thirty to forty Fez community members met in Meknes and swore a commitment to bring the Yaavetz back as their rabbi.
story_body: During Hanukkah 5487 (December 1726), some thirty to forty leading members of the Fez community traveled to Meknes and committed under oath to support Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur if he would return to Fez. The agreement, which detailed financial terms and pledged unconditional obedience to his rulings, was eventually ratified in Adar Sheni 5489 once the move actually took place. The signed parchment survives in the Ibn Tzur archive at the Agudat Chasidei Chabad library.

title_en: Yaavetz returns from Meknes to Fez after eleven years
summary_en: In Adar Sheni 5489, after roughly eleven years serving in Meknes, the Yaavetz returned to Fez.
story_body: In Adar Sheni 5489 (spring 1729), after some eleven years leading the Meknes community, Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur returned to Fez. The Fez community formally re-ratified its earlier oath of support just before his arrival. His marriage-records pinkas, which had recorded 'Meknesa' as the place of entry since 5480, switches back to 'Fez' from 5489 onward.

title_en: Death of Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur, son of the Yaavetz, in Salé
summary_en: Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur, son of the Yaavetz, died around age 25 on 3 Av 5502 during Chol HaMoed in Salé.
story_body: On 3 Av 5502 (summer 1742), Rabbi Reuven ibn Tzur — son of the Yaavetz and a young scholar of about twenty-five — passed away in Salé during Chol HaMoed. Rabbi Eliyahu Tzarfati delivered a eulogy for him on 21 Av, preserved in the work 'Na'ar Bocheh.' He was buried in Alcazar (Ksar), and his death left Rabbi Refael Oved as the Yaavetz's only surviving son.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Yaavetz) in Fez
summary_en: The Yaavetz passed away on the eve of Shabbat, 2 Tevet 5513, five months shy of his eightieth birthday, and was buried 3 Tevet.
story_body: Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur — the Yaavetz, author of Mishpat u'Tzedakah B'Yaakov and one of Morocco's foremost halachic authorities — passed away on the night of Shabbat, 2 Tevet 5513 (December 1752) in Fez, just under five months before what would have been his eightieth birthday. He was buried on Sunday, 3 Tevet. His marriage-records pinkas, in continuous use since 5466, passed to his descendants who maintained it until 5617.

title_en: Death of Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, son of the Yaavetz
summary_en: Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur, the Yaavetz's son and successor, died on Friday, 19 Iyar 5529.
story_body: On Friday afternoon, 19 Iyar 5529 (May 1769), Rabbi Refael Oved ibn Tzur passed away in Fez. He had inherited his father's rabbinic mantle, served as a senior dayan, and continued the family's marriage-registration practice. His own son Rabbi Shlomo Shmuel ibn Tzur recorded the entry in the family pinkas, citing his grandfather the Yaavetz's note that Refael Oved had been born on 3 Shevat 5466.

title_en: Passing of Mitteler Rebbe (Rabbi Dovber)
summary_en: The Mitteler Rebbe passed away on 9 Kislev 5588, leaving Chabad without a confirmed successor.
story_body: On 9 Kislev 5588 (late November 1827) the Mitteler Rebbe, Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, passed away in Niezhin. His son-in-law Rabbi Menachem Mendel (the future Tzemach Tzedek) was the natural successor, but for an extended period he refused to formally accept the leadership of Chabad. During this transitional time the chassidim of the movement were unsettled about who would lead them.

title_en: R. Nathan Halevi of Polotzk urges Tzemach Tzedek to accept leadership
summary_en: Less than three months after the Mitteler Rebbe's passing, R. Nathan Halevi Horowitz of Polotzk wrote a halachic responsum to Tzemach Tzedek hinting that he should accept the nesius.
story_body: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Adar 5588 (February 1828) R. Nathan Halevi Horowitz of Polotzk sent a halachic she'eilah to Rabbi Menachem Mendel. He closed it with the unusual chassidic phrase 'prepared to obey him, desirous of his success,' and signed using his mother's name ('Nathan Halevi son of Chayena') as one would in a pidyon-nefesh to a Rebbe. The letter was thus both a halachic query and a coded plea that Tzemach Tzedek accept the leadership of Chabad.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek still refusing to accept pidyonot
summary_en: As late as Tishrei 5590 Tzemach Tzedek crossed out R. Nathan's mother's name from a responsum, signalling he was not yet receiving pidyonot.
story_body: On 8 Tishrei 5590 (October 1829) R. Nathan Halevi again signed a responsum to Tzemach Tzedek with his mother's name. Tzemach Tzedek struck the word 'Chayena' from the autograph, refusing to receive the letter as a pidyon-nefesh. A few weeks later he again deleted the honorifics 'light of our eyes' and 'his servant' from another of Nathan's letters, evidence that he had not yet fully assumed the role of Rebbe.

title_en: Lubavitch becomes the center of Chabad
summary_en: The town of Lubavitch became the worldwide center of Chabad in 5574 with the arrival of the Mitteler Rebbe.
story_body: In 5574 (1813/14) the Mitteler Rebbe established his court in Lubavitch, and the town began its 102-year run as the headquarters of the worldwide Chabad movement. Four successive Rebbes would reside there: the Mitteler Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, the Rebbe Maharash, and the Rebbe Rashab. Alongside the Rebbe the town always had its own moreh tzedek (community rabbi) for everyday halachic questions.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek begins nesius in Lubavitch
summary_en: Rabbi Menachem Mendel (the Tzemach Tzedek) began his leadership of Chabad from Lubavitch in 5588.
story_body: Following the Mitteler Rebbe's passing in late 5588, the Tzemach Tzedek eventually took up the mantle of Chabad leadership in Lubavitch. His nesius would extend until 5626 (1866). Under him Lubavitch became a major center of halachic responsa and chassidic teaching.

title_en: Rebbe Maharash begins nesius in Lubavitch
summary_en: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (Maharash) assumed Chabad leadership from Lubavitch in 5626.
story_body: After the passing of the Tzemach Tzedek in 5626 (1866), his son Rabbi Shmuel became the new Rebbe of Chabad. He continued to reside and lead from Lubavitch until his own passing in 5643 (1882). During this period R. Avraham Zeligsohn served as the town's moreh tzedek.

title_en: Rebbe Rashab begins nesius in Lubavitch
summary_en: Rabbi Sholom Dovber (Rashab) became Rebbe of Chabad in Lubavitch in 5643.
story_body: Upon the passing of the Maharash in 5643 (1882), his son Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn (Rashab) assumed leadership of Chabad. He remained in Lubavitch for the next three decades, founding the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva and corresponding extensively with the town's moreh tzedek R. Dovid Yakobson.

title_en: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz studies with MaHaRiL of Yanovich
summary_en: In 5572 the young R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz, later moreh tzedek of Lubavitch, studied under R. Yehuda Leib of Yanovich.
story_body: After marrying into a Yanovich family, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz settled there as a melamed and studied Torah with the Alter Rebbe's brother, the MaHaRiL of Yanovich, in 5572 (1812). Years later he would cite halachic teachings he heard from MaHaRiL during this period in his own responsa.

title_en: R. Shmuel Segal of Rohatchov travels to the Land of Israel
summary_en: The moreh tzedek of Rohatchov, R. Shmuel Segal, made aliyah in 5584 after obtaining a passport in Mohilev.
story_body: R. Shmuel Segal, moreh tzedek of Rohatchov, prepared for nearly a year before traveling to Eretz Yisrael in 5584 (1824). He spent several weeks in Mohilev obtaining a passport, leaving R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz and other local rabbis to handle pressing halachic questions in his absence. His departure precipitated R. Yissachar Ber's increased involvement in Rohatchov's rabbinical affairs.

title_en: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz becomes moreh tzedek of Bychov Chadash
summary_en: In 5587, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz was appointed moreh tzedek of the town of Bychov Chadash.
story_body: After several years of teaching and engaging in halachic rulings in Rohatchov, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz formally took up the moreh tzedek post in Bychov Chadash in 5587 (1827). By 27 Sivan 5587 he was writing responsa from his new post on questions such as tefillin parchment, sending them to the Tzemach Tzedek and other leading rabbis. He would remain there until his next post in Lubavitch.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek defends R. Yissachar Ber against removal in Bychov Chadash
summary_en: In 5591 townspeople of Bychov Chadash sought to replace R. Yissachar Ber, and the Tzemach Tzedek issued a sharp responsum defending him.
story_body: In 5591 (1831) residents of Bychov Chadash attempted to install a new moreh tzedek in place of R. Yissachar Ber after they brought in a relative for the position. The Tzemach Tzedek responded with a stern ruling (Yoreh Deah 343) that custom across Israel held a moreh tzedek's appointment to be permanent and that it was absolutely forbidden to remove a qualified scholar without cause. Despite this, R. Yissachar Ber left for Lubavitch within two years.

title_en: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz appointed moreh tzedek of Lubavitch
summary_en: In 5593 R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz took up the rabbinical post in Lubavitch, where he served for ten years.
story_body: After leaving Bychov Chadash in 5593 (1833), R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz established his residence in Lubavitch as the town's moreh tzedek. He served there for a decade alongside the Tzemach Tzedek, engaging in extensive halachic correspondence with the Rebbe and serving as a conduit for questions from rabbis throughout the region. Many of these responsa have since been published in Kovetz Yagdil Torah.

title_en: R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz becomes moreh tzedek of Konotop
summary_en: In 5603 R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz left Lubavitch to take up the rabbinate of Konotop, where he remained until his death.
story_body: After ten years as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch, R. Yissachar Ber Horowitz accepted the post of moreh tzedek in Konotop in 5603 (1843). He continued his halachic correspondence from there, including extensive teshuvot reflecting on his earlier years. He became known posthumously as 'the Rav of Konotop,' and the Tzemach Tzedek referred to him as such in marginal notes on his old responsa.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek's Shulchan Aruch printed in Zhitomir
summary_en: In 5616 R. Avraham haKohen of Lubavitch was among the rabbis approving the Zhitomir printing of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch.
story_body: The Lubavitch moreh tzedek R. Avraham b. Avigdor haKohen joined the approbations for the 5616 (1856) Zhitomir edition of the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch. He served as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch throughout most of the later years of the Tzemach Tzedek, occasionally co-signing responsa or signing in the Rebbe's stead.

title_en: R. Shmuel HaLevi Levin serves as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch
summary_en: By 15 Tammuz 5627 R. Shmuel b. Shlomo HaLevi Levin was serving briefly as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch.
story_body: After R. Avraham haKohen's tenure, R. Shmuel b. Shlomo Tzvi HaLevi Levin briefly served as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch. A receipt he issued to a shochet on 15 Tammuz 5627 (July 1867) preserves his title. He was nicknamed 'the Rav of Lubavitch' for the rest of his life, though his actual tenure was short, ending when R. Avraham Zeligsohn was installed in the post.

title_en: Maharash sells chametz to R. Avraham Zeligsohn
summary_en: A surviving 5634 chametz-sale document records the Maharash transferring his chametz to R. Avraham Zeligsohn before Pesach.
story_body: A document from 5634 (1874) preserves the Rebbe Maharash's sale of chametz to R. Avraham b. Yosef Zeligsohn, who served as moreh tzedek of Lubavitch throughout the Maharash era. The document is reproduced in Tikunei Mikvaot Le-Takanat Rabbeinu, p. 185.

title_en: Rashab corresponds with R. Dovid Yakobson on Lubavitch mikveh
summary_en: In 5667 the Rashab wrote at length to the Lubavitch moreh tzedek about the laws of the town's newly built mikveh.
story_body: When a new mikveh was constructed in Lubavitch in 5667 (1907), the Rashab and the town's moreh tzedek R. Dovid b. Bentzion Yakobson exchanged a series of substantial halachic letters on the laws of mikvaot. These letters are preserved in Igrot Kodesh of the Rashab, vol. 1, nos. 167-171. R. Yakobson was the son-in-law of R. Avraham Zeligsohn and had inherited the post despite his relatively young age.
