title_en: Passing of R. Shmuel HaLevi Levin in Jerusalem
summary_en: R. Shmuel HaLevi Levin, formerly moreh tzedek of Lubavitch, passed away on 18 Marcheshvan 5674 in Jerusalem.
story_body: R. Shmuel b. Shlomo Tzvi HaLevi Levin, the former Lubavitch moreh tzedek, died on 18 Marcheshvan 5674 (November 1913) in his Jerusalem home, having purchased his burial plot three years earlier. He was buried in the Old Cemetery (har hazeitim). The Kolel Chabad chevra kadisha register identifies him as 'the elder, who was called the Rav of Lubavitch.'

title_en: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz appointed second rabbi of Lubavitch
summary_en: On 23 Av 5675 the householders of Lubavitch appointed wartime refugee R. Elchanan Yakubovitz as a second rabbi alongside R. Dovid Yakobson.
story_body: When R. Elchanan b. Avraham Shimon Yakubovitz, former rosh mesivta of Telz, fled to Lubavitch during World War I, the householders of the town's two main shuls appointed him as a second rabbi on 23 Menachem Av 5675 (August 1915). The forty signatories agreed to a monthly salary of thirty rubles and authorized him to rule on routine questions in the Shliove and Lachluka street synagogues. The Rashab approved, and Yakubovitz also taught in the Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.

title_en: Rashab evacuates Lubavitch as the war front approaches
summary_en: In Marcheshvan 5676 the Rashab and his household evacuated Lubavitch ahead of the advancing front line.
story_body: As World War I drew nearer to Lubavitch, the Rashab departed the town with his family in Marcheshvan 5676 (October/November 1915), ending the 102-year period in which Lubavitch served as the worldwide capital of Chabad. The newly installed second rabbi R. Elchanan Yakubovitz also left at this time, his tenure as Lubavitch's rabbi having lasted only a few months.

title_en: Russian government certification of Lubavitch rabbinic appointment
summary_en: On 2 September 1916 Russian authorities formally certified R. Dovid Yakobson's confirmation of the 1915 rabbinical appointment letter.
story_body: More than a year after the original 23 Av 5675 Hebrew rabbinical appointment letter for R. Elchanan Yakubovitz was drafted, the document received Russian civil certification on 2 September 1916. The Lubavitch starosta endorsed it with his seal alongside R. Dovid Yakobson's signature attesting that the 40 Hebrew signatures were genuine. The delay points to the dislocations of the wartime evacuation period.

title_en: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz publishes Even Shimon
summary_en: After returning to his native Latvia in 5678, R. Elchanan Yakubovitz published the first volume of his Even Shimon in 5689.
story_body: Following his evacuation from Lubavitch and a brief tenure in Russia, R. Elchanan Yakubovitz returned to Latvia in 5678 (1918). He resumed teaching as a rosh mesivta in several yeshivot and in 5689 (1929) printed the first volume of his halachic work Even Shimon, named after his father R. Avraham Shimon.

title_en: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz emigrates to the Land of Israel
summary_en: In 5693 R. Elchanan Yakubovitz emigrated to Eretz Yisrael and settled in Jerusalem.
story_body: In 5693 (1933) R. Elchanan Yakubovitz left Latvia for Eretz Yisrael, settling in Jerusalem. There he published the second volume of Even Shimon and remained until his death. He represents one of the few Lubavitch-era rabbinical figures whose career spanned both the late Russian period and the British Mandate yishuv.

title_en: Passing of R. Elchanan Yakubovitz in Jerusalem
summary_en: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz, formerly second rabbi of Lubavitch, passed away in Jerusalem on 24 Elul 5701.
story_body: R. Elchanan Yakubovitz, the last man to bear the title 'rabbi of Lubavitch' before the dissolution of the community, died in Jerusalem on 24 Elul 5701 (September 1941). With his death the direct rabbinical line of the historic Chabad town came to an end. His biographical notes were preserved by his son R. Aharon Yakubovitz.

title_en: R' Mordechai Banet writes recommendation for R' Yehuda Asad
summary_en: R' Mordechai Banet of Nikolsburg wrote a letter to R' Aharon, av beis din of Sardhel, recommending support for R' Yehuda Asad.
story_body: Dated 16 Sivan 5586, the letter from the elderly R' Mordechai Banet of Nikolsburg praises R' Yehuda Asad's diligence and mastery of halacha, urging R' Aharon to strengthen his standing in the community. The letter was part of the process that led to R' Asad's appointment as dayan.

title_en: R' Yehuda Asad accepted as dayan in Sardhel
summary_en: R' Yehuda Asad was appointed dayan in Sardhel on the recommendation of his teacher R' Aharon Suditz-Bichler and the Chasam Sofer.
story_body: In the year 5586, R' Yehuda Asad (later author of Yehuda Yaaleh) was received as dayan in the Hungarian community of Sardhel. His appointment came through the recommendations of R' Aharon Suditz-Bichler, the Chasam Sofer, and R' Mordechai Banet.

title_en: R' Yitzchak Yaakov accepted as additional rabbi in Romny
summary_en: R' Yitzchak Yaakov ben Moshe was received as a second rabbi in the Chassidic town of Romny.
story_body: Romny, a Chassidic town in the Poltava region near Haditch (burial place of the Alter Rebbe), already had R' Menachem Nachum as rabbi when R' Yitzchak Yaakov was added in 5589. He would later correspond with the Tzemach Tzedek on halachic matters.

title_en: R' Eliyahu writes to Tzemach Tzedek about Romny rabbinate transition
summary_en: R' Eliyahu ben Meshulam Feivish wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek explaining the controversy that forced his in-law R' Menachem Nachum to leave Romny for Chechersk.
story_body: Dated 28 Nissan 5595, the letter recounts how six years of communal dispute in Romny led R' Menachem Nachum to accept a position in Chechersk. R' Eliyahu reluctantly agreed to temporarily serve as moreh tzedek in Romny until a permanent replacement could be found, and posed Pesach-related halachic questions to the Tzemach Tzedek.

title_en: R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch visits Lubavitch seeking the Tzemach Tzedek's help
summary_en: R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch of Krutsa visited the Tzemach Tzedek in Tishrei 5596, receiving a loan, blessings, and recommendation letters.
story_body: Struggling with poverty and poor health, R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch sought guidance from the Tzemach Tzedek about finding a rabbinic position. The Rebbe lent him money to cover debts, blessed him to find a fitting position, and wrote a recommendation to R' Peretz Chen of Beshenkovichi.

title_en: R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch writes letter from Romny rabbinate
summary_en: From his new post in Romny, R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch wrote to the Tzemach Tzedek thanking him and detailing his journey to obtain semicha and a position.
story_body: Dated 7 Adar 5596, the letter recounts how R' Menachem Tzvi Hirsch travelled from Lubavitch through Beshenkovichi, Vitebsk (with R' Yitzchak Isaac), Mohilov (with R' Meir Berlin), and finally Homel where R' Yitzchak Isaac Epstein recommended him for the Romny position. He sought to repay the loan and asked for blessings for healing.

title_en: R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna immigrates to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna, longtime moreh tzedek of Bobruisk, made aliyah and settled in Jerusalem.
story_body: After serving as moreh tzedek of Bobruisk until 5611, R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna immigrated to the Holy Land and settled in Jerusalem. His departure opened the way for R' Hillel of Paritch to be appointed as sole rabbi of Bobruisk, including over the misnagdic community.

title_en: Maharil of Kopust writes to R' Aharon of Belnitz about Bobruisk rabbinate
summary_en: Maharil of Kopust wrote to R' Aharon Lipschitz of Belnitz urging him to travel with Bobruisk lay leaders to finalize his appointment as their rabbi.
story_body: Dated 24 Sivan 5611, this letter from the son of the Tzemach Tzedek to R' Aharon Lipschitz indicates that Bobruisk's leaders had come to receive him as rav. The appointment ultimately did not materialize, and R' Hillel of Paritch was chosen instead.

title_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark receives recommendation as rabbi of Horki
summary_en: The sons of the Tzemach Tzedek wrote to the Horki community urging them to firmly support R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark with a permanent salary.
story_body: Dated 15 Teves 5620, the joint letter from Maharil of Kopust, R' Chaim Shneur Zalman of Liadi, and R' Yisroel Noach of Niezhin praised R' Meshulam Zalman as 'a renowned moreh tzedek both in psak and in chassidus' and urged the community to retain him with a strengthened salary.

title_en: R' Hillel of Paritch passes away
summary_en: R' Hillel of Paritch, the renowned chassid and rabbi of Bobruisk, passed away on 11 Menachem Av 5624.
story_body: R' Hillel had succeeded R' Baruch Mordechai Itigna as rabbi of Bobruisk after the latter made aliyah in 5611. He served as sole rabbi over the entire community, including the misnagdic faction who held his words in awe, until his passing on 11 Av 5624.

title_en: Maharil of Kopust passes away
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Schneersohn, the Maharil of Kopust and son of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 3 Cheshvan 5627.
story_body: The Maharil, a son of the Tzemach Tzedek, was one of the founders of the Kopust branch of Chabad after his father's passing. He had been involved in many rabbinic appointments across Chabad communities, including those in Bobruisk, Romny, and Horki.

title_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moves from Horki to Starodub
summary_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark left his Horki rabbinate to serve as rav in Starodub, where R' Chaim Shimon Dov Zhivov succeeded him in Horki.
story_body: After approximately a decade in Horki, R' Meshulam Zalman moved to Starodub around 5622. The Horki position was filled by R' Chaim Shimon Dov Zhivov, later author of Shivim Tmarim, who would serve there for about 25 years.

title_en: R' Eliezer Orlozarow begins rabbinate in Romny
summary_en: R' Eliezer Orlozarow, author of Hagahos Eliezer, began his rabbinate in Romny in 5623.
story_body: Succeeding earlier rabbis of the Chassidic town, R' Eliezer Orlozarow served as rabbi of Romny for nearly four decades. He would continue in this position until his passing in 5661.

title_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark arrested in Starodub with 80 Jews
summary_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark was arrested in Starodub along with 80 other Jews and imprisoned for two years.
story_body: In 5641, R' Meshulam Zalman and 80 fellow Jews of Starodub were arrested and held in prison for two years (5641-5643). The Rebbe Maharash corresponded about the situation in letters preserved in his Igros Kodesh.

title_en: R' Mordechai Margolios appointed rabbi of Disna
summary_en: R' Mordechai Margolios was received as rabbi of Disna in 5644.
story_body: Following the long tenure of R' Mordechai, a chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek who had served in Kamin and then Disna, R' Mordechai Margolios was appointed rabbi of Disna in 5644.

title_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark appointed rabbi of Vitebsk
summary_en: After the death of R' Zalman Ostrovner, R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark was appointed rabbi of Vitebsk.
story_body: Following R' Zalman Ostrovner's passing in 5646-7 in Vitebsk, R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moved from Starodub to take the position. He would serve only about two years before moving on to another Belarusian community.

title_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moves to Nevel
summary_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark moved from Vitebsk to assume the rabbinate of Nevel.
story_body: By the start of summer 5648, R' Meshulam Zalman was already serving in Nevel, where a major fire had occurred that summer causing his books to be moved repeatedly. He would serve as rabbi of Nevel until his passing five years later.

title_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark passes away in Nevel
summary_en: R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark, rabbi of Nevel, passed away on 28 Menachem Av 5653.
story_body: After serving in Horki, Starodub, Vitebsk, and finally Nevel, R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark passed away on 28 Av 5653. His son R' Yechezkel Feivel succeeded him in the Nevel rabbinate, and his grandson R' Avraham Yaakov Neumark later published Eshel Avraham.

title_en: R' Eliezer Orlozarow passes away in Romny
summary_en: R' Eliezer Orlozarow, longtime rabbi of Romny, passed away in 5661.
story_body: After nearly four decades serving as rabbi of Romny since 5623, R' Eliezer Orlozarow died in 5661. He was succeeded by R' Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn (descendant of the Tzemach Tzedek through the Maharil of Kopust), with R' Akiva Yankilevsky (Orlozarow's son-in-law) appointed as additional moreh tzedek.

title_en: R' Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn passes away in Romny
summary_en: R' Chaim Yeshaya Schneersohn, rabbi of Romny and descendant of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away on 15 Kislev 5688.
story_body: R' Chaim Yeshaya, a great-grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek through the Maharil of Kopust, had served Romny since 5661. His passing left the Romny rabbinate vacant during the harsh Soviet years, eventually leading to R' Yani Gurarie being offered the position.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva opens in Romny under R' Yani Gurarie
summary_en: R' Shneur Zalman Yisroel Yaakov ('Yani') Gurarie arrived in Romny to open and head a Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva.
story_body: Having earlier lived in Kremenchug, R' Yani Gurarie came to Romny in 5685 to establish an underground branch of Tomchei Tmimim during the Soviet anti-religious crackdown. The yeshiva operated for three years amid escalating harassment from the Yevsektsiya.

title_en: R' Yani Gurarie sentenced to five months hard labor by Soviet authorities
summary_en: After a Soviet show trial during Pesach 5688, R' Yani Gurarie was sentenced to five months of forced labor for running the underground Romny yeshiva.
story_body: Following an earlier 5687 prosecution that was commuted by amnesty, the Yevsektsiya brought a fresh protokol against R' Gurarie in Teves 5688 and staged a public show trial (pokazatelni sud) on Pesach. Despite intense efforts, he was sentenced to five months of forced labor, after which the yeshiva closed.

title_en: Rebbe Rayatz advises R' Yani Gurarie on Romny rabbinate
summary_en: On 28 Tammuz 5688, the Rebbe Rayatz responded to R' Yani Gurarie endorsing his acceptance of the Romny rabbinate provided it would not cause controversy.
story_body: After the Romny yeshiva was shut down and R' Gurarie served his forced labor sentence, the community offered him the vacant rabbinate. The Rebbe Rayatz instructed him to actively pursue accepting the position, provided he was certain it would not become a matter of communal dispute.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim Romny closes after Soviet persecution
summary_en: The Tomchei Tmimim yeshiva in Romny closed in 5689 amid the Soviet crackdown on Jewish education.
story_body: According to the memoirs of R' Mordechai Shusterman, who had traveled to Romny to study, the yeshiva ceased operating in 5689, forcing students to return home. With the yeshiva closed, R' Yani Gurarie was left without a position before being offered the Romny rabbinate.

title_en: R' Yehoshua Eliyahu signs Horki community takkanos
summary_en: R' Yehoshua Eliyahu ben Yosef signed community regulations for Horki on 3 Teves 5610.
story_body: As rabbi of Horki, R' Yehoshua Eliyahu signed takkanos for the community on 3 Teves 5610, published in Ohalei Shem. He had succeeded R' Yehoshua of Horki, who died in 5602, and would later be succeeded by R' Meshulam Zalman Neumark.

title_en: R' Yehoshua of Horki passes away
summary_en: R' Yehoshua, rabbi of Horki and correspondent of the Tzemach Tzedek, passed away in the summer of 5602.
story_body: R' Yehoshua served as rabbi of Horki in the early years of the Tzemach Tzedek's leadership. His final psak was issued on Erev Shabbos in Nissan 5602, and the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa to him appear in Even HaEzer. He was succeeded by R' Yehoshua Eliyahu ben Yosef.

title_en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor grants smicha to Rafael of Amdur
summary_en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor of Kovno issues a rabbinic ordination certificate to Rabbi Rafael ben Shimshon of Amdur.
story_body: On 23 Tevet 5647, the famed posek and av beis din of Kovno, Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor (author of Be'er Yitzchak), tested Rabbi Rafael of Amdur and found him fluent in Shas and capable of original Torah insights. He issued a full kabbalas smicha—yoreh yoreh, yadin yadin—stating that any community that accepts him as rav will derive pride and nachas from him.

title_en: Spektor declines to issue an amulet, sends blessing for Yitzchak Yaffe's daughter
summary_en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor responds that he does not give amulets and instead sends a healing blessing for the ailing daughter of Yitzchak Yaffe.
story_body: Writing from Kovno on 20 Sivan 5647 in reply to a letter of 17 Sivan, Rabbi Spektor explains that he has never given amulets and that it is simply not his way. In their stead he extends a heartfelt blessing for the full recovery of Yitzchak Yaffe's daughter. He closes by noting that his weakened eyes make writing difficult.

title_en: Spektor acknowledges donations from Zekharia Lifshitz for fire victims
summary_en: Rabbi Spektor confirms receipt of funds donated and collected by Rabbi Zekharia Lifshitz for victims of a fire.
story_body: On 24 Elul 5647, days before the new year, Spektor wrote from Kovno acknowledging the money Lifshitz contributed and gathered for those left destitute by fire. He invoked the blessing of the perishing upon Lifshitz and offered an effusive year-end wish for him and his family to be inscribed and sealed for good life and abundant divine favor.

title_en: Birth of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch
summary_en: Rabbi Hillel ben Meir HaLevi Malisov, later known as 'Rabbi Hillel Paritcher,' is born in 5555.
story_body: The great chossid, mekubal and author of Pelach HaRimon was born in 5555 (1795) to Rabbi Meir HaLevi of Alisov. He would become one of the most prominent figures of early Chabad chassidus and a senior mashpia, later serving as mara d'asra of Babruysk after Rabbi Baruch Mordechai departed for Eretz Yisrael.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch in Cherson
summary_en: The famed chossid Rabbi Hillel of Paritch passes away on 11 Menachem Av 5624 during a journey, in the city of Cherson.
story_body: During one of his travels, Rabbi Hillel of Paritch—author of Pelach HaRimon and longtime av beis din of Babruysk—passed away in Cherson on 11 Menachem Av 5624. An ohel was built over his grave, and many chassidim journeyed there to prostrate themselves at his resting place.

title_en: Rabbi Baruch Mordechai of Babruysk moves to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: Rabbi Baruch Mordechai, longtime rav of Babruysk, departs for the Holy Land circa 5611.
story_body: Around 5611, the chassidic gaon Rabbi Baruch Mordechai left his rabbinate in Babruysk to settle in Eretz Yisrael. Following his departure the townspeople accepted Rabbi Hillel of Paritch as their rav and av beis din.

title_en: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav appointed rabbi of Dvinsk-Dinaburg
summary_en: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav assumes the rabbinate of Dvinsk-Dinaburg around the year 5625, succeeding Rabbi Yehuda Leib Batlan.
story_body: After serving as rav in Babruysk, Smilovitch and Homel, Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav was appointed rav of Dvinsk-Dinaburg around 5625, following Rabbi Yehuda Leib Batlan. He was a leading talmid of the Tzemach Tzedek and Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homel and a recognized posek in his region, especially in the laws of writing gittin.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav, rav of Dvinsk
summary_en: Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav, longtime rav of Dvinsk and chossid of the Tzemach Tzedek, passes away on erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5647.
story_body: Born around 5570-5571 and ordained by the Tzemach Tzedek at age eighteen, Rabbi Aryeh Leib Zivav served in the rabbinate of Babruysk, Smilovitch, Homel and finally Dvinsk-Dinaburg. He passed away on Monday, erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5647. Most of his responsa never reached our hands; only a small bundle written during his Homel years was preserved in manuscript.

title_en: Chiddushei HaRim of Gur certifies a shochet's sharpened knife
summary_en: The Chiddushei HaRim writes from Gur on 7 Adar Sheni 5622 attesting that he examined a shochet's knife and found him expertly skilled in honing it.
story_body: Rabbi Yitzchak Meir Alter, the first Gerrer Rebbe and author of Chiddushei HaRim, wrote to his chossid Rabbi Meir Shachna Reich on Sunday, 7 Adar Sheni 5622. He confirmed having tested the shochet's blade himself—finding the man sensitive to even the finest pgima and capable of restoring the knife to proper condition.

title_en: Conference of Chabad rabbis convenes in Lubavitch at the Rashab's invitation
summary_en: A special assembly of Chabad rabbis gathers in Lubavitch during Cheshvan 5669 at the personal invitation of the Rebbe Rashab.
story_body: In Cheshvan 5669, Rabbi Sholom DovBer of Lubavitch (the Rebbe Rashab) summoned a special conference of Chabad rabbis. Among the attendees was Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Bezpolov, rav of Poltava, who remained at the gathering at least until 17 Cheshvan, as reflected in the published Igros Kodesh of the Rebbe Rashab.

title_en: Poltava community appoints Adermann as kosher meat overseer
summary_en: Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Bezpolov and the Poltava community committee formalize a contract appointing Rabbi Shemaya Adermann to supervise the porging and sale of kosher meat in Poltava.
story_body: On Monday, 29 Marcheshvan 5669, the Poltava rav Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Bezpolov together with the community's elected committee signed an agreement with Rabbi Shemaya Adermann, who undertook to uphold the full set of regulations they enacted to safeguard the kashrus of meat in the city. The document carries the rav's stamp and the signatures of community officers including Aharon HaKohen Glezer, Chaim Zissel Chernigover and others. A puzzling secondary date of 2/11/1903 is appended at the bottom of the signatures.

title_en: R. Shmuel ibn Danan sells future inheritance share to brother in Fez
summary_en: R. Shmuel ibn Danan formally sold his anticipated inheritance from his still-living father, R. Saadia, to his brother Yitzchak for 500 ouguiyas.
story_body: On 29 Shevat 5457 (1697) in Fez, R. Shmuel ibn Danan, son of the elder R. Saadia, sold to his brother Yitzchak whatever he would inherit from their still-living father, both the firstborn share and the regular share, in exchange for 500 ouquiyot. Because the inheritance was 'a thing not yet in the world,' a standard kinyan was legally insufficient, so the sale was reinforced by a severe oath that Shmuel would repay the sum in full if the sale ever lapsed. The shtar was signed by R. Yehuda ibn Atar and R. Avraham ibn Masud ibn Atia.

title_en: Heirs of R. Binyamin Navarro grant mechilah to Avraham Tzarfati
summary_en: The widow and heirs of R. Binyamin Navarro waived all claims against Avraham Tzarfati while preserving joint ownership of a parcel of land inherited from Navarro.
story_body: On 13 Elul 5457 (1697) in Fez, Yosef Piso ben R. Moshe, Yitzchak Navarro, and Avraham ibn Lachsin (acting under power of attorney for Chana, widow of R. Binyamin Navarro) executed a sweeping mechilah to Avraham Tzarfati ben R. Meir, waiving every claim and grievance from the dawn of creation, even up to 1,000 ouquiyot. Only their shared ownership in a known parcel of land inherited from R. Binyamin remained between them. R. Yehuda ibn Atar and R. Avraham ibn Masud ben Atia signed the deed.

title_en: Fez beit din pesharah on the shop of Yitzchak's heirs
summary_en: A Fez beit din ratified a corrected compromise allowing R. Maimon to collect a supplement at redemption time, safeguarding the heirs' interest in a disputed shop.
story_body: In the last third of Kislev 5459 (late 1698) in Fez, the beit din finalized a ruling concerning a shop linked to one Yitzchak, ruling that his relatives who inherited would pay in full to rescue the shop from claimants and that R. Maimon would also be empowered to collect an additional sum at the time of redemption. After a clerical error in the amount, '30' was corrected to '20' between the lines before the remaining dayanim signed. The document was signed by R. Menachem Sirero, R. Vidal Hatzarfati, R. Yehuda ibn Atar, R. Shmuel Hatzarfati, and endorsed by R. Moshe ibn Hamu.

title_en: Widow Alaz acknowledges Yaakov ibn Atar's debt of 400 ouquiyot
summary_en: Alaz, widow of R. Yitzchak ben Mordechai Adhan, and her son Mordechai formally recognized that Yaakov ben Avraham ibn Atar still owed 400 ouquiyot from orphan funds entrusted to him to lend out.
story_body: On 18 Shevat 5463 (1703) in Fez, Alaz and her son Mordechai issued a mechilah to Yaakov ben Avraham ibn Atar, formally acknowledging that of orphan funds entrusted to him to be lent out on pledges in the customary manner, 400 ouquiyot remained outstanding. A debt note for that exact sum was executed the same day. Over the following years Yaakov repaid in installments noted on the back of the shtar, until only about 104 ouquiyot remained when he became impoverished.

title_en: Fez beit din awards 1.5 shops to heirs of R. Refael Moshe ibn Tzur
summary_en: Fez beit din settled a dispute between R. Yitzchak ibn Tzur and the kahal's treasurers over three shops his late father had owned, granting 1.5 to the heirs and 1.5 to the poor.
story_body: On 29 Iyar 5466 (1706) in Fez, R. Yitzchak ben R. Refael Moshe ibn Tzur sued the community treasurers, R. Yitzchak Hatzarfati and R. Saadia Aflalo, over three shops in the New Vegetable Market that had belonged to his father. The shops had been sealed when R. Refael Moshe departed for Tetouan years earlier, after which the kahal opened them and used them in his prolonged absence. Witness testimony, a former attempt to claim them by R. Moshe HaKohen on behalf of the heirs, and the surviving doorpost markings led the beit din — R. Yehuda ibn Atar, R. Shmuel Hatzarfati, and R. Yaakov ben R. Reuven ibn Tzur — to award one and a half shops to the heirs and one and a half to the poor of the kahal. The treasurers and parnasim of the community signed their agreement.

title_en: R. Yehuda ibn Atar orders Yaakov ben Atar to borrow at interest for Adhan orphans
summary_en: R. Yehuda ibn Atar compelled impoverished Yaakov ben Atar to borrow from gentiles at interest to repay the Adhan orphans, enabling the orphan Esther to marry.
story_body: On 13 Sivan 5468 (1708) in Fez, with Yaakov ben Avraham ibn Atar having sworn poverty and unable to repay the widow Alaz and her sons Mordechai and Yosef on the debts to their late father R. Yitzchak ben Mordechai Adhan, R. Yehuda ibn Atar intervened. Moved by Yaakov's pursuit by many creditors and by the plight of Esther, a daughter who had reached marriageable age without dowry, R. Yehuda ordered Yaakov to borrow 50 ouquiyot from gentiles on credit and pay an additional 25 to the heirs within eighteen months. In return, the widow and orphans waived every claim against Yaakov, freed him from oaths and bans, and committed to indemnify him against any future claim.

title_en: Esther bat Yitzchak Adhan renounces inheritance for her dowry
summary_en: The orphan Esther formally renounced all claims to her late father's estate in exchange for the dowry her mother and brothers were providing for her marriage.
story_body: On 25 Iyar 5468 (1708) in Fez, Esther bat the late R. Yitzchak ben Mordechai Adhan, confirmed to be of full age, formally relinquished every claim and right she had against her mother Alaz and her brothers in exchange for the dowry they were providing for her marriage. She additionally granted them by way of an open, public, healthy-person's gift all the documents, notes, and remaining property from her father's estate, on land and movables alike. The deed was signed in Fez by R. Shlomo Amiel and R. Moshe ben Makhluf ben Maman, written up on 19 Sivan 5468 at the request of Yaakov ben Atar, who had a stake in the underlying mechilah.

title_en: Sale of R' Yehuda Uziel's synagogue in Fes to R' Emanuel Mansano
summary_en: R' Yosef ben Menachem Uziel sold two-thirds of the synagogue inherited from R' Yehuda Uziel to R' Emanuel Mansano on 19 Marcheshvan 5470 in Fes.
story_body: Following an existing mortgage, R' Yosef sold two-thirds of the synagogue (including Torah scrolls, ark, benches, and ritual items) to R' Emanuel Mansano for 680 ounces. R' Yaakov ibn Tzur, holding a one-sixth share, asserted neighbor's right and the parties compromised so that Mansano and Ibn Tzur each took one-third. The document was confirmed by the dayanim of Fes, including R' Yehuda ibn Attar.

title_en: Testimony of investment in mortgaged building in Fes
summary_en: In mid-Tevet 5470, R' Yitzchak ben David ve-Chayun added 52 ounces of building repairs to his mortgage on R' Chaim Yaakov's upper-story property in Fes.
story_body: R' Yitzchak rebuilt half of a shared wall in the mortgaged upper story, spending on lime, sand, bricks, debris removal, and workers' wages and meals. The owner R' Chaim Yaakov consented before the court to add this sum to the mortgage, so that on redemption the principal and addition would be paid together. The ruling was signed by R' Yehuda ibn Attar and other Fes dayanim.

title_en: Heirs of R' Yitzchak ben David ve-Chayun add further building repairs to mortgage
summary_en: In Tishrei 5476, the orphans of R' Yitzchak ben David ve-Chayun added expenses for repairs to a mortgaged property in Fes.
story_body: Witnesses Yaakov ben Mordechai Azulai (mason) and Yaakov Punitz (carpenter) testified before the Fes beit din that the orphans had paid for essential repairs to the bathroom wall, the roof, the courtyard floor, doors, and beams of the mortgaged property. These sums of roughly 5.25 and 12 ounces were added to the existing mortgage, to be repaid in full at redemption.

title_en: Rivkah bat Shem Tov Cohen waives inheritance upon marriage to R' Shmuel Elbaz
summary_en: On 27 Tevet 5477, Rivkah, daughter of the late R' Shem Tov Cohen, formally relinquished her claims on her father's estate after receiving an oversized dowry from her mother Reina ahead of her marriage to R' Shmuel Elbaz.
story_body: Rivkah's mother provided her with cash and goods worth approximately 1,000 ounces, far more than her legal portion of the estate. Rivkah and, on 1 Shevat, her betrothed R' Shmuel Elbaz (later author of Vayomer Shmuel) renounced all further claims against the estate. The dayanim R' Yehuda ibn Attar, R' Yaakov ibn Attar, R' Yaakov ibn Tzur and R' Avraham Tzarfati ratified the waiver.

title_en: R' Yehoshua Serero appointed cantor of Ibn Ravuach synagogue in Fes
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Adar 5482, the rabbis of Fes confirmed R' Yehoshua Serero as permanent cantor at the synagogue named for R' Saadia ibn Ravuach, overruling a competing appointment.
story_body: After the death of cantor R' Yaakov ibn Danan, the congregation had endorsed Serero's appointment, but a later writ claimed Ibn Danan had instructed that R' Yosef ibn Shikrun succeed him. The Fes beit din ruled the earlier congregational decision authoritative and barred any other cantor. The dispute was significant enough that the rabbis of Meknes - including R' Moshe Toledano, R' Yaakov ibn Tzur, and R' Moshe Berdugo - co-signed in support.

title_en: Publication of Vayomer Shmuel by R' Shmuel Elbaz in Casablanca
summary_en: R' Shmuel Elbaz's halachic work Vayomer Shmuel was published in Casablanca in 5689 (1929).
story_body: R' Shmuel Elbaz, son of R' Yitzchak, was the same figure who in 1717 had married Rivkah bat Shem Tov Cohen of Fes and consented to her inheritance waiver. His subsequent work Vayomer Shmuel appeared in print in Casablanca centuries later, in 1929, cementing his reputation among the rabbinic authorities of Morocco.

title_en: Beit Din ruling on Ibn Saadon vs. Ibn Danan debt in Fez
summary_en: Rabbi Yehuda ibn Attar issued a ruling in Fez requiring the heir of R' Shlomo ibn Danan to pay the Ibn Saadon brothers from his courtyard property.
story_body: The Ibn Saadon brothers had sold ostrich feathers to R' Shlomo ibn Danan on credit and were never fully paid before his death. His son R' Shmuel claimed his father had paid more than recorded and that non-Jewish creditors had seized all the inherited land. R' Yehuda ibn Attar ruled that the creditors could collect from the 'almasriya' still in the heir's courtyard, subject to mutual oaths.

title_en: Pawn-sale deed of courtyard property from Saadia to Yeshua in Fez
summary_en: Saadia Cabalero pledged a house in the courtyard of Yissachar ibn Zazon to R' Yeshua ben Yissachar for 150 ounces, with formal cancellation of secret protests.
story_body: Saadia obligated himself to repay 150 ounces by the end of Nisan, failing which the mortgaged house would pass to Yeshua. The deed extensively voided any prior moda'a (secret protest) by Saadia and provided that scribes and any future court could repeatedly write cancellations of such protests. Witnessed in Fez by Avraham Serero and Shaul.

title_en: Transfer of Fez mortgage deed from Yeshua ibn Zazon to R' Yaakov Halevi
summary_en: Yeshua ibn Zazon sold the Cabalero mortgage deed to R' Yaakov Halevi ben Shmuel via the four-cubits-of-land method.
story_body: On 25 Kislev 5478, Yeshua transferred all his rights in the pawn deed to R' Yaakov Halevi, swearing he had not collected on it and accepting responsibility for any future challengers including R' Shlomo Cabalero. Witnessed by Yaakov ibn Attar and Yaakov HaTzarfati in Fez.

title_en: Widow of R' Yaakov Halevi sells Fez mortgage to R' Avraham Toledano
summary_en: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 5483, the widow of R' Yaakov Halevi formally conveyed the long-traveled pawn deed in Fez to R' Avraham ben Baruch Toledano.
story_body: Acting with her late husband's interest, the widow used the kinyan-and-four-cubits-of-land form to convey the mortgage deed and all rights it carried. She swore she had not collected on it and would not transfer it again. Witnessed by Shmuel ibn Saadon and Mordechai Tzaba.

title_en: Fez Beit Din confirms transfer of mortgage to R' Avraham Toledano
summary_en: On 7 Adar Sheni 5483, the Fez Beit Din formalized the orphans' half-share in the mortgage in favor of R' Avraham Toledano.
story_body: Acting on behalf of the heirs of R' Yaakov Halevi, R' Yehuda ibn Attar and fellow dayanim conveyed the orphans' half of the rights in the mortgage to R' Avraham Toledano. The ruling cleared and emptied the orphans' lien on the pawn document.

title_en: R' Avraham Toledano conveys Fez mortgage to Rabbi Yaakov ibn Tzur (Yaavetz)
summary_en: On 18 Sivan 5483, R' Avraham Toledano transferred the chain-of-title mortgage deed to R' Yaakov ibn Tzur (the Yaavetz), then rabbi of Meknes.
story_body: R' Yaakov ibn Tzur served as rabbi of Meknes from circa 5478-5488 (1717/8-1727/8). Despite his seat in Meknes, in 5483 he acquired this Fez pawn deed, which had passed through many hands since 5476. Witnessed by Yehuda Halevi and David Shacrun in Fez.

title_en: Settlement between Moshe Vechiyon and Moshe ibn Assoulin in Fez
summary_en: On 14 Iyar 5483, the Fez Beit Din ratified a compromise between Moshe ben Yitzchak Vechiyon and Moshe ben Ayyush ibn Assoulin closing all mutual claims.
story_body: Vechiyon was owed about 170 ounces; mediators settled the dispute and Shlomo ben Masoud ibn Botbol assumed a written obligation for the agreed sum. The parties mutually released all past money, oath, and gilgul-shevua claims, retaining only an outstanding loan with extended repayment until Sukkot eve. Witnessed by R' Yehuda ibn Attar and Yitzchak Maimran.

title_en: Fez Beit Din settlement over R' Yitzchak ibn Assoulin's estate
summary_en: On 25-27 Kislev 5488, the Fez Beit Din finalized a compromise between Chaim Levi and R' Moshe ibn Assoulin regarding the estate of his deceased brother R' Yitzchak.
story_body: Chaim, who had married R' Yitzchak's widow, demanded an accounting of the estate that R' Moshe had managed during years of famine, while R' Moshe claimed nothing remained. Mediators settled the case for sixteen ounces, all other claims were mutually waived, and a dwelling was preserved for the orphan Ayyush. R' Yehuda ibn Attar and Shmuel Gabbai presided and witnessed.

title_en: MaHaRiL writes to R' Aaron of Belinitz seeking him as judge
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib (later Admur of Kopust) wrote to R' Aharon of Belinitz on the night of 15 Menachem Av תרט"ו, requesting that he serve as a judge (borer) in a din Torah on his behalf.
story_body: While his father the Tzemach Tzedek was still alive, the future MaHaRiL of Kopust faced a major din Torah and needed to choose an arbitrator. On the night of 15 Av תרט"ו he wrote to R' Aharon Lipshitz, moreh tzedek of Belinitz, declaring his settled intent to choose him. The letter is one of four surviving epistles documenting the affair, and represents the start of a months-long negotiation over the choice of arbitrator.

title_en: R' Hillel of Paritch declines to serve as borer due to a vow
summary_en: R' Hillel of Paritch refused appeals from the Tzemach Tzedek and his son to be the borer in the MaHaRiL's din Torah, citing a 31-year-old vow never to serve as judge or arbitrator, only as a deciding shalish.
story_body: The Tzemach Tzedek and his son MaHaRiL both wrote to the famed mashpia R' Hillel of Paritch (author of Pelach HaRimon) asking him to serve as their borer. Hillel replied that 31 years earlier he had taken a vow on da'as ha-makom never to act as dayan or borer, only as a deciding shalish — a safeguard he refused to lift even for the Rebbe's family. He had instituted this restriction because borerim sometimes act 'shelo k'das' by advocating only for the side that chose them.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek pens responsum seeking to release R' Hillel's vow
summary_en: In response to R' Hillel of Paritch's refusal, the Tzemach Tzedek composed a teshuvah seeking a halachic path to permit annulment of Hillel's vow against serving as borer, later printed in Shu"t Tzemach Tzedek Yoreh Deah siman 181.
story_body: When R' Hillel cited his old vow as blocking his service as borer, the Tzemach Tzedek personally researched whether the vow could be released. He drafted a responsum on the question, joined by responsa from R' Yitzchak Aizik of Homel (author of Chana Ariel) and R' Shneur Zalman of Vielizh. The Tzemach Tzedek's reply was eventually published in Shu"t Tzemach Tzedek, Yoreh Deah siman 181.

title_en: MaHaRiL switches choice of borer from R' Hillel to R' Aharon
summary_en: On the night of 4 Mar Cheshvan תרט"ז, MaHaRiL wrote to R' Aharon of Belinitz that — given Hillel's refusal — he and his father had decided that Aharon should now serve as borer, and pressed him urgently to accept.
story_body: Months of correspondence with R' Hillel of Paritch failed to produce his acceptance as borer. On 4 Mar Cheshvan תרט"ז the MaHaRiL wrote definitively to R' Aharon of Belinitz that the decision had been made to switch back to him, promising to cover travel costs and a fitting honorarium, and stressing 'I have no one else fit for this matter.' The location of the din Torah was still undetermined, perhaps near Berditchev.

title_en: R' Aharon of Belinitz formally agrees to serve as MaHaRiL's borer
summary_en: By Monday of parshat Naso תרט"ז, R' Aharon of Belinitz had sent his consent to serve as borer for MaHaRiL, who replied that the news had 'revived our soul.'
story_body: The negotiation dragged on for nearly a year. Only at the start of summer תרט"ז did R' Aharon respond affirmatively, his reply delivered by his son. MaHaRiL responded warmly on yom beis parshas Naso, promising to share with him the responsa from the Tzemach Tzedek, R' Yitzchak Aizik of Homel, and R' Shneur Zalman of Vielizh.

title_en: R' Yissachar Ber Melamed writes a veksel in Lubavitch
summary_en: On Friday, 12 Mar Cheshvan תרט"ו, R' Yissachar Ber Melamed signed a veksel — an open promissory note — in the town of Lubavitch, payable to the bearer for three silver rubles by mid-Adar.
story_body: Open promissory notes (vekslach) were widely used in shtetl commerce: merchants could pay for goods with them, and sellers could pass them on as cash. The bearer would collect from the original signer on the appointed day. This veksel, written in Lubavitch by R' Yissachar Ber son of Meir Melamed, is one of three surviving shtarot from the town between תרט"ו-תרח"י.

title_en: R' Noach Moshe records debt for Likkutei Torah purchase in Lubavitch
summary_en: On 16 Shevat תרי"ח R' Noach Moshe son of Binyamin signed in Lubavitch a debt note for six silver rubles for a Likkutei Torah purchased for the Lubavitcher minyan of the town of Dokshitz.
story_body: The new Likkutei Torah of the Tzemach Tzedek had become a prized acquisition for chasidic communities. R' Noach Moshe, while visiting Lubavitch, bought a copy on behalf of the Lubavitcher shul of Dokshitz, signing a debt note to be paid 'when the seller is in Dokshitz.' The shtar is a small witness to early Likkutei Torah distribution.

title_en: Chassidim sign debt note to the Tzemach Tzedek in Lubavitch
summary_en: On the night of 5 Tevet תרח"י the chassidim R' Yitzchak Chaim Dovber Wilensky and R' Aryeh Leib son of R' Nachum Noach signed a shtar in Lubavitch acknowledging a 15-ruble debt to the Tzemach Tzedek, due within a month and a half.
story_body: The shtar may record a loan from the Tzemach Tzedek to two chassidim staying in Lubavitch, or possibly a ma'amad obligation pledged to the Rebbe. R' Yitzchak Chaim Dovber HaLevi Wilensky was among the great chassidim of the era, active in the courts of the Tzemach Tzedek, the Maharash, and the Rashab. He had arrived in Lubavitch shortly after his marriage around age 18-19.

title_en: First edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Zhitomir
summary_en: The first edition of Likkutei Torah — the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses on Vayikra, Bamidbar, Devarim and Shir HaShirim — was brought to press in Zhitomir in תר"ח by the brothers R' Yehuda Leib and R' Chaim Shneur Zalman, sons of the Tzemach Tzedek.
story_body: The Likkutei Torah collected the Alter Rebbe's chassidic discourses on the latter three Chumashim and Shir HaShirim. Two of the Tzemach Tzedek's sons — the future Maharil of Kopust and R' Chaim Shneur Zalman — funded and oversaw the first printing in Zhitomir in תר"ח, with their names appearing on the title page and in the haskamos.

title_en: Passing of the Tzemach Tzedek
summary_en: The third Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek (R' Menachem Mendel Schneersohn), passed away on 13 Nissan תרכ"ו.
story_body: The Tzemach Tzedek's passing on 13 Nissan תרכ"ו shaped subsequent Chabad publishing history. When his sons brought a second edition of Likkutei Torah to press in the summer that followed, they declined to put their names on the title page out of mourning, leaving only R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil — the manager of the project — credited.

title_en: Second edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Zhitomir
summary_en: The second edition of Likkutei Torah was brought to press in Zhitomir in תרכ"ו by the mashpia R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil (Rashbatz), funded by the sons of the Tzemach Tzedek.
story_body: The summer of תרכ"ו saw a reprinting of Likkutei Torah, this time managed by the famed mashpia R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil. Because it appeared only months after the Tzemach Tzedek's passing, the title page omitted the names of his sons who had financed it and named only the Rashbatz. The third edition (Vilna תרל"ח) later clarified that the second edition too had been funded for the benefit of the Tzemach Tzedek's family.

title_en: MaHaRiL of Kopust sends Rashbatz funds and instructions for printing
summary_en: On 21 Menachem Av תרכ"ו the Maharil of Kopust wrote to the Rashbatz enclosing 100 silver rubles toward his share of the Likkutei Torah printing along with a long list of detailed instructions.
story_body: Among the last letters of the Maharil of Kopust — written about two and a half months before his passing — was this note to R' Shmuel Betzalel Sheftil enclosing his share of the printing costs of the second edition of Likkutei Torah, plus a 'long memo' detailing the printing specifics. The letter highlights the close working partnership between the rebbe and his publishing manager.

title_en: Passing of MaHaRiL of Kopust
summary_en: R' Yehuda Leib Schneersohn, the Admur of Kopust (MaHaRiL), passed away on 3 Mar Cheshvan תרכ"ז.
story_body: The MaHaRiL of Kopust, eldest son of the Tzemach Tzedek and founder of the Kopust line, passed away on 3 Mar Cheshvan תרכ"ז, about two and a half months after his last letter to the Rashbatz concerning the Likkutei Torah second edition. He had served as Rebbe briefly following his father's passing in Nissan of that year.

title_en: Third edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Vilna
summary_en: The third edition of Likkutei Torah was printed in Vilna in תרל"ח, including a notice clarifying that publication rights belonged to the grandsons of the Tzemach Tzedek.
story_body: The Vilna תרל"ח edition of Likkutei Torah included a printed statement that the haskamot of the great rabbis of the generation forbade reprinting without the permission of the Tzemach Tzedek's grandchildren, the sons of his son R' Menachem Mendel. The notice retroactively clarified that the prior תרכ"ו edition had also been undertaken for the Tzemach Tzedek's family.

title_en: Third edition of Siddur with Da"Ch printed in Königsberg
summary_en: The third edition of the Alter Rebbe's Siddur with Chassidic explanations was printed in Königsberg, Prussia in תרי"ב at the press of A. Zamter, with most copies disguised as a much older Berditchev printing to evade Russian censorship.
story_body: Following the תקצ"ז decree against Hebrew presses in Russia, presses in Prussian border towns — Königsberg, Johannisberg, Memel, Danzig — produced sefarim for the Russian market. Books destined for smuggling bore disguised title pages omitting the printer and bearing a falsely earlier date. Most copies of this siddur read 'printed in Berditchev' with the year encoded as תקצ"א, but a small batch made for Königsberg's local Jews received a second title page openly declaring 'Königsberg... at the press of A. Zamter, in the year ועבדתם את ה' בכל לבבכם.'

title_en: Russian decree against Hebrew presses
summary_en: The Russian government issued the gezeirat hadefusim in תקצ"ז, drastically restricting Hebrew printing presses in the empire and pushing chassidic publishing to Prussian border towns.
story_body: The תקצ"ז decree (gezeirat hadefusim) shuttered most Hebrew presses inside Russia. In response, Hebrew presses sprang up in Prussian towns near the Russian border — Königsberg, Johannisberg, Memel, Danzig — producing sefarim aimed primarily at the Russian Jewish market. Books were smuggled in with disguised title pages, omitting place and printer or even falsifying the year, so as to claim if seized to be old volumes legally predating the decree.

title_en: Rashab signs printing contract for fifth edition of Likkutei Torah
summary_en: On 19 Adar I תרס"ב the Rebbe Rashab signed a contract with a Vilna printing house to produce the fifth edition of Likkutei Torah, with the plates remaining his property.
story_body: The Rashab personally oversaw a new, carefully corrected fifth edition of Likkutei Torah. He signed the printing contract on 19 Adar I תרס"ב, with the printing plates remaining his property. He aimed to lower the price from 5-6 silver rubles per copy to roughly 2 rubles, so that even middle-class Jews could afford the set. The Rebbe and R' Shmuel Sofer (Rabinowitz) personally proofed the text.

title_en: Rashab announces affordable Likkutei Torah project
summary_en: On 6 Iyar תרס"ב the Rebbe Rashab wrote that the new Likkutei Torah edition would cost no more than 2 rubles — down from 5-6 — so it would become accessible even to chassidim of modest means.
story_body: In a letter dated 6 Iyar תרס"ב the Rashab explained the motivation behind the fifth edition: existing copies cost chassidim 5-6 silver rubles with great difficulty in obtaining them, while the new edition would be priced around 2 rubles and well-proofed. The project reflected his broader concern with making Chabad chassidic texts widely available.

title_en: Fifth edition of Likkutei Torah printed in Vilna
summary_en: The Rashab's carefully corrected fifth edition of Likkutei Torah was printed at the Romm press in Vilna in תרס"ד, with extensive new hagahot and a 'mode'ah rabbah' explaining the proofing effort.
story_body: After two years of intensive proofing — by R' Shmuel Sofer (Rabinowitz) and the Rashab personally, drawing on original manuscripts and reliable copies — the fifth edition appeared in Vilna in תרס"ד. A 'mode'ah rabbah' was inserted noting newly added hagahot that had been omitted from earlier editions due to copyist errors, and a corrections list (luach hatikun) was added at the end of part two.

title_en: Romm Vilna invoice for printing Likkutei Torah issued
summary_en: The Romm publishing house in Vilna issued an invoice on 7 June 1904 (8 Menachem Av תרס"ד) totaling 2,801.71 rubles for the printing of Likkutei Torah on Vayikra, Bamidbar, Devarim and Shir HaShirim.
story_body: The detailed invoice from Romm's Vilna press itemized paper costs for 1,900 and 1,500 copies of the two volumes, printing fees, plate costs, binding (covers), and corrections. Against advance payments totaling 1,100 rubles in 1902-1903, a balance of 1,701.71 rubles remained owed as of the invoice date.

title_en: Rashab reports on stereotype plates in Rostov during WWI
summary_en: On 21 Menachem Av תרע"ח, writing from Rostov during WWI, the Rashab informed his son the Rayatz that the stereotype plates of Likkutei Torah and Tanya, and the printing house generally, were intact.
story_body: During the displacement of WWI the Rashab settled in Rostov-on-Don. From there, on 21 Av תרע"ח, he wrote to his son the future Rebbe Rayatz that the stereotype plates of Likkutei Torah and Tanya and the rest of the press equipment had survived intact — a fact that would later enable a sixth edition to be printed from those plates in תרפ"ח.

title_en: Sixth edition of Likkutei Torah printed from existing plates
summary_en: The sixth edition of Likkutei Torah was printed in תרפ"ח from the original stereotype plates of the תרס"ד Vilna edition, which had survived WWI intact in the Rashab's possession.
story_body: Per his תרס"ב contract with the Vilna printer, the Rashab retained ownership of the stereotype plates of Likkutei Torah. Having confirmed in 1918 that the plates remained whole, the sixth edition could be issued in תרפ"ח directly from those same plates without resetting the type.

title_en: Wedding of R' Moshe Ashkenazi and Devora Krasik
summary_en: The chassid R' Moshe Ashkenazi married Devora Krasik, daughter of R' Chaim Eliezer Krasik and Leah née Gurary, on 5 Elul תש"ב in Tel Aviv.
story_body: On 5 Elul תש"ב the chassid R' Moshe Ashkenazi married Devora Krasik in Tel Aviv. As a wedding gift, R' Nachum Yehoshua Ershler, shochet u-bodek of Königsberg, presented the couple with his rare copy of the third edition of the Siddur with Da"Ch — the small Königsberg-printed batch with the openly-acknowledged title page — inscribed with blessings for them to celebrate their golden jubilee.

title_en: Passing of R' Moshe Ashkenazi
summary_en: The chassid R' Moshe Ashkenazi passed away on 23 Tevet תשס"ח; his rare wedding-gift Siddur with Da"Ch later passed via his son-in-law R' Nachman Yosef Tversky to the library.
story_body: R' Moshe Ashkenazi, who had received the unusual Königsberg-imprint Siddur with Da"Ch at his 1942 wedding, passed away on 23 Tevet תשס"ח. The siddur — one of only a handful of copies printed openly for Königsberg's own Jewish residents rather than smuggled into Russia — was given by his son-in-law R' Nachman Yosef Tversky to the Lubavitch library, where it provided definitive evidence that the disputed third edition had in fact been printed in Königsberg in תרי"ב.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek's Shu"t Even Ha'ezer Volume 1 printed in Vilna
summary_en: The first volume of the Tzemach Tzedek's responsa on Even Ha'ezer was printed in Vilna, with proceeds going to his sons and grandsons.
story_body: The volume bore the notation that it was brought to press by the Tzemach Tzedek's sons and grandsons, who received the income from sales. The publication was managed by R. Refael Mordechai Schneersohn and R. Meshulam Shilem Reich. After printing, copies were distributed among descendants for sale.

title_en: Death of R. Avraham Mertzbacher of Munich
summary_en: R. Avraham Mertzbacher, who built a rare collection of 156 manuscripts and 4,332 books in Munich, died on 21 Sivan 5645.
story_body: Mertzbacher had assembled his important collection between 1866 and 1885, including 43 incunabula printed before 1500. After his death, his son Dr. Yitzchak Eizik Mertzbacher inherited the library and later sought to sell it, prompting interest from the Rebbe Rashab.

title_en: Rashab travels to Worishofen for medicinal waters
summary_en: In winter 5661, the Rebbe Rashab traveled abroad to the medicinal waters at Worishofen, where he met Dr. Yitzchak Eizik Mertzbacher about purchasing his late father's library.
story_body: During this trip the Rashab encountered Dr. Mertzbacher, who wished to sell his father's important book and manuscript collection. The Rashab became interested in acquiring the collection to establish a Jewish library under religious ownership.

title_en: Rashab requests Rabinowitz catalog from his son for Mertzbacher library evaluation
summary_en: On 5 Chanukah 5661, the Rashab wrote from abroad to his son (the future Rebbe Rayatz) in Lubavitch asking him to find and send the Rabinowitz book catalog urgently.
story_body: The Rashab needed the catalog of R. Rafael Nata Rabinowitz to help evaluate the prices of the Mertzbacher collection he was negotiating to buy. He stressed the urgency and also asked for a list of his own books.

title_en: Rashab writes to R. Yeshaya Berlin about funding Mertzbacher library purchase
summary_en: On 4 Shvat 5661, the Rashab wrote to the wealthy chassid R. Yeshaya Berlin of Riga estimating the Mertzbacher collection price at 35,000-40,000 rubles and pressing him to commit to funding the purchase.
story_body: The Rashab compared prices using the Rabinowitz catalog and argued that Baron David Ginzburg would surely buy the manuscripts and early printings at any price if he knew. He pressed R. Berlin to decide, noting that hesitation prevented serious negotiations with Mertzbacher.

title_en: Rashab presses for decision on Mertzbacher purchase
summary_en: On 26 Shvat 5661, the Rashab wrote again to R. Yeshaya Berlin after receiving a letter from Hirschenger in Munich requesting the return of the catalog and an answer from Mertzbacher.
story_body: Mertzbacher had wondered why the Rashab was not communicating about the purchase. The Rashab pressed Berlin to give a definite yes or no so he could respond appropriately, since negotiations could not proceed without the funder's commitment.

title_en: Rashab discusses renewed Mertzbacher library negotiations
summary_en: On 25 Adar 5662, the Rashab informed R. Yeshaya Berlin that Mertzbacher was again willing to sell after a year's delay and asked Berlin for a final decision.
story_body: After Mertzbacher had earlier refused to sell, three weeks earlier he had written that he wanted to sell. The Rashab also revealed he had proposed the purchase to R. Yaakov Horowitz of Riga in Hamburg, and suggested perhaps Berlin and Horowitz could form a partnership.

title_en: Rashab's letter on building a Jewish library in Riga
summary_en: On 10 Menachem Av 5662, the Rashab sent the Mertzbacher catalog with supplement to R. Ze'ev Wolf, instructing him to negotiate a price of 30,000-35,000 rubles and outlining his vision for a Jewish library in Riga.
story_body: The Rashab urged that since maskilim maintained great libraries for non-religious purposes, a God-fearing Jew should fund this acquisition. He proposed that R. Yeshaya Berlin dedicate 3-4 rooms of his large house in Riga for the library and a study hall, so observant Jews could come to learn. The purchase ultimately did not materialize.

title_en: Chafetz Chaim writes about sales of completed Mishnah Berurah
summary_en: On Sunday Parshat Vayetze 5668, the Chafetz Chaim wrote that with God's help he had completed the Mishnah Berurah on the full Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim and listed prices for his works.
story_body: He sent his emissary R. Yitzchak ben Yisrael Yosef of Cizevo to distribute his books in towns near Warsaw, asking Jews to assist him. He specified prices for each volume: Mishnah Berurah parts 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 at 1.20 rubles each, part 4 at 90 kopeks bound, with 6.60 rubles for the complete set.

title_en: Chafetz Chaim flees Radin to Russia with his yeshiva
summary_en: In summer 5675, as Germany was about to conquer Radin, the Chafetz Chaim fled with a large portion of his yeshiva into Russia, beginning a six-year exile.
story_body: He resided first in Smilavitchi, then Shumyatch, then Snovsk. He remained in Russia until summer 1921, when he returned to Radin. The Chafetz Chaim later wrote about being well-received and supported by communities in all three Russian locations.

title_en: Chafetz Chaim writes to Rabbi Moshe Madeyevski about relocating to Charal
summary_en: On Sunday Parshat Emor 5679, the Chafetz Chaim wrote to the rabbi of Charal asking help to find lodging there because of terrible food prices where he was then living.
story_body: He sent a beloved student ahead to find a residence and necessities, noting he had no acquaintances in Charal. The famine of the period during his Russian exile forced him to consider moving to find a place where prices were not so high.

title_en: Chafetz Chaim decides to leave Russia and return to Radin
summary_en: In Adar 5681, the Chafetz Chaim left Snovsk to return to Radin after Soviet authorities forced public Sabbath desecration on the whole town including his yeshiva students.
story_body: He wrote that the authorities imposed labor on the entire city on weekdays and Shabbat, including yeshiva students from the beis medrash whom he could not save. He concluded one must leave a place where God's name is publicly desecrated, even considering travel to Eretz Yisrael via Odessa, though he first returned to Radin.

title_en: Chafetz Chaim's letter from 5 Selichot 5681
summary_en: On 5 Selichot 5681, the Chafetz Chaim wrote reflecting on his six years of wandering in Russia, in Smilavitchi, Shumyatch and Snovsk, and his return.
story_body: He described how God had finally fulfilled their wish to leave Russia after the Soviet authorities imposed forbidden labor on all, even yeshiva students. He thanked the communities that had supported the yeshiva splendidly throughout the exile.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe leaves Lubavitch due to approaching war
summary_en: In autumn 1915, due to the approaching enemy and the war, R. Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn left Lubavitch in the Mohilev district, storing his library of 35 wooden crates in the Kokorov warehouses in Moscow.
story_body: The library, containing only religious books and prayer books in Hebrew, had been assembled over decades by his father and grandfather. The crates remained in those Moscow warehouses for years, becoming the subject of repeated requests for their return.

title_en: Decision to transfer Schneersohn library to Rumyantsev Museum
summary_en: On 16 December 1919, Soviet authorities ruled regarding the disposition of the Schneersohn library that would lead to its transfer to the Rumyantsev Museum.
story_body: This was one of two key decisions cited by the Soviet Scientific Council, the other being 21 May 1921, that resulted in the library being given by Narkompros to the Rumyantsev Museum, later renamed the Russian State Library named after Lenin.

title_en: Second Soviet decision concerning the Schneersohn library
summary_en: On 21 May 1921, Soviet authorities issued a second ruling that, together with the 16 December 1919 decision, transferred the Schneersohn library to the Rumyantsev Museum.
story_body: These two decisions formed the legal basis the Soviet Scientific Council cited in 1924 when refusing to return the library to the Frierdiker Rebbe, even though he had earlier received a positive response from the libraries department of Narkompros.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe requests release of library to Rostov
summary_en: In summer 5682, the Frierdiker Rebbe submitted a renewed request to be permitted to take his library from the Moscow warehouses to his home in Rostov.
story_body: Earlier he had been unable to retrieve the books because he lacked a place to store them. Though Narkompros had approved his request in principle, that year the books were still not returned to him.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe moves to Leningrad
summary_en: In early summer 1924, R. Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn moved from Rostov to Leningrad, where he now had room to store the long-confiscated library.
story_body: This relocation prompted his subsequent declaration to Soviet authorities requesting the library be sent to his new Leningrad address. He explained he could now store the books, having previously lacked space.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe submits declaration in Leningrad demanding return of library
summary_en: In June 1924, the Frierdiker Rebbe submitted a formal declaration from Leningrad arguing that his library, never abandoned and used for scholarly work, must be returned to him under Soviet law.
story_body: He argued that Soviet law did not nationalize private libraries, especially those used by scholars, that the books had always been under his supervision, and that prior Narkompros approval proved the library had never been ownerless. He stressed the books were religious texts relevant only to a narrow circle of Jewish religious specialists.

title_en: Soviet Scientific Council refuses to return Schneersohn library
summary_en: On 23 June 1924, the Soviet Scientific Council informed the Frierdiker Rebbe that they could not fulfill his request because the library had already been transferred to the Rumyantsev Museum, now the Russian State Public Library named after Lenin.
story_body: The response cited decisions of 16 December 1919 and 21 May 1921 as basis for the transfer by Narkompros. It was signed by Pinkevich, acting chairman of the Scientific Council, and Zinkov, chairman of scientific libraries. This refusal prompted the Rebbe to file another similar request in winter 5685.

title_en: Passing of the Rogatchover Gaon
summary_en: The Rogatchover Gaon (Rabbi Joseph Rosen) passed away in Dvinsk on 11 Adar 5696.
story_body: Rabbi Joseph Rosen, the renowned Rogatchover Gaon of Dvinsk, passed away on 11 Adar 5696 (March 5, 1936). Immediately after the shiva, his widow Rebbetzin Rivka organized a committee to print his manuscripts. His death set in motion decades of efforts to publish his extensive Torah writings.

title_en: Dvinsk committee letter to Rabbi Goldfein on printing Rogatchover writings
summary_en: The Dvinsk committee wrote to Rabbi Abba David Goldfein, the Rogatchover's son-in-law, asking him to come edit the manuscripts.
story_body: On 19 Adar 5696, immediately after the shiva, a member of the committee organized by Rebbetzin Rivka wrote on her behalf to her son-in-law Rabbi Abba David Goldfein in his name, asking him to come to Dvinsk for several months to edit and prepare the Rogatchover's manuscripts for publication.

title_en: Second Dvinsk letter to Rabbi Goldfein
summary_en: A second letter was sent to Rabbi Goldfein urging a reply about coming to Dvinsk.
story_body: Two weeks after the first letter, on 7 Nissan 5696, the Dvinsk committee wrote again to Rabbi Abba David Goldfein. Rebbetzin Rivka was anxiously awaiting his reply about coming to organize the publication of her late husband's manuscripts.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Abba David Goldfein
summary_en: Rabbi Abba David Goldfein, the Rogatchover's son-in-law, passed away on 19 Iyar 5696.
story_body: At the time the Dvinsk committee was writing him about editing the Rogatchover's manuscripts, Rabbi Abba David Goldfein was lying ill with severe heart disease. He passed away on 19 Iyar 5696, and the planned editorial project never came to fruition under him.

title_en: Publication of first volume of Tzofnat Paneach responsa
summary_en: The first volume of the Rogatchover's responsa 'Tzofnat Paneach' was published in 5700.
story_body: After Rebbetzin Rachel Tzitran, the Rogatchover's daughter, came from the Land of Israel to Dvinsk, she began handling the publication of her father's writings. In 5700 (1940) the first volume, Responsa Tzofnat Paneach, was finally issued.

title_en: Arrest of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson
summary_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, father of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, was arrested in March 1939.
story_body: In March 1939, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was arrested by Soviet authorities. From the moment of his imprisonment, his physical strength deteriorated rapidly day by day, though his spirit remained strong. His suffering was intensified by the absence of Jewish spiritual life in his place of exile.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson in Alma-Ata
summary_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson passed away in exile in Alma-Ata on 20 Av 5704.
story_body: The Rebbe's father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, passed away on 20 Menachem Av 5704 (August 1944) in Alma-Ata, capital of Kazakhstan. He had been allowed, after great efforts of devoted friends working at risk to their lives, to move from the village of Chili to Alma-Ata, where conditions were better both materially and spiritually because a Jewish community existed there.

title_en: Rebbe's letter to Rabbi Mordechai Savitsky on the Rogatchover
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Mordechai Savitsky praising his frequent citations of the Rogatchover Gaon.
story_body: On 17 Tevet 5715, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Mordechai Savitsky acknowledging receipt of his books Beit Mordechai vol. 2 and Mayim Adirim vol. 1. The Rebbe noted a special thread he saw in the books — Savitsky's frequent citation of the Rogatchover Gaon — and remarked on the wonder that scholars overlooked the wealth of insights in the Rogatchover's writings.

title_en: Rabbi Menachem Kasher receives Rogatchover microfilms
summary_en: In 5716, Rabbi Menachem Kasher received the Rogatchover's manuscripts and began preparing them for publication.
story_body: Rebbetzin Rachel Tzitran had photographed much of her father's writings on microfilm and sent them to family in America for safekeeping. In 5716 (1956), Rabbi Menachem Kasher received these manuscripts and began the work of editing them for the Tzofnat Paneach series on Talmud and Torah.

title_en: Publication of Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot
summary_en: The first volume issued by Rabbi Kasher, Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot, appeared in 5719.
story_body: In 5719 (1959), Rabbi Menachem Kasher published the first volume of his edition of the Rogatchover's writings, Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot. As soon as it appeared, Kasher sent a copy to the Rebbe.

title_en: Rebbe's letter with notes on Tzofnat Paneach Makkot
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher with comments on the newly issued Tzofnat Paneach Makkot.
story_body: On 23 Sivan 5719, immediately after receiving the new volume of Tzofnat Paneach on Tractate Makkot, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher with notes and observations on its content. This letter appears in Igrot Kodesh vol. 18, letter 6903.

title_en: Rebbe's second letter to Kasher on Tzofnat Paneach
summary_en: The Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher again on the substance of his notes on the Rogatchover.
story_body: After Rabbi Kasher replied to the Rebbe's notes on Tzofnat Paneach Makkot, the Rebbe wrote back on 15 Tammuz 5719 further engaging with the substance of the discussion. This second letter appears as Igrot Kodesh letter 6936.

title_en: Kasher's Pesach Sheni letter on Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus
summary_en: Rabbi Kasher updated the Rebbe on the imminent appearance of Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus.
story_body: On Pesach Sheni 5721, Rabbi Menachem Kasher wrote to the Rebbe that Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus was nearly finished and would be completed within a month. He also mentioned having submitted volumes on Leviticus and on Tractates Horayot, Eduyot and the minor tractates for printing in Israel.

title_en: Kasher's letter thanking the Rebbe for Joint Distribution Committee support
summary_en: Rabbi Kasher thanked the Rebbe for unsolicited intervention with the JDC to support the Tzofnat Paneach project.
story_body: On 24 Sivan 5721, Rabbi Kasher wrote to the Rebbe with heartfelt thanks. JDC representatives had told Kasher that during their yechidut with the Rebbe, in the middle of discussing their own support for Chabad activities, the Rebbe had taken the opportunity to praise the Tzofnat Paneach project and urge them to support it.

title_en: Publication of Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus
summary_en: Tzofnat Paneach on the Book of Exodus appeared in the summer of 5721.
story_body: In the summer of 5721 (1961), Rabbi Menachem Kasher's volume of Tzofnat Paneach on the Book of Exodus was published. As soon as the Rebbe received it, he reviewed it, wrote comments, and sent them back to Kasher.

title_en: Rebbe's letter urging publication of Rogatchover on Talmud
summary_en: The Rebbe urged Rabbi Kasher to prioritize publishing a Tzofnat Paneach volume on a yeshiva tractate.
story_body: On 1 Menachem Av 5721, the Rebbe wrote to Rabbi Kasher acknowledging Tzofnat Paneach on Exodus and urging that, if possible, he should publish a volume on a Talmudic tractate studied in yeshivot in time for the upcoming zman. The Rebbe noted that volumes on Talmud make a different first impression than volumes on Chumash.

title_en: Passing of Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson
summary_en: Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, the Rebbe's mother, passed away in New York on 6 Tishrei 5725.
story_body: Rebbetzin Chana Schneerson, mother of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, kept the Tehillim that had belonged to her husband Rabbi Levi Yitzchak in his Kazakhstan exile. She recited Tehillim from it until her passing in New York on 6 Tishrei 5725 (September 1964), having brought it with her when she left Russia.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kasher
summary_en: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kasher, editor of the Tzofnat Paneach series, passed away on 27 Cheshvan 5744.
story_body: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Kasher, who edited and published the Rogatchover's Tzofnat Paneach series including the Klalei HaTorah V'HaMitzvot volumes, passed away on 27 Marcheshvan 5744 (November 3, 1983). The continuation of his publication project passed to others.

title_en: Polish gentile delivers Maharik with Alter Rebbe's glosses
summary_en: In summer 5746 a Polish gentile arrived in the U.S. with a Maharik responsa volume bearing the Alter Rebbe's marginal glosses.
story_body: In the summer of 5746 (1986), a Polish gentile came to the United States carrying a copy of Responsa Maharik (Lvov 5558) that contained marginal annotations in the handwriting of the Alter Rebbe of Chabad. He claimed it had come to him by inheritance from his grandfather. A Chabad chassid purchased the volume and returned it to the Chabad library.

title_en: Publication of Klalei HaTorah V'HaMitzvot volume 3
summary_en: Rabbi Pinchas Teitz edited and published volume 3 of Klalei HaTorah V'HaMitzvot in 5746.
story_body: In 5746 (1986), Rabbi Pinchas Teitz edited and published volume 3 of the Rogatchover's Tzofnat Paneach — Klalei HaTorah V'HaMitzvot, picking up where Rabbi Kasher had left off. Teitz also began preparations for volume 4. The Rebbe responded with thanks and encouragement to expedite the fourth volume.

title_en: Publication of HaTamim journal first issue
summary_en: The first issue of HaTamim was published in Warsaw in 5695, including a letter of the Baal Shem Tov.
story_body: The first issue of the HaTamim journal was published in Warsaw in 5695 (1935). It contained the first printing of a handwritten letter of the Baal Shem Tov addressed to his disciple Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polnoye, alongside notes on its provenance in the handwriting of the Rebbe Rayatz.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Aharon David Gordon in Shklov
summary_en: Rabbi Aharon David Gordon, stepson of Rabbi Avraham Avli of Vilna, died in Shklov on 12 Av 5611.
story_body: Rabbi Aharon David Gordon (Shklover), stepson of Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler of Vilna, passed away in Shklov on 12 Av 5611 (August 9, 1851). He and his brother had organized about sixty of Rabbi Avraham Avli's responsa, intending to publish them as Be'er Avraham, though that edition never appeared. After his death the manuscripts passed to his son.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler of Vilna
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler, av beit din of Vilna, passed away in 5596.
story_body: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler, who served as av beit din of Vilna, passed away in 5596 (1836). He had been born in 5524 (1764) in Posval. Several volumes of his responsa and novellae written from Vilna in 5593–5594 survived in the Chabad library archives.

title_en: Birth of Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler was born in Posval in 5524.
story_body: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler, future av beit din of Vilna, was born in Posval in 5524 (1764). He came from a family that had served in the Posval rabbinate for generations, including his grandfather, father, and brother.

title_en: Rabbi Avraham Avli leaves Posval
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler left the town of Posval in 5546.
story_body: In 5546 (1786), at about age 24, Rabbi Avraham Avli Posveler left the town of Posval. By that point he had already served in the rabbinate there and was known as a major Torah scholar, as attested to in the responsa of Tiferet Tzvi.

title_en: Printing of Responsa Maharik in Lvov
summary_en: The Lvov edition of Responsa Maharik was printed in 5558.
story_body: The Lvov edition of Responsa Maharik was printed in 5558 (1798). A copy of this edition bearing handwritten marginal glosses of the Alter Rebbe of Chabad survived for nearly two centuries before being returned to the Chabad library in 1986.

title_en: Florence printing of Orchot Chaim
summary_en: The first edition of Orchot Chaim by Rabbi Aharon HaKohen of Lunel was printed in Florence in 5510.
story_body: About two hundred years after the second edition of Orchot Chaim was completed in Majorca, the first printed edition of part one appeared in Florence in 5510 (1750), using the earlier mahadura kama text. Efforts by Maharam Padua to print the later edition had not succeeded.

title_en: Berlin edition of Orchot Chaim part two
summary_en: Rabbi M. Schlesinger published part two of Orchot Chaim with an introduction in Berlin in 5662.
story_body: In 5662 (1902), Rabbi M. Schlesinger published part two of Orchot Chaim in Berlin. In his introduction he explained the existence of two recensions of the work, noting that in the second edition — completed after the author reached Majorca and studied under Rabbi Shem Tov Falco — Rabbi Shem Tov is cited about fifteen times in part two alone.

title_en: R. Avraham David Wahrman begins rabbinate in Yazlovich
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham David Wahrman began serving as rabbi of Yazlovich in 5550 (1790).
story_body: Rabbi Avraham David of Buchach, a leading Galician halachist, started his rabbinic career in Yazlovich in 1790. He served there for twenty-four years, during which time he recorded daily every new Torah insight that came to him. Across his full fifty-year rabbinate this discipline produced tens of thousands of pages of chiddushim on the four parts of Shulchan Aruch, Tanach, and Talmud.

title_en: R. Avraham David Wahrman becomes rabbi of Buchach
summary_en: Rabbi Avraham David Wahrman moved from Yazlovich to the rabbinate of Buchach in 5574 (1814).
story_body: After twenty-four years in Yazlovich, R. Avraham David transferred to the rabbinate of Buchach in 1814, where he remained for the rest of his life. He continued his daily practice of writing chiddushim across all areas of Torah. None of his writings were printed during his lifetime.

title_en: Alter Rebbe of Chabad passes away on 24 Tevet
summary_en: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe and founder of Chabad, passed away on 24 Tevet 5573.
story_body: The Alter Rebbe died on 24 Tevet 5573, during the flight from Napoleon's invasion of Russia. His grandson the future Tzemach Tzedek was 23 years old at the time. Almost all of the Tzemach Tzedek's surviving halachic writings date from after this date, making the rare manuscript in which he still refers to his grandfather as living an unusually early specimen.

title_en: Death of R. Avraham David of Buchach
summary_en: R. Avraham David Wahrman's rabbinate in Buchach ended in 5601 (1841).
story_body: The Buchach rabbinate of R. Avraham David ended in 1841 after twenty-seven years. Across his fifty years of rabbanus in two communities he had filled tens of thousands of pages with chiddushim that remained in manuscript. Printing would begin only forty-five years later.

title_en: Highly accurate Amsterdam Tanach printed
summary_en: An exceptionally accurate Tanach was printed in Amsterdam in 5426–5427 (1666–1667), later used by the Tzemach Tzedek.
story_body: This Amsterdam edition of the Tanach was edited by Jewish and Christian scholars and regarded as essentially error-free, with Latin glosses on certain words. Printing began in 5426 and concluded with approbations dated 5427. The Tzemach Tzedek later owned a copy, used it to recite the haftarah, and added marginal notes on textual readings, on minhag differences for which haftarah to read, and on triennial division points.

title_en: Radal of Bichov replies to Lubavitch rabbi on get question
summary_en: On 11 Av 5596, R. David Luria of Bichov sent a halachic response to R. Yissachar Ber HaLevi Horowitz, rabbi of Lubavitch.
story_body: R. Yissachar Ber HaLevi Horowitz, rabbi of Lubavitch, wrote to the Radal about a get question because the Tzemach Tzedek was away from home. The Radal replied briefly on Monday 11 Menachem-Av 5596, apologizing for the haste due to fast-day weakness and asking not to be troubled with further questions, given his resolution to refrain from issuing responsa for several years. He suggested the question be put again to the Tzemach Tzedek on his return.

title_en: R. Mordechai Shneur Zalman Schneersohn responds to R. Yosef Tumarkin
summary_en: On 21 Adar I 5624 (1864), R. Mordechai Shneur Zalman Schneersohn of Zhitomir wrote a halachic response to R. Yosef Tumarkin of Kremenchug.
story_body: R. Mordechai Shneur Zalman Schneersohn — son of the Rebbe of Avruch and grandson of the Tzemach Tzedek — served as a posek in Zhitomir. On 21 Adar I 5624 he replied to R. Yosef Tumarkin of Kremenchug on issues of hafrashas terumah and chalah, the copying costs of some manuscripts, and a question on the Ohr HaChaim to parshas Vayeira. He died young, and most of his writings have been lost.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek's final illness begins in Kislev
summary_en: The Tzemach Tzedek became gravely ill in Kislev 5620, beginning a six-year illness that lasted until his passing.
story_body: In Kislev 5620 the Tzemach Tzedek fell seriously ill and remained so for more than six consecutive years until his passing.
