title_en: Pereshel-Weintraub facsimile of the Hamburg 1728 Abarbanel Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub issued in New York a facsimile of the Hamburg 1728 Abarbanel Haggadah by Yaakov Sofer of Berlin.
story_body: In 5740 (1980), Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah by Yaakov Sofer of Berlin, who had copied it from the 1695 Amsterdam edition. The 26-leaf octavo edition included Abarbanel's commentary and bilingual introductions. It continued their annual Haggadah facsimile project.

title_en: Pereshel-Weintraub facsimile of the Amsterdam 1662 Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub issued in New York a facsimile of the 1662 Amsterdam Haggadah.
story_body: In 5741 (1981), Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub published in New York a facsimile reproduction of the 1662 Amsterdam-printed Haggadah. The 24-leaf octavo edition included bilingual English-Hebrew introductions by the publishers. It was part of their annual program of reissuing rare Haggadot in the period before Passover.

title_en: Pereshel-Weintraub facsimile of the Frankfurt 1710 Mateh Aharon Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub published in New York a facsimile of the Frankfurt 1710 'Mateh Aharon' Haggadah.
story_body: In 5742 (1982), Tuvia Pereshel and Munish Weintraub published in New York a facsimile of the 1710 Frankfurt printing of the Haggadah with the 'Mateh Aharon' commentary by Aharon Teomim. The 27-leaf octavo edition came with illustrations and a bilingual Hebrew-English introduction by the publishers. It maintained their tradition of preserving rare Haggadot.

title_en: Pereshel facsimile of the Offenbach 1722 Avodat HaGefen Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel issued in New York a facsimile of the 1722 Offenbach 'Avodat HaGefen' Haggadah by Yehuda Leib and his son Ze'ev Wolf.
story_body: In 5743 (1983), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1722 Offenbach Haggadah with the 'Avodat HaGefen' commentary by Yehuda Leib ben Eliyahu and his son Ze'ev Wolf. The 20-page octavo edition came with illustrations and an introduction by Pereshel. It continued his series of resurrecting noteworthy early modern Haggadot.

title_en: Pereshel facsimile of the Sulzbach 1755 Abarbanel Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1755 Sulzbach Abarbanel Haggadah.
story_body: In 5745 (1985), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1755 Sulzbach Haggadah with Don Isaac Abarbanel's commentary and a Kabbalistic interpretation. The 14-leaf octavo edition included a Hebrew introduction by Pereshel. It contributed to his ongoing series of rare Haggadah facsimiles for the Passover holiday.

title_en: Pereshel facsimile of the Babad Amsterdam 1769 manuscript Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1769 Amsterdam 'Babad Haggadah' manuscript.
story_body: In 5747 (1987), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah written in Amsterdam in 5529 (1769) by Yehoshua ben Mordechai Babad of Volochisk. The 47-page octavo edition included a bilingual English-Hebrew introduction by Pereshel. The 'Haggadat Babad' continued his annual facsimile project.

title_en: Pereshel facsimile of Meshulam Zimel's 1719 Vienna manuscript Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of Meshulam Zimel ben Moshe's 1719 Vienna manuscript Haggadah created for Natan Oppenheim.
story_body: In 5748 (1988), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah written by Meshulam Zimel ben Moshe in Vienna in 5479 (1719) for Natan Oppenheim. The 28-leaf octavo edition included a bilingual Hebrew-English introduction by Pereshel. It continued his annual project of reissuing rare Haggadah manuscripts.

title_en: Pereshel facsimile of Yosef of Leipnik's 1733 manuscript Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of Yosef ben David of Leipnik's 1733 illustrated manuscript Haggadah.
story_body: In 5749 (1989), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of an illustrated manuscript Haggadah by Yosef ben David of Leipnik from 5493 (1733). The 48-page octavo edition included a bilingual Hebrew-English introduction by Pereshel. The work continued his annual series of facsimiles of rare Haggadot.

title_en: Pereshel facsimile of the Livorno 1825 Ladino Haggadah
summary_en: Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1825 Livorno Ladino Haggadah.
story_body: In 5752 (1992), Tuvia Pereshel published in New York a facsimile of the 1825 Livorno Haggadah with Ladino translation. The 34-leaf octavo edition (including cover) came with an introduction by Pereshel. It marked his ongoing commitment to resurrecting rare printed Haggadot for new generations.

title_en: First Chassidic Haggadah 'Chelkat Binyamin' by Binyamin of Zalozitz printed in Lvov
summary_en: Binyamin of Zalozitz, a disciple of the Maggid of Zlotchov, published the first Chassidic Haggadah commentary 'Chelkat Binyamin' in Lvov.
story_body: In 5554 (1794), 'Chelkat Binyamin', the first published Chassidic Haggadah commentary, was issued in Lvov by Rabbi Binyamin, maggid of Zalozitz, a leading disciple of Rabbi Yechiel Michel of Zlotchov. The 25-leaf quarto included a transcription of the Haggadah with the Kavanot of the Arizal. It marked a milestone in the printed dissemination of Chassidic teachings on the Passover liturgy.

title_en: Lublin Haggadah 'Sefer HaZmanim' by Yaakov Leiner of Izbica
summary_en: Yaakov ben Mordechai Yosef Leiner of Izbica's 'Sefer HaZmanim', including a Haggadah commentary based on the Arizal, was printed in Lublin.
story_body: In 5663 (1903), Yaakov ben Mordechai Yosef Leiner of Izbica published 'Sefer HaZmanim' in Lublin, printed by Moshe Schneidmesser and the widow Nechama Hershenhorn. The first part contained essays and homilies on the month of Nissan and its laws, an explanation of the Haggadah according to the Arizal's text, and material on dew, Sefirat HaOmer, the entire Passover holiday, Iyyar, and Pesach Sheni. The 55-leaf quarto reflected the teachings of the Izbica Chassidic dynasty.

title_en: Haggadah 'Yismach Yisrael' of Alexander Chassidut reprinted in Bnei Brak
summary_en: The 'Yismach Yisrael' Haggadah commentary by Yerachmiel Yisrael Yitzchak of Alexander was reprinted with extensive additions in Bnei Brak.
story_body: In 5753 (1993), the Haggadah with the 'Yismach Yisrael' commentary by Rabbi Yerachmiel Yisrael Yitzchak of Alexander was reissued in Bnei Brak with many added materials. The 176-page octavo edition served the Alexander Chassidic community and admirers of their teachings. It demonstrated the continued vitality of classical Polish Chassidic Haggadah commentary.

title_en: Haggadah 'Kedushat Levi' compilation from the Berditchever's works issued in Bnei Brak
summary_en: Machon Nachalat Tzvi issued a Haggadah 'Kedushat Levi' compiled from the writings of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and his disciples in Bnei Brak.
story_body: In 5750 (1990), Machon Nachalat Tzvi, edited by Shimon Hirshler, published in Bnei Brak the Haggadah 'Kedushat Levi', an anthology of Pardes-style commentaries on the Haggadah, Shir HaShirim, and the holiday, drawn from the writings of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and his disciples and sons. The 252-page octavo edition also incorporated material from Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah. It made the Berditchever's teachings on Passover available in consolidated form.

title_en: New York Haggadah with 'Divrei Binah' and 'Toldot Adam' Biala commentaries
summary_en: A Haggadah with the 'Divrei Binah' (Yitzchak Yaakov of Biala) and 'Toldot Adam' (Yehoshua of Ostrova) commentaries was published in New York.
story_body: Around 5721 (1961), a Haggadah was issued in New York featuring the 'Divrei Binah' commentary by Rabbi Yitzchak Yaakov of Biala and the 'Toldot Adam' commentary by Rabbi Yehoshua of Ostrova. The 91-page octavo edition included a preface by the Admor of Biala. It represented the publishing efforts of the Biala Chassidic dynasty in postwar America.

title_en: Haggadah 'Kol Yehuda' on the teachings of Belz Rebbes printed in London
summary_en: A Haggadah 'Kol Yehuda' built on Belz teachings by Chaim Yehuda Segal Deutsch was printed in London with material from Rebbe Aharon of Belz.
story_body: In 5722 (1962), the Haggadah 'Kol Yehuda', interwoven with teachings from the Belz Rebbes by Rabbi Chaim Yehuda Segal Deutsch, was published in London. The 212-page octavo edition included notes by the author's son and added Passover discourses from Rebbe Aharon Rokeach of Belz. It contributed to the Belz Chassidic community's postwar publishing renaissance.

title_en: Breslov Haggadah 'Or Zoreach' arranged by Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski, killed in 1919
summary_en: The Breslov Haggadah 'Or Zoreach' based on Rebbe Nachman's writings was published in Jerusalem, compiled by Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski (Alter of Teplik), who was killed sanctifying God's name in 1919.
story_body: In 5687 (1927), the Breslov community in Jerusalem published the Haggadah 'Or Zoreach', based on the writings of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov and arranged by the late Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski known as Alter of Teplik, who was killed sanctifying God's name in 5679 (1919). The 53-page octavo edition brought Rebbe Nachman's distinctive interpretation of the Haggadah to a wide audience. It served as a foundational text for the Breslov Chassidic community.

title_en: Martyrdom of Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski (Alter of Teplik), Breslov Chassid
summary_en: Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski, known as Alter of Teplik and compiler of the 'Or Zoreach' Breslov Haggadah, was killed sanctifying God's name.
story_body: In 5679 (1919), during the turbulent post-revolutionary period in Ukraine marked by widespread pogroms, the Breslov Chassid Moshe Yehoshua Bzhilianski — known as Alter of Teplik — was killed in sanctification of God's name. He had been working on a Breslov Haggadah called 'Or Zoreach' based on the writings of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov. The Haggadah was eventually published posthumously in Jerusalem in 1927 by his Breslov colleagues.

title_en: Warsaw Haggadah with Sfat Emet and Tiferet Shlomo commentaries
summary_en: A Haggadah combining the 'Sfat Emet' (Yehuda Aryeh Leib of Gur) and 'Tiferet Shlomo' (Shlomo HaKohen of Radomsk) commentaries was printed in Warsaw.
story_body: In 5685 (1925), a Haggadah featuring the 'Sfat Emet' commentary by Rebbe Yehuda Aryeh Leib Alter of Gur and the 'Tiferet Shlomo' by Rabbi Shlomo HaKohen, head of the Radomsk court, was issued in Warsaw by Yitzchak Meir Alter. The 83-leaf octavo edition was printed by Kupferstoch and Kramarsh. Leaves 2-4 apparently were never printed.

title_en: Vienna Haggadah 'Maadanei Melech' by Asher Horowitz of Dzikov
summary_en: The Haggadah 'Maadanei Melech' by Rebbe Asher Horowitz of Dzikov, residing in Vienna, was published there.
story_body: In 5694 (1934), the Haggadah 'Maadanei Melech' by the Admor Asher ben Meir Horowitz of Dzikov, who was then residing in Vienna, was published by the Appel Brothers in Vienna. The 80-page octavo edition served the Dzikov-Ropshitz Chassidic community and disciples of the Horowitz dynasty. It became one of the notable Hungarian-Galician Chassidic Haggadot of the interwar period.

title_en: Haggadah 'BiMesila' anthology of Zidichov dynasty teachings published in New York
summary_en: Moshe Aharon Moshkovitz compiled and published in New York the 'BiMesila' Haggadah anthology of teachings from the Zidichov, Komarno, Sambor, and Rozdol dynasties.
story_body: In 5749 (1989), Moshe Aharon Moshkovitz published in New York the Haggadah 'BiMesila', a collection of Torah novellae from the Chassidic dynasties of Zidichov, Komarno, Sambor, and Rozdol, drawn from the writings of the Rebbes and their descendants. The 232-page octavo work gathered material from printed books and manuscripts. It served as a comprehensive anthology of these closely related Galician Chassidic courts.

title_en: Przemyśl Haggadah 'Bet HaYayin' by Meir Yehuda Libush Langerman of Turka
summary_en: Meir Yehuda Libush Langerman of Turka published the Haggadah 'Bet HaYayin' incorporating teachings of Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura in Przemyśl.
story_body: Around 5658 (1898), the Haggadah 'Sefer Bet HaYayin' by Meir Yehuda Libush Langerman, head of the rabbinical court of Turka, was issued in Przemyśl by Zupnik, Knoller, and Wolf. The 52-leaf quarto featured 'Likkutim Tilpiot' built largely on the teachings of Rebbe Avraham Yaakov of Sadigura. It represented the Sadigura-Ruzhin Chassidic tradition's interpretation of the Passover liturgy.

title_en: Warsaw Haggadah with 'Shem MiShmuel' commentary by Shmuel Bornstein of Sochatchov
summary_en: The 'Shem MiShmuel' Haggadah commentary by Rebbe Shmuel Bornstein of Sochatchov was published in Warsaw.
story_body: In 5688 (1928), the Haggadah with the 'Shem MiShmuel' commentary by Rebbe Shmuel ben Avraham Bornstein of Sochatchov was published in Warsaw, edited by Chanoch Heinich Falman. Printed by Wegmeister, the 64-leaf octavo edition became one of the central Chassidic Haggadah commentaries of the interwar era. It distilled the Sochatchov Chassidic teachings on Passover.

title_en: Bnei Brak Haggadah 'Siach Avot' from Lechovitch-Koidanov dynasties
summary_en: Yaakov Tzvi Meir Erlich compiled the 'Siach Avot' Haggadah of Lechovitch-Koidanov teachings, published in Bnei Brak.
story_body: In 5751 (1991), Yaakov Tzvi Meir Erlich compiled and the Siach Avot Institute published in Bnei Brak the 'Siach Avot' Haggadah, a collection of holy teachings from the Lechovitch and Koidanov Rebbes. The 236-page octavo edition added Seder laws and customs, Exodus material, and Passover and Sefirat HaOmer letters. It served the Belarussian Chassidic dynasty's contemporary followers.

title_en: Bnei Brak Haggadah 'Birkat Moshe' of Lelov Chassidut
summary_en: Simcha Krakowski compiled and published the 'Birkat Moshe' Haggadah of Lelov Chassidic teachings in Bnei Brak.
story_body: In 5751 (1991), Simcha Krakowski compiled and published in Bnei Brak the Haggadah 'Birkat Moshe' according to the customs and teachings of the Lelov Rebbes, with material from Rabbi Moshe Mordechai Biderman of Lelov and Rabbi Shimon Natan Nata Biderman. The 148-page octavo edition combined teachings, Pesach customs, and conduct guides. It served the Lelov community and admirers of their distinct Chassidic path.

title_en: New York Haggadah 'Eshei Yisrael' on Modzitz teachings by Taub family
summary_en: An 'Eshei Yisrael' Haggadah featuring Modzitz dynasty teachings by Yisrael Taub and his son Shaul Yedidya Eliezer Taub was published in New York.
story_body: In 5707 (1947), the Haggadah 'Eshei Yisrael' was published in New York, featuring two commentaries: 'Divrei Yisrael' by Rebbe Yisrael Taub of Modzitz and 'Yisa Berachah' by his son Rebbe Shaul Yedidya Eliezer Taub of Modzitz. Material from Rebbe Yechezkel of Kazmir and Rebbe Shmuel Eliyahu of Zvolin was also included. The 119-page octavo edition preserved the musical-Chassidic legacy of the Modzitz dynasty in postwar America.

title_en: Munkacs Haggadah 'Tiferet Banim' by Tzvi Hirsch Shapira
summary_en: The Haggadah 'Tiferet Banim' with Pardes-style commentary by Tzvi Hirsch Shapira of Munkacs was published in Munkacs.
story_body: In 5674 (1914), the Haggadah with a Pardes-style commentary called 'Tiferet Banim' by Tzvi Hirsch Shapira, head of the Munkacs rabbinical court, was published in Munkacs by Kahn and Fried. The 82-leaf octavo edition represented the Munkacs Chassidic and rabbinical tradition. It contributed to the rich tradition of Carpathian Chassidic Haggadah commentaries.

title_en: Munkacs Haggadah with 'Sha'ar Yissachar' commentary by Chaim Elazar Shapira
summary_en: A Haggadah commentary based on Chaim Elazar Shapira of Munkacs's 'Sha'ar Yissachar' manuscript was published in Munkacs.
story_body: In 5698 (1938), a Haggadah with a commentary on the Pesach Aggadah drawn from the manuscript of Rebbe Chaim Elazar Shapira of Munkacs's work 'Sha'ar Yissachar' was published in Munkacs by Grafia Press. The 54-leaf octavo edition preserved the teachings of the famed Munkacher Rebbe on the Passover Seder. It appeared just before the Holocaust devastated the Munkacs Chassidic community.

title_en: Sighet Haggadah with 'Tzemach Hashem L'Tzvi' commentary by Tzvi Hirsh of Nadvorna
summary_en: A new Haggadah commentary 'Tzemach Hashem L'Tzvi' by Tzvi Hirsh of Nadvorna, with his father Shalom Zelig's pamphlet, was printed in Sighet.
story_body: In 5670 (1910), the Haggadah with the new commentary 'Tzemach Hashem L'Tzvi' by Tzvi Hirsh of Nadvorna was published in Sighet by Avraham Kaufman and Sons. The 39-leaf duodecimo edition included a 'Divrei Shalom' pamphlet by the author's father, Shalom Zelig. It served the Galician Nadvorna Chassidic community.

title_en: Warsaw Haggadah 'Tiferet Ish' by Alter Yisrael Shimon Perlov of Novominsk
summary_en: The 'Tiferet Ish' Haggadah by Alter Yisrael Shimon Perlov of Novominsk was published in Warsaw with an appendix on Chad Gadya by Mordechai of Chernobyl.
story_body: In 5693 (1933), the Haggadah 'Tiferet Ish' by Rebbe Alter Yisrael Shimon ben Yaakov Perlov of Novominsk was published in Warsaw by the Feder Brothers. The 96-plus-24-page octavo edition included a brief manuscript work by the author on Shir HaShirim and concluded with a commentary on Chad Gadya by his ancestor Rebbe Mordechai of Chernobyl. It represented the Novominsk Chassidic dynasty's interpretive tradition.

title_en: Jerusalem Spinka Haggadah with Imrei Yosef and Chakal Yitzchak commentaries
summary_en: A Spinka-rite Haggadah with the 'Imrei Yosef' and 'Chakal Yitzchak' commentaries from the Weiss dynasty was published in Jerusalem.
story_body: In 5724 (1964), a Haggadah following the Spinka rite was published in Jerusalem featuring the 'Imrei Yosef' commentary by Rebbe Yosef Meir Weiss of Spinka and the 'Chakal Yitzchak' commentary by Rebbe Yitzchak Aizik Weiss of Spinka. The 239-page octavo edition served the Spinka Chassidic community. It transmitted the teachings of the Carpathian dynasty to the Israeli Spinka community.

title_en: Jerusalem Haggadah 'Hallel Nirtzeh' and 'Chasdei David' by Greenwald brothers
summary_en: A Haggadah featuring the 'Hallel Nirtzeh' commentary by Moshe Greenwald and 'Chasdei David' by Eliezer David Greenwald was issued in Jerusalem.
story_body: In 5749 (1989), a Haggadah featuring two commentaries by the brothers Moshe Greenwald ('Hallel Nirtzeh') and Eliezer David Greenwald ('Chasdei David') was published in Jerusalem by Kollel Arugat HaBosem. The 177-page edition included drashot for Shabbat HaGadol and explanations of Sefirat HaOmer and Ketzirat HaOmer alongside laws of bedikat and biur chametz. It was published in honor of the wedding of Eliezer Tzvi and Leah Toiba Safrin.

title_en: New York 'Birkat Avraham' Haggadah by Avraham Landa of Cichanow with grandson's commentary
summary_en: A 'Birkat Avraham' Haggadah by Avraham Landa of Cichanow with grandson Menachem Mendel Chaim Landa's commentary was issued in New York.
story_body: In 5710 (1950), the Haggadah 'Birkat Avraham' was published in New York by Yaakov Werdiger of Pardes Publishing, drawing on the 'Chesed L'Avraham' commentary by Rabbi Avraham Landa, head of the Cichanow rabbinical court, and 'Ateret Zekenim' by his grandson Rabbi Menachem Mendel Chaim Landa of Zawiercie. The 49-leaf octavo edition was a photo-offset of an earlier Piotrkow edition. It served Polish Chassidic survivors and their descendants in postwar America.

title_en: Lvov Haggadah 'Gevurot Yisrael' (Maggid of Kozhnitz) and 'Mateh Moshe'
summary_en: A Pardes-style Haggadah with 'Gevurot Yisrael' by Yisrael of Kozhnitz and 'Mateh Moshe' by Moshe Eliyakum Briya was issued in Lvov.
story_body: Around 5624 (1864), a Haggadah was published in Lvov featuring two commentaries on the Pardes pattern: 'Gevurot Yisrael' by the Maggid Rabbi Yisrael of Kozhnitz, and 'Mateh Moshe' by his son Moshe Eliyakum Briya. Additional drashot on Pesach, the four cups, and 'Kadesh U'Rechatz', plus drashot on Sefirat HaOmer and a commentary on Chad Gadya by Rebbe Mordechai of Chernobyl, were included. The 34-leaf quarto edition was printed by Sh.L. Flecker.

title_en: Jerusalem Haggadah 'Aryeh D'Bei Ilai' of Shinava-Stropkov Chassidut
summary_en: An 'Aryeh D'Bei Ilai' Haggadah pamphlet from the Shinava-Stropkov community, drawing on 'Divrei Yechezkel Shraga', was published in Jerusalem.
story_body: In 5716 (1956), a pamphlet entitled 'Aryeh D'Bei Ilai' was published in Jerusalem by the Shinava-Stropkov Chassidic council, containing essential matters drawn from the 'Divrei Yechezkel Shraga' Haggadah commentary, along with responsa and letters from holy Geonim. The surviving copy contains only 32 pages of the original. It served the Shinava-Stropkov community after the Holocaust.

title_en: Vilna 'Siddur with Likutei Torah' of Chabad's Alter Rebbe
summary_en: A Siddur with selected Chassidic discourses (Likutei Torah) from the Alter Rebbe's writings, arranged by the order of prayer, was issued in Vilna.
story_body: In 5672 (1912), a Siddur was published in Vilna containing Likutei Torah—Chassidic discourses drawn from the writings of the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman of Liadi, arranged according to the order of the prayers. The 360-leaf octavo edition made the Alter Rebbe's Chassidic teachings accessible alongside the daily liturgy. It served the Chabad community of Lithuania and beyond in the years before the Russian Revolution.

title_en: Zhitomir 'Seder HaTefilah' with Chabad Chassidic discourses by Alter Rebbe
summary_en: A two-volume Seder HaTefilah following the Arizal nusach with Chabad Chassidic discourses by the Alter Rebbe was printed in Zhitomir.
story_body: In 5623-5624 (1863-1864), a Seder HaTefilah containing all annual prayers according to the Arizal nusach was printed in Zhitomir, accompanied by Divrei Elokim Chayim Chassidic discourses by the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman. The two-volume quarto edition came to a total of 310 leaves. It became a foundational printed Siddur for the Chabad community.

title_en: Publication of Maamarei Admor HaZaken (collected discourses of the Alter Rebbe) in New York
summary_en: A collection of the Alter Rebbe's Chassidic discourses on the Torah portions and festivals was published in New York.
story_body: In 5743 (1983), 'Maamarei Admor HaZaken' was published in New York, containing the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman of Liadi's Chassidic discourses on the Torah portions and festivals. The Bereishit-Shemot volume ran 504 pages and the Vayikra-Devarim volume ran 1086 pages. The work made the Alter Rebbe's wealth of Chassidic teachings systematically available.

title_en: Publication of Maamarei Admur HaEmtza'i (Mittler Rebbe) discourses in New York
summary_en: Two volumes of the Mittler Rebbe Dovber's discourses on Vayikra were published in New York.
story_body: In 5745-5746 (1985-1986), 'Maamarei Admur HaEmtza'i' (the Mittler Rebbe Dovber Schneuri) on Sefer Vayikra was published in New York in two octavo volumes. Volume 1 ran 442 pages and Volume 2 contained pages 443-931, totaling almost 1000 pages. The work added critical primary-source Chabad material to the available canon.

title_en: Publication of Maamarei Maharash on Likutei Torah in New York
summary_en: The Chabad Maharash Rebbe Shmuel's discourses 'Torat Shmuel - Likutei Torah - Matzah Zu - 5640' were published in New York.
story_body: In 5705 (1945), 'Torat Shmuel - Likutei Torah - Matzah Zu - 5640' was published in New York, containing the Chassidic discourses of the Maharash Rebbe Shmuel Schneersohn of Lubavitch. The 94-page edition focused on the Pesach-related discourse 'Matzah Zu' delivered in 5640 (1880). It served the Chabad community's tradition of studying the Rebbes' annual maamarim.

title_en: Publication of Rashab Maamarim Likut Vol. 2 in New York
summary_en: Volume 2 of 'Sefer HaMaamarim - Likut' of the Rashab Rebbe was published in New York.
story_body: In 5753 (1993), 'Sefer HaMaamarim - Likut' Volume 2 of the Chabad Rashab Rebbe Shalom Dovber Schneersohn was published in New York. The 328-page octavo edition added to the publication of the fifth Chabad Rebbe's prolific Chassidic output. It maintained the Chabad publishing effort to release the discourses of the Rebbe Rashab in systematic order.

title_en: Publication of Rayatz's Kuntres Chag HaPesach 5708 in New York
summary_en: The Chabad Rayatz Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak's 'Kuntres Chag HaPesach 5708' was published in New York.
story_body: In 5708 (1948), Kuntres Chag HaPesach of the Chabad Rayatz Rebbe Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn was published in New York. The 29-page octavo edition contained the sixth Chabad Rebbe's discourses for the festival. It was issued during the Rebbe Rayatz's American years following his arrival in 1940.

title_en: Berditchev publication of Magen Avot drashot by Rebbe Mahara'sh of Kapust
summary_en: The Magen Avot drashot of Rebbe Shlomo Zalman of Kapust (the Mahara'sh of Kapust) on Sefer Vayikra were published in Berditchev.
story_body: In 5662 (1902), 'Magen Avot' — drashot of the Chabad-Kapust Rebbe Shlomo Zalman (Mahara'sh of Kapust) on Sefer Vayikra — was published in Berditchev. The 50-leaf folio edition preserved the teachings of the Kapust branch of Chabad, which split from the main Lubavitch line. It served the Kapust-Chabad community in the Russian Empire.

title_en: Berditchev Siddur 'Seder Tefilah' with Maharid of Liadi's commentary
summary_en: A Seder Tefilah Siddur with the Maharid of Liadi's Chassidic 'Pirush HaMilot' commentary was printed in Berditchev.
story_body: In 5673 (1913), a Seder Tefilah following the Arizal nusach as composed by the Alter Rebbe was published in Berditchev, accompanied by a Chassidic 'Pirush HaMilot' commentary by Rebbe Yitzchak Dovber Schneersohn (Maharid of Liadi). The two-volume octavo edition came with 217 plus 231 leaves of teachings. It supplemented the Chabad liturgical canon with the Maharid's distinctive interpretation.

title_en: 'Sod Kedoshim' Haggadah of the Alter Rebbe and Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye
summary_en: A 'Sod Kedoshim' Haggadah with commentaries by the Chabad Alter Rebbe and his disciple Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye was published.
story_body: In 5626 (1866), the Haggadah 'Sod Kedoshim' was published — possibly in Königsberg or Warsaw — featuring two commentaries: one by the Chabad Alter Rebbe Schneur Zalman of Liadi, and one by his disciple Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye. The 49-leaf quarto edition transmitted core Chabad teachings on the Passover Seder. It became a foundational Chabad Haggadah commentary.

title_en: Vilna publication of 'Maamar Yetziat Mitzrayim' by Yitzchak Aizik of Homil
summary_en: Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik HaLevi Epstein of Homil's 'Maamar Yetziat Mitzrayim' Chabad commentary was published in Vilna.
story_body: In 5637 (1877), 'Maamar Yetziat Mitzrayim' — a Chassidic Chabad commentary by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik HaLevi Epstein of Homil — was published in Vilna. The 29-leaf quarto edition expounded the inner meaning of the Exodus narrative according to Chabad Chassidic teaching. It served as a key text for Chabad students of the early Russian period.

title_en: Rebbe's first edition of Haggadah 'Likutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim' in New York
summary_en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson published his Haggadah 'Likutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim' in New York for the first time.
story_body: In 5706 (1946), the Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson published for the first time his Haggadah 'Likutei Minhagim u'Ta'amim' (Anthology of Customs and Reasons) in New York. The 47-page octavo edition presented a systematic anthology of Chabad customs and explanations for the Seder. It established the foundational Lubavitch Haggadah for subsequent decades and was reprinted dozens of times with additions over the following half-century.

title_en: Paris Haggadah of the Rebbe with French translation
summary_en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe's Haggadah with 'Likutei Ta'amim u'Minhagim' was published in Paris with a French translation.
story_body: In 5745 (1985), the Lubavitcher Rebbe's Haggadah with 'Likutei Ta'amim u'Minhagim' was issued in Paris with a French translation. The 191-page octavo edition (plus 173 French pages) served the growing French Chabad community. It marked a key expansion of the Rebbe's Haggadah into European languages.

title_en: Publication of 'At Our Rebbe's Seder Table' in English by Eliyahu Touger
summary_en: Eliyahu Touger published 'At Our Rebbe's Seder Table' in English in New York, an anthology of the Lubavitcher Rebbe's talks on the Haggadah.
story_body: In 5755 (1995), Eliyahu Touger published 'At Our Rebbe's Seder Table' in English in New York. The 119-page octavo edition collected the Lubavitcher Rebbe's talks on the Haggadah translated into English. It made the Rebbe's Pesach teachings accessible to English-speaking Chabad followers worldwide.

title_en: Lubavitcher Rebbe publishes Haggadah for children with English translation
summary_en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe issued a Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach with English Seder laws for children in New York.
story_body: In 5705 (1945), a Haggadah following the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with laws and Seder signs in English at its end. The 32-page octavo edition was designed for children. It launched the Lubavitcher Rebbe's project of producing Haggadot specifically suited for educating Jewish youth.

title_en: Hebrew-English Haggadah for children illustrated by Nachum Waldman and Boruch Gorkin
summary_en: A children's Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Nachum Waldman and Boruch Gorkin.
story_body: Around 5747 (1987), a Haggadah following the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Nachum Waldman and Boruch Gorkin. The 64-page octavo edition (also issued in a miniature format) targeted Chabad children. It contributed to the Rebbe's educational vision for Pesach observance.

title_en: Leeds Chabad children's Haggadah with English translation
summary_en: A children's Chabad Haggadah translated into English and illustrated for children was published by Tzeirei Agudat Chabad of Leeds.
story_body: In 5747 (1987), Tzeirei Agudat Chabad of Leeds published a Haggadah for children translated into English and illustrated. The 67-page octavo edition served the British Chabad children's community. It demonstrated Chabad's commitment to producing locally adapted children's Haggadot worldwide.

title_en: Hebrew-English Chabad Haggadah illustrated by Zalman Kleiman
summary_en: A Chabad Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Zalman Kleiman was published in New York.
story_body: In 5752 (1992), a Haggadah following the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach was published in New York with English translation by Yaakov Emanuel Schochet and illustrations by Zalman Kleiman. The 81-page quarto edition also appeared in a miniature format. Kleiman's distinctive illustrations became iconic in Chabad children's Haggadah publishing.

title_en: Chabad Russian-translation Haggadah issued by FREE in New York
summary_en: FREE published its 15th-edition Russian translation Haggadah in New York to serve Russian-speaking Jewish immigrants.
story_body: In 5751 (1991), the FREE organization (Friends of Refugees of Eastern Europe) published in New York the 15th edition of a Russian-translation Haggadah. The 36-page quarto edition served the wave of Russian-speaking Jewish immigrants arriving from the collapsing Soviet Union. It exemplified the Chabad-FREE initiative to make Jewish observance accessible to Soviet Jewry.

title_en: Chabad Russian-translation Haggadah by Dovber Chatzkelevich
summary_en: Dovber Chatzkelevich translated a Chabad Haggadah into Russian, published in New York.
story_body: In 5750 (1990), an 80-page octavo Haggadah with Russian translation by Dovber Chatzkelevich was published in New York. It served the rapidly expanding Russian-speaking Jewish community as the Iron Curtain began to fall. It joined the Chabad effort to provide Jewish liturgical texts in Russian for newly accessible Soviet Jews.

title_en: Chabad Spanish-translation Haggadah by Natan Greenblatt
summary_en: Natan Greenblatt translated a Chabad Haggadah into Spanish, with Zalman Kleiman's illustrations, published in New York.
story_body: In 5752 (1992), a Chabad Haggadah with Spanish translation by Natan Greenblatt and illustrations by Zalman Kleiman was published in New York. The landscape-format 17-page-plus-50-leaf edition served the growing Spanish-speaking Chabad communities in Latin America and the United States. It expanded the Chabad Haggadah project into the Spanish-speaking Jewish world.

title_en: Chabad Portuguese-translation Haggadah by Shmuel Asher Bigon
summary_en: Shmuel Asher Bigon translated a Chabad Haggadah into Portuguese, illustrated by Zalman Kleiman, published in New York.
story_body: In 5752 (1992), Shmuel Asher Bigon's Portuguese translation of the Chabad Haggadah, with Zalman Kleiman's illustrations, was published in New York. The 84-page quarto edition served Brazilian and Portuguese-speaking Jewish communities. It continued the Chabad project of issuing the Haggadah in major world languages.

title_en: Chabad Persian-translation Haggadah by Yehoshua Netaneli
summary_en: Yehoshua Netaneli's Persian translation of the Chabad Haggadah was published in New York.
story_body: In 5746 (1986), Yehoshua Netaneli's Persian-language translation of the Chabad Haggadah was published in New York. The 68-page octavo edition served the Persian-speaking Jewish community of Iranian background. It supported the Chabad project of reaching Persian Jews displaced by the 1979 Iranian Revolution.

title_en: Chabad Haggadah for Kfar Chabad youth published
summary_en: Tzeirei Agudat Chabad in the Holy Land published a Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach for Kfar Chabad youth.
story_body: In 5721 (1961), Tzeirei Agudat Chabad in the Holy Land published a Haggadah for youth visiting Kfar Chabad. The 32-page sixteenmo edition was based on the Chabad Alter Rebbe's nusach. A second printing followed in 5732 (1972) for the next generation of Israeli Chabad youth.

title_en: Kfar Chabad Haggadah with additions on matzah campaign
summary_en: A Kfar Chabad Haggadah added material on chametz, matzah, the Mivtza Matzah campaign, and the 12 Pesukim was published.
story_body: In 5737 (1977), Kfar Chabad published a Haggadah following the Alter Rebbe's nusach with added sections on chametz and matzah, the Mivtza Matzah campaign, and the 12 Pesukim (twelve verses). The 69-page duodecimo edition served the Israeli Chabad community. It exemplified the Rebbe's worldwide matzah campaign.

title_en: Kfar Chabad Haggadah with 'Pesach BiTzva'im' children's booklet
summary_en: Menachem Mendel Brod edited a Kfar Chabad Haggadah with a 'Pesach BiTzva'im' (Pesach in Color) photographic children's booklet.
story_body: In 5747 (1987), Menachem Mendel Brod edited a 40-page Haggadah printed in blue letters in Kfar Chabad, accompanied by a 22-leaf 'Pesach BiTzva'im' (Pesach in Color) booklet with photographs and illustrations for the Seder night. The duodecimo edition served Chabad children visually and pedagogically. It exemplified Chabad's emphasis on visual learning for Pesach.

title_en: Kfar Chabad Haggadah with 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' practical guide by Yekutiel Green
summary_en: Yekutiel Green compiled the 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' practical Chabad Haggadah guide, published in Kfar Chabad.
story_body: In 5746 (1986), Yekutiel Green's practical Chabad Haggadah guide 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' was published in Kfar Chabad following the Alter Rebbe's nusach. The 127-page octavo edition included practical guidance and Chabad anthological 'pearls'. A revised expanded edition followed in 5754 (1994).

title_en: English-language 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' Chabad Haggadah translated by Moshe Miller
summary_en: Moshe Miller translated Yekutiel Green's 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' Chabad Haggadah into English.
story_body: In 5755 (1995), Moshe Miller's English translation of Yekutiel Green's Chabad practical guide Haggadah 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' was published. The 334-page octavo edition expanded access to Chabad Pesach teaching for English-speaking Jews worldwide. It served as a definitive English Chabad Pesach resource.

title_en: Shmuel Horowitz's Yiddish children's Haggadah 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' in New York
summary_en: Shmuel Horowitz published 'V'Higadta L'Vincha' in Yiddish, a children's Mah Nishtanah and Seder guide with illustrations, in New York.
story_body: In 5743 (1983), Shmuel Horowitz published in New York 'V'Higadta L'Vincha', a Yiddish-language children's guide containing Mah Nishtanah, Seder laws and customs for cheder-aged children, with explanations and illustrations. The 31-page octavo edition served the Yiddish-speaking Chabad community in America. It maintained the Yiddish heritage in Chabad children's Pesach education.

title_en: Albany Haggadah 'Kuntres Marbeh L'Saper' on personalities in the Haggadah
summary_en: Yisrael Rubin, Chabad shaliach in Albany, published 'Kuntres Marbeh L'Saper' with notes on the personalities mentioned in the Haggadah.
story_body: In 5756 (1996), Yisrael Rubin, the Chabad shaliach in Albany, New York, published 'Kuntres Marbeh L'Saper' (The Albany Haggadah), containing notes and studies on the personalities mentioned in the Haggadah. The 110-plus-10-page octavo edition exemplified the personalized scholarly Haggadah pamphlets produced by Chabad emissaries. It served the Albany Chabad community.

title_en: Tefilot LeKol HaShanah with Chinuch HaDat introduction printed in Vilna
summary_en: A Tefilot LeKol HaShanah following the Arizal nusach with laws drawn from the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was printed in Vilna.
story_body: In 5671 (1911), 'Tefilot LeKol HaShanah' was printed in Vilna following the Arizal nusach with laws drawn from the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch, marginal notes by 'Torah Or', reading marks, tagim and other details. It opened with an essay titled 'Chinuch HaDat V'HaLashon' (Religious and Linguistic Education). The 168-leaf octavo edition served the Chabad community of Lithuania before World War I.

title_en: Sefer Avodas HaLevi by Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Staroshelye published
summary_en: First edition of Avodas HaLevi by Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Staroshelye was published in Lvov.
story_body: Rabbi Aharon HaLevi of Staroshelye was a leading disciple of the Alter Rebbe whose writings became foundational texts of Chabad chassidus. This first edition of Avodas HaLevi was printed in Lvov in 5602 (1842) and is now displayed in the Library's exhibition of works by the great Chabad chassidim.

title_en: Maamar HaShiflus VeHaSimcha by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published
summary_en: First edition of Maamar HaShiflus VeHaSimcha by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil appeared in 5628.
story_body: Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was a leading chassid of the Alter Rebbe, Mitteler Rebbe, and Tzemach Tzedek. His Maamar HaShiflus VeHaSimcha, an explication of chassidic teachings on lowliness and joy, was first printed in 5628 (1868) and is now exhibited at the Lubavitch Library.

title_en: Likkutei Biurim on Kuntres HaHispaalus by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch published
summary_en: First Warsaw edition of Likkutei Biurim on Kuntres HaHispaalus by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch was printed in 5628.
story_body: Rabbi Hillel of Paritch, a foremost chassid of the Mitteler Rebbe and Tzemach Tzedek, wrote extensive commentaries on the Rebbeim's chassidic discourses. His Likkutei Biurim on Kuntres HaHispaalus was first printed in Warsaw in 5628 (1868).

title_en: Imrei Noam by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch published in Vilna
summary_en: First edition of Imrei Noam by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch was printed in Vilna in 5636.
story_body: Rabbi Hillel of Paritch wrote his own chassidic discourses and commentaries on those of the Rebbeim. Imrei Noam was first printed in Vilna in 5636 (1876) and is displayed at the Lubavitch Library exhibition of the great Chabad chassidim.

title_en: Maamar Yetzias Mitzrayim by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published
summary_en: First Vilna edition of Maamar Yetzias Mitzrayim by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was printed in 5637.
story_body: This discourse on the Exodus by the great chassid Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was first printed in Vilna in 5637 (1877). It is one of several of his works exhibited in the Lubavitch Library's Rabboseinu exhibition.

title_en: First printing of the Alter Rebbe's portrait with engraver's signature
summary_en: The first printed portrait of the Alter Rebbe, signed by engraver Glatzbesky, appeared in 5649.
story_body: The earliest known printing of the Alter Rebbe's portrait bears the signature of the engraver Glatzbesky. Below the image are lines in Hebrew and Russian signed by the publishers Rabbi Shmaryahu Schneersohn and Z. Sh"Tz. The print is now displayed at the Lubavitch Library.

title_en: First printing of the Tzemach Tzedek's portrait in Vilna
summary_en: The Tzemach Tzedek's portrait was first printed in Vilna in 5656 with Hebrew and Russian captions.
story_body: A printed portrait of the third Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, was issued in Vilna in 5656 (1896) with bilingual Hebrew-Russian text beneath. The image is preserved in the Lubavitch Library and exhibited alongside other portraits of the Rebbeim.

title_en: Birth of Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka
summary_en: The Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka was born in 5661; the Rashab sent a mazal tov letter to mark her birth.
story_body: The Rebbetzin Chaya Mushka, future wife of the seventh Rebbe, was born in 5661 (1901). Her grandfather, the Rebbe Rashab, wrote a personal mazal tov letter on the occasion of her birth, which is preserved and displayed at the Lubavitch Library exhibition on family purity and Chabad life events.

title_en: Chana Ariel by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published in Berditchev
summary_en: First edition of Chana Ariel by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was printed in Berditchev in 5672.
story_body: Chana Ariel is a major chassidic work by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil, an outstanding disciple of the first three Chabad Rebbeim. The first edition appeared in Berditchev in 5672 (1912) and is exhibited at the Lubavitch Library.

title_en: Maamar Shnei HaMeoros by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil published
summary_en: First edition of Maamar Shnei HaMeoros by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was printed in Poltava in 5675.
story_body: This chassidic discourse by Rabbi Yitzchak Aizik of Homil was first printed in Poltava in 5675 (1915). It is one of several of his works in the Lubavitch Library's exhibition devoted to the great chassidim of Chabad.

title_en: Pelach HaRimon by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch published in Vilna
summary_en: First edition of Pelach HaRimon by Rabbi Hillel of Paritch printed in Vilna in 5678.
story_body: Pelach HaRimon, one of Rabbi Hillel of Paritch's major chassidic compositions, was first printed in Vilna in 5678 (1918). The volume is displayed at the Lubavitch Library exhibition celebrating the great Chabad chassidim.

title_en: Alter Rebbe micrographic portrait copyrighted in Washington
summary_en: A micrographic portrait of the Alter Rebbe formed of letters of his Tanya was copyrighted in Washington in 1924.
story_body: Artist Natanel Chazan created a portrait of the Alter Rebbe in which the image is composed entirely of the letters of his Tanya. The print was copyrighted in Washington, D.C. in 1924 and is now part of the Lubavitch Library's exhibition of portraits of the Rebbeim.

title_en: Rayatz launches family purity campaign on first US visit
summary_en: During his first US visit in 5690, the Rayatz founded women's leagues for family purity in numerous American towns.
story_body: On his first visit to the United States in 5690 (1930), the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe (Rayatz) confronted widespread ignorance of family purity and founded leagues of women in many towns to strengthen observance. This work is described in Toldos Chabad B'Artzos HaBris chapter 11.

title_en: Gertrude Zuckerkandel paints portraits of the Rebbe Rashab
summary_en: Artist Gertrude Zuckerkandel signed and dated four paintings of the Rebbe Rashab in 1935.
story_body: Four previously unpublished portraits of the Rebbe Rashab were found in a wall-cabinet of the Rayatz's yechidus room. Three are signed by Gertrude Zuckerkandel and dated 1935 (5695) — fifteen years after the Rashab's passing — leading to scholarly discussion as to whether they depict the Rashab from memory or are partly based on his son the Rayatz.

title_en: Piskei HaSiddur by Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh published in Jerusalem
summary_en: First edition of Piskei HaSiddur by Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh was printed in Jerusalem in 5697.
story_body: Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh, author of Ketzos HaShulchan, published his Piskei HaSiddur in Jerusalem in 5697 (1937). It is displayed at the Lubavitch Library's exhibition of works by the great chassidim of Chabad.

title_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson arrested by Soviet authorities
summary_en: The Rebbe's father, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson of Yekaterinoslav, was arrested in 5699 for his work spreading Judaism.
story_body: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson, kabbalist and rabbi of Yekaterinoslav and father of the seventh Rebbe, was arrested by the Soviet regime in 5699 (1939) as punishment for promoting Jewish observance. A photograph of him taken on the day of his arrest is preserved in the Lubavitch Library.

title_en: First Mesibos Shabbos children's parade
summary_en: A children's parade through the city streets was held in 5703 to publicly affirm Torah and mitzvos.
story_body: While the Rebbe headed the Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch before his nesius, he ran the Mesibos Shabbos campaign for children. In 5703 (1943) a public parade was organized through main streets, with children carrying signs about Torah and mitzvos after hearing the Rebbe speak. A special booklet with photos was published. The parade later became an annual Lag BaOmer event.

title_en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson released from Soviet exile
summary_en: After five years of Soviet exile, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was released in 5704.
story_body: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson was released from Soviet exile in 5704 (1944). A photograph taken after his release so changed his appearance that the Rebbe, on first seeing it, wrote in disbelief 'AAZ"L?' — 'is this truly my late father?' During his exile his wife Rebbetzin Chana joined him and produced ink from local plants so he could write his Torah glosses.

title_en: Tzeirei Agudas Chabad founded in Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In summer 5711 the Rebbe founded Tzeirei Agudas Chabad in Eretz Yisrael to spread Judaism among youth.
story_body: Soon after assuming the nesius, the Rebbe founded the Tzeirei Agudas Chabad youth organization in Eretz Yisrael in the summer of 5711 (1951), as described in the introduction to Igros Kodesh vol. 5. The organization was tasked with spreading Yiddishkeit and chassidus among broad circles of Jewish youth.

title_en: Agudas Nshei UVnos Chabad founded
summary_en: The Rebbe founded Agudas Nshei UVnos Chabad in 5711 to strengthen Jewish observance among women.
story_body: In the same year 5711 (1951), the Rebbe founded Agudas Nshei UVnos Chabad, the women's and girls' organization, to lead campaigns for general Jewish observance and especially family purity, kashrus, and kosher education.

title_en: Alter Rebbe portrait printed by Kehot
summary_en: Kehot published a print of the Alter Rebbe's portrait in 5712.
story_body: Kehot Publication Society issued a print of the Alter Rebbe's portrait in 5712 (1952), with a colored version also produced by an artist. Both versions hang in the Lubavitch Library's portrait exhibition.

title_en: Tzemach Tzedek and Rayatz portraits printed by Kehot
summary_en: Kehot issued portrait prints of the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rayatz in 5713.
story_body: In 5713 (1953), Kehot Publication Society printed portraits of both the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rayatz writing chassidus. A colored version of the Rayatz print was also produced. The prints are displayed in the Lubavitch Library.

title_en: First Chabad girls' summer camp founded
summary_en: The Rebbe founded the first Chabad girls' summer camp, Machaneh Emunah, in summer 5713.
story_body: In summer 5713 (1953) the Rebbe founded a dedicated summer camp for girls, later named Machaneh Emunah. The Rebbe explained that the influence achievable in summer camp far exceeds that of the school year. The camp model rapidly spread to Chabad centers worldwide.

title_en: Rebbe launches Shmurah Matzah campaign on Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh
summary_en: At a Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh 5714 farbrengen the Rebbe called for distributing shmurah matzah broadly.
story_body: At the Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh farbrengen of 5714 (1954), the Rebbe declared a request — 'lu yeyasher cheili' even a mitzvah — that all who can influence others should ensure they receive shmurah matzah for Pesach. The campaign grew over the years into a worldwide distribution reaching hundreds of thousands of Jews.

title_en: Arba Minim campaign launched
summary_en: The Rebbe founded the Arba Minim campaign in 5714 to bring the four species to Jews on Sukkos.
story_body: In 5714 (1954) the Rebbe established the campaign of bringing the four species to fellow Jews on Sukkos. Letters in Igros Kodesh vol. 12 describe inviting passersby to make the blessing and visiting hospitals and convalescent homes, which the Rebbe noted was particularly successful in 5716.

title_en: Rebbe receives Slavita Sefer Torah
summary_en: Late in 5714 the Rebbe received the Slavita Sefer Torah, written by the imprisoned Slavita brothers, and kept it close ever after.
story_body: In late 5714 (1954) the Rebbe received the small Sefer Torah of the Slavita brothers — the holy printers arrested by the Tzarist government, who read from this scroll during their many years of imprisonment. From then on the Rebbe used it for his aliyos on Shabbos and Monday/Thursday, and held it during Hakafos. A wall-mounted Aron Kodesh was built to house it and later transferred to the Library.

title_en: Tzeirei Agudas Chabad founded in the United States
summary_en: In 5715 the Rebbe founded Tzeirei Agudas Chabad in the United States.
story_body: In 5715 (1955), the Rebbe founded Tzeirei Agudas Chabad in the United States. In a special letter (Igros Kodesh vol. 11 letter 3429), he laid out a detailed program of activity for spreading Judaism and chassidus among broad circles of Jewish youth.

title_en: First Chabad boys' summer camp Gan Yisroel founded
summary_en: The Rebbe founded the first Chabad boys' summer camp, Gan Yisroel, in summer 5716.
story_body: In summer 5716 (1956) the Rebbe founded the first boys' summer camp and named it Gan Yisroel. The Rebbe personally visited the camps from 5716 through 5720 (1956-1960), and at a Shavuos 5716 talk explained the unique educational influence camps exert on children.

title_en: Beis Lubavitch established in London
summary_en: A central Chabad building was purchased in London in 5718 and named 'Beis Lubavitch' by the Rebbe.
story_body: In 5718 (1958), a building was purchased in London to serve as a regional Chabad headquarters. The Rebbe instructed it be named 'Beis Lubavitch' (Igros Kodesh vols. 17-18). When construction was completed, the building's key was sent to the Rebbe, who responded with a special letter expressing great satisfaction at the milestone.

title_en: Rebbe declares 'U'fartzta' expansion on 12 Tammuz
summary_en: At a 12 Tammuz 5718 sicha the Rebbe declared the 'U'fartzta' campaign of unrestricted outreach.
story_body: In a sicha on 12 Tammuz 5718 (summer 1958), the Rebbe announced the campaign of 'U'fartzta' — bursting through all barriers in spreading chassidus and Judaism. This call, repeated throughout 5718-5719, marked the beginning of a major expansion in the shlichus enterprise (Igros Kodesh vol. 18 letter 6541).

title_en: Purim children's campaign letter sent by Rebbe's secretariat
summary_en: In early Adar 5721 the Rebbe's secretariat sent a general letter urging organized Purim observance by children.
story_body: At the beginning of Adar 5721 (1961), the Rebbe directed his secretariat to send a general letter to institutions, rabbis, yeshiva heads, teachers, and parents, urging organized efforts to ensure every child observes the mitzvos of Purim — especially mishloach manos and matanos l'evyonim — themselves (Igros Kodesh vol. 20 letter 7598).

title_en: First Chabad charter flight from Eretz Yisrael to the Rebbe
summary_en: In Elul 5722 the first charter flight of chassidim from Eretz Yisrael came to the Rebbe, carrying a wooden amud as a gift.
story_body: In Elul 5722 (August/September 1962), the first chartered flight of chassidim traveled from Eretz Yisrael to be with the Rebbe. They brought an amud (prayer-leader's stand) crafted at the trade school in Kfar Chabad. The amud was presented at a special farbrengen the Rebbe held in honor of the guests on the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723.

title_en: Special farbrengen for charter-flight guests on eve of Rosh Hashana 5723
summary_en: On the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723 the Rebbe held a special farbrengen for visiting chassidim and explained the meaning of the amud.
story_body: At the special farbrengen held on the eve of Rosh Hashana 5723 (September 1962) for the chassidim who had come on the charter flight, the Rebbe spoke about the maaleh of the amud they had presented. He related the famous story in which the Mitteler Rebbe asked his father the Alter Rebbe what he had prayed with on Rosh Hashana, and was answered 'with the shtender' — for all is G-dliness and 'He alone is, and there is none besides Him.'

title_en: Tefillin campaign launched during the Six-Day War
summary_en: In summer 5727 during the Six-Day War the Rebbe launched the first formal mitzvah campaign — Mivtza Tefillin.
story_body: During the Six-Day War in summer 5727 (1967), the Rebbe launched Mivtza Tefillin, the first of his formal mitzvah campaigns, citing the verse that the nations will see G-d's name on Israel — interpreted as the tefillin of the head — and thereby fear them, bringing victory over their enemies.

title_en: First Beis Chabad opens in Los Angeles
summary_en: The first Beis Chabad opened in Los Angeles in 5729; its golden key was sent to the Rebbe.
story_body: In 5729 (1969) the first 'Beis Chabad' opened in Los Angeles, and its golden key was delivered to the Rebbe. The Rebbe replied to those presenting the key that a chain of Chabad Houses would now spread across the length and breadth of the country, and wrote a special letter marking the occasion.

title_en: Likkutei Levi Yitzchak printed by Kehot
summary_en: Kehot published Likkutei Levi Yitzchak on Zohar and on Tanya in 5730 from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's exile-era glosses.
story_body: The marginal notes that Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson wrote on his few books during his Soviet exile of 5699-5704 (1939-1944) miraculously reached his son the Rebbe, who from 5730-5743 (1970-1983) prepared them for print. The first volumes — Likkutei Levi Yitzchak on Zohar and on Tanya — were published by Kehot in 5730 (1970).

title_en: Toras Levi Yitzchak on Shas printed by Kehot
summary_en: Kehot published Toras Levi Yitzchak on Shas in 5731 from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's notes.
story_body: In 5731 (1971), Kehot published Toras Levi Yitzchak on the Talmud, derived from the glosses Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson — father of the seventh Rebbe — had written during his Soviet exile.

title_en: Rebbe calls to 'conquer the world' with Torah on 15 Shvat
summary_en: On 15 Shvat 5731 the Rebbe issued a call to 'conquer' the world through Torah study.
story_body: In a sicha on 15 Shvat 5731 (1971), the Rebbe issued a call to 'conquer' the world through the study of Torah (Likkutei Sichos vol. 6 p. 312). This call became the foundation of Mivtza Torah and a series of subsequent Torah-related campaigns.

title_en: Rebbe's 70th birthday: Vaad 71 Mosdos established
summary_en: On his 70th birthday, 11 Nissan 5732, the Rebbe established the Vaad 71 Mosdos to found 71 new institutions.
story_body: On 11 Nissan 5732 (1972), the Rebbe's 70th birthday, he declared that rather than slowing his pace at this age, activity must be intensified and expanded. He established the 'Vaad 71 Mosdos' — a project to found 71 new institutions during the coming 71st year of his life, fueling a major expansion of shlichus.

title_en: Rebbe directs founding of libraries on 6 Tishrei
summary_en: At a 6 Tishrei 5733 farbrengen the Rebbe directed founding sacred-book libraries worldwide.
story_body: At the 6 Tishrei 5733 (1972) farbrengen, the Rebbe directed his chassidim to found libraries of sacred books across the world. Dozens of new libraries opened at Chabad Houses in various countries, including one founded by Tzeirei Agudas Chabad of New York which the Rebbe named 'Sifriyat Levi Yitzchak' in honor of his father.

title_en: Mitzvah Tank name adopted by the Rebbe
summary_en: In 5734 the Rebbe adopted the name 'Mitzvah Tank' for outreach vehicles and called their operators 'tankistim.'
story_body: In 5734 (1974) the Rebbe adopted the name 'Tank HaMitzvos' (Mitzvah Tank) for the outreach vehicles used by shluchim to bring Yiddishkeit to every corner, with their operators called 'tankistim.' The Rebbe regularly handed out coins or bills for tzedakah through them to express appreciation for their work.

title_en: Rebbe declares 'House Full of Books' campaign on Shabbos Bamidbar
summary_en: On Shabbos Parshas Bamidbar 5734 the Rebbe launched the 'Bayis Malei Sefarim — Yavneh VeChachameha' campaign.
story_body: On Shabbos Parshas Bamidbar 5734 (1974), the Rebbe announced a special campaign — 'A House Full of Books — Yavneh and Her Sages' — urging every Jew to fill his home with sacred books and to increase Torah study.

title_en: Rebbe calls women and girls to light Shabbos candles
summary_en: On 24 Elul 5734 the Rebbe issued a special call for every woman and girl to light Shabbos candles.
story_body: In a special sicha on 24 Elul 5734 (1974), the Rebbe called for every Jewish woman and girl — including girls below marriageable age, from the age of education — to light Shabbos and Yom Tov candles. The campaign produced an enormous worldwide distribution of candlesticks and educational materials.

title_en: Rebbe launches Chanukah candle distribution on Shabbos Vayeshev
summary_en: On Shabbos Parshas Vayeshev 5734 the Rebbe directed intensifying the worldwide distribution of menorahs and Chanukah candles.
story_body: At the Shabbos Parshas Vayeshev 5734 farbrengen (December 1973), the Rebbe directed intensified efforts that every Jewish home light Chanukah candles, with menorahs distributed free to those unable to afford them, and that soldiers in Eretz Yisrael also be helped to fulfill the mitzvah (Sichos Kodesh 5734 p. 196).

title_en: Family Purity campaign launched on 15 Tammuz
summary_en: On 15 Tammuz 5735 the Rebbe directed launching a broad education campaign for family purity.
story_body: In a special sicha on 15 Tammuz 5735 (1975), the Rebbe directed the launching of a broad education and outreach campaign to strengthen family purity observance (Likkutei Sichos vol. 13 pp. 259-260). This established family purity as one of the ongoing mivtzaim of Chabad.

title_en: Yagdil Torah institute founded on 20 Av
summary_en: At a 20 Av 5736 farbrengen the Rebbe announced founding centers in Jerusalem and New York to collect the Rebbeim's chiddushei Torah.
story_body: At the 20 Menachem Av 5736 (1976) farbrengen, the Rebbe announced the founding of a special institute — with centers in both Jerusalem and New York — to collect novellae of the Lubavitcher Rebbeim and publish them in a special compilation. The publication was later named 'Yagdil Torah.'

title_en: Institute for preparing Rebbeim's maamarim founded on Shavuos 5738
summary_en: On Shavuos 5738 the Rebbe announced founding an institute to prepare the Rebbeim's chassidic discourses for print.
story_body: In a special sicha on Shavuos 5738 (1978), the Rebbe announced the opening of an institute dedicated to preparing the chassidic discourses of the previous Rebbeim for publication. The institute produced the series of Maamarei Admur HaZaken, Maamarei Admur HaEmtzaei, Ohr HaTorah of the Tzemach Tzedek, Toras Shmuel of the Rebbe Maharash, and Sefer HaMaamarim of the Rashab and Rayatz — about two hundred new volumes prepared from manuscript.

title_en: Aseres HaDibros children's campaign announced
summary_en: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5740 the Rebbe launched a campaign that all children attend shul to hear Aseres HaDibros on Shavuos.
story_body: In a special sicha on Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5740 (1980), the Rebbe announced a special Shavuos campaign — that all children, even toddlers, be brought to synagogue to hear the reading of the Aseres HaDibros (Likkutei Sichos vol. 23 p. 50).

title_en: Rebbe issues call against family planning on Shabbos Naso
summary_en: On Shabbos Parshas Naso 5740 the Rebbe issued a special call against family planning.
story_body: On Shabbos Parshas Naso 5740 (1980), the Rebbe issued a special call for a campaign against family planning, and repeated and amplified the call in many sichos throughout that summer.

title_en: Tzivos Hashem founded
summary_en: In 5741 the Rebbe founded the Tzivos Hashem children's organization based on 'gather the little ones.'
story_body: In 5741 (1981) the Rebbe founded Tzivos Hashem, the children's organization, building on the verse 'Hakhel… the children' so that even young boys and girls would influence their friends to walk in the ways of Torah and chassidus.

title_en: Children's Sefer Torah project launched in Nissan 5741
summary_en: In Nissan 5741 the Rebbe directed beginning a special Sefer Torah in Jerusalem uniting Jewish children before bar mitzvah.
story_body: In Nissan 5741 (1981) sichos, the Rebbe directed the writing of a special Sefer Torah in Jerusalem in which Jewish children below bar mitzvah age would unite by purchasing letters.

title_en: Tomchei Tmimim and Beis Rivkah Sifrei Torah announced
summary_en: On the eve of Rosh Hashana 5742 the Rebbe directed beginning a Sefer Torah for Tomchei Tmimim students and one for Beis Rivkah girls.
story_body: In a special sicha on the eve of Rosh Hashana 5742 (1981), the Rebbe directed the writing of a special Sefer Torah by Yeshivas Tomchei Tmimim for its students, and a separate Sefer Torah by Beis Rivkah for its female students.

title_en: Toras Levi Yitzchak Yalkut Shimoni supplement published
summary_en: Kehot published a Toras Levi Yitzchak supplement on Yalkut Shimoni and tractate Gittin in 5739.
story_body: In 5739 (1979), Kehot published a supplementary volume of Toras Levi Yitzchak — comprising glosses on Yalkut Shimoni and on tractate Gittin from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's exile-era writings.

title_en: Toras Levi Yitzchak Tehillim and Purim supplement published
summary_en: Kehot published a Toras Levi Yitzchak supplement on Tehillim and Purim in 5743.
story_body: In 5743 (1983), Kehot published the final supplement of Toras Levi Yitzchak, comprising notes on Tehillim and on Purim from Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Schneerson's writings. This concluded the publishing of his Soviet-exile glosses that the Rebbe had been preparing since 5730.

title_en: Daily Rambam study program instituted on Acharon shel Pesach
summary_en: On Acharon shel Pesach 5744 the Rebbe instituted daily Rambam study in three tracks.
story_body: In a special sicha on Acharon shel Pesach 5744 (1984), the Rebbe instituted the daily study of Rambam's Mishneh Torah in three tracks — three chapters per day, one chapter per day, and Sefer HaMitzvos (Likkutei Sichos vol. 27 p. 229).

title_en: 'Shliach Oseh Shliach' program launched on Shabbos Bereishis
summary_en: On Shabbos Bereishis 5745 the Rebbe announced the 'shliach oseh shliach' program to appoint additional shluchim.
story_body: On Shabbos Bereishis 5745 (1984), the Rebbe announced the 'shliach oseh shliach' program — each shliach to appoint an additional shliach for his city — and pledged to fund two-thirds of the new shluchim's first-year expenses (Hisva'aduyos 5745 vol. 1 p. 461). This led to the founding of the annual Kinus Hashluchim near 770, held each year around Rosh Chodesh Kislev.

title_en: Beis Chabad expansion campaign declared on 5th candle of Chanukah
summary_en: On the 5th candle of Chanukah 5746 the Rebbe established expanding Beis Chabad as a special mivtza and pledged matching funds.
story_body: In a special sicha on the 5th candle of Chanukah 5746 (December 1985), the Rebbe established expansion of Beis Chabad as a special campaign (Likkutei Sichos vol. 25 p. 400). He pledged to contribute matching funds to anyone who would found or expand a Beis Chabad in their place of shlichus.

title_en: Children's home declared a Beis Chabad on Shabbos Vayigash
summary_en: On Shabbos Vayigash 5747 the Rebbe directed Tzivos Hashem children to designate a room in their home as a Beis Chabad.
story_body: On Shabbos Parshas Vayigash 5747 (December 1986), the Rebbe directed children of Tzivos Hashem to fix a special sign in their home declaring that the room — or the home — is a 'Beis Chabad' (Hisva'aduyos 5747 pp. 208-212).

title_en: Painting of Rebbe receiving pidyonos
summary_en: Artist A.K. Tiefenbrun painted the Rebbe receiving pidyonos in 5752.
story_body: In 5752 (1992) the artist A.K. Tiefenbrun painted a depiction of the Rebbe receiving pidyonos. The work is displayed in the Lubavitch Library's exhibition of portraits of the Rebbeim.

title_en: Lubavitch Library exhibition hall opens on 18 Elul
summary_en: The Lubavitch Library exhibition hall opened on 18 Elul 5754.
story_body: The exhibition hall of the Library of Agudas Chasidei Chabad - Ohel Yosef Yitzchak - Lubavitch opened on 18 Elul 5754 (September 1994). Over the following years it hosted a sequence of major exhibitions on Chabad history, manuscripts, sacred objects, and the work of the seventh Rebbe.

title_en: Rabboseinu exhibition opens on 18 Elul
summary_en: The Rabboseinu exhibition of the Lubavitch Library opened on 18 Elul 5756.
story_body: The fourth exhibition of the Library — Taarukhas Rabboseinu — opened on 18 Elul 5756 (1996), the joint birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe. It displayed first editions of the Rebbeim's works, manuscripts, sacred objects, and portraits, with dedicated cases for the Baal Shem Tov, Maggid of Mezeritch, and each of the Chabad Rebbeim.

title_en: Chabad activities exhibition opens on Lag BaOmer 5757
summary_en: The fifth Library exhibition on Chabad activities, shlichus and mivtzaim opened on Lag BaOmer 5757.
story_body: On Lag BaOmer 5757 (1997) the fifth major Library exhibition opened — Taarukhas Chabad: HaPe'ilus, HaShlichus UMivtza'ei HaMitzvos. It presented the worldwide network of more than two thousand institutions run by the Rebbe's shluchim and the mivtzaim he founded over the half-century of his nesius, organized into thirteen themed display cases.

title_en: Rebbe declares Mivtza Torah, Mezuzah, Tzedakah, Bayis Malei Sefarim, Neshek
summary_en: During 5734, the Rebbe declared the mitzvah campaigns of Torah, Mezuzah, Tzedakah, a House Full of Books, and Shabbat Candles.
story_body: In the year 5734 (1973–74), the Lubavitcher Rebbe launched several mitzvah campaigns aimed at strengthening Jewish observance worldwide. These included Mivtza Torah, Mezuzah, Tzedakah, Bayis Malei Sefarim (Yavneh v'Chachameha), and Neshek (Shabbat candle lighting). The campaigns were a hallmark of the Rebbe's outreach efforts.

title_en: Rebbe declares Mivtza Kashrut and Taharat HaMishpacha
summary_en: In 5735, the Rebbe declared the campaigns of Kashrut and Taharat HaMishpacha (family purity).
story_body: Continuing his series of mitzvah campaigns, in the year 5735 (1974–75) the Rebbe declared Mivtza Kashrut and Mivtza Taharat HaMishpacha. These campaigns aimed to strengthen observance of dietary laws and family purity among world Jewry.

title_en: Rebbe declares Mivtza Chinuch and Ahavat Yisrael; year of education
summary_en: In 5736, the Rebbe declared the campaigns of Chinuch and Ahavat Yisrael and designated the year as a 'Year of Education.'
story_body: In 5736 (1975–76), the Rebbe declared the campaigns of Chinuch (Jewish education) and Ahavat Yisrael (love of fellow Jew), and proclaimed the year a 'Year of Education.' He spoke about education at numerous farbrengens that summer and instructed children to memorize the Twelve Pesukim and sayings of Chazal. Special children's rallies were held at which the Rebbe addressed the children and listened to their recitation.

title_en: Previous Rebbe declares 'Immediate Teshuvah, Immediate Redemption'
summary_en: In 5701, the Frierdiker Rebbe (Rayatz) declared the campaign of 'L'alter L'teshuvah, L'alter L'geulah.'
story_body: In 5701 (1940–41), Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the sixth Lubavitcher Rebbe, declared the famous slogan 'L'alter L'teshuvah, L'alter L'geulah' (immediate repentance, immediate redemption) shortly after arriving in the United States. This call set the tone for ongoing Chabad efforts to hasten the redemption.

title_en: Frierdiker Rebbe begins writing Torah scroll to greet Moshiach
summary_en: In 5702, the Frierdiker Rebbe began writing a special Torah scroll to greet Moshiach.
story_body: In 5702 (1941–42), the Previous Rebbe initiated the writing of a special Sefer Torah intended to welcome Moshiach. He began the writing but did not complete it in his lifetime; the completion would only be announced decades later by his son-in-law and successor.

title_en: Rebbe announces completion of Moshiach Torah scroll
summary_en: In the winter of 5730, the Rebbe announced the completion of the Sefer Torah to greet Moshiach, finished on Yud Shevat.
story_body: In the winter of 5730 (1970), the Rebbe announced the completion of the Sefer Torah for greeting Moshiach that the Frierdiker Rebbe had begun writing in 5702. The scroll was finished on Yud Shevat. Special pamphlets were printed publicizing the writing, and individuals purchased letters in the Torah.

title_en: Rebbe initiates study of Beit HaBechirah during Bein HaMetzarim
summary_en: On the eve of Shabbat Mevarchim Menachem Av 5736, the Rebbe called for study of the laws of the Beit HaMikdash during the Three Weeks.
story_body: In a special sichah delivered on Thursday night, the eve of Shabbat Mevarchim Menachem Av 5736 (1976), the Rebbe urged the study of topics related to the Beit HaBechirah during the days of Bein HaMetzarim. From that year onward, the Rebbe repeated this call at the start of the Three Weeks each year. Model replicas of the Beit HaMikdash were constructed to facilitate this study, one of which was given to the Rebbe.

title_en: Rebbe calls to publicize teachings on yearning for redemption
summary_en: On 7 MarCheshvan 5746, the Rebbe called for publicizing teachings of Jewish leaders that yearning for the redemption hastens its arrival.
story_body: In a special sichah delivered on 7 MarCheshvan 5746 (October 1985), the Rebbe urged that the words of great Jewish leaders be publicized — namely, that the desire and anticipation for the redemption itself hastens its coming. This was part of the Rebbe's increasing emphasis on the imminence of Moshiach.

title_en: Rebbe declares duty to bring Moshiach in famed 27 Nissan sichah
summary_en: On 27 Nissan 5751, the Rebbe declared that every individual must do all in their power to bring Moshiach and publicize the redemption.
story_body: In a famous sichah delivered on 27 Nissan 5751 (April 11, 1991), the Rebbe declared that the obligation rests on every Jew to do everything possible to bring about the coming of Moshiach and to publicize the message of redemption on the broadest scale. The sichah marked a turning point in Chabad's intensified Moshiach campaign in its final years.

title_en: Chassidut exhibit marking 300 years since the Baal Shem Tov's birth
summary_en: In 5758 the Chabad library mounted an exhibit of early chassidic books marking 300 years since the Baal Shem Tov's birth.
story_body: The Chabad library curated an exhibit of foundational chassidic works printed during the first jubilee following the Baal Shem Tov's passing (5520–5570). The exhibit opened toward Shavuot — the Baal Shem Tov's yahrzeit — and ran until 18 Elul 5758, marking 300 years since his birth on 18 Elul 5458 (1698).

title_en: Birth of the Baal Shem Tov
summary_en: Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov was born on 18 Elul 5458 in Okup.
story_body: The founder of the chassidic movement, Rabbi Israel ben Eliezer, known as the Baal Shem Tov, was born on 18 Elul 5458 (1698) in the town of Okup. He passed away in Medzhibuzh in 5520 (1760).

title_en: Passing of the Baal Shem Tov in Medzhibuzh
summary_en: The Baal Shem Tov passed away in Medzhibuzh in 5520.
story_body: Rabbi Israel Baal Shem Tov, founder of chassidut, passed away in Medzhibuzh in 5520 (1760). His yahrzeit falls on Shavuot. Throughout his lifetime (5494–5520), not a single chassidic book was printed.

title_en: Toldot Yaakov Yosef — first printed chassidic book
summary_en: Toldot Yaakov Yosef, the first chassidic book ever printed, was published in Koretz in 5540.
story_body: Toldot Yaakov Yosef by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, a disciple of the Baal Shem Tov, was printed in Koretz in 5540 (1780). It was the very first printed chassidic work — no chassidic book had been published during the lifetimes of either the Baal Shem Tov or the Maggid of Mezritch.

title_en: Passing of the Maggid of Mezritch
summary_en: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezritch, passed away in Anipoli in 5533.
story_body: Rabbi Dov Ber, the Maggid of Mezritch, successor to the Baal Shem Tov and teacher of the leading chassidic figures of the next generation, passed away in Anipoli in 5533 (1772–73).

title_en: Maggid Devarav LeYaakov first printed in Koretz
summary_en: Maggid Devarav LeYaakov, teachings of the Maggid of Mezritch, was first printed in Koretz in 5541.
story_body: Following the first chassidic book by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, the teachings of the Maggid of Mezritch were printed under the title Maggid Devarav LeYaakov in Koretz in 5541 (1781). It was the first publication of the Maggid's own teachings.

title_en: Ben Porat Yosef printed in Koretz
summary_en: Ben Porat Yosef, by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, was printed in Koretz in 5541.
story_body: Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne's second work, Ben Porat Yosef, was printed in Koretz in 5541 (1781). It contains chassidic teachings, responsa, and novellae.

title_en: Tzofnat Pa'aneach printed in Koretz
summary_en: Tzofnat Pa'aneach by Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne was printed in Koretz in 5542.
story_body: The third printed work of Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Tzofnat Pa'aneach, appeared in Koretz in 5542 (1782) as part of the earliest wave of chassidic publishing.

title_en: Likutim Yekarim — early Baal Shem Tov teachings printed in Lvov
summary_en: Likutim Yekarim, gathering Baal Shem Tov's teachings, was printed in Lvov in 5552.
story_body: Likutim Yekarim, an early compilation of the Baal Shem Tov's teachings together with those of his disciples, was printed in Lvov in 5552 (1792). It appeared roughly twelve years after the first printed works of his disciple Rabbi Yaakov Yosef of Polonne.

title_en: Keter Shem Tov part 1 printed in Zhovkva
summary_en: Keter Shem Tov part 1, anthology of Baal Shem Tov teachings, was printed in Zhovkva in 5554.
story_body: Keter Shem Tov, an anthology of the Baal Shem Tov's teachings, was first printed in Zhovkva (Zalkva). Part 1 appeared in 5554 (1794) and Part 2 the following year, becoming one of the most widely studied collections of Baal Shem Tov teachings.

title_en: Tzava'at HaRivash printed in Zhovkva
summary_en: Tzava'at HaRivash, attributed to the Baal Shem Tov, was printed in Zhovkva in 5555.
story_body: Tzava'at HaRivash, a collection of practices and teachings attributed to the Baal Shem Tov, was printed in Zhovkva in 5555 (1795). This work would later become a flashpoint of controversy when Avigdor of Pinsk cited it in his denunciations against the Alter Rebbe.

title_en: Noam Elimelech printed in Slavuta
summary_en: Noam Elimelech by Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk was printed in Slavuta in 5554.
story_body: Noam Elimelech, one of the foundational works of Polish chassidut by Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, was printed in Slavuta in 5554 (1794), edited and published by his disciple Rabbi Zecharia Mendel of Yaroslav.

title_en: Or HaMeir printed in Koretz
summary_en: Or HaMeir by Rabbi Zev Wolf of Zhitomir was printed in Koretz in 5558.
story_body: Or HaMeir, the work of Rabbi Zev Wolf of Zhitomir on the weekly Torah portion and festivals, was printed in Koretz in 5558 (1798), the year following his passing.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk
summary_en: Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, author of Noam Elimelech, passed away in 5547.
story_body: Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, a leading disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch and author of Noam Elimelech, passed away in 5547 (1787). He shaped the development of chassidut in Poland and Galicia.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk in Tiberias
summary_en: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, who led chassidim to Eretz Yisrael, passed away in Tiberias in 5548.
story_body: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, a disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch, led a group of chassidim to settle in Eretz Yisrael in 5537 (1777). He passed away in Tiberias in 5548 (1788).

title_en: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk leads chassidim to Eretz Yisrael
summary_en: In 5537, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk led a group of chassidim on aliyah to Eretz Yisrael.
story_body: Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk, a disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch, led a major group of chassidim on aliyah to Eretz Yisrael in 5537 (1777). They settled primarily in Tiberias, founding one of the earliest chassidic communities in the Holy Land.

title_en: Passing of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov in Uman
summary_en: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, great-grandson of the Baal Shem Tov, passed away in Uman in 5571.
story_body: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov (5532–5571 / 1772–1810), great-grandson of the Baal Shem Tov, passed away in Uman, where his gravesite remains a major pilgrimage destination for his followers.

title_en: Likutei Moharan printed in Ostroh
summary_en: Likutei Moharan, the central work of Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, was printed in Ostroh in 5568.
story_body: Likutei Moharan, the foundational chassidic text of the Breslov movement by Rabbi Nachman of Breslov, was first printed in Ostroh in 5568 (1808), during the author's lifetime.

title_en: Tanya first publicly circulated in manuscript
summary_en: The Tanya was first circulated publicly in manuscript copies around the year 5552.
story_body: Around 5552 (1792), Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi's Tanya began circulating publicly in handwritten manuscript copies. The Alter Rebbe initially did not wish to print it, but the proliferation of copyists' errors eventually persuaded him to release it to the printers.
